2611.33158.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
2611.33158.abstract: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies. We introduce OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on each robot's kinematics in a specific scene to produce embodiment-specific behavior. This kinematic graph represents the robot's joint positions, motion axes, and connectivity to its visual observation, allowing the policy to account for how its embodiment related to objects and surfaces in the scene. A flow-matching policy predicts relative joint motions for each node, enabling control across robots with different degrees of freedom and kinematic configurations. To learn how physical structure shapes behavior at scale, we procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible robot embodiments; next, we develop algorithms to generate robot trajectories in simulation for all embodiments; finally, we train across diverse simulated manipulation tasks. On 2,000 embodiment-scene-held-out evaluation episodes, OmniAct achieves 63.0% success, compared to 17.8% for pi 0.5 and 57.9% for the strongest baseline; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it achieves 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra's 41.1%. On a previously unseen real-world robot, it achieves nearly twice the success rate of the next best method, MolmoAct2. Beyond task success, we observe that OmniAct learns distinct manipulation strategies that exploit the capabilities and accommodate the limitations of different morphologies. Project: https://omniact.github.io/

llm.title_ja: OmniAct: 100万体の異なる形態に対応するクロスボディメント・マニピュレーションポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 各ロボットの運動学に直接条件付けを行い、異なる自由度や形態に適応した行動を生成するクロスボディメント・マニピュレーションポリシーを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のクロスボディメント手法は共通の行動表現を用いるが、ロボットの形態の違いがマニピュレーション戦略にどう影響するかを捉えきれていない。
llm.method: 運動学グラフを入力として各ノードの相対関節運動を予測するフローマッチングポリシーを導入し、100万体の多様なロボット形態を用いて学習する。
llm.result: 2,000の評価エピソードで63.0%の成功率を達成し、既存ベースラインやpi 0.5を大きく上回る性能を示した。

2611.33145.title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
2611.33145.abstract: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated. Existing benchmarks primarily assess spatial reasoning in static images or synthetic indoor environments, where semantic shortcuts often suffice, making it difficult to faithfully evaluate spatial reasoning capabilities in the wild. In light of this, we present Lost on Campus, a benchmark for evaluating ESR in large-scale real-world outdoor 3D environments reconstructed by 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our benchmark introduces a unified reasoning-action evaluation framework that seamlessly integrates diagnostic QA for isolated reasoning with closed-loop interactive navigation for active reasoning under multimodal instructions. To enable fine-grained diagnosis, we evaluate six capability aspects of ESR: action grounding, spatial foresight, metric awareness, goal-directed planning, ego-allocentric localization, and spatio-temporal consistency. Extensive experiments reveal that: (i) Compared to indoor settings, real-world outdoor environments impose substantially higher demands on spatial reasoning, where existing models exhibit poor performance; (ii) VLMs still struggle with fine-grained visual alignment, with failures in spatial foresight and ego-allocentric localization emerging as primary bottlenecks; (iii) Improving multimodal interaction capabilities and long-term spatial reasoning is crucial for advancing embodied intelligence. These findings highlight that faithful evaluation of ESR demands benchmarks tightly coupling perception, reasoning and action within realistic and continuous environments.

llm.title_ja: Lost on Campus: 野外の大規模3D環境におけるビジョン言語モデルの身体化された空間推論評価
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dガウススプラッティングで再構築した大規模実世界野外環境を用いて、VLMの身体化された空間推論を評価するベンチマークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは主に静止画像や合成屋内環境での空間推論を評価しており、野外の実世界環境での性能を適切に評価できていない。
llm.method: 診断的QAとクローズドロープの対話型ナビゲーションを統合した、統合型の推論・行動評価フレームワークを導入する。
llm.result: 実世界野外環境は屋内よりも高い空間推論能力を要求し、既存モデルは微視的な視覚アライメントやego-allocentricな局所化に苦労していることが判明した。

2611.33144.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
2611.33144.abstract: Learning for dexterous manipulation is limited by the scarcity of high-quality demonstrations: retargeting from human video is imprecise, teleoperation gives no force feedback to the operator, and exoskeleton-based collection is hard to scale up. We present PyRUA-Dex, a framework that enables coding agents to develop dexterous manipulation through programmatic policy, without the need of demonstrations. The programmatic policy is developed in two stages: during exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses the successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for enhanced robustness and execution efficiency. In simulated environments, PyRUA-Dex achieves SOTA on Bench2Dex with a score of 72.9 and reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, PyRUA-Dex learns to play piano, write calligraphy, and other tasks efficiently: learning a new piece from sheet music takes as little as 30 minutes. These results suggest that PyRUA-Dex is an effective framework for developing dexterous manipulation policies with coding agents in the absence of high quality dexterous manipulation demonstrations.
2611.33144.comment: 23 pages, 9 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://vme0522.github.io/PyRUA-Dex/

llm.title_ja: PyRUA-Dex: コーディングエージェントを用いた器用な両手マニピュレーションのためのプログラム的ポリシー学習
llm.tldr_ja: デモンストレーションなしで、コーディングエージェントを活用してプログラム的ポリシーにより器用な両手マニピュレーションを開発するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 器用なマニピュレーションの学習は、人間動画からのリターゲットの不正確さや、触覚フィードバックの欠如、データ収集の拡張性の低さによって制限されている。
llm.method: 探索段階でエージェントが並列にスキルを探索し、蒸留エージェントがタスクライブラリとプログラムに要約、その後の改善段階でランダム化により頑健性を高める。
llm.result: シミュレーション環境のBench2DexおよびDexJoCoでSOTAを達成し、実世界のピアノ演奏や書道などのタスクを効率的に学習できた。
keywords_ja: 両手マニピュレーション
コーディングエージェント
プログラム的ポリシー

2611.33143.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
2611.33143.abstract: Embodied spatial intelligence requires agents to gather information through exploration and interaction, then use it to reason and act. Existing benchmarks insufficiently distinguish correct outcomes from completion of these task requirements. We introduce ROAM-Bench to evaluate these abilities under robot motion and collision constraints. Independent checks use simulation state and episode records to assess outcomes and task requirements, with stronger checks of geometry, coverage, or placement. It comprises 250 manually validated tasks across 11 types in five groups and 27 indoor environments, covering object and room search, counting, geometric judgments, direction reasoning, and relocation. Human evaluators achieve 84% strict task success on 100 sampled tasks, with every correct outcome satisfying the required checks. Across seven frontier vision-language models, we identify two complementary failure modes: correct outcomes with unmet task requirements, and incorrect outcomes despite passing stronger checks. Oracle-input diagnostics show that more complete target observations and calibrated feedback improve final spatial judgments.

llm.title_ja: ROAM-Bench: 証拠検証を通じた身体化された能動的空間知能の評価
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの移動や衝突の制約下で、探索と相互作用を通じた能動的空間知能を評価するためのベンチマークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークでは、正しい結果とタスク要件の達成を十分に区別できていない。
llm.method: シミュレーションの状態やエピソード記録を用いて、幾何学、カバレッジ、配置などの独立した厳格な検証を行う250の手動検証済みタスクを構築する。
llm.result: 7つの最先端ビジョン言語モデルの評価から、タスク要件を満たさない正しい結果や、強力な検証を通過しても不正解になるという2つの補完的な失敗モードが特定された。

2611.33141.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
2611.33141.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) build policies on pretrained video-generation models, on the premise that predicting how a scene evolves helps determine how to act. However, generating future scenes is expensive for real-time control. This motivates efficient proxies for future imagination, but how to train such proxies without sacrificing action-prediction quality remains unclear. An effective proxy need not generate a high-resolution frame; it only needs to provide enough information to distinguish between possible futures. This leads to the design principle behind iWAM: rather than denoising an entire future frame, can we condition the action policy on intermediate features from a single video-model evaluation? We show that the answer is yes. Exploiting the reversible dynamics of flow-matching models, we invert each training future into the corresponding latent noise vector. However, a single velocity evaluation at this latent does not necessarily yield informative features for action prediction. We therefore learn a bidirectional flow map that amortizes future-generation computation, enabling a single model evaluation to provide effective conditioning features. At inference, we sample a latent noise vector from the prior and condition the policy using just one video-backbone forward pass. Across simulated benchmarks and real robots, iWAM recovers the generalization benefits of WAMs while substantially reducing its inference cost.

llm.title_ja: iWAM: 鮮明な将来予測を伴わない世界モデルからの効率的な行動予測
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの動画生成モデルの可逆的なダイナミクスを利用し、将来のフレーム全体のデノイジングを行わずに効率的な行動条件付けを実現する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の世界・行動モデルは将来のシーン生成に高い計算コストがかかり、リアルタイム制御の足かせとなっている。
llm.method: フローマッチングモデルの可逆的ダイナミクスを利用し、学習時の未来を潜在ノイズベクトルに反転させ、双方向フローマップを学習して単一モデル評価で効果的な条件付け特徴を提供する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機ロボットにおいて、世界モデルの汎化性能を維持しつつ推論コストを大幅に削減することに成功した。

2611.33137.title: Physicl Scenes: An Artist-created 3D Dataset for Learning Perception and Action
2611.33137.abstract: We present Physicl Scenes, a high-quality artist-created and curated dataset of 6,499 3D scenes spanning household rooms, public interiors, and outdoor spaces. The dataset combines detailed geometry, physically based materials, and carefully composed environments with object- and part-level semantic annotations, providing rich, joint supervision for visual and embodied learning. We demonstrate its value as training data across inverse rendering, 3D reconstruction, scene understanding, and mobile manipulation. Across these tasks, training state-of-the-art methods with our scenes improves performance over alternative synthetic datasets. In addition, we introduce a mobile manipulation benchmark, evaluating vision-language-action models performing physical pick and place in diverse 3D scenes with realistic layouts, and using our part annotations to also score where each object is grasped. Our dataset will be released publicly to facilitate research in visual and embodied AI.

llm.title_ja: Physicl Scenes: 知覚と行動の学習に向けたアーティスト作成の3Dデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: 詳細な幾何学、物理ベースの素材、オブジェクトおよびパーツレベルのセマンティックアノテーションを組み合わせた6,499のアーティスト作成3Dシーンデータセットを提案する。
llm.problem: 視覚的および身体化された学習のための、リッチで統合的な教師信号を持つ高品質な3Dシーンデータが不足している。
llm.method: 家庭、公共施設、野外の部屋を網羅する高品質な3Dシーンを構築し、逆レンダリング、3D再構成、シーン理解、モバイルマニピュレーションの訓練データとして活用する。
llm.result: 最先端手法の訓練データとして用いることで、他の合成データセットと比較して逆レンダリングやモバイルマニピュレーション等の性能が向上した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.33130.title: Exploratory Midtraining for Robot Policies
2611.33130.abstract: Robot policies predominantly learn from human-collected data emphasizing competent behavior, limiting coverage of the low-level behaviors needed to support autonomous improvement. We study how a form of midtraining can be used to build coverage over diverse low-level behaviors that connect challenging states of the robot and its environment to states from which further progress is possible ("connected behavioral coverage"). We also examine how this coverage supports downstream adaptation and online improvement. To this end, we introduce $β$-Data, a dataset collected via adversarial teleoperation, where a human adversary reversibly perturbs the environment while a human operator continues toward completion without resetting. We relabel trajectory segments with local outcomes in natural language and finetune a pretrained policy conditioned on recent action history. The resulting policy exhibits sustained use of more low-level behaviors. Across manipulation tasks in simulation and on three real-robot platforms, our approach yields more favorable data scaling laws, better zero-shot generalization, and more effective use of additional rollout time than training on standard demonstrations. During online finetuning, these policies need fewer rollouts to collect successful experience and reach higher success rates, suggesting that midtraining can prepare robots for both more robust task execution and continued autonomous improvement. Our project page and robot videos are available at https://kshitiz-1225.github.io/exploratory-midtraining-robot-policies/.

llm.title_ja: ロボットポリシーのための探索的ミッドトレーニング
llm.tldr_ja: 敵対的テロップ操作により困難な状態から進行可能な状態へ繋ぐ多様な低レベル行動のカバレッジを構築するミッドトレーニング手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 人間の優秀なデモンストレーションに基づく学習だけでは、自律的な改善を支える低レベル行動のカバレッジが制限される。
llm.method: 敵対的テロオペレーションで収集したβ-Dataを用い、軌跡セグメントに自然言語の局所結果をラベル付けして、過去の行動履歴を条件とした事前学習済みポリシーをファインチューニングする。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび3つの実機プラットフォームにおいて、データスケーリング則の改善、ゼロショット汎化性能の向上、オンラインファインチューニング時の試行回数削減を実現した。

2611.33118.title: Neural Implicit Representation for Bathymetry Estimation using Sidescan Sonar Imagery
2611.33118.abstract: Bathymetry measurement and estimation is critical for understanding the structure of underwater environments. While multibeam echosounders (MBES) provide accurate depth measurements, their deployment on surface vessels limits spatial resolution in deep water. Sidescan sonar (SSS), in contrast, can be deployed on autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) to operate closer to the seafloor, enabling high-resolution acoustic imaging. However, the inherent ambiguity in measurements and the limited observation coverage of sonar datasets degrade the performance of state-of-the-art methods for underwater bathymetry estimation from SSS. In this paper, we propose a differentiable neural rendering framework for SSS that enables effective estimation of bathymetry from SSS measurements. Our approach incorporates a measurement model based on SSS geometry, explicitly accounting for its wide elevation aperture and associated ambiguities. We evaluate our method on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating improved robustness and accuracy compared to alternative approaches.
2611.33118.comment: 7 pages, 8 figures. This paper is accepted by IEEE OCEANS 2026 Monterey

llm.title_ja: サイドスキャンソナー画像を用いた海底地形推定のためのニューラル暗黙的表現
llm.tldr_ja: 広範な仰角アパチャーとそれに伴う曖昧さを明示的に考慮したサイドスキャンソナー用の微分可能ニューラルレンダリングフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: サイドスキャンソナーの計測における固有の曖昧さと限定された観測範囲が、海底地形推定手法の性能を低下させている。
llm.method: サイドスキャンソナーの幾何学に基づく計測モデルを組み込んだ微分可能ニューラルレンダリングフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 合成および実世界のデータセットを用いた評価において、従来手法と比較して優れた頑健性と精度を示した。
keywords_ja: サイドスキャンソナー
ニューラルレンダリング

2611.33054.title: EmbodiSafety: Benchmarking Risk Understanding and Response in Embodied AI
2611.33054.abstract: Progress in embodied foundation models is largely measured by task success, while the physical safety of their decisions remains underexamined. Safety evaluations centered on rule following and binary judgments do not adequately assess whether embodied models understand environmental hazards and make safe decisions. We introduce EmbodiSafety, comprising 1,092 snapshot tasks and 540 trajectory tasks across 844 visual scenarios to assess safety over short and long horizons. Six response modes cover direct execution, refusal, clarification, constrained execution, autonomous recovery, and human escalation. Distinguishing recovery from human intervention makes the boundary of safe autonomy an explicit evaluation target. Our protocol assesses mode correctness, risk identification, and actionable handling, with complete decision accuracy requiring all applicable checks to pass. Claude-Opus-5.5 achieves the highest complete decision accuracy among reference models, reaching 56.1% on snapshots and 61.5% on trajectories. We further develop a data construction pipeline and curate 40k examples for safety alignment. Supervised training on this corpus raises the complete decision accuracy of Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B.

llm.title_ja: EmbodiSafety: 身体化AIにおけるリスク理解と応答のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 短期的・長的な安全性を評価するため、844の視覚的シナリオにわたる1,092のスナップショットタスクと540の軌跡タスクを含むベンチマークを提案する。
llm.problem: ルール遵守や二値的な判断を中心とした従来の安全性評価では、身体化モデルが環境のハザードを理解し安全な意思決定を行えるかを十分に評価できない。
llm.method: 直接実行、拒否、明確化、制約付き実行、自律回復、人間へのエスカレーションの6つの応答モードを設定し、モードの正しさ、リスク識別、実用的な対応を評価するプロトコルを構築する。
llm.result: Claude-Opus-5.5が最高精度を記録し、さらに4万件のデータを用いたキュレーションと教師あり学習によりQwenモデルの意思決定精度が向上した。

2611.33040.title: At the Limit: Autonomous Vehicle Drifting under Generative Policies
2611.33040.abstract: Autonomous drifting requires agile control despite tire-force saturation and highly nonlinear vehicle dynamics. We propose an online reinforcement learning method for flow policies that combines stochastic differential equation (SDE) sampling for exploration with value-based policy optimization. This method supports both training from scratch and fine-tuning a policy pretrained on expert demonstrations. After training, control actions can be generated using either SDEs or ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Experiments on circular and eight-shaped drifting in an F1TENTH digital twin platform show that both training strategies can achieve effective real-time drift control, with tighter tracking, higher success rates, and better robustness under noisy conditions.

llm.title_ja: 限界への挑戦: 生成ポリシーによる自動運転車のドリフト制御
llm.tldr_ja: 確率微分方程式のサンプリングによる探索と価値ベースのポリシー最適化を組み合わせた、フローポリシーのためのオンライン強化学習手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 自動運転車のドリフト制御には、タイヤ力の飽和や高度に非線形な車両ダイナミクスが存在する中で敏捷な制御が求められる。
llm.method: SDEサンプリングによる探索と価値ベースのポリシー最適化を組み合わせたオンライン強化学習手法を設計し、SDEまたはODEを用いて制御行動を生成する。
llm.result: F1TENTHデジタルツインプラットフォームでの円形および8字型ドリフト実験により、効果的なリアルタイム制御、高精度な追従、高い成功率を実現した。

2611.33014.title: Training Lightweight Gaze Models without Target Gaze Annotation: What Makes a Good Teacher?
2611.33014.abstract: Model-generated labels offer a scalable route to training lightweight vision models, but what makes a model a good teacher, and can we tell before training a student? We study this in gaze target estimation, where interactive robots need models that are both accurate and efficient. In a controlled comparison of eleven supervision conditions, we vary only the source of gaze-point labels, keeping the student, training protocol and 361k training samples fixed, across three video datasets, two student sizes and three seeds; every student is evaluated against human annotation. Three findings emerge. First, imperfect model-generated labels can replace human annotation: Gaze-LLE, never trained on the target datasets' gaze annotation, trains students that match annotation-trained ones on ViT-Tiny and are significantly more accurate on ViT-Small (average distance error 0.187 vs 0.196), and the ViT-Tiny student runs 32$\times$ faster than its teacher on a laptop CPU. Second, apparent competence can conceal unreliable supervision: given another person's face centre in the prompt, InternVL3 and Qwen3-VL return it on 93.4% and 81.1% of test samples, and a copy-the-coordinate baseline matches InternVL3's labels and students. Without that coordinate, both models fall far behind the specialist. Third, good teachers can be identified before training: validation label error ranks student test error (Spearman's $ρ= 0.91$), and ten annotated clips single out the two specialist teachers in 95% of draws. These findings give practical principles for assessing supervision, exposing shortcuts and selecting teachers for lightweight models.

llm.title_ja: ターゲット視線アノテーションなしの軽量視線モデルの学習: 良い教師モデルとは何か
llm.tldr_ja: 教師モデルの検証ラベル誤差が学生のテスト誤差を正確にランク付けできることを示し、ターゲットデータセットの注釈なしで軽量視線モデルを効果的に訓練する原則を明らかにた。
llm.problem: インタラクティブなロボットに必要な高精度かつ効率的な視線推定モデルの学習において、モデル生成ラベルの品質や良い教師の条件が事前に不明である。
llm.method: 11の教師条件を比較し、学生モデル、訓練プロトコル、361kの訓練サンプルを固定した制御比較実験を行う。
llm.result: 不完全なモデル生成ラベルが人間の注釈の代わりになり得ること、さらに検証ラベル誤差によって事前に良い教師モデルを識別できることが判明した。

2611.33013.title: RFW-W: Scaling Physical Asset Universes for Generative Embodied Simulation
2611.33013.abstract: Scaling embodied simulation requires diverse objects with executable physical representations. We present RFW-W, a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable asset sources to task-conditioned scene composition. Its reported inventories comprise 1,010,386 asset records: 524,611 rigid assets in 1,212 categories (RFW-R), 402,410 articulated assets in 531 categories (RFW-A), and 83,365 jointly verified deformables in 485 categories (RFW-S). These taxonomies contribute 2,228 dataset--category entries. RFW-R couples category-guided generation with collision geometry, composed physical properties, and interaction annotations; RFW-A uses reusable agent-authored procedural generators with explicit part and joint structure; RFW-S uses structure-aware simulation representations, calibration, and independent testing. A common interface preserves physical requirements specific to each asset type for retrieval and scene assembly. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that RFW-R provides broader asset coverage and stronger scene-fulfillment capabilities than existing datasets. Across five RoboTwin tasks, using 100 demonstrations per task for each asset source, policies trained on RFW-R achieve macro success rates of 71.2% in clean settings and 41.8% under randomization, exceeding the strongest baseline by 15.8 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively. RFW-W provides a scalable and unified asset foundation for generating physically grounded, task-conditioned embodied worlds.

llm.title_ja: RFW-W: 生成的身体化シミュレーションに向けた物理アセットユニバースのスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 剛体、可動関節体、変形可能なアセットのソースをタスク条件付きシーン構成に結びつける物理アセットユニバース「RFW-W」を提案する。
llm.problem: 身体化シミュレーションの拡張には、実行可能な物理表現を持つ多様なオブジェクトが必要である。
llm.method: 剛体、可動関節体、変形可能なアセットを網羅する100万件超のレコードを収集し、共通インターフェースを通じて物理的要件を保持してシーン構築を行う。
llm.result: RoboTwinタスクにおいて、RFW-Wで訓練されたポリシーは従来よりも優れたマクロ成功率を達成し、拡張性とシーン構築能力を示した。

2611.33010.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
2611.33010.abstract: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. Across five policies spanning Vision-Language-Action models, World Action Models, and agentic policies, every mirror condition reduces aggregate success rates: averaged over the three conditions, the drop ranges from 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points across policies, and it reaches 62.5 points on the mirrored tabletop. Because a mirror is also a physical obstacle, we compare it against geometrically matched non-reflective panels; 50--88\% of mirror-specific failures occur without recorded robot--panel contact, so direct collisions alone do not explain the degradation. Trajectory and contact analyses instead reveal recurring behaviors consistent with phantom targeting of reflected objects and spatial mislocalization of real ones. Targeted diagnostics further characterize grasping near reflections, policy-dependent pushing progress, and physical-target interaction under main-camera occlusion. Real-robot experiments with $π_{0.5}$ and FastWAM also show lower overall success rates under the upright-mirror and mirrored-tabletop conditions. These findings reveal a shared vulnerability to reflective environments across diverse robot policies and motivate reflection-aware evaluation of embodied intelligence. Code is available at https://github.com/iPPLab/robodojo-mirror.
2611.33010.hf_summary_en: A new benchmark shows that many robot manipulation policies perform worse when mirrors are present, often because they confuse reflections with real objects rather than simply colliding with the mirror.

llm.title_ja: エンボディドAIは鏡テストに不合格：単純な鏡がロボットポリシーをいかに破るか
llm.tldr_ja: 新しいベンチマークにより、多くのロボット操作ポリシーは鏡が存在すると性能が低下し、単なる衝突ではなく反射を実物と混同することが原因であることが示された。
llm.problem: 反射面のある環境において、現在のロボット操作ポリシーがどのように性能を落とすかという脆弱性の検証。
llm.method: 鏡を含むタスク条件を持つベンチマークRoboDojo-Mirrorを構築し、複数のロボットポリシーの成功率や軌跡・接触を分析した。
llm.result: 全ての鏡の条件で成功率が10.8〜56.7ポイント低下し、直接の衝突だけでなく反射物への誤認や空間の誤認識が原因であることを明らかにした。

2611.32986.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
2611.32986.abstract: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps. Thus, we propose CAPER (Capacity-Aware Part-grounding and Evidence Refinement), a manual-guided robotic assembly framework that enables VLMs to generate assembly procedures with two modules--PartGround and PlanRefine. PartGround aligns step-level manual evidence with product-specific inventory and part-reference information to identify exact Part IDs and quantities, transforming free-form hardware prediction into evidence-guided assignments represented in a shared Assembly Intermediate Representation (Assembly IR). PlanRefine audits PartGround assignments against finite inventory by removing the lowest-confidence assignments. Uncertain identity cases remain marked for review in the Assembly IR. We evaluate CAPER on the IKEA Assembly in the Wild (IAW) dataset. Experiment results show that CAPER reaches a Finite-inventory Consistency Rate of 83.33% and produces zero observed out-of-inventory Part-ID occurrences. At the plan level, PlanRefine removes all observed inventory-overuse pairs (9 -> 0) and excess units (51 -> 0). Overall, the results indicate that PartGround and PlanRefine improve part reliability, while also enhancing finite-inventory consistency and local prediction accuracy. Project page and video: https://xhzzzz123.github.io/CAPER/
2611.32986.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Project page and video: https://xhzzzz123.github.io/CAPER/

llm.title_ja: CAPER: 信頼性の高い手動ガイド付きロボット組立計画のためのPartGroundとPlanRefine
llm.tldr_ja: VLMがマニュアルから組立手順を生成する際の問題を解決するため、PartGroundとPlanRefineの2つのモジュールを備えた組立計画フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: VLMをロボットのタスク計画に用いてマニュアルから手順を導出する際、部品の正確な識別情報の混同やサポート外の部品ID予測、ステップ間の不整合が生じる。
llm.method: マニュアルの証拠と製品固有の在庫情報を整合させて正確な部品IDと数量を特定する「PartGround」と、有限在庫に基づいて割り当てを監査する「PlanRefine」を導入する。
llm.result: IKEA Assembly in the Wildデータセットでの実験により、有限在庫一貫性率が83.33%に達し、在庫超過の割り当てが完全に排除された。

2611.32979.title: File Size as a Potential Dataset Bias in Audio-Visual Deepfake Data
2611.32979.abstract: Deepfake detection benchmarks are commonly designed to evaluate whether models can distinguish authentic from manipulated audiovisual content. However, benchmark construction pipelines may introduce unintended associations between class labels and simple file-level properties. In this work, we identify a potential file-size bias in two widely used audio-visual deepfake datasets. In the 1M-Deepfakes Detection Challenge dataset, a score derived from file size alone achieves 70.13% AUC on the validation set. When file size is considered together with video duration, simple file-level methods exceed 90% AUC on 1M and 85% AUC on FakeAVCeleb. Although the same pattern is not observed in DFDC, the results suggest that the observed association is dataset-dependent rather than an inherent property of deepfake videos. We discuss several possible explanations, including differences in encoding, compression, source data, manipulation procedures, and post-processing, although the present analysis does not establish the underlying cause. We further discuss whether the factors associated with file size may also leave traces in decoded video or audio, and consequently whether they could influence content-based deepfake detection, as an important direction for future work. Our findings highlight the importance of examining simple file-level properties when constructing and evaluating deepfake datasets and benchmarks.
2611.32979.comment: Accepted in WACV Workshop 2027 (Workshop Synthetic Realities and Data in Biometric Analysis and Security (SynRDinBAS))

llm.title_ja: ファイルサイズはオーディオビジュアルディープフェイクデータにおける潜在的なデータセットバイアスか
llm.tldr_ja: 広く使われている2つのオーディオビジュアルディープフェイクデータセットにおいて、ファイルサイズとクラスラベルの間に意図しない関連性が存在することを明らかにした。
llm.problem: ディープフェイク検出のベンチマーク構築パイプラインが、クラスラベルとファイルレベルの単純なプロパティの間に意図しない関連性を持ち込んでいる可能性がある。
llm.method: 1M-Deepfakes Detection Challengeなどのデータセットを対象に、ファイルサイズや動画の長さを特徴とした単純なファイルレベル手法のAUCを検証する。
llm.result: ファイルサイズ単体や動画の長さとの組み合わせで高いAUC（70.13%以上）が達成され、データセット構築時のエンコーディング等に依存したバイアスが存在することが示唆された。
llm.limitation: 本解析では根本的な原因の特定には至っていない。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出
データセットバイアス

2611.32967.title: VidForce: Predicting Force-Aware Articulation by Observing Humans
2611.32967.abstract: People can anticipate how an object moves and the effort an interaction may require by watching others. How can embodied agents acquire this understanding from video? Force measurements provide direct sensory supervision, but require specialized equipment and remain limited in quantity. We introduce VidForce, which estimates an interaction trajectory together with a force profile from a third-person RGB video; 2D contact clicks and textual object-action prompts are optional. Our approach makes limited instrumented measurements useful for interpreting human interactions through learned physical prototypes as a prior. The prototypes share learned force levels and temporal profiles across interactions of comparable effort, with visual and semantic cues determining their contribution to each observation. Geometric and vision-language features adapt this prior to the observed interaction, while a joint conditional flow refines an initial tracked trajectory together with the force profile. Paired human and instrumented-gripper recordings provide measured force references for supervising human video, and a separately trained torque model demonstrates that the formulation extends to other sensory quantities. We evaluate trajectory recovery and force estimation through baseline comparisons and controlled ablations on held-out interactions from the Hoi! dataset. On this evaluation subset, VidForce achieves 6.6 cm ATE, peak-force MAE and RMSE of 4.81 N and 5.92 N, respectively, and force-profile RMSE of 5.52 N. On real-world videos, VidForce infers motion and force reliably and consistently despite the variability in human execution. We further deploy VidForce on a Spot robot, where trajectories and force profiles estimated from human demonstrations drive real-world articulated-object manipulation, and report success rates across repeated trials. Project page: https://rafaymhddn.github.io/vidforce

llm.title_ja: VidForce: 人間の観察に基づく力認識型関節運動の予測
llm.tldr_ja: 三人称視点のRGB動画から、物理プロトタイプを事前知識として利用して、相互作用の軌跡と力プロファイル共同で推定する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 力計測は直接的な感覚的教師信号を与えるが、専用の設備が必要でありデータ量も限られている。
llm.method: 学習済みの物理プロトタイプを事前知識として活用し、幾何学的およびビジョン言語特徴を用いて適応させ、結合条件付きフローにより軌跡と力プロファイルを洗練させる。
llm.result: Hoi!データセットを用いた評価で優れた軌跡回復と力推定精度を実現し、実世界のSpotロボットにおけるマニピュレーションにも応用できることを示した。

2611.32960.title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles
2611.32960.abstract: Level 4 autonomous vehicles require fault-tolerant architectures that preserve critical driving functions under sensing, computing, communication, power, and actuation failures. As these systems progress toward industrial scalability, architectural complexity, validation burden, integration effort, and lifecycle cost become increasingly relevant. This study proposes an Operational Design Domain (ODD)-based, safety-constrained systems-engineering framework for architecture rationalization. ODD-specific capabilities, physical fault assumptions, post-fault operational policies, and spatial sensing requirements are propagated through an integrated safety-feasibility gate. Architecture transformations, including removal, relocation, functional reassignment, and consolidation, are evaluated only within the resulting safety-feasible design space, followed by lifecycle-cost sensitivity and robust multiobjective Pareto analysis. A generic, synthetically parameterized Level 4 architecture is used as a demonstrative computational case study. Within this modeled design space, direct ablation showed limited rationalization potential, whereas directional redistribution and functional consolidation generated a broader set of safety-feasible candidates. Under the illustrative lifecycle-cost model, the best nominal candidate achieved a 5.55% normalized cost reduction and remained cost-reducing across all 5,000 sampled points in the prescribed uncertainty domain. The analysis identified 15 non-dominated architecture-policy solutions representing seven physical transformations. The results support capability-based, policy-conditioned, and lifecycle-aware architecture rationalization under the stated assumptions, with safety retained as a non-compensatory feasibility constraint. The reported transformations are design candidates rather than validated production architectures.

llm.title_ja: 安全性駆動型冗長性から価値駆動型アーキテクチャへ: レベル4自動運転車のためのODDベースの合理化フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: レベル4自動運転車を対象に、ODDに基づく安全制約付きのシステム工学フレームワークを提案し、ライフサイクルコストを考慮したアーキテクチャの合理化を行う。
llm.problem: レベル4自動運転システムの商業化が進むにつれて、アーキテクチャの複雑さ、検証負担、ライフサイクルコストが大きな課題となっている。
llm.method: ODD固有の能力や物理的故障の仮定、空間センシング要件を統合安全・実現可能性ゲートに通し、安全性制約を満たす設計空間内でアーキテクチャの変換や統合を評価する。
llm.result: 合成パラメータ化されたケーススタディにおいて、機能的統合により安全性を維持しつつ5.55%の正規化コスト削減を実現する最適候補を特定した。
keywords_ja: システムアーキテクチャ

2611.32944.title: DynaMimic: A Physics-Informed World Model for Humanoid Motion Tracking
2611.32944.abstract: Whole-body motion tracking enables humanoid robots to reproduce diverse skills from human demonstrations. Existing model-free reinforcement learning methods either distill motion specialists into a single policy at the cost of performance or train a generalist policy directly using cluster-scale computation. SuperMimic reduces this computational cost through a differentiable world model that implicitly learns the physics shared across motions by predicting the next state from the current state and action. However, this implicit formulation may not fully capture the underlying physical processes. Errors around changes of support can accumulate over imagined rollouts used to train the tracking policy. To address this challenge, we introduce DynaMimic, a differentiable world model that explicitly incorporates shared physics into state prediction. Specifically, its network predicts a contact wrench at each candidate support link and a residual generalized force. DynaMimic then uses these predictions to compute the next state through closed-form Lagrangian forward dynamics. Across 60 full LAFAN1 motions, DynaMimic reduces mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) by 18.6% relative to SuperMimic. For terrain tracking, we give both methods the same local height maps. Relative to terrain-conditioned SuperMimic, DynaMimic reduces MPJPE by 14.9% on A3 Parkour (66.15 to 56.28~mm) and by 10.8% on GRAIL terrain clips (141.88 to 126.57~mm). On a real A3 humanoid, the learned policies can perform diverse skills, such as floor recovery, cartwheel and a box vault.

llm.title_ja: DynaMimic: ヒューマノイド動作追従のための物理情報世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 各支持リンクでの接触レンチと残差一般化力を明示的に予測し、閉形式のラグランジュ順方向ダイナミクスで次の状態を計算する微分可能世界モデルを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の暗黙的モデルベース手法では基礎となる物理プロセスを完全に捉えきれず、支持脚の切り替え時に誤差が蓄積する。
llm.method: 各支持リンクの接触レンチと残差一般化力を予測し、ラグランジュ順方向ダイナミクスを用いて次の状態を計算する微分可能世界モデルを構築する。
llm.result: 60のLAFAN1動作および不整地追従において、SuperMimicと比較してMPJPE（関節位置誤差平均）を大幅に削減し、実機ヒューマノイドでの多様なスキル実行に成功した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
物理シミュレーション

2611.32937.title: Self-Sensing Compliant Anthropomorphic Hand for Speed-Dictated Shared Force Control in Teleoperation
2611.32937.abstract: In vision-based teleoperation of robotic hands, the operator receives no haptic feedback and therefore struggles to regulate the grasp force, while adding tactile sensors to the fingers increases wiring, cost and integration complexity. Compliant hands offer an alternative, as their mechanical compliance, usually treated only as a passive property for safe and adaptive grasping, can also serve as a source of information. Here, we show that the elastic transmission of a compliant, tendon-driven anthropomorphic hand can itself act as the sensor for shared-control telemanipulation. Series springs in the tendon routing are read by potentiometers in a forearm-mounted motor box, from which the hand estimates its joint states and finger forces without any external sensors. Building on this self-sensing, we develop a contact-aware shared-control framework for VR-based teleoperation. The robot hand is controlled through a mapping from the operator's hand kinematics until a contact is detected proprioceptively. Control then switches to a finger-level force controller whose set point is determined by the operator's grasping speed, and control authority can be allocated to individual fingers. Experiments validate the system's force estimation and increased grasp success rate compared with direct teleoperation for fragile and heavy objects. These results show that compliance can serve not only for passive adaptation but also as an intrinsic sensing resource for physical human-robot collaboration.
2611.32937.comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible. Project page: https://huijiang-wang.github.io/selfsensing-hand/

llm.title_ja: 速度指令型共有力制御のための自己センシング柔軟性人間型ハンド
llm.tldr_ja: 腱駆動型ロボットハンドの弾性伝達機構自体をセンサーとして利用し、外部センサーを追加せずに自己センシングと接触認識を実現するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ビジョンベースの遠隔操作では触覚フィードバックがなく把持力の調節が困難であり、指に触覚センサーを追加すると複雑さやコストが増加する。
llm.method: 腱配線の直列バネを前腕のモーターボックス内のポテンショメータで読み取り、外部センサーなしで関節状態と指の力を推定した上で、接触検知後に力制御へ切り替える。
llm.result: 壊れやすい物体や重い物体の把持において、直接遠隔操作と比較して力推定精度と把持成功率が向上した。

2611.32932.title: HARI4D: Hand-Articulation Aware 4D Reconstruction of Human-Object Interaction
2611.32932.abstract: Reasoning about human-object interaction from RGB cameras is important for gaming, VR environments, and robot learning. Yet 4D reconstruction from a monocular RGB camera is challenging, especially when articulated hands are involved. Prior full-body works neglect hands during reconstruction, causing them to penetrate into, or float from the object. We present HARI4D, a hand-articulation-aware method for reconstructing spatially and temporally consistent 4D human-object interaction from monocular RGB video. We introduce a history-aware object tracker that provides robust and stable tracking. Based on these tracks, we improve the interaction configuration through coarse-to-fine reasoning that follows the order of object manipulation: ReachNet first brings the full body and arms to the object during contact, and TouchNet then finalizes hand articulation according to temporal context and local object geometry. On ARCTIC, unseen in training, our method reduces the object error by 56% and improves hand contact F1 from 0.866 to 0.921 over prior art. Our method recovers accurate full body-object interaction with coherent hand articulations and applies to online videos. Our code and pretrained models will be released.

llm.title_ja: HARI4D: 人間とオブジェクトの相互作用における手首の関節運動を考慮した4D再構成
llm.tldr_ja: 単眼RGB動画から、履歴を考慮したオブジェクトトラッカーと、段階的な粗密推論を用いて人間とオブジェクトの相互作用を4D再構成する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 単眼RGBカメラからの4D再構成は、手部の関節運動が考慮されないと手オブジェクトの貫通や浮きが生じるという課題がある。
llm.method: 履歴を考慮したオブジェクトトラッカーを導入し、ReachNetで身体と腕をオブジェクトに接触させ、TouchNetで時間的文脈と局所的幾何学に基づいて手部の関節運動を最終決定する。
llm.result: ARCTICデータセットを用いた評価で、オブジェクト誤差を56%削減し、手の接触F1スコアを0.866から0.921に向上させた。
keywords_ja: 人間オブジェクト相互作用

2611.32900.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
2611.32900.abstract: World models support embodied decision-making by predicting future environment states. In embodied visual tracking, uncertain target motion and robot-induced viewpoint changes jointly affect visual observations, making future-state prediction challenging. We propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which incorporates predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions. A Geometry--Progress module jointly models geometric paths and single-step travel distances through shared motion modes and path-conditioned progress distributions. This formulation captures uncertainty in route selection and motion progress while preserving their dependence. Action-induced coordinate transformations express predicted paths in the next robot frame, providing geometrically grounded conditions for future visual-state prediction. Future visual feature reconstruction supervises the motion predictor through the conditioned transition branch, linking explicit motion representations to subsequent observations. The model is jointly optimized with motion likelihood, feature reconstruction, and expert-action supervision, enabling the tracking policy to combine visual context with predictive motion cues.Experiments on three embodied tracking benchmarks demonstrate improved tracking performance and cross-environment generalization with a lightweight $0.5$B backbone.

llm.title_ja: 身体性ビジュアルトラッキングのための動作条件付き世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 予測されたターゲット動作とロボットのエゴモーションを潜在状態遷移に組み込んだ、身体性ビジュアルトラッキングのための動作条件付き世界モデルを提案する。
llm.problem: 不確実なターゲットの動きとロボット視点の変化が視覚的観測に影響するため、将来の状態予測が困難である。
llm.method: 予測されたターゲット動作分布とロボットのエゴモーションを潜在状態遷移に組み込み、幾何学的パスと移動距離を共同でモデル化する。
llm.result: 3つの身体性トラッキングベンチマークにおいて、軽量な0.5Bバックボーンで追従性能とクロス環境汎化の向上が示された。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルトラッキング

2611.32876.title: MemHand: Memory-Enhanced World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
2611.32876.abstract: Recovering the continuous world-space motion of both hands from egocentric video is essential for applications such as human-to-robot policy transfer and augmented reality. Achieving this goes beyond reconstructing the hands from each individual frame, as the context that a frame needs is often spread over time, especially around occlusions or when a hand moves out of sight. Recent works have explored how to exploit temporal context, yet they mostly draw it from fixed-length windows. Such windows cannot guarantee that every frame has the context required to reconstruct the hands in world space with accurate poses and metric scale. To address this limitation, we introduce MemHand, a memory-enhanced framework for world-space hand motion reconstruction. MemHand maintains two complementary forms of memory. The Short-Term Event Memory keeps the context of the well-observed hand around each occlusion or out-of-sight event and supplies it to frames with weak or missing visual evidence. In addition, since the metric scale holds over the whole recording, the Long-Term Scale Memory retains the most reliable observations across the video as scale anchors within a bounded state. Across benchmarks featuring severe occlusions and frequent out-of-sight intervals, MemHand achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and generalizes well to unseen domains. Benefiting from the synergy of both memories, it cuts W-MPJPE by 57\% on ARCTIC and 70\% on HOT3D relative to StableHand, delivering continuous and metrically accurate world-space hand poses and trajectories. We will release our code and models at the project page: https://irmvlab.github.io/memhand.github.io

llm.title_ja: MemHand：一人称視点動画からのメモリ強化型ワールド空間ハンドモーション再構成
llm.tldr_ja: オクルージョンや視野外への移動に対応するため、短期イベントメモリと長期スケールメモリを活用するメモリ強化型ハンドモーション再構成フレームワークMemHandを提案する。
llm.problem: 視野外やオクルージョン時に必要な長時間の時間的コンテキストが単一フレームのウィンドウでは不足し、ワールド空間での連続的な手形状の復元が困難である。
llm.method: 短期イベントメモリで一時的な視覚情報の欠落を補い、長期スケールメモリで動画全体にわたるメートルスケールの整合性を維持する。
llm.result: ARCTICおよびHOT3DベンチマークにおいてW-MPJPEを大幅に削減し、連続的かつ高精度なワールド空間の手のポーズと軌道を実現した。
keywords_ja: ハンドモーション再構成

2611.32858.title: What Does a Skill Vocabulary Cost? A Closed-Loop Decomposition over Demonstrated Motions
2611.32858.abstract: Discrete skill policies execute motions drawn from a finite vocabulary. In most current methods, this vocabulary is a latent codebook learned jointly with a selector and a decoder. When such a policy fails in closed loop, the failure cannot be traced to the vocabulary, to the choice of skill or to its execution. We present Movement Prototype Quantization (MPQ), which places a library of demonstrated motions after a trained policy instead of inside it. MPQ replaces each predicted action chunk with its nearest library element, corrects that element toward the prediction within a bound, and trains no parameters. Across six architectures, including a 7B vision-language-action model, the wrapped policy is statistically equivalent to the original. A reference policy executed through the library is therefore a baseline for any selector over the same library. Substituting a selector's components one at a time attributes its shortfall to them. On LIBERO-90, with selectors on three backbones, quantization costs nothing and the choice of skill costs at most 2 points under the reference's placement and correction. The selectors' own placement and correction account for nearly all of the remaining gap, up to 12 points. Offline reconstruction predicts none of these differences and misjudges library size, design and transfer across benchmark suites. Project page: https://intuitive-robots.github.io/mpq.
2611.32858.comment: 27 pages, 7 figures, 18 tables. Project page: https://intuitive-robots.github.io/mpq

llm.title_ja: スキル語彙のコストとは何か：実演動作に対する閉ループ分解
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシーの内部ではなく外部に実演動作のライブラリを配置し、パラメータ学習なしでアクションチャンクを最近傍要素に置換・補正するMovement Prototype Quantization（MPQ）を提案する。
llm.problem: 従来の内在的スキルコードブックでは、閉ループ制御の失敗原因が語彙、スキルの選択、実行のどれにあるのか特定できない。
llm.method: 訓練済みポリシーの後に実演動作のライブラリを配置し、予測されたアクションチャンクを最近傍要素に置き換えて境界内で補正する。
llm.result: 6つのアーキテクチャで元のポリシーと統計的に同等でありながら、選択コンポーネントの不足要因を正確に切り分けられることを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・アクションモデル

2611.32846.title: DOPER: Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited
2611.32846.abstract: We present DOPER, an RGB pose estimation framework that shares a visual backbone across object detection, segmentation, and keypoint prediction to recover the 6D pose of known objects through Perspective-n-Point. Starting from synthetic training, DOPER adapts to real observations using partial supervision while retaining synthetic keypoint labels. Calibrated multi-view observations provide geometric constraints for keypoint supervision. During inference, optional heatmap refinement fits a rigid pose directly to the predicted keypoint distributions, resolving ambiguous correspondences without depth input or a learned pose refiner. Starting from underspecified CAD models, DOPER progressively refines the object representation and pose estimator. Results on SPEED+ and SHIRT further demonstrate effective adaptation to illumination changes and accurate temporal pose estimation. Across the evaluated single-view and multi-view configurations, DOPER achieves state-of-the-art detection AP results on HANDAL, HOPEv2, HOT3D, and T-LESS while using only RGB and running in real time (35 Hz per object model on one GB300). These results demonstrate the effectiveness of jointly learning detection and pose keypoints, with real observations and geometric constraints.
2611.32846.comment: 35 pages including appendices. Project page: https://nvlabs.github.io/DOPER/ Code: https://github.com/NVlabs/DOPER

llm.title_ja: DOPER：深層物体姿勢推定の再検討
llm.tldr_ja: 物体検出、セグメンテーション、キーポイント予測の間で視覚バックボーンを共有し、RGB画像のみから既知物体の6D姿勢を実時間で高精度に推定するフレームワークDOPERを提案する。
llm.problem: 正確な6D姿勢推定には通常深度入力や学習済み姿勢細密化器が必要であり、照明変化や曖昧な対応関係の処理が難しい。
llm.method: 合成データ学習から始め、部分教師あり学習と較正された複数視点の幾何学的制約を用いて実環境観測に適応させる。
llm.result: HANDAL、HOPEv2、HOT3D、T-LESSにおいてRGBのみで最先端の検出精度を達成し、高速（35 Hz）に動作した。

2611.32813.title: Atomic Policy: Composing Atomic Manipulation Skills with Agentic Reasoning
2611.32813.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation requires robots to translate task intent into physical interactions as the scene changes. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer semantic and spatial reasoning, while visuomotor policies provide fine-grained control. Yet ambiguous goals and dependencies between actions make their integration challenging. We introduce Atomic Policy, a framework that composes learned manipulation skills through grounded steering and execution feedback. A VLM estimates the symbolic state and goal, and a PDDL solver constructs a skill plan. An agentic harness steers each skill through language, visual pointing, or both, and verifies its outcome to guide phase transitions and replanning. A common phase-level interface supports specialized policies and generalist action models. Experiments in simulation and on a real robot show how Atomic Policy improves task following and supports recovery in complex, long-horizon manipulation. Project page: https://aaronzkd.github.io/atomic-policy/

llm.title_ja: Atomic Policy：エージェント推論による原子操作スキルの構成
llm.tldr_ja: VLMによる記号状態推定とPDDLソルバーによる計画生成を組み合わせ、言語や視覚的指示で各スキルを誘導・検証しながら長期タスクを実行するAtomic Policyを提案する。
llm.problem: 曖昧な目標やアクション間の依存関係が存在する長期的なマニピュレーションにおいて、VLMと視覚運動ポリシーの統合が困難である。
llm.method: VLMでシンボル状態と目標を推定し、PDDLソルバーでスキル計画を立てた上で、エージェント型ハーネスが言語や視覚的指示で各スキルを誘導・検証する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験において、複雑な長期マニピュレーションにおけるタスク追従性とリカバリ能力の向上が示された。
keywords_ja: 長期マニピュレーション

2611.32803.title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation
2611.32803.abstract: Recent advances in multi-robot manipulation have shown how robots can collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. However, successful coordination does not reveal which robots are actually needed. The same task may require different teams as robot capabilities change, resources become unavailable, or objects replace robotic support. We argue that reliable multi-robot manipulation requires physical necessity reasoning: understanding what a task demands, which resources can fulfill those demands, and which are truly necessary. We introduce MRBench, a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation. It comprises eight tasks with distinct concurrency and reach constraints, each evaluated under five configurations that change the required resources while preserving the task goal. Our evaluation reveals that existing coordination agents perform well with reference teams but struggle when robot embodiments change or passive objects can replace robotic support. To address this gap, we propose MRScissors, which separates task requirements from measured physical capabilities and identifies minimal feasible teams through constrained search. Across two model backbones, MRScissors achieves 85.4% and 91.2% team-selection accuracy, outperforming the strongest baselines by 10.4 and 9.5 points, respectively. Together, these findings expose a critical gap between coordinating robots and understanding their physical necessity.

llm.title_ja: MRBench：異種マルチロボットマニピュレーションにおける物理的必要性推論のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: タスクの要求、それを満たすリソース、そして真に必要なものを理解する物理的必要性推論を評価するためのベンチマークMRBenchと、最小限の実行可能チームを特定するMRScissorsを提案する。
llm.problem: 協調に成功しても、ロボットの能力変化やリソース不足時にどのロボットが実際に必要であるかを既存のエージェントは識別できない。
llm.method: タスク要件と測定された物理的能力を分離し、制約付き探索によって最小限の実行可能なチームを特定するMRScissorsを導入する。
llm.result: MRScissorsは2つのモデルバックボーンで85.4%および91.2%のチーム選択精度を達成し、既存のベースラインを大きく上回った。

2611.32797.title: Supply Geometry, Learn Execution: Screw Attention for Zero-Shot Policy Transfer in Robot Manipulation
2611.32797.abstract: We present the Screw Attention Policy, a geometry-centric manipulation framework that supplies task geometry explicitly and learns only execution. The policy operates on object poses, relative SE(3) transforms, and joint screw axes provided by perception and robot models. The policy requires only 30K learned parameters. Trained entirely in simulation on a single robot arm, the policy generalises to new scene layouts, transfers zero-shot across robot embodiments, and deploys directly on a real robot, without adaptation or fine-tuning. It achieves 96% success on LIBERO, 85.8% under layout changes, 80.2% across five unseen robot arms, and 21 of 24 trials on a real robot. These results suggest that much of what manipulation policies learn at scale is geometric structure that can instead be supplied.

llm.title_ja: 幾何情報の提供と実行の学習：ロボットマニピュレーションにおけるゼロショット方策転移のためのスクリューアテンション
llm.tldr_ja: タスクの幾何学情報を明示的に与え、実行部分のみを学習することで、シミュレーション訓練のみで実機や未知のロボットアブディメントへゼロショット転移可能なScrew Attention Policyを提案する。
llm.problem: マニピュレーションポリシーが大スケールで学習する内容の多くは幾何学構造でありながら、暗黙的に学習されているため汎化が難しい。
llm.method: 物体ポーズ、相対SE(3)変換、関節スクリュー軸などの幾何情報を明示的に入力し、パラメータ数を絞ったポリシーで実行のみを学習する。
llm.result: LIBEROで96%の成功率を収め、レイアウト変更や5つの未知のロボットアーム、実機実験において高いゼロショット転移性能を実証した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション学習

2611.32788.title: Keypose or Dense? A Controlled Comparison of Action Representations for Stage-Structured Manipulation
2611.32788.abstract: Most imitation policies that predict chunks of future actions use the dense action representation, in which the chunk holds one control target per step. In stage-structured manipulation, where a task can be divided into stages with definable endpoints, the keypose action representation instead sets each step of the chunk to the endpoint of the stage that step belongs to, and a speed-capped servo supplies the motion. We compare the two in several simulated manipulation tasks and on a real robot, with the same chunk length and matched demonstrations, observations, policy architectures and update budgets; in simulation, each one's execution rule is selected on tuning scenes. When the simulated demonstrations are slowed, paused and rerouted, dense success falls sharply while keypose stays roughly level, across three policy architectures and with endpoints extracted from the recorded demonstrations; keypose also leads under object-size and position shift. With clean demonstrations, keypose leads only when they are scarce and is otherwise close to or behind dense across the simulated tasks, provided that the demonstrations and execution rule suit its executor; when they do not, it falls far below dense. The same dependence on the executor appeared on a real robot learning to open a drawer from human demonstrations: dense succeeded more often, and keypose improved substantially only after its executor's rotation and forward speed were adjusted to the demonstrations. These results suggest that keypose trades sensitivity to such variation in the demonstrations for sensitivity to execution that departs from them.

llm.title_ja: キーポーズか密か？段階構造化マニピュレーションにおける行動表現の制御された比較
llm.tldr_ja: 段階構造化マニピュレーションにおいて、各ステップをステージのエンドポイントに設定するキーポーズ表現と、従来の密な行動表現をシミュレーションと実機で比較し、その特性の違いを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 模倣学習において密な行動表現が広く使われているが、実演データの変化や実行時の逸脱に対する感度が十分に比較されていない。
llm.method: 同じチャンク長、実演データ、観測、ポリシーアーキテクチャを用いて、密な行動表現とキーポーズ表現の性能を比較検証する。
llm.result: キーポーズ表現は実演データの変動に対する頑健性を持つ一方で、実行時の逸脱に対して敏感であり、デモの性質や実行器の調整に強く依存することが示された。

2611.32786.title: Simulator-as-Proxy World Model for Robot Manipulation
2611.32786.abstract: Video world models for robots are increasingly conditioned on a simulated or rendered proxy of the scene, on the assumption that the video will show what the proxy shows. Testing this assumption requires a proxy whose state is explicit and can be perturbed. We present SimPWM (Simulator-as-Proxy World Model): given a calibrated camera, it represents, from the first frame alone, the robot by its 3D model and the objects the gripper may touch as 3D points; a rule-based simulator with no trained parameters moves them under the actions, and a video model renders the result. SimPWM returns the realistic video together with the simulated state. We then freeze the simulated objects while the arm moves as recorded and check whether the video still shows the object lifted. On DROID episodes from unseen setups, the answer differs for the arm and for the objects. With each of three base video models, the arm follows the proxy (robot IoU 0.75-0.78, against at most 0.69 for end-to-end models); rendering the robot alone already gives this. What the simulated objects add is the object state: against a robot-only proxy, they cut missed pick-ups from 54% to 38%, and the video follows them only with some base models: on rigid objects, freezing them lowers the lift rate of MiniMax-H3, fine-tuned on episodes whose simulation agrees with the real video, from 42% to 10%, but that of LTX-2.3, trained on the same episodes, only from 57% to 49%, as if it inferred the grasp from the arm motion; more than half of the remaining lifts of MiniMax-H3 are of cloth and rope, which the simulator carries rigidly. With any base model, the simulated state records what the simulation did; under perturbed actions, a video that disagrees with it reveals that the video ignores the simulated state.
2611.32786.comment: 27 pages. Project page: https://sim-pwm.pages.dev Code: https://github.com/TingtingLiao/SimPWM

llm.title_ja: ロボットマニピュレーションのためのシミュレータプロキシ型世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 較正されたカメラとパラメータのないルールベースシミュレータを用いて、ロボットの3Dモデルと物体の3D点群から現実的な動画とシミュレート状態を出力するSimPWMを提案する。
llm.problem: ビデオ世界モデルがシミュレートされたプロキシのシーンに条件付けられている場合、動画がプロキシの状態を正しく反映しているか検証する必要がある。
llm.method: 最初フレームのみからロボットを3Dモデルで、接触対象の物体を3D点群で表現し、ルールベースシミュレータで動作させてビデオモデルでレンダリングする。
llm.result: SimPWMを用いることで、ロボットアームの追従精度が向上し、シミュレートされた物体状態によって把持失敗や把持率の評価が改善されることが示された。

2611.32780.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
2611.32780.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are transforming recommender systems into content-aware decision systems. In these systems, multimodal compression and cross-modal fusion are often viewed as robustness-enhancing mechanisms against content manipulation, as compression can filter noisy signals and cross-modal consensus can suppress inconsistent anomalies. We challenge this assumption by showing that the same process can expose a compression-to-consensus (C2C) bias in ranking decisions. Signals that remain salient after compression and receive consistent support across modalities can gain disproportionate influence in candidate comparison, offering an exploitable direction for content manipulation. In this paper, we introduce C3H, a novel inference-time attack that exploits this vulnerability. Rather than relying on noisy perturbations or training-time poisoning, C3H promotes a target item by tailoring its multimodal content to align with the decision criteria implicitly expressed by the recommender. Extensive experiments demonstrate that C3H substantially increases target-item exposure while maintaining overall recommendation utility. Code is available at https://github.com/GuoweiGuan666/C3H.

llm.title_ja: C3H：マルチモーダルLLM推薦システムにおける圧縮から合意への基準ハイジャック
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダルLLMベースの推薦システムにおいて、圧縮とマルチモーダル合意のプロセスがランク付けのバイアスを生む脆弱性を突く推論時攻撃手法C3Hを提案する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダルの圧縮やクロスモーダル合意はコンテンツ操作に対する頑健性向上とみなされているが、ランク付け決定において圧縮から合意へのバイアス（C2C）を露呈させる。
llm.method: 推薦システムが暗黙的に表現する決定基準に一致するようにターゲット項目のマルチモーダルコンテンツを調整する推論時攻撃を行う。
llm.result: C3Hにより、全体の推薦ユーティリティを維持しながらターゲット項目の露出度を大幅に増加させられることが示された。

2611.32765.title: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See?
2611.32765.abstract: In Minecraft, a common testbed for embodied agents, semantic tools such as mineBlock pick targets from the simulator's loaded world state without a visibility test, so a buried ore the agent has never seen is one call away, and scores cannot show whether the agent searched. We formalize the missing requirement as evidence closure: every decision of an agent system, including those inside its tools, may depend on the world only through facts for which the agent holds evidence. EviCraft is a runtime and benchmark that enforces closure below the agent and makes the admission rule an experimental variable: a perception-grounded regime (G) admits only what is in line of sight or returned by the agent's own actions, and a loaded-state regime (L) reproduces standard tool stacks, with agents, tools, and worlds held fixed. On Survival, the regime effect exceeds the strongest agent's lead: under G, three mid-sized agents reach the diamond in 32%-40% of runs, against 76%-94% under L, and the strongest agent under G scores below each of them under L. In two models, removing only the line-of-sight test closes 93%-96% of the score gap, and loading state only inside tools recovers 70%-98%, so safeguards on observations and queries leave most of the leak open. In open-ended acquisition, the gain from L concentrates in items that depend on buried resources or mobs. Code and benchmark are available at https://github.com/AllenReder/EviCraft

llm.title_ja: EviCraft：マインクラフトのエージェントは自分に見えないものを見つけられるか？
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントの意思決定が保持している証拠に基づいた事実のみに依存すべきという「エビデンス閉鎖性」を定式化し、それを検証するためのランタイムおよびベンチマークEviCraftを提案する。
llm.problem: マインクラフト等の環境において、セマンティックツールがシミュレータの世界状態から視認性テストなしにターゲットを取得するため、エージェントが実際に探索したかを評価できない。
llm.method: エージェントの下で閉鎖性を強制するランタイムを構築し、視線内や自身のアクションによる結果のみを許可する知覚グラウンド環境などを実験変数として導入する。
llm.result: 視線テストの有無がスコアの大部分を左右し、標準的なツールスタックでは見えない埋蔵資源への依存が大きいことが示された。

2611.32760.title: Risk-Informed Path Planning: Collision and Grounding Avoidance Application for Autonomous Surface Vessels
2611.32760.abstract: Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) must demonstrate safety before and during operations, necessitating online risk assessment to guide decision-making at sea. This paper presents a risk-informed Rapidly Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) path planner that integrates a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) as an online risk model. The BBN evaluates the probability and severity distribution of hazardous events, which are aggregated into a bounded scalar risk index. During the search, this risk index is evaluated at sample points along candidate edges. The planner optimizes a composite cost function comprising path distance, heading change penalties, and accumulated risk, subject to a hard constraint enforcing a risk acceptance limit. Each search tree vertex stores the BBN posterior at its state, enabling the tree to function as an explainable risk map for individual hazards. We define design requirements for the BBN to serve as the risk model in this context and introduce a runtime model that translates replanning deadlines into strict limits on single risk calculation times. The planner is demonstrated in a simulated harbor entry scenario involving collision and grounding hazards. Measured run times validate that the planner operates within the computational bounds predicted by the runtime model for a single replanning cycle.

llm.title_ja: リスクを考慮した経路計画：自律水上船舶のための衝突および座礁回避アプリケーション
llm.tldr_ja: ベイズ信念ネットワーク（BBN）をオンラインリスクモデルとして統合し、複合コスト関数とハード制約に基づいて経路を最適化するリスク考慮型RRT*パスプランナーを提案する。
llm.problem: 海上の自律水上船舶（MASS）は運航前および運航中の安全性を実証する必要があり、意思決定を導くためのオンラインリスク評価が不可欠である。
llm.method: 探索木のサンプル点でBBNによる確率および深刻度分布を評価し、パス距離やヘディング変化ペナルティ等と合わせた複合コスト関数を最適化する。
llm.result: シミュレートされた港湾進入シナリオにおいて、提案するプランナーが計算上の制限時間内で動作することが検証された。

2611.32727.title: Support2Sim: Visually Faithful Real2Sim with Stable Object Supports
2611.32727.abstract: Reconstructing a scene for physics simulation requires recovering its spatial layout and the support relationships that govern its behavior. We present Support2Sim, a Real2Sim system that reconstructs simulation-ready scenes from a single RGB image. Our design objective is to maximize source fidelity, support realization, and stability within a practical time budget for scene generation. Support2Sim infers a support graph, which a contact-guided pose initializer uses to propose poses for objects with multiple supports. The initializer generates and ranks candidates by geometric fit and source-image agreement. A coarse-to-fine refiner allocates a fixed search budget across supported objects and evaluates pose updates with physics rollouts. After an accepted update, it searches from the new pose at a finer translation and rotation scale. We benchmark our method on 50 scenes spanning four datasets. Compared with the strongest baseline, Support2Sim improves source-mask IoU after 10 seconds by 21.4 pp, realizes 87.1% versus 73.2% of intended supports, and reduces mean object drift from 79.6 to 45.3 mm. See our project page at https://support2sim.github.io for more details.

llm.title_ja: Support2Sim：安定した物体支持関係に基づく視覚的に忠実なReal2Sim
llm.tldr_ja: 単一のRGB画像からシミュレーションに適したシーンを再構成するため、支持グラフと物理演算ロールアウトを用いて物体のポーズを初期化・洗練するSupport2Simを提案する。
llm.problem: 物理シミュレーション用のシーン再構成では、空間レイアウトと、その動作を支配する支持関係を正しく復元する必要がある。
llm.method: 支持グラフを推論し、接触ガイド付きポーズ初期化器で複数支持を持つ物体のポーズ候補を提案・ランク付けし、粗いところから細かい段階へ物理演算で評価・洗練する。
llm.result: 4つのデータセットにわたる50のシーンにおいて、ソースマスクのIoUを大幅に改善し、意図された支持関係の実現と物体ドリフトの低減を達成した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.32722.title: AG-WAM: Attention-Guided World Action Model for Accurate and Efficient Robot Manipulation
2611.32722.abstract: Recently developed World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict future observations and robot actions, providing predictive context for control. However, existing WAMs typically learn implicit attention allocation with limited explicit action-relevant attention guidance, leading to limited performance. To unleash strong capabilities of WAMs, we introduce explicit attention guidance as a unifying principle and propose our Attention-Guided WAM (AG-WAM), an end-to-end framework with three plug-and-play attention guidance modules that directly reformulate internal attention paradigm in WAMs: the Content-Adaptive Predictive Attention module, the Guidance-Point Visual Attention module, and the State-Conditioned Text Attention module. Without any external plugin module adopted, our end-to-end framework with the unifying principle of explicit attention guidance boosts the accuracy and efficiency of WAMs. Without using any private embodied training data, our AG-WAM establishes new state-of-the-art performance on multiple public robotic manipulation benchmarks including LIBERO-X, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin-2.0, significantly outperforming other methods, even those using massive private embodied training data by a notable margin, meanwhile notably improving training and inference efficiency.

llm.title_ja: AG-WAM：正確かつ効率的なロボットマニピュレーションのためのアテンション誘導型世界行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 内部のアテンションパラダイムを直接再構築する3つのプラグイン可能なアテンション誘導モジュールを導入し、WAMの精度と効率を向上させるAttention-Guided WAM（AG-WAM）を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のワールド行動モデル（WAMs）は暗黙的なアテンション割り振りに依存しており、行動に関連する明示的なアテンション誘導が不足しているため性能が制限されている。
llm.method: コンテンツ適応型予測アテンション、誘導ポイント視覚アテンション、状態条件付きテキストアテンションの3つのプラグインモジュールをエンドツーエンドフレームワークに統合する。
llm.result: LIBERO-XやRoboTwin-2.0などの複数の公開マニピュレーションベンチマークで新たな最先端性能を達成し、学習および推論効率を向上させた。

2611.32718.title: Seeing to Drive on a Single Board: Attention-Free Depth for Onboard Robot Navigation
2611.32718.abstract: A small ground robot can carry one camera and a few watts of compute, but the depth foundation models that could turn that camera into a range sensor are vision transformers sized for GPUs. We bring one to a Raspberry Pi 5 with the Hailo-8L, an accelerator that runs every layer in integer arithmetic, attention included. Quantised for it, Depth Anything V2 loses large parts of the scene, and we measure why: at 449 tokens, 91% of softmax weights fall below one int8 step while carrying 17-33% of the attention mass. Our answer is to distil, not quantise. An attention-free ResNet-34 U-Net student of Depth Anything V2-Large (24.5M parameters) runs at 27.1 FPS on the chip, its int8 output matches its float twin (Pearson 0.99993), and on held-out scenes of its simulated yard it is the most accurate depth network on the chip (AbsRel 0.269 against 0.354-0.530). On 1,000 stereo-verified points of a real outdoor drive it is not resolvably different from the vendor's Depth Anything V2-Small build, while running faster (27.1 vs 21.6 FPS). Ranging obstacles by where they meet the floor needs only the camera height, so mapping, hybrid-A* planning and SLAM run on the Pi's own CPU. In real-time hardware-in-the-loop tests in a Gaussian-splat reconstruction of a real yard, the stack reaches the goal without contact in 7.9$\pm$1.1 of 10 scenes, against 9.2$\pm$0.4 with exact obstacles, and in 7.7$\pm$0.7 on its own pose with simulated wheel odometry (ten seeds each; 8.2$\pm$0.4 with the real Pi and Hailo-8L in the loop, five seeds). The source code, pre-trained models and data are available at https://github.com/itaim18/DANIEL.
2611.32718.comment: 13 pages, 14 figures, 5 tables. Code, models and data: https://github.com/itaim18/DANIEL

llm.title_ja: シングルボードでのビジョン駆動型走行：車載ロボットナビゲーションのためのアテンションフリー深度推定
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模な深度基盤モデルをRaspberry Pi 5とHailo-8Lアクセラレータ上で効率的に動作させるため、アテンションフリーのResNet-34 U-Net学生モデルによる蒸留手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 小型地上ロボットに搭載可能な低電力コンピュート環境では、高度な深度基盤モデル（Vision Transformer）をそのまま実行することが困難である。
llm.method: Depth Anything V2-Largeの知識を、int8整数演算アクセラレータ上で高速動作するアテンションフリーのResNet-34 U-Netに蒸留して実装する。
llm.result: 実機の検証済みポイントおよびシミュレート環境において、高い深度精度と高速なフレームレート（27.1 FPS）を両立し、安定した障害物回避ナビゲーションを実現した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2611.32715.title: Semidefinite Programming for Cold-Start GNSS Doppler-Based Alignment: A Comparison with Nonlinear Least Squares
2611.32715.abstract: Initial attitude alignment between local navigation frames and the Earth-centered Earth-fixed (ECEF) frame is a critical prerequisite for multi-sensor integrated navigation, such as Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)/inertial/odometry fusion, before global and local measurements can be jointly processed. While GNSS Doppler-based alignment eliminates the need for carrier-phase ambiguity resolution or multi-antenna hardware, solving this non-convex problem via local nonlinear least squares (NLS) suffers from local minima, whereas direct semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxation incurs high latency and omits local covariance outputs. This study systematically compares NLS and SDP on a unified maximum-likelihood Doppler objective across Monte Carlo simulations and three real-world driving datasets. We demonstrate that attaching a modular dual SDP certifier to a standard manifold NLS solver recovers the global accuracy of direct SDP within 0.001 degrees, reduces real-world 95th-percentile yaw errors from over 86 degrees down to 2.88 degrees to 4.70 degrees, and cuts median solve times by up to an order of magnitude while preserving native Jacobian covariances. We conclude that candidate-driven certification bridges local estimation and global optimization due to two structural advantages: (1) our theoretical comparison reveals that SDP relaxation enlarges the feasible region while preserving the lifted cost, allowing Lagrangian duality to verify whether a fixed NLS candidate attains the global lower bound without invoking a full SDP solver, and (2) the candidate-driven architecture acts as a non-intrusive module that plugs directly into existing navigation pipelines without replacing the local estimator, preserving native tangent-space covariance outputs and low typical latency.

llm.title_ja: コールドスタートGNSSドップラーベース整定のための半正定値プログラミング：非線形最小二乗法との比較
llm.tldr_ja: モジュラー型デュアルSDP証明器を標準的なマニフォールドNLSソルバーに組み合わせることで、計算遅延を抑えつつ大域的な精度を回復する半正定値プログラミング手法を提案する。
llm.problem: GNSSドップラーベースの初期姿勢整定において、局所的非線形最小二乗法（NLS）は局所的最小値に陥りやすく、直接的な半正定値プログラミング（SDP）緩和は高レイテンシーを伴う。
llm.method: 共通の最尤ドップラー目的関数のもとでNLSとSDPを比較し、NLS候補が下限に達しているかを検証するデュアルSDP証明器をアタッチする。
llm.result: 実世界の駆動データにおいて、大域的精度を回復しつつ、95パーセンタイルの方位誤差を大幅に削減し、中央値の解決時間を大幅に短縮した。
keywords_ja: 半正定値プログラミング

2611.32705.title: Knocked Off Course: Tracing Uncommanded Motion from Perception to Action in Embodied VLAs
2611.32705.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable simultaneous processing of egocentric video and textual target descriptions to produce action commands for embodied tracking platforms. However, these platforms rarely move exactly as commanded, in part due to unexpected environmental disturbances such as wind, unleveled terrain, and road bumps. Here we study how such models handle uncommanded egomotion. First, we explore performance across diverse disturbances by benchmarking three tracking VLAs on three datasets. We find that models differ in which environmental disturbances hurt them most, but all are sensitive to sudden target loss. Tracing egomotion from pixels to emitted actions, we identify two gaps. In representation, motion is reliably recovered through explicit relations between frames, but aggressive compression of past frames weakens small-motion readouts. In action, large rotations do reach the decision state, yet the decoded direction carries only a few percent of a mirrored rotation's effect on the turn. Targeting both gaps, we fine-tune one model, Uni-NaVid, on data amounting to just 1.7% of its original training set in a ladder of analysis-motivated variants. These gain 5-22 points after target-loss without degrading clean success; after a smooth loss, the best one improves success by 72% (relative), recovering 76% of its gap to clean. We also show that targeted fine-tuning improves recovery partly via a text-mediated action dependency, without new architecture, large-scale data collection or training from scratch.

llm.title_ja: コースアウト：身体性VLAにおける知覚から行動への意図しない動きの追跡
llm.tldr_ja: 風や不整地などの環境外乱に対する身体性VLAモデルの脆弱性をピクセルから行動まで追跡し、ターゲット見失い後のリカバリ性能を改善する微調整手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 身体性トラッキングプラットフォームで利用されるVLAモデルは、環境外乱によって正確にコマンド通りに移動できず、予期せぬターゲット見失いに敏感である。
llm.method: ピクセルから出力行動までエゴモーションを追跡し、表現ギャップと行動ギャップを特定した上で、Uni-NaVidモデルをわずかなデータでターゲット指向に微調整する。
llm.result: ターゲット見失い後の成功率が大幅に向上し、クリーンな成功率を落とすことなく外乱からのリカバリ性能が改善された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・アクションモデル

2611.32686.title: CAPTA: Identifying LLMs Behind AI Agents
2611.32686.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents access remote services through tools to complete user tasks, often via API calls. In this setting, a remote service may want to identify the backend LLM of an agent to launch model-specific attacks, including prompt injection or selective delivery of manipulated content. However, the service cannot directly query the backend model and must instead collect observable responses through its interactions with the agent, making identification challenging. In this paper, we present Completely Automated Preference Test to tell LLMs Apart (CAPTA), a model identification approach inspired by CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart), which distinguishes humans from automated programs. CAPTA presents multiple-choice questions as verification challenges, using differences in models' selection preferences to identify the backend LLM. It selects questions based on cross-model option-generation diversity and uses LLM-guided search to optimize their option sets. Our evaluation shows that CAPTA achieves 99.0% mean identification accuracy with only 10 questions across 25 LLMs from 10 model families. We further evaluate CAPTA with four widely used agents and seven representative LLMs, achieving 99.7% mean identification accuracy across all 28 agent-LLM combinations with 30 submitted answers.

llm.title_ja: CAPTA：AIエージェントの背後にあるLLMの特定
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントとの対話から得られる選択の好みの違いを利用して、バックエンドのLLMを高精度に特定する完全自動化選好テスト（CAPTA）を提案する。
llm.problem: リモートサービスのプロバイダは、モデル固有の攻撃や操作を行うためにエージェントのバックエンドLLMを知りたいが、直接クエリを投げることはできない。
llm.method: モデルの選択選好の多様性に基づく多肢選択式の検証課題を作成し、LLMガイド付き探索を用いてオプションセットを最適化する。
llm.result: 25のLLMモデルおよび4つのエージェントと7つのLLMの組み合わせにおいて、少数の質問で99%以上の平均特定精度を達成した。

2611.32683.title: DeCoNav-Act: Benchmarking Collective Physical Capability in Multi-Robot Mobile Manipulation
2611.32683.abstract: Robot teams can split workloads or combine complementary bodies, but only if each robot leaves the shared world in a state its teammate can use. Existing multi-robot benchmarks emphasize task allocation and skill sequencing, rarely testing whether the resulting physical states are usable. To evaluate collective physical capability, we introduce DeCoNav-Act, a benchmark for language-guided multi-robot mobile manipulation in a shared physics simulation. Its 350 homogeneous and 150 heterogeneous tasks, each verified by joint reference execution, span two coordination mechanisms: parallel workloads in shared space and physical dependencies in which one robot establishes a condition for a teammate to use. Beyond team success, DeCoNav-Act measures path efficiency and handoff coverage and success, and adds a diagnostic from verified pre-handoff states. Evaluating sensor-grounded adaptations of ASPIRE and RAX and our agent CoMoMa, we find that with GPT-5.6-luna no method completes a task, at most 8.8% of dependencies are reached, and even from pre-handoff states no handoff is completed; with GPT-6.1-sol, CoMoMa establishes the condition in 26.5% of trials, but only 4.1% succeed.

llm.title_ja: DeCoNav-Act：マルチロボットモバイルマニピュレーションにおける集合的物理能力のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 共有空間での並列作業と、一方が他方のための条件を整える物理的依存関係という2つの協調メカニズムを通じて集合的物理能力を評価するベンチマークDeCoNav-Actを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のマルチロボットベンチマークはタスク割当やスキル順序付けに重点を置いており、その結果生じる物理的状態が相棒にとって使用可能かどうかをほとんどテストしていない。
llm.method: 同種および異種のタスクを含み、チームの成功だけでなく経路効率、ハンドオフの成功率、事前ハンドオフ状態からの診断を行うシミュレーション環境を構築する。
llm.result: 最先端のエージェントやモデルを用いても、複雑な物理的依存関係やハンドオフを完遂することは非常に困難であることを実験で明らかにした。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション
物理シミュレーション

2611.32665.title: DiffGR00T: Execution-Aware Differentiable Training for Humanoid Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.32665.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have achieved strong results in arm-centric manipulation, yet humanoid whole-body control (WBC) requires dynamic balance and tightly coupled full-body coordination. Existing hierarchical humanoid VLAs typically decouple motion generation from physical execution, leaving tracking and balance errors unable to directly optimize the VLA generator. We propose DiffGR00T, an end-to-end differentiable training framework that couples GR00T N1.7 with SONIC, a pretrained whole-body behavior foundation model. To enable execution-aware differentiable training, we replace the non-differentiable simulator with a learned, action-conditioned world model, allowing multi-step body-execution losses to backpropagate through the frozen whole-body controller and the flow-matching sampler directly into the VLA action head. On four HumanoidArena simulation tasks, DiffGR00T improves average task success by 12.5 percentage points over the supervised base VLA (59.2% to 71.7%), demonstrating that execution-aware gradients effectively align high-level motion generation with closed-loop whole-body dynamics.
2611.32665.comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. Conference preprint. Corresponding author: Hesheng Wang

llm.title_ja: DiffGR00T：ヒューマノイド全身ビジョン・言語・アクションモデルのための実行認識型微分可能訓練
llm.tldr_ja: 非微分可能なシミュレータを学習済みのアクション条件付き世界モデルに置き換えることで、マルチステップの身体実行損失をVLAアクションヘッドに逆伝播させるDiffGR00Tを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の階層型ヒューマノイドVLAは動作生成と物理実行を切り離しているため、追跡誤差やバランス誤差をVLA生成器に直接最適化させることができない。
llm.method: 事前学習済みの全身行動基盤モデルと学習済み世界モデルを組み合わせ、フローマッチングサンプラーを通して実行認識型の勾配をVLAに逆伝播させる。
llm.result: 4つのHumanoidArenaシミュレーションタスクにおいて、教師ありベースVLAと比較して平均タスク成功率を12.5ポイント向上させた。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
ビジョン・言語・アクションモデル
微分可能シミュレーション

2611.32654.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
2611.32654.abstract: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning.
