Meanwhile, most policy improvement methods learn dynamics and values in separate models, increasing training overhead and limiting representation sharing between these complementary objectives. We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretraining stage. Our key insight is that visual prediction encourages control-relevant features, while value supervision promotes task-relevant representations; together, they shape a representation suited to policy learning. Built on an image-editing backbone, DexWAC predicts, for each action chunk, the visual latent and proprioception at its endpoint together with its reward and continuation, so the world model alone efficiently yields complete imagined transitions without generating intermediate video frames. After adapting the world model and critic on real rollouts, we improve the pretrained actor through either PPO on imagined rollouts or critic-guided best-of-$N$ selection. DexWAC surpasses the large-scale pretrained VLA and WAM baselines in simulation and achieves 75% average success on two real-world tasks, compared with 45% for $π_{0.5}$. Its world model is more accurate and faster than video-based baselines, and ablations confirm that learning dynamics and value together improves the policy.

llm.title_ja: DexWAC: 器用なロボットマニピュレーションのための統合された世界・アクター・クリティックモデル
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚予測と価値の監督を単一のロボット事前学習段階で統合したモデル「DexWAC」を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実世界タスクで大規模事前学習済みVLAやWAMベースラインを凌駕する性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 既存のポリシー改善手法はダイナミクスと価値を別々のモデルで学習するため、トレーニングのオーバーヘッドが増加し表現の共有が制限されること。
llm.method: アクター、行動条件付き世界モデル、およびブートストラップされたクリティックを単一のプレトレーニング段階で同時に学習する統合モデル「DexWAC」の導入。
llm.result: シミュレーションで大規模事前学習済みVLAおよびWAMベースラインを上回り、実世界の2つのタスクで75%の平均成功率を達成（π0.5は45%）。

2611.32650.title: LaWanle: Why Can't Leading Driving Models Make a Simple Turn?
2611.32650.abstract: We were surprised to find that leading end-to-end driving models across major paradigms, despite scoring close to human drivers on NAVSIM, cannot reliably make a simple 90-degree turn in photorealistic closed-loop simulators. To investigate why, we build LaWanle, a benchmark of turns drawn from three such simulators. Driving each turn from several starts, we find that the same model passes it from one start and fails it from another, and that the two drives look alike until they enter the junction. Rotating the car by a few degrees at the junction entry can fail a turn it otherwise passes. Conversely, a slight heading correction to the plans can rescue about half of the failed turns we tested. Such errors arise when a model drives by itself, so we post-train an open-source lane-keeping model with closed-loop DAgger on its lateral path. Training 5% of its parameters is enough to raise its turn pass rate from 19% to 76%. The gain transfers to the two other benchmarks, where the policy also scores among the leading models. Further fine-tuning on recovery data repairs the deviations it is trained on but, against a control trained equally long, improves turns on none of the three benchmarks, and every variant stays far below a human driver.

llm.title_ja: LaWanle: なぜ主要な自動運転モデルは簡単な曲がり角を曲がれないのか？
llm.tldr_ja: 主要なエンドツーエンド自動運転モデルがフォトリアルなシミュレータで単純な90度ターンを確実に行えない原因を調査し、クローズドールDaggerによる後学習でターン成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 主要なエンドツーエンド自動運転モデルが、NAVSIMで人間並みのスコアを出しながらも、フォトリアルなクローズドール・シミュレータで単純な90度ターンを確実に実行できないこと。
llm.method: 3つのシミュレータから抽出したターンのベンチマーク「LaWanle」を構築し、オープンソースの車線維持モデルに対して側方経路でクローズドールDAggerによる後学習を実施する。
llm.result: パラメータの5%をトレーニングするだけで、ターンの成功率が19%から76%に向上し、他の2つのベンチマークにも利得が転移した。
llm.limitation: 回復データでの追加微調整は訓練された偏りを修正するが、同期間訓練されたコントロールと比較して3つのベンチマークすべてでターンを改善せず、どのバリアントも人間の運転手には遠く及ばない。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習

2611.32649.title: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
2611.32649.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) lets agents acquire new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time. The same frontier agents now operate both computers and robots, yet their ICL remains insufficiently assessed: existing benchmarks are largely offline, rely on text or static images, and risk training-data contamination, while robot evaluations are limited to method-level ablations. We present ICLWorld, an online benchmark that evaluates the ICL of agents from digital to physical worlds, covering computer use and robot use, together with UIverse, a unified harness that turns every environment into a user interface. We build 30 environments, record 630 demonstration videos (10+ hours), and design 160 tasks with customized, often counter-intuitive rules that cannot be satisfied without learning from the context. Each task comes with three rule versions, given as text or video, and we test generalization at three levels, from replaying the demonstration to new instances and unseen environments. Across six frontier models, the strongest agents, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, succeed on 82% and 76% of computer-use runs but only 27% and 26% of robot-use runs, and a no-rule control reduces success to at most 8%. GPT-6 Astra succeeds under all three rule versions on only 38% of computer-use tasks, half its rate under a single rule, and answers 98% of robot rule questions correctly yet completes only 20% of these tasks. Frontier agents learn rules comparably well from video and from text and transfer them across environments, whereas weaker agents rely on text and lose most of their video-based success once the demonstrated situation is resampled. These findings reveal substantial gaps between the digital and the physical world and between identifying a rule and acting on it.
2611.32649.comment: Project page: https://iclworld.github.io Code: https://github.com/ICLWorld/ICLWorld Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aoraku/ICLWorld

llm.title_ja: ICLWorld: デジタル世界から物理世界におけるエージェントのコンテキスト内学習のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: デジタル世界から物理世界にわたるエージェントのコンテキスト内学習（ICL）を評価するオンラインベンチマーク「ICLWorld」を提案し、最先端モデルにおけるデジタル・物理間の大きな性能ギャップを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存のコンテキスト内学習（ICL）ベンチマークは主にオフラインで、テキストや静止画像に依存し訓練データの汚染リスクがあり、ロボット評価は手法レベルのアブレーションに限定されていること。
llm.method: コンピュータ操作とロボット操作をカバーし、あらゆる環境をUIに変換する統合ハーネス「UIverse」を備えたオンラインベンチマーク「ICLWorld」を構築し、30環境・160タスクを設計した。
llm.result: 最強のエージェントであるClaude Opus 5.5とGPT-6 Astraはコンピュータ操作で76〜82%成功した一方、ロボット操作では26〜27%にとどまり、デジタル世界と物理世界の間に大きなギャップがあることが判明した。

2611.32642.title: BARE: Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion for Humanoid Robots
2611.32642.abstract: Dynamic obstacle avoidance is essential for safely deploying humanoid robots in real-world environments, where rapidly approaching objects require immediate evasive responses. Recent advances in reflexive evasion have focused primarily on quadrupeds, which typically rely on large-scale whole-body maneuvers. In contrast, humanoids can exploit their rich body articulation to evade through small, localized body adjustments. By moving threatened body regions without repositioning the entire body, these responses may require less execution time and less surrounding free space. However, local adjustments can alter mass distribution or support conditions, making it challenging to achieve rapid evasion while maintaining whole-body stability. To this end, we propose BARE (Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion), a humanoid reflexive evasion framework guided by human motion priors that enables rapid local evasion while maintaining whole-body stability. A risk-guided motion adapter is designed to select reference motions from a retargeted human evasive motion library based on the threatened body region and to adjust their temporal phases based on collision urgency, allowing the robot to reach evasive postures before potential contact. Conditioned on the adapted reference and link-level collision risk, a reflexive evasion policy learns through reinforcement learning to coordinate local body adjustments with whole-body stabilization. We validate BARE in simulation and real-world experiments, demonstrating its ability to perform targeted local evasion while maintaining whole-body stability.

llm.title_ja: BARE: ヒューマノイドロボットのための身体認識型反射回避
llm.tldr_ja: 人間運動事前分布に導かれたヒューマノイドの反射的回避フレームワーク「BARE」を提案し、全身の安定性を維持しながら迅速な局所回避を実現した。
llm.problem: 急速に接近する物体に対する動的障害物回避において、ヒューマノイドの局所的な身体調整は質量分布や支持条件を変化させ、全身の安定性を保ちながら迅速な回避を行うことが困難であること。
llm.method: リスク誘導型モーションアダプターを用いて人間の回避モーションライブラリから参照動作を選択し、リンクレベルの衝突リスクを条件付けられた強化学習により局所的調整と全身安定化を協調させるフレームワーク「BARE」の提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界実験において、全身の安定性を維持しながら標的を絞った局所回避を実行できる能力を実証した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.32639.title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
2611.32639.abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables vision-language-action policies to improve through environmental interaction. However, in long-horizon manipulation, sparse success/failure feedback provides little information about where policies encounter bottlenecks. Moreover, repeated full-task rollouts also leave these bottlenecks weakly analyzed and insufficiently practiced. To this end, we introduce ReFocus, a progress-guided multi-round RL framework that alternates between Global and Local RL to identify task-specific bottlenecks and allocate additional practice to them. Specifically, during Global RL, we decompose each task into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of subtasks. Then a DAG-based Progress Reward is leveraged for both policy training and bottleneck diagnosis. Based on the identified bottlenecks, ReFocus selects Adaptive Practice Windows, defining task segments from an entry stage to a target stage. It allocates additional interaction to these segments during Local RL while updating the entire policy. After that, it evaluates the policy to perform the full task for the next round of RL, forming an iteration between Global and Local RL. Experiments on LIBERO-Long and RoboCasa365 show that ReFocus achieves success rates of 97.8% and 51.3%, respectively, compared with 90.6% and 39.3% for the $π_{0.5}$ baseline. Furthermore, we evaluate a real-world adaptation on three long-horizon tasks. On BreadBaker, ReFocus achieves 95% success, compared with 30% for the $π_{0.5}$. Project page: https://refocus-robotics.github.io.
2611.32639.hf_summary_en: ReFocus alternates global and local reinforcement learning with DAG-based progress rewards and adaptive practice windows to target task bottlenecks, improving long-horizon manipulation success over a π0.5 baseline.

llm.title_ja: ReFocus: 長期的なロボットマニピュレーション強化学習のための進捗誘導型適応的練習
llm.tldr_ja: グローバル強化学習とローカル強化学習を交互に行いタスクのボトルネックを特定・集中的に練習するフレームワーク「ReFocus」を提案し、長期マニピュレーションの成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 長期的なマニピュレーションにおいて、スパースな成功・失敗フィードバックではポリシーがどこでボトルネックに直面しているかの情報がほとんど得られず、全体タスクの繰り返しでは練習が不十分になること。
llm.method: タスクをサブタスクの有向非巡回グラフ（DAG）に分解し、DAGベースの進捗報酬を用いてグローバルRLとローカルRLを交互に実行、適応的練習ウィンドウを割り当てるフレームワーク「ReFocus」の導入。
llm.result: LIBERO-LongとRoboCasa365でそれぞれ97.8%と51.3%の成功率を達成し、BreadBakerの実世界タスクでは95%の成功率を記録した。

2611.32622.title: RoboRecast: Intent-Preserving Demonstration Augmentation via Diagnosis-Driven Optimization
2611.32622.abstract: Collecting diverse real-world manipulation demonstrations is costly, motivating the use of simulation to augment existing demonstrations for robot policy learning. When objects, layouts, or robots change, transferring motions from a source demonstration can produce behavior that is semantically implausible or physically infeasible in the new setting. We introduce RoboRecast, an agentic optimization framework that preserves the interactions required by the source task while jointly optimizing the simulated scene and robot motion to make those interactions executable in the target setting. When an interaction fails, the agent uses simulation feedback to diagnose the cause, revise the relevant scene or motion parameters, and test whether the revision resolves the failure. This flexibility allows RoboRecast to generate synthetic data from both human and robot demonstrations and to adapt them to new layouts, objects, and robot embodiments. When target demonstrations are available, adding RoboRecast data improves policy success on both real-world single-arm and simulated bimanual tasks. Even without demonstrations in the target configuration, RoboRecast adapts source demonstrations to support policy learning with new objects or robot embodiments.
2611.32622.comment: 18 pages, including supplementary material. Corresponding author: Ruizhen Hu

llm.title_ja: RoboRecast: 診断駆動型最適化による意図保持デモンストレーション拡張
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーションフィードバックを用いてシーンとロボットの動きを共同最適化し、ソースデモンストレーションを新しい環境に適応させるエージェント型最適化フレームワーク「RoboRecast」を提案した。
llm.problem: 物体、レイアウト、ロボットが変化した際に、ソースデモンストレーションからの動作の移行が新しい環境で意味的に不自然であったり物理的に実行不可能になったりすること。
llm.method: シミュレーションフィードバックを使用して失敗の原因を診断し、シーンや動作のパラメータを修正・テストするエージェント型最適化フレームワーク「RoboRecast」の導入。
llm.result: RoboRecastデータを追加することで、実世界の単腕タスクとシミュレーションの双腕タスクの両方でポリシーの成功率が向上した。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーション拡張

2611.32584.title: An XR-Based System for Enhanced Spatial Awareness in Mobile Robot Teleoperation
2611.32584.abstract: Teleoperation of mobile robots represents a critical capability for operations in hazardous environments, yet maintaining adequate situational awareness remains challenging without effective visualization and control interfaces. This work presents a multi-modal extended reality (XR) system for robot teleoperation and scene exploration that integrates immersive visual and haptic feedback modalities. To address motion sickness commonly induced by 360-degree camera feeds in head-mounted displays (HMDs), the system employs a fixed dual-camera configuration: a forward-facing camera for primary navigation and a rear-facing camera for enhanced situational awareness without operator discomfort. For navigation in confined or low-visibility conditions, a 16-channel Velodyne LiDAR generates real-time 2D occupancy grid maps, which are converted into vibrational haptic feedback on handheld controllers to provide intuitive, non-visual obstacle detection. User evaluation with 20 participants demonstrates that this haptic modality significantly reduces the cognitive load associated with obstacle avoidance during teleoperation.
2611.32584.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Author accepted manuscript published in the 2026 IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics (AIM)
2611.32584.journal_ref: 2026 IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics (AIM), 2026

llm.title_ja: 移動ロボット遠隔操作における空間認識向上のためのXRベースシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 固定デュアルカメラとLiDARベースの振動触覚フィードバックを統合したマルチモーダルXRシステムを提案し、移動ロボット遠隔操作時の認知的負荷を大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: 危険な環境での移動ロボット遠隔操作において、効果的な視覚および制御インターフェースがないと十分な状況認識を維持することが困難であること。
llm.method: 前方および後方の固定デュアルカメラ構成と、16チャンネルLiDARによる2D占有格子マップをハンドヘルドコントローラの振動触覚フィードバックに変換するマルチモーダルXRシステムの開発。
llm.result: 20人の参加者による評価実験により、提案する触覚モダリティが障害物回避に関連する認知的負荷を大幅に削減することが示された。

2611.32582.title: Design, Control, and Teleoperation of a Dexterous Robotic Hand with Soft-Rigid Hybrid Fingers
2611.32582.abstract: Adding compliance to robot hands results in higher grasp quality and robust contact with the environment. Soft hands are inherently compliant, but are typically more complex to control and model than rigid equivalents. We extend prior work on soft-rigid hybrid robot fingers into a five-fingered dexterous gripper --- an integrated tendon-driven hand that is highly compliant and controllable. Structural compliance combined with a rigid skeleton, when realized in a five-fingered hand, allow us to use linear control to achieve soft-grasping generality. We evaluate the use of this hand in a variety of teleoperated manipulation tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of the overall mechanical design and control strategy. Our contributions include: (1) Mechanical design of the a five-fingered Soft-Rigid Hybrid Hand, composed of 12 active degrees of freedom, demonstrating a high degree on generalization enabled by the soft-rigid architecture, with our gripper, able to complete 28 of the 33 (84.8\%) grasp postures in the human range. (2) Precise, high bandwidth (up to 1432deg/s extension speed, compared with 700deg/s for the equivalent human joint). (3) Position and task space controllers for the soft-rigid hybrid finger and whole hand. (4) A teleoperation framework for control of this hand, as well as demonstrations of its efficacy in a variety of grasping and manipulation tasks Further tests illustrate the hand's advantages in completing non-rigid manipulation tasks, such as picking up thin deformable objects (such as a dollar bill or folding cloth) as well as in interfacing with soft or delicate targets.

llm.title_ja: 軟硬ハイブリッド指を持つ器用なロボットハンドの設計、制御、および遠隔操作
llm.tldr_ja: 軟硬ハイブリッド構造を持つ5本指の器用なハンドを設計・制御し、多様な把持・マニピュレーションタスクや変形可能な薄い物体の扱いで優れた性能を発揮することを実証した。
llm.problem: ロボットハンドにコンプライアンス（柔軟性）を追加すると把持品質が向上するが、柔らかいハンドは本質的に剛性のある同等品に比べて制御やモデル化が複雑であること。
llm.method: 12の能動的自由度を持ち、線形制御を用いてソフト把持の一般性を実現する5本指の軟硬ハイブリッドハンド（Soft-Rigid Hybrid Hand）の機械設計、位置・タスク空間コントローラ、および遠隔操作フレームワークの開発。
llm.result: 人間の可動域における把持姿勢の84.8%を完了でき、ドル札や布の折り畳みなどの非剛体マニピュレーションタスクや繊細なターゲットの扱いに優れていることを実証した。

2611.32579.title: Follow-Bench 2.0: An End-to-End 3D Benchmark for Socially-Aware Robot Person Following
2611.32579.abstract: Socially-aware robot person following (RPF) requires a mobile robot to follow a designated person in dynamic human environments while maintaining target identity, avoiding obstacles and pedestrians, and preserving socially comfortable formations. Existing benchmarks only partially evaluate this coupled problem: embodied visual tracking benchmarks emphasize target visibility with limited social interaction, person re-identification benchmarks study perception without closed-loop control, and motion-planning benchmarks often assume ground-truth target and pedestrian states. We introduce Follow-Bench 2.0, an end-to-end 3D benchmark for evaluating socially-aware RPF under coupled perception--planning challenges. Built in Unreal Engine, Follow-Bench 2.0 provides difficulty-leveled scenarios with diverse pedestrian flows, lighting and weather conditions, cluttered layouts, bottlenecks, queueing behaviors, distractors, and temporary target occlusions. The benchmark supports modular perception--planning pipelines, end-to-end visual policies, and foundation-model-based active trackers under a unified closed-loop protocol. It further evaluates both back- and side-following configurations and reports safety--comfort metrics covering task success, target visibility, target recovery, social-space intrusion, following formation, and motion smoothness. Experiments show that RPF-oriented modular pipelines substantially outperform current end-to-end visual policies on close and socially comfortable following, but also reveal that socially-aware RPF remains far from solved in interaction-heavy environments and especially in side-following. Follow-Bench 2.0 therefore provides a diagnostic platform for studying how perception errors, occlusions, crowd interactions, and following configurations jointly affect robot person following.
2611.32579.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (ED Track). Project page: https://medlartea.github.io/follow-bench-v2/

llm.title_ja: Follow-Bench 2.0: 社会的配慮型ロボット追従のためのエンドツーエンド3Dベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 動的な人間環境での社会的配慮型ロボット追従（RPF）を評価するためのエンドツーエンド3Dベンチマーク「Follow-Bench 2.0」を提案し、現在の手法の課題を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは、視覚追跡、人物再識別、モーションプランニングのいずれか部分的にしか評価しておらず、結合された社会的配慮型ロボット追従（RPF）を十分に評価できていないこと。
llm.method: Unreal Engine上に構築され、多様な歩行者の流れ、照明、閉塞シナリオを含む難易度別のシナリオを備えたエンドツーエンド3Dベンチマーク「Follow-Bench 2.0」の開発。
llm.result: RPF指向のモジュール型パイプラインがエンドツーエンドの視覚ポリシーを大幅に上回る一方、インタラクションの多い環境やサイドフォローでは社会的配慮型RPFが依然として未解決であることを示した。

2611.32564.title: MXI-MemICL: Towards In-Context Robot Manipulation through Self-Retrieved Interaction Memory
2611.32564.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) offers robots a way to acquire new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates. However, existing robotic ICL methods either rely on large-scale pretraining constrained by scarce, costly robot interaction data or require additional annotations yet struggle to generalize across tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose MXI-MemICL, a framework for memory-guided ICL in vision-language-action (VLA) models. By treating demonstrations as retrievable memory, MXI-MemICL enables in-context manipulation without additional large-scale pretraining or specialized annotations. Specifically, a visual-action causal encoder turns actions and their observed effects in demonstrations and completed interactions into reusable memory to guide execution. To retrieve experience suited to upcoming execution, an intention predictor forecasts the next stage's intent and uses it to query memory. The retrieved experience conditions the language backbone through experience-token prefixes and gated cross-attention, guiding action generation with a learned gate that regulates its influence. MXI-MemICL improves success over the baseline by +8.2% and +14.4% on RoboCasa365 and RoboTwin 2.0. Real-robot experiments show a +9.0% gain, with demonstrations adding +5.0% on seen and +16.7% on unseen tasks. The code will be made publicly available.

llm.title_ja: MXI-MemICL: 自己検索型インタラクションメモリを通じたコンテキスト内ロボットマニピュレーションに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: デモンストレーションを検索可能なメモリとして扱い、大規模な事前学習や追加のアノテーションなしでコンテキスト内マニピュレーションを可能にするフレームワーク「MXI-MemICL」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のロボットICL手法は、希少で高価なロボットインタラクションデータに制約された大規模事前学習に依存するか、追加のアノテーションを必要としつつタスク間で汎化することが困難であること。
llm.method: 視覚行動因果エンコーダを用いて行動と観測された効果を再利用可能なメモリに変換し、意図予測器が次の段階の意図を予測してメモリをクエリするフレームワーク「MXI-MemICL」の提案。
llm.result: RoboCasa365およびRoboTwin 2.0でベースラインをそれぞれ+8.2%および+14.4%上回る成功率を達成し、実ロボット実験でも未見のタスクで+16.7%の向上を記録した。

2611.32550.title: Self-supervised quality evaluation of grid maps without ground truth
2611.32550.abstract: Maps are widely used in the robotics community for localization and path planning and the ability to identify incorrect or inaccurate regions of a map is an area of active research interest. For large environments, manual edits of the map can be very time consuming and a tool which can assist a map editor is needed. With this paper, we contribute to robot introspection through self-assessment of map quality, using only a given map as input to be independent of the underlying mapping algorithm. Current methods for map quality assessment rely on ground-truth or labelled information for training classifiers, both of which can be difficult to obtain. In this paper, we propose a self-supervised learning approach to map quality assessment of 2D occupancy grid maps which identifies regions of a map that require further investigation. We leverage an autoencoder for patches extracted from the map to capture the dominant structure of the map. By evaluating the reconstruction loss of a patch reconstructed with the learned model, we can evaluate whether it contains an unusual structure, which indicates the need of further investigation. We evaluate our method on the outcome of state-of-the-art grid mapping methods using benchmark datasets as well as maps from warehouse environments, highlighting the application to more complex environments. We show that the method identifies regions with sparse data, clutter, and misregistrations.

llm.title_ja: 正解データに依存しないグリッドマップの自己教師あり品質評価
llm.tldr_ja: マップ自体を入力としてグリッドマップの品質を自己教師あり学習で評価する手法を提案し、疎なデータや誤登録のある領域を特定できることを示した。
llm.problem: 大規模環境においてマップの手動修正には膨大な時間がかかり、正解データやラベル付き情報に依存せずにマップの不正確な領域を特定するツールが必要であること。
llm.method: マップから抽出されたパッチの支配的な構造を捉えるオートエンコーダを活用し、再構成されたパッチの再構成誤差を評価して異常な構造を検出する自己教師あり学習アプローチの提案。
llm.result: ベンチマークデータセットや倉庫環境のマップにおいて、スパースなデータ、クラッター、および誤登録のある領域を効果的に識別できることを示した。

2611.32547.title: Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation
2611.32547.abstract: Real-world generative problems in biology, medical imaging, or robotics, rarely come with perfectly paired source and target distributions. While unbalanced Optimal Transport (uOT) provides a robust framework to bridge unpaired datasets via minimum-length paths in probability space, existing formulations based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geometry introduce a structural bias toward high density regions, often triggering mode collapse. We introduce Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT), a novel uOT formulation grounded in contact geometry that decouples density transport direction from mass growth to eliminate structural bias. This allows CuOT to adapt sampling steps to the local data structure, naturally reducing step sizes in high-density regions to prevent overshooting and ensuring stable convergence. The result is a stable, scalable path-length minimization solver that consistently outperforms WFR-based methods on biological dynamics reconstruction, unpaired image-to-image translation, and video generation.
2611.32547.comment: 50 pages, 20 figures; accepted for poster presentation at NeurIPS 2026
2611.32547.journal_ref: The Fortieth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, 2026

llm.title_ja: 生成モデルのための接触幾何学: 不均衡最適輸送定式化
llm.tldr_ja: 密度輸送の方向と質量増加を分離して構造的バイアスを排除する接触幾何学に基づいた新しい不均衡最適輸送定式化「CuOT」を提案し、生成モデルの安定した収束を実現した。
llm.problem: 不均衡最適輸送（uOT）の既存の定式化は高密度領域に対する構造的バイアスを導入し、モード崩壊を引き起こすことが多いこと。
llm.method: 接触幾何学に基づいて密度輸送の方向と質量増加を切り離し、高密度領域でのステップサイズを自動的に縮小して安定した収束を保証する新しいuOT定式化「Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT)」の導入。
llm.result: 生物学的ダイナミクスの再構築、ペアなし画像間変換、および動画生成において、WFRベースの手法を一貫して上回る安定したスケーラブルなパス長最小化ソルバーを実現した。

2611.32534.title: EmbodiedStudio: A Task-Driven Simulation Generation Platform for Embodied Learning and Evaluation
2611.32534.abstract: Training and evaluating robots across diverse tasks requires a supply of simulation environments suited to those tasks. While recent scene and task generators offer a promising way to expand this supply, delivering a usable task environment still faces two practical gaps: generated scenes that look plausible in appearance often fail to support the intended task interactions or remain physically stable in simulation, and generated scoring programs frequently attempt task conditions without implementing them faithfully. We present EmbodiedStudio, a task-driven simulation generation platform that bridges these gaps by jointly authoring scene, task, robot-behavior, and rubric programs under closed-loop simulation feedback and independent review. Crucially, as the coding agent iteratively debugs scenes, behaviors, and stateful rubrics in simulation, this closed-loop process natively yields both forward construction experience for learning to build environments and physical execution experience for policy learning, all bound to frozen environment revisions for repeatable evaluation. Across scene generation, rubric evaluation, ablations, and learning studies, EmbodiedStudio substantially improves task readiness and rubric faithfulness while improving physical stability and retaining actionable supervision signals for layout authoring and policy adaptation.

llm.title_ja: EmbodiedStudio: 身体性学習と評価のためのタスク駆動型シミュレーション生成プラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: クローズドールシミュレーションのフィードバックと独立したレビューを通じてシーン、タスク、ロボット動作、ルーブリックプログラムを共同作成するプラットフォーム「EmbodiedStudio」を提案した。
llm.problem: 生成されたシーンが外観上は自然に見えても意図したタスク相互作用をサポートしなかったりシミュレーション内で物理的に不安定であったりすること、および生成された採点プログラムがタスク条件を忠実に実装していないこと。
llm.method: クローズドールシミュレーションのフィードバックの下でシーン、タスク、ロボットの挙動、ルーブリックプログラムを共同でオーサリングし反復的にデバッグするタスク駆動型シミュレーション生成プラットフォーム「EmbodiedStudio」の導入。
llm.result: タスクの準備完了性とルーブリックの忠実度を大幅に向上させつつ、物理的安定性を高め、ポリシー適応のための実用的な監視信号を保持することを示した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション生成
評価プラットフォーム

2611.32533.title: Next-Manip: On-Demand Agent-Policy Collaboration for Robotic Manipulation
2611.32533.abstract: General-purpose robotic manipulation requires task reasoning, failure recovery, and precise control, yet limited manipulation data make these abilities difficult to obtain from a single policy. Recent multimodal agents show promise in task reasoning and recovery but lack reliable fine-grained control and incur high inference cost, whereas learned policies provide efficient fine-grained execution but struggle beyond their learned skills. Although their complementary strengths suggest combining the two, doing so requires repeatedly deciding which executor should act as task demands change. Instead of relying on the agent for each decision, we present Next-Manip, an on-demand agent--policy collaboration framework that decouples executor allocation from costly agent inference. We propose an Agent Invocation Controller (AIC) that allocates control between the policy and the agent through a lightweight classifier of current execution demands. We further introduce Task Dynamics Context (TDC), which packages informative manipulation changes from in-context examples into compact task references to support both agent reasoning and executor allocation. Across two simulation benchmarks and real-world experiments, Next-Manip achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing agent inference costs.

llm.title_ja: Next-Manip: ロボットマニピュレーションのためのオンデマンド・エージェント-ポリシー協調
llm.tldr_ja: 実行要求の分類に基づいてエージェントとポリシーの制御を動的に割り当てるオンデマンド協調フレームワーク「Next-Manip」を提案し、高額な推論コストを削減しつつ最先端の性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 汎用ロボットマニピュレーションにはタスク推論、失敗回復、精密制御が必要であるが、限られたマニピュレーションデータのために単一のポリシーからこれらの能力を得ることが困難であること。
llm.method: 現在の実行要求の軽量分類器を介してポリシーとエージェント間で制御を割り当てる「Agent Invocation Controller (AIC)」と、インコンテキスト例からの変化をコンパクトなタスク参照にパッケージ化する「Task Dynamics Context (TDC)」の導入。
llm.result: 2つのシミュレーションベンチマークおよび実世界実験において、エージェントの推論コストを削減しながら最先端のパフォーマンスを達成した。
keywords_ja: エージェント・ポリシー協調

2611.32529.title: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners
2611.32529.abstract: Learned driving planners keep being updated after deployment as new logs arrive, yet continual learning evaluations rarely ask whether an update improves on the deployed model, and their verdicts rest on unstated evaluation choices. We present ContinualDrive, a deployment-anchored benchmark for post-deployment continual learning of driving planners. It updates a deployed planner on real-world nuPlan logs one scenario-type group at a time, evaluates the same checkpoints in open and closed loop, makes four measurement axes explicit (evaluation loop, reference checkpoint, temporal aggregation and stream protocol), and anchors a three-valued release verdict to the deployed checkpoint. We study two planners (PlanTF and Diffusion Planner) under full fine-tuning and adapter or LoRA updates, with and without replay or gradient projection, in three task orders. Verdicts can reverse or vanish when one axis changes: open-loop ADE ranks the final PlanTF model above the deployed one in half of its core-suite runs, whereas every closed-loop score ranks it below; backward transfer misses this loss, which on average is already present when each group has just been learned; and regime rankings vary far less across training seeds than across task orders. In the core suite of full and adapter updates, no regime measurably improved on the deployed planner in closed loop; on a panel more than ten times larger every evaluated final checkpoint trails it, and joint training on all groups recovers much of the loss without exceeding its nuPlan closed-loop score. We distill these findings into a reporting contract and will release the code and all checkpoints.
2611.32529.comment: 34 pages (8 main pages + references + 22-page supplement), 4 figures in the main text. Code: https://github.com/continualdrive/benchmark . Project page: https://lzrbit.github.io/continualdrive/

llm.title_ja: ContinualDrive: 学習済み運転プランナーの継続的更新のための展開アンカー型マルチ軸ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 学習済み自動運転プランナーのデプロイ後における継続的学習を評価するための展開アンカー型ベンチマーク「ContinualDrive」を提案し、評価軸の変更によって判定が大きく変動することを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 学習済み運転プランナーは新しいログの到着に伴いデプロイ後に継続的更新されるが、継続的学習の評価では更新がデプロイ済みモデルを改善するかどうかが問われることが稀であり、その判定が未明示の評価選択に依存していること。
llm.method: 実際のnuPlanログを用いてデプロイ済みプランナーをシナリオタイプごとに更新し、オープンループおよびクローズドロピの両方で評価、4つの測定軸を明示してデプロイ済みチェックポイントに対して判定を下すベンチマーク「ContinualDrive」の構築。
llm.result: コアスイートのフルおよびアダプター更新において、どの訓練手法もクローズドールでデプロイ済みプランナーを有意に改善せず、評価軸の変更により判定が逆転または消滅することが示された。

2611.32523.title: AirLeg: A Robust and Accurate Self-Supervised Visual-Inertial-Leg SLAM System
2611.32523.abstract: Visual-inertial-leg (VIL) state estimation offers cost-effective localization for legged robots, adding only a camera to the onboard IMU and joint encoders. However, learning-based leg odometry is limited by its supervision: networks trained in simulation suffer from the sim-to-real gap, while real-world labels require costly sensors or inherit the errors of visual estimates. To address this, we present AirLeg, a self-supervised VIL SLAM system in which vision and leg proprioception improve each other from training to deployment. We pre-train the leg odometry network in simulation and adapt it to the robot without ground truth through imperative learning, where multi-sensor bundle adjustment uses the leg odometry to refine the visual map, which in turn supervises the network. During deployment, the fused estimates adapt the network online. To improve both localization and this supervision, a dual-window estimator fuses vision, IMU, and leg odometry, relates loaded feet to the visually reconstructed terrain through a deformation-aware constraint, and weights the constraints by variance component estimation. AirLeg completes all 17 GrandTour sequences with the lowest average error (0.19 m) among 19 methods. On a low-cost quadruped, it achieves the lowest drift (0.6%) with only 0.5 h of unlabeled data, in real time on an embedded computer.

llm.title_ja: AirLeg: 堅牢で高精度な自己教師あり視覚・慣性・脚部SLAMシステム
llm.tldr_ja: 正解データを必要とせず視覚と脚部プロプリオセプションが互いに学習・改善し合う自己教師ありVIL SLAMシステム「AirLeg」を提案し、低コスト四脚ロボットで低ドリフトなリアルタイム推定を実現した。
llm.problem: 学習ベースの脚部オドメトリはシミュレーション環境でのシム・トゥ・リアルギャップに苦しむ一方、実世界のラベル付けには高価なセンサーが必要か視覚推定の誤差を引き継ぐこと。
llm.method: シミュレーションで脚部オドメトリネットワークを事前学習し、マルチセンサーバンドル調整を用いて視覚マップでネットワークを自己教師あり適応させるシステム「AirLeg」の提案。
llm.result: 17のGrandTourシーケンス全てで19手法中最低の平均誤差（0.19m）を達成し、低コスト四脚ロボット上でわずか0.5時間の未ラベルデータにより最低のドリフト（0.6%）をリアルタイムで実現した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.32513.title: DiffAnchor: Anchor-Space Diffusion for Monocular 3D Hand Pose Estimation
2611.32513.abstract: Accurate and efficient monocular 3D hand pose estimation is an important perception capability for embodied human interaction and dexterous manipulation. Recent diffusion-based methods model pose uncertainty by iteratively denoising 3D joint coordinates. However, directly diffusing the final joints requires the generative process to simultaneously explore plausible poses and recover precise coordinates, often relying on additional denoising steps or multiple hypotheses and consequently increasing inference cost. In this work, we propose DiffAnchor, a few-step anchor-space diffusion framework that diffuses anchors rather than joints. Our key insight is that stochastic exploration does not need to operate directly on the final output. Instead, diffusion searches for informative intermediate anchors that serve as local 3D regressors, while anchor-to-joint offset prediction and weighted aggregation complete precise joint localization. Specifically, fixed context anchors provide stable global references, whereas noisy dynamic anchors are iteratively refined toward informative joint regions. An importance-guided anchor selection and replenishment mechanism further retains useful anchors, removes ineffective ones, and explores insufficiently covered regions. This design reduces the precision burden of the diffusion process and enables accurate prediction using only a few denoising steps and a single hypothesis. Extensive experiments on HO-3D V2, NYU, ICVL, and InterHand2.6M demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on the first three benchmarks and competitive performance on challenging interacting-hand estimation, while maintaining inference efficiency comparable to deterministic regression baselines.
2611.32513.comment: 10 pages. Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Embodied AI

llm.title_ja: DiffAnchor: 単眼3D手姿勢推定のためのアンカー空間拡散モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 最終的な関節ではなく中間アンカーを拡散させる少数ステップのアンカー空間拡散フレームワーク「DiffAnchor」を提案し、高い推論効率を維持しながら最先端の性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 拡散ベースの手姿勢推定手法では、最終的な関節座標を直接ノイズ除去すると、妥当な姿勢の探索と正確な座標の復元を同時に行う必要があり推論コストが増加すること。
llm.method: 最終出力ではなく有益な中間アンカーを確率的に探索し、アンカー・関節間オフセット予測と重み付き集約によって正確な関節位置特定を行うフレームワーク「DiffAnchor」の提案。
llm.result: HO-3D V2、NYU、ICVLの3つのベンチマークで最先端の性能を達成し、インタラクティブハンド推定でも競争力のある性能を示しながら、決定的回帰ベースラインと同等の推論効率を維持した。

2611.32510.title: GeoVLDrive: Geometry-Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
2611.32510.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) planners inherit semantic knowledge from pretrained vision-language models, but their reasoning is rarely grounded in 3D scene structure and its evolution over time. We introduce GeoVLDrive, a geometry-grounded VLA framework for 3D spatiotemporal reasoning and planning. Multi-layer features from a 3D foundation model augment the vision-language backbone through gated cross-attention. A structured latent chain of thought (CoT) organizes future scene geometry, key-agent motion, and meta-actions into ordered, separately supervised latent states. An action expert generates trajectory proposals from these states and multi-layer scene features, and ranks them using scene-grounded, interacting score tokens. We also introduce NAVSIM 3DQA to train and evaluate metric 3D spatial and motion understanding. GeoVLDrive achieves 91.8 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2. On NAVSIM 3DQA, the geometry-grounded backbone scores 89.2% overall, 4.6 percentage points above the fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-2B baseline. On LingoQA, the backbone achieves 68.6% Lingo-Judge accuracy.

llm.title_ja: GeoVLDrive: 幾何学に接地した自動運転のための視覚言語推論
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dシーン構造と時系列の進化に基づいた幾何学接地型のVLAフレームワーク「GeoVLDrive」を提案し、NAVSIMベンチマークで優れたプランニングおよび3D空間理解性能を達成した。
llm.problem: VLAプランナーは事前学習済み視覚言語モデルからセマンティック知識を受け継ぐが、その推論が3Dシーン構造や時間の経過に伴う進化にほとんど接地していないこと。
llm.method: 3D基盤モデルからの多層特徴で視覚言語バックボーンを拡張し、構造化された潜在的思考連鎖（CoT）で将来のシーン幾何学、主要エージェントの動き、メタアクションを整理して軌跡提案を生成するフレームワーク「GeoVLDrive」の提案。
llm.result: NAVSIM v1で91.8 PDMS、NAVSIM v2で90.9 EPDMSを達成し、NAVSIM 3DQAでは89.2%のスコアを記録してファインチューン済みQwen3-VL-2Bベースラインを上回った。

2611.32502.title: MRCT: An Object-Centric Two-Layer Control Architecture for Heavy-Payload Multi-Robot Transportation
2611.32502.abstract: Cooperative transportation of heavy payloads by heterogeneous mobile manipulators requires coordinated payload motion, force distribution, and compliant physical interaction. This paper presents MRCT, an object-centric two-layer control architecture for multi-robot transportation. At the object level, a model predictive controller (MPC) generates a coordinated contact-force reference for the payload. At the robot level, whole- body impedance control (WBIC) modules on individual robots realise the reference through a confidence-based blending of velocity-tracking and impedance torques. The blending mechanism emphasises tracking when the joint-velocity error is small and increases compliance when tracking degrades because of abrupt reference changes or physical disturbances. Simulation and hardware experiments with a heterogeneous team comprising a single-arm and a dual-arm mobile manipulator transporting a near-rated table payload demonstrate accurate object tracking, regulated contact forces, and stable payload orientation. Parameter sensitivity studies, obstacle-avoidance transportation, and step-load disturbance experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of MRCT for reliable cooperative transportation under the evaluated conditions

llm.title_ja: MRCT: 重量物ペイロードの複数ロボット協調輸送のためのオブジェクト中心型2層制御アーキテクチャ
llm.tldr_ja: オブジェクトレベルのMPCとロボットレベルの全身インピーダンス制御を組み合わせた複数ロボット協調輸送のための2層制御アーキテクチャ「MRCT」を提案し、正確な追従と安定した輸送を実現した。
llm.problem: 異種移動マニピュレータによる重量ペイロードの協調輸送には、協調されたペイロードの運動、力の分散、およびコンプライアントな物理的相互作用が必要であること。
llm.method: オブジェクトレベルでモデル予測コントローラ（MPC）が協調接触力参照を生成し、ロボットレベルの全身インピーダンス制御（WBIC）モジュールが速度追跡とインピーダンス トルクの信頼度ベースのブレンドでそれを実現するアーキテクチャ「MRCT」の提案。
llm.result: 単腕および双腕の移動マニピュレータからなる異種チームによる実験において、正確なオブジェクト追跡、接触力の制御、および安定したペイロード向きの維持を実証した。

2611.32493.title: CoFiNav: VLM-Guided Coarse-to-Fine Semantic Navigation for Open-Ended Last-Mile UAV Delivery
2611.32493.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) delivery is an important application of the low-altitude economy, enhancing the flexibility and accessibility of last-mile logistics. Existing UAV delivery methods generally rely on precise terminal coordinates, predefined terminal specifications, or task-specific localization procedures, limiting the scope and flexibility of delivery. As UAV logistics becomes more intelligent, open-ended semantic descriptions offer a new paradigm for specifying terminal destinations. However, conventional aerial navigation methods have limited ability to generalize to delivery scenarios that require open-vocabulary terminal navigation. To enable this broader delivery paradigm, we propose CoFiNav, a VLM-guided coarse-to-fine UAV semantic navigation framework that progressively grounds relation-defined terminal destinations through hierarchical semantic search and active 3D observation. Given a task description, a coarse prior map from OpenStreetMap (OSM), and accumulated observations, CoFiNav uses a vision-language model (VLM) to determine which unresolved entity or spatial relation should be verified next. A geometry-aware module converts the semantic observation request into feasible viewpoints using RGB images and LiDAR, while conventional motion planning handles safe execution. Experiments across multiple urban environments show that CoFiNav outperforms representative adapted baselines in success rate while requiring shorter flight paths and fewer observations.

llm.title_ja: CoFiNav: オープンエンド型ラストマイルUAV配送のためのVLM誘導型粗から密へのセマンティックナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: VLMを用いて関係性で定義された目的地を階層的検索と能動的3D観測で段階的に接地するUAVセマンティックナビゲーションフレームワーク「CoFiNav」を提案し、優れた配送成功率と効率的な飛行経路を実現した。
llm.problem: 既存のUAV配送手法は正確な終端座標や事前定義された仕様に依存しており、オープンボキャブラリーによる終端ナビゲーションへの汎化能力が限られていること。
llm.method: OpenStreetMapの粗い事前マップと蓄積された観測情報から、VLMを使用して検証すべきエンティティや空間関係を決定し、幾何学認識モジュールがRGB画像とLiDARを用いて視点を生成するフレームワーク「CoFiNav」の導入。
llm.result: 複数の都市環境における実験で、従来の適応ベースラインと比較してより短い飛行経路と少ない観測数で高い成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックナビゲーション

2611.32483.title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
2611.32483.abstract: Driving world models anticipate action consequences through representations of how the world evolves. For autonomous driving, these representations must capture both the surrounding scene and the ego vehicle's motion under a candidate plan. We propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that incorporates executable code as part of its world representation. Code represents ego dynamics by expressing how the vehicle state evolves under plan execution, while a learned visual model captures scene-dependent consequences. Executing the code produces a candidate-conditioned motion sequence, which is evaluated relative to the prior plan and recorded motion history. The resulting execution consequences and learned scene outcomes jointly represent the candidate's future, enabling the planner to assess both what a plan may lead to and how the vehicle transitions into that future. The selected plan becomes part of the next decision's execution context, linking successive choices within the model. CodeWAM achieves 93.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest, 92.1 EPDMS on v2 navtest, and 50.6 EPDMS on NAVHARD. Further experiments demonstrate improved pairwise execution consistency and gains on Hydra-MDP and DrivoR without additional training, supporting executable code as a complementary representation for driving world models.

llm.title_ja: CodeWAM：エンドツーエンド自動運転のためのコード・ワールド・アクション・モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 実行可能なコードをワールド表現に組み込んだ駆動型ワールドモデル「CodeWAM」を提案し、候補条件付きの動作シーケンスを生成・評価することで NAVSIM で優れた性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 自動運転のワールドモデルは、周囲のシーンと候補計画に基づく自車運動の両方を捉える必要がある。
llm.method: 車両状態の進化を表す実行可能コードと、シーンに応じた結果を捉える視覚モデルを組み合わせたCodeWAMを提案する。
llm.result: NAVSIM v1 navtestで93.6 PDMS、v2で92.1 EPDMS、NAVHARDで50.6 EPDMSを達成した。

2611.32476.title: ViTacLab: Physically Consistent Visuo-Tactile Simulation, Benchmarking, and Representation Learning for Robotic Manipulation
2611.32476.abstract: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich robotic manipulation, but existing visuo-tactile simulators trade physical fidelity for scalability, and benchmarks largely focus on two-finger grippers. We present ViTacLab, a framework comprising ViTacSim, ViTacBench, and ViTacPolicy. ViTacSim uses a tri-modal tactile primitive: a global sparse contact-force lattice, a local dense force array, and tactile images. Anchored to PhysX contact-solver outputs, it corrects normal inconsistency through local stiffness alignment and reconstructs tangential forces under decoupled slip-stick regimes while preserving GPU parallelism. A joint projection preserves the sparse wrench and enforces local friction cones. ViTacBench spans parallel grippers, dexterous hands, and bimanual systems, with tasks ranging from vision-dominant to tactile-dominant regimes. ViTacPolicy aggregates variable numbers of heterogeneous tactile inputs using spatial-pose embeddings and a Transformer, and aligns force-array and tactile-image modalities through a two-stream VQ-VAE with a shared codebook. Controlled Hertzian-reference indentation and real-sensor sliding tests reduce normal and tangential force RMSE from 2.31 and 1.85 N to 0.42 and 0.53 N, respectively. Throughput reaches 2,482.9 tactile-pipeline FPS at 256 parallel environments. Simulation and real-world experiments show gains on several contact-rich tasks, while low absolute success on tactile-dominant tasks highlights the remaining difficulty of purely tactile control.

llm.title_ja: ViTacLab：物理的に一貫した視覚・触覚シミュレーション、ベンチマーク、およびロボットマニピュレーションのための表現学習
llm.tldr_ja: 物理的忠実度とスケーラビリティを両立した視覚・触覚シミュレーション、ベンチマーク、ポリシー学習を統合したフレームワーク ViTacLab を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の視覚・触覚シミュレータは物理的忠実度とスケーラビリティのトレードオフがあり、ベンチマークも二指グリッパーに偏っている。
llm.method: 接触力格子、局所力配列、触覚画像からなる三モダリティ触覚プリミティブを用い、 PhysXの接触ソルバー出力にアンカーしたViTacSimを構築した。
llm.result: 法線および接線方向の力のRMSEをそれぞれ0.42 Nと0.53 Nに削減し、256並列環境で2,482.9 FPSのスループットを達成した。
llm.limitation: 触覚ドミナントなタスクにおける絶対的な成功率の低さは、純粋な触覚制御の難しさが残ることを示している。
keywords_ja: 視覚触覚シミュレーション
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.32475.title: ROVO: Robust Rotation-Only Visual Odometry for UAVs at Low and Moderate Altitudes
2611.32475.abstract: Image noise can confound rotation and translation estimates in monocular visual navigation for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) at low and moderate altitudes, where even small perturbations may cause large errors in translation direction. Inspired by angular cues in long-range visual perception, we propose rotation-only visual odometry (ROVO) for monocular aerial imagery. ROVO estimates pairwise rotations from matched images, robustly averages them over overlapping windows, and aligns consecutive windows through shared frames. By retaining only orientation in the trajectory state, it prevents uncertain landmark depth from propagating to later estimates. In trajectory simulation, sliding-window ROVO achieved a mean orientation error just 10.7% as large as that of the conventional SLAM baseline. On real flight data, ROVO achieved rotation accuracy comparable to ORB-SLAM3 and DPVO under the original Bell412 settings. With a narrower FoV or at higher flight altitude, ROVO reduced relative rotation RMSE by 19.7--69.4% compared with the next-best method in each comparison. Code and simulation tools are available at https://github.com/sssxxxkkkk/ROVO.

llm.title_ja: ROVO：低・中高度UAVのための堅牢な回転のみのビジュアルオドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 画像ノイズによる姿勢推定の誤差を防ぐため、トラジェクトリ状態に方位のみを保持する単眼空撮向け回転のみのビジュアルオドメトリ（ROVO）を提案する。
llm.problem: UAVの低・中高度飛行における単眼視覚ナビゲーションでは、画像ノイズが回転・平行移動の推定を撹乱し、大きな誤差を引き起こす。
llm.method: マッチング画像からペアワイズ回転を推定し、重なり合うウィンドウ上で堅牢に平均化し、共有フレームを通じて連続するウィンドウを整列させるROVOを提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの平均方位誤差は従来のSLAMベースラインのわずか10.7%となり、実飛行データでも高い回転精度を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルオドメトリ

2611.32473.title: OmniPersist: Persistent Dynamic World Modeling via Coupled Panoramic Evolution
2611.32473.abstract: Action-conditioned world models play a vital role in robotics and autonomous driving, yet existing video diffusion models struggle to maintain dynamic object persistence. When the camera turns away and returns, out-of-view moving entities fail to evolve plausibly in latent space, often mutating or vanishing entirely due to bounded perspective views. To resolve this issue, we propose OmniPersist, a unified framework that couples perspective video generation with panoramic evolution within a single-stage diffusion model, without relying on auxiliary models or initial panoramic inputs. To maintain efficiency, we model the panoramic stream at a lower frame rate, bridging both views across space and time via Geometric Anchoring (GeoAnch) for spatial correspondence and Temporal Compensation (TemComp) for temporal aggregation. OmniPersist is agnostic to camera-control architectures, supporting both latent-level and attention-level conditioning. Extensive experiments on a newly constructed dynamic benchmark across image-to-video and video continuation tasks demonstrate consistent gains in visual quality, camera controllability, revisit consistency, and dynamic persistence.

llm.title_ja: OmniPersist：結合型パノラマ進化による永続的動的世界モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: パノラマ進化とパースペクティブ動画生成を単一ステージの拡散モデル内で結合し、カメラ外の動的オブジェクトの永続性を維持するフレームワーク OmniPersist を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の動画拡散モデルは、視点の限界によりカメラが背を向けて戻った際に動的オブジェクトが変異したり消失したりする。
llm.method: 幾何学的アンカリング（GeoAnch）と時間的補正（TemComp）を介して空間と時間を架橋し、パースペクティブ動画生成とパノラマ進化を結合する。
llm.result: 動的ベンチマークを用いた実験において、視覚品質、カメラ制御性、再訪の一貫性、動的永続性の面で一貫した向上が実証された。

2611.32464.title: Gamification in the age of AI: surveying player perceptions of motivation, manipulation, and data protection
2611.32464.abstract: Modern games and applications increasingly employ artificial intelligence (AI), user modeling, and gamification to influence user behavior, sustain engagement, and monetize attention. Although these mechanisms can enhance motivation and enjoyment, they also raise concerns about manipulation, personal data usage, and transparency. To examine how players perceive these dynamics, we conducted a survey with 28 adult participants. Respondents expressed strong concerns about the collection and exploitation of personal information in games and gamified applications, while also reporting low awareness and a limited sense of control over how their data is used. They evaluated progression features such as leveling systems and leaderboards as motivating. In contrast, they rated retention-focused mechanics such as daily login rewards and random reward reveals as highly manipulative. Participants reported that these systems can create fear of missing out or resemble gambling. Participants also expressed support for regulatory measures that limit exploitative design and protect vulnerable users. These findings reveal a clear gap between increasingly powerful engagement strategies and user trust, illustrating the need for more responsible and transparent gamification practices.

2611.32447.title: ObsBridge: Observation-Grounded Conditioning for Ego Trajectory Prediction
2611.32447.abstract: Pedestrian forecasting from ego-view observations is challenging because occlusion, limited visibility, and tracking errors corrupt observed motion histories. Such errors are particularly consequential for autonomous robot navigation. Existing paradigms typically either impute noisy history positions before forecasting or jointly train an auxiliary history reconstruction branch. However, predictors trained on clean histories may be sensitive to residual errors in recovered histories at deployment. Meanwhile, auxiliary reconstruction still computes inter-agent interactions over raw, corrupted coordinates. We investigate conditioning future prediction on both recovered historical states and raw observation evidence, with progressive training to accommodate imperfect recovery. Building on this insight, we propose ObsBridge, a flow-based trajectory forecasting framework with observation-grounded historical bridging. Specifically, ObsBridge first employs a frozen estimator to recover historical motion from agent-relative and ego-relative positions, image-plane locations, and visibility states. During training, we introduce an agent-wise curriculum that gradually replaces clean teacher histories with complete estimated histories before context encoding. This progressively exposes the predictor to estimated histories during training. Furthermore, we design a residual geometry adapter to fuse the encoded motion with original observation evidence. We aggregate the resulting representations through social attention to condition the flow-based trajectory generator. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that ObsBridge outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On EgoTraj-TBD, it reduces minADE@20 by 6.5\% and minFDE@20 by 8.7\%. The code will be provided at https://github.com/shawnliang420/ObsBridge.

llm.title_ja: ObsBridge：エゴ軌跡予測のための観測グラウンド条件付け
llm.tldr_ja: 不完全な履歴の復元に対処するため、復元された履歴状態と生データの観測証拠の両方に将来予測を条件付けるフローベースの軌跡予測フレームワーク ObsBridge を提案する。
llm.problem: エゴ視点からの歩行者予測では、オクルージョンや追跡エラーが観測された運動履歴を破損させるためロボットナビゲーションで問題となる。
llm.method: エージェント・エゴの相対位置などから履歴を復元する固定推定器を用い、プログレッシブなカリキュラム訓練と残差ジオメトリアダプターを統合する。
llm.result: EgoTraj-TBDにおいて、minADE@20を6.5%、minFDE@20を8.7%削減し、最先端手法を上回った。

2611.32413.title: A Face Robot which Imitates Human Musculoskeletal Skin System and Its Evaluation on Basic Movement of Facial Expression
2611.32413.abstract: Facial robots require many coordinated, smallamplitude motions, but accommodating these motions in a compact face remains difficult. This paper presents an anatomically inspired facial-robot platform that reproduces the layered organization of the human facial musculoskeletal system. The platform comprises bone, muscle, and skin components whose geometry, shape, and attachment locations are derived from three-dimensional anatomical data. Wire-driven, compliant muscle components are routed through PTFE tubes, allowing actuation to be placed away from the face. We describe the selection and fabrication of 65 muscles (34 muscle types) required to reproduce the 47 target action units (AUs) in the Facial Action Coding System (FACS). We then evaluate the reproducibility of individual AUs in two stages: muscle actuation without skin and actuation after the silicone skin is attached. Forty of the 47 target AUs were reproduced with the muscle components, and 30 were reproduced after skin attachment. These results demonstrate the feasibility of reproducing a broad range of FACS facial expressions using an anatomically inspired musculoskeletal structure. The proposed platform provides a foundation for the systematic development and evaluation of future anatomically inspired facial robots
2611.32413.comment: Accepted to IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2026, website - https://haraduka.github.io/musculoskeletal-face/, youtube - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eRuoUJ056uc

llm.title_ja: 人間の筋骨格皮膚システムを模倣した顔面ロボットと、その表情基本動作に関する評価
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の顔面筋骨格組織の階層構造を解剖学的に再現した顔面ロボットプラットフォームを開発し、FACSに基づく表情の再現性を評価した。
llm.problem: 顔面ロボットは多数の協調した微小振幅動作をコンパクトな顔の中に収めることが困難である。
llm.method: 3次元解剖学的データから形状や位置を導出し、 PTFEチューブを経由するワイヤ駆動の柔軟な筋肉コンポーネントを65個作製した。
llm.result: 47の目標アクションユニット（AU）のうち、筋肉コンポーネントのみで40、シリコン皮膚装着後で30が再現された。

2611.32409.title: Delay-Tolerant Formation Tracking for Multi-AGV Systems via Reference-Shift Coupling
2611.32409.abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) that transport a load together must keep a formation while each vehicle tracks its own reference, and they coordinate over wireless links with link-dependent, time-varying and jumping delays. We propose a cascade design for differential-drive AGVs modelled as kinematic unicycles: delayed data from the neighbours drive only a second-order filter that shifts each vehicle's own reference, and an unmodified gain-scheduled tracking law follows the shifted reference. A saturation keeps the shifted reference feasible, and the feed-forward is exact, so the tracking loop never sees the network. We prove that tracking and formation errors remain bounded for arbitrary delays and converge for every bounded delay and every directed, possibly switching, graph. We also construct a strict Lyapunov function with explicit constants and prove exponential convergence and a local input-to-state estimate with delay-independent gains. On undirected graphs, the coupling attenuates the formation error caused by persistent local errors by at least the factor lambda/(lambda+Lambda*lambda_2(L)) (leak lambda, coupling gain Lambda, algebraic connectivity lambda_2(L)), for any delay. Every inequality is verified with an event-driven, error-controlled simulation. A robustness study on a high-fidelity AGV model (drive dynamics, slip, localisation errors, clock offsets, lossy Wi-Fi) comprises 4,894 runs, including paired comparisons against tuned baselines. The cascade never failed, with latencies up to 4 s, 90% packet loss and up to 12 vehicles, whereas a direct delayed coupling failed when its gain saturated the drives. Coupling reduced the formation error after traction losses by 21-32% and after safety stops by up to 47%, at the price of tracking accuracy. Localisation bias and clock offsets, which no coupling law can observe, limit the achievable accuracy.

llm.title_ja: リファレンスシフト結合によるマルチAGVシステムの遅延耐性フォーメーション追従
llm.tldr_ja: 通信遅延やパケットロスが存在するマルチAGVシステムにおいて、リファレンスをシフトするカスケード設計によりフォーメーション追従誤差の有界性を証明した。
llm.problem: 荷物を共同運搬するAGVは各車が自身の参照を追従しつつフォーメーションを維持する必要があるが、ワイヤレスリンクには時間変動・ジャンプ遅延が存在する。
llm.method: 近傍からの遅延データを車両自身の参照をシフトする2次フィルタのみに入力し、未変更の追従則に従わせるカスケード設計を提案する。
llm.result: 最大4秒の遅延や90%のパケットロスにおいて追従ループが破綻せず、トラクション損失後のフォーメーション誤差を21〜32%削減した。
keywords_ja: フォーメーション制御

2611.32381.title: Does Research-Paper Context Improve LLM-Generated Quadruped Navigation? An Exploratory Simulation Study
2611.32381.abstract: Large language models can write competent robot navigation code, but not only does the research on the topic advance, a model may also, due to the volume of findings, fail to recall relevant findings and apply them to the task at hand. In this work, we test whether providing particular research papers as context improves the LLM-written navigation code for the Go2 quadruped, with the LLM (Claude Opus 5) and locomotion policy frozen. Specifically, we compare the navigation controllers the LLM writes when provided with and without particular papers across three settings: behavior trees, navigators edited from a shared base, and controllers written from scratch. When a maze's shortest route is blocked mid-episode, 2 of 8 controllers written with the context of an incremental-replanning paper complete all four trips under Isaac Sim physics, against 7 of 8 without it (two-sided Fisher's exact test, p = 0.041). This difference appears only under physics: in an idealized kinematic simulator, the controllers written with and without the paper are indistinguishable. We hypothesize that an LLM provided research papers as context tends to overweight both their content and their goals -- in this case, the efficiency of incremental replanning -- negatively affecting the fulfillment of the main task and leading to less robust code.

llm.title_ja: 研究論文のコンテキストはLLMによる四足歩行ロボットのナビゲーションを改善するか？ 探索的シミュレーション研究
llm.tldr_ja: 四足歩行ロボットGo2のLLM製ナビゲーションコード生成において、特定の研究論文をコンテキストとして与えることの影響をシミュレーションで検証した。
llm.problem: LLMはロボットのナビゲーションコードを作成できるが、関連する最新の研究成果を思い出してタスクに適用できない場合がある。
llm.method: Claude Opus 5を用い、インクリメンタル再計画などの特定論文をコンテキストとして与える場合と与えない場合で、生成される制御器を比較した。
llm.result: 物理シミュレーション環境において、論文のコンテキストを与えられたコントローラは、タスク遂行において予期せぬ過剰重み付けの副作用が生じる場合があることを示した。

2611.32357.title: CriticJEPA: World Models Are Better Critics Than Optimizers
2611.32357.abstract: Visual world models enable goal-directed planning by predicting action outcomes. Gradient-based planners optimize actions to lower predicted goal cost, but continued optimization can exploit prediction errors after execution stops improving. Comparing plans requires informative relative scores; improving them also requires reliable update directions. Exact-state execution reveals that a frozen hierarchical world model ranks goal-conditioned proposals even when its rankings among outputs of prolonged gradient search are uninformative. Effective planning pairs goal-directed candidates with predictions that distinguish their outcomes. We introduce CriticJEPA, which learns goal-conditioned flow proposals from reward-free trajectories and uses frozen rollouts to select among them at every hierarchy level. Forward selection forms a complete planner; short anchored updates refine candidates before selection. Across visual navigation and manipulation, CriticJEPA increases success at a fraction of the planning compute, transferring shared settings across independently trained models, hierarchy depths, and unseen tasks while keeping every world-model weight fixed.

llm.title_ja: CriticJEPA：ワールドモデルはオプティマイザよりも優れた批評家である
llm.tldr_ja: 報酬なしの軌跡から目標条件付きのフロー提案を学習し、フローズンなロールアウトを用いて計画の階層ごとに選択を行う「CriticJEPA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 勾配ベースのプランナーは予測された目標コストを下げるように動作を最適化するが、長時間の最適化は予測誤差を利用してしまう。
llm.method: 報酬なしの軌跡から目標条件付きフロー提案を学習し、すべての階層レベルでフローズンロールアウトを使用して候補を選択するCriticJEPAを提案する。
llm.result: 視覚ナビゲーションとマニピュレーションにおいて、少ない計算量で成功率を向上させ、重みを固定したまま異なるタスクへ転移できることを示した。

2611.32353.title: Any2Act: Scaling In-Context Robot Learning from Heterogeneous Demonstrations
2611.32353.abstract: Robot in-context learning (ICL) enables a policy to perform unseen tasks by following contextual demonstrations, without task-specific fine-tuning. This is increasingly valuable as large language models reasoning at low frequency can specify tasks through demonstrations and delegate high-frequency execution to such a policy. However, methods conditioned on human videos are bounded by scarce human-robot pairs, while those conditioned on robot demonstrations accept only one or two source types at limited scale. We present Any2Act, a foundation model for robot ICL. Our key insight is that a demonstration should be expressed in the camera layout and action space of the robot that performs it (the executor), not of whoever provided it (the demonstrator). This unified embodiment-grounded representation decouples learning to follow from admitting a new source. Any2Act learns to follow once, from robot-to-robot pairs that already take this form in 1.2M real trajectories spanning 10K tasks. Human videos, simulation, UMI, and other robots are then translated into this representation, and source-routed adapters trained on only a few hundred pairs each absorb the residual gap while the pretrained model stays frozen. For long horizons, a training-free tracker feeds only the demonstration window around the executor's progress, bounding the context and rolling back to redo failed steps. From a single demonstration, Any2Act achieves 57.5% success on unseen tasks without fine-tuning, exceeding VLAs fine-tuned on 50 demonstrations per task; other demonstrators retain 74-91% of the success achieved with the executor's own demonstrations.

llm.title_ja: Any2Act：異種実演からのコンテキスト内ロボット学習のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: デモ提供者の違いや異種デバイスを統一されたエンボディメント表現に変換し、タスク特化型のファインチューニングなしで未見タスクを遂行する汎用基盤モデル Any2Act を提案する。
llm.problem: 人間の動画に条件付けられた手法はペアデータの不足に悩まされ、ロボットデモに基づく手法は限られたスケールしか受け入れられない。
llm.method: デモを実演者の表現ではなく、実行するロボットのカメラレイアウトや行動空間で表現する共通のエンボディメント表現を採用する。
llm.result: 単一のデモからファインチューニングなしで未見タスクに対して57.5%の成功率を達成し、50回のデモでファインチューニングされたVLAを凌駕した。

2611.32351.title: LookAnything: A Foundation Model for Holistic Gaze Following
2611.32351.abstract: Human gaze provides a rich window into attention and intent, making its understanding essential for applications ranging from social signal analysis to human-robot interaction. Existing methods typically employ highly customized architectures relying on auxiliary inputs like head crops or depth maps, causing cascading errors and inference overhead. Trained on single domains and confined to isolated gaze following with heatmap outputs, they lack flexibility and generalization for diverse interactive scenarios. To bridge this gap, we present LookAnything, a foundation model that unifies diverse gaze-centric tasks for holistic gaze following. Benefiting from large-scale multi-task and cross-domain training, LookAnything flexibly adapts to various settings, generating diverse outputs (points, boxes, heatmaps, and language) and supporting broad gaze-centric localization, description, and reasoning. At its core, we introduce learnable gaze-prior queries to promote gaze-aware representation learning, eliminating the need for auxiliary external inputs. To facilitate this paradigm, we construct HoliGaze, a comprehensive corpus and benchmark comprising 311K question-answer pairs across 5 capability dimensions and 9 distinct tasks. Experiments demonstrate that LookAnything consistently outperforms 33 leading vision-language models on holistic gaze following, while remaining highly competitive with dedicated specialists across 5 conventional target detection benchmarks. Evaluation on unseen datasets and deployment on a real robot further validate its strong out-of-domain generalization and flexible adaptation in real-world scenarios.

llm.title_ja: LookAnything：全体的な視線追従のための基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な視線中心タスクを統一し、学習可能な視線事前クエリを用いて外部の補助入力を不要にする全体的な視線追従の基盤モデル LookAnything を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の視線追従手法は、頭部クロップや深度マップなどの補助入力に依存し、単一ドメインに特化しているため汎用性や柔軟性に欠ける。
llm.method: 大規模なマルチタスク・クロスドメイン訓練を通じて、点、ボックス、ヒートマップ、言語など多様な出力を柔軟に適応させるモデル設計とし、HoliGazeベンチマークを構築した。
llm.result: 全体的な視線追従において33の主要な視覚言語モデルを一貫して上回り、実ロボットへの展開で優れた外挿汎化性能を示した。

2611.32335.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
2611.32335.abstract: Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP). To enable broader evaluation, we collect a new dataset, WHOLE, using a UAV platform across Weak-geometry, High-dynamic, Omnidirectional, Low-light, and Easy scenarios. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and WHOLE demonstrate competitive rendering quality and improved geometric accuracy relative to perspective systems. Compared with existing panoramic baselines, GOLD-SLAM improves mean PSNR by 5.56-9.10 dB and reduces mean Depth-L1 by 71.9-83.9%. To assess deployment feasibility on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs, we evaluate an embedded configuration of GOLD-SLAM on a Jetson Orin NX (16 GB), demonstrating online operation at the cost of reconstruction quality.

llm.title_ja: GOLD-SLAM：ガウス・スプラッティング全方位LiDAR-深度SLAM
llm.tldr_ja: パノラマ全方位カバーとLiDAR深度の不整合を克服し、高品質なレンダリングと高精度な幾何学的再構成を球面ドメインで実現する GOLD-SLAM を提案する。
llm.problem: 全方位カメラのパノラマカバレッジとLiDARの視野の不整合が、LiDAR深度事前情報に依存するパノラマ・ガウススプラッティングSLAMの大きな課題となっている。
llm.method: 球面ドメインでトラッキングとマッピングを行い、LiDARのない領域では視覚特徴量を活用するとともに、DAEP（Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning）を導入した。
llm.result: パノラマベースラインと比較して平均PSNRを5.56〜9.10 dB改善し、平均Depth-L1を71.9〜83.9%削減した。
keywords_ja: ガウススプラッティング

2611.32308.title: Putting a Robot on a Phone Call: Layered Signaling, Bounded Occupancy and Turn Arbitration over WebRTC
2611.32308.abstract: We put a Thor robot on a browser voice call, with speech sent from Safari, answers played through the robot's loudspeaker and transcripts returned to the phone. We separate HTTPS signaling, relayed WebRTC media and speech generation into independently observable routes. The browser prefetches relay credentials and allows a 500 ms window after its first relay candidate. The backend starts speech and WebRTC-answer preparation concurrently within a 55 s deadline. A session slot and a non-blocking speaker lock coordinate calls with local voice access. A 2 s gate gives the controller an opportunity to suppress chat before playback. Fifteen of sixteen first dials reached ready-to-speak, comprising seven of eight Wi-Fi calls with a median of 5.57 s and eight of eight cellular calls with a median of 6.76 s. All twenty scored occupancy and recovery scenarios admitted a later call. During five 60 s outages, the backend released the line while the phone remained offline. Across 40 controlled replays, enabling the gate suppressed chat when the controller decided at 1 s. At 3 s, chat and controller feedback both played in sequence, with no overlapping output in any trace. Two additional boundary traces exposed a receipt naming a later feedback item and a new call's query returning its predecessor's feedback. These measurements cover application events on one platform and simulated controller decisions, with acoustic output and task correctness outside their scope.

llm.title_ja: ロボットを音声通話に乗せる：WebRTCにおける階層的シグナリング、有限占有、ターン調停
llm.tldr_ja: ブラウザベースの音声通話システムにロボットを接続し、シグナリング、WebRTCメディア、音声生成を独立して監視可能な経路に分離する仕組みを構築した。
llm.problem: ロボットをリアルタイムの音声通話システムに統合する際、シグナリング、音声生成、遅延、および複数データの調停を適切に管理する必要がある。
llm.method: HTTPSシグナリング、WebRTCメディア、音声生成を分離し、バックエンドでの並行準備、セッションスロット、スピーカーロック、制御用の2秒ゲートを導入した。
llm.result: Wi-Fiおよびセルラー回線でのテストにおいて、通話の接続準備完了や占有・回復シナリオが正常に機能し、音声の重複のない出力が確認された。
llm.limitation: 音響出力やタスクの正確性は評価の範囲外である。

2611.32304.title: Sparse Poison, Strong Hijack: Efficient Trajectory-Level Backdoors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Only 1\% Poisoning
2611.32304.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models advance robotic manipulation, but their reliance on demonstrations exposes them to backdoor threats. Among these threats, trajectory-level targeted backdoors are particularly challenging and may pose greater safety risks than behavior-disrupting attacks: rather than merely causing task failures or local action deviations, they must sustain closed-loop redirection to complete an attacker-specified multi-step task. To reliably induce such behaviors, existing methods typically rely on high poisoning rates to obtain sufficient target-trajectory supervision. However, high poisoning rates may compromise clean-task performance, whereas low rates leave target-trajectory supervision scarce and backdoor learning vulnerable to interference from dominant clean-task updates. To resolve this trade-off at low poisoning rates, we propose a two-stage co-optimization framework guided by vision, language, and action. Stage I freezes the policy and uses differentiable rendering and multimodal supervision to optimize a 3D trigger's texture, translation, and scale, strengthening trigger-target associations from limited poisoned demonstrations. Building on the optimized trigger, Stage II applies source-selective dual-LoRA adaptation to decouple clean and backdoor updates and mitigate their interference, followed by learned column-wise calibration and analytic fusion into a unified policy. Experiments on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, $π_0$, and $π_{0.5}$ across four LIBERO suites show consistent gains over all evaluated attack baselines. With only 1% poisoned data, our method achieves 86.4% target success and 95.2% clean-task success on OpenVLA-OFT in LIBERO-Spatial. Real-robot trials also demonstrate trajectory-level hijacking.
2611.32304.comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, including supplementary material. Simin Huang and Jiawei Chen contributed equally. Code: https://github.com/vla-attack/Sparse_Poison_Strong_Hijack

llm.title_ja: スパースな汚染、強力な乗っ取り：わずか1%の汚染データによるビジョン・言語・行動モデルの効率的な軌跡レベルバックドア攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: わずか1%の汚染データを用いて、VLAモデルのクリーンタスク性能を維持しながら攻撃者が指定したマルチステップの軌跡を実行させるバックドア攻撃フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルは実演データへの依存からバックドア攻撃の脅威にさらされており、特に軌跡レベルのターゲット型バックドアは両立が難しい。
llm.method: ステージIで3Dトリガーのテクスチャ等を最適化し、ステージIIでソース選択型デュアルLoRA適応を用いてクリーン更新とバックドア更新を分離する2段階協調最適化フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: LIBERO-SpatialでのOpenVLA-OFTにおいて、わずか1%の汚染データで86.4%のターゲット成功率と95.2%のクリーンタスク成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.32260.title: EgoLoAF: Learning Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from Egocentric Demonstrations with Hand-Object Affordances
2611.32260.abstract: Training humanoid vision-language-action (VLA) models relies heavily on costly real-robot teleoperation. Recent efforts convert egocentric human demonstrations into humanoid training data. However, most methods still require wearable motion trackers and leave important hand-object interaction cues implicit. Many also mix in real-robot teleoperation data for VLA post-training. These dependencies limit scalable data collection, while implicit interaction cues make precise contact harder to learn. To overcome these limitations, we propose EgoLoAF, the first paradigm to derive all training data for humanoid loco-manipulation directly from egocentric demonstrations without wearable motion trackers. We post-train the VLA on the converted data alone, without real-robot teleoperation demonstrations, and use explicit hand-object interaction cues to guide action generation. Specifically, to obtain humanoid action targets, we estimate torso motion from recorded camera poses and reconstruct both hand trajectories from video. From the same recording, we use each hand's current pose relative to the object to represent hand-object affordances. During post-training, we inject these affordances into the action expert through cross-attention while keeping the vision-language backbone frozen. Additionally, we release 128,400 egocentric demonstration episodes spanning 1,000 hours and 1,284 tasks, together with converted humanoid action trajectories and rendered robot-view observations. Across four real-world tasks, EgoLoAF nearly achieves teleoperation performance (73.1 vs. 74.4 in mean Task Progress Score), while achieving a mean 4.03 times improvement in data-collection efficiency.

llm.title_ja: EgoLoAF：手と物体のAffordanceを用いたエゴセントリック実演からのヒューマノイド Loco-Manipulation の学習
llm.tldr_ja: ウェアラブルモーショントラッカーを使用せず、エゴセントリックな実演動画から手と物体の関係性（アフォーダンス）を抽出し、ヒューマノイドのロコモーションとマニピュレーションを学習するフレームワーク EgoLoAF を提案する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイド用VLAの訓練は高価な実機テレオペデータやウェアラブルトラッカーに依存し、インタラクションの手がかりが不十分である。
llm.method: カメラポーズから胴体運動を推定し、ビデオから両手の軌跡および手・物体のアフォーダンスを再構成し、クロスアテンションを介して行動専門家に注入する。
llm.result: 実世界タスクにおいて、実機テレオペに匹敵する性能（タスク進捗スコア73.1 vs 74.4）を達成し、データ収集効率を4.03倍に向上させた。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
エゴセントリック映像

2611.32256.title: RoboDemo: Reconciling Demonstration Intent and Execution Progress for Long-Horizon Manipulation
2611.32256.abstract: Long-horizon robot manipulation requires more than predicting the next action from the current observation. The policy must maintain a global procedural prior that specifies the expected progress of each subtask stage, while also tracking the realized progress produced by its interactions. To this end, we propose RoboDemo, a demonstration-augmented manipulation framework built on Dual-Cascaded Test-Time-Training. RoboDemo accepts either a task-relevant human demonstration video or a semantically compatible robot video retrieved from simulation corpus as reference, allowing us to evaluate its applicability with and without paired human demonstrations. Task semantics and physical motion information from the reference video are then transferred into persistent demonstration-intent memory. During deployment, we causally compress online observations, robot states, and executed actions into interaction-progress memory. To keep reference intent stable while interaction progress continually evolves, reference and execution video tokens independently update their respective fast-weight states. The action expert performs cascaded memory reads, first obtaining reference guidance and then refining it using realized progress, allowing the policy to adapt to execution deviations without overwriting the stored intent. RoboDemo achieves 90.7% success on Imitator Game and 73.3% success across three real-world household tasks. Real-world videos, code and hf-weights are available in our project website.

llm.title_ja: RoboDemo：長期マニピュレーションのための実演意図と実行進捗の調停
llm.tldr_ja: 実演動画から得られるタスク意図のメモリと、オンライン観測から得られる実行進捗のメモリを二重カスケードで処理し、長期マニピュレーションを頑健に行うフレームワーク RoboDemo を提案する。
llm.problem: 長期的なロボットマニピュレーションでは、現在の観測から次の行動を予測するだけでなく、一連のサブタスクの進捗を維持・追跡する必要がある。
llm.method: 参照動画から永続的な実演意図メモリを構築し、オンライン観測をインタラクション進捗メモリに圧縮し、二重カスケード型テスト時訓練（TTT）により行動を生成する。
llm.result: Imitator Gameで90.7%、3つの現実の家庭用タスクで73.3%の成功率を達成した。

2611.32245.title: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
2611.32245.abstract: Composing frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) skills under an agentic planner promises scalable long-horizon manipulation without long-horizon demonstrations, yet strong atomic skills routinely fail at seams even under a correct plan. Standard remedies reset the robot's pose or draft entry conditions in language, missing the physical cause we uncover via causal interventions: even after re-homing, a frozen VLA rigidly retraces its habitual trajectory and collides with displaced scene residue, whether or not it can see it. We propose the Skill Envelope, a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Exploiting the insight that the rigidity making a frozen skill fragile at seams also makes its trajectory predictable in advance, we expose each envelope as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions), establishing a division of labor where VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation and code repairs out-of-distribution states. On LIBERO-Goal with frozen $π_{0.5}$, our zero-failure envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793); using it for skill ordering and code repair lifts success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Together, these results show that reliable VLA composition hinges on measuring a policy's physical workspace rather than guessing preconditions in language. Ongoing work closes the loop with autonomous LLM orchestration, synthesized free-object recovery, and cross-policy evaluation on cluttered benchmarks and real hardware.

llm.title_ja: VLAは実行し、コードは修復する：3Dスキルエンベロープによるエージェント型マニピュレーションの合成ギャップの架橋
llm.tldr_ja: フローズンなVLAが継ぎ目で失敗する物理的原因を分析し、ポリシーがスイープする3D空間を幾何学的プレコンディションとして定義する「スキルエンベロープ」を提案して合成ギャップを解消する。
llm.problem: フローズンなVLAスキルをエージェントプランナーのもとで組み合わせると、正しい計画であっても継ぎ目で頻繁に失敗する。
llm.method: 成功した実行中にスキルがスイープするボリュームをポリシー測定された3D幾何学的プレコンディション（スキルエンベロープ）として捉え、検出と配置のための古典的3Dツールとして活用する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Goalにおいて、フローズンなπ0.5を用いた場合の複数ステップのシーケンスの成功率を大幅に向上させ、プリビレッジドなリセットと同等の性能を達成した。

2611.32241.title: Motion Chain of Thought: Disentangling Motion Semantics from Visual Appearance for Robotic Manipulation
2611.32241.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) aim to construct a unified architecture capable of understanding world state evolution and guiding action generation. However, existing visual branches focus on predicting static visual observation, rather than reflecting potential transition information that captures the evolution of world states under motion interactions. This leads to representational entanglement between high-level physical condition evolution and low-level action trajectory generation within the Action Model, creating a structural bottleneck while weakening the predictive capability of world evolution modeling for action generation. We propose PILOT (Physical Inference for Latent Optimized Trajectories), whose core Representational Deduction (RD) bridges this gap by integrating motion chain-of-thought (CoT) guidance as a native model capability.
