Specifically, RD aims to encourage the action branch to explicitly model potential state transition tokens, which are retained as CoT in the reasoning space to guide fine-grained motion trajectory. Experiments demonstrate that RD not only improves the success rate and generalization ability of WAMs in complex robotic manipulation tasks but also enhances the model's physical interpretability by decoupling high-level motion semantics from low-level trajectory details. Furthermore, the abundant state transition supervision signals introduced by RD effectively alleviate the sparse supervision in action generation, supporting data-efficient real-robot adaptation with reduced demonstration sets.

llm.title_ja: モーション思考の連鎖：ロボットマニピュレーションのための視覚的外観からのモーションセマンティクス分離
llm.tldr_ja: 状態遷移トークンを推論空間に思考の連鎖（CoT）として保持し、高レベルのモーションセマンティクスと低レベルの軌跡を分離してマニピュレーションを高度化する PILOT を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のワールドアクションモデルの視覚分岐は静的視覚の予測に集中しており、高レベルの状態進化と低レベルの軌跡生成の間で表現の絡み合いが生じている。
llm.method: モデルのネイティブ機能としてモーションCoTのガイダンスを統合し、潜在的状態遷移トークンを明示的にモデル化する表現演繹（RD）を導入した。
llm.result: 複雑なロボットマニピュレーションタスクにおける成功率と汎化性能が向上し、データ効率の高い実機適応が実現された。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル
モーションセマンティクス

2611.32238.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
2611.32238.abstract: Agent-orchestrated robot systems combine the general reasoning capability of multimodal agents with the precise physical control of learned visuomotor policies. Yet such systems often fail at the moment of handoff: a policy is reliable only from a limited set of start states, while the agent may invoke it outside this region. We call this region the policy's handoff boundary. Existing whole-task policies typically have handoff boundaries that are narrow and difficult for an agent to characterize, making reliable coordination challenging. We propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning, which explicitly shapes and then expands the handoff boundary of a visuomotor policy. First, Boundary-Explicit Training fine-tunes the policy on contact segments with diverse start poses, yielding a wide and well-defined boundary that can be communicated to the agent through a simple handoff protocol. Second, Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement retrains the policy on curated successful system rollouts, extending the boundary toward earlier stages of each task and allowing the agent to hand over sooner with fewer language-model calls. Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboDojo, our system outperforms the strongest baseline by over 26 percentage points, reaching 98.4% success in randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, while further reducing its API cost and execution time by 41.3% and 37.5%, respectively. These results suggest that the key to robust agent-policy orchestration lies not only in improving either component individually, but also in explicitly shaping the boundary between them.

llm.title_ja: エージェント連携型ロボットマニピュレーションのための境界認識型ポリシー学習
llm.tldr_ja: ビュモータポリシーのハンドオフ境界を明示的に形成・拡張する「境界認識型ポリシー学習」を提案し、マルチモーダルエージェントとポリシーの協調ロバスト性を高める。
llm.problem: エージェント連携型システムでは、ポリシーが限定された開始状態でのみ信頼性があり、エージェントがその領域外でポリシーを呼び出すと失敗する。
llm.method: 多様な開始ポーズでの接触セグメントでポリシーをファインチューニングする「Boundary-Explicit Training」と、成功したロールアウトで再学習する「Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement」を提案する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0のランダム化されたシーンで98.4%の成功率に達し、ベースラインを26%以上上回りつつAPIコストと実行時間を削減した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション
マルチモーダルエージェント

2611.32233.title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
2611.32233.abstract: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol that continuously advances environment time during model inference and control-interface delays, paired with time-sensitive metrics. Evaluating over 30 methods, we find that the best-performing approach is the trained VLA, yet it achieves only 8.3% temporal success even on Easy-level tasks, with persistent challenges in generalization and transfer. These findings reveal fundamental limitations in current robotic systems and highlight the need to jointly optimize physical competence, temporal reasoning, and execution latency.

llm.title_ja: Roboclock: 時間を意識したロボット知能のための統合ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 時間的制約に焦点を当てたロボット操作のための統合ベンチマーク「RoboClock」を提案し、現行のロボットシステムの限界を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存のロボットベンチマークは空間的正しさや論理的タスク完了を重視し、実世界の時間的制約を無視している。
llm.method: 3種類の時間的制約を持つ60のタスクと、遅延を考慮した評価プロトコルを統合したベンチマーク「RoboClock」を構築した。
llm.result: 最先端のVLAでも簡単なタスクで時間的成功率が8.3%にとどまり、汎化と転移に課題があることが判明した。

2611.32228.title: Disentangling Visual Dynamics for World Model Planning
2611.32228.abstract: Visual world models enable planning through predictive latent states. However, entangled agent and exogenous dynamics can obscure task progress. Disentangling visual dynamics for planning requires addressing two challenges: 1) suppressing cross-factor interference while retaining useful information; and 2) linking factors to task-relevant signals, since stability alone does not ensure meaningful planning distances. Therefore, we introduce FactorWorld, a disentangled visual dynamics framework for world model planning. To separate agent and exogenous dynamics, we propose a Counterfactual Consensus Residual Factorizer (CCRF) guided by bidirectional counterfactual pairs. CCRF separates shared context from dynamic residuals, combining average and worst-partner constraints to suppress interference with state and motion supervision to retain useful information. To translate these factors into planning decisions, we introduce semantic routing to refine full-representation task predictions for state estimation, trajectory scoring, and task-adapted planning. Experiments on MiniGrid, MetaDrive, and CARLA show improved bidirectional factor stability across two backbones. On MiniGrid, factor routing raises mean SR from 78.80% to 82.40%. Across four continuous control tasks, including Push-T, FactorWorld achieves mean success rates ranging from 91.67% to 100% across tasks. These results demonstrate that combining decoupled visual dynamics with explicit tasks can significantly improve the planning capabilities of world models.

llm.title_ja: 世界モデルの計画に向けた視覚ダイナミクスの分離
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントと外因性のダイナミクスを分離するフレームワーク「FactorWorld」を提案し、世界モデルの計画能力を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: エージェントと外因性のダイナミクスが絡み合うことで、タスクの進捗が曖昧になり、効果的な計画が妨げられる。
llm.method: 反事実的コンセンサス残差因子分解器（CCRF）と意味的ルーティングを用いて視覚ダイナミクスを分離・活用するFactorWorldを提案した。
llm.result: MiniGridや連続制御タスク（Push-T等）において、平均成功率の大幅な向上と双方向の因子安定性の改善を実現した。

2611.32226.title: Relation Before Action: Explicit Relation Modeling for Latent Action Pretraining
2611.32226.abstract: Learning latent actions from unlabeled video sequences offers a promising way to acquire reusable action representations without relying on embodiment-specific control annotations. However, existing latent-action pretraining approaches commonly couple the modeling of visual transitions with action inference, directly mapping paired observations or derived transition cues into latent action codes. This formulation leaves two distinct tasks entangled: characterizing the relational structure of an observed transition and abstracting it into a compact action representation. We propose RELACT, a relation-first framework that explicitly separates transition relation modeling from predictive action abstraction. RELACT first constructs a structured relation representation $R$ that captures how visual elements and their interactions evolve across observations. It then infers a compact, state-conditioned stochastic latent action $U$, whose predictive effects are learned through action-conditioned latent dynamics. The resulting action representation can be grounded in native control spaces for model-based planning or used to supervise downstream embodied policies. Extensive experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain image-goal navigation, goal-conditioned manipulation, and downstream policy adaptation demonstrate improved predictive action representations and consistent gains in planning and control, supporting the effectiveness and generality of relation-first latent action pretraining.

llm.title_ja: 行動の前の関係：潜在行動事前学習のための明示的な関係モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的遷移の関係モデリングと予測的行動抽象化を明示的に分離する「RELACT」フレームワークを提案し、計画と制御を改善した。
llm.problem: 既存の潜在行動事前学習は視覚的遷移のモデリングと行動推論を結合しており、関係構造の性格付けと抽象化が絡み合っている。
llm.method: 遷移の関係を捉える構造化された表現を構築し、状態条件付きの確率的潜在行動を推論する関係優先フレームワークRELACTを提案した。
llm.result: 画像目標ナビゲーションや目標条件付き操作などの多様な実験において、予測的行動表現と制御性能の一貫した向上を示した。

2611.32218.title: PoseVLN: Learning Geometric State Evolution for Vision-Language Navigation
2611.32218.abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to relate past experience, current spatial state, and future motion while following natural-language instructions. Recent approaches improve these capabilities through long-horizon memory, state-aware reasoning, and future prediction, yet these components are often modeled separately, leaving navigation state evolution insufficiently connected across time. We argue that camera pose provides a natural geometric representation for bridging past, present, and future states. Based on this insight, we propose PoseVLN, a pose-aware VLN framework that jointly learns navigation decisions and geometric state evolution. PoseVLN organizes visual memory and the current observation in an episode-relative coordinate frame, and jointly predicts the next K navigation actions together with a local $Δ$Pose over the same horizon. The predicted $Δ$Pose is composed with the current trajectory-level pose to obtain the future pose state, which is recursively propagated throughout navigation, forming a continuous geometric state evolution from past memory to future motion. Experiments on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE Val-Unseen splits demonstrate the effectiveness of explicitly modeling geometric state evolution, with PoseVLN outperforming the strongest compared baselines by 2.6 and 2.9 percentage points in success rate, respectively, using only single RGB observations.
2611.32218.comment: 26 pages, 6 figures, including appendix. Project page: https://houpengyu123.github.io/PoseVLN/

llm.title_ja: PoseVLN: 視覚言語ナビゲーションのための幾何学的状態進化の学習
llm.tldr_ja: カメラのポーズを幾何学的表現として利用し、ナビゲーション決定と幾何学的状態進化を共同で学習する「PoseVLN」を提案した。
llm.problem: VLNにおいて過去の経験、現在の空間状態、将来の動きが別々にモデル化され、時間を通じて十分に接続されていない。
llm.method: エピソード相対座標系で視覚メモリを整理し、次のナビゲーション行動と局所ポーズ変化を共同で予測して再帰的に伝播させるPoseVLNを提案した。
llm.result: R2R-CEおよびRxR-CEのVal-Unseenスプリットにおいて、単一のRGB観測のみで既存の最強ベースラインを上回る成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション
ロボットナビゲーション

2611.32216.title: NativeDrive: Native Multimodal Foundations for Autonomous Driving
2611.32216.abstract: Autonomous driving requires semantic understanding and fine-grained scene perception for precise action prediction. Vision-language-action models (VLAs) inherit semantic priors, but low-dimensional action labels provide limited structural supervision. Some studies extend VLAs with visual generation tasks or adopt video-based world-action models (WAMs), but both approaches introduce appearance-reconstruction overhead, which is less relevant to planning. Native multimodal models offer an alternative to unify understanding and generation within one backbone. On this basis, we propose NativeDrive, a native encoder-free multimodal driving framework adapting the unified backbone for policy learning and introduce a dense supervision task tailored to driving. The Native Action Interface reuses the understanding expert's token-prediction interface for the discrete policy and adapts the generation expert for continuous policy. Driving Semantic Editing reuses the generation expert's editing capability for dense scene-structure supervision during training, while inference runs only the selected planning policy. NativeDrive achieves competitive planning performance among unified understanding-and-generation models on NAVSIM v1 and v2, with ablations validating its components' effectiveness. Code will be released.
2611.32216.comment: 16 pages, 8 figures, 7 tables, including supplementary material

llm.title_ja: NativeDrive: 自動運転のためのネイティブマルチモーダル基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 理解と生成のバックボーンを統合し、自動運転向けに特化した高密度な教師ありタスクを導入したフレームワーク「NativeDrive」を提案した。
llm.problem: 自動運転のVLAは低次元の行動ラベルによる構造的監督が限られており、動画ベースの世界行動モデルは不要な外観再構成のオーバーヘッドが生じる。
llm.method: 理解と生成のバックボーンをポリシー学習に適応させ、離散・連続ポリシー向けにトークン予測や編集機能を再利用するNativeDriveを提案した。
llm.result: NAVSIM v1およびv2において、統合型理解・生成モデルの中で競争力のある計画性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル基盤モデル
エンドツーエンド計画

2611.32206.title: Seeing Is Not Reaching: Instruction Shortcuts Override Visual Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.32206.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) are expected to inherit visual grounding from vision-language models, yet often reach for an object's training location after it has been moved. Across six VLAs, we identify two shortcuts: a scene shortcut, where the arm follows the scene's original task despite a new instruction, and an instruction shortcut, where the instruction retrieves the requested object's training location. In $π_{0.5}$, the instruction shortcut persists even though object-name attention follows the moved target. We call this Seeing Is Not Reaching. To determine whether this grounding is unused or overridden, we separately mask an image-mediated grounding pathway and a direct instruction-to-action pathway. Masking the grounding pathway eliminates reaches to moved targets, whereas masking the direct pathway increases them. Thus, grounding already guides action but is often overridden by the instruction shortcut, which acts through the direct pathway. We introduce Pathway-Separated Guidance (PSG), which amplifies grounding and suppresses the shortcut without training or external target locations. On LIBERO-PRO Object under Position perturbations, PSG raises the target-reaching rate from 22.0% to 52.6% and task success from 16.6% to 40.8%, while largely preserving performance on the original tasks.
2611.32206.comment: 31 pages, including supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/QZhang2111/psg

llm.title_ja: 見ることは到達することにあらず: VLAモデルにおける指示ショートカットが視覚的グラウンディングを上書きする現象
llm.tldr_ja: VLAモデルにおいて指示ショートカットが視覚的グラウンディングを上書きする現象を解明し、性能を向上させる「PSG」を提案した。
llm.problem: VLAは対象が移動させられた後でも、訓練時の位置へ向かってしまうシーンショートカットや指示ショートカットの問題を抱えている。
llm.method: 画像介在グラウンディング経路と直接的な指示・行動経路を分離・制御し、グラウンディングを増幅してショートカットを抑制するPSGを提案した。
llm.result: LIBERO-PRO Objectの物体位置摂動タスクにおいて、目標到達率を22.0%から52.6%へ、タスク成功率を16.6%から40.8%へ向上させた。
keywords_ja: 視覚的グラウンディング

2611.32186.title: SkillHarness: Execution-Aware Coordination with Plug-and-Play Skills for Long-Horizon Traversal
2611.32186.abstract: Traversing complex terrain requires robots to coordinate diverse locomotion skills while adapting to unseen obstacles and changing environments. Although perceptive reinforcement learning enables agile locomotion, conventional multi-terrain locomotion rely on fixed policy, limiting adaptability and skill extensibility. Perceptual disturbances and unreliable skill transitions further challenge robust execution. To address these challenges, we propose SkillHarness, an execution-aware coordination framework that integrates a flexible, plug-and-play locomotion skill library. To enhance traversal robustness, we introduce a perceptive reinforcement learning approach that preserves task-relevant environmental references while continuously updating proprioceptive feedback, reducing sensitivity to perceptual fluctuations. A vision-language-guided Harness coordinates navigation and skill execution through event-triggered reasoning, geometric feasibility verification, and execution-phase constraints. By flexibly composing and extending available skills, SkillHarness adapts to unseen terrain and task combinations without retraining the locomotion policies. The framework further incorporates execution feedback and retrospective decision revision to improve skill selection and avoid inappropriate skill switching. We evaluate SkillHarness across diverse terrain configurations, perceptual disturbances, and multi-obstacle traversal tasks to assess its adaptability and reliability in long-horizon traversal.

llm.title_ja: SkillHarness: 長期移動に向けたプラグアンドプレイ型スキルによる実行認識型協調
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な移動スキルを柔軟に統合・調整し、見慣れない地形やタスクに適応する実行認識型協調フレームワーク「SkillHarness」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のマルチ地形移動は固定ポリシーに依存しており、適応性やスキルの拡張性が制限され、知覚の乱れによって困難が生じる。
llm.method: 知覚的強化学習とビジョン言語誘導型ハネスを組み合わせ、イベント駆動型推論や幾何学的検証によりスキルを協調させるSkillHarnessを提案した。
llm.result: 多様な地形構成、知覚的乱れ、複数障害物の横断タスクにおいて、適応性と信頼性を実証した。

2611.32185.title: OVOK: A Recursive Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Video-Based Articulated Robot State Estimation
2611.32185.abstract: Recovering articulated robot state from video supports metric spatial sensing for manipulation, scene reconstruction, and action planning. Yet the problem is ill-posed: different intrinsics, camera-to-robot poses, and joint angles can explain similar observations. Prior task-specific regressors typically assume known intrinsics, fit one robot through laborious data collection and robot-specific training, and still transfer poorly across scenes. Foundation models apply to any robot zero-shot, but their estimates have large errors. We present OVOK (One Video to Kinetics), a recursive self-improving agentic framework for this task. Under a human-authored protocol, an agentic initializer constructs robot-specific OVOK-4k; a proposer--executor--verifier loop then jointly evolves tools and executable workflows from feedback. Updated tools and workflows are accepted only when the verifier judges a positive improvement. The retained workflow is frozen for accurate inference. Experiments demonstrate that the evolved workflow achieves state-of-the-art results on DREAM-V and RoboKeyGen-V, delivering robust and accurate estimates.
2611.32185.comment: 24 pages, including appendix. Submitted to CVPR 2027

llm.title_ja: OVOK: 動画ベースの多関節ロボット状態推定のための再帰的自己改善エージェントフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 動画から多関節ロボットの状態を再帰的に自己改善しながら高精度に推定するフレームワーク「OVOK」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のタスク固有回帰器は既知の内在的パラメータ等を仮定し、特定のロボットに依存しており、シーン間の汎化性能が低い。
llm.method: 人間が作成したプロトコルに基づき、エージェント初期化器と提案・実行・検証ループを組み合わせてツールとワークフローを進化させるOVOKを提案した。
llm.result: DREAM-VおよびRoboKeyGen-Vにおいて、頑健かつ高精度な状態推定で最先端の結果を達成した。
keywords_ja: エージェントフレームワーク

2611.32184.title: Wind-Aware Trajectory Planning for Deformable Aerial Formations
2611.32184.abstract: Coordinated aerial transport in dense urban environments requires drone formations to navigate confined spaces and adapt to spatially varying winds around buildings. Formation deformation enables passage through narrow spaces but changes individual drone velocities and the local winds they encounter, coupling formation motion with aerodynamic effects. We propose Family-Air, a wind-aware trajectory-family planner that constructs a virtual tube as shared collision-free flight space and jointly optimizes formation-center motion, deformation, and timing. A shared affine transformation represents a continuous trajectory family, incorporating spatially varying wind and deformation-induced velocities into a unified air-relative motion objective. The optimization enforces virtual-tube containment, inter-drone separation, and kinematic feasibility. Simulations across four urban wind-field scenarios demonstrate the importance of local wind-deformation coupling. Flight simulations further show improvements in trajectory tracking accuracy. These results demonstrate the potential of wind-aware trajectory-family planning for coordinated aerial transport in complex urban environments.

llm.title_ja: 変形可能なドローン編隊のための風を考慮した軌道計画
llm.tldr_ja: 都市環境での協調飛行のため、空間的に変動する風や変形効果を統合的に最適化する風考慮型軌道計画手法「Family-Air」を提案した。
llm.problem: 狭い空間を通過するための編隊変形は個々のドローンの速度と局所的な風を変化させ、運動と空気力学的効果を結合させる。
llm.method: 仮想チューブを共有の衝突回避空間とし、編隊中心の運動、変形、タイミングを共同で最適化する風考慮型軌道ファミリープランナーを提案した。
llm.result: 都市の風場シナリオのシミュレーションにおいて、局所的な風と変形の結合の重要性と軌道追従精度の向上を示した。

2611.32162.title: Reading Geometric Anchors: Viewpoint Generalization in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation with RGB-Only Deployment
2611.32162.abstract: Moving the camera changes where objects appear in an image, challenging RGB-based imitation learning. A common strategy pairs synthesized views with the same demonstrated action, but ignores supporting physical correspondence across views. By predicting depth with camera calibrations, 3D policies may handle it yet suffer the issue of varied observed point sets. To address these limitations, we propose ReGeoAnch, a geometry-anchored imitation learning framework for viewpoint generalization. Specifically, we build global anchors in the robot base frame and local anchors in the gripper frame, providing shared physical references across viewpoints. Furthermore, Decoupled Appearance-Guided Geometric Readout uses Point-to-Anchor Aggregation (PAA) to obtain comparable and stable geometry around anchors beyond pointwise correspondence. A controllable and decoupled information flow, Anchor-to-Policy Readout (APR), leverages complementary visual and geometric information and supports viewpoint generalization: view-dependent appearances are queried by view-invariant robot state to select task-relevant anchors, with geometric values alone to form the final readout. We further introduce Cross-View Readout Consistency to align the directions of policy readouts from paired source and synthesized target views. Experiments on 12 manipulation tasks across MetaWorld and ManiSkill3 demonstrate improved viewpoint generalization over baseline policies.

llm.title_ja: 幾何学的アンカーの読み取り：RGBのみのデプロイメントによるロボット操作のための模倣学習における視点汎化
llm.tldr_ja: カメラ視点の変化に対応するため、グローバル・ローカルの幾何学的アンカーを利用して視点汎化を実現する模倣学習フレームワーク「ReGeoAnch」を提案した。
llm.problem: カメラの移動による対象物の見え方の変化が、RGBベースの模倣学習において大きな課題となる。
llm.method: ロボットベースおよびグリッパフレームに幾何学的アンカーを構築し、視覚的・幾何学的情報を分離して読み取るReGeoAnchを提案した。
llm.result: MetaWorldとManiSkill3の12の操作タスクにおいて、ベースラインポリシーを上回る視点汎化性能を示した。

2611.32152.title: RoboProbe: Benchmarking Physical Plausibility of Robot World Models
2611.32152.abstract: Evaluating the physical plausibility of generated videos is critical for reliable robotic planning with world models. These videos inform action proposal and assessment before real-world execution, so undetected physical violations can lead to erroneous assessments of action feasibility and safety. Yet current video generators often produce physically implausible interactions. Detecting such violations directly with vision-language models (VLMs) remains challenging as physical verification requires evidence-grounded spatiotemporal reasoning beyond high-level semantic understanding. We develop five law-specific metrics for evaluating physical plausibility by combining spatiotemporal evidence from segmentation, tracking, 3D geometry, or appearance comparisons with targeted VLM reasoning: Contact fidelity, Object persistence, Solidity, Robot deformation, and Object deformation. Building on this metric suite, we introduce RoboProbe, an agentic evaluation framework that coordinates metric execution and selectively refines evaluations through constrained actions. To evaluate the physical plausibility of robot world models, we further introduce RP-Bench, with 761 human-labeled generated videos and 130 real demonstrations of 239 manipulation tasks from 12 robot datasets. On RP-Bench, all five metrics achieve AUROCs above 0.85 and outperform the evaluated learned judges, prior evaluators, and a frames-only Gemini baseline. Applying these metrics to five video generators reveals distinct patterns of physical violations across models, in both violation types and frequencies.

llm.title_ja: RoboProbe: ロボット世界モデルの物理的妥当性のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 生成された動画の物理的妥当性を評価するための5つの指標とエージェント型評価フレームワーク「RoboProbe」を提案した。
llm.problem: 現在の動画生成器は物理的にあり得ない相互作用を生成することが多く、既存のVLMによる直接的な検証には限界がある。
llm.method: セグメンテーションや追跡、3D幾何学の証拠とVLM推論を組み合わせた5つの法則固有の指標と、それを実行する評価フレームワークRoboProbeを提案した。
llm.result: RP-Benchにおいてすべての指標が0.85以上のAUROCを達成し、既存の評価者やベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2611.32119.title: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering
2611.32119.abstract: Episodic-memory embodied question answering enables agents to answer questions based on previously recorded visual observations of the surrounding scenes. However, growing observation histories, varying observation quality across viewpoints, and limited computational resources make it challenging to construct and maintain compact visual memories while retrieving sufficient evidence for question answering. To address these challenges, we introduce CoverMem, which incorporates three key components: (1) a coverage-constrained memory construction method that selects a compact set of informative full frames satisfying object-quality and representative-scene coverage requirements; (2) a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy that locally reselects only the affected frames to satisfy updated coverage requirements as observations arrive; and (3) a budgeted complementary frame selection method that balances question relevance, additional support for question requirements, and redundancy with selected frames within a fixed budget. Experimental results on three benchmarks covering diverse environments and question types demonstrate that CoverMem improves question-answering performance under limited visual budgets.

llm.title_ja: CoverMem: 予算制限された身体化質問応答のためのカバレッジ制約付き視覚メモリ
llm.tldr_ja: 限られた計算リソースとメモリ予算の中で、情報量の多い視覚メモリを効率的に構築・維持するフレームワーク「CoverMem」を提案した。
llm.problem: エピソード記憶に基づく身体化質問応答では、観測履歴の増大や視点ごとの品質のばらつきに対し、コンパクトな視覚メモリを維持することが困難である。
llm.method: カバレッジ制約付きメモリ構築、インクリメンタルなメンテナンス戦略、予算制約付きの補完的フレーム選択を統合したCoverMemを提案した。
llm.result: 多様な環境と質問タイプを用いた3つのベンチマークにおいて、限られた視覚予算下での質問応答性能の向上が示された。

2611.32108.title: Duo: Towards Spatiotemporal Action Coordination in Bimanual Policies
2611.32108.abstract: Bimanual manipulation requires each arm to perform distinct motions while coordinating with the other. Common flow-based robotic policies combine both arms' actions into one token per future timestep, giving attention distinct positions across time but not across arms. We introduce Duo, a simple but effective design that models spatial and temporal dependencies within one shared action head. Specifically, Duo separates both arms into two action tokens per timestep, allowing each arm's motion to interact via cross-arm attention during flow matching. On RoboTwin 2.0, Duo improves the overall success of all four base policies, from 0.45B to 3.62B parameters, with gains of 12.55 and 9.02 percentage points for FLOWER (0.89B) and $π_{0.5}$ (3.62B), respectively. Despite its compact size, FLOWER-Duo achieves the best randomized-generalization, precision, and memory scores on RoboDojo. In real-world tasks, it outperforms $π_{0.5}$ in both success rate and execution speed, while scaling effectively with increasing training data. To provide deeper insight into the design of Duo, we conduct systematic ablations on inter-arm coordination, action grouping, and token granularity, confirming that cross-arm attention drives the improvement while arm-wise interaction offers the best accuracy-compute trade-off.

llm.title_ja: Duo: 両手用ポリシーにおける時空間行動協調に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: 両手のアクションを共有の行動ヘッド内で時空間的に協調させるシンプルな設計「Duo」を提案し、両手操作性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 従来フローベースのポリシーは両手のアクションを1つのタイムステップにつき1つのトークンにまとめ、腕間での注意機構が不足している。
llm.method: 各タイムステップで両手を2つの行動トークンに分離し、フローマッチング中にクロスアーム注意を介して相互作用させるDuoを提案した。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0においてベースポリシーの成功率を大幅に向上させ、実世界タスクでも成功率と実行速度で優れた性能を示した。

2611.32101.title: Ego2Real: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Visuo-Tactile Demonstrations
2611.32101.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric human demonstrations offers a scalable path toward robot skill acquisition. Vision alone, however, provides limited information about physical contacts and the demonstrator's force intent, leading to ambiguities in interpreting hand-object interactions. Capturing human touch via tactile sensing is therefore crucial for reliable human-to-robot dexterous skill transfer. We present Ego2Real, a framework that leverages egocentric demonstrations and tactile gloves to transfer bimanual dexterous manipulation skills to robotic hands. Ego2Real incorporates tactile supervision at two complementary stages: (1) tactile-guided hand-object interaction reconstruction, which uses measured tactile signals to refine hand poses and contact geometry; and (2) contact-informed reinforcement learning, which translates human contact patterns into robotic contact rewards. By combining refined motion references with physical contact rewards during training, Ego2Real guides anthropomorphic robotic hands to emulate demonstrated contact behaviors while adapting to their own morphology and actuation. Experiments show that incorporating tactile supervision into both reconstruction and policy learning yields higher manipulation success rates, underscoring the importance of enriching egocentric demonstrations with tactile observations to improve their quality and transferability.

llm.title_ja: Ego2Real: 視点視覚・触覚デモンストレーションからの両手器用操作の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 触覚グローブを用いた一人称視点のデモンストレーションから触覚情報を活用し、両手器用操作スキルをロボットへ転移するフレームワーク「Ego2Real」を提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚情報のみでは物理的接触や力の意図に関する情報が不足し、手と物体の相互作用の解釈に曖昧さが生じる。
llm.method: 触覚データを用いた手・物体相互作用の再構築と、人間の接触パターンをロボットの接触報酬に翻訳する接触情報付き強化学習を組み合わせたEgo2Realを提案した。
llm.result: 触覚指導を再構築とポリシー学習の両方に組み込むことで、器用な操作の成功率が向上することを示した。

2611.32098.title: ActiveBridge: Scaling Active Prior for Robots through Egocentric Perception-Interaction Modeling
2611.32098.abstract: Robotics foundation models are now widely used for manipulation, and egocentric videos offer rich data for scaling. However, existing methods overlook the human active priors captured in egocentric videos, which limits performance in unstructured scenes. They act on given observations instead of actively seeking information as humans do. We propose ActiveBridge, a training framework that learns these human active priors and transfers them to robots through world-action modeling. We design a robot that actively controls its viewpoint through head actions to acquire the visual information needed for manipulation using a single head camera, without wrist cameras. During human training, an instruction-conditioned model jointly predicts future egocentric videos and synchronized head-wrist action trajectories, with head actions providing explicit supervision for active perception. Experiments show that ActiveBridge outperforms baselines on active manipulation tasks, while ablations demonstrate the benefit of joint head-wrist action supervision.

llm.title_ja: ActiveBridge: 一人称視点知覚・相互作用モデリングによるロボットのアクティブプライ者のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 一人称視点動画から人間の能動的な事前知識（アクティブプライア）を学習し、世界行動モデルを通じてロボットへ転移するフレームワーク「ActiveBridge」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の手法は非構造化シーンにおいて人間が持つ能動的な情報探索の事前知識を無視し、与受された受動的な観測に依存している。
llm.method: ヘッドアクションで視点を能動的に制御しながら、将来の動画と同期されたヘッド・手首の行動軌跡を予測するモデルを学習するActiveBridgeを提案した。
llm.result: 能動的操作タスクにおいてベースラインを上回り、ヘッドと手首の行動の共同監督の有効性を示した。

2611.32093.title: MARGIN: A Risk-Aware Agent for Robot Program Refinement
2611.32093.abstract: Robot-programming agents improve executable control policies through repeated testing and repair, yet binary success saturates while execution risk persists across unseen scenes. We introduce MARGIN, a risk-aware agent that converts successful robot rollouts into actionable evidence for program refinement. Its near-miss margin measures the fraction of the execution budget remaining in the slowest successful development rollout. The agent uses this signal to prioritize fragile programs, guide targeted repairs, and select revisions that preserve development success while increasing execution headroom. An exact safe-racing rule accelerates success-based candidate evaluation. We evaluate MARGIN across LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-90, and Robosuite. In our 80-task LIBERO-Pro reproduction, 78 programs attain perfect development success while accounting for substantial failures on unseen seeds. The near-miss margin predicts held-out failures with an AUC of 0.774, and low-margin programs exhibit 2.97 times higher failure risk. Across two independent evaluation rounds spanning 37 unique LIBERO-Pro tasks, MARGIN reduces executed control steps by 10.7% and 15.0%, with reductions of 18.0-20.0% on LIBERO-90 and Robosuite. Safe racing reduces fixed-sequence candidate-evaluation episodes by 53.5% while retaining identical selections, and paired execution probes improve acceptance decisions by identifying hidden regressions. Together, these results establish near-miss evidence as an effective basis for risk-aware, budget-efficient robot program refinement.

llm.title_ja: MARGIN: ロボットプログラム洗練のためのリスク認識型エージェント
llm.tldr_ja: 成功したプログラムの実行マージンを活用して脆弱なプログラムを優先的に修正するリスク認識型エージェント「MARGIN」を提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットプログラミングエージェントの成功率は飽和する一方で、未知のシーンでは依然として実行リスクが残る。
llm.method: 最も遅い成功デプロイメントの実行バジェットの余剰を示す「ニアミス・マージン」を用いてプログラムの修正と評価を行うMARGINを提案した。
llm.result: LIBERO-Pro等の実験において、実行制御ステップを10.7%〜20.0%削減しつつ、失敗リスクの高いプログラムを効果的に特定した。

2611.32081.title: KeyMemVLA: Subtask-Guided Key Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
2611.32081.abstract: Memory-dependent long-horizon manipulation requires vision-language-action (VLA) policies to infer task progress and recall evidence absent from current observations. Under a limited memory budget, the challenge is to retain history that resolves stage ambiguity and supports subsequent decisions. We present KeyMemVLA, a subtask-guided key memory framework based on progress indication and decision-evidence retention. A two-level annotation process selects subtasks satisfying either criterion and labels their final frames as keyframes to supervise online memory writes. A shared vision-language backbone jointly learns subtask, action, and keyframe prediction. At inference, the policy first predicts the current subtask from the instruction, visual context, and memory, then uses this semantic condition to predict actions and future memory-write positions. Actual observations are retained at the selected times during execution. We introduce KMBench to evaluate active memory retention for decisions across subtasks. Evaluations on RMBench-$M(n)$, RoboTwin-MeM, KMBench, and real-world manipulation tasks show higher average success rates than the compared baselines. Ablation studies and representation analysis support the roles of key memory and explicit task-progress semantics. These results highlight the value of coupling sparse key memory with online progress inference for history-dependent control.

llm.title_ja: KeyMemVLA: サブタスク誘導型キーメモリによる長期ロボット操作
llm.tldr_ja: サブタスクの進行状況と決定の証拠を保持するスパースなキーメモリをVLAポリシーに統合したフレームワーク「KeyMemVLA」を提案した。
llm.problem: メモリ依存の長期操作において、限られたメモリ予算の中で、ステージの曖昧性を解消し後続の決定を支える履歴を保持することが困難である。
llm.method: サブタスク、行動、キーフレームを共同で予測し、予測された重要時点で実際の観測をオンラインで書き込んで保持するKeyMemVLAを提案した。
llm.result: 各種ベンチマークや実世界の操作タスクにおいて、ベースラインと比較して高い平均成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.32053.title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
2611.32053.abstract: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.

llm.title_ja: EffectWAM: ロボット操作のための行動にグラウンディングされた効果の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的予測と実行可能な制御を結びつける世界行動モデル「EffectWAM」を提案し、行動グラウンディングによる性能向上を示した。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルにおいて、視覚変化の予測と実際のロボットの行動・状態との間の確実なグラウンディングが必要とされる。
llm.method: 独立にエンコードされた将来の観測と現在の観測の差分として効果を表現し、エンドエフェクタのポーズ等の測定された変化を視覚表現に学習させるEffectWAMを提案した。
llm.result: 2万時間以上の多様なデータで訓練され、複数のベンチマークにおいて行動グラウンディングによる一貫した性能向上を示した。
keywords_ja: 行動グラウンディング

2611.32025.title: View Management with Gaussian Placement and Opacity Regularization for Online 3DGS
2611.32025.abstract: The realistic rendering of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has drawn interest from real-time applications that require maps to be built online. This led to coupling 3DGS with SLAM, providing camera poses and initial Gaussians for the map. However, the map is still optimized with designs inherited from conventional SLAM, which train only on keyframes selected for localization and regularize geometry with uncertain frontend depth. These designs overlook the model complexity of a 3DGS map: with millions of parameters but few views of each region, the map overfits to sparse inputs. Resolving this is challenging, as every view and Gaussian added to the map competes for the same real-time budget. We close this gap from both sides. To add views while keyframes preserve the structure of the map, we progressively admit non-keyframe images as mapping updates complete and allocate the limited updates across different groups of frames according to the supervision each group provides. To control the model complexity of the map, edge-guided initialization places new Gaussians where image detail requires them. To complement the uncertain frontend depth, Self-Referenced Opacity Regularization (SOR) uses accumulated rendering evidence, at no extra rendering cost, to suppress the opacity of Gaussians that persistently contribute in front of a map-derived surface reference. Together, these designs improve both the appearance and the geometry of online maps within the real-time budget.

llm.title_ja: オンライン3DGSのためのガウス配置と不透明度正則化によるビュー管理
llm.tldr_ja: オンライン3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) において、非キーフレームの段階的導入や不透明度正則化によりマップの品質と計算効率を改善する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: オンラインSLAMと結びついた3DGSマップは、少数のキーフレームのみで最適化されるため疎な入力に対して過学習し、計算予算の制約がある。
llm.method: 非キーフレームの段階的追加、エッジ誘導による新しいガウスの配置、および不透明度を抑制する自己参照不透明度正則化（SOR）を導入した。
llm.result: リアルタイムの計算予算の制限内で、オンラインマップの外観と幾何学的精度の両方を改善した。
keywords_ja: オンラインマッピング

2611.32017.title: Learning Agent States for Latent Action Modeling
2611.32017.abstract: Latent action models (LAMs) learn action-like latents from unlabeled video by coupling frame-pair inference with latent-conditioned prediction, enabling policy and world-model pretraining. However, what the latent must explain depends on the representation space used for action inference and transition prediction. When this space entangles the agent's evolving physical state with visual context, such as background and persistent agent appearance, inferred latents can encode information unrelated to the agent's actions. To address this challenge, we propose Agent-State LAM, which jointly learns a compact agent-state representation and latent actions modeling its transitions. The compact state aggregates dense visual features into a shared space for both action inference and forward prediction. To guide what this state retains, we introduce spatially matched temporal discrimination (SMTD), which trains the state to distinguish its source frame from nearby frames through spatially flexible matching with frozen local visual features. Rather than comparing global frame representations, SMTD scores each frame by emphasizing its strongest local feature matches across spatial locations. This scoring allows background and persistent agent appearance to remain matched across frames despite displacement, making these shared cues less informative for identifying the source frame and encouraging the representation to capture the agent's evolving physical state. Extensive experiments on distracting control tasks and six real robot video datasets demonstrate improved action recovery, downstream control, and world-model prediction. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Mid-Push/Agent-State-LAM.
2611.32017.comment: 27 pages, 12 figures, 20 tables. Project page: https://agent-state-lam.github.io

llm.title_ja: 潜在行動モデリングのためのエージェント状態の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 背景やエージェントの永続的な外見から行動を分離し、コンパクトなエージェント状態と潜在行動を共同で学習する「Agent-State LAM」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の潜在行動モデルは、エージェントの物理的状態と背景などの視覚コンテキストが絡み合う空間で行動を推論するため、無関係な情報をエンコードしてしまう。
llm.method: 高密度な視覚特徴を共有空間に集約し、空間的に柔軟なマッチングで背景などの共通の手がかりを無視して物理的状態の遷移を捉えるAgent-State LAMを提案した。
llm.result: 妨害要素のある制御タスクや6つの実ロボット動画データセットにおいて、行動の復元、下流制御、世界モデル予測の改善を示した。

2611.32016.title: RoboHarness-RL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for VLM-Based Robot Manipulation
2611.32016.abstract: Agentic harnesses enable frontier vision-language models (VLMs) to manipulate robots through perception, planning, and control tools, yet achieving comparable performance with compact open-weight VLMs remains challenging. We present RoboHarness-RL, an agentic reinforcement learning framework for improving VLM-based robot manipulation through tool calls. Starting from supervised fine-tuning on successful teacher demonstrations, the VLM further improves through multi-turn reinforcement learning with task-outcome rewards, without relying on vision-language-action models or world action models. To support efficient multi-turn training, we develop LiteHarness, which uses hierarchical memory to keep interaction contexts compact while preserving task performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, RL raises success from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and from 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro; these gains extend to randomized RoboTwin scenes unseen during training (26.4% to 38.0%). Behavioral analysis further shows that RL reduces repetitive-call rates by up to $4\times$, shortens successful executions, and improves recovery from negative feedback. Project page: https://aim-uofa.github.io/RoboHarness-RL/

llm.title_ja: RoboHarness-RL: VLMベースのロボットマニピュレーションのためのエージェント強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: VLMベースのロボット操作において、タスク結果報酬を用いたマルチターン強化学習により成功率を向上させるフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: コンパクトなオープンウェイトVLMで最先端の視覚言語モデルと同等のマニピュレーション性能を達成することが困難であること。
llm.method: 教師デモンストレーションによる教師あり微調整から始め、タスク結果報酬を用いたマルチターン強化学習によってVLMをさらに改善する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0で成功率が31.2%から44.0%に向上し、LIBERO-Proで57.8%から73.3%に向上した。

2611.31976.title: CodeHOI: Code with Agents for Physically Plausible 4D Hand-Object Interaction
2611.31976.abstract: Modeling 4D hand-object interaction (HOI) is fundamental to understanding manipulation. This requires physics, since hands move objects only by touch and each material responds differently. Yet existing methods ignore this physics or simulate only a narrow range of matter. Programs can instead describe any matter with its physics, but coding agents omit the hand that drives the interaction. We close this gap with CodeHOI, to our knowledge the first agentic framework that writes physically plausible 4D HOI as programs. To write one, an Object Agent first builds each object with the physics of its matter. An HOI Agent then specifies the hands by their contacts and simulates each kind of matter with an established physics solver. Finally, an Evaluator Agent checks each result against physical laws. We also introduce CodeHOI-Bench with 100 reconstruction and generation tasks across four kinds of matter. With off-the-shelf frontier models, CodeHOI writes interactions that are plausible for every kind of matter and remain so when transferred to an independent physics engine. It thereby enables coding agents to write physically plausible HOI across diverse matter.

llm.title_ja: CodeHOI: 物理的に自然な4次元手-物体インタラクションのためのエージェントによるコード生成
llm.tldr_ja: 物理法則に従った4次元の手と物体のインタラクションをプログラムとして記述する初めてのエージェントフレームワークCodeHOIを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の手-物体インタラクション手法は物理法則を無視するか、限られた種類の物質しかシミュレートしないこと。
llm.method: オブジェクトエージェント、HOIエージェント、評価エージェントが協調して、物理ベースの4次元インタラクションをプログラムとして記述する。
llm.result: あらゆる種類の物質に対して自然なインタラクションを記述でき、独立した物理エンジンに転移してもその自然さが維持される。
keywords_ja: 手-物体インタラクション
物理シミュレーション

2611.31956.title: TACTUS: Unifying Surgical Action Understanding in Time and Space
2611.31956.abstract: Advancing surgical automation requires a comprehensive spatio-temporal understanding of how instruments act on tissue throughout an action. Existing surgical benchmarks, however, largely define supervision through task-specific targets, leaving the relationships between action semantics, instrument motion, and tissue interaction incompletely specified. To address this limitation, we introduce TACTUS (Tool, Action, Contact and Trajectory Understanding in Surgery), a new dataset and benchmark that establishes a unified annotation framework for complete surgical actions. The framework jointly specifies tool and action identities, nested action and interaction windows, instrument-specific landmark trajectories, and tissue-region tracks. To construct these annotations at scale, we develop a two-tier pipeline combining human annotation, point tracking, and model-generated spatial prompts. Using this pipeline, we re-annotate 141 videos from five public sources, producing 22,995 action clips spanning 2.9 million frames. The dataset comprises 15,668 Gold clips with human spatial prompts followed by review and re-checking, and 7,327 Silver clips combining human semantic and temporal annotations with model-generated spatial prompts. We further introduce TactusNet, the companion reference network, to benchmark semantic, temporal, and spatial prediction from shared video features. Across TactusNet and 13 published baselines, tool-action accuracy reaches 95.8% with per-head encoder fine-tuning, while the best temporal recall and contact Dice reach 46.6% at temporal IoU 0.7 and 0.351, respectively. Moreover, adding Silver improves the default TactusNet's pair accuracy from 93.8% to 95.5%. Together, these contributions establish a foundation for learning and evaluating the instrument-tissue interactions underlying future surgical automation.
2611.31956.comment: 32 pages, 11 figures, including supplementary material. Lurui Wang and Hao Ding contributed equally. Mathias Unberath is the corresponding author. Project page: https://ruifreddie.github.io/TACTUS/

llm.title_ja: TACTUS: 時間と空間における外科的動作理解の統合
llm.tldr_ja: 外科手術の完全な動作を統合的にアノテーションするための新しいデータセットとベンチマークであるTACTUSを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の外科用ベンチマークはタスク固有のターゲットによる監視に依存しており、動作セマンティクスと組織の相互作用の関係が不完全であること。
llm.method: 人間のアノテーション、ポイントトラッキング、モデル生成の空間プロンプトを組み合わせた2段階パイプラインにより大規模にアノテーションを構築する。
llm.result: 5つの公開ソースから141本の動画を再アノテーションし、ツール・動作の精度が最大95.8%に達した。

2611.31954.title: Perception Is Enough, at the Right Scale: Scale-Adaptive Token Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.31954.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models must process continuous streams of visual observations, and the resulting computational cost limits real-time robotic control. Token pruning reduces this cost, but a fixed semantic scale of perceptual representation can overlook information needed at different stages of manipulation. We show that perceptual semantics can guide effective token selection without relying on internal attention when the selection scale adapts to the scene's evolving semantic structure. Based on this observation, we introduce TauPrune-VLA, a training-free method that controls the scale of the retained perceptual representation through a single perception temperature $τ$. To adapt this scale as manipulation proceeds, TauPrune-VLA updates $τ$ online using trends in perceptual semantics, with robot-state changes and action magnitude regulating the adjustment strength. While these semantics evolve over the course of manipulation, they remain relatively stable between consecutive frames. This continuity allows retention indices computed from the current observation to be applied at the next policy invocation, enabling token selection to run asynchronously with inference and reducing pruning overhead. Evaluated across diverse VLA models and simulation benchmarks, TauPrune-VLA achieves up to a $1.86\times$ inference speedup while maintaining near-baseline task success rates. We further validate its effectiveness on two real-world robotic platforms.
2611.31954.comment: 10 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://lin0e0.github.io/TauPrune-VLA/

llm.title_ja: 知覚だけで十分（適切なスケールであれば）: 視覚言語行動モデルのためのスケール適応型トークン枝刈り
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的意味構造の変化に応じて選択スケールを適応させることで、VLAモデルの推論を高速化する学習不要の手法TauPrune-VLAを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルの連続的な視覚観測処理に伴う高い計算コストがリアルタイム制御を制限していること。
llm.method: 単一の知覚温度を用いて保持する知覚表現のスケールを制御し、ロボット状態の変化と行動の大きさに基づいてオンラインで更新する。
llm.result: 多様なVLAモデルとシミュレーションベンチマークにおいて、タスク成功率を維持したまま最大1.86倍の推論高速化を達成した。

2611.31952.title: VLG-Drive: Unifying Vision-Language and Geometric Priors for Autonomous Driving
2611.31952.abstract: A driving planner needs both scene semantics, which vision-language models (VLMs) provide, and spatial structure, which geometric foundation models recover from visual history. We present VLG-Drive, which keeps both models frozen and trains only a fusion interface and a planner from trajectory labels. At each camera-grid cell, the interface fuses the paired VLM and geometry features into one joint token through a geometry-anchored residual, and a command-conditioned planner reads these tokens to predict the ego trajectory. VLG-Drive achieves 31.78 EPDMS on NavHard under perturbed initial states, the highest among the compared methods, and 88.27 PDMS on NavTest from cameras alone. Pointwise fusion outperforms independent VLM and geometry streams on both benchmarks. In closed-loop driving on 420 HUGSIM scenarios, VLG-Drive outperforms all compared planners. These results indicate that a lightweight planner trained on fused features of frozen vision-language and geometric foundation models is an effective alternative to adapting either model for planning.

llm.title_ja: VLG-Drive: 自動運転のための視覚言語と言何学的事前知識の統合
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結させた視覚言語モデルと幾何学的基礎モデルの融合特徴量を用いて効率的な軌道予測を行う自動運転プランナーVLG-Driveを提案する。
llm.problem: 駆動プランナーにはVLMが提供するシーンの意味論と、幾何学的モデルが復元する空間構造の両方が必要であること。
llm.method: 両方のモデルを固定し、幾何学的にアンカーされた残差を用いた融合インターフェースと軌道ラベルから学習するプランナーのみを訓練する。
llm.result: NavHardベンチマークで最高性能を達成し、閉ループ駆動のHUGSIMシナリオにおいても比較手法を上回る性能を示した。

2611.31925.title: Learning When a Robot Should Ask For Help: Adaptive Intervention Requests in Human-Robot Teaming
2611.31925.abstract: Robots operating in complex environments occasionally encounter situations where autonomous navigation fails. Requesting and receiving a timely intervention from their human supervisor can be critical for failure prevention or recovery. However, requesting help too frequently or at inappropriate times can increase operator workload and reduce team efficiency, while delayed requests may lead to prolonged downtime or unrecoverable failures. In addition to alert timing, the human, robot and task context also influences the intervention outcomes. This paper proposes an algorithm for learning to generate adaptive human intervention requests during human-robot teaming. A help-seeking policy is trained via offline reinforcement learning based on past intervention helpfulness and autonomous progress. This learned alert policy enables a robot to selectively request human help when the intervention outcome is likely to be beneficial. We evaluate the proposed policy in different task environments and user expertise levels in simulation, followed by evaluation in a physical user study. Our findings demonstrate that the learned policy improves exploration efficiency, reduces unnecessary alerts, and enhances novice user support without compromising expert performance in real-time human-robot teaming missions.

llm.title_ja: ロボットが助けを求めるべき時期の学習: 人間とロボットの協調における適応的な介入要求
llm.tldr_ja: 過去の介入の有用性と自律的な進捗に基づいて、ロボットが選択的に人間の助けを求めるポリシーをオフライン強化学習で学習するアルゴリズムを提案する。
llm.problem: 不適切なタイミングでの介入要求は作業効率を低下させ、遅れた要求は長時間の停止や回復不能な失敗につながること。
llm.method: 過去の介入の有用性と自律的進捗に基づいたオフライン強化学習により、ヘルプ要請ポリシーを訓練する。
llm.result: 学習されたポリシーにより、探索効率が向上し、不要なアラートが削減され、実時間での人間とロボットの協調ミッションにおいて初心者ユーザのサポートが強化された。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンインタラクション

2611.31922.title: TANDEM: Temporal Anchor Densification With Reliability-Aware Memory for Lightweight Sparse Depth Completion in Endoscopic Robotic Navigation
2611.31922.abstract: For endoscopic robotic surgery, accurate dense depth perception serves as a foundational capability, which enables navigation, instrument localization, and tissue interaction. However, endoscopic video lacks reliable metric depth, while metric measurements obtained via tracking, time-of-flight sensing, or instrument contact only cover a small fraction of pixels in each frame, rendering sparse depth completion an urgent and unsolved challenge. In this work, we propose Temporal Anchor Densification with Reliability-Aware Memory (TANDEM), a causal sparse depth completion framework for endoscopic video. It adopts a lightweight design and leverages the video stream: past measurements re-projected into the current view recover the metric evidence unavailable within a single sparse frame. To keep this evidence interpretable, accurate, and efficient, an explicit memory scores each re-projected measurement with analytic re-observation, age, and motion-parallax factors without overriding current measurements. A compact network then reconstructs depth via reliability-weighted gradient integration and a frequency-gated reference prior. We evaluate TANDEM on the C3VD colonoscopy and StereoMIS laparoscopy datasets. With only 5.58 M parameters, TANDEM reduces the root mean square error by 11.7% and 32.0%, respectively, compared with the strongest baseline, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy. It also remains accurate under pose errors of the magnitude reported for endoscopic pose estimation. Code will be released at https://github.com/Wk-cpu-art/TANDEM upon acceptance.
2611.31922.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, 2026. 11 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables

llm.title_ja: TANDEM: 内視鏡ロボットナビゲーションにおける信頼性認識メモリを用いた時間的アンカー高密度化による軽量スパース深度補完
llm.tldr_ja: 内視鏡ビデオにおいて、過去の測定値を再投影し信頼性に基づいて統合することで高精度な深度推定を行う因果的スパース深度補完フレームワークTANDEMを提案する。
llm.problem: 内視鏡ビデオには信頼性の高いメートル深度が欠けており、スパースな深度補完が緊急かつ未解決の課題であること。
llm.method: 過去の測定値を現在のビューに再投影し、再観測性・経過時間・運動視差などの要素でスコア付けする明示的なメモリを用いて深度を再構築する。
llm.result: C3VDおよびStereoMISデータセットにおいて、パラメータ数を抑えつつ最強のベースラインと比較してRMSEを大幅に削減し、最先端の精度を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2611.31919.title: DUALingo: A Dual-Hand Instruction-Guided Dataset for Affordance Grounding on 3D Objects
2611.31919.abstract: Affordance grounding localizes where an agent should interact with an object to perform a task. Many everyday manipulation tasks, however, require bimanual affordance, in which two hands assume complementary and cooperative roles to accomplish a shared goal. Existing 3D affordance datasets primarily ground single interaction regions, and manually annotating dual-hand, cooperative contacts does not scale. To address this gap, we introduce DUALingo, a large-scale dataset for task-conditioned, role-aware bimanual 3D affordance grounding on diverse everyday objects. DUALingo represents each task as two cooperative, hand-agnostic roles, each grounded as a heatmap on the object surface. It contains 271K free-form tasks on 71K objects, generated by a fully automated pipeline of open-weight foundation models without human labeling. Expert ratings and a validated LLM judge confirm the quality of the resulting annotations. Trained on DUALingo, existing 3D affordance models learn to ground both cooperative roles from natural-language instructions, with the best-performing model achieving a more than threefold improvement in aIoU over the zero-shot baseline, from 10.3 to 37.8. Robotic manipulation demonstrations illustrate the actionability of the predicted bimanual affordances in performing cooperative tasks. These results position DUALingo as a scalable foundation for learning everyday bimanual affordances. Project page: https://nycu-pair-labs.github.io/DUALingo/

llm.title_ja: DUALingo: 3D物体上のアフォーダンスグラウンディングのための両手指示型データセット
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のアノテーションなしで自動生成された、多様な日常オブジェクトに対するタスク条件付き・役割認識型の両手3DアフォーダンスデータセットDUALingoを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の3Dアフォーダンスデータセットは単一の相互作用領域を対象としており、両手の協調的な接触を手動でアノテーションすることは拡張性がないこと。
llm.method: オープンウェイトの基盤モデルを用いた完全自動化パイプラインにより、各タスクを2つの協調的役割としてモデル化し、オブジェクト表面のヒートマップとしてアノテーションを生成する。
llm.result: DUALingoで訓練された既存の3Dアフォーダンスモデルは自然言語指示から両方の協調的役割を学習でき、ゼロショットベースラインに対して3倍以上のaIoU向上を達成した。

2611.31910.title: ReJEPA: Bounded Predictive Regulation for Latent World Models
2611.31910.abstract: Latent world models learn representations by predicting future states in an abstract embedding space rather than reconstructing raw pixels. When training across multi-frame sequences, however, not all frames and spatial regions are equally informative or predictable. We argue that forcing a world model to minimize every prediction error may be unnecessary and harmful. Under standard $L_2$ loss, unbounded gradients force the encoder and predictor to overfit noisy or transient frames at the expense of core physical structure, while amplifying gradient conflict with representation regularizers. Conversely, $L_1$ loss bounds large gradients, but its constant gradient magnitude near zero disrupts the local smoothness required for planning. We resolve this tension with \textbf{ReJEPA}, a bounded predictive regulation principle that combines bounded gradients for large errors with smooth quadratic behavior near zero, instantiated simply via the element-wise $\log\cosh$ loss. As a drop-in training replacement across Temporal Straightening, LeWorldModel, and V-JEPA~2.1, $\log\cosh$ consistently outperforms $L_2$, a curvature-matched quadratic control, $L_1$, and Smooth-$L_1$ baselines without altering architectures or inference procedures. Notably, the gains grow with environmental complexity, scaling from simple navigation to contact-rich manipulation and real-world autonomous driving on NAVSIM. Probing and geometric analyses confirm that relaxing the penalty on extreme errors yields representations that better capture physical states and align with the true planning cost landscape.

llm.title_ja: ReJEPA: 潜在世界モデルのための有界予測規制
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模な誤差に対する有界な勾配とゼロ近傍の滑らかな二次的挙動を組み合わせた損失関数により、物理状態を捉える表現を学習するReJEPAを提案する。
llm.problem: 標準的なL2損失を用いた世界モデルの訓練では、勾配が爆発してノイズの多いフレームに過学習し、表現正則化と競合すること。
llm.method: 要素ごとのlog cosh損失を用いて、大きな誤差に対する有界勾配とゼロ付近の滑らかな二次特性を組み合わせた有界予測規制原理を実装する。
llm.result: アーキテクチャや推論手順を変更することなく、ナビゲーションから接触を伴う操作、自動運転に至るまで一貫してL2やL1などのベースラインを上回った。

2611.31903.title: Beyond Expert Replay: Cross-Instruction Anchoring for Continual Vision-Language-Action Learning
2611.31903.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models need to continually acquire new manipulation skills while retaining the ability to follow previously learned instructions. Experience replay (ER) can mitigate catastrophic forgetting, but retaining only a small number of historical expert frames per task leaves many old-instruction responses without direct supervision. Under limited replay, we observe a structured failure mode in which an earlier instruction can trigger a subsequently learned, competing goal. To address this gap, we propose Cross-Instruction Anchoring (XIA), which supplements expert replay with instruction-conditioned response preservation. At each task boundary, XIA freezes the previous policy as a teacher and matches its responses to old instructions paired with current observations. This extends supervision beyond stored historical examples without requiring additional expert replay data. Experiments across multiple VLA architectures and three LIBERO suites demonstrate improved success rates and reduced forgetting compared with ER under identical historical expert-data budgets. Additional RoboCasa and real-world experiments further support the effectiveness of XIA.
2611.31903.comment: 19 pages, 12 figures, 10 tables, including supplementary material

llm.title_ja: エキスパートリプレイを超えて: 継続的視覚言語行動学習のためのクロスインストラクションアンカリング
llm.tldr_ja: 過去のポリシーを教師として利用し、指示条件付きの応答保持を行うことで、視覚言語行動モデルの継続学習における破滅的忘却を軽減するXIA手法を提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルの継続学習において、制限された経験リプレイでは古い指示に対する直接的な監視が不足し、競争的目標を引き起こす構造的失敗モードが存在すること。
llm.method: タスク境界ごとに過去のポリシーを教師として凍結し、現在の観測とペアになった古い指示に対する応答を一致させるクロスインストラクションアンカリング（XIA）を適用する。
llm.result: 複数のVLAアーキテクチャとLIBEROスイートでの実験により、従来のエキスパートリプレイと比較して成功率が向上し忘却が軽減された。

2611.31901.title: PreWAM: Exploring the Design of Latent Future Prediction for World-Action Modeling
2611.31901.abstract: World-action models combine action generation with future prediction, allowing visual transitions to serve as supervision for policy learning. Our controlled study of prediction spaces shows that spatially structured semantic features support better overall generalization under visual perturbations and make motion information more readily recoverable from learned predictive representations. Building on these observations, we introduce PreWAM, a world-action model that organizes future supervision around state changes in a prediction space defined by pretrained DINO features. Specifically, Residual World Prediction jointly learns source-relative changes and their resulting future states to emphasize dynamic information while preserving future-state semantics. Temporal-Scale Prediction conditions world queries on temporal distance to capture both short-term local motion and longer-horizon state evolution. These predictive objectives jointly shape a shared vision-language backbone with action supervision during pretraining and downstream policy learning. Experiments across the LIBERO benchmark family, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world robotic manipulation demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved generalization and robustness under diverse distribution shifts.

llm.title_ja: PreWAM: 世界行動モデリングのための潜在的将来予測の設計の探索
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みのDINO特徴量に基づく予測空間で状態変化を予測する将来予測を組織化した世界行動モデルPreWAMを提案し、汎化性能を向上させる。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルにおいて、視覚的摂動に対する頑健性を持ちつつ、学習された予測表現から動作情報を容易に復元できる適切な予測空間の設計が求められていること。
llm.method: 動的情報を強調しつつ将来の状態のセマンティクスを保持するため、ソース相対的な変化とその将来状態を共同で学習する「残差世界予測」と「時間スケール予測」を導入する。
llm.result: LIBERO、SimplerEnv、RoboTwin 2.0、および実機ロボット実験において、優れたマニピュレーション性能と分布シフトに対する頑健性を示した。

2611.31894.title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
2611.31894.abstract: Large language model (LLM) coding agents can iteratively self-improve robot manipulation skills in simulation benchmarks, yet real-world tasks provide neither ground-truth success scorers nor resettable practice environments. Our key observation is that a single real demonstration simultaneously specifies scene geometry, defines the terminal success criterion, and serves as a physical reference trajectory for verifying world fidelity---all decoupled from the source robot's kinematics. We present {RESET}: we reconstruct a contact-rich world and derive a frozen read-only criterion from one demonstration ({R}ebuild); check that world against the demonstration by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency ({E}xamine); evolve modular white-box task graphs and skill code from per-node failure evidence ({S}elf-improve); deploy frozen code on real robots with zero runtime LLM calls ({E}xecute); and share the verified world and criterion with unseen robots without new demonstrations ({T}ransfer). On 8 manipulation tasks, each rebuilt from one real demonstration, RESET achieves 97% average success on unseen layouts in simulation, whereas zero-shot code reaches 27%, per-task fine-tuned pi0.5 policies 31%, and Diffusion Policy 50%; injecting reconstruction defects shows that practice tolerates many reconstruction errors, that geometric errors can still stall or mislead it, and that the check flags most of them while physical randomization covers the rest. Without any target demonstrations, 3 heterogeneous robots acquire the same task skills in the shared world: a robot with similar arms copies 95% of its skill functions unchanged from the source robot, while robots with different arms and hands write their own. In real-robot experiments, the resulting programs run on 4 robots and succeed in 80% of 280 trials.

llm.title_ja: RESET: 1つのデモンストレーション、1つの検証済みワールド、複数身体にわたる自己改善型スキル
llm.tldr_ja: 1つの実世界デモンストレーションから接触豊かなワールドを再構築し、検証を経て自己改善されたタスクプログラムを複数の異なるロボットに展開するフレームワークRESETを提案する。
llm.problem: LLMコーディングエージェントはシミュレーションでスキルを自己改善できるが、実世界タスクには正解の成功スコネアやリセット可能な環境が存在しないこと。
llm.method: 1つのデモンストレーションからワールドと成功基準を再構築（Rebuild）、オープンループ再生で検証（Examine）、失敗の証拠からタスクグラフを自己改善（Self-improve）、コードを実行（Execute）、異なるロボットへ転移（Transfer）する。
llm.result: シミュレーション上の8つの操作タスクで平均97%の成功率を達成し、ターゲットのデモンストレーションなしで3種類の異なる異種ロボットにスキルを習得させた。

2611.31868.title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
2611.31868.abstract: Robots must often keep working after the world changes, as when a block moves or the camera shifts while the robot still acts on what it saw before. Recent work showed that one change during a task lowers success for every policy tested, but did not separate the effect of its timing from the cost of the changed world, or measure what it costs afterwards. We introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases on CALVIN's five-instruction chains, each with one change to the objects, the camera, the robot, or the instruction. Each case compares three runs that are identical until the affected instruction begins: one without the change, one with it in place from that moment, and one in which it arrives while the robot is moving. The second run against the first gives the cost of the changed world, and the third against the second the effect of meeting it mid-motion. On 1,526 held-out cases per policy, with hypotheses fixed in advance, each of ten released policies loses 4.4 to 9.9 percentage points on the affected instruction over the eight core changes. Whether timing matters depends on the change: one that alters what the robot sees costs 5.4 points less mid-motion than from the start, whereas a change to the scene itself or to the robot shows no detectable effect. Rewinding the robot to the start of the instruction removes the benefit for every policy; the stricter test we fixed in advance, that the rewound run then matches the second run, passes for three. The cost also outlasts the affected instruction: the change stays in place, and a policy that still completes that instruction is 5.0 to 16.8 points less likely to complete the next one.
2611.31868.comment: 34 pages (8-page main paper and 23-page supplementary material), 19 figures, 28 tables. Project page: https://forall-labs.github.io/CALVIN-MAX/

llm.title_ja: CALVIN-MAX: 実行中の環境変化はいつロボットポリシーに悪影響を与えるのか？
llm.tldr_ja: 環境変化のタイミングとその変化自体のコストを分離して評価する7,828ケースのベンチマークCALVIN-MAXを構築し、ポリシーへの影響を分析する。
llm.problem: タスク途中の環境変化がロボットポリシーの成功率を低下させることは知られているが、変化のタイミングの影響と変化自体のコストが切り分けられていないこと。
llm.method: 同一の初期条件から、変化なし、最初からの変化、移動中の変化の3つの実行を比較する7,828のケースからなるベンチマークを構築して検証する。
llm.result: 10種類のポリシーすべてにおいて影響を受ける指示の成功率が4.4〜9.9ポイント低下し、視覚的な変化では移動中の方が最初からより影響が少ないなどの違いが示された。

2611.31863.title: Ada-BFM: Adapting Behavior Foundation Models for Humanoid Scene Interaction
2611.31863.abstract: Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose humanoid control through pretraining on large-scale behavioral data. However, their proficiency in whole-body coordination does not readily extend to scene interaction, which requires adapting motion to scene-dependent geometric constraints and contact dynamics. To bridge this gap, we introduce Ada-BFM, a post-training framework that adapts pretrained BFMs for humanoid scene interaction. Ada-BFM augments the original architecture with a lightweight adapter, enabling interaction-specific adjustments while leveraging pretrained control capabilities. Rather than producing a separate controller for each task, the framework yields a shared model for each interaction domain, supporting diverse tasks involving terrain or object interaction. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate that Ada-BFM enables diverse scene interaction behaviors, accelerates learning compared with training from scratch, and largely preserves pretrained behavioral competence. These findings establish Ada-BFM as an effective and efficient approach to extending the capabilities of BFMs beyond their pretraining settings while retaining their strengths in general whole-body control.

llm.title_ja: Ada-BFM: ヒューマノイドのシーンインタラクションに向けた行動基盤モデルの適応
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの行動基盤モデルに軽量なアダプターを追加することで、全身の協調能力を維持しながらシーンに応じた幾何学的制約に適応させるフレームワークAda-BFMを提案する。
llm.problem: 行動基盤モデルの全身協調における習熟度は、シーン依存の幾何学的制約や接触力学への適応を必要とするシーンインタラクションに容易に拡張できないこと。
llm.method: 元のアーキテクチャに軽量なアダプターを導入し、事前学習済みの制御能力を活用しながらインタラクション固有の調整を行うポストトレーニングフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーションと実機における広範な実験により、多様なシーンインタラクション動作が可能になり、ゼロからの学習に比べて学習が加速されることを示した。
keywords_ja: シーンインタラクション

2611.31850.title: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
2611.31850.abstract: Large-scale pretraining provides embodied models with general capabilities, but reliable task execution still requires post training. In multitask settings, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) faces distribution mismatch between training and deployment, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) is limited by sparse rewards and uneven learning progress across tasks. Multi-teacher on policy distillation (MOPD) consolidates expert capabilities through dense supervision on the model's own trajectories, but achieving performance beyond the teachers remains challenging. We propose a two-stage post training framework for flow-based embodied models, constructing distillation objectives from the velocity regression formulation of conditional flow matching. Stage 1 efficiently consolidates expert capabilities through MOPD. Stage 2 combines RL with teacher distillation that weights velocity errors according to the sampling noise, where distillation is restricted to failed trajectories to supplement sparse rewards with dense guidance without directly constraining successful behaviors. Experiments across multiple models and benchmarks show that the framework outperforms joint SFT and exceeds the corresponding teachers' aggregate success rates. Sample efficiency comparisons show higher success rates than direct RL with fewer environment interactions.

llm.title_ja: フローベースの身体性基盤モデルのための2段階ポストトレーニング
llm.tldr_ja: マルチティーチャーによるポリシー蒸留とノイズ重み付け強化学習を組み合わせた2段階のポストトレーニングフレームワークにより、フローベースの身体性モデルの性能を向上させる。
llm.problem: マルチタスク環境において、教師あり微調整は分布のミスマッチに直面し、強化学習は報酬のスパース性と学習の不均一性によって制限されること。
llm.method: ステージ1で教師の能力をマルチティーチャーポリシー蒸留（MOPD）により統合し、ステージ2でサンプリングノイズに応じて速度誤差を重み付けする強化学習と教師蒸留を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 複数のモデルとベンチマークにおいて、統合された教師の成功率を超え、より少ない環境インタラクションで高い成功率を達成した。

2611.31844.title: BendGS: Observation-Conditioned Gaussian Self-Modeling for Continuum Robots
2611.31844.abstract: Visual self-models learn from images how a robot moves under motor commands. Continuum robots need them even more, as they bend continuously without measured joint angles or fixed link geometry. Existing continuum self-models predict point clouds, image-space curves, or future images, but not the next 3D shape, appearance, and tip pose together from an observed body. 3D Gaussians offer a renderable representation of shape and appearance, yet articulated Gaussian self-models rely on joint angles to drive deformation. In this work, we propose BendGS, which uses a virtual backbone estimated from observation to drive command-conditioned Gaussian deformation, enabling next-state prediction for continuum robots without measured joint angles. In Gaussian modeling, a feed-forward network reconstructs the robot as 3D Gaussians from multi-view images, and the backbone, a chain of coordinate frames, is fitted to back-projected depth points to estimate the bending state. In transition, a network predicts its change under a relative motor command to deform the bound Gaussians. The deformed Gaussians render the next images and the 3D shape, and the distal frame gives the tip pose. Training losses use RGB-D images and masks, without bending or tip labels. On simulated and real robots, BendGS achieves the lowest Chamfer distance, best image quality, and lowest tip errors among the compared methods.

llm.title_ja: BendGS: 連続体ロボットのための観測条件付きガウス自己モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 関節角度の計測なしに、マルチビュー画像から仮想骨格を推定して3Dガウス変形を駆動し、連続体ロボットの次状態を高精度に予測するBendGSを提案する。
llm.problem: 連続体ロボットは関節角度や固定リンク形状の計測なしに連続的に曲がるため、既存の自己モデルでは3D形状・外観・先端姿勢を同時に予測できないこと。
llm.method: マルチビュー画像から3Dガウスとしてロボットを再構築するフィードフォワードネットワークと、逆投影された深度点にフィットさせて曲げ状態を推定する仮想骨格チェーンを用いる。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機の連続体ロボットにおいて、比較手法の中で最も低いチャフェ距離、最高の画像品質、最小の先端誤差を達成した。

2611.31843.title: Co-DRIS: Physics-Informed Predictive Belief and Variable-Impedance Learning for Reactive Catching under Coupled Uncertainty
2611.31843.abstract: Reactive robotic manipulation is acutely sensitive to simultaneous sensing noise, measurement dropouts, joint execution errors, and contact parameter variations. While single-frame frameworks like Domain-Randomized Instance Set (DRIS) achieve strong robustness under isolated uncertainties (86.4%), they degrade severely when perception and actuation uncertainties co-occur (27.6% across 10 coupled stress scenarios) due to memoryless encoding and fixed high-stiffness PD control. We propose Co-DRIS + SuperMimic, a perception-action co-design framework coupling: (i) an inertial world-frame physics-informed world model combining exact ballistic kinematics with a zero-initialized contact residual to roll forward missing observations and accelerate training via zero-cost counterfactual dropout consistency; (ii) an action-conditioned dual-stream causal GRU belief encoder resolving the denoising-vs-lag deadlock; and (iii) phase-aware variable-impedance soft-catching that transitions the 7-DoF Franka Research 3 arm into an overdamped regime (zeta/zeta0 ~ 2.26x) at the torque layer. Under unbiased 3-seed tail evaluation on unseen throws (15,360 throws/scenario), our method achieves 89.6 +/- 0.4% on standard benchmarks (+10.5% on 4-sigma noise to 70.5%) and 66.6 +/- 0.5% across 10 coupled/dropout stress scenarios (+39.0% over DRIS; +30.4% on 50% dropout). We further validate impedance decoupling, causal contact triggering under +0.65 s flight-time shifts, and cross-task transfer to steel-plate ping-pong bouncing (87.5% to 100.0%) and FR3+Hand catching (+8.4% under 4x noise with 6-13% lower peak impact force).

llm.title_ja: Co-DRIS: 結合された不確実性下でのリアクティブキャッチングのための物理情報に基づく予測的信念と可変インピーダンス学習
llm.tldr_ja: 知覚と運動の不確実性が同時に存在する環境下でのリアクティブキャッチングを成功させるため、物理情報に基づく世界モデルと可変インピーダンス制御を統合した共設計フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 単一フレームのフレームワークは単一の不確実性に対しては頑健だが、知覚と作動の不確実性が同時に発生すると性能が著しく劣化すること。
llm.method: 弾道運動学とゼロ初期化接触残差を組み合わせた物理情報に基づく世界モデル、行動条件付き因果GRU信念エンコーダ、位相認識型可変インピーダンスソフトキャッチングを統合する。
llm.result: 標準ベンチマークおよび10種類の結合ストレスシナリオにおいて従来法を大きく上回り、実機のキャッチング成功率や衝撃力の軽減を実現した。
keywords_ja: 可変インピーダンス制御

2611.31835.title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control
2611.31835.abstract: Actor-critic methods achieve high returns in robotic control, yet trained actors exhibit high-frequency action oscillations. Most smoothness methods constrain the actor, whereas PAVE regularizes the critic by separately penalizing action-gradient variation and encouraging negative action curvature. The same gradient change, however, moves the critic's preferred action farther where the critic is flat, and separate penalties do not measure this motion. We characterize this motion through the greedy shift, which approximates greedy-action displacement across state transitions to first order under local concavity. Since displacement alone does not reflect its critic-value consequences, the analysis further shows that the shift's curvature-weighted energy approximates the value lost by retaining the previous greedy action to second order. Based on this relationship, POISE regularizes the curvature-weighted energy along temporal and spatial state displacements. It employs a saddle-free curvature metric and reward-scale-consistent scaling while leaving the actor unchanged. On six continuous control tasks with TD3, POISE reduces the smoothness score on every task by $5.9\times$ on average ($4.5\times$ geometric mean), compared with $2.2\times$ ($1.9\times$) for the strongest baseline, and achieves the lowest score on five tasks. Paired return intervals include zero on four tasks, with a 14% increase on Ant and an 11% decrease on Hopper.

llm.title_ja: POISE: 滑らかなアクター・クリティック制御のための曲率認識型批評家正則化
llm.tldr_ja: 貪欲行動の変位とその曲率加重エネルギーを用いて批評家を正則化し、アクターを変更することなく高周波な行動の振動を大幅に削減するPOISEを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボット制御においてアクター・クリティック手法は高い報酬を得るものの、訓練されたアクターが高周波な行動の振動を示すこと。
llm.method: 状態遷移にわたる貪欲行動の変位を近似する「貪欲シフト」を導入し、その変位の曲率加重エネルギーに基づいて時間的・空間的な状態変位に沿って批評家を正則化する。
llm.result: 6つの連続制御タスクにおいてTD3と比較して平均で5.9倍スムーズネススコアを改善し、ほとんどのタスクで最低のスコアを達成した。
keywords_ja: アクター・クリティック

2611.31826.title: VG-GP: Uncertainty-Gated Visuo-Geometric Memory for Negative-Transfer-Resistant Grasp Adaptation
2611.31826.abstract: Pretrained antipodal grasping networks generalize well to canonical shapes but frequently fail zero-shot on novel objects with irregular mass distributions, thin rims, or unfamiliar handles. While episodic experience memory adapts a frozen base policy without retraining, naive retrieval suffers from visual appearance bias, negative transfer from overriding working base grasps, and degenerate closed-loop acquisition. We present VG-GP, a plug-and-play Visuo-Geometric Gaussian Process memory framework for closed-loop $SE(2)$ residual grasp transfer. First, we fuse color-invariant surface-normal DINOv2 features, canonical $SE(2)$ gripper-aligned 3D local heightmaps, and contact-geometry descriptors under a product kernel with Automatic Relevance Determination (ARD) lengthscales learned strictly on source objects. Second, we model the joint posterior over the base grasp and candidate $SE(2)$ alternatives, overriding the base policy only when the joint-covariance Lower Confidence Bound (LCB) clears a risk-sensitive threshold. Third, an online counterfactual curation gate using single-record necessity and sufficiency interventions quarantines source experiences causing negative transfer. Fourth, we close the acquisition loop via Bayesian Expected Improvement (EI) over equal-budget $SE(2)$ probes. Across 42 disjoint YCB objects in ManiSkill3 (20 source, 12 development, 10 held-out test), VG-GP wraps a pretrained GR-ConvNet base policy and raises physical lift rate across all 22 unseen objects from 38.6% (34/88) to 53.4% (47/88) with zero regressions (+13 rescues, 0 losses; object-clustered 95% CI [+6.8%, +22.7%], exact McNemar $p = 0.00024$). On the 10 held-out objects, EI active acquisition reaches 45.0% (18/40 vs. 32.5% base, 5/7 of oracle headroom), achieves 55.0% probe divergence over passive fallback, and monotonically reduces epistemic uncertainty.

llm.title_ja: VG-GP: 負の転移に強い把持適応のための不uncertaintyゲート付き視覚幾何学的メモリ
llm.tldr_ja: 未知の物体に対する把持適応において、視覚的・幾何学的なガウス過程メモリを用いてベースポリシーを安全に補正し把持成功率を向上させるVG-GPフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みの把持ネットワークは標準的な形状には汎化するものの、不規則な質量分布や未知のハンドルを持つ新規物体に対してゼロショットで失敗すること。
