Our project page is at https://wrist-video-policy.github.io.

llm.title_ja: 一般化可能なロボットポリシーとしての手首カメラ動画拡散
llm.tldr_ja: 動画予測を通じて操作の展開を学習し、幾何学的推定を通じて実行可能な動作を復元するクローズドロピカル・マニピュレーションフレームワーク「Wrist Video Policy (WVP)」を提案した。
llm.problem: 汎用的なマニピュレーションポリシーは、新しいタスクの実行、未知のシーンでの動作、およびロボットの身体へのスキル転移を行う必要がある。
llm.method: 将来の手首視点を予測する動画ジェネレータと、事前学習済み3Dモデルから適応させたポーズ推定器を組み合わせ、モデルステッチングによりRGBデコードをバイパスして潜在表現を直接マッピングする。
llm.result: ファインチューニングなしで多様なロボットアームへ転移可能であり、卓上やランドリールームの設定においてゼロショットOOD評価で50%以上の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: マニピュレーションポリシー

2611.31079.tldr_en: Wrist Video Policy is presented, a closed-loop manipulation framework that learns how manipulation unfolds through video prediction and recovers executable motion through geometric estimation and generalizes to tasks ranging from precise grasping and inserting to handling deformable objects.

2611.31054.title: Completing analytical conversion scheme among DH, Hayati, CPC and POE models for manipulator calibration
2611.31054.abstract: Building on Mooring's decomposition of the calibration procedure into four stages - modeling, measurement, identification, and correction - this paper investigates the role of analytical kinematic model conversion algorithms within the calibration framework and their potential to improve calibration performance. Four prominent and widely cited kinematic models: Denavit-Hartenberg (DH), Hayati (HAY), Complete and Parametrically Continuous (CPC), and Product of Exponentials (POE), - are considered. A systematic analysis of the existing conversion relationships reveals that, although most conversions among these models have already been established in the literature, a direct analytical conversion between POE and HAY, and CPC and HAY remains unavailable. Relying instead on a sequential combination of the existing POE-DH and DH-HAY conversions, for example, introduces several limitations. To address this gap, we develop a constructive analytical conversion between POE-HAY and HAY-CPC models based on Lie group theory, formally established through a set of lemmas and propositions. The proposed algorithms are illustrated using an RRRP SCARA robot and an RRHHHH Puma 560 manipulator. The direct POE-HAY conversion is compared with the sequential POE-DH-HAY approach, as well as HAY-CPC in terms of several relevant criteria, demonstrating the advantages of the proposed solution. Finally, we demonstrate the practical significance of the completed analytical conversion framework in an open-loop kinematic calibration experiment on an ABB IRB 1600 manipulator, using an API Radian EMSD3 Laser Tracker for measurements. The experimental results demonstrate that proper model selection combined with completed analytical conversion scheme directly improves calibration accuracy.

llm.title_ja: マニピュレータ較正のためのDH、Hayati、CPC、POEモデル間の中間解析的変換スキームの完結
llm.tldr_ja: Lie群理論に基づき、従来存在しなかったPOE-HAYおよびHAY-CPC間の直接的な解析的変換を構築し、較正精度の向上を実証した。
llm.problem: 主要な運動学モデル（DH、HAY、CPC、POE）の間で、POEとHAY、およびCPCとHAYの直接的な解析的変換が未だ利用できなかった。
llm.method: Lie群理論に基づき、一連の補題と命題を通じてPOE-HAYおよびHAY-CPCモデル間の構成的な解析的変換を開発する。
llm.result: ABB IRB 1600マニピュレータを用いた実機実験により、適切なモデル選択と完成された解析的変換スキームが較正精度を直接向上させることが示された。

2611.31053.title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation
2611.31053.abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer. However, coarse progress feedback cannot identify which physical preconditions held, leaving search unguided, while task-specific optimization easily overfits to individual scenes, making cross-task transfer brittle. We introduce ReWeave, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights. Keeping execution policies and perception frozen, ReWeave co-optimizes coupled context, workflows, and control loops. As new evidence revises the topology, ReWeave reprojects past trials onto the updated task understanding, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width. Across tasks, matching verified local mechanisms to unmet preconditions consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups ($0.34\times$ full concatenation) within a compact shared harness capable of continual learning. ReWeave improves held-out success from 89.00% to 98.75% on LIBERO-PRO and from 25.50% to 58.25% on RoboDojo, while uncovering retained progress in 89% of 159 failed RoboDojo development trials and translating stronger offline reasoning into higher online performance. On eight unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks, the shared harness reaches 51.3% success versus 41.3% for direct distillation, rising to 75.0% after continual learning.
2611.31053.comment: 22 pages, 7 figures, including supplementary material. Project page at https://xuyicheng-zju.github.io/ReWeave/ and code at https://github.com/xuyicheng-zju/ReWeave
2611.31053.hf_summary_en: ReWeave jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights, improving success and enabling continual learning across tasks.

llm.title_ja: ReWeave：身体性ハーネス最適化とクロス・タスク・メタ蒸留のための創発的物理タスク・トポロジー
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシーの重みを更新することなく、インタラクションから身体性エージェントハーネスと創発的物理タスク・トポロジーを共同で最適化するフレームワーク「ReWeave」を提案した。
llm.problem: 長期的身体性タスクには、インタラクションを通じてのみ明らかになる物理的依存関係があり、タスク特有の最適化は個別のシーンに過剰適合しやすい。
llm.method: 実行ポリシーと知覚を固定したまま、結びついたコンテキスト、ワークフロー、制御ループを共同最適化し、トポロジーの更新に基づいて過去の試行を再投影して探索を誘導する。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROで成功率を89.00%から98.75%に、RoboDojoで25.50%から58.25%に向上させ、継続学習を可能にした。
keywords_ja: エージェントハーネス

2611.31053.tldr_en: ReWeave is introduced, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights, and reprojects past trials onto the updated task understanding, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width.

2611.31038.title: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine
2611.31038.abstract: Flow-matching policies integrate a velocity field from a fixed, observation-independent Gaussian source. However, since the source is unimodal and identical across all tasks, the limited representational capacity of Gaussian distributions constrains how far a policy can scale with growing task diversity. Moreover, the source factorizes over time steps and control dimensions, discarding the coordination that manipulation requires. We introduce Boltz-Flow, which replaces Gaussian initialization with a more powerful, observation- and instruction-conditioned Boltzmann source while leaving the base VLA unchanged. Boltz-Flow parameterizes this source with a conditional Boltzmann machine that assigns an energy value to each binary source state. A listwise objective, supervised entirely by offline demonstrations, aligns this energy with the quality of actions produced after frozen flow integration. At inference, the energy defines an Ising instance whose solution is decoded into continuous noise before a single standard integration. We use a physical coherent Ising machine during training. Experiments show that Boltz-Flow improves $π_{0.5}$ across three benchmarks, outperforming the compared strong policy baselines and competing noise optimization methods on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 and ranking second only to LEAP on LIBERO-Plus. Additional experiments show gains under noise-adapted fine-tuning, with action-to-action warm starts, and on the SmolVLA backbone.

llm.title_ja: Boltz-Flow：ボルツマンマシンを用いた高品質なロボット行動の生成
llm.tldr_ja: ガウス初期化を条件付きボルツマンソースに置き換えることで、タスク多様性と動作の協調性を高める「Boltz-Flow」を提案した。
llm.problem: フローマッチングポリシーは、固定されたタスク非依存のガウスソースを使用するため、タスクの多様性に対する表現力が制限され、時間ステップ間で分散されてしまう。
llm.method: ベースVLAを変更せずに、各バイナリスース状態にエネルギー値を割り当てる条件付きボルツマンマシンでソースをパラメータ化するBoltz-Flowを導入する。
llm.result: LIBEROやRoboTwin 2.0においてπ0.5の性能を向上させ、強力なポリシーベースラインや競合するノイズ最適化手法を上回った。

2611.31038.tldr_en: Boltz-Flow is introduced, which replaces Gaussian initialization with a more powerful, observation- and instruction-conditioned Boltzmann source while leaving the base VLA unchanged, outperforming the compared strong policy baselines and competing noise optimization methods on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 and ranking second only to LEAP on LIBERO-Plus.

2611.31037.title: SurgeCount: A Protocol-Guided Composition Harness for Bimanual Surgical Sponge Counting
2611.31037.abstract: We present SurgeCount, a system for auditable robotic surgical sponge counting that composes learned skills under a written procedural protocol. Retained sponges cause preventable harm, and surgical teams count every sponge before closure to reduce that risk. The robot repeatedly isolates one deformable sponge from a tangled pile and places it in the next numbered counting-tray slot, requiring handling of occluded grasp threads while preserving step order. We train one subtask-conditioned policy on eleven short skills and learn when each skill ends. At each learned boundary, a stateful vision-language model selects the next skill from an operator-authored specification of step order, visual verification, and recovery. This creates temporal commitment to each subtask and enables failures to be recovered by recomposing existing skills rather than using a dedicated recovery policy. We evaluate five methods across 100 real-robot trials using 20 matched layouts. SurgeCount fills 47 of 60 ordered slots and completes 12 of 20 procedures, compared with 27 of 60 and 3 of 20 for the strongest of four end-to-end policies trained on the same data. Replacing the detailed protocol prompt with a minimal prompt reduces performance to 29 of 60 slots and 5 of 20 completed procedures. These results show that long-horizon performance depends not only on visuomotor capacity, but also on how learned skills are committed, verified, and composed. This tabletop proof of concept motivates further evaluation of protocol-guided robotic sponge counting in clinically representative settings.
2611.31037.comment: 19 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Accepted to the Findings Track of Machine Learning for Health (ML4H) 2026

llm.title_ja: SurgeCount：両手外科用スポンジ数えのためのプロトコル誘導型合成ハーネス
llm.tldr_ja: 記述された手順プロトコルのもとで学習済みスキルを合成する、監査可能なロボット外科用スポンジ計数システム「SurgeCount」を提案した。
llm.problem: 医療事故を防ぐために手術チームはすべてのスポンジを数える必要があるが、ロボットによる自動化では隠れた把持糸の処理や手順の順序維持が課題となる。
llm.method: 短時間のスキルから構成されるサブタスク条件付きポリシーを訓練し、状態管理型ビジョン言語モデルが、あらかじめ記述された手順プロトコルに基づいて次のスキルを選択する。
llm.result: 100回の実機トライアルにおいて、最強のエンドツーエンドポリシーと比較してより多くのスロットを埋め、手順を完了できることを示した。

2611.31037.tldr_en: The results show that long-horizon performance depends not only on visuomotor capacity, but also on how learned skills are committed, verified, and composed.

2611.31022.title: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?
2611.31022.abstract: Omnidirectional videos (ODVs) capture dynamic environments with a full $360^\circ$ field of view, providing rich spatial context and temporal dynamics for applications such as virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and embodied intelligence. Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made great progress in spatial and temporal understanding, yet their ability to comprehend the immersive 360 spatio-temporal information conveyed by ODVs remains largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we first introduce OmniV-Bench, a Benchmark designed to comprehensively evaluate the capabilities of MLLMs on spatio-temporal Omnidirectional Video understanding. OmniV-Bench contains 4,123 high-quality ODVs collected from diverse scenes, along with 8,923 human-annotated question-answer pairs spanning 11 fine-grained tasks across three categories, i.e., general, spatial, and spatio-temporal understanding. Extensive benchmark experiments reveal that the spatio-temporal complexity of ODVs poses significant challenges for current MLLMs. To address these limitations, we further propose OmniV-Harness, an agentic harness that enhances ODV understanding through viewpoint-guided evidence initialization and task-relevant evidence acquisition with adaptive tool use. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that OmniV-Harness consistently improves immersive spatio-temporal reasoning ability of MLLMs. Both OmniV-Bench and OmniV-Harness will be released upon publication.

llm.title_ja: OmniV-Bench：MLLMは没入型時空間シーンを理解できるか？
llm.tldr_ja: 全方位動画（ODV）の時空間理解におけるマルチモーダル大規模言語モデル（MLLM）の能力を評価するためのベンチマーク「OmniV-Bench」を提案した。
llm.problem: 最新のMLLMは空間および時間的理解において大きな進歩を遂げているが、ODVが伝える没入型の360度時空間情報の理解力は未探索のままである。
llm.method: 多様なシーンから収集された4,123件の高品質ODVと8,923件の人手によるQ&AペアからなるOmniV-Benchを構築し、視点誘導型証拠初期化等を行うエージェントハーネスを提案する。
llm.result: ODVの時空間的複雑さが現在のMLLMにとって大きな課題であることを明らかにするとともに、提案するエージェントハーネスが一貫して推論能力を向上させることを示した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2611.31022.tldr_en: Omnidirectional videos understanding is improved through viewpoint-guided evidence initialization and task-relevant evidence acquisition with adaptive tool use with OmniV-Harness, an agentic harness that enhances ODV understanding through viewpoint-guided evidence initialization and task-relevant evidence acquisition with adaptive tool use.

2611.31021.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
2611.31021.abstract: Spatial reasoning across multiple views requires inferring the 3D relations between objects and the camera from 2D observations, which depends on cross-view correspondence and scene geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) do not reliably extract. Pretrained vision encoders already capture this information in their latent features, with CLIP linking objects to image regions, DINOv3 matching semantics across views, and VGGT encoding multi-view geometry. However, VLMs do not benefit from these features when we present them directly in context as grayscale feature images. We therefore propose LatentParse, a training-free framework that parses latent features into explicit spatial evidence for VLMs. In LatentParse, an analyst VLM probes the features of all three encoders with predefined tools that locate objects, track them across views, and measure motion between views. It then distills the results into a concise text report, which is provided together with the images to the VLM to answer the question. We evaluate LatentParse on MMSI-Bench, MV-RoboBench and SPAR-Bench, where it improves all five VLMs over the photo-only baseline by 0.7-2.4 percentage points on average. On MMSI-Bench, it raises Qwen3.8-27B from 34.4% to 39.5%, with the largest improvements of 19.2 percentage points on the camera-related questions. These results suggest that latent features become useful for spatial reasoning once they are parsed into relation evidence, without training. Code is available at https://github.com/Harvard-AI-and-Robotics-Lab/LatentParse.

llm.title_ja: マルチモーダル空間推論のための視覚潜在表現の解析
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みエンコーダの潜在特徴を事前定義されたツールで解析し、テキストレポートに蒸留してVLMの空間推論を強化する訓練不要のフレームワーク「LatentParse」を提案した。
llm.problem: 複数視点にわたる空間推論は2D観測からオブジェクトとカメラの3D関係を推論することに依存するが、VLMはこれを確実に抽出できない。
llm.method: アナリストVLMが、オブジェクトの位置特定や視点間の追跡を行う定義済みツールを用いて3つのエンコーダの特徴を検出し、その結果をテキストレポートとしてVLMに提供する。
llm.result: MMSI-BenchやMV-RoboBench等の評価において、写真のみのベースラインと比較して5つのVLMすべての性能を平均0.7〜2.4ポイント向上させた。

2611.31021.tldr_en: LatentParse, a training-free framework that parses latent features into explicit spatial evidence for VLMs, suggests that latent features become useful for spatial reasoning once they are parsed into relation evidence, without training.

2611.31002.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
2611.31002.abstract: Agentic Robotics, in which foundation models act as coding agents to control robots through executable programs, has emerged as a compelling paradigm for embodied intelligence. Yet unlike software engineering, where massive executable environments power post-training, robotics remains constrained by small, manual benchmarks and in-distribution evaluation. To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline. Each runs in an isolated, Harbor-compatible harness that hides privileged states and grading logic to mirror real-world sensing. From the same pipeline, we hold out 500 unseen tasks to establish RoboUniverse-Verified, an expert-verified zero-shot benchmark. Evaluating 11 closed- and open-source models reveals a huge gap: frontier models reach 85.8\% success, while open-source baselines lag at 2.6\% to 10.0\%, bottlenecked by low-level grasping, deformable-object manipulation, and post-contact physical control. Finally, we collect about 17K multi-turn trajectories totaling 0.79B tokens with GPT-6 Astra and perform full-parameter supervised fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, yielding RoboUniverse-35B-A3B. Our model achieves substantial zero-shot gains on RoboUniverse-Verified, lifting the success rate from 0.8\% to 21.2\%, while achieving zero-shot task completions across LIBERO-MAX, RoboCasa, RoboTwin 2.0, and a real Franka arm. We open-source the RL-ready environments and model to lay the foundation for large-scale reinforcement learning in Agentic Robotics.

llm.title_ja: RoboUniverse-10K：リアルからシミュレーション環境を通じたエージェントロボティクスのスケーリング時代へ
llm.tldr_ja: 実世界動画から自動構築された10,000以上のインタラクティブな物理シミュレーション環境「RoboUniverse-10K」を構築し、エージェントロボティクスのためのモデルを開発した。
llm.problem: ロボット工学は、ソフトウェア工学のような大規模な実行可能環境によるポストトレーニングが不足しており、小規模な手動ベンチマークに制約されている。
llm.method: 自動Real2Simパイプラインを用いて10,807件のインタラクティブな物理環境を構築し、GPT-6 AstraによるマルチターントラジェクトリでQwenモデルをファインチューニングする。
llm.result: 構築されたモデル（RoboUniverse-35B-A3B）は、RoboUniverse-Verifiedでのゼロショット成功率を0.8%から21.2%に引き上げ、実機のFrankaアーム等でもタスクを完了した。
keywords_ja: エージェントロボティクス
シミュレーション環境

2611.31002.tldr_en: This work introduces RoboUniverse-10K, 10,807 interactive, resettable, and verifiable physics environments built from real-world videos via an automated Real2Sim and quality assurance pipeline, and open-source the RL-ready environments and model to lay the foundation for large-scale reinforcement learning in Agentic Robotics.

2611.30997.title: Generalizing Agentic Robotics via Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
2611.30997.abstract: Building general-purpose robots is a central goal in robotics. Agentic robotics pursues this goal with planners that control robots through tool calls. However, existing methods either rely on proprietary models accessed through APIs, which incur high costs and latency, or post-train a planner with reinforcement learning (RL) in a single domain, requiring a separate specialist for each domain with incompatible tools. In large language model (LLM) post-training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) has been used to consolidate domain specialists into a single generalist. Yet whether MOPD can build a generalist planner for agentic robotics, how well it performs, and how it compares with other consolidation methods remain unexplored. In this paper, we systematically study these questions: we introduce Robo-MOPD, which trains a single student on closed-loop rollouts in simulation under token-level supervision from matching frozen specialists, and compare it with weight merging, off-policy specialist supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-domain online RL. Experiments on LIBERO-PRO and RoboCasa365 show that a single 9B Robo-MOPD planner reaches 72.9% and 44.8% success (58.9% average), surpassing all consolidated baselines in average success and both 9B specialists on their respective benchmarks. Robo-MOPD excels on long-horizon tasks, outperforming multi-domain online RL by 13.0 percentage points on LIBERO-10.

llm.title_ja: マルチ教師オンポリシー蒸留によるエージェントロボティクスの一般化
llm.tldr_ja: 複数ドメインの専門家モデルの知識を単一の汎用プランナーに統合するマルチ教師オンポリシー蒸留手法「Robo-MOPD」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のエージェントロボティクス手法は高コスト・高レイテンシなプロプライエタリAPIに依存するか、単一ドメインに限定された強化学習を用いており、ドメインごとに専門家が必要となる。
llm.method: シミュレーション内のクローズドロールアウトにおいて、一致する凍結された専門家からのトークンレベルの監督のもとで、単一の学生モデルを訓練する「Robo-MOPD」を導入する。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROおよびRoboCasa365において単一の9B Robo-MOPDプランナーが平均58.9%の成功率を達成し、すべての統合ベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: エージェントロボティクス

2611.30997.tldr_en: Robo-MOPD is introduced, which trains a single student on closed-loop rollouts in simulation under token-level supervision from matching frozen specialists, and is compared with weight merging, off-policy specialist supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-domain online RL.

2611.30989.title: WorldLeague: Benchmarking Physical Agency
2611.30989.abstract: AI systems can now operate Blender, follow instructions in complex video games, and manipulate objects with robot arms. What range of physical goals can today's AI systems achieve autonomously? Answering this question requires testing systems on tasks that demand different combinations of perception, memory, planning, and action. We introduce \textbf{WorldLeague}, a benchmark that compares AI systems on a common set of \textbf{60 simulated robot tasks} by measuring progress toward each task's physical goal from the robot's trajectory. Robots explore scenes to gather evidence in \textbf{WorldSeek}, rearrange objects in \textbf{WorldShape}, and adapt to changes in \textbf{WorldShift}. Tying these goals to a single control interface limits which AI systems can be compared. In WorldLeague, vision-language models (VLMs) choose targets and motions, while vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs) use their native controls. For each of six capability dimensions, we measure how much progress a system makes toward its goals (Interactive Score) and how often it achieves them (physical success rate). Together, these measures form the system's \emph{Physical Agency Profile}. Among 13 representative AI systems, Claude Fable 5.2 achieves 13 of the 60 goals and earns the highest mean Interactive Score (28.58/100). Fable leads in four dimensions, while GPT-6.1-Sol and GPT-6-Astra tie for first on rule-following tasks. Even when VLMs answer every final question correctly, they receive an Interactive Score of zero in 71.8\% of those episodes. WorldLeague gives Embodied AI, Physical AI, and Agentic AI a shared basis for comparing what AI systems achieve autonomously, from partial progress toward a physical goal to full goal completion. Project Webpage: https://xyangzhou.github.io/WorldLeague
2611.30989.hf_summary_en: WorldLeague benchmarks 13 AI systems on 60 simulated robot tasks spanning exploration, rearrangement, and adaptation, measuring progress and success to compare autonomous physical goal achievement.

llm.title_ja: WorldLeague：物理的エージェンシーのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: WorldLeagueは、探索、再配置、適応にわたる60のシミュレートされたロボットタスクで13のAIシステムをベンチマークし、進捗状況と成功率を測定して自律的な物理的ゴールの達成度を比較する。
llm.problem: 多様な知覚、記憶、計画、行動の組み合わせを要求するタスクでAIシステムの物理的ゴールの達成度をテストする必要性
llm.method: 60のシミュレートされたロボットタスクにおける物理的目標への進捗をロボットの軌跡から測定する共通ベンチマークWorldLeagueの導入
llm.result: Claude Fable 5.2が60目標中13を達成し、最高平均インタラクティブスコア（28.58/100）を獲得した
keywords_ja: 物理的エージェンシー

2611.30989.tldr_en: WorldLeague gives Embodied AI, Physical AI, and Agentic AI a shared basis for comparing what AI systems achieve autonomously, from partial progress toward a physical goal to full goal completion.

2611.30963.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
2611.30963.abstract: Robotic manipulation policies can improve action prediction by anticipating how objects move and how their spatial relationships change. World Action Models (WAMs) learn to predict future visual observations, but their training objectives typically leave the underlying 3D geometric transitions implicit. To alleviate this problem, we introduce Foresight Forcing ($\mathcal{F}^{2}$), a WAM that learns a spatial transition representation from changes in a pretrained 3D feature space. During training, a frozen 3D foundation model extracts patch-wise feature differences from aligned current and future observations that provide dense supervision for geometry-aware feature transitions. We distill these targets into spatial transition queries, which are progressively refined from the current observation, language instruction, and proprioceptive state, and use them alongside current visual features to generate actions. At deployment, the policy predicts the queries without future observations or the 3D teacher. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin2.0 demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved robustness, including 95.01% average success on RoboTwin2.0 Full. On six real-world manipulation tasks, $\mathcal{F}^{2}$ achieves a mean task score of 85.8%.

llm.title_ja: Foresight Forcing：ロボットマニピュレーションのための空間的先読み学習
llm.tldr_ja: Foresight Forcingは、事前学習済み3D特徴空間の変化から空間遷移表現を学習するWAMであり、多様なロボットマニピュレーションタスクで高い性能と頑健性を実証した。
llm.problem: WAMの訓練目的が背後にある3D幾何学的遷移を暗黙的なままにしていること
llm.method: 事前学習済み3D基礎モデルからパッチごとの特徴差分を利用して幾何学を意識した特徴遷移の密な指導を提供するForesight Forcing（F^2）の導入
llm.result: RoboTwin2.0 Fullで平均95.01%の成功率を示し、6つの実世界マニピュレーションタスクで平均85.8%のタスクスコアを達成した
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション
世界アクションモデル

2611.30963.tldr_en: Foresight Forcing is introduced, a WAM that learns a spatial transition representation from changes in a pretrained 3D feature space that is progressively refined from the current observation, language instruction, and proprioceptive state and used alongside current visual features to generate actions.
2611.30963.hf_summary_en: Foresight Forcing distills geometry-aware spatial transition queries from a frozen 3D foundation model to improve robotic manipulation action prediction without requiring future observations at deployment.

2611.30957.title: SayDo: Benchmarking the Safety of Frontier Models from Chat to Closed-Loop Robot Control
2611.30957.abstract: Frontier vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used as high-level robot controllers, yet their safety is evaluated almost entirely in text. We introduce SayDo, a benchmark that assesses the propensity of frontier models to cause harm in embodied contexts. SayDo comprises eleven laboratory and household tasks that pair a benign instruction with a hazard latent in the scene. Tasks are implemented in six settings along an embodiment gradient, from chat questions about an imagined robot to closed-loop control of a simulated robot arm. Benign controls, safe-alternative variants and scripted operator pushback complement each task. Across six open- and closed-weight VLMs and 11,480 episodes, hazardous-action rates rise from 14% in chat to 47% in the simulator, and from 2% to 80% for the most affected model. The increase is largely driven by open-weight models. We find that models flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes and give way to pushback about twice as often when controlling robots as in chat. The safest models also show signs of overcaution on benign controls. Safety evaluations run in text therefore do not predict the safety behavior of the same models when used as robot controllers.

llm.title_ja: SayDo：チャットから閉ループロボット制御までのフロンティアモデルの安全性ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: SayDoは、無害な指示と危険性を対にした11の実験室・家庭内タスクを通じて、体現化された文脈におけるフロンティアモデルの危害を及ぼす傾向を評価する。
llm.problem: フロンティア視覚言語モデル（VLM）がロボットの高レベルコントローラーとして使用されているにもかかわらず、その安全性がほとんどテキストのみで評価されていること
llm.method: チャットの質問からシミュレートされたロボットアームの閉ループ制御に至るまでの体現化の勾配に沿った11のタスクを含むSayDoベンチマークの導入
llm.result: 危険な行動の割合がチャットでの14%からシミュレーターでの47%へと増加し、オープンウェイトモデルで顕著であった

2611.30957.tldr_en: SayDo is introduced, a benchmark that assesses the propensity of frontier models to cause harm in embodied contexts and flag hazards before acting in 73% of unsafe episodes and give way to pushback about twice as often when controlling robots as in chat.

2611.30928.title: Personalization of a Commercial Powered Knee Prosthesis Under Clinically Realistic Conditions via Reinforcement Learning: A Feasibility Study
2611.30928.abstract: Personalization of powered prosthesis control to individual user needs remains a significant challenge. To address this challenge, policy iteration with constraint embedded (PICE), a reinforcement learning (RL) tuning approach, has been developed and validated. This feasibility study investigated whether the developed approach can personalize a commercial powered knee prosthesis under clinically realistic conditions. To reduce the time for personalization, tuning was initialized with a policy learned offline from one non-disabled participant walking on a treadmill and was then applied to three other non-disabled participants walking with the knee through a bypass adapter on a 5-meter walkway. All participants reached the goal within 8-18 tuning steps (1.7-4.2 minutes of walking), reducing the knee-kinematic feature error by 64-90% on average. These results support the feasibility of implementing the RL-based tuning approach in clinically realistic conditions with space and equipment constraints.

llm.title_ja: 強化学習による臨床的に現実的な条件下での商用動力付き膝プロテーゼのパーソナライゼーション：実現可能性調査
llm.tldr_ja: PICEという強化学習チューニングアプローチを用いることで、空間や設備の制約がある臨床的に現実的な条件下でも商用動力付き膝プロテーゼを迅速にパーソナライズできることを示した。
llm.problem: 個々のユーザーのニーズに合わせて動力付きプロテーゼの制御をパーソナライズすることの難しさ
llm.method: 制約を組み込んだポリシー反復（PICE）という強化学習チューニングアプローチを臨床的に現実的な条件下で適用・検証する
llm.result: 全参加者が8〜18回のチューニングステップで目標に到達し、膝の運動学的特徴の誤差を平均64〜90%削減した
keywords_ja: 動力付き膝プロテーゼ
パーソナライゼーション

2611.30928.tldr_en: The results of this feasibility study support the feasibility of implementing the RL-based tuning approach in clinically realistic conditions with space and equipment constraints.

2611.30918.title: CoSel: Cooperation as Selection for End-to-End Driving
2611.30918.abstract: Cooperative driving can extend a vehicle's awareness beyond its own sensors, but existing cooperative end-to-end methods inject shared information into the planner and rely on cooperative driving demonstrations to learn how to use it. The moments in which shared information should change a driving decision are rare in such data, providing limited supervision for learning this behavior. We argue that cooperation need not be learned by the planner. Instead, reacting to shared information requires predicting how surrounding agents will move and selecting a response from the candidate trajectories of an ego planner. We introduce CoSel, a cooperation-as-selection framework that leaves the planner and its ego-only input unchanged. A separately trained cooperative predictor uses observations from the ego vehicle, roadside units, and connected automated vehicles to predict surrounding agents and their future motion. CoSel evaluates the planner's candidate trajectories against these predictions, preserves the planner's choice when it remains safe, and selects the closest safe alternative when shared information reveals additional risk. Each safety intervention is traceable to the shared evidence that triggers it. In closed-loop evaluation, CoSel achieves a driving score of 70.7 on V2Xverse, outperforming the best compared cooperative method by 7.5 points, and the highest average driving score of 85.8 on MDrive. Under missing ego detections, the collision count of CoSel increases only from 17 to 19 in 72 scenarios, compared with 19 to 32 for an existing cooperative end-to-end model.

llm.title_ja: CoSel：エンドツーエンド自動運転のための選択としての協調
llm.tldr_ja: CoSelは、周囲のエージェントの動きを予測して自己プランナーの候補軌跡と比較し、追加のリスクが検出された際に安全な代替案を選択する協調フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 協調的エンドツーエンド手法において共有情報を利用する方法を学習するための指導データが不足していること
llm.method: プランナーを変更せず、周囲の予測に基づいて候補軌跡を評価し安全な代替案を選択する協調・アズ・セレクションフレームワーク（CoSel）の導入
llm.result: V2Xverseで70.7の運転スコアを達成し、MDriveで最高平均運転スコア85.8を記録した

2611.30918.tldr_en: CoSel is introduced, a cooperation-as-selection framework that leaves the planner and its ego-only input unchanged and preserves the planner's choice when it remains safe, and selects the closest safe alternative when shared information reveals additional risk.

2611.30907.title: DexLatentWorld: 3D Cross-Embodiment Latent Action World Models for Zero-Shot Robotic Manipulation
2611.30907.abstract: World models facilitate planning and control in robotic manipulation by enabling agents to anticipate the consequences of their actions. However, they typically rely on action-labelled interaction data that is costly to acquire and difficult to scale. These models are also often tied to the specific embodiment they were trained on, limiting transferability to previously unseen robot morphologies. We introduce a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations. A contrastive objective is used to encourage consistent representations of motion across embodiments. The resulting unified latent action space serves directly as the search space for model-predictive control, where sampled latent actions condition particle-based future predictions. Executable robot commands are then recovered from the predicted geometric motion without requiring an embodiment-specific action decoder. Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that the learned latent actions exhibit controllable and compositional motion, transfer to unseen robot embodiments, and support zero-shot manipulation with unseen gripper geometries. Following task-agnostic adaptation, our model achieves 90%, 92%, and 60% success on reaching, grasping, and placing, respectively, compared with DexWM's reported 72%, 58%, and 28%. Finally, we demonstrate zero-shot real-world manipulation with an unseen dexterous hand, achieving an 86% success rate across 50 trials on five diverse tasks involving pushing, grasping, and lifting everyday objects. These results highlight the potential of geometry-grounded latent actions as a unified, transferable interface for world-model-based robotic manipulation. Project materials, including demonstration videos and source code, are available at https://vinaymohan0409.github.io/DexLatentWorld/.

llm.title_ja: DexLatentWorld：ゼロショットロボットマニピュレーションのための3Dクロスエンボディメント潜在行動世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: DexLatentWorldは、人間のマニピュレーション実演の点群観測から連続的な行動表現を直接学習する3D潜在行動世界モデルであり、未見のロボット形状へのゼロショット転移を可能にする。
llm.problem: 既存の世界モデルがコストのかかる行動ラベル付きインタラクションデータや特定のエンボディメントに依存していること
llm.method: 人間の実演の点群観測から連続行動表現を学習し、対比学習目的関数で一貫した表現を促す3D潜在行動世界モデルの導入
llm.result: 未見の器用な手を用いたゼロショット実世界マニピュレーションで、5つの多様なタスクにわたり50試行中86%の成功率を達成した
keywords_ja: クロスエンボディメント
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.30907.tldr_en: A 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations and exhibits controllable and compositional motion, transfer to unseen robot embodiments, and support zero-shot manipulation with unseen gripper geometries is introduced.

2611.30900.title: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind
2611.30900.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). However, most of them encode a sample of past frames again at every decision and are trained on isolated decisions, so computation is redundant and the usable history is short. They also learn from their own mistakes through outcome rewards that give one scalar to a whole episode. We ask whether a navigator can encode each frame only once, at a constant cost per step, and still remember what matters and learn efficiently from its mistakes. We present GlanceNav, a streaming navigator built on a hybrid MLLM. Its Gated DeltaNet layers carry a recurrent state through the whole episode, while its attention layers keep a short window of recent observations and a small bank of keyframes, selected by how much each frame changes the recurrent state. This constant-size memory keeps the cost per step fixed and allows training on whole episodes with the same memory as at inference. Because the entire memory can also be copied in constant time, we further propose Counterfactual Rewind (CoRe), a reinforcement learning stage that rewinds a drifting rollout to its closest approach to the goal, lets an expert correct a few actions, and credits decisions by the resulting change in outcome. Trained only on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE training splits, with 1,000 instructions for reinforcement learning, a 4B GlanceNav reaches success rates of 71.9% and 73.6% on R2R-CE and RxR-CE val-unseen. On R2R-CE, it outperforms the strongest previous single-RGB method trained without external data by 9.1 points, while running at 104 ms per step.

llm.result: R2R-CEおよびRxR-CEのval-unseenでそれぞれ71.9%および73.6%の成功率を達成し、1ステップあたり104 msで動作した
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2611.30898.title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
2611.30898.abstract: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model. Native LAM operates one pretrained video diffusion transformer as both IDM and FDM, with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge between the two, and trains on counterfactual temporal pairs that differ in motion alone, so that the registers distill a video's dynamics into a compact native latent action. We further propose a pretraining paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, Pretraining Actions from World models (PAWlicy), in which Native LAM serves as a dynamics teacher on large-scale video; unlike world action models, it never generates video. Native latent actions outperform existing LAMs on the LARY benchmark in both action classification and control regression, and replay the same motion on new robots, in new scenes, and from human hands to robots, although no transfer objective is used in training. With a 3.8B model, PAWlicy reaches a 93.6% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 trained with domain-randomized demonstrations, the highest among VLAs. On RoboDojo, it is competitive on every dimension we evaluate, and its Precision, evaluated by us, is on par with the leading leaderboard entries. On real robots, it improves over the pi_0.5 baseline on both tasks. Both stages use only public data and a publicly released world model.
2611.30898.comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, 6 tables. Project page: https://pawteam-eai.github.io/native-lam/
2611.30898.hf_summary_en: Native LAM distills compact latent actions from a pretrained video diffusion transformer via learnable dynamics registers, and PAWlicy uses these actions to pretrain VLA policies without generating video, achieving strong robotic control and cross-embodiment transfer.

llm.title_ja: ネイティブ潜在行動モデルとしての世界モデル

2611.30889.title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Surprisingly Effective In-Context Robot Learners
2611.30889.abstract: Can foundation models pretrained for generic numerical prediction serve as in-context robot learners? We investigate this question through tabular foundation models (TFMs), which are pretrained to infer input-output relationships from labeled examples in context. We introduce TabAct, which casts visual imitation as numerical prediction: frozen visual features and robot proprioception form the inputs, future action chunks form the targets, and each demonstration time step provides one labeled example that conditions a frozen TFM for closed-loop control. The predictor receives no robot-specific training or target-task fine-tuning. With one target-task demonstration available to each method, TabAct with TabICLv2 achieves the highest average success among all evaluated methods on both LIBERO and Meta-World, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.9 and 5.8 percentage points, respectively. Additional demonstrations improve control without updating model weights: with five demonstrations, success reaches 94.2% on LIBERO-Object. These results demonstrate that generic numerical pretraining can provide an effective foundation for in-context robot learning.

llm.title_ja: 表形式基盤モデルは文脈内ロボット学習において驚くほど効果的である
llm.tldr_ja: TabActは視覚的模倣を数値予測に変換することで、事前学習された表形式基盤モデルをロボットの文脈内学習に活用し、LIBEROやMeta-Worldで高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 一般的な数値予測のために事前学習された基盤モデルを文脈内ロボット学習に活用できるかという課題
llm.method: 視覚的特徴と固有受容感覚を入力、将来の行動チャンクをターゲットとする数値予測として視覚模倣をキャストするTabActの導入
llm.result: LIBEROおよびMeta-Worldで既存の最強ベースラインをそれぞれ20.9および5.8パーセンテージポイント上回る平均成功率を達成した

2611.30889.tldr_en: TabAct is introduced, which casts visual imitation as numerical prediction: frozen visual features and robot proprioception form the inputs, future action chunks form the targets, and each demonstration time step provides one labeled example that conditions a frozen TFM for closed-loop control.

2611.30874.title: Bridging Continuous-Time MAPF and Industrial AGV Fleet Coordination with Lazy Priority-Based Search
2611.30874.abstract: Continuous-time multi-agent path finding on roadmaps (MAPF$_R$) offers a principled way to coordinate robot fleets with geometric collision avoidance, yet its deployment on industrial automated guided vehicle (AGV) infrastructures remains challenging, as highly connected and redundant roadmaps amplify both safe-interval reasoning and multi-agent interaction handling. To bridge this gap, we formalize AGV-MAPF$_R$-CTC, a configuration-space variant of MAPF$_R$ with precomputed continuous-time conflicts that enables the reuse of MAPF$_R$ solvers for AGV fleet coordination with minimal changes. We then revisit continuous-time priority-based search (CPBS), identifying the boundary conditions required by its safe interval path planning (SIPP) low-level planner under priority-induced constraints and enabling earlier solution detection. As a central contribution, we analyze the structure of the priority search space, clarifying which agents are affected by each priority refinement and when replanning can be avoided. Building on this analysis, we introduce a novel algorithm, Lazy-CPBS, which materializes high-level nodes lazily: a child's plans are computed only when it is expanded, so siblings that are never expanded cost no low-level search. Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks and on industrial AGV roadmaps imported from a proprietary digital-twin simulator show that CPBS-based solvers remain effective well beyond the agent counts reachable by optimal MAPF$_R$ solvers, while Lazy-CPBS substantially reduces CPBS overhead and offers the most consistent robustness/runtime trade-off across industrial layouts.
2611.30874.comment: 18 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems

llm.title_ja: 遅延優先度ベース探索による連続時間MAPFと産業用AGVフリート調整の架け橋
llm.tldr_ja: AGV-MAPF_R-CTCの定式化とLazy-CPBSアルゴリズムの導入により、複雑な産業用ロードマップ上で多数のエージェントを効率的かつ確実に調整できることを示した。
llm.problem: 連続時間マルチエージェント経路探索（MAPF_R）を産業用の無人搬送車（AGV）インフラに展開する際の複雑な安全区間推論とマルチエージェント干渉の処理の難しさ
llm.method: 事前計算された連続時間衝突を持つ構成空間バリアントAGV-MAPF_R-CTCの定式化と、高レベルノードを遅延評価するLazy-CPBSアルゴリズムの開発

keywords_ja: マルチエージェント経路探索

2611.30836.title: Can Multimodal Fusion MakeSense for Embodied Vision in Degraded Sensing?
2611.30836.abstract: Embodied vision systems rely on complementary sensors to perceive and act as conditions change. Even models that accept arbitrary sensor subsets can exhibit negative fusion: adding a sensor increases prediction error. We propose MakeSense, a multimodal fusion framework that preserves sensor-specific evidence in private streams and combines information through shared bottleneck tokens. Training pairs full and subset views of the same degraded observations, penalizing higher error with more sensors. Where geometry permits, the distance readout uses range measurements alone, while the rest of the prediction draws on all available inputs. Paired tests across five datasets reveal helpful and harmful sensor additions. MakeSense reduces negative fusion on MM-Fi. With lightweight adapters and per-dataset training, the same design improves UAV localization on MMAUD, cooperative 3D detection on V2X-Real, few-shot pose transfer to RELI11D, and command prediction on Humanoid-Everyday, where a world model trained on the frozen core's outputs forecasts future fused states more accurately than a linear baseline at longer tested horizons. MakeSense supports embodied sensing across human activity, aerial systems, robotics, and autonomous driving.

llm.title_ja: マルチモーダル融合は劣化したセンシングにおける体現化視覚にとって意味があるのか？
llm.tldr_ja: MakeSenseは、プライベートストリームでセンサー固有の証拠を保持し共有ボトルネックトークンを介して情報を組み合わせることで、センサー追加による予測誤差の増加を防ぐマルチモーダル融合フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 体現化視覚システムにおいて、センサーを追加することが逆に予測誤差を増加させる「負の融合」が発生すること
llm.method: センサー固有の証拠をプライベートストリームに保持し、共有ボトルネックトークンを介して情報を結合するMakeSenseフレームワークの提案
llm.result: MM-Fiにおける負の融合を削減し、UAVのローカリゼーションや協調3D検出などのタスクで性能を向上させた
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.30813.title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
2611.30813.abstract: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.
2611.30813.hf_summary_en: A shared flow-matching policy that reads dense patch tokens from multiple vision encoders improves success on egocentric bimanual tasks, and inverse-dynamics readout of commanded motion is a strong pre-training signal, while recognition, depth, and correspondence transfer unreliably.

llm.title_ja: HIVE-Bench：エゴセントリックロボットマニピュレーションに向けたパッチレベル視覚表現の評価

llm.method: 7つのファミリーから得られた20のエンコーダーのパッチトークンを共有フローマッチングポリシーで読み取るHIVE-Benchの導入

2611.30784.title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
2611.30784.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

llm.title_ja: ドメインランダム化を超えて：学習されたダイナミクスにおける脚式ロボットの実世界ポリシー適応
llm.tldr_ja: 学習されたダイナミクスモデルをデプロイ先の目標条件に適応させるフレームワークを提案し、極端な物理的変動下でも歩行タスクで優れた適応性を示した。
llm.problem: 静的なドメインランダム化で訓練された強化学習ポリシーが、ペイロードの変化や摩擦の変動などの未モデル化された動的変動に対して性能低下を起こすこと
llm.method: ポリシーとダイナミクスモデルの両方に教師・生徒パラダイムを適用し、学習されたダイナミクスモデルをオンポリシー強化学習パイプラインに統合するフレームワークの提案
llm.result: 自重の80%に達するペイロードや油潤滑された低摩擦面などの極端な物理的変動下で競争力のある適応性を示した

2611.30784.tldr_en: This work proposes a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model.

2611.30777.title: AvatarAnyone: Agentic Reconstruction of Mesh-Based Layered Avatars from YouTube Video
2611.30777.abstract: We introduce AvatarAnyone, a method for reconstructing avatars from casual YouTube videos as layered meshes, with each garment and footwear as a separate mesh layered on top of the body mesh. In such videos, people differ in garment classes, clothing types, and layers, and each combination needs a different reconstruction. A single fixed layered reconstruction pipeline therefore fails. AvatarAnyone solves this problem with AI agents that plan a custom optimization for each person's reconstruction. The agents predict the garment classes, the clothing type, and the layering. They use these predictions to choose an initialization and stage the optimization. Because the avatars are layered meshes, they support applications such as virtual try-on and cloth simulation. We change the clothing layers of an avatar and render it in different garments and poses. We can also simulate a clothing layer as cloth over the animated body with a standard cloth simulator. Most existing avatars are one fused surface or a set of Gaussians and cannot do this. We load the avatars directly into Blender, Unreal Engine, and robotics simulators such as MuJoCo. As the avatars are meshes, they support contact modeling with other objects. We show results from around 150 YouTube videos. On four datasets, AvatarAnyone outperforms existing mesh-based methods for animatable monocular reconstruction. Our project page is available at https://miraymen.github.io/avataranyone.

llm.title_ja: AvatarAnyone：YouTubeビデオからのメッシュベース階層型アバターのエージェント的再構築
llm.tldr_ja: AvatarAnyoneは、AIエージェントを用いて各人物のカスタム最適化を計画することで、YouTubeのカジュアル動画から衣服や履物がレイヤーとして分かれたメッシュベースの階層型アバターを再構築する。
llm.problem: 多様な衣類のクラスや種類、レイヤーを持つカジュアルなYouTube動画の人々に対して、単一の固定された階層型再構築パイプラインが失敗すること
llm.method: AIエージェントが衣類のクラス、種類、重ね着を予測し、カスタム最適化を計画して初期化とステージングを行う手法の提案
llm.result: 約150本のYouTubeビデオを用いた実験で、アニメーション可能な単眼再構築において既存のメッシュベース手法を上回る性能を示した

2611.30765.title: Object Count Generalization Is an Interface Problem: Warping a Frozen Skill Instead of Retraining It
2611.30765.abstract: Reinforcement learning policies for robot manipulation degrade when the number of objects N in the scene grows beyond the training range. This is a covariate shift that also changes the dimension of the state. We propose WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights. WAVE has three parts. First, a selection policy picks the one object the robot works on next. Second, a warping policy reads a local view of the scene around that object, whose size does not depend on N. It emits a multiplier and an offset for every quantity the skill reads and every action it outputs. Third, the skill acts under this affine warp. It is shown a scene that holds a single object, while the warp steers it around the objects it is not shown and edits the actions that are sent to the robot. Both the selection and warping policies are trained with PPO on the multi-object reward and use the skill as a black box, so WAVE is task-general and skill-agnostic. It requires only that the skill was trained on the same embodiment and that every object has a goal pose. We also bound the number of attempts needed to place all N objects, assuming positive expected net progress per attempt, and measure this progress for each object count. We evaluate WAVE on cube arrangement tasks with a gantry robot and with a Franka Panda arm. Trained with at most nine cubes, it generalizes zero-shot to several times its training count, on the gantry to scenes of up to thirty cubes. Published methods that learn multi-object manipulation show count generalization up to six objects. Fine-tuning the skill, learning from the same local view without it, and an entity transformer, even when distilled from the pretrained skill, all collapse within their training counts under the same training budget.
2611.30765.comment: 37 pages, 15 figures, 15 tables. Submitted to International Conference on Learning Representations 2027. Code, videos and full results are available at https://hhi-robot-learning.github.io/wave-website/

llm.title_ja: オブジェクト数の一般化はインターフェースの問題である：スキルを再学習する代わりに凍結されたスキルをワープする
llm.tldr_ja: WAVEは、単一オブジェクト用の事前学習済みスキルを重みの更新なしで多数のオブジェクトに拡張する選択ポリシーとワーピングポリシーを提案し、ゼロショットでの個数一般化を実現した。
llm.problem: トレーニング範囲を超えてオブジェクト数Nが増加した際にロボットマニピュレーション用の強化学習ポリシーが劣化すること
llm.method: 単一オブジェクトの周囲の局所的なビューを読み取りスキルへの入出力を編集するアフィンワープを適用するWAVE（Warping Actions and Views of an Expert）フレームワークの導入
llm.result: 最大9個のキューブで訓練され、最大30個のキューブのシーンに対してゼロショットで一般化できることを示した

keywords_ja: オブジェクト数一般化

2611.30765.tldr_en: WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights, is proposed, which requires only that the skill was trained on the same embodiment and that every object has a goal pose.

2611.30741.title: Place-Revisit Consistency Evaluation of Reference Poses
2611.30741.abstract: Reference trajectories are widely used to evaluate odometry and simultaneous localization and mapping systems. However, local inconsistencies in benchmark reference poses can bias such evaluations. This paper presents a place-revisit consistency evaluation method for reference poses in mobile sensing datasets. When a platform revisits a previously observed place after a sufficient temporal gap, the relative pose implied by the reference trajectory should agree with relative poses estimated directly from onboard sensors. We instantiate this idea with lidar scan registration and stereo-image pose estimation, and apply it to the KITTI Odometry and SNAIL Radar. The KITTI analysis identifies several revisit regions where the public reference poses disagree with sensor-derived relative poses, with median translation discrepancies up to 6.60 m. Representative point-cloud overlays further localize these discrepancies and support the use of place revisits as a benchmark-validation tool.
2611.30741.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, LBS 2026 Nanjing China

llm.title_ja: 参照ポーズの場所再訪一貫性評価
llm.tldr_ja: モバイルセンシングデータセットにおいて、プラットフォームが同じ場所を再訪した際のセンサー推定値と参照軌跡の相対ポーズの不一致を利用して参照ポーズを検証する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: ベンチマークの参照ポーズにおける局所的な一貫性の欠如がオドメトリやSLAMシステムの評価にバイアスを与えること
llm.method: LiDARスキャン登録とステレオ画像ポーズ推定を用いて、場所再訪時のセンサー推定相対ポーズと参照軌跡を比較する場所再訪一貫性評価手法の導入

2611.30739.title: Coordinating Perception and Planning for Test-Time Adaptation in End-to-End Driving under Distribution Shifts
2611.30739.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved significant milestones, yet its reliance on the i.i.d. assumption renders it vulnerable to real-world distribution shifts. While Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) offers a promising paradigm for on-the-fly enhancement, its application to driving is hindered by two barriers: (i) multi-task adaptation dependency, where updates to upstream perception also affect downstream planning, while perception confidence alone does not directly assess these downstream effects; and (ii) continuous adaptation instability, where recursive online updates over long horizons cause compounding parameter drift. To address these challenges, we propose P2-TTA, a plug-and-play TTA framework for the continual adaptation of end-to-end driving models. P2-TTA coordinates adaptation through a joint objective combining perception entropy minimization with a retrospective temporal planning consistency objective derived from observed ego motion. To stabilize online updates, we use an EMA teacher as a moving parameter reference and reject candidate updates that increase historical planning loss. Extensive experiments across multiple models demonstrate that, by updating an average of 0.11 per mille of parameters with an average adaptation time of 19.9 ms on different backbones, P2-TTA achieves average recovery rates of 36.4%, 30.0%, and 9.3% for L2, collision rate, and PDMS, respectively, under severe distribution shifts. Under a shared perception-planning objective, P2-TTA achieves the highest L2 and collision recovery among the compared TTA baselines on UniAD.

llm.title_ja: 分布シフト下のエンドツーエンド自動運転におけるテスト時適応のための知覚と計画の協調
llm.tldr_ja: P2-TTAは、知覚のエントロピー最小化と観察された自己の動きから得られる遡及的時間的計画一貫性目的を組み合わせることで、エンドツーエンド自動運転モデルを継続的に適応させるフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 実世界の分布シフトに脆弱なエンドツーエンド自動運転において、知覚と下流の計画のマルチタスク適応依存性と継続的適応の不安定性という2つの障壁が存在すること
llm.method: 知覚エントロピー最小化と遡及的時間的計画一貫性を統合した共同目的関数を使用し、EMA教師モデルでオンライン更新を安定化させるP2-TTAフレームワークの提案
llm.result: 重大な分布シフト下において、L2誤差、衝突率、PDMSの平均回復率がそれぞれ36.4%、30.0%、9.3%を達成した
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド自動運転

2611.30739.tldr_en: P2-TTA coordinates adaptation through a joint objective combining perception entropy minimization with a retrospective temporal planning consistency objective derived from observed ego motion, and achieves the highest L2 and collision recovery among the compared TTA baselines on UniAD.

2611.30734.title: EgoDepth-Bench: Benchmarking Metric Depth for Egocentric Manipulation
2611.30734.abstract: We introduce EgoDepth-Bench, comprising 941,233 synchronized samples collected across 37 distinct physical environments. Each sample combines six calibrated RGB views with metric depth in the native fisheye view, reconstructed from five active-infrared stereo modules. A calibrated ball-bar confirms millimeter-level geometric accuracy, with a median error of 1.27 mm on a known sphere spacing. Environment-held-out splits enable evaluation of generalization to unseen environments. Across monocular, stereo, and multi-view models, the benchmark measures both depth accuracy and prediction coverage, including on hands and objects. Fine-tuning MapAnything on EgoDepth-Bench reduces metric AbsRel from 0.708 to 0.091 and scale-aligned AbsRel from 0.327 to 0.072 on unseen environments. These results demonstrate that EgoDepth-Bench provides effective supervision and enables rigorous evaluation of metric and relative depth estimation in egocentric manipulation. The project page provides the evaluation code and interactive RGB-depth sequences.
2611.30734.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Project page: https://egodepth-bench.github.io/

llm.title_ja: EgoDepth-Bench：エゴセントリックマニピュレーションのためのメトリック深度ベンチマーク

2611.30667.title: LLM-Guided Compositional Continual Learning for Robot Manipulation with Gated Low-Rank Experts
2611.30667.abstract: General-purpose manipulation robots must acquire new skills over time without forgetting prior ones or retraining from scratch. We present a continual learning framework that represents each skill as a dedicated expert sub- network in a Progressive Neural Network (PNN). New tasks reuse prior knowledge through low-rank adaptation (LoRA) modules on lateral connections controlled by learnable per-parent gates, enabling explicit attenuation of individual transfer paths while reducing the parameter cost of dense PNN laterals. For long-horizon deployment, a frozen local large language model decomposes natural-language instructions into sub-tasks, routes them to suitable experts, and requests a new expert only when the library is insufficient. Using a shared task-space action interface, we evaluate the framework on twelve MetaWorld tasks and in a Sawyer-to-Panda-to-UR5e cross-embodiment transfer experiment, showing improved task success relative to learning from scratch when demonstrations are limited. Real-robot manipulation experiments further demonstrate that the proposed framework supports compositional execution and expert orchestration.

llm.title_ja: ゲート付き低ランク専門家を用いたロボットマニピュレーションのためのLLM誘導型構成的継続学習
llm.tldr_ja: 過去のスキルを忘れることなく新しいスキルを効率的に獲得するため、LLMによるタスク分解とPNNベースの低ランク適応を組み合わせた継続学習フレームワークを提案し、限定されたデモンストレーションにおいてタスク成功率の向証とクロスエンボディメント転移を実現した。

llm.method: 学習可能なゲートで制御される低ランク適応（LoRA）モジュールを備えたPNNと、言語指示を部分タスクに分解して適切な専門家に割り当てる凍結されたローカルLLMを活用する。
llm.result: 12個のMetaWorldタスクおよび異種ロボット間のクロスエンボディメント転移実験において、限定されたデモンストレーションからのゼロからの学習と比較してタスク成功率が向上した。

2611.30667.tldr_en: A continual learning framework that represents each skill as a dedicated expert sub- network in a Progressive Neural Network in a Progressive Neural Network is presented, showing improved task success relative to learning from scratch when demonstrations are limited.

2611.30659.title: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics
2611.30659.abstract: Learning how actions change visual states is essential for prediction and decision-making in embodied tasks. Existing action-conditioned JEPA world models typically predict future representations at discrete observation intervals, leaving the temporal evolution of action effects implicit. We introduce ActField, a continuous-time JEPA world model that explicitly models latent state evolution through an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time. ActField separates action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss further support accurate long-horizon prediction. Together, these components provide a structured and temporally continuous formulation for predicting action-conditioned visual dynamics. Experiments across LIBERO, DROID, and BEHAVIOR demonstrate improved visual prediction fidelity and more accurate action-induced motion prediction over existing world models. Further evaluations on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate the utility of ActField in improving downstream policy planning through VLM-guided action selection.

llm.title_ja: ActField：連続時間潜在ダイナミクスとしての行動効果の学習
llm.tldr_ja: ActFieldは、物理的時間にわたって積分された行動条件付きベクトル場を通じて潜在状態の進化を明示的にモデル化する連続時間JEPA世界モデルであり、長期的予測の精度を向上させる。
llm.problem: 既存の行動条件付きJEPA世界モデルが離散的な観察間隔で将来の表現を予測し、行動効果の時間的進化を暗黙的なままにしていること
llm.method: 行動に依存しない進化と行動起因の変化を分離し、物理的時間にわたって積分されるベクトル場を用いる連続時間JEPA世界モデル（ActField）の提案
llm.result: LIBERO、DROID、BEHAVIORにおいて、既存の世界モデルよりも優れた視覚的予測忠実度と行動起因のモーション予測精度を実証した

2611.30659.tldr_en: ActField is introduced, a continuous-time JEPA world model that explicitly models latent state evolution through an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time, separating action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context.

2611.30658.title: Active Observation for Robust Visual Servoing in Robotic Manipulation
2611.30658.abstract: Robust visual servoing during robotic grasping remains challenging, as approach-phase occlusion frequently disrupts closed-loop control. To address this, we present an active observation framework in which one arm of an existing dual-arm platform carries an RGB-D camera as an active observer while the other executes grasping. The observer repositions to maintain or recover a shared target-gripper view within the feasible shared-view workspace. Occlusion during the final approach is particularly acute: fixed eye-to-hand lacks an active recovery mechanism once the target is hidden, while eye-in-hand can suffer from self-occlusion and sensitivity to hand-eye calibration. The observer first uses an active two-phase viewpoint strategy to align high-precision RGB-D axes with task-relevant error components. If visibility later degrades, an occlusion-triggered exploration module pauses the worker arm and scores candidate viewpoints by observation quality to recover a shared target-gripper view. Because both objects are detected in a single RGB-D image, the resulting Relative Servo Error avoids differencing two independently transformed target and gripper estimates. We evaluate the system on a dual 6-DoF Piper platform using an open-vocabulary detector with text prompts, without task-specific fine-tuning or demonstrations. Across 50 randomized trials per object, the system achieves 94% grasp success versus 76% for a reactive viewpoint baseline and 64% for a fixed camera. On triggered severe-occlusion trials, recovery takes $1.8 \pm 0.6$ s on average.

2611.30646.title: Part-wise Certified State Estimation of Articulated Objects from Passive Stereo
2611.30646.abstract: Robots in manufacturing often handle thin, hinged objects known from CAD models that change shape during the task, like folding cartons. Monitoring such tasks requires estimating the object's articulation state, its pose and the shape of any semi-deformable part. Learning-based estimators generalise across objects but lose precision while handling thin parts. Model-based fitting is precise but often needs accurate depth, a close initial estimate and a clean object mask. We present part-wise certification of an articulated object's state, estimated from passive stereo. Our estimator rivals the precision of the best model-based fitting method without using depth, a close initial estimate or a mask. We detect the corners that the CAD model defines in both stereo images and fit the articulated model to them. Geometric certificates, which we extend from rigid to articulated objects, then tell whether to trust each part, because the fit returns a state even for hidden parts. Certified estimates on unlabelled video become labels that improve sim-to-real transfer. On five of seven simulated objects, we locate the parts we certify three to five times more precisely than the strongest learned baseline on the same readings, given depth and true masks. On a real folding carton, our median corner error on the end panels is 2.1% of the carton's size, at least 40% lower than every learned baseline and also lower than a depth-based fit initialised near the true state.

llm.title_ja: パッシブステレオを用いた関節型物体のパーツごとの証明付き状態推定
llm.tldr_ja: 深度情報や初期値、マスクを用いずに、CADモデルから定義されたコーナーを検出し、幾何学的証明を用いて関節型物体の状態を高精度に推定する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 学習ベースの推定器は薄いパーツの扱いで精度が落ち、モデルベースのフィッティングは正確な深度や近い初期値、クリーンなマスクを必要とする点。
llm.method: ステレオ画像からCADモデルのコーナーを検出し、関節型モデルをフィッティングして幾何学的証明を適用する。
llm.result: 実際の折りたたみカートンにおいて、中央値コーナー誤差がカートンサイズの2.1%となり、学習ベースラインより40%以上低減した。

2611.30637.title: SWEEP-Bench: Do Embodied Policies Act on the Speed They See?
2611.30637.abstract: Robot policies must adapt to the speed of moving objects, yet existing benchmarks rarely measure this ability across diverse tasks and speeds. We introduce SWEEP-Bench, a simulation benchmark with 80 conveyor-belt manipulation tasks spanning 16 skill categories, each evaluated at 13 belt speeds (0.10-0.40 m/s). Objects are transported through physical contact with a visibly moving belt. Each task has a static counterpart, and each evaluation episode uses the same randomized scene at all 13 speeds. We fine-tune eight vision-language-action and world-action models on demonstrations spanning the full speed range, comparing observations from the current frame alone with those including two past frames. For six models, the success rate peaks at intermediate speeds, and their failures indicate that they tend to produce actions suited to the average demonstration speed rather than to the actual one. Past frames raise the success rate by 10-40 percentage points for three models, and linear probes show that the belt speed is also most linearly decodable from these three. Adding ground-truth speed input to four of the models improves all of them, and a speed estimated from the images keeps most of this gain. These results show that SWEEP-Bench exposes speed-dependent failures and suggest that past frames help only policies from which the speed is most decodable, such as those pretrained on multiple frames. Project page: https://damin3927.github.io/SWEEP-Bench
2611.30637.hf_summary_en: A simulation benchmark shows that robot manipulation policies often fail at non-average conveyor speeds, while past frames or speed inputs improve models when speed is linearly decodable.

llm.method: 16種類のスキルカテゴリと13種類のベルト速度を含むシミュレーションベンチマークを構築し、複数のVLA・世界モデルを評価する。

2611.30636.title: ABI: Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations for Zero-Shot Test-Time Guidance
2611.30636.abstract: Behavior-cloning policies show strong ability in sequential control by generating coherent multi-step action chunks, yet their purely imitative objective limits zero-shot generalization to unseen tasks. While offline reinforcement learning offers principled policy improvement, existing methods either require task-specific reward supervision or remain tied to a specific actor during critic training or policy deployment, inflating training cost and restricting cross-policy generalization. We observe that evaluating actions under the data-collecting behavior largely preserves their relative value ordering across target policies, offering a way around actor coupling. Combining this property with reward-free successor prediction, we propose Actor-Free Behavior-Induced Representations (ABI) to learn multi-horizon action-chunk representations from unlabeled trajectories without reward supervision or actor training. At test time, pairing the frozen representation with lightweight task readouts forms a chunk critic that guides target policies without parameter updates and transfers directly across distinct unseen policies. Our analysis establishes when the value ordering is preserved across policies and when selecting among proposed chunks improves closed-loop return. Across 65 locomotion, navigation, and manipulation tasks, ABI's chunk critic guides weak imitation policies to match or surpass zero-shot RL baselines with high sample efficiency, outperforms existing zero-shot critics on identical proposals, and improves externally trained RL actors without retraining. From raw pixels, ABI delivers substantial guidance gains and surpasses prior zero-shot RL baselines on visual manipulation, highlighting its potential for visuomotor control.

llm.title_ja: ABI：ゼロショットテスト時ガイダンスのためのアクターフリー行動誘導表現
llm.tldr_ja: 報酬教師信号やアクター訓練なしで未調整の軌跡からマルチホライズンの行動チャンク表現を学習し、パラメータ更新なしで未見のポリシーをガイドする手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 模倣学習ポリシーの純粋な模倣目的が、未見タスクへのゼロショット汎化を制限していること。

llm.result: 65の移動、ナビゲーション、マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、ゼロショットRLベースラインを上回る誘導性能を達成した。

2611.30632.title: GeoMerge-OPD: Balanced Skill Integration in Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.30632.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models excel at individual robotic skills, yet integrating heterogeneous skills into a single policy remains a key challenge for general-purpose robotic control, especially in whole-body tasks with differing manipulation and locomotion requirements. Common multi-skill integration strategies, such as joint fine-tuning and parameter merging, can induce unintended actions during closed-loop execution, severely degrading individual skills. Task-conditioned analysis of expert updates reveals response energy concentrated in a few dominant directions and opposing expert responses along high-energy directions within a shared, task-relevant response subspace. This structure co-occurs with unintended action shifts after merging. We propose GeoMerge-OPD, combining response-space regularization, parameter merging, and on-policy distillation. During independent expert fine-tuning, G-isometry constrains update-response gains within task-activation subspaces; the expert parameters are then statically merged into a student with preliminary multitask capabilities. Fine-tuned task experts serve as teachers, providing velocity-field supervision at the environment observations and intermediate action-flow states visited by the student to calibrate residual behavioral deviations. Experiments with two VLA backbones show strong, balanced humanoid skill integration on SIMPLE and consistent performance on LIBERO and LIBERO-PRO, outperforming joint fine-tuning and multitask reinforcement-learning baselines while maintaining robustness under perturbations.

llm.title_ja: GeoMerge-OPD：ビジョン言語行動モデルにおけるバランスの取れたスキル統合

2611.30597.title: ViDiHand2: Unifying Video Diffusion Priors and Hand Geometry for 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild
2611.30597.abstract: Learning robot manipulation from egocentric human videos requires accurate metric 3D hand motion. Recent methods leverage pretrained video diffusion model (VDM) priors to recover occluded hands directly from full-frame videos, but their appearance-based depth regression generalizes poorly to unseen cameras. In this work, we propose ViDiHand2, a geometry-driven framework that reformulates VDM-based hand depth estimation from direct regression into fine-grained geometric constraint solving. Specifically, we introduce Fine-Grained Geometric Lifting and Clip-Level Ray Fitting, which recover metric depth by enforcing geometric consistency between pixel-aligned 2D joints and the metric structure of MANO hands, while leveraging temporal observations across the clip. Since the lifting relies on these 2D joints, to improve robustness under occlusion and image truncation, we further develop Confidence-Gated Fusion to adaptively combine geometrically lifted joints with MANO predictions according to localization confidence. Finally, we enhance the VDM backbone to better capture spatial-temporal representations and produce the per-frame 2D joint and MANO predictions that both steps rely on. Extensive experiments on seven public datasets demonstrate that ViDiHand2 consistently outperforms 18 baselines, reducing in-the-wild absolute joint error by 42% and detection failures by 8.82x compared with the best baseline on each metric, while running at 57 FPS. The project page is available at https://vidihand2.github.io/.
2611.30597.comment: Main text 8 pages with supplementary material, 54 pages in total
2611.30597.tldr_en: This work proposes ViDiHand2, a geometry-driven framework that reformulates VDM-based hand depth estimation from direct regression into fine-grained geometric constraint solving, and introduces Fine-Grained Geometric Lifting and Clip-Level Ray Fitting, which recover metric depth by enforcing geometric consistency between pixel-aligned 2D joints and the metric structure of MANO hands.

2611.30572.title: VeriTouch: Verified Visuo-Tactile World Models that Improve Robot Policy Learning
2611.30572.abstract: Scaling visuo-tactile policy learning is constrained by the high cost of real-world data collection and the difficulty of building realistic simulations. Generative models offer a scalable source of training data, yet useful demonstrations require plausible tactile feedback, temporal alignment with visual contact, and accurate actions. To this end, we present VeriTouch, a framework for generating and verifying synthetic visuo-tactile trajectories for policy learning. Conditioned on initial images and task instructions, our world model, VeriGen, jointly generates high-fidelity dual-view videos and realistic tactile sequences over complete manipulation trajectories. By integrating a dedicated tactile expert with a pretrained video model, it captures realistic visual details and tactile deformation dynamics through joint visuo-tactile modeling. Our multimodal verifier VeriEval then checks visual quality while focusing on tactile reliability, assessing tactile realism, contact-force plausibility, and temporal alignment between visible contact and tactile signals, thereby directly filtering out unreliable sequences. Finally, our inverse dynamics model, VeriIDM, combines global scene information from both camera views with fine-grained gripper details and motion across neighboring frames to extract actions from verified videos. Experiments on five real-world tasks show that synthetic data improves all four evaluated policies, with further scaling synthetic trajectories substantially boosting policy performance without additional real-world data collection.

llm.title_ja: VeriTouch：ロボットのポリシー学習を改善する検証済み視覚・触覚世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 初期画像とタスク指示に基づき、高忠実度なデュアルビュービデオと現実的な触覚シーケンスを生成し、マルチモーダル検証器でフィルタリングした上で逆動力学モデルにより行動を抽出するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 実世界のデータ収集が高コストであり、現実的なシミュレーションの構築が困難であるため、視覚・触覚ポリシー学習のスケーリングが制限されていること。
llm.method: 世界モデルVeriGenによる視覚・触覚の同時生成、マルチモーダル検証器VeriEvalによる品質フィルタリング、および逆動力学モデルVeriIDMによる行動抽出を行う。
llm.result: 5つの実世界タスクにおいて、合成データが評価した4つすべてのポリシーを改善し、ポリシー性能を大幅に向上させた。

2611.30572.tldr_en: VeriTouch is presented, a framework for generating and verifying synthetic visuo-tactile trajectories for policy learning and shows that synthetic data improves all four evaluated policies, with further scaling synthetic trajectories substantially boosting policy performance without additional real-world data collection.

2611.30555.title: RoboInF: A Benchmark for Instruction Fidelity in Robotic Manipulation
2611.30555.abstract: Precise language control requires embodied models to follow instructions governing both task outcomes and execution. Although recent methods train policies to follow increasingly detailed commands, existing benchmarks often assess instruction following alongside perception, planning, and generalization to unfamiliar scenes. Higher task success therefore offers limited evidence of closer adherence to instructions. We introduce RoboInF, a benchmark measuring how reliably manipulation policies adapt their behavior to changes in an instruction. For each of eight tasks, six to twelve expert-validated instruction branches vary the requested goal, procedure, or manipulation detail while holding the initial scene and robot state fixed. Task-specific checkers verify the terminal goal and use recorded trajectories, contacts, and event sequences to assess compliance throughout execution. The accompanying RoboInF-4K dataset pairs 4,242 expert demonstrations with simulator-derived annotations of motion and contact. We evaluate leading manipulation policies ($π_{0.5}$ and OpenWAM) and inference-only agents (GPT-6 Astra and Qwen3.8-Flash). All four models exhibit a gap between task completion and faithful execution, indicating substantial room for fine-grained instruction following.

llm.title_ja: RoboInF：ロボットマニピュレーションにおける指示忠実度のためのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 初期シーンを固定したまま目標や手順を変更する専門家検証済みの指示分岐を用いて、マニピュレーションポリシーが指示の変更に適応する信頼性を測定するベンチマークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは指示遂行能力を認識や計画、汎化と同時に評価するため、タスク成功率が高くても指示への厳密な準拠を示す証拠としては不十分であること。
llm.method: 8つのタスクに対して6〜12の指示分岐を用意し、終了目標や実行中のコンプライアンスを検証するチェッカーを導入する。
llm.result: 主要な4つのモデルすべてにおいてタスク完了と忠実な実行の間に乖離が見られ、微細な指示追従において大きな改善余地があることが示された。

2611.30555.tldr_en: RoboInF is introduced, a benchmark measuring how reliably manipulation policies adapt their behavior to changes in an instruction and leading manipulation policies and inference-only agents are evaluated and all four models exhibit a gap between task completion and faithful execution, indicating substantial room for fine-grained instruction following.

2611.30550.title: Body and Soul: Decoupling Robotic Brain and Policy with RoboHarness-Zero
2611.30550.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can execute individual skills but fail to complete tasks that require combining several of them. In our audit of Xiaomi-Robotics-1, an estimated 43\% of failures involve choosing the wrong target or losing track of task progress. Wrapping a frozen VLA in a vision-language model (VLM) harness is a natural remedy. Existing harnesses can gain substantially from task- and policy-specific preparation, raising the question of how much of that gain transfers to a new task or policy. An ideal harness should (i) need minimal preparation for a new task, (ii) need no redesign for a new policy, and (iii) preserve standalone capabilities the policy already has. To the best of our knowledge, our \ours{} is the first harness built this way. Its premise is that choosing targets and tracking progress are easy for a VLM such as GPT-6 without task preparation, while the frozen VLA already handles continuous, contact-rich motion.
