The frozen VLA therefore executes continuous control while the VLM plans zero-shot and monitors execution; when progress stalls or targets drift, the VLM first rephrases the instruction and, only as a fallback, executes short generated code over generic motion primitives before returning fine control to the VLA. The supervision rules stay fixed across policies, requiring only a thin interface adapter and an automatically profiled skill configuration per policy. On 200 RoboCasa365 scenes, \ours{} with GPT-6 Astra raises the success rate of frozen Xiaomi-Robotics-1 from \textbf{\color{blue}57.5\%} to \textbf{\color{blue}70.5\%} and preserves \textbf{\color{blue}90.4\%} of its standalone successes (104/115) while rescuing 37 of 85 failures. On a shared 50-scene subset, the same rules add 8 to 10 percentage points to each of four other frozen policies, while existing preparation-based harness systems often fail to transfer to a new policy.

llm.title_ja: ボディ・アンド・ソウル：RoboHarness-Zeroによるロボットの脳とポリシーの切り離し
llm.tldr_ja: VLMがゼロショットで計画と実行監視を行い、フリーズされたVLAが連続的な接触を伴う動作を実行することで、ポリシーの再設計を不要にしながら複数スキルの組み合わせを可能にするフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーは単一スキルを実行できるものの、複数のスキルを組み合わせるタスクの完了に失敗すること。
llm.method: VLM（GPT-6など）による計画・監視と、汎用動作プリミティブに基づくフォールバックコードの実行を組み合わせたハーネスを構築する。
llm.result: RoboCasa365のシーンにおいて、Xiaomi-Robotics-1の成功率を57.5%から70.5%へと向上させ、スタンドアロンの成功を90.4%維持した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.30550.tldr_en: The authors' harness is the first harness built this way, and its premise is that choosing targets and tracking progress are easy for a VLM such as GPT-6 without task preparation, while the frozen VLA already handles continuous, contact-rich motion.

2611.30534.title: DelayOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation from a Synchronous Teacher for Real-time Asynchronous Policies
2611.30534.abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur substantial inference latency due to their large vision-language backbones and iterative denoising. Asynchronous execution reduces this latency by generating the next action chunk while executing the current one, but the new chunk is conditioned on a stale observation, degrading performance as the delay increases. We investigate this mismatch by comparing actions predicted from observations at planning and execution times. We find that these predictions differ little on expert demonstrations but diverge substantially on the policy's own delayed rollouts, particularly in failed episodes. Motivated by this observation, we propose DelayOPSD, which trains an asynchronous policy to imitate its synchronous counterpart on the policy's own rollouts. Specifically, a synchronous teacher, obtained from the same policy using the observation at execution time, supervises a delayed student that observes only the earlier frame and the actions still being executed. The student learns to match the teacher throughout its own denoising process. Under a 10-step delay, training SmolVLA on demonstrations achieves only 70.2% success, comparable to naive asynchronous execution (70.4%), whereas training on its own rollouts improves success to 78.7%. Across LIBERO and Kinetix, DelayOPSD achieves the highest average success among the compared methods, without introducing additional modules at deployment. On a real robot, it further improves success from 46% to 62%.

llm.title_ja: DelayOPSD：リアルタイム非同期ポリシーのための同期的教師からのオンポリシー自己蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: 古い観測に基づく遅延した学生モデルが、実行時の観測を用いる同期的教師モデルのデノイジングプロセス全体を模倣するように訓練するオンポリシー自己蒸留手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 非同期実行において、新しい行動チャンクが古い観測に条件付けられるため、遅延が増加するにつれて性能が低下すること。
llm.method: ポリシー自身のロールアウト上で、同期教師モデルが遅延した学生モデルを指導するオンポリシー自己蒸留を行う。
llm.result: 10ステップの遅延下で、デモデータのみの訓練やナイーブな非同期実行と比較して成功率を大幅に向上させ、実機でも46%から62%へと成功率を改善した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.30534.tldr_en: DelaysOPSD is proposed, which trains an asynchronous policy to imitate its synchronous counterpart on the policy's own rollouts, without introducing additional modules at deployment, without introducing additional modules at deployment.

2611.30516.title: JEPA-ICL: Progress-Aligned Latent Plans for In-Context Robotic Manipulation
2611.30516.abstract: Demonstrations show how a task can be completed, but differences in embodiment, appearance, and execution speed make it difficult to identify the guidance relevant to the robot's current progress. We introduce JEPA-ICL, a vision-language-action framework that couples predictive planning with demonstration learning. The policy learns to plan by predicting ordered future states in JEPA feature space up to subtask completion, capturing what remains to be accomplished. These plans guide action generation and locate relevant stages in demonstrations, whose JEPA-supervised content features provide progress-aligned context. Learning from this context, in turn, updates the shared policy that produces the plans and actions. This coupling connects anticipating the robot's own execution with reusing demonstrated experience. On the Imitator Game, JEPA-ICL achieves 80.0% seen-task success under C15 pretraining, outperforming Zero-WAM by 12.0 percentage points. Without contextual demonstrations, JEPA-ICL outperforms the VLA-JEPA variant without human-video pretraining, improving success rates from 96.1% to 97.6% on LIBERO and from 62.9% to 73.2% on LIBERO-Plus. With demonstration-based training and contextual guidance at inference, LIBERO-Plus success further increases from 73.2% to 75.2%.

llm.title_ja: JEPA-ICL：インコンテキストロボットマニピュレーションに向けた進捗整合型潜在プラン
llm.tldr_ja: JEPA特徴空間においてサブタスク完了までの順序付き未来状態を予測することで計画を学び、それが行動生成を導きつつデモ内の適切な段階を特定するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 身体性や外観、実行速度の違いにより、ロボットの現在の進捗に関連するデモ内のガイダンスを特定することが困難であること。
llm.method: JEPA特徴空間での未来状態予測による予測的計画の学習と、デモからのインコンテキスト学習を結合する。
llm.result: Imitator Gameにおいて80.0%の既知タスク成功率を達成し、LIBEROやLIBERO-Plusでも優れた性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル
インコンテキスト学習

2611.30516.tldr_en: JEPA-ICL, a vision-language-action framework that couples predictive planning with demonstration learning, is introduced, a vision-language-action framework that couples predictive planning with demonstration learning that outperforms the VLA-JEPA variant without human-video pretraining.

2611.30511.title: AXE: AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge Technical Report
2611.30511.abstract: This report presents a comprehensive pipeline for developing an end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving model for the Physical AI AV Track. The framework consists of data curation, HD map auto-labelling, data-driven imitation learning, and simulator-based reinforcement learning. To ensure safety in the closed-loop setting, we introduce a selection-based E2E planning approach that leverages object detection and BEV segmentation to filter out trajectory candidates likely to cause collisions or off-road driving. Trained on NVIDIA NuRec and the NVIDIA PAI-AV dataset, our method scores a fixed vocabulary of trajectory candidates for collision, drivable-area compliance, and progress learned from simulated rollouts, and selects the best candidate that passes the filter. This design highlights the effectiveness of combining E2E planning with perception-based trajectory filtering for safe and reliable closed-loop autonomous driving.
2611.30511.comment: Innovation Award winner, Physical AI AV Track (PAI-AV), AlpaSim E2E Closed Loop Challenge 2026, with results shared at the NeurIPS 2026 World Models in Physical AI Workshop. 15 pages, 10 figures, 4 tables

llm.title_ja: AXE：AlpaSim E2Eクローズドループチャレンジ技術報告書
llm.tldr_ja: データキュレーション、自動ラベリング、模倣学習、シミュレーション強化学習を組み合わせ、物体検出とBEVセグメンテーションによる選択的軌跡フィルタリングを用いるエンドツーエンド自動運転パイプラインを提案する。
llm.problem: 複雑な交通環境における信頼性の高いクローズドループ自動運転の実現が困難であること。
llm.method: 物体検出とBEVセグメンテーションを用いて衝突やコースアウトの危険がある軌跡候補をフィルタリングし、最適な候補を選択する。
llm.result: Physical AI AV Trackにおいて優れた走行スコアを記録し、クローズドループ自動運転における安全性と信頼性を示した。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習

2611.30511.tldr_en: A selection-based E2E planning approach that leverages object detection and BEV segmentation to filter out trajectory candidates likely to cause collisions or off-road driving is introduced to ensure safety in the closed-loop setting.

2611.30495.title: DexDuet: Learning Contact-Preserving Bimanual Dexterity from Human Demonstrations
2611.30495.abstract: Human demonstrations provide a rich source of bimanual dexterous skills, yet transferring them to robot hands remains challenging. Existing methods primarily optimize object trajectory tracking, often overlooking how human hands interact with the object. Even with accurate tracking, robots may contact incorrect object parts or slide their fingers, resulting in unstable manipulation. We present DexDuet, a framework that learns contact-preserving bimanual dexterity from a single human demonstration. DexDuet employs two interaction rewards to preserve human hand-object configurations and contacts. To enable coordinated manipulation, we factorize the bimanual policy into two weight-sharing per-hand policies that condition on each other's states. We further propose assisted reference-state initialization (A-RSI), an adaptive curriculum that adjusts object assistance and training starts across demonstration segments to overcome difficult manipulation phases. Across four benchmarks spanning three simulators and five robot embodiments, DexDuet improves object-tracking ADD-AUC by 11 to 41 points over the corresponding baselines while consistently achieving better contact preservation. Notably, among 122 paired runs with comparable object-tracking accuracy, DexDuet preserves the human's contacts better in 117 cases. Code and videos are available at https://rcl-robotics.github.io/Dexduet.io/

llm.title_ja: DexDuet：人間のデモンストレーションからの接触保持型両手器用さの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の手と物体の構成や接触を維持する2つのインタラクション報酬を導入し、お互いの状態に条件付けられた重み共有型ポリシーによって両手協調操作を実現するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 人間のデモンストレーションをロボットハンドに移行する際、物体軌跡の追跡のみに注目すると不適切なパーツに接触したり滑ったりして不安定になること。
llm.method: 人間と物体の接触を保持するインタラクション報酬の導入、両手ポリシーの因数分解、および適応型カリキュラムによる初期化を行う。
llm.result: 3つのシミュレータと5つのロボットを用いたベンチマークで、オブジェクト追跡精度を大幅に向上させつつ、優れた接触保持を実現した。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーション学習

2611.30490.title: EgoStudy: How Does Scaling Egocentric Data Affect VLA and WAM Pretraining?
2611.30490.abstract: Egocentric human manipulation data offer a scalable resource for training dexterous robot policies. However, how effectively robots can learn and benefit from these data remains unclear due to the embodiment gap between humans and robots. We present EgoStudy, a systematic, controlled study of egocentric data for robot learning. Holding the robot dataset fixed, we vary the scale and diversity of egocentric data, data processing strategies, and co-training configurations. We investigate three questions: (1) Which data processing and pretraining choices most effectively exploit egocentric data? (2) Which components of robot action prediction benefit most from scaling these data? (3) How do scaling effects differ between vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs)? Our experiments yield three main findings. First, data diversity, alignment between trajectories, and detailed language annotations are key factors in effective transfer. Second, scaling egocentric data yields larger gains in predicting end-effector translation than in predicting fine-grained finger movements. Third, WAMs perform better when egocentric data are limited, whereas VLAs exhibit greater gains as the amount of egocentric data increases. Together, these findings provide practical guidance on processing and using egocentric data to train VLAs and WAMs, while clarifying the benefits and limitations of scaling these data.

llm.title_ja: EgoStudy：エゴセントリックデータのスケーリングはVLAおよびWAMの事前学習にどのような影響を与えるか？
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットデータセットを固定した状態で、エゴセントリックデータの規模や多様性、処理戦略、共同訓練設定を体系的に調査し、VLAと世界行動モデルに対するスケーリング効果を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 人間とロボットの身体性のギャップのため、ロボットがエゴセントリックデータからどの程度学習し恩恵を受けられるかが不明確であること。
llm.method: データの多様性、軌跡間のアラインメント、および詳細な言語アノテーションを変化させ、VLAとWAMへの影響を比較分析する。
llm.result: データ多様性とアラインメントが重要であること、スケーリングによりエンドエフェクタ移動の予測が大きく向上することなどを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: エゴセントリックデータ
ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.30490.tldr_en: EgoStudy, a systematic, controlled study of egocentric data for robot learning, provides practical guidance on processing and using egocentric data to train VLAs and WAMs, while clarifying the benefits and limitations of scaling these data.

2611.30477.title: OVOGO: Offline Value-Guided On-Policy Generative Optimization for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.30477.abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action models can benefit from robot experience collected during deployment, but repeatedly acquiring new physical interactions for policy improvement is costly. Offline reinforcement learning provides a natural way to reuse collected experience, while flow-based policies offer an additional opportunity because fresh generation trajectories can be cheaply resampled from the current policy at replay observations. This motivates separating offline value learning from on-policy optimization of the generative process. We propose OVOGO, an offline reinforcement learning framework that realizes this separation for flow-based VLAs. A central challenge in this formulation is to learn a critic that remains grounded in logged robot experience while providing useful value signals for newly generated actions. OVOGO introduces a Return-Anchored Ranking Critic that combines in-sample distributional value learning with guarded local ranking, improving discrimination among generated actions without assigning them artificial return targets. The frozen critic then provides group-relative value signals for selected-transition optimization of fresh action candidates sampled from the current flow policy. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, DexJoCo, and LIBERO, as well as a real-robot dexterous manipulation task, show that OVOGO improves the initial VLA across all four settings and achieves higher success rates than the evaluated offline adaptation and value-guided baselines. These results suggest that offline robot experience can be repeatedly reused for value learning while inexpensive generative sampling supports policy optimization, providing an effective approach to experience-based post-training of flow-based VLAs.

llm.title_ja: OVOGO：フローベースのビジョン言語行動モデルに向けたオフライン価値誘導型オンポリシー生成的最適化
llm.tldr_ja: オフラインの価値学習と生成プロセスのオンポリシー最適化を分離し、サンプリングされた行動候補に対してグループ相対的な価値信号を提供するオフライン強化学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: フローベースのVLAポリシーはデプロイ時の経験を活用できるが、新しい物理的インタラクションの取得にはコストがかかること。
llm.method: リターン係留型ランキング批評家を用いて、記録された経験に基づいた価値学習と新しく生成された行動の最適化を行う。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0、DexJoCo、LIBERO、および実機の器用なマニピュレーションタスクにおいて、初期VLAの性能とベースラインを上回る成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.30477.tldr_en: OVOGO introduces a Return-Anchored Ranking Critic that combines in-sample distributional value learning with guarded local ranking, improving discrimination among generated actions without assigning them artificial return targets, providing an effective approach to experience-based post-training of flow-based VLAs.

2611.30463.title: Autonomous UAV Navigation in an Unknown Environment via Multi-Trajectory Model Predictive Control
2611.30463.abstract: A novel model predictive control (MPC) formulation, named multi-trajectory MPC (mt-MPC), is presented and applied to the problem of autonomous navigation of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in an unknown environment. The UAV is equipped with a LiDAR sensor, providing only a partial description of the surroundings and resulting in time-varying constraints as the vehicle navigates among the obstacles. The control system layout is hierarchical: the low-level loops stabilize the vehicle's trajectories and track the set-points commanded by the high-level, mt-MPC controller. The latter is required to plan the UAV trajectory trading off safety, i.e. to avoid collisions with the uncertain obstacles, and exploitation, i.e. to reach an assigned target location. To achieve this goal, mt-MPC considers different future state trajectories in the same Finite Horizon Optimal Control Problem (FHOCP), enabling a partial decoupling between constraint satisfaction (safety) and cost function minimization (exploitation). Recursive feasibility and, consequently, persistent obstacle avoidance guarantees are derived under the assumption of a time invariant environment. The performance of the approach is studied in simulation and compared with that of a standard MPC, showing good improvement.

llm.title_ja: マルチ軌跡モデル予測制御を用いた未知環境におけるUAVの自律ナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 同一の有限地平最適制御問題内で複数の将来状態軌跡を考慮し、制約充足（安全性）とコスト関数最小化（探索）の部分的な分離を可能にするマルチ軌跡MPC（mt-MPC）を提案する。
llm.problem: LiDARの部分的な情報のみを持つ未知環境において、時間とともに変化する障害物回避と目標到達を両立させること。
llm.method: 階層型の制御レイアウトを構築し、高レベルのmt-MPCコントローラで複数の将来状態軌跡を考慮して安全性を保証する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて標準的なMPCと比較して良好な性能向上が示された。
llm.limitation: 時間不変な環境という仮定に基づいている点。

2611.30463.tldr_en: A novel model predictive control formulation, named multi-trajectory MPC (mt-MPC), is presented and applied to the problem of autonomous navigation of an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in an unknown environment, enabling a partial decoupling between constraint satisfaction (safety) and cost function minimization (exploitation).

2611.30461.title: LiveMirror: Real-Time Diffusion Virtual Try-On on a Consumer GPU and Its Self-Supervised Adaptation to Indian Ethnic Wear
2611.30461.abstract: Diffusion virtual try-on (VTO) models produce convincing garment transfers from a single product photograph, but at hundreds of milliseconds to seconds per image every deployment today is offline or falls back to AR mirrors that need a rigged 3D asset per product. We present LiveMirror, a live-camera try-on mirror that renders a flat garment photograph onto a moving person with a diffusion model on one 16 GB consumer GPU. Its core is asynchronous keyframe try-on: generation never blocks the display, every displayed frame is an optical-flow warp of the latest generated keyframe, and keyframes are replaced only through a cross-fade. The display runs at camera rate (25 FPS at 720p) while a new try-on arrives every 370-490 ms; we measure the residual flicker, give a stage-by-stage latency budget, and report which accelerations (step count, consistency LoRA, tiny decoder, compilation) keep garment prints intact. We then show that the same GPU fixes the model's biggest cultural blind spot: try-on models trained on VITON-HD and DressCode render a knee-length kurta or sherwani as a torso-length top or a dress over bare legs. A thigh-covering mask, self-supervised pairs built automatically from 24.9k on-model e-commerce photographs, and 3.2 GPU-hours of attention-only fine-tuning of CatVTON halve the perceptual error on ethnic wear (LPIPS 0.137 to 0.077 on IndoFashion, 0.135 to 0.073 on Atlas; 200 held-out pairs per source) with no regression on Western tops. A two-pass hem-aware mask then removes the remaining failure, recoloured trousers below the hem, on all but 3-4% of pairs at no training cost; in the mirror the hem comes from the previous keyframe for free. The adapted model beats FASHN VTON 1.5 on every aggregate ethnic-wear metric at about $20\times$ lower inference cost, and its weights drop straight into the mirror.

llm.title_ja: LiveMirror：コンシューマGPU上のリアルタイム拡散バーチャル試着とインド民族衣装への自己教師あり適応
llm.tldr_ja: 非同期キーフレーム試着を採用し、生成処理が表示をブロックすることなくカメラフレームレートでの動作を実現する、1台のコンシューマGPU上で動作するライブカメラ試着ミラーを提案する。
llm.problem: 拡散バーチャル試着モデルは推論に何百ミリ秒から数秒かかり、オフラインであるか、製品ごとに事前にリグされた3Dアセットを必要とすること。
llm.method: 非同期キーフレーム生成、オプティカルフローによるワープ、クロスフェード、および自己教師あり微調整による文化的な適応を行う。
llm.result: 16GBのコンシューマGPU上で25 FPSの表示と370〜490 msごとの試着更新を実現し、インド民族衣装の知覚誤差を半減させた。

2611.30461.tldr_en: LiveMirror is presented, a live-camera try-on mirror that renders a flat garment photograph onto a moving person with a diffusion model on one 16 GB consumer GPU, and it is shown that the same GPU fixes the model's biggest cultural blind spot.

2611.30449.title: CHAMP: Coordinated Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Whole-Body Motion Priors
2611.30449.abstract: Coordinating locomotion and dexterous manipulation is fundamental to humanoid robots operating in human environments. A key challenge is learning motion priors from diverse data and using them effectively for coordinated robot control. We present CHAMP, a unified framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that combines whole-body motion pretraining with adaptive feature extraction. CHAMP pretrains a vision-language model to predict future body and hand motion from approximately 2,298 hours of heterogeneous human and robot data. A shared motion representation enables unified whole-body motion learning across embodiments from datasets with body annotations, hand annotations, or both. To ground these motion priors in robot control, we introduce a Coordination-oriented Action Expert (CAE) and train it on replay data generated using the target controller. Through sparse routing, CAE adaptively selects, transforms, and fuses features from multiple layers of the pretrained model to jointly generate body and hand actions. In experiments, CHAMP achieves overall success rates of 84.8% on seven simulated tasks and 91.4% on seven real-world tasks with a Unitree G1, outperforming the evaluated baselines in both settings. In particular, CHAMP achieves 70.0% success on the long-horizon popcorn-serving task, compared with 40.0% for the best-performing baseline.

llm.title_ja: CHAMP：全身モーション事前学習による協調型ヒューマノイド移動・操作
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な人間やロボットのデータから全身モーションの事前学習を行い、スパースルーティングを用いた協調指向型行動エキスパートによってボディと手の行動を統合生成するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 人間の環境で稼働するヒューマノイドロボットにとって、移動と器用な操作の協調が不可欠であるが、多様なデータからモーション事前学習を行って効果的に制御することが困難であること。
llm.method: 全身モーション事前学習済みビジョン言語モデルと、リプレイデータで訓練された協調指向型行動エキスパート（CAE）を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 7つのシミュレーションタスクで84.8%、Unitree G1を用いた7つの実世界タスクで91.4%の成功率を達成し、ベースラインを上回った。

2611.30449.tldr_en: CHAMP is a unified framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that combines whole-body motion pretraining with adaptive feature extraction and introduces a Coordination-oriented Action Expert (CAE) and adaptively selects, transforms, and fuses features from multiple layers of the pretrained model to jointly generate body and hand actions.

2611.30438.title: ROSE-Drive: Runtime Orchestration and System Evolution for Autonomous Driving
2611.30438.abstract: End-to-end driving models have made substantial progress, yet reliable closed-loop driving in complex traffic remains challenging. Beyond improving individual models, system-level orchestration offers a complementary approach by coordinating driving capabilities and computation. We introduce ROSE-Drive (Runtime Orchestration and System Evolution), a model-agnostic framework that jointly orchestrates driving execution and computation. It coordinates frozen driving models with driving skills, perception tools, and feedback controllers. A distilled vision-language model (VLM) proposes driving tasks and scene relations. Shared physical state and persistent tasks support capability composition, task continuity, and adaptive scheduling. The orchestrator combines model and skill outputs across control channels, maintains task responsibility through handover, and uses execution feedback to select controllers, reuse valid motion references, and schedule model inference. Offline revisions use execution records to refine skills and their coordination through a stable task interface. Successive system stages inherit these revisions while model, perception, and VLM weights remain fixed. Evaluations with four driving models on Bench2Drive v0.0.3, Bench2Drive v0.0.4, and Fail2Drive show accumulated capability and transfer before target-benchmark revision. On held-out Longest6, driving score (DS) rises from 25 to 52 for AutoMoT and from 22 to 47 for SimLingo across system stages, while both systems skip new model inference on over 71% of control steps.

llm.title_ja: ROSE-Drive：自動運転のためのランタイムオーケストレーションとシステム進化
llm.tldr_ja: フリーズされた駆動モデル、駆動スキル、認識ツール、フィードバックコントローラを協調させ、実行フィードバックを利用してコントローラの選択やモデル推論のスケジュールを行うモデル非依存のフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンドの駆動モデルが進展しているものの、複雑な交通環境における信頼性の高いクローズドループ運転の実現が困難であること。
llm.method: 蒸留されたビジョン言語モデルが駆動タスクやシーン関係を提案し、オーケストレータが制御チャネルをまたいでモデルやスキルの出力を統合する。
llm.result: Hold-outのLongest6において、AutoMoTの駆動スコアが25から52へ、SimLingoが22から47へと向上し、多くの制御ステップでモデル推論をスキップした。
keywords_ja: オーケストレーション

2611.30438.tldr_en: ROSE-Drive is introduced, a model-agnostic framework that jointly orchestrates driving execution and computation that combines model and skill outputs across control channels, and uses execution feedback to select controllers, reuse valid motion references, and schedule model inference.

2611.30402.title: GeLiFiSH: Recursive LiDAR Keypoint Estimation with Ground and Moving Object Segmentation
2611.30402.abstract: LiDAR registration and loop closure often rely on sparse keypoints, which must remain repeatable across sessions, viewpoints, and sensors. To handle differing scan patterns, detectors typically operate on accumulated submaps, which introduces latency and processes each submap independently, so repeated observations are never fused. Height-based detectors also reference structure to an estimated ground, so its inconsistency across sessions propagates into the keypoints. Moreover, dynamic objects leave ghost trails that can be mistaken for static structure. We present GeLiFiSH (Geometric LiDAR Filtering with Sequential Hypothesis testing), a learning-free filter that recursively estimates persistent keypoints at scan rate. A height-structure detector runs on a rolling voxel map, and detections initialize tracks with a position, covariance, and existence probability, accepted or rejected by a sequential probability ratio test. Ground segmentation provides a sensor-agnostic height reference, and moving object segmentation removes dynamic points before map insertion. On SemanticKITTI, HeLiMOS, and HeLiPR, spanning five LiDARs and multiple sessions, GeLiFiSH attains the highest average keypoint repeatability among the compared detectors and the second-highest cross-session registration recall from keypoints alone, behind ISS which extracts four times as many keypoints. With one parameter set and no sensor-height prior, both ground and moving object segmentation modules outperform their baselines on average.

llm.title_ja: GeLiFiSH：地面および動的物体セグメンテーションを用いた再帰的LiDARキーポイント推定
llm.tldr_ja: ローリングボクセルマップ上で高さ構造検出器を動作させ、順序確率比検定によりキーポイントを追跡・フィルタリングすることで、スキャンレートで持続的なキーポイントを再帰的に推定する学習不要のフィルタを提案する。
llm.problem: LiDAR登録やループクロージャで用いられるキーポイントはセッションや視点間で繰り返し観測される必要があるが、高さベースの検出器は推定された地面の不整合や動的物体のゴーストの影響を受けること。
llm.method: 高さ構造検出器、順序確率比検定によるトラック管理、センサー非依存の地面セグメンテーション、動的物体セグメンテーションを組み合わせる。
llm.result: SemanticKITTIなどの5つのLiDARと複数セッションにわたるデータにおいて、平均キーポイント再現率で最高値を達成した。

2611.30402.tldr_en: GeLiFiSH (Geometric LiDAR Filtering with Sequential Hypothesis testing), a learning-free filter that recursively estimates persistent keypoints at scan rate, is presented, a learning-free filter that recursively estimates persistent keypoints at scan rate.

2611.30389.title: AgentMoT: An Agentic Mixture-of-Transformers for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
2611.30389.abstract: Driving models need to choose which capabilities to use and when to reconsider their decisions. We introduce AgentMoT, a Mixture-of-Transformers with built-in agent reasoning and system scheduling. Combinations of agent, world, and action experts form three jointly trained pathways for direct-action, vision-language-action, and world-action computation. The Router selects a native pathway, while the agent expert supplies reasoning and selects skills. Execution feedback raises wake-up requests, and the agent self-scheduler learns whether to reconsider the task decision or keep it. Mandatory requests invoke the agent directly. The relative-capability principle guides these choices by relating the benefit of additional computation or intervention to its cost. After open-loop initialization, dual-loop evolution trains the Router, agent, and self-scheduler from closed-loop experience while failure-driven updates refine skills and execution feedback. AgentMoT achieves state-of-the-art results on Bench2Drive v0.0.3 and v0.0.4, with 94.48/92.33 driving score and 85.45/82.73% success rate, respectively. With skills disabled, learned routing improves over the strongest fixed pathway by 1.79 driving-score points and 4.09 percentage points of success rate on v0.0.3. Ablation studies further show gains from closed-loop agent learning, two-view queries, and event-triggered wake-up.

llm.title_ja: AgentMoT: エージェント型Mixture-of-Transformersによるエンドツーエンド自動運転
llm.tldr_ja: エージェント推論とシステムスケジューリングを組み込んだMixture-of-TransformersであるAgentMoTを提案し、Bench2Driveで最高性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 自動運転モデルにおいて、どの能力をいつ使用すべきか、いつ再検討すべきかを適切に選択することが課題である。
llm.method: エージェント、世界、行動の専門家を組み合わせ、ルーターや自己スケジューラーによって直接行動やVLA計算を行う。
llm.result: Bench2Drive v0.0.3およびv0.0.4で最高性能（駆動スコア94.48/92.33）を達成した。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習

2611.30389.tldr_en: This work introduces AgentMoT, a Mixture-of-Transformers with built-in agent reasoning and system scheduling that achieves state-of-the-art results on Bench2Drive v0.0.0.3 and v0.0.4.

2611.30388.title: BASE: A Backend-Agnostic Streaming Embodiment Layer for Full-Duplex Conversational Avatars
2611.30388.abstract: Many end-to-end spoken dialogue models can now converse in real time and full duplex, and turning them into 3D avatars requires full-body gestures, listening feedback, and turn-taking. Existing methods couple the motion generator tightly to one dialogue model by reading its internal states or training speech and motion jointly. The motion module must then be retrained whenever the dialogue model changes, cannot be attached to cloud APIs that expose only audio, and entangles role, voice, and motion style. We propose BASE, a backend-agnostic streaming embodiment layer whose only interface to the dialogue model is its emitted speech. First, a conversation state manager driven solely by audio handles speaking, listening, idling, barge-in, and proactive turns on one timeline, while role, voice, motion style, and 3D appearance are set independently. Second, to run an offline 2 s flow-matching gesture model on live audio, we reformulate inference as sliding-window continuation with overlapped look-ahead ensembling, which removes seam jitter. Third, we show that the remaining streaming gap comes from errors accumulating in the self-generated motion history rather than missing future speech; our Drift-Aware History Perturbation (DAHP) reduces this gap in about 50 min on one GPU by injecting inference-like drift into ground-truth training histories, and transfers to a second generator. On BEAT2, streaming BASE reaches an FGD of 0.342, on par with the tightly coupled MIBURI (0.333), and viewers prefer its body motion over MIBURI's in 82% of forced-choice judgments. Without retraining, the same layer drives a cascaded pipeline, three open full-duplex models, and a cloud API in real time.

llm.title_ja: BASE: 全二重会話型アバターのためのバックエンド非依存ストリーミング体現レイヤー
llm.tldr_ja: 会話モデルから出力される音声のみをインターフェースとし、リアルタイムかつ全二重で3Dアバターの全身ジェスチャー等を駆動するBASEを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の手法はモーション生成器が単一の対話モデルと密結合しており、対話モデルの変更時に再学習が必要になる。
llm.method: 音声のみで駆動する会話状態管理、スライディングウィンドウ継続による推論の再定常化、DAHPによるドリフト対策を導入する。
llm.result: BEAT2においてストリーミングBASEはFGD 0.342を達成し、既存の密結合手法と同等の性能を示した。

2611.30388.tldr_en: BASE is proposed, a backend-agnostic streaming embodiment layer whose only interface to the dialogue model is its emitted speech, and it is shown that the remaining streaming gap comes from errors accumulating in the self-generated motion history rather than missing future speech.

2611.30363.title: SOAR: temporal Structure-guided One-step Action generation for Robotic manipulation
2611.30363.abstract: Efficient robotic manipulation requires temporally coordinated actions with low inference latency. Multi-step diffusion and flow policies progressively refine action trajectories but require costly iterative inference, whereas one-step policies eliminate iterative trajectory refinement to reduce inference cost. We introduce **SOAR**, a structure-guided one-step generative policy that improves action quality while preserving one-step efficiency. SOAR predicts an observation-conditioned discrete cosine transform (DCT) representation of future actions, capturing temporal variations across multiple frequency bands to provide explicit guidance from key temporal structural information. Unlike velocity-parameterized one-step flow policies that recover clean actions indirectly from a predicted velocity field, SOAR directly generates clean action trajectories in action space. This aligns the model output with the executable control target and provides a direct interface for structural calibration. The predicted structure further corrects the generated trajectory according to their spectral discrepancy, without requiring an additional evaluation of the generative backbone. During training, the corresponding MeanFlow velocity is derived from the calibrated clean action and used for consistency learning, while an endpoint objective aligns training with the pure-noise condition used for one-step inference. Across 53 Adroit and Meta-World tasks, SOAR achieves 83.9% overall success with only 8.7 ms inference latency. When applied to the VLA model, π0.5, SOAR further achieves 97.2% on LIBERO and 71.7% on RoboTwin 2.0. Real-world experiments and extensive ablations further validate its effectiveness and efficiency.

llm.title_ja: SOAR: ロボットマニピュレーションのための時間構造誘導型1ステップ行動生成
llm.tldr_ja: 時間的構造情報を活用して1ステップの効率性を維持しつつ行動品質を向上させる構造誘導型1ステップ生成ポリシーSOARを提案した。
llm.problem: マルチステップの拡散・フローポリシーは反復推論コストが高く、1ステップポリシーは反復洗練を排除するが品質が課題となる。
llm.method: 観測条件付きの離散コサイン変換表現を予測し、行動空間でクリーンな行動軌跡を直接生成する。
llm.result: 53のAdroitおよびMeta-Worldタスクで平均83.9%の成功率を8.7msの推論遅延で達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.30354.title: STAR: Structure-Aware Temporal Action Recovery for Point Supervised Temporal Action Localization
2611.30354.abstract: Point supervised temporal action localization is becoming the need of time in this era of ever growing and non-stop video data. Existing method mainly rely on snippet level action response to generate pseudo labels. However, these labels often suffer from boundary ambiguity, over extended proposals, and weak temporal structure. To address these issues, we propose STAR, a structure-aware Temporal Action Recovery framework for point supervised temporal action localization. STAR works by enhancing the base S model with temporal difference interaction with attention module to capture forward and backward snippet changes, and introduces the learning of start, core, and end roles to model the internal temporal structure of actions. In addition, STAR further improves the pseudo label generation through All point proposal ranking and Rolebank based structural re-ranking, which suppress neighbor crossing and structurally inconsistent proposals. Finally, temporal action detector to STAR feedback supervision transfers high quality detector prediction back to the STAR model through soft start, core, end, action, and background targets. This helps to further refine the pseudo labels. Extensive experiments on four standard benchmarks shows the effectiveness of STAR. By using I3D features, STAR achieves 67.2% at AVG@0.1:0.7 on THUMOS'14, 58.1% on GTEA, 74.6% on BEOID, and 31.7% at AVG@0.5:0.95 on ActivityNet-1.3, outperforming previous point supervised methods across multiple benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: STAR: 点教師あり時間的行動局所化のための構造認識型時間的行動復元
llm.tldr_ja: 時間的差分相互作用と役割ベースの再ランキングにより、点教師あり時間的行動局所化の擬似ラベル生成を改善するSTARを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の点教師あり手法は、境界の曖昧さや過剰なプロポーザル、弱い時間的構造に悩まされている。
llm.method: アテンションモジュールによる時間的差分相互作用の強化と、開始・コア・終了の役割学習を導入する。
llm.result: THUMOS'14などの4つの標準ベンチマークで従来手法を上回る性能を達成した。

2611.30354.tldr_en: The proposed STAR, a structure-aware Temporal Action Recovery framework for point supervised temporal action localization outperforming previous point supervised methods across multiple benchmarks, and improves the pseudo label generation.

2611.30312.title: One Policy, Many Bodies: Cooperative Human-Object Interaction with Heterogeneous Teams
2611.30312.abstract: Physics-based human-object interaction (HOI) has enabled multiple characters to cooperatively transport objects, but existing cooperative controllers largely assume homogeneous embodiments and predefined interaction tasks. We ask whether a single physics-based policy can enable cooperation across diverse embodiments, team compositions, and interaction skills. We present MorphHOI, a decentralised framework built on a key insight: effective heterogeneous cooperation requires a unified representation across embodiments while accounting for differences in their physical capabilities. To realise this insight, we introduce a canonical body interface that unifies observation and action spaces, together with an embodiment-conditioned transformer that adapts cooperative decisions to the physical capabilities of each agent and its teammates. To extend cooperation to new interaction skills, we reuse the learned cooperative policy through task-specific tokens and lightweight adaptation, preserving its original capabilities. Our framework achieves success rates of up to 96.7\% on seen embodiments, 95.6\% on unseen embodiments, and 91.4\% on novel payloads. Furthermore, the learned cooperation extends to diverse interaction skills with high success rates, including box carrying, transport on stairs, and waypoint following, while preserving previously acquired cooperative capabilities.

llm.title_ja: One Policy, Many Bodies: 異種チームによる協調的人間-物体相互作用
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な身体やチーム構成にまたがる協調を単一の物理ベースポリシーで実現する分散型フレームワークMorphHOIを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の協調コントローラーは主に同種の身体や事前定義された相互作用タスクを前提としている。
llm.method: 観察・行動空間を統一する標準化された身体インターフェースと、身体の物理的能力に適応するトランスフォーマーを導入する。
llm.result: 見たことのある身体で最大96.7%、未知の身体で95.6%、新しいペイロードで91.4%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: マルチエージェント協調
物理ベースシミュレーション

2611.30312.tldr_en: MorphHOI is presented, a decentralised framework built on a key insight: effective heterogeneous cooperation requires a unified representation across embodiments while accounting for differences in their physical capabilities, which extends to diverse interaction skills with high success rates.

2611.30310.title: Seeing Together, Acting Apart: Shared Environmental Understanding for Multi-Robot Navigation
2611.30310.abstract: Multi-robot embodied systems are typically designed to collaborate by coordinating actions, sharing trajectories, or learning joint policies. We ask a complementary question: can collaboration emerge before decision-making, by first building a shared understanding of the environment? We introduce Shared Environmental Understanding, a policy-agnostic representation that aggregates partial egocentric observations from multiple robots into a shared latent world model. This shifts collaboration from the policy space to the representation space, enabling decentralized decision-making with shared environmental context. To this end, we propose Shared Environment Encoding and Retrieval (SEER), a framework that organizes multi-robot observations into a shared memory, retrieves relevant context via spatio-temporal similarity, and encodes it using a predictive latent world model. The resulting representations are injected into downstream navigation agents as tokens. Experimental results demonstrate that SEER captures action-relevant environmental structure and consistently improves navigation performance across both specialized VLN agents and general vision-language model agents, while preserving single-agent capabilities.

llm.title_ja: Seeing Together, Acting Apart: マルチロボットナビゲーションのための共有環境理解
llm.tldr_ja: 複数のロボットの部分的な自己中心観測を共有の潜在世界モデルに集約し、表現空間での協調を可能にするSEERを提案した。
llm.problem: マルチロボットシステムは行動の調整や軌跡の共有によって協調するように設計されているが、表現の共有からのアプローチは不十分である。
llm.method: マルチロボットの観測を共有メモリに整理し、時空の類似性によって関連コンテキストを回収し、予測的潜在世界モデルで符号化する。
llm.result: ナビゲーション性能を継続的に向上させつつ、単一エージェントの能力を維持できることを示した。

2611.30310.tldr_en: This work proposes Shared Environment Encoding and Retrieval (SEER), a framework that organizes multi-robot observations into a shared memory, retrieves relevant context via spatio-temporal similarity, and encodes it using a predictive latent world model.

2611.30308.title: ConsisX: Cross-View Consistency Thinking in 3D for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.30308.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models integrate visual perception and language understanding from vision-language models (VLMs) with action prediction for robotic manipulation. Although multi-view observations provide complementary scene information, VLMs model cross-view interactions based on 2D feature similarity, which can lead to physical inconsistency in the form of cross-view incorrect association between distinct entities and cross-view information fragmentation about the same entity. To address these challenges, we propose ConsisX, a novel VLA framework that integrates cross-view association and entity coherence to enable cross-view consistency thinking in 3D for physically consistent robotic manipulation. Specifically, Cross-View Association Modeling (CAM) is proposed to introduce cross-view spatial proximity constraints in a shared 3D space to reduce cross-view incorrect association. Entity Coherence Organization (ECO) is designed to organize cross-view local information into coherent 3D entity evidence, thereby addressing cross-view information fragmentation. Consistent Action Conditioning (CAC) is introduced to condition action prediction on task-relevant 3D entity evidence for cross-view consistent action execution. Experiments on 3 real-world manipulation tasks and 4 simulation benchmarks establish ConsisX as an effective and competitive framework for robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: ConsisX: 視覚言語行動モデルのための3Dにおける視点間一貫性思考
llm.tldr_ja: 3D空間における視点間関連付けと実体一貫性を統合し、物理的に一貫したロボットマニピュレーションを実現するConsisXを提案した。
llm.problem: マルチビュー観測は補完的な情報を提供するが、2D特徴量に基づく従来のVLMは視点間の不正確な関連付けや情報の断片化を引き起こす。
llm.method: 共有3D空間での空間近接制約を導入するCAMと、局所情報を統合するECO、一貫した行動実行のためのCACを統合する。
llm.result: 3つの実世界マニピュレーションタスクと4つのシミュレーションベンチマークで有効性と競争力を実証した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.30308.tldr_en: Cross-View Association Modeling is proposed to introduce cross-view spatial proximity constraints in a shared 3D space to reduce cross-view incorrect association, and Entity Coherence Organization (ECO) is designed to organize cross-view local information into coherent 3D entity evidence, thereby addressing cross-view information fragmentation.

2611.30307.title: Robust Lateral String Stability and Error Attenuation for Heterogeneous Vehicle Platoons
2611.30307.abstract: Keeping an entire vehicle platoon close to its planned path is essential for navigating road boundaries and obstacles safely. Followers may rely on predecessor information for lateral guidance, which couples their lateral dynamics and allows errors to propagate downstream. This paper develops a robust lateral string stability framework to study this propagation and achieve downstream error attenuation in heterogeneous platoons under varying longitudinal motion and local perturbations. Arc-length-based feedback linearization gives each vehicle the same nominal lateral error dynamics, with parameter uncertainty and external disturbances represented as local perturbations. We define robust $\mathcal L_2$ lateral string stability in terms of platoon-length-uniform error bounds and derive a sufficient condition for achieving it. Furthermore, we show that the same condition guarantees platoon-length-uniform $\mathcal L_\infty$ error bounds. For the considered control formulations, predecessor tracking (PT) can accumulate lateral errors, whereas desired-path tracking (DT) prevents this accumulation. We propose a learn-from-predecessor (LFP) strategy with explicit gains for downstream error attenuation and characterize how intervehicle perturbation differences limit this attenuation. Simulations validate the theoretical findings under vehicle heterogeneity, varying longitudinal motion, and local perturbations.

llm.title_ja: ロバストな横方向ストリング安定性と異種車両プラトーンのための誤差減衰
llm.tldr_ja: 異種車両プラトーンにおける横方向誤差の伝播を研究し、下流での誤差減衰を実現するロバストな横方向ストリング安定性フレームワークを開発した。
llm.problem: 追従車が先行車情報に依存して横方向の誘導を行うと、動的特性が結合し誤差が下流に伝播して蓄積される。
llm.method: アーク長ベースのフィードバック線形化を用いて各車両に共通の横方向誤差ダイナミクスを与え、十分条件を導出する。
llm.result: 車両の異種性、縦方向運動の変化、局所的な外乱の下で理論的結果をシミュレーションにより検証した。

2611.30291.title: Beyond Which: Where, How, and When in Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.30291.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models typically rely on vision-language model (VLM) features as the primary perceptual source for action prediction, showing strong generalization across diverse robotic manipulation tasks. Although VLM features can identify which entities are relevant to action prediction, precise manipulation also requires understanding where task-relevant entities are located within the spatial layout, how their geometric structure constrains physical interaction, and when spatial or geometric information should make a greater contribution to action prediction. To this end, we introduce {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA to organize VLA perception and action prediction around which, where, how, and when. Specifically, {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA retains VLM-based semantic entity perception which and further introduces spatial distance perception where and geometric structure perception how with adaptive spatial-geometric guidance when to enrich the perceptual information available for action prediction. Experiments across real-world settings and simulation benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of {\mathcal{W}^{3}\mathcal{H}}-VLA.

llm.title_ja: Beyond Which: 視覚言語行動モデルにおけるWhere, How, When
llm.tldr_ja: VLAの知覚と行動予測をWhich、Where、How、Whenに基づいて統合的に組織化するW3H-VLAを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のVLAモデルはVLM特徴量に依存しているが、正確なマニピュレーションには位置や幾何学的構造の理解が必要である。
llm.method: 意味的実体知覚Whichに、空間距離知覚Whereと幾何学構造知覚Howを適応的空間幾何学ガイダンスWhenとともに導入する。
llm.result: 実世界の設定とシミュレーションベンチマークを通じてW3H-VLAの効果性と優れた性能を実証した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.30291.tldr_en: This work introduces W3H-VLA to organize VLA perception and action prediction around which, where, how, and when and introduces spatial distance perception where and geometric structure perception how with adaptive spatial-geometric guidance when to enrich the perceptual information available for action prediction.

2611.30265.title: SGPC: Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint for Stable Off-Policy Safe Reinforcement Learning
2611.30265.abstract: Off-policy safe reinforcement learning (RL) faces a challenging trade-off between task optimality and constraint feasibility. In primal-dual methods, the coupled optimization of cumulative reward and constraint penalties through adaptive Lagrange multipliers may induce oscillatory policy updates near the safety boundary and amplify the effect of unreliable reward estimates outside the safe set. To address these issues, we formulate a new constrained optimization problem (COP) for safe RL by introducing a Safety-Guiding Policy (SGP) and a corresponding Safety-Guiding Policy Constraint (SGPC). The proposed COP augments the standard COP in safe RL with a conditional safety-guidance constraint. During actor updates, the current actor is evaluated using the learned cost critic. If it is predicted to be outside the safe set, SGP provides a nearby lower-cost training reference, and SGPC guides actor optimization toward this reference. Once the policy enters the safe set, the added constraint becomes inactive, and the formulation reduces to the original COP. This formulation leads to a plug-in actor-training constraint that can be integrated into off-policy safe RL algorithms. By applying primal-dual optimization to the auxiliary COP, we finally derive an SGPC-based off-policy safe RL algorithm and implement it in two representative off-policy algorithms, yielding SAC-SGPC and TD3-SGPC. Experiments on multiple Safety-Gymnasium benchmarks demonstrate that SGPC achieves a better optimality-safety trade-off by substantially reducing constraint violations and cost oscillations while maintaining competitive or better task returns.

llm.title_ja: SGPC: 安定したオフポリシー型安全強化学習のための安全性誘導ポリシー制約
llm.tldr_ja: 安全性誘導ポリシーと対応する制約を導入することにより、制約違反と振動を大幅に削減して最適な方策とのトレードオフを改善するSGPCを提案した。
llm.problem: オフポリシー型の安全強化学習では、報酬最適性と制約充足性の間のトレードオフや最適化時の振動が課題となる。
llm.method: 条件付き安全性誘導制約を標準的な制約付き最適化問題に統合し、安全集合外のときに近傍の低コストな参照へと導く。
llm.result: Safety-Gymnasiumベンチマークにおいて、制約違反とコスト振動を大幅に削減しつつ競争力のあるタスク報酬を維持した。

2611.30265.tldr_en: Experiments on multiple Safety-Gymnasium benchmarks demonstrate that SGPC achieves a better optimality-safety trade-off by substantially reducing constraint violations and cost oscillations while maintaining competitive or better task returns.

2611.30264.title: Skill-Adaptive Noise Scheduling for Diffusion Policies
2611.30264.abstract: Recent advances in diffusion policies have demonstrated strong effectiveness when integrated into hierarchical skill-based learning frameworks, leveraging offline data to capture multimodal and temporally abstracted behaviors. However, prior approaches have rarely considered the diffusion process as a learnable component, adopting fixed noise schedules applied uniformly across skills, regardless of their distinct behavioral contexts. Such a design fundamentally limits the achievable performance, particularly for contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks where different skills exhibit distinct couplings between action dimensions. In this paper, we present a skill-adaptive noise diffusion framework (SaND) which introduces a learnable, skill-conditioned noise schedule that modulates the diffusion process per action dimension, adapting the noising dynamics to each skill. To prevent the learned noise schedule from collapsing into trivial solutions, we employ an auxiliary inverse objective that reconstructs the skill embedding from the Legendre coefficients of the derivative of the noise schedule, encouraging the schedules to remain skill-discriminative. This formulation naturally enables adaptive control over the denoising steps for each skill, where noise schedules are clustered in the Legendre coefficient space, and the appropriate number of denoising steps is determined at the point where reconstruction error abruptly increases. At inference, we identify each skill embedding's cluster from its noise schedule and apply the corresponding number of denoising steps, dedicating more compute to skills requiring fine-grained control and less to simpler ones. In simulation and on real robot hardware, SaND outperforms existing skill learning and planning baselines on contact-rich and dexterous manipulation tasks, achieving higher success rates while requiring fewer denoising steps.
2611.30264.comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

llm.title_ja: 拡散ポリシーのためのスキル適応型ノイズスケジューリング
llm.tldr_ja: 行動次元ごとのノイズダイナミクスを各スキルに適応させる学習可能なスキル条件付きノイズスケジュールを導入するSaNDフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の拡散ポリシーは拡散プロセスを固定コンポーネントとみなし、スキル特有の文脈を考慮せず一律のノイズスケジュールを適用している。
llm.method: スキル埋め込みを再構築する補助逆目的関数を用いて、スキルごとに区別可能なノイズスケジュールを学習する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実ロボットのハードウェア実験において、接触の多い器用なマニピュレーションタスクで既存手法を上回った。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.30264.tldr_en: A skill-adaptive noise diffusion framework (SaND) is presented which introduces a learnable, skill-conditioned noise schedule that modulates the diffusion process per action dimension, adapting the noising dynamics to each skill.

2611.30254.title: Innata-0: A Native Embodied World System with Model-Agent Co-Design
2611.30254.abstract: The physical world is open-ended, dynamic, and partially observable. While foundation models have advanced embodied intelligence, standalone models struggle with long-horizon execution, and simply integrating models with agents may lead to inconsistencies between planning and physical control. To support reliable and adaptive behaviors in the physical world, we introduce Innata-0, a native embodied world system. Innata-0 jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths. The model, Innata-0-WAM, adopts a tri-tower Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates understanding, prediction, and action generation. The agent, Innata-0-Agent, coordinates long-horizon execution through memory, verification, and recovery. A co-design protocol is further proposed to align model training with agent execution and leverage validated experiences to support subsequent adaptation and model improvement. Extensive evaluations demonstrate strong embodied capabilities across understanding, world prediction, and robotic manipulation. Innata-0 represents our first step toward physical intelligence, and we see it as the beginning of a much longer journey.

llm.title_ja: Innata-0: モデルとエージェントの共同設計によるネイティブ体現型世界システム
llm.tldr_ja: 体現型世界・行動モデルとエージェントを共同設計し、長期的実行における一貫性と適応性を高めたネイティブ世界システムInnata-0を提案した。
llm.problem: オープンエンドで動的な物理世界において、単体のモデルは長期実行が難しく、単純な統合では計画と物理制御の間に不整合が生じる。
llm.method: 理解・予測・行動生成を統合するMixture-of-Transformersアーキテクチャと、記憶・検証・リカバリーを行うエージェントを共同設計する。
llm.result: 理解、世界予測、ロボットマニピュレーションにわたって強力な体現型能力を実証した。
keywords_ja: モデル・エージェント共同設計

2611.30254.tldr_en: Innata-0 is introduced, a native embodied world system that jointly designs an embodied world-action model and an agent to combine their complementary strengths and demonstrates strong embodied capabilities across understanding, world prediction, and robotic manipulation.
2611.30254.hf_summary_en: Innata-0 is a native embodied world system that co-designs a world-action model and an agent to enable reliable long-horizon physical behaviors through integrated understanding, prediction, action generation, memory, verification, and recovery.

2611.30226.title: VeriWorld: A Verifiable Visual SWE-Bench for Spatial Reasoning in 3D Environments
2611.30226.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for spatial tasks such as navigation and manipulation, where they must infer geometry and object relationships from visual input in order to act correctly. Existing benchmarks usually test perception and reasoning in isolation, making it hard to tell whether failures come from visual understanding, downstream reasoning, or the bridge between them. We introduce VeriWorld, a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments with executable actions and deterministic verification. For task families where all three channels are well-defined, we evaluate matched visual, structured, and combined input conditions on the same instance, environment, and verifier; families without a clean visual/structured/combined split are reported separately. This design supports controlled comparisons of perception, reasoning, and their interaction. Using this setup, we uncover two diagnostic findings. First, models often perform much better when task-relevant information, such as object identity, current state, or target location, is given explicitly than when it must be read from the rendered scene, revealing a recurring visual-to-structure gap. Second, action-space and harness design can change outcomes even under the same task and information condition, showing that interaction protocol is itself a confounding variable. VeriWorld is open-sourced to support reproducible and fine-grained evaluation of spatial reasoning in VLMs.
2611.30226.comment: 32 pages, 5 figures. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations and Datasets Track. Code at https://github.com/VITA-Group/VeriWorld and dataset at https://huggingface.co/datasets/yanyanzheng96/VeriWorld

llm.title_ja: VeriWorld: 3D環境における空間推論のための検証可能なビジュアルSWE-Bench
llm.tldr_ja: 実行可能な行動と決定論的な検証を備えた対話型3D環境における空間推論ベンチマークVeriWorldを提案し、VLMの視覚から構造へのギャップを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは知覚と推論を個別にテストするため、失敗の原因がどこにあるのかを特定することが困難である。
llm.method: 同一のインスタンス、環境、検証器に対して、視覚的、構造的、および両者を組み合わせた入力条件を比較評価できる仕組みを構築する。
llm.result: 明示的に情報が与えられた場合にモデルの性能が大幅に向上するという視覚から構造へのギャップを発見した。

2611.30226.tldr_en: VeriWorld is open-sourced to support reproducible and fine-grained evaluation of spatial reasoning in VLMs, a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments with executable actions and deterministic verification.

2611.30209.title: RoboAda: Adapting Frozen Robot Policies at Test Time to Physics They Cannot See
2611.30209.abstract: Pretrained robot policies decide what to do from camera images, yet some of the physics that decides whether their plans succeed is not visible. An object may look light but be 100 times heavier, and a weakened joint or a lagging controller leaves no trace in the image. When the physics at deployment differs from training, the plan is often still right but is executed as if nothing had changed. Training on such variations in advance cannot handle unseen changes, while adapting once deployed either changes the plan, leaving the miscalibrated commands in place, or updates a robot model by gradient steps that do not know how reliable they are and can make the robot worse even when nothing has changed. We propose RoboAda, which keeps the policy and its plan unchanged and corrects the commands that carry it out by inferring at test time how the robot turns commands into motion. The key observation is that the robot's own motion reveals the change: after each action chunk, an inverse-dynamics model of the original robot converts the observed motion into the commands it would have needed, yielding free labels at every step. Competing hypotheses of how the robot responds, including that nothing has changed, are weighted by how well they predict these labels, and the next chunk is sent with the commands that best realize the plan under them. RoboAda needs no reward, no gradient step and no data from the changed robot. We evaluate RoboAda with five frozen policies on LIBERO, two world action models and three vision-language-action models. Under eleven physical shifts, it more than doubles their average success, from 27.8% to 62.9%. It beats the best of seven test-time adaptation methods by 17.3 points on Cosmos Policy, and largely preserves the policies' success when nothing has changed. On bimanual RoboTwin 2.0 in joint space, it raises success under joint-target offsets from 24.9% to 78.8%.

llm.title_ja: RoboAda: 見えない物理変化に適応するテスト時凍結ロボットポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: テスト時にロボットの逆ダイナミクスモデルを利用して行動コマンドを修正し、報酬や勾配なしで未見の物理変化に適応するRoboAdaを提案した。
llm.problem: デプロイ時の物理的環境が訓練時から変化している場合、計画は正しくてもコマンドが適切に実行されない問題がある。
llm.method: 観測された運動から必要なコマンドを逆推論し、複数の応答仮説の重み付けを行って次の行動チャンクを修正して送信する。
llm.result: LIBERO上の5つの凍結ポリシーにおいて、11の物理的シフト下で平均成功率を27.8%から62.9%へと2倍以上に向上させた。

2611.30209.tldr_en: RoboAda is proposed, which keeps the policy and its plan unchanged and corrects the commands that carry it out by inferring at test time how the robot turns commands into motion, and largely preserves the policies's success when nothing has changed.

2611.30204.title: Counterfactual Velocity Steering for World Action Models
2611.30204.abstract: Flow-based robot policies generate actions by repeatedly evaluating a conditional velocity field, so test-time bias correction seems simple: query the action expert under a task-agnostic condition and subtract that velocity from the task-conditioned prediction. We show this is often wrong. On Fast-WAM across 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, mean-instruction predictions align strongly with task-conditioned velocities (cosine approximately 0.94-0.95). Averaging eight completed-state references barely cancels this direction: their mean norm is 98.3% of the mean individual norm. References thus contain a large shared transport component, not only harmful bias, and aggressive subtraction damages generation. We propose a same-state diagnostic and shrinkage analysis showing that the optimal correction scale depends on reference signal-to-noise. This motivates geometry-calibrated action debiasing, which removes only the component orthogonal to the task velocity and predicts a small task-dependent scale from instruction geometry. In controlled RoboTwin experiments, corrupting instructions still permits 25.1% success (50 tasks, 20 episodes), whereas dynamic visual corruption nearly eliminates success. A fixed centered orthogonal correction reaches 92.7% versus a 92.1% baseline in one randomized 1000-trial sweep, but gains are non-monotonic and within run-to-run variation. An angular scale pilot has an offline oracle-gated bound of 94.5%; its best learned online realization reaches 92.5%. These results identify shared flow and train-serve mismatch as central obstacles and provide a reproducible foundation for conditional correction.

llm.title_ja: 世界行動モデルのための反実仮想速度ステアリング
llm.tldr_ja: 世界行動モデルにおける共通フローや訓練・サービス間の不一致の課題を分析し、タスク直交成分のみを除去する幾何学的較正デビアシングを提案した。
llm.problem: フローベースのロボットポリシーにおいて、タスク非依存条件でのクエリ速度を単純に差し引くバイアス修正は、共有トランスポート成分を含むため不適切である。
llm.method: 同一状態診断と縮小分析を行い、参照信号の信号対雑音比に応じた幾何学的較正行動デビアシングを適用する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0の実験において、固定された中心直交補正が92.7%の成功率に達することを示した。
keywords_ja: フローベースポリシー

2611.30204.tldr_en: This work proposes a same-state diagnostic and shrinkage analysis showing that the optimal correction scale depends on reference signal-to-noise, and identifies shared flow and train-serve mismatch as central obstacles and provide a reproducible foundation for conditional correction.

2611.30195.title: Quantization for Action, Execution for Deployment: Joint Precision and Execution Selection for World Action Models
2611.30195.abstract: World action models guide robots by predicting the effects of actions or generating commands from observations. A model may compare hundreds of candidate futures before acting, repeatedly reading weights that must fit in device memory. Post-training quantization reduces the number of bits used to store pretrained weights, but a smaller model is not necessarily a deployable one: temporary tensors can exceed graphics processing unit (GPU) memory limits, while even small prediction errors can change the selected action. This creates two coupled challenges: identifying bit assignments that preserve task performance and determining which of them meet real execution constraints, without exhausting costly task trials. We present PTQ4WAM, a framework for choosing layer-wise bit assignments and execution routes under memory, latency and task-evaluation budgets. Calibration measurements guide candidate proposals, optionally with a language model agent. We profile full-model routes on the GPU before spending task trials on feasible assignments. Fusing group rescaling and reading visual history in place can make an otherwise infeasible assignment deployable. Across 15 workloads from four model families, the median task score is 99.2% of the corresponding 32-bit floating-point (FP32) score. On fixed GPU replays, the median speedup over FP32 is 2.36 times and the median reduction in peak allocated memory is 71.5%. The code will be released soon.

llm.title_ja: Quantization for Action, Execution for Deployment: 世界行動モデルのための共同精度・実行選択
llm.tldr_ja: メモリ・遅延・タスク評価の制約下でレイヤーごとのビット割り当てと実行ルートを選択するフレームワークPTQ4WAMを提案した。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルの事後量子化において、小さいモデルは一時テンソルがGPUメモリ制限を超えたり、予測誤差が行動に影響を与えたりする課題がある。
llm.method: 較正測定に基づいて候補を提案し、グループ再スケーリングとビジュアル履歴のインプレース読み込みを融合してデプロイ可能にする。
llm.result: 15のワークロードにおいて、32ビット浮動小数点数（FP32）スコアの99.2%のタスクスコアを維持しつつ、中央値で2.36倍の高速化を達成した。

2611.30195.tldr_en: PTQ4WAM, a framework for choosing layer-wise bit assignments and execution routes under memory, latency and task-evaluation budgets, is presented and Calibration measurements guide candidate proposals, optionally with a language model agent.

2611.30193.title: Visual-RFT++: Extending Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning to Multimodal Tool Use
2611.30193.abstract: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) has recently become a central paradigm for advancing Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), as demonstrated by systems such as OpenAI's o3 and the R1 series. Despite significant progress in LLMs, how to leverage RFT to unify visual perception, step-by-step reasoning, and agentic tool use into one coherent training paradigm remains an open challenge. In this work, we present Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning++ (Visual-RFT++), a unified framework that extends RFT to both visual perception tasks and multimodal agentic workflows, enabling LVLMs to reason with images, act upon images, and evaluate their own outputs using verifiable reward. With Visual-RFT++, open-source LVLMs not only show significant gains on diverse visual perception tasks, but also acquire agentic abilities such as web searching for real-time information and code-based image manipulation (e.g., cropping, rotation, and analysis). Across visual perception tasks, including fine-grained classification, few-shot detection, reasoning grounding, and open-vocabulary detection, Visual-RFT++ delivers strong gains over SFT, including a +24.3 percentage points improvement in one-shot fine-grained classification and +21.0 percentage points on COCO's 4-shot setting and +15.4 percentage points on LVIS with around several hundred samples. To evaluate agentic behaviors, we introduce the Multimodal Agentic Tool Bench (MAT) with MAT-Search and MAT-Coding. Visual-RFT++ surpasses its baseline by +18.6 F1 / +13.0 EM percentage points on MAT-Coding and +10.3 F1 / +8.7 EM percentage points on MAT-Search. It also shows gains of 29.3 F1 and 25.9 EM percentage points on multi-hop QA benchmarks such as 2Wiki and HotpotQA, demonstrating strong cross-modal generalization. Visual-RFT++ introduces a data-efficient and reward-driven framework that strengthens both visual reasoning and agentic adaptability.
2611.30193.comment: Our code is available at https://github.com/Liuziyu77/Visual-RFT

llm.title_ja: Visual-RFT++: 視覚的強化学習ファインチューニングのマルチモーダルツール使用への拡張
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的知覚タスクとマルチモーダルエージェントワークフローの両方に強化学習ファインチューニングを拡張した統合フレームワークVisual-RFT++を提案した。
llm.problem: 大規模推論モデル向けに強化学習ファインチューニングが進展する中、視覚知覚やエージェントのツール使用を統一的な訓練パラダイムに統合することは課題である。
llm.method: 画像を用いた推論、行動、出力評価を検証可能な報酬を用いて行うマルチモーダルなエージェントワークフローを構築する。
llm.result: ファイングレイン分類などの視覚タスクでSFTを大きく上回り、MATベンチマークやマルチホップQAでも優れた汎化性能を示した。
keywords_ja: 強化学習ファインチューニング

2611.30193.tldr_en: This work presents Visual Reinforcement Fine-Tuning++ (Visual-RFT++), a unified framework that extends RFT to both visual perception tasks and multimodal agentic workflows, enabling LVLMs to reason with images, act upon images, and evaluate their own outputs using verifiable reward.

2611.30188.title: Calibrating World Action Models: From Adaptive System 2 Takeover to Self-Evolution
2611.30188.abstract: World action models (WAMs) deliver fast visuomotor control, yet degrade sharply in challenging scenes and act blindly when about to fail; conversely, foundation-model-based agents generalize and recover reliably, but incur prohibitive latency and cost when queried at every step. To achieve both WAM (System 1)-level speed and agent (System 2)-level reliability--- we propose \textbf{\oursfull (\ours)}, a framework that calibrates WAMs' confidence--- adaptively triggering System~2 only when necessary, and distilling System~2's knowledge to form an evolving System~1. First, \ours equips a frozen WAM with \textbf{calibrated self-assessment}: a single lightweight judgment token reading internal video--action features is trained via our proposed \textbf{cross-fitted temporal-difference (TD) learning} using only binary rollout success/failure signals. It can predict a \textbf{calibrated success probability} at negligible overhead without affecting action predictions. Second, this calibrated success probability schedules control chunk by chunk---invoking System~2 to resolve bottlenecks when confidence drops, and handing control back to the WAM once confidence recovers, preserving WAM-like speed while approaching System~2 reliability. Third, as System~2 intervenes only when the WAM lacks confidence, its takeover trajectories directly capture the WAM's capability gaps. JiL distills these takeovers into the WAM to repair those gaps so System~1 can operate standalone without System~2 at test time, while our mastered-skill anchoring and dynamic confidence gating prevent degrading existing capabilities.

llm.title_ja: 世界行動モデルの較正: 適応型システム2テイクオーバーから自己進化へ
llm.tldr_ja: 世界行動モデル（WAM）に較正された自己評価機能を付与し、必要な場合にのみシステム2を適応的に呼び出すことで、速度と信頼性を両立するJiLを提案した。
llm.problem: WAMは高速な制御を行うが困難な場面で性能が大きく低下し、逆にエージェントベースの手法はレイテンシとコストが非常に高い。
llm.method: クロスフィット時間差分学習を用いて軽量な判断トークンを訓練し、確信度が低下したときのみシステム2を呼び出してモデルを修正する。
llm.result: WAMの高速性を維持しながらシステム2の信頼性に近づき、WAM単体での自己自律稼働を実現した。

2611.30188.tldr_en: A framework that calibrates WAMs'confidence--- adaptively triggering System~2 only when necessary, and distilling System~2's knowledge to form an evolving System~1, to achieve both WAM (System 1)-level speed and agent (System 2)-level reliability.

2611.30184.title: OmniSLAM: Evidence-Authorized Revision of Persistent Object Maps
2611.30184.abstract: A new surface observation can extend an object map while contradicting an earlier object assignment. Treating both updates as a single merge can join unrelated objects; keeping all earlier assignments leaves fragmented objects unresolved. We present a revision module that makes these decisions separately. Historical merges require shared-mask evidence to outweigh separate-object explanations across views, including after removal of any one observation. New measured points are assigned through local competition among object seeds supported by image masks. On two preselected KITTI-360 windows, the method improves mean building/car instance AP50:90 from 17.259 to 18.762. On four further spatial holdouts, AP rises from 20.263 to 23.171, although unconditional revision reaches 23.251. Controlled comparisons attribute the gains to protecting existing identities, consolidating selected fragments, and assigning new points locally. The results also show where conservative merge decisions suppress useful updates. A garage recording demonstrates the same revision module on LiDAR--inertial--visual mapping outputs.
2611.30184.tldr_en: A map-revision module that separates historical identity changes from new-surface admission is presented, identifying where observation-supported revision improves object maps and where conservative decisions still limit recovery.

2611.30179.title: Trustworthy agentic lunar robotics: safety-constrained contingent planning with a foundation-model planner
2611.30179.abstract: Sustained lunar-base operations require robots that restore equipment and deliver cargo under conditions unforeseen before deployment. Flown space autonomy executes pre-validated procedures and enters a safe hold outside their scope, whereas foundation models synthesize plans on site that cannot be verified before execution. We formulate these operations as safety-constrained contingent planning with irreversible actions, erroneous records, three-valued physical evidence, and costly, deadline-constrained sensing. We propose asymmetric knowledge-level replanning (AKR), which treats the planner as an untrusted black box: reversible actions run on the planner's assumptions, and irreversible actions run only after a minimum-cost sensing cover verifies every precondition. Under sound measurements, no irreversible action executes on a false precondition for any planner or record, the sensing cost before an irreversible action is bounded below for every sound knowledge-based policy, and execution with a complete planner ends in a verified goal or a certified hold. AKR executed no hazardous action in 21,000 Monte Carlo trials with sound observations or in 58 full-stack runs; the FF-Replan acting rule executed one in 7% of those trials. The median AKR run took 1.10 times the fastest run on the same mission, against 1.50 under the K-replanner acting rule. AKR completed 20 of 21 contingency and sequential-fault runs with an unchanged task model; the original PLEXIL and EUROPA$\rightarrow$PLEXIL procedures completed none.

llm.title_ja: 信頼性の高いエージェント型月面ロボット: 基盤モデルプランナーを用いた安全性制約付き条件付計画
llm.tldr_ja: プランナーを信頼できないブラックボックスとして扱い、可逆・不可逆な行動の制御を分離して安全性を保証する非対称知識レベル再計画（AKR）を提案した。
llm.problem: 月面基地の運用では未予測の条件下で機器の復旧や貨物配送が必要となるが、基盤モデルは事前に検証できない計画を生成する課題がある。
llm.method: 可逆行動はプランナーの仮定で実行し、不可逆行動は最小コストのセンシングカバーが前提条件を検証した後にのみ実行する。
llm.result: 21,000回のモンテカルロ試行および58回のフルスタック実行において有害な行動を一切実行せず、高い完了率を達成した。

2611.30179.tldr_en: This work proposes asymmetric knowledge-level replanning (AKR), which treats the planner as an untrusted black box: reversible actions run on the planner's assumptions, and irreversible actions run only after a minimum-cost sensing cover verifies every precondition.

2611.30178.title: Quantizing in the Loop: Drift-Aware Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.30178.abstract: Deploying large vision-language-action (VLA) models on resource-constrained robots demands extreme compression, yet existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods frequently collapse at ultra-low bit-widths ($\le$ 2 bits). We trace this failure to two mismatches in standard pipelines. First, calibrating on static offline demonstrations induces distribution shift: minor quantization perturbations drive the policy into unseen states where uncalibrated errors compound. Second, minimizing the layer-wise weight reconstruction error is a flawed proxy, as action generation depends only on the representations consumed by the action head. We present LoopQ, an on-policy ultra-low-bit quantization framework. LoopQ closes the loop by calibrating on states from the quantized policy's own rollouts. It then adds readout-aligned fine-tuning, which freezes the trellis codes and optimizes only lightweight lookup tables and scaling factors to align the backbone readout with the full-precision teacher. With all linear layers at 2 bits, LoopQ achieves a 60.4% success rate on LIBERO-Plus with GR00T N1.7, close to the 61.8% of full precision. Even at 1 bit per weight, $π_{0.5}$ still completes 80.0% of LIBERO tasks. With 8-bit activations, the 2-bit $π_{0.5}$ runs on integer kernels on an embedded NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor, with 4.1$\times$ smaller weights and 44% less memory. On a real AgileX Piper arm, it stays within one success of full precision on each of three tasks. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/ForeverBlue816/LoopQ
2611.30178.comment: The paper is currently under review. Code and models: https://github.com/ForeverBlue816/LoopQ

llm.title_ja: ループ内量子化：ドリフトを考慮した超低ビット視覚・言語・行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ポリシー自体のロールアウト状態での較正と読み出し整列ファインチューニングを行うことで、性能低下を抑えた超低ビットVLA量子化フレームワークLoopQを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の事後量子化（PTQ）は、静的データの較正による分布シフトや重み再構成誤差の不適切さにより超低ビットで破綻する。
llm.method: 量子化ポリシー自身のロールアウト状態での較正を行い、トレリスコードを固定してルックアップテーブル等を最適化するLoopQを提案する。
llm.result: 全線形層2ビットでLIBERO-Plusにおいて60.4%の成功率を達成し、実機のアームでも高精度を維持した。

2611.30178.tldr_en: LoopQ is presented, an on-policy ultra-low-bit quantization framework that closes the loop by calibrating on states from the quantized policy's own rollouts, which adds readout-aligned fine-tuning, which freezes the trellis codes and optimizes only lightweight lookup tables and scaling factors to align the backbone readout with the full-precision teacher.

2611.30173.title: Confidently Lost: Silent Failure and Edge Deployment of Dense Visual SLAM under Photon Starvation
2611.30173.abstract: Dense visual SLAM built on learned two-view geometry is evaluated in good light; in low light it fails silently. Two frames of 9-level quantized noise, no scene at all, give MASt3R-SLAM's network a cross-view geometric self-consistency of 0.936; a real dark frame pair gives 0.935. Starved of structure, the network invents the same geometry for both views and the system trusts the agreement: on a dark sequence it consumes 1,605 frames, emits 7 keyframes, rejects no factor-graph edges and reports full frame rate, while over 95% of the correspondences it accepts violate the ground-truth epipolar geometry. One inflated statistic is read by two subsystems against thresholds in opposite directions, so keyframing starves while relocalization accepts almost every candidate. The same statistic, read at keyframe-pair baselines, separates the confident collapse from working runs on the ETH3D dark sequences without ground truth or extra computation (in-sample). Low-light-adapted weights take tracked trajectories from 1/6 to 5/6, as does retuning two thresholds; neither yields accurate ones, because the adaptation withdraws confidence from wrong geometry rather than finding right geometry. Replayed on a Jetson AGX Orin carried by a legged robot, the mechanism's signature reproduces on the two darkest of four routes, and which of its faces appears varies with route geometry and sensor encoding. The network does not lose confidence in the dark; it manufactures it.
2611.30173.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027

llm.title_ja: 自信を持った迷子：光量不足下における密なビジュアルSLAMのサイレント失敗とエッジ展開
llm.tldr_ja: 学習ベースの密なビジュアルSLAMは低照度下で構造の欠如を自己矛盾のない幾何学として誤認し、誤った確信を持って破綻することを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 暗所において密なビジュアルSLAMが誤った幾何学を高い確信度で生成し、検証されずにシステム全体が誤動作する。
llm.method: 低照度下のデータセットとエッジデバイスを用いた、視覚SLAMの挙動と統計量の詳細な分析。
llm.result: 暗所ではネットワークが幾何学を「製造」し、不正確な軌跡を出力することがシミュレーションおよび四足歩行ロボットの実機で確認された。

2611.30173.tldr_en: Low-light-adapted weights take tracked trajectories from 1/6 to 5/6, as does retuning two thresholds; neither yields accurate ones, because the adaptation withdraws confidence from wrong geometry rather than finding right geometry.

2611.30171.title: Audio-Visual Rearrangement
2611.30171.abstract: We introduce Audio-Visual Rearrangement (AVR), a novel task in which an agent hears a spoken request, retrieves a suitable object, and delivers it to the requesting user or an instruction-specified destination. AVR requires the agent to understand the spoken request and acoustically localize the speaker for delivery. To support this task, we construct a dataset covering three query types: explicit target specification, speaker-relative spatial references, and implicit user intent, spanning eight subtypes with diverse object selection and delivery requirements. Moreover, we propose a framework that integrates a motion-aware spatial audio module into an audio-visual large language model to encode spatial cues from the spoken request and update them as the agent moves. We further incorporate auxiliary supervision for speech understanding, spatial audio perception, and visual grounding through multitask instruction tuning to improve action prediction. Experiments establish baseline performance in both seen and unseen environments, laying the groundwork for future research on embodied intelligence and human-robot interaction. The code will be publicly available soon.

llm.title_ja: 音声・視覚リアレンジメント
llm.tldr_ja: 音声による要求を理解して適切なオブジェクトを回収・配送する新しいタスク「AVR」を提案し、運動認識型空間オーディオモジュールを統合したフレームワークを開発した。
llm.problem: エージェントが音声による指示を理解し、音響的に発話者を局所化して物体を配送する統合的なタスクの不在。
llm.method: マルチタスク指示チューニングにより、音声理解、空間オーディオ知覚、視覚的接地を統合するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 既知および未知の環境でのベースライン性能を確立し、embodied AIとHRIの基礎を築いた。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.30171.tldr_en: This work introduces Audio-Visual Rearrangement (AVR), a novel task in which an agent hears a spoken request, retrieves a suitable object, and delivers it to the requesting user or an instruction-specified destination, and proposes a framework that integrates a motion-aware spatial audio module into an audio-visual large language model to encode spatial cues from the spoken request and update them as the agent moves.

2611.30166.title: Toward Open Room-Scale Scanning with Consumer LiDAR via Depth-Inertial Odometry
2611.30166.abstract: Room scanning with consumer LiDAR today depends on ARKit, whose tracking and map update are a black box: an application receives depth and poses but cannot inspect how they were produced, so an error in a scan cannot be traced to its cause. This paper examines whether an open alternative, one whose every stage can be inspected, is feasible on the device. Mobile-LIO is a depth-inertial odometry pipeline that uses the phone's depth and inertial data and no ARKit poses.
