On seven ScanNet++ iPhone recordings it completed every scene with 0.2-2.0 m deviation from the ARKit-derived reference, where six open-source LiDAR-inertial estimators run as configured for dedicated scanners had at least 4.46 m in 41 of 42 runs (two of the six also failed a noise-free adapter check, and Mobile-LIO has a speed cap they lack; the comparison is not controlled and does not rone 15 Pro Max, a buildwith corrected phone code kept up with the sensor in 14 of 15 replay runs of three 7-13 s recordings; e estimator before thosecorrections. Laser-scanned meshes give the accuracy. Within 3 m, recorded depth differed from the m on three held-out scenes,maps fused with ARKit poses that the dataset scales and aligns to the mesh la a median 1.8-2.3 cm from 17 cm. Because thepipeline is open, the gap could be examined: in the scene with the largest error, noise-free renderefrom 1.97 m to 0.04 m, sorecorded depth, whose error reached 20-54 cm at 5-7 m, contributed alongside the estimator. An open de tracked on phone depth and kept up with the sensor in short phone replays, but it is not yet as accurate as ARKit-pose maps, whicheach only the coarsestUSIBD accuracy level (LOA10); its accuracy on the device was not measured.

llm.title_ja: 深度慣性オドメトリを用いたコンシューマー向けLiDARによるオープンな部屋スケールスキャニングに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: ARKitに依存せず、すべての段階を検証可能なオープンな深度慣性オドメトリパイプラインMobile-LIOを提案し、モバイルデバイスでの部屋スキャン性能を評価した。
llm.problem: 既存の部屋スキャンはブラックボックスのARKitに依存しており、エラーの原因追跡が困難である。
llm.method: デバイスの深度データと慣性データのみを使用するオープンな深度慣性オドメトリパイプラインMobile-LIOを構築した。
llm.result: ScanNet++の録画においてARKit基準から0.2〜2.0mの偏差でシーンを完了し、既存の推定手法を大きく上回る精度を示した。
llm.limitation: ARKitポーズを用いたマップほど正確ではない点、および精度向上の余地がある。
keywords_ja: モバイルロボティクス

2611.30166.tldr_en: This paper examines whether an open alternative, one whose every stage can be inspected, is feasible on the device, and examines Mobile-LIO, a depth-inertial odometry pipeline that uses the phone's depth and inertial data and no ARKit poses.

2611.30149.title: LeadVLA: Learning Follower-Aware Route Execution for Robot Leading
2611.30149.abstract: Robot leading requires executing a route while continuously adapting to a designated follower. Existing robot-leading systems often mediate follower understanding and physical route execution through explicit states, planners, or modular interfaces; directly learning this coupling through end-to-end trajectory prediction can instead entangle route execution with follower response. We introduce LeadVLA, a structured multimodal policy that preserves the route as an explicit Path reference while learning a Pace for route progress and a Residual for local follower- and scene-conditioned adaptation. To make this problem trainable and measurable, we develop LeadInfra, a configurable Unreal Engine-based closed-loop data-generation infrastructure from which we instantiate an approximately 4M-sample training corpus, and LeadBench, a standardized benchmark with 108 fully held-out closed-loop episodes. LeadVLA achieves the highest task success (39.6%) among evaluated robot policies on LeadBench while maintaining strong route fidelity and follower responsiveness, and transfers to unseen real-world environments without real-world policy fine-tuning. Project Page: https://louiszengCN.github.io/LeadVLA_PAGE/

llm.title_ja: LeadVLA：ロボット先導のためのフォロワーを考慮したルート実行の学習
llm.tldr_ja: ルートの参照パス、ペース、フォロワー適応の残差を構造化して学習するマルチモーダルポリシー「LeadVLA」を提案し、実機環境へのゼロショット移転を実現した。
llm.problem: ロボットの先導において、明示的なプランナーやモジュールによるフォロワー理解と軌跡予測の統合が困難である。
llm.method: 明示的なパス参照、ペース、および残留適応を学習する構造化マルチモーダルポリシーLeadVLAと、データ生成基盤LeadInfraを開発した。
llm.result: LeadBenchにおいて最高成功率（39.6%）を達成し、現実世界の未見環境への転移に成功した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルポリシー
シミュレーションデータ
ヒューマンロボット協調

2611.30149.tldr_en: LeadVLA, a structured multimodal policy that preserves the route as an explicit Path reference while learning a Pace for route progress and a Residual for local follower- and scene-conditioned adaptation, is introduced.
2611.30149.hf_summary_en: LeadVLA is a structured multimodal policy that separates route execution into explicit path, pace, and residual components, trained and evaluated with generated closed-loop data and a benchmark, achieving the highest success among tested robot policies and transferring to unseen real environments without fine-tuning.

2611.30145.title: RMR-VLA: Recurrent Memory Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.30145.abstract: Long-horizon, history-dependent robotic manipulation often requires acting on visual cues that have disappeared, such as an object indicated earlier or a target hidden under a moving cup. The key challenge is to maintain what past evidence means for the next action as the scene changes. We introduce Recurrent Memory Reasoning (RMR), an explicit reasoning step that connects memory to action inside a vision-language-action model (VLA), with no external reasoning model. At each update, the VLA first infers an event from visual evidence, then revises the task state and grounds a subgoal in the current scene to guide action generation. Carrying the state and subgoal across updates lets remembered identities and task progress determine the current target, doubling RoboMME success over an otherwise identical model without recurrence. Joint training lets one VLA both reason and act; because its memory decisions are text tokens with exact likelihoods, GRPO refines them from rollout rewards without making action generation stochastic. Among the compared methods, RMR-VLA achieves the best results on RoboMME (66.46% overall, 79.83% on the Reference category) and LIBERO-Mem (90.08%).

llm.title_ja: RMR-VLA：視覚・言語・行動モデルのためのリカレントメモリ推論
llm.tldr_ja: 外部の推論モデルを用いず、メモリと行動を接続する明示的な推論ステップ（RMR）をVLAに導入し、隠れた対象や過去の手がかりに基づく長期的なマニピュレーションを可能にした。
llm.problem: 長期かつ履歴に依存するロボット操作において、視覚的の手がかりが消えた際の状態維持と行動への反映が困難である。
llm.method: 視覚的証拠からイベントを推論し、タスク状態を改訂してサブゴールを接地するリカレントメモリ推論（RMR）をVLAに組み込む。
llm.result: RoboMMEおよびLIBERO-Memにおいて、従来モデルの2倍の成功率を達成し優れた性能を示した。
keywords_ja: リカレントニューラルネットワーク

2611.30145.tldr_en: Recurrent Memory Reasoning is introduced, an explicit reasoning step that connects memory to action inside a vision-language-action model (VLA) with no external reasoning model, doubling RoboMME success over an otherwise identical model without recurrence.

2611.30133.title: Value function based Reward shaping for safety in quadrupeds
2611.30133.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has progressed from simple control tasks to complex real-world challenges with large state spaces. While RL excels in these tasks, training time remains a limitation. Reward shaping is a popular solution, but existing methods often rely on value functions, which face scalability issues. This paper presents a novel safety-oriented reward-shaping framework inspired by barrier functions, offering simplicity and ease of implementation across various environments and tasks. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed reward formulations, we conduct simulation experiments on the Unitree Go1 quadruped robot in Isaacgym. The policy was better than the existing baselines and reduced safety violations from 27% to 0.1% without almost any compromise on the performance.

llm.title_ja: 四足歩行ロボットの安全性のための価値関数ベースの報酬シェイピング
llm.tldr_ja: バリア関数にインスパイアされた新しい安全性指向の報酬シェイピングフレームワークを提案し、Isaacgymを用いたシミュレーションで安全性違反を大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: 強化学習におけるトレーニング時間の制限と、既存の報酬シェイピング手法における価値関数のスケーラビリティの課題。
llm.method: バリア関数に着想を得たシンプルで実装しやすい安全性指向の報酬シェイピングフレームワークを設計した。
llm.result: Unitree Go1を用いたシミュレーションにおいて、性能をほとんど落とさずに安全性違反を27%から0.1%に削減した。

2611.30133.tldr_en: A novel safety-oriented reward-shaping framework inspired by barrier functions is presented, offering simplicity and ease of implementation across various environments and tasks, and is evaluated on the effectiveness of the proposed reward formulations.

2611.30120.title: AxE: Benchmarking Agent-Environment Generalization of Video World Models via Grounded Events
2611.30120.abstract: Edge cases are not the long tail; they are the norm. An embodied system deployed across changing environments, bodies, objects, and tasks will routinely encounter combinations that were absent from its training data. General-purpose physical intelligence therefore requires world models that reuse prior knowledge, predict consequences, and adapt with little or no additional training. Yet current evaluations of conditional video generation emphasize visual quality, prompt alignment, or isolated physical plausibility, leaving systematic generalization difficult to measure. We introduce AxE Bench, a benchmark that organizes condition changes along eight factors of the acting agent and of its environment, and pairs every original condition with controlled variants that change one side or both. WBench-plus applies the same structure to an existing multi-turn benchmark, pairing each WBench scenario with variants on the environment side, through its world setting or camera behavior, or on the agent side, through its interaction instructions. Additionally, to score generated futures, we develop an evaluation harness that combines vision-language reasoning with targeted computer-vision evidence, converting each video into temporally localized events and comparing generated events with reference events in both time and semantics. We summarize each model with the AxE Score, event Fidelity weighted by its Stability across original-variant pairs. Across twenty models, generated events match reference events far more often in timing than in content: no model exceeds a Fidelity of 13.01, the highest Stability is 0.55, and the highest AxE Score is 7.10. Together, these components turn world-model generalization from an informal aspiration into a falsifiable evaluation program for real and simulated interactions. Our project website can be found at: AxEBench.github.io

llm.title_ja: AxE：接地されたイベントを通じたビデオ世界モデルのエージェント環境汎化のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントと環境の条件変更に基づく8つの要因で汎化性能を評価するベンチマーク「AxE Bench」を提案し、既存のビデオ世界モデルの課題を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 現在のビデオ世界モデルの評価は視覚品質や孤立した物理的妥当性に偏っており、体系的な汎化性能の測定が困難である。
llm.method: エージェントと環境の条件変更を整理したAxE Benchと、ビジョン言語推論とコンピュータビジョンを組み合わせた評価ハーネスを開発した。
llm.result: 20モデルの評価により、生成されたイベントの内容はタイミングよりも一致しにくいことが示され、最高AxEスコアは7.10にとどまった。

2611.30120.tldr_en: AxE Bench is introduced, a benchmark that organizes condition changes along eight factors of the acting agent and of its environment, and pairs every original condition with controlled variants that change one side or both, and WBench-plus applies the same structure to an existing multi-turn benchmark, pairing each WBench scenario with variants.

2611.30111.title: RoboThink: Let the Agent Think, Let the Policy Act
2611.30111.abstract: Robot policies act in real time but fail without knowing why, whereas a reasoning agent that watches the robot can often tell what went wrong. Existing systems either hand the agent control, which takes minutes per episode, or let it send instructions. Yet a policy follows a new instruction only from a fresh start, since a half-finished task leaves it in states outside its training data. Nor can an instruction fix how the robot moves. If a drift keeps pulling the hand to the left, "push right, slightly" is not a task the policy has learned. We propose RoboThink, in which the agent thinks and the policy learns to act on the agent's guidance. An instruction channel tells the policy what to do. When the user says "the milk, not the butter" after the robot has started, the agent rewrites the instruction and the robot undoes its own motion, with no training. A feedback channel tells it how to move. It is taught from the agent alone with agent-labelled DAgger, role tokens and counterfactual feedback, and is read only by the policy's action module. On LIBERO, RoboThink with Claude Opus 5.5 raises success from 0.09 to 0.87 under an unknown constant drift and from 0.42 to 0.84 under a random one. It also completes misheard and changed requests in 0.91 to 1.00 of the episodes. Acting alone, GPT-6 Astra needs 2.1 min per success and over a million tokens per episode, whereas RoboThink needs 55 s and 8k tokens. The same recipe works across policies, for both vision-language-action models and world action models, and across robots, from one arm to two arms and a mobile manipulator. On all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks with two arms, success rises from 0.12 to 0.74 under the constant drift and from 0.31 to 0.56 under the random one. Finally, the agent is a plug-in. A policy taught by one agent works with other agents, including open-weight ones, and grows stronger with a stronger agent, without retraining.

llm.title_ja: RoboThink：エージェントに思考させ、ポリシーに行動させる
llm.tldr_ja: エージェントが思考して指示やフィードバックを与え、ポリシーがそれを元に行動する「RoboThink」を提案し、外乱や動的な指示変更に対する頑健性を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: ロボットポリシーは実時間で動作するが失敗理由が分からず、エージェントに直接制御を渡すと多大な時間とトークンを消費する。
llm.method: 指示チャンネルとフィードバックチャンネルを設け、エージェントが思考したガイダンスに基づいてポリシーが行動する枠組みを構築した。
llm.result: LIBEROおよびRoboTwinにおいて、一定のドリフトやランダムなドリフト、動的な指示変更に対して高い成功率と効率的な処理を実現した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボット協調

2611.30111.tldr_en: The proposed RoboThink, in which the agent thinks and the policy learns to act on the agent's guidance, works across policies, for both vision-language-action models and world action models, and across robots, from one arm to two arms and a mobile manipulator.

2611.30101.title: Agent on Guard: Self-Improving Runtime Intervention for Robust Robotic Manipulation
2611.30101.abstract: Robot foundation policies provide learned execution capabilities, while programming agents can reason about failures and construct recovery behaviors. Combining them effectively requires learning when intervention helps and when the policy can reliably resume. This challenge is inherently temporal: the physical world continues to evolve during reasoning, and a useful recovery may become infeasible before a decision takes effect. We introduce Agent on Guard (AoG), a hierarchical framework that improves collaboration between a frozen base policy and a programming agent through physical experience. An evolving outer planner allocates control as the physical state evolves, aligning decisions with the physical clock with attention to observation freshness, remaining recovery windows, and the time required for reasoning, recovery, and subsequent execution. Coupled inner loops jointly refine intervention timing, recovery skills, and handoff conditions. Rather than judging recovery by local correction alone, AoG uses downstream task progress, failure recurrence, final outcomes, and resource consumption to improve both recovery behaviors and scheduling. This turns temporary agent solutions into reusable collaboration capabilities that complement the frozen policy. On RoboDojo-Sim, AoG achieves a success rate of 50.57% and a task score of 57.26, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 11.22 percentage points and 10.68 points, respectively. It also reduces end-to-end episode latency by 80.4% and online token consumption by 85.1% relative to the GPT-6 Astra agent.

llm.title_ja: エージェントの監視：頑健なロボット操作のための自己改善型ランタイム介入
llm.tldr_ja: フローズンベースポリシーとプログラミングエージェントの協調を物理的時間に合わせて最適化する階層型フレームワーク「Agent on Guard (AoG)」を提案した。
llm.problem: 学習済みのポリシーと失敗からの復旧を行うプログラミングエージェントを組み合わせる際、物理的変化の時間的整合性を保つことが困難である。
llm.method: 観測の新鮮さや推論時間を考慮しながら制御を割り当てる、階層型フレームワークAoGを導入した。
llm.result: RoboDojo-Simにおいて、既存ベースラインを上回る成功率を達成し、レイテンシとトークン消費量を大幅に削減した。

2611.30101.tldr_en: This work introduces Agent on Guard (AoG), a hierarchical framework that improves collaboration between a frozen base policy and a programming agent through physical experience that turns temporary agent solutions into reusable collaboration capabilities that complement the frozen policy.

2611.30099.title: Policy-intrinsic Demonstration Curation
2611.30099.abstract: Fine-tuning a robot policy for a new target task requires target demonstrations, but only a few are available. Demonstrations of other tasks can fill this gap, and demonstration curation selects the useful ones among these candidates. Retrieval-based curation selects the candidates that are most similar to the target demonstrations. Since it does not use the policy, any candidate that looks similar receives a high score. Performance-aware curation therefore estimates the effect of each candidate on the policy. However, this requires training on the candidates and takes a long time. We propose a third branch, policy-intrinsic curation, which uses the policy and still takes little time. It estimates this effect with forward passes of the pretrained policy and needs no training. We instantiate this branch with PICKER (Policy-Intrinsic Curation from Known Errors). It selects the candidates on which the policy makes errors that agree with those on the target demonstrations. PICKER reaches success rates comparable to those of performance-aware curation and takes about as long as retrieval-based curation. Its selection is also stable across seeds.
2611.30099.comment: 15 pages (including 1 page of references and 6 pages of appendices), 5 figures, 7 tables

llm.title_ja: ポリシー内因的デモンストレーション選定
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みポリシーの順伝播のみを利用し、訓練を行わずに有効なデモンストレーションを選定する手法「PICKER」を提案した。
llm.problem: 新しいタスクのファインチューニングにはデモンストレーションが必要だが少数しか得られず、既存の選定手法は時間がかかるか精度が低い。
llm.method: 事前学習済みポリシーのエラーが目標デモンストレーションのエラーと一致する候補を選ぶポリシー内因的キュレーション手法PICKERを開発した。
llm.result: 性能認識型キュレーションと同等の成功率を達成しつつ、検索ベースのキュレーションと同等の高速な処理時間を実現した。
keywords_ja: デモンストレーション選定
ファインチューニング

2611.30099.tldr_en: A third branch, policy-intrinsic curation, is proposed, which uses the policy and still takes little time and selects the candidates on which the policy makes errors that agree with those on the target demonstrations.

2611.30083.title: MotionServe: Efficient Multi-Robot Serving by Exploiting Robot Execution Slack
2611.30083.abstract: As robotic arms undertake diverse manipulation tasks, a deployment may need to serve many task-specific vision-language-action (VLA) policies concurrently. Dedicating a GPU to each robot is costly, motivating shared-GPU inference. Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) allows compatible policies to share a frozen backbone with lightweight policy-specific adapters, reducing model-weight memory and enabling cross-policy batching. However, robot inference must keep pace with physical execution. With action chunking, robots continue executing buffered actions while awaiting new predictions, and the remaining buffered time provides each robot's execution slack for serving its next request. Once this slack is exhausted, the robot stalls until new actions arrive, interrupting task progress. Observing earlier preserves more slack but can lead to disruptive replanning and lower task success, whereas delaying dispatch to form larger batches can improve GPU efficiency but consumes slack and risks stalls. To balance these competing demands, we present MotionServe, a shared-GPU serving system that coordinates robot observation timing with server-side batch formation. MotionExec selects observation triggers based on motion structure in predicted action chunks, allowing inference to overlap with remaining buffered execution. SlackBatch combines the resulting per-robot execution budgets with estimated outstanding GPU work to determine when to wait, which requests to batch, and when to dispatch them. We evaluate X-VLA on LIBERO and SimplerEnv's WidowX tasks and OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO, with up to 96 simulated robots sharing one NVIDIA H200 GPU. At 96 robots, MotionServe reduces mean stall per episode by 43.4% and 32.6% and improves task success by 8.98 and 2.30 percentage points, respectively, over each model's lowest-stall baseline. Backbone sharing also reduces weight memory for 96 policies by 97.6% and 91.1%.

llm.title_ja: MotionServe：ロボットの実行スラックを活用した効率的なマルチロボットサービング
llm.tldr_ja: アクションチャンキングの実行余裕（スラック）を利用して複数のロボットでVLAポリシーを効率的に共有・推論するシステム「MotionServe」を提案した。
llm.problem: 複数のロボットがタスク特化型のVLAポリシーを共有GPUで同時に実行する際、推論遅延が物理的な実行を妨げる。
llm.method: 予測アクションの運動構造に基づいて観測トリガーを選択するMotionExecと、バッチ形成を調整するSlackBatchを統合したサービングシステムを構築した。
llm.result: 96台のシミュレーションロボットで検証し、平均ストール時間を大幅に削減しタスク成功率を向上させた。

2611.30083.tldr_en: MotionServe is presented, a shared-GPU serving system that coordinates robot observation timing with server-side batch formation that reduces mean stall per episode and improves task success over each model's lowest-stall baseline, and SlackBatch combines the resulting per-robot execution budgets with estimated outstanding GPU work to determine when to wait.

2611.30078.title: RadarOSV: Unified 3D Scene and Motion Perception from mmWave Radars
2611.30078.abstract: Millimeter-wave radar offers weather-resilient sensing for 3D occupancy prediction. Existing radar occupancy methods mainly model geometry, with limited joint modeling of semantics and motion. Cascaded imaging radar provides fine spatial detail but has a limited unambiguous velocity range, whereas single-chip radar offers a wider range but coarser spatial resolution. We propose RadarOSV, to our knowledge the first radar-only framework that jointly predicts occupancy, dynamic object semantics, and ground-relative velocity from raw radar data in unified voxels, by exploiting complementary measurements from both radars. Its Polar-to-Cartesian Geometry (PCG) backbone maps polar imaging-radar features into Cartesian voxels through fixed and deformable sampling, guiding cross-radar fusion for geometry and attribute prediction. Single-chip detection outputs provide class evidence, while raw Doppler spectra supply motion features and radial-velocity candidates. The velocity readout selects from these candidates using fused features to resolve aliasing, then combines the selected radial estimate with learned motion. Ego-motion compensation uses radar-estimated velocity, so inference requires no external odometry or other sensors. On K-Radar, single-frame PCG achieves 40.7% mIoU within 12.8 m, compared with RadarOcc's reported 34.3%. On the BRIDGE-Liv dataset, compared with a cascaded-radar baseline predicting the same outputs with external ego velocity, RadarOSV improves macro-averaged accuracy across four dynamic object classes within annotated object regions from 63.1% to 75.5% and reduces object radial-velocity MAE against manual Doppler annotations from 1.03 to 0.51 m/s, while maintaining geometric occupancy mIoU.

llm.title_ja: RadarOSV：ミリ波レーダーによる統合型3Dシーンおよびモーション知覚
llm.tldr_ja: 単一チップとカスケードイメージングレーダーの測定値を統合し、ボクセル単位で占有率、動的オブジェクトのセマンティクス、速度を共同予測する初のレーダー専用フレームワーク「RadarOSV」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のレーダー占有手法は幾何学のモデリングに偏っており、セマンティクスとモーションの統合的なモデリングが不足している。
llm.method: 極座標から直交座標への幾何学的バックボーン（PCG）を用い、単一チップレーダーとイメージングレーダーのデータを融合する。
llm.result: K-RadarやBRIDGE-Livデータセットにおいて、動的物体の精度向上と速度の平均絶対誤差の大幅な削減を実現した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.30078.tldr_en: This work proposes RadarOSV, to their knowledge the first radar-only framework that jointly predicts occupancy, dynamic object semantics, and ground-relative velocity from raw radar data in unified voxels, by exploiting complementary measurements from both radars.

2611.30077.title: PushMimic: Learning Adaptive Humanoid Box Pushing via Dynamic Motion Augmentation and Reference Distillation
2611.30077.abstract: Humanoid box pushing is challenging when the physical properties of the task, such as the box mass and the ramp inclination, are unknown before the push begins. This paper presents PushMimic, a framework that learns adaptive humanoid box pushing from a single level-ground kinematic reference motion. The learned policy adapts its pushing posture to these properties without observing them. PushMimic augments the reference motion into a dynamically feasible motion dataset over these properties with sampling-based trajectory optimization, and distills the dataset into one motion tracking policy in one stage of training. Simulation results over box masses from 5 to 15 kg and ramp inclinations up to 15 degrees show that PushMimic raises the success rate from 57.8% to 88.8% compared with a baseline that tracks the original reference motion. It also reduces the cost of push of the arms by 22%. Hardware experiments on a Unitree G1 humanoid show that the policy adapts its torso pitch during continuous pushing on an inclined treadmill, with box masses up to 19 kg and ramp inclinations up to 12.6 degrees. PushMimic therefore needs only one reference motion, instead of one for every box mass and ramp inclination.
2611.30077.comment: 9 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables. Website at https://silvery107.github.io/pushmimic/

llm.title_ja: PushMimic：動的モーション拡張と参照蒸留による適応型ヒューマノイド箱押し学習
llm.tldr_ja: 箱の質量や斜面の傾きが未知の状況下で、単一の基準モーションから適応的な箱押し動作を1段階で学習するフレームワーク「PushMimic」を提案した。
llm.problem: 箱の質量や傾斜などの物理特性が未知であるヒューマノイドの箱押し動作の適応が困難である。
llm.method: 軌跡最適化を用いて基準モーションを動的かつ実行可能なモーションデータセットに拡張し、1つのポリシーに蒸留する。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの成功率を大幅に向上させ、Unitree G1を用いた実機実験で未知の傾斜や重量に対する適応を確認した。

2611.30077.tldr_en: This paper presents PushMimic, a framework that learns adaptive humanoid box pushing from a single level-ground kinematic reference motion that needs only one reference motion, instead of one for every box mass and ramp inclination.

2611.30072.title: HERO: Hierarchical Region-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Exploration
2611.30072.abstract: Autonomous exploration is widely used to map unknown environments, yet maintaining both path efficiency and low online computation remains difficult as environment scale increases. Hierarchical planners reduce global search through coarse regional representations but often rely on handcrafted local viewpoint-selection rules. Graph-based reinforcement learning can improve local decisions, but its inference cost grows with the exploration graph and global direction is usually represented only implicitly. To address these limitations, we present HERO, a hierarchical framework that assigns distinct responsibilities to global planning and learned local decision-making, enabling each level to focus on the function it is best suited to perform. To reduce the growing inference cost of graph-based policies, HERO restricts learned target selection to reachable candidates within the current region while using region-level planning to provide long-horizon guidance. To avoid informative targets causing excessive deviation from this global direction, the proposed Dual-Branch Graph Policy balances Frontier Utility with guidance toward the next region, improving both local exploration and global progress. Experiments on unseen 2D maps show the lowest overall mean path length and target-decision cost among the evaluated methods. MARSIM simulations and deployments at three real-world sites further demonstrate the framework's applicability with LiDAR-based mapping and chassis dynamics.

llm.title_ja: HERO：自律探索のための階層的・領域認識型強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 大域的なリージョンレベルの計画と学習ベースの局所的決定を組み合わせることで、パス効率を維持しつつ計算コストを削減する自律探索フレームワーク「HERO」を提案した。
llm.problem: 環境の大規模化に伴い、自律探索においてパスの効率性と低いオンライン計算量を両立させることが困難である。
llm.method: フロンティアの有用性と次の領域への誘導をバランスさせる「デュアルブランチグラフポリシー」を用いた階層型フレームワークを設計した。
llm.result: 未知の2Dマップでの実験において、最短の平均パス長と低い意思決定コストを達成し、実機でも有効性を示した。

2611.30067.title: FolioWeaver: A LayerGraph-Grounded Agent for Layered Image Generation and Editing
2611.30067.abstract: Layered image generation separates images into compositable layers, allowing users to manipulate individual elements independently. However, such asset-level editability does not enable the generation system to interpret successive feedback, perform targeted edits, and preserve unaffected content. We introduce FolioWeaver, a LayerGraph-grounded agent that unifies layered-image generation and iterative editing through a persistent Executable Scene State. FolioWeaver constructs a LayerGraph and generates independent visual assets conditioned on a shared scene reference. An Editing Agent performs feedback-driven modifications and self-repair through scoped actions, selective layer execution, and visual verification, enabling targeted updates while reusing unchanged assets. We also publicly release LayerFolio, a dataset of 100,377 human-reviewed layered scenes spanning six visual domains, together with two evaluation protocols: AtomicQA for measuring requirement satisfaction and CBLP for assessing layer organization. Experiments demonstrate that FolioWeaver achieves superior layer organization and composite fidelity compared with direct layered-generation methods. Analyses validate the contributions of component adaptation, execution-grounded repair, and cross-domain training. FolioWeaver advances layered-image generation toward persistent, controllable, and iterative visual creation. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/FolioWeaver/LayerFolio.

llm.title_ja: FolioWeaver：レイヤーグラフに基づいたレイヤー画像生成・編集エージェント
llm.tldr_ja: 永続的な実行可能シーン状態を用いて、レイヤー画像の生成と反復的な編集を統合するエージェント「FolioWeaver」を提案した。
llm.problem: アセットレベルの編集性を持つレイヤー画像生成システムでは、フィードバックの解釈や対象を絞った編集、変更のないコンテンツの保持が困難である。
llm.method: LayerGraphを構築し、共有シーン参照に条件付けられた視覚アセットを生成、編集エージェントによるフィードバック駆動の修正を行う。
llm.result: 直接的なレイヤー生成手法と比較して優れたレイヤー構成と合成忠実度を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルクリエイション

2611.30067.tldr_en: FolioWeaver is introduced, a LayerGraph-grounded agent that unifies layered-image generation and iterative editing through a persistent Executable Scene State, and achieves superior layer organization and composite fidelity compared with direct layered-generation methods.

2611.30064.title: How Latent Transition Geometry Matters for Planning in World Models
2611.30064.abstract: World models support planning by predicting how the environment evolves under candidate actions. However, one-step predictive accuracy alone does not characterize multi-step planning utility, which depends on distinguishing candidate futures. This raises a natural question: How does latent transition geometry shape planning? We investigate this through an action-conditioned transition-field view, using curvature regularization as a controlled intervention. Across four continuous-control tasks, appropriately tuned regularization improves planning, while excessive regularization can be detrimental. By decomposing the transition field into affine and non-affine components, we find that regularization reduces action sensitivity mainly through the non-affine component. To assess its role in planning, we directly manipulate the non-affine action response in frozen models and show that it affects candidate selection and closed-loop success. Further analysis shows that curvature generally brings predicted futures closer together, while preserving more of the differences along the goal direction. This helps explain why the planning effects vary across tasks. We observe broadly consistent planning trends across five sampling- and gradient-based solvers on LeWM and similar rollout-geometry trends on DINO-WM. Qualitative attention visualizations reveal accompanying shifts toward task-relevant visual structure. Together, these findings clarify how latent transition geometry influences multi-step planning.

llm.title_ja: 世界モデルの計画において潜在遷移幾何学がどのように重要であるか
llm.tldr_ja: 世界モデルの多ステップ計画における潜在遷移幾何学の役割を調査し、曲率正則化が非アフィン成分を通じて行動感度や計画性能に与える影響を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 単一ステップの予測精度だけでは多ステップ計画の有用性を特徴付けられず、潜在遷移幾何学が計画にどう影響するか未解明である。
llm.method: 曲率正則化を制御介入として用いたアクション条件付き遷移場の視点から、連続制御タスクにおける影響を分析する。
llm.result: 適切に調整された正則化により計画性能が向上し、曲率が予測された未来の軌道をゴール方向に沿って近づけることを示した。

2611.30064.tldr_en: By decomposing the transition field into affine and non-affine components, this work finds that regularization reduces action sensitivity mainly through the non-affine component, which helps explain why the planning effects vary across tasks.

2611.30047.title: RoboLiveMem: Is Robot Memory Solved When the World Does Not Wait?
2611.30047.abstract: Robot agents built on frontier vision-language models now solve most robot memory benchmarks. Does this mean they can remember what they need in a home, where people and machines keep moving things? Existing memory benchmarks cannot answer this question, because they pause the simulator while the model thinks: nothing can change during a decision, so whatever the robot remembers is still true when it acts. We introduce RoboLiveMem, a benchmark that runs the same memory tasks twice, once with the world paused while the model thinks and once with the world running. It contains 29 task families in three tiers, from 16 realistic BEHAVIOR-1K scenes of homes, workshops and a restaurant to controlled ManiSkill tasks. Every task mixes real changes with harmless look-alikes and runs without any change, so that no fixed strategy succeeds, and most tasks have a twin that keeps the change in view, which separates forgetting from acting too late. Testing 16 models on 34,176 episodes, we find three surprises. (1) Paused results hide the problem: when a remembered object changes in a realistic scene, the 8 Claude and GPT models succeed in 97% of episodes on average with the world paused, but in only 50% with the world running, and their ranking changes: Claude Opus 5.5, which never fails when paused, succeeds in 44%. (2) Speed is not the fix: slower models do no worse, and models given only 2 s per decision still fall at least 36 points below their paused success. (3) Models see the change but act on camera frames from before it ended. Looking again just before acting closes most of the realistic gap, yet when identical objects are swapped several times, all nine models we test still lose points to memory.

llm.title_ja: RoboLiveMem：世界が待ってくれないとき、ロボットの記憶は解決されたか？
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレータを一時停止せず現実的に環境が変化する中でロボットの記憶タスクを評価するベンチマーク「RoboLiveMem」を提案し、既存モデルの重大な性能低下を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存のロボット記憶ベンチマークは思考中にシミュレータを一時停止するため、実環境での動的な変化に対応する能力を評価できない。
llm.method: 世界が動いたまま実行される環境と一時停止する環境の両方でテストを行うベンチマークRoboLiveMemを構築し、16モデルを評価した。
llm.result: 一時停止時には高精度だったモデルが、動的な環境では成功率が著しく低下し、記憶の課題が未解決であることを示した。

2611.30041.title: Spiking World-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
2611.30041.abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict how the world responds to actions and offer a promising path toward general embodied intelligence, but they are large and run the network many times per plan, so they are hard to deploy on robots. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) compute with sparse binary spikes and use additions instead of multiplications, which saves power. However, existing WAMs use dense videos as the world state, so a spiking version would spend most of its computation on the background. We therefore introduce SpikingWAM, the first spiking WAM, which uses a sparse task skeleton as the world state. Inspired by biological motor control, which attends only to the key positions of a task, the Task Skeleton State (TSS) keeps the keypoints of the arm and the task objects, and a small spiking front end estimates the object keypoints from images. Body Frame Spike Coding (BFSC) and Grid Coincidence Attention (GCA) keep millimetre precision, and the Persistent Single Step Readout (PSR) runs the network once per plan. On the simulated benchmarks LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, SpikingWAM achieves competitive success rates with far less energy than ANN methods and surpasses all compared methods on LIBERO-Plus. Real robot experiments further confirm its effectiveness. These results show that a task skeleton lets spiking networks implement WAMs at very low energy, offering a new solution for low power embodied intelligence. Project page: https://wxqnl.github.io/spikingwam/

llm.title_ja: ロボット操作のためのスパイキング世界行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 疎なタスクスケルトンを世界状態として利用することで、極めて低い電力で動作する世界行動モデル（WAM）のスパイク版「SpikingWAM」を提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の世界行動モデルはサイズが大きく高頻度で実行されるためロボットへの展開が難しく、スパイクニューラルネットワークを適用するには背景の計算コストが大きい。
llm.method: アームと物体のキーポイントを保持するタスクスケルトン状態（TSS）と、低電力なスパイキングフロントエンドを組み合わせたSpikingWAMを開発した。
llm.result: LIBEROなどのシミュレーションおよび実機実験において、ANN手法よりもはるかに少ないエネルギーで優れた成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: スパイキングニューラルネットワーク

2611.30041.tldr_en: SpikingWAM is introduced, the first spiking WAM, which uses a sparse task skeleton as the world state, and shows that a task skeleton lets spiking networks implement WAMs at very low energy, offering a new solution for low power embodied intelligence.

2611.30026.title: Design of a Compact Cable-driven 4-DoF Salamander Robotic Limb with Large Range of Motion and High Load Capacity
2611.30026.abstract: A compact yet agile and powerful limb is essential for amphibious legged robots that transition between spine-based swimming and leg-based terrestrial walking, as salamanders do. Salamander limbs combine large ranges of motion (ROM), multiple degrees of freedom (DoFs), and high load capacity. These features enable swinging and body-weight support during walking, as well as folding alongside the body during swimming. Their proximal kinematics can be represented by three rotational DoFs at the hip and one at the knee. Replicating these capabilities within a compact robotic limb is challenging with direct-drive architectures, because multiple joint-mounted actuators must be sufficiently spaced or placed distally to avoid self-collision, increasing limb size and rotational inertia. Here we present a cable-driven 4-DoF salamander robotic limb with a spatial cable-routing architecture that relocates actuators proximally while preserving large ROM and load capacity. Transmission-induced coupling is mitigated by mechanically compensating multi-segment cable paths, model-based feedforward decoupling, and output-side joint angle feedback. Compared with a direct-drive limb, the proposed design reduces mass by 20.4%, projected envelope area by 20.5%, and estimated effective yaw-axis inertia by 31.9%. Experiments verify independent, decoupled control over joint-angle ranges of 45 deg, 118 deg, 118 deg, and 135 deg for hip pitch, yaw, roll, and knee flexion/extension, respectively. During lifting tests, the limb supported an equivalent vertical load of at least 5.4 times its own weight. The proposed limb provides a compact, biologically representative platform for future studies of salamander locomotion and neural control.

llm.title_ja: 大きな可動域と高い耐荷重を持つコンパクトなケーブル駆動4自由度サンショウウオロボット四肢の設計
llm.tldr_ja: サンショウウオの四肢の動きを模倣し、アクチュエータを近位に配置する空間ケーブルルーティングアーキテクチャを用いたコンパクトで高耐荷重な4自由度ロボット四肢を設計した。
llm.problem: 水陸両用ロボットに必要な大きな可動域と高耐荷重を持つ四肢を直接駆動方式で実現すると、サイズや回転慣性が増大する。
llm.method: 複数セグメントのケーブル経路の機械的補償やモデルベースのフィードフォワード非結合を用いたケーブル駆動4自由度四肢設計を提案した。
llm.result: 直接駆動型に比べて質量、投影外形面積、慣性を削減し、自重の5.4倍以上の垂直負荷を支える高い耐荷重と独立した関節制御を実証した。
keywords_ja: 生物学的ロボティクス

2611.30024.title: FlexWAM: Learning Flexible Visual Routing for World Action Models
2611.30024.abstract: Humans dynamically adjust their reliance on sensory modalities across manipulation stages. Although existing World Action Models (WAMs) fuse multi-camera observations, they struggle to adapt their reliance on individual views based on the current observations. This raises a central question: how can the action expert integrate complementary visual evidence while prioritizing the views most relevant to the current action? FlexWAM addresses this challenge through three modules. First, we alternate within-view and cross-view attention to capture view-specific dynamics and complementary cues. For action prediction, View-Routed Action Attention uses an observation-conditioned router to prioritize relevant views. To calibrate routing, we train a critic using counterfactual view credit, estimated from action loss sensitivity upon suppressing each view's contribution to action attention. We evaluate FlexWAM with two video backbones on five challenging real-world manipulation tasks across two robot platforms. The two variants improve mean task success by 16.4 and 23.0 percentage points over the strongest baseline. Project website: https://flexwam.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: FlexWAM: 世界行動モデルのための柔軟な視覚的ルーティングの学習
llm.tldr_ja: FlexWAMは、行動予測において現在の観測に最も関連する視点を優先的に統合するため、ビュー固有のダイナミクスと反実仮想ビュー信用度に基づくルーターを用いて、5つの実世界マニピュレーションタスクでベースラインを大幅に改善した。
llm.problem: 既存の世界行動モデルは複数のカメラ観測を融合するものの、現在の観測に基づいて個別の視点への依存度を適応させることに苦労している。
llm.method: 視点内・視点間アテンションを交互に行い、観測条件付きルーターと反実仮想ビュー信用度で訓練されたクリティカルを用いて関連視点を優先する。
llm.result: 2つのビデオバックボーンを用いた5つの困難な実世界マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、平均タスク成功率を最強のベースラインと比較して16.4および23.0パーセントポイント向上させた。

2611.30024.tldr_en: FlexWAM addresses the challenge of how can the action expert integrate complementary visual evidence while prioritizing the views most relevant to the current action through three modules, which alternate within-view and cross-view attention to capture view-specific dynamics and complementary cues.

2611.30022.title: MOVER: Planning Beyond Motion
2611.30022.abstract: Residual world models forecast a driving scene through its temporal change, so feature components that stay constant over time vanish from the residual pathway. We ask whether evidence with weak temporal change, such as a waiting pedestrian or a stopped vehicle, can be used more effectively for planning, and introduce MOVER, a complementary event-routing mechanism. A training-time teacher measures how each spatially grounded event query responds when a past frame is removed from shared history and contrasts that sensitivity with the event's pooled temporal residual, prioritizing events that depend on history but receive weak residual evidence. A student predicts the resulting priorities from unperturbed history, so the teacher adds no inference cost. Under fixed total routing mass, one distribution scales a low-rank future bird's-eye-view update and biases trajectory-conditioned event reading. On nuScenes, MOVER reduces ResWorld's UniAD-style average L2 from 0.65 to 0.55 m and its collision rate from 0.23% to 0.12% without direct planner ego status (0.50 m and 0.09% with it), adding 4.1 ms per frame. Matched controls show that the complementary teacher outperforms either signal alone and that the allocation acts mainly during training. Adapted to BridgeDrive-LEAD, MOVER reaches a 96.52 +/- 0.65 driving score over three seeds on the 220-route Bench2Drive closed-loop benchmark, exceeding matched controls in each paired seed by a margin within seed variation.

llm.title_ja: MOVER: モーションを超えた計画
llm.tldr_ja: MOVERは、時間的変化が弱い環境的手掛かりを効率的に利用するための補完的なイベントルーティング機構を導入し、自動運転の計画精度と安全性を向上させる。
llm.problem: 残留世界モデルは時間的変化を通じて駆動シーンを予測するため、待ち歩行者や停止車両などの時間的変化が弱い要素の証拠が消失してしまう。
llm.method: 過去フレーム削除に対する感度と時間的残差を比較する教師モデルを用いてイベントの優先順位を測定し、摂動のない履歴から生徒モデルが予測する。
llm.result: nuScenesにおいて平均L2誤差を0.65mから0.55mに減少させ、衝突率を0.23%から0.12%に低減し、Bench2Driveベンチマークで高いスコアを達成した。
keywords_ja: イベントルーティング

2611.30022.tldr_en: This work asks whether evidence with weak temporal change, such as a waiting pedestrian or a stopped vehicle, can be used more effectively for planning, and introduces MOVER, a complementary event-routing mechanism that outperforms either signal alone or signal alone and acts mainly during training.

2611.30007.title: One Latent World for Heterogeneous LiDARs: A Scan Pattern Agnostic 4D World Model via Direct Ray Decoding
2611.30007.abstract: LiDAR world models generate and predict metric 3D observations in the form of LiDAR scans. They typically synthesize scans following the scan pattern of their training sensor or render them from an intermediate 3D surface or field. However, following one scan pattern limits transfer to LiDARs with other patterns, and rendering from intermediate geometry can cause incorrect depths and false returns. In this paper, we propose a scan pattern agnostic 4D LiDAR world model that decouples the scene from sensor observation, so one spatial latent can be observed by heterogeneous LiDARs at the same mounting position without regeneration. Our decoder predicts the hit probability and depth of each ray directly from the latent, combining global scene context with local features retrieved at a preliminary depth. Without an intermediate surface or field, it reduces incorrect depths and false returns, and as each ray is decoded independently from one latent, LiDARs that share a ray receive the same return and observe one consistent scene. Finally, a diffusion transformer generates scenes in this latent and predicts 4D sequences from observed latents warped by the given ego and object motion. On KITTI-360 and nuScenes, our model generates realistic scenes and reduces the registration error between predicted frames by about 70% relative to the best compared world model. Its decoder yields 19 to 28% lower depth error than the rendering used by other world models, and generated scans benefit several downstream tasks. Our code will be open-sourced. More details are available at https://minwoo0611.github.io/OneLatentWorld.

llm.title_ja: 異種LiDARのための1つの潜在世界：直接レイデコードによるスキャンパターン非依存の4D世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: シーンをセンサー観測から切り離し、直接レイデコードによって異種LiDARが同一の空間潜在表現を共有して一貫したシーンを観測できるようにする、スキャンパターン非依存の4D世界モデルを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来のLiDAR世界モデルは特定の訓練センサーのスキャンパターンに従うか中間幾何形状からレンダリングするため、異種LiDARへの転移が制限され誤った深度や不正確なリターンを引き起こす。
llm.method: グローバルなシーン文脈と局細特徴を組み合わせ、潜在表現から各レイのヒット確率と深度を直接予測するデコーダーを構築し、拡散Transformerと組み合わせる。
llm.result: KITTI-360およびnuScenesにおいて現実的なシーンを生成し、予測フレーム間の登録誤差を約70%削減し、他の世界モデルのレンダリングに比べて19〜28%低い深度誤差を達成した。

2611.30007.tldr_en: A scan pattern agnostic 4D LiDAR world model that decouples the scene from sensor observation, so one spatial latent can be observed by heterogeneous LiDARs at the same mounting position without regeneration is proposed.

2611.30004.title: EnvTrap: Revealing the Environment-Only Attack Surface in Embodied AI via Consequence-Blind Action Execution
2611.30004.abstract: As AI models evolve from text and vision to physical agents, embodied AI faces a fundamentally different attack surface. Prior attacks on embodied systems have used crafted instructions, adversarial visual inputs, and training-time policy modifications; we study environment-only object rearrangements with unchanged models and instructions. We reveal an attack surface in safety-critical spatial relations among existing objects. An adversary who rearranges objects, without modifying instructions or accessing models, can cause hazardous consequences. In this work, we propose EnvTrap, a diagnostic pipeline that constructs paired safe, trap, and null-trap (benign but misleading) embodied scenarios. We demonstrate that environment-only perturbations raise hazardous-action rates to an average of 83.4% across the five evaluated action policies, with similar vulnerability patterns confirmed in world models. On a consequence-prediction task, model accuracy remains near chance, while human evaluators achieve high accuracy. We further propose a consequence-aware defense that reduces trap trigger rates by an average of 76.3 percentage points across action policies in simulation and by 62.9 percentage points pooled across physical backends. Together, these findings link environment-only attacks to a broader deficit in physical reasoning: embodied models recognize task-relevant objects yet fail to anticipate how spatial relations change the consequences of acting on them. EnvTrap makes this gap directly testable and turns hazardous layouts into training scenarios for safer embodied action. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/INKSIR/Envtrap.

llm.title_ja: EnvTrap：結果を考慮しない行動実行を通じた具現化AIにおける環境のみの攻撃表面の解明
llm.tldr_ja: EnvTrapは、モデルや指示を変更せずにオブジェクトを再配置するだけで危険な結果を引き起こす環境のみの攻撃表面を明らかにするとともに、結果を考慮した防御手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 具現化AIは、指示の改変や視覚的入力の改変といった従来の攻撃に加え、安全性に関わる空間関係に潜む環境起因の脆弱性を見落としている。
llm.method: 安全、トラップ、ヌルトラップのシナリオを構築する診断パイプライン「EnvTrap」を提案し、結果を考慮した防御によってトラップトリガー率を削減する。
llm.result: 環境のみの摂動により、評価された5つの行動ポリシー全体の平均で危険な行動率が83.4%に上昇し、提案する防御手法によりシミュレーションで平均76.3ポイント、物理バックエンドで62.9ポイント削減された。

2611.30004.tldr_en: This work proposes EnvTrap, a diagnostic pipeline that constructs paired safe, trap, and null-trap embodied scenarios and demonstrates that environment-only perturbations raise hazardous-action rates to an average of 83.4% across the five evaluated action policies, with similar vulnerability patterns confirmed in world models.

2611.29980.title: TeleMultiStream: An Integrated Robot Teleoperation System with Low-Latency Multi-Stream Video Feedback
2611.29980.abstract: Training embodied-intelligence models requires large-scale, high-quality demonstration data. Robot teleoperation provides an important means of collecting these data. Low-latency teleoperation also helps human operators take control promptly and provide corrective demonstrations in DAgger-based interactive learning. This paper presents TeleMultiStream, a robot teleoperation system that combines multi-stream WebRTC video feedback with UDP pose downlink. The system supports heterogeneous video sources and uses buffer reuse, bounded queues, and native XR rendering to reduce processing and waiting. In wired-LAN ZED Mini tests, TeleMultiStream's software and high-performance hardware encoding modes achieved dominant-interval Glass-to-Glass latency medians of 60 and 66~ms, respectively. These medians were 26.8\% and 19.5\% lower than the 82-ms RobotVision-PC reference, respectively. At the lower tested resolutions, the two TeleMultiStream encoding modes provided comparable visual latency. Their respective medians in three-stream Configuration~1 were 72 and 66~ms. In the higher-resolution Configuration~2, high-performance hardware encoding outperformed software encoding in latency and CPU utilization. It reduced mean encoding time from 11.85 to 8.80~ms and the dominant-interval Glass-to-Glass median from 94 to 88~ms. Its CPU utilization was approximately 67\%, compared with 265\% for software encoding. During three-stream reception with high-performance hardware encoding, the mean corrected one-way UDP latencies at 100~Hz were 1.576 and 1.800~ms in Configurations~1 and~2, respectively. Mean estimated packet loss was 0.0033\% in both configurations. These results support responsive teleoperation for robot demonstration collection.

llm.title_ja: TeleMultiStream: 低遅延マルチストリーム映像フィードバックを統合したロボット遠隔操作システム
llm.tldr_ja: TeleMultiStreamは、マルチストリームWebRTCビデオフィードバックとUDPポーズダウンリンクを組み合わせ、バッファ再利用やネイティブXRレンダリングを活用することで低遅延なロボット遠隔操作を実現する。
llm.problem: ロボット知見モデルの訓練データ収集に不可欠なロボット遠隔操作において、遅延の大きさがデータ収集やインタラクティブ学習での迅速な介入を妨げている。
llm.method: マルチストリームのWebRTCビデオフィードバックとUDPポーズダウンリンクを統合し、バッファ再利用、境界付きキュー、ネイティブXRレンダリングを適用する。
llm.result: 有線LAN環境のテストにおいて、ソフトウェアおよび高性能ハードウェアエンコーディングモードでガラス間遅延の中央値がそれぞれ60 msおよび66 msを達成し、従来参照値より大幅に低下した。

2611.29980.tldr_en: TeleMultiStream, a robot teleoperation system that combines multi-stream WebRTC video feedback with UDP pose downlink, supports heterogeneous video sources and uses buffer reuse, bounded queues, and native XR rendering to reduce processing and waiting.

2611.29977.title: Conartist: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Computer-Using Agents against Multi-Step Prompt Injection
2611.29977.abstract: Harnesses secure Computer-Using Agents by enforcing security constraints and defending against prompt injection attacks. However, we find that two core security mechanisms of agent harnesses remain vulnerable. First, consistency checking prevents agents from deviating from legitimate user objectives, while attackers can bypass it by embedding malicious actions that appear logically consistent with legitimate task execution. Second, risk auditing proactively examines high-risk operations. Yet, the auditing process itself would introduce additional exploitable actions that violate security boundaries. To evaluate above defects we found, we propose Conartist, a cascaded adaptive prompt injection framework comprising two progressive stages. First, Conartist employs a goal-pollution strategy to establish deceptive causal dependencies between legitimate user objectives and malicious operations, progressively embedding attack steps into legitimate task workflows. However, these task-coupled attacks remain susceptible to risk auditing. To address this limitation, Conartist further analyzes security-auditing feedback from controlled attack exploration to identify exploitable auditing patterns. Conartist then adaptively refines its deception strategies to either avoid triggering risk auditing or induce additional high-risk operations. Extensive experiments across five backbone models demonstrate the effectiveness of Conartist, achieving attack success rates of 32.12% on 576-instance tool use benchmark and 66.67% in the Reddit GUI benchmark, outperforming the SOTA attack by 14.41 and 29.17, respectively. By analyzing one of the most popular Agent, Openclaw, we furthermore concluded seven realistic exploitable attack patterns, which reveals that security mechanisms designed to prevent malicious actions can themselves be manipulated to facilitate attacks.

llm.title_ja: Conartist: マルチステッププロンプトインジェクションに対するコンピュータ利用エージェントの適応的エージェント型レッドチーミング
llm.tldr_ja: Conartistは、目標汚染戦略とセキュリティ監査フィードバックの分析を組み合わせたカスケード型の適応的プロンプトインジェクションフレームワークにより、エージェントのセキュリティ機構を回避する。
llm.problem: コンピュータ利用エージェントの整合性チェックやリスク監査といった主要なセキュリティメカニズムは、論理的に一貫した悪意ある行動や監査プロセスの悪用によって依然として脆弱である。
llm.method: 正当な目標と悪意ある操作の間に欺瞞的な因果依存関係を構築する目標汚染戦略を用い、監査フィードバックから悪用可能なパターンを特定して適応的に洗練させる。
llm.result: 5つのバックモデルを用いた実験において、ツール使用ベンチマークで32.12%、Reddit GUIベンチマークで66.67%の攻撃成功率を達成し、既存の最先端攻撃を上回った。
keywords_ja: プロンプトインジェクション

2611.29977.tldr_en: Conartist, a cascaded adaptive prompt injection framework comprising two progressive stages, which employs a goal-pollution strategy to establish deceptive causal dependencies between legitimate user objectives and malicious operations, and which reveals that security mechanisms designed to prevent malicious actions can themselves be manipulated to facilitate attacks.

2611.29969.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes
2611.29969.abstract: Situated 3D reasoning requires embodied agents to interpret objects, scene geometry, and viewpoint dependent spatial relations. Existing methods learn grounded interactions from supervised traces, but largely imitate prescribed evidence acquisition patterns rather than optimizing the support that the returned evidence provides for the correct answer. Moreover, outcome rewards provide limited credit for intermediate tool choices and may leave infrequent tools underexplored. An effective agent should instead adaptively decide what to ground, which tool to invoke, and how to assess the utility of returned evidence. To this end, this paper presents CARE-3D, a reinforcement post-training framework for adaptive grounded reasoning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on grounding instructions first establishes valid interactions, after which Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) optimizes the agent while keeping the 3D grounding module frozen. CARE-3D combines Counterfactual Attribution of Returned Evidence for evidence sensitive credit assignment, and Group Coverage Sampling to preserve tool coverage. Experiments on MSQA and Beacon3D show consistent gains over SFT and GRPO using only answer and format rewards, especially in spatial reasoning and grounding answer coherence. Our code is available at \href{https://github.com/xiaoqian-UQ/CARE-3D}{CARE-3D}.

llm.title_ja: CARE-3D: 位置特定された3Dシーンにおける証拠に基づくエージェント推論のための強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: CARE-3Dは、逆事実的属性割当とグループカバレッジサンプリングを組み合わせた事後強化学習フレームワークにより、適応的な3D空間推論とツール選択を実現する。
llm.problem: 既存の手法は教師あり軌跡から模倣学習を行うため証拠獲得パターンが固定化されやすく、中間的なツール選択に対する報酬が限定的で探索が不十分になる。
llm.method: 教師あり微調整の後に、3Dグランディングモジュールを固定したままグループ相対政策最適化（GRPO）を適用し、逆事実的属性割当とグループカバレッジサンプリングを行う。
llm.result: MSQAおよびBeacon3Dの実験において、答えとフォーマットの報酬のみを使用しながら、空間推論とグランディングの整合性において一貫した性能向上を示した。

2611.29969.tldr_en: CARE-3D is presented, a reinforcement post-training framework for adaptive grounded reasoning that combines Counterfactual Attribution of Returned Evidence for evidence sensitive credit assignment, and Group Coverage Sampling to preserve tool coverage.

2611.29947.title: SAGE-Drive: Benefit-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving Planning
2611.29947.abstract: Explicit reasoning enables autonomous vehicles (AVs) to interpret complex traffic interactions and support trajectory planning, but introduces additional computational demands. Determining when explicit reasoning can improve planning accuracy remains a key challenge, as its benefits vary across driving scenarios. To address this challenge, this study proposes Scene-Adaptive Gating of Explicit Reasoning for Driving (SAGE-Drive), a benefit-aware adaptive reasoning framework for autonomous driving planning. First, paired planning outcomes with and without explicit reasoning are analyzed to measure the reasoning benefit, i.e., the reduction in planning error achieved by explicit reasoning, which serves as the supervision label. SAGE-Drive then learns to predict these benefits using geometric features of the initial trajectory planned without reasoning and multimodal scene information, and invokes explicit reasoning only for the scenarios with the highest predicted benefits under a predefined reasoning budget. Experiments on 1,497 paired driving scenarios reveal that explicit reasoning improves planning accuracy in 53.5% of cases while degrading it in 46.5%, yielding a near-zero average benefit. On the test set, with a 20% reasoning budget, SAGE-Drive achieves an average displacement error (ADE) of 1.5191 m, compared with 1.5252 m for random selection. At a 35% budget, it achieves an ADE of 1.5148 m, close to the 1.5141 m obtained when reasoning is applied to every scenario. These findings establish the predicted reasoning benefit as an effective criterion for reasoning selection, allowing explicit reasoning to be invoked where it improves planning accuracy at a fraction of its computational cost.

llm.title_ja: SAGE-Drive: 自動運転計画のための利益認識型適応推論
llm.tldr_ja: SAGE-Driveは、明示的推論による計画精度の向上度合い（利益）を予測し、計算予算の制約下で利益の高いシナリオにのみ推論を適用する適応型フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 自動運転における明示的推論は複雑な交通相互作用の解釈を助けるが、計算負荷が高く、その利益がシナリオごとに異なるため適切な適用判断が課題となる。
llm.method: 初期軌跡の幾何学的特徴とマルチモーダルシーン情報から推論による誤差削減効果を予測し、事前定義された予算内で利益の大きいシナリオでのみ明示的推論を起動する。
llm.result: 1,497対の運転シナリオの実験において、20%の推論予算でランダム選択よりも優れた平均変位誤差（ADE）を達成し、計算コストを抑えつつ全シナリオ推論に近い性能を実現した。

2611.29947.tldr_en: This study proposes Scene-Adaptive Gating of Explicit Reasoning for Driving (SAGE-Drive), a benefit-aware adaptive reasoning framework for autonomous driving planning that establishes the predicted reasoning benefit as an effective criterion for reasoning selection, allowing explicit reasoning to be invoked where it improves planning accuracy at a fraction of its computational cost.

2611.29918.title: TidyFlow: Geometry-Aware Tabletop Arrangement Generation with Human-Aligned Tidiness Evaluation
2611.29918.abstract: Generating tidy tabletop arrangements that align with human organizational preferences requires considering both functional relationships among objects and geometric constraints within limited tabletop space. We present TidyFlow, a tabletop arrangement generation framework that integrates conditional Flow Matching with topology-aware geometric refinement. We construct two tabletop arrangement datasets based on functional grouping and geometric constraints, namely General Tabletop Layouts (GTL) and Workstation Tabletop Layouts (WTL), and introduce a six-dimensional tidiness scoring function. Conditional Flow Matching is employed to learn a multimodal distribution of target arrangements conditioned on object attributes and tabletop geometry. To address geometric errors in generated layouts, we construct topology-aware refinement data based on collision and boundary-violation patterns, and employ a pair-aware attention network to iteratively refine object poses. Experiments demonstrate that, after three refinement iterations, TidyFlow improves geometric validity from 23.21% to 88.91% on GTL and from 10.58% to 57.91% on WTL. Furthermore, a human preference study demonstrates a positive correlation between the proposed tidiness scores and human rankings, achieving a Spearman correlation coefficient of 0.5543.

llm.title_ja: TidyFlow: 人間の整頓好みに合わせた幾何学認識型テーブルトップ配置生成
llm.tldr_ja: TidyFlowは、条件付きフローマッチングとトポロジー認識型の幾何学的洗練を統合し、機能的関係と幾何学的制約を考慮した整頓されたテーブルトップ配置を生成する。
llm.problem: 人間の組織的選好に一致する整頓されたテーブルトップ配置の生成には、限られたスペース内での機能的関係と幾何学的制約の両方を考慮する必要がある。
llm.method: 条件付きフローマッチングにより目標配置のマルチモーダル分布を学習し、衝突および境界違反パターンに基づくペア認識アテンションネットワークで姿勢を反復的に洗練させる。
llm.result: 3回の洗練反復後、GTLで幾何学的有効性を23.21%から88.91%に、WTLで10.58%から57.91%に向上させ、人間による評価でも高い相関を示した。

2611.29918.tldr_en: This work presents TidyFlow, a tabletop arrangement generation framework that integrates conditional Flow Matching with topology-aware geometric refinement, and constructs two tabletop arrangement datasets based on functional grouping and geometric constraints, and introduces a six-dimensional tidiness scoring function.

2611.29913.title: MoMa-NMP: Scene-Scale Neural Motion Planning for Mobile Manipulators
2611.29913.abstract: Mobile manipulators operating in homes and other complex environments must coordinate their base and arm over long horizons, navigating around obstacles, through narrow passages, and between constrained workspaces. Neural motion planners can provide fast closed-loop planning from partial observations, but scaling them to room-sized environments is difficult because generating high-quality training trajectories is itself a challenging motion-planning problem. To address this, we introduce MoMa-DemoSmith, a demonstration-generation pipeline that separates the problem into global path discovery for large complex scenes and local motion refinement for collision avoidance. This key separation enables the generation of millions of challenging whole-body trajectories across our procedurally generated scenes. We train MoMa-NMP on these demonstrations through behavior cloning (BC) followed by privileged on-policy distillation, achieving 87.0% success on our simulation benchmark and 77.5% across 80 trials in unseen real-world scenes. See video results at https://adamhkan.com/moma-nmp/.

llm.title_ja: MoMa-NMP: モバイルマニピュレータのためのシーン規模のニューラルモーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: MoMa-NMPは、大域的経路探索と局所モーション洗練を分離したデモ生成パイプラインを通じて、複雑なシーンにおけるモバイルマニピュレータの長期全身軌跡計画を効率的に学習する。
llm.problem: 家庭などの複雑な環境で活動するモバイルマニピュレータはベースとアームを長期間にわたり協調させる必要があるが、高品質な訓練軌跡の生成が困難なためシーン全体への拡張が難しい。
llm.method: 大域的経路探索と局所運動洗練を分離した「MoMa-DemoSmith」で数百万の軌跡を生成し、行動クローンと特権的オンポリシー蒸留によりニューラルモーションプランナーを訓練する。
llm.result: シミュレーションベンチマークで87.0%の成功率を達成し、未見の実世界シーンにおける80回の試行でも77.5%の成功率を記録した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレータ
モーションプランニング

2611.29913.tldr_en: MoMa-DemoSmith is introduced, a demonstration-generation pipeline that separates the problem into global path discovery for large complex scenes and local motion refinement for collision avoidance and enables the generation of millions of challenging whole-body trajectories across the authors' procedurally generated scenes.

2611.29912.title: SuperNav-1.5: Structured Spatial Memory For Agentic Navigation Systems
2611.29912.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of scene-level memory design for efficient navigation across sessions and successive object goals. Recent methods commonly represent a scene using scene graphs or image--text records. However, dense scene-graph representations impose substantial reasoning and context overhead on multimodal large language models, while image--text records cannot be directly converted into executable geometric routes. To address these limitations, we propose SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent. The memory consists of an area-segmented occupancy map annotated with agent-maintained, map-grounded memory nodes. This map guides the agent toward unvisited areas and provides executable routes to known locations. For multi-session navigation, we introduce agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map. Together, these designs enable efficient navigation across session and successive object goals. Experiments show that our method outperforms baselines on single-object, multi-object, and demand-driven navigation benchmarks, with particularly strong gains in path efficiency. Multi-session evaluation demonstrates that the constructed memory can be reused, while deployment on a real quadruped robot further shows the system's applicability. Project Page: https://zju3dv.github.io/SuperNav-1.5/
2611.29912.tldr_en: This paper proposes SuperNav-1.5, an agentic navigation system equipped with a structured spatial memory constructed by the agent, and introduces agent-guided relocalization, whereby the agent infers an area prior from current observations and stored memory records to constrain geometric matching and localize the robot within the stored map.

2611.29907.title: UnderGrasp: Envelopment-Oriented Grasp Refinement for an Underactuated Gripper
2611.29907.abstract: Underactuated grippers can form enveloping grasps through passive compliance, while the terminal pose and single width predicted by generic grasp generators do not fully capture the approach-closure process. Conventional collision filtering also struggles to distinguish harmful interference from acceptable contact. We present UnderGrasp, a post-hoc grasp refinement and evaluation framework for an underactuated gripper that reuses grasp candidates and quality priors from a frozen generator. The model jointly encodes the target, local environment, support surface, and approach-path geometry to propose diverse combinations of insertion depth, pre-grasp width, and target closing width for each candidate. These actions are ranked by combining separately predicted envelopment and interaction quality with upstream priors, balancing grasp feasibility, envelopment, and scene disturbance rather than rejecting all environmental contact. The back end is trained solely on configuration and interaction labels generated by gripper-specific simulations, without real-robot grasp labels. Real-robot experiments with an underactuated gripper show that UnderGrasp improves the overall success rate (SR) and the envelopment rate (ER) among successful grasps from 0.55/0.12 to 0.82/0.55 with AnyGrasp, and from 0.42/0.08 to 0.65/0.36 with GraspNet. In contrast, increasing the fixed insertion depth to 40 mm improves ER to 0.35 but reduces SR to 0.52, supporting the value of adaptive refinement. For trials involving target or environmental contact during approach, the conditional success rates increase from 0.36 to 0.89 and from 0.25 to 0.86, respectively, demonstrating more reliable execution under contact. Project page: https://dishenliu2004-hub.github.io/undergrasp-site/

llm.title_ja: UnderGrasp: 低駆動グリッパのための包絡指向把持洗練
llm.tldr_ja: UnderGraspは、ターゲット、局所環境、アプローチ経路の幾何学を共同でエンコードし、接触を拒絶するのではなく把持の可能性と環境との相互作用のバランスをとることで低駆動グリッパの把持成功率を向上させる。
llm.problem: 低駆動グリッパはパ受動的追従により包絡把持を形成できるが、一般的なジェネレータが予測する終端姿勢や単一の幅はアプローチ・クロージャー過程を十分に捉えられず、従来の衝突フィルタリングは有害な干渉と受容可能な接触を区別しにくい。
llm.method: 凍結されたジェネレータの把持候補と品質事前分布を再利用し、挿入深度、把持前幅、目標閉じ幅の多様な組み合わせを提案・評価する事後洗練フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: AnyGraspおよびGraspNetを用いた実機実験において、把持成功率（SR）と包絡率（ER）を大幅に向上させ、接触を伴う試行でも信頼性の高い実行を実証した。

2611.29907.tldr_en: UnderGrasp is presented, a post-hoc grasp refinement and evaluation framework for an underactuated gripper that reuses grasp candidates and quality priors from a frozen generator to propose diverse combinations of insertion depth, pre-grasp width, and target closing width for each candidate.

2611.29899.title: World Models and the Law
2611.29899.abstract: Current AI may have a model of how we use human language, but this does not translate into a reliable representation of physical reality. World models promise to fill this gap by learning how an environment changes over time and predicting the consequences of an action, and they are already used to steer robots and generate explorable worlds. This article asks how AI regulation in three major legal contexts, the European Union, California, and China, copes with the distinctive challenges they raise. I propose a definition and a taxonomy of world models based on who or what acts on their predictions, and identify the risks of misplaced reliance on them. I argue that existing rules tend to cover world models but leave three questions open, i.e., action provenance, trajectory validity, and the weight of simulated evidence, and recommend ways to fill these gaps.

llm.title_ja: 世界モデルと法
llm.tldr_ja: 本稿では、EU、カリフォルニア、中国の主要な法規制が世界モデルの抱える特異な課題にどのように対処しているかを検討し、行動の正当性、軌跡の妥当性、シミュレーションされた証拠の重みという3つの未解決の空白に対する解決策を提言する。
llm.problem: 現在のAIは物理的現実を信頼性高く表現できず、世界モデルは環境の変化学習や行動結果の予測によってこの隙間を埋めようとするが、法規制上の新たなリスクや未解決の課題を生じさせている。
llm.method: 誰または何が予測に基づいて行動するかという基準に基づいた世界モデルの定義と分類法を提案し、現在の法規制の適用範囲と空白を分析する。
llm.result: 既存の規制が世界モデルを概ねカバーしているものの、行動の証明、軌跡の有効性、シミュレーション証拠の重みに関する3つの疑問が未解決であることを明らかにし、その填補を推奨した。

2611.29899.tldr_en: It is argued that existing rules tend to cover world models but leave three questions open, i.e., action provenance, trajectory validity, and the weight of simulated evidence, and recommend ways to fill these gaps.

2611.29897.title: Motion Mamba 2.0: Autoregressive Diffusion Mamba for Long-Horizon Humanoid Control
2611.29897.abstract: Long-horizon, real-time controllable motion generation is essential for interactive animation and humanoid robotics, where an agent must respond to changing instructions and spatial goals while moving. Existing autoregressive diffusion methods generate motion incrementally, but bounded attention caches limit access to distant history, while repeated denoising introduces substantial inference overhead. We present Motion Mamba 2.0, a Mamba-based root-body diffusion architecture that integrates local attention, resumable recurrent states, and persistent content memory (PCM) for long-horizon controllable motion generation. PCM transforms compressed motion history from Mamba recurrent states, together with state changes and text-conditioned features, into dynamically updated content slots accessible to local attention. To enable efficient inference, we further develop an execution scheme tailored to this architecture, combining CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and execution-flow simplification while preserving the canonical history update. Evaluations on retargeted HiPHI demonstrate accurate terminal control over rollouts of up to 39.52 s, while short-horizon comparisons on BONES Seed and retargeted HumanML3D show that the model also retains strong spatial control and text-motion matching. On an RTX 4090, the optimized execution reduces median complete-window latency from 1685.35 to 276.14 ms, achieving a median paired speedup of 6.138$\times$ while preserving identical outputs and committed states in the tested rollouts. Moreover, we conduct extensive real-world evaluation on the Unitree G1, demonstrating sequential text-guided action composition, expressive motion, and interactive locomotion through keyboard and mouse control.

llm.title_ja: Motion Mamba 2.0: 長期ヒューノイド制御のための自己回帰型拡散Mamba
llm.tldr_ja: Motion Mamba 2.0は、局所アテンション、再開可能なリカレント状態、持続的コンテンツメモリ（PCM）を統合することで、長期間にわたる高精度なヒューマノイドモーション生成と効率的な推論を実現する。
llm.problem: 既存の自己回帰型拡散手法はモーションを段階的に生成するが、有限のアテンションキャッシュが遠い履歴へのアクセスを制限し、繰り返しのノイズ除去が推論のオーバーヘッドを引き起こす。
llm.method: Mambaのリカレント状態からの圧縮されたモーション履歴を、状態変化やテキスト条件付き特徴量とともに、局所アテンションからアクセス可能な動的更新スロット（PCM）に変換し、CUDA Graphなどで最適化する。
llm.result: 最大39.52秒のロールアウトで正確な端末制御を示し、最適化された実行により推論遅延を大幅に削減（6.138倍の高速化）し、Unitree G1を用いた実機でのインタラクティブな移動制御を実現した。

2611.29886.title: Active sensing as control over sensory acquisition
2611.29886.abstract: The term "active sensing" is used across neuroscience and engineering to describe a wide range of sensing behaviors, but there is no consensus on what makes sensing "active." We propose that the behaviors grouped under this label are better understood as forms of control over sensory acquisition and develop a framework that distinguishes three interacting forms of control. Mechanistic control physically structures sensory input, strategic control modulates sensing in closed loop through adaptive and attentional processes, and agentic control concerns the sensing policies available to an agent and its authority to choose among them. These forms of control can occur separately or in combination, and have distinct consequences for sensory input, perception, behavior, and performance. The framework clarifies active-passive comparisons and provides a common basis for analyzing biological, engineered, and hybrid sensing systems by asking what is controlled, how, and by whom.

llm.title_ja: 感覚獲得の制御としての能動的センシング
llm.tldr_ja: 本稿では、「能動的センシング」を感覚獲得に対する制御の形式として再定義し、機械的制御、戦略的制御、エージェント的制御の3つの相互作用する形式を区別するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 神経科学やエンジニアリングにおいて「能動的センシング」という用語は多様な感覚行動に広く使われているが、何がセンシングを「能動的」にするのかについてのコンセンサスが存在しない。
llm.method: 感覚入力を物理的に構造化する機械的制御、閉ループで注意プロセスを調節する戦略的制御、利用可能なポリシーとその選択権に関するエージェント的制御の3つを区別するフレームワークを開発する。
llm.result: 能動的・受動的比較を明確にし、生物学的、人工的、およびハイブリッドなセンシングシステムを分析するための共通の基礎を提供する。

2611.29886.tldr_en: A framework is developed that clarifies active-passive comparisons and provides a common basis for analyzing biological, engineered, and hybrid sensing systems by asking what is controlled, how, and by whom.

2611.29884.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
2611.29884.abstract: Particle filters flexibly represent complex, multimodal beliefs but expose them as weighted, unordered sets incompatible with conventional fixed-dimensional policies. We study particle-belief encodings as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies while holding belief estimation and policy optimization fixed. We compare statistical summaries, cumulant-generating-function (CGF) features, and permutation-invariant set encoders. Trainable encoders are learned end-to-end or pretrained through belief reconstruction or task-specific prediction. Across eight tasks, pooling-based set encoders and gradient CGF features are reliable end-to-end, while the Set Transformer achieves the highest performance with appropriate pretraining. Task-specific pretraining helps when its target captures decision-relevant belief structure, whereas reconstruction pretraining and latent alignment provide more selective benefits. For selecting and training particle-belief encoders in partially observable Markov decision processes, our results show that an encoding that reconstructs the belief well is not necessarily a good input for control.

llm.title_ja: 部分観測下での強化学習のためのパーティクル信念表現
llm.tldr_ja: 本場で評価されたように、パーティクルフィルタによる信念表現を強化学習ポリシーの入力として活用する際、信念を適切に再構成するエンコーディングが必ずしも制御にとって最適とは限らないことを示す。
llm.problem: パーティクルフィルタは複雑でマルチモーダルな信念を柔軟に表現するが、重み付きの順序なし集合であるため従来の固定次元ポリシーと互換性がない。
llm.method: 統計的サマリー、キュムラント生成関数（CGF）特徴量、置換不変集合エンコーダーなどを用いたパーティクル信念エンコーディングを、強化学習ポリシーの入力として比較検証する。
llm.result: 8つのタスクを通じて、プーリングベースの集合エンコーダーや勾配CGF特徴量がエンドツーエンドで信頼性が高く、適切な事前学習を行ったSet Transformerが最高の性能を達成したことを示した。
keywords_ja: パーティクルフィルタ

2611.29884.tldr_en: The results show that an encoding that reconstructs the belief well is not necessarily a good input for control, and that an encoding that reconstructs the belief well is not necessarily a good input for control.

2611.29873.title: ProMix: Efficient Data Mixture Optimization for Robotic Imitation via Proxy-Reference DRO
2611.29873.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel in open-world manipulation, yet their performance often saturates when training data are naively pooled across heterogeneous robots, tasks, and environments. Distributionally robust data mixture optimization, exemplified by Re-Mix, can recover much of this performance, but its weight search requires training full-scale policies twice on the entire corpus, placing it out of reach for most laboratories. We present ProMix, a compute-efficient instantiation of the proxy-reference DRO recipe for robotic imitation learning: a 15M-parameter proxy learns per-domain sampling weights by minimizing worst-case excess loss against a frozen reference model, and the learned weights transfer, without re-tuning, to VLA backbones up to 7B parameters. We further provide, to our knowledge, the first controlled analysis of the reference model's role in robotic DRO, showing that removing it induces over-pessimism toward noisy, low-quality domains (-3.8% average and -14.3% worst-domain success rate), and that entropy regularization is needed to prevent weight collapse. Evaluated on 9500 real-world episodes from the Open-X Embodiment dataset, ProMix improves the average success rate over uniform mixing from 68.4% to 76.2%, matching Re-Mix within evaluation noise while reducing mixture-optimization cost to a backbone-independent 11 GPU-hours - versus 16 GPU-hours at the 50M comparison scale and 192 GPU-hours at 7B for full-scale searches - with a +17.1% absolute gain on the worst-case domain.

llm.title_ja: ProMix: プロキシ参照DROによるロボット模倣学習のための効率的なデータ混合最適化
llm.tldr_ja: ProMixは、軽量なプロキシモデルを用いて最悪ケースの過剰損失を最小化することでドメインごとのサンプリング重みを学習し、大規模なVLAバックボーンにそのまま適用できる計算効率の良いデータ混合最適化フレームワークである。
llm.problem: ビジョン・言語・行動（VLA）モデルはオープンワールドのマニピュレーションに優れるが、異種ロボットやタスク、環境間でデータを単純にプールすると性能が飽和し、従来のロバスト最適化は再学習のコストが非常に高い。
llm.method: 1,500万パラメータのプロキシモデルが凍結された参照モデルに対する最悪ケースの超過損失を最小化してドメインごとの重みを学習し、最大7BパラメータのVLAバックボーンに転移させる。
llm.result: Open-X Embodimentデータセットの9500エピソードを用いた評価において、一様混合と比較して平均成功率を68.4%から76.2%に向上させ、計算コストを大幅に削減しつつ最悪ドメインの性能を改善した。

2611.29873.tldr_en: ProMix is presented, a compute-efficient instantiation of the proxy-reference DRO recipe for robotic imitation learning: a 15M-parameter proxy learns per-domain sampling weights by minimizing worst-case excess loss against a frozen reference model, and the learned weights transfer, without re-tuning, to VLA backbones up to 7B parameters.

2611.29868.title: Arcadian: Open-Source Humanoid Ecosystem for Accessible and Customizable Research and Education
2611.29868.abstract: Reproducing and modifying a meter-scale humanoid remains challenging for research and teaching groups with limited fabrication resources and engineering support. This paper presents Arcadian, an open-source humanoid ecosystem that offers accessible and customizable humanoid hardware and software with community support. Arcadian aims to strike a balance among cost-effectiveness, structural durability, and full customizability, lowering the barrier to entry for research and education. Specifically, this meter-scale humanoid adopts metal-embedded 3D printing to achieve a high strength-to-cost ratio, eliminating the need for computer numerical control (CNC) machining while retaining design flexibility. Extensive simulation and hardware tests validate the design: a reinforcement-learning (RL) locomotion policy trained in simulation transfers to the hardware, and a virtual reality (VR) teleoperation interface drives both arms for simple manipulation tasks. The robot is around one meter tall and costs approximately $6,800 to build. All computer-aided design (CAD) models, the bill of materials, assembly documentation, and training and deployment code are publicly released, distributed through Tnkr.ai and MakerWorld and supported by a Discord server and a project forum through which community feedback informs design updates. The ecosystem resources are available at https://anonymous-humanoid.gitbook.io/docs.

llm.title_ja: Arcadian: アクセシブルでカスタマイズ可能な研究・教育のためのオープンソース・ヒューマノイドエコシステム
llm.tldr_ja: Arcadianは、金属埋め込み3Dプリントを採用してコストパフォーマンスと耐久性を両立させ、シミュレーションから強化学習やVR遠隔操作の展開を可能にするオープンソースのヒューマノイドエコシステムである。
llm.problem: 限られた製作リソースや工学サポートしか持たない研究・教育グループにとって、メートスケールのヒューマノイドの再現と改良は依然として困難である。
llm.method: CNC加工を不要にしつつ設計の柔軟性を保持する金属埋め込み3Dプリントによるハードウェア設計を行い、シミュレーションで訓練した強化学習移動ポリシーとVR遠隔操作インターフェースを統合する。
llm.result: 高さ約1m、製作コスト約6,800ドルのヒューマノイドを実現し、シミュレーションで訓練した強化学習移動ポリシーの実機転移や、両腕による簡易マニピュレーションの遠隔操作に成功した。

2611.29868.tldr_en: This paper presents Arcadian, an open-source humanoid ecosystem that offers accessible and customizable humanoid hardware and software with community support, and aims to strike a balance among cost-effectiveness, structural durability, and full customizability.

2611.29850.title: Ego2Wrist: Bootstrapping Wrist-View Synthesis from Egocentric Video
2611.29850.abstract: Wrist cameras provide an action-centric view that is directly relevant to robot manipulation. However, collecting human wrist-camera videos at scale is challenging due to cumbersome setups that can interfere with natural hand movements. In contrast, head-mounted human egocentric videos are much easier to scale.
