Candidate outcomes are evaluated in simulation and composed into latent-command sequences that accomplish the task. Ablations show that neither action-space nor latent-space exploration alone provides the same capability as their coupling. Across diverse out-of-distribution tasks, simulation-based searching using this method produces contact-rich behaviors, including hurdling, manipulating articulated objects, and opening doors through non-prehensile contact. Over ten seeds, LJS completes more of each humanoid task than when searching in either space alone. Beyond humanoids, it also steers a goal-conditioned dexterous hand policy through four assembly tasks better than searching in goal space directly.

llm.title_ja: Latent Jacobian Steer: 事前学習済みヒューマノイドコントローラーからの接触豊かなOOD行動の誘出
llm.tldr_ja: 直接的な関節行動空間におけるサンプリングと、学習済みの凍結されたコントローラーの入力潜在空間のセマンティクスを結合するLatent Jacobian Steer（LJS）を提案する。
llm.problem: 生データの関節行動探索は事前学習済みの調整を乱す可能性があり、潜在空間探索は所望の物理的効果に向けにくい。
llm.method: タスク関連の関節行動摂動をサンプリングし、ポリシーヤコビアンの減衰局所逆行列を通じて候補の潜在コマンドを取得して実行する。
llm.result: シミュレーションベースの探索により、ハードリングや把持を伴わないドア開放などの接触豊かな行動を生成し、タスクをより多く完了できた。

2611.27338.tldr_en: This work proposes Latent Jacobian Steer (LJS), which couples sampling in direct joint-action space with the semantics of the learned frozen controller's input latent space and produces contact-rich behaviors, including hurdling, manipulating articulated objects, and opening doors through non-prehensile contact.

2611.27327.title: Embodied Interaction Policy: A Unified Model for Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction
2611.27327.abstract: Real-time human-robot social interaction requires continuous coordination between speech and physical behavior. Existing systems often separate interaction agents from motion generation, complicating coordination as conversational states change. We propose \textbf{Embodied Interaction Policy (EIP)}, a unified streaming framework that couples an Audio-Interaction expert with a motion expert through layer-wise joint attention. This allows motion generation to directly access the evolving interaction context. A chunk-wise causal mask prevents access to future context, while a vocal token encodes speaking state and the semantic emotion of the response. We construct \textbf{Embodied Interaction Dataset (EI-Data)} from co-speech and dyadic interaction data and train our model in two stages to learn state-adaptive and emotion-conditioned behavior. Combined with the frozen interaction expert, EIP supports continuous robot motion during proactive responses and interruption-aware turn-taking. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate improved motion quality over representative gesture-generation baselines. Compared with a representative cascaded system, EIP achieves higher interaction success and reduces warm-start latency by 64\%. Physical deployment and user studies further demonstrate improved motion naturalness and interaction comfort.
2611.27327.comment: 24 pages, 8 figures, 11 tables. Project page: https://youqiang-gui.github.io/EIP/

llm.title_ja: Embodied Interaction Policy: 全二重ヒューマン・ロボット協調のための統合モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 音声対話エキスパートとモーションエキスパートをレイヤーごとの結合注意により結合する、統合ストリーミングフレームワークEmbodied Interaction Policy（EIP）を提案する。
llm.problem: リアルタイムのヒューマン・ロボット社会的インタラクションでは、会話状態の変化に伴う協調を複雑にする、対話エージェントとモーション生成の分離が存在する。
llm.method: 音声対話エキスパートとモーションエキスパートをレイヤーごとの結合注意機構で結合し、チャンクごとの因果マスクを適用する。
llm.result: 代表的なジェネレーションベースラインと比較してモーション品質が向上し、インタラクション成功率の向上とウォームスタートレイテンシの64%削減を実現した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマン・ロボット協調

2611.27327.tldr_en: Combined with the frozen interaction expert, EIP supports continuous robot motion during proactive responses and interruption-aware turn-taking and achieves higher interaction success and reduces warm-start latency by 64\%.

2611.26617.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
2611.26617.abstract: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.

llm.title_ja: 1つの事前分布、2つの動力学：自己教師あり潜在行動学習のためのビデオ拡散Transformerの転用
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みのビデオ生成モデルを逆動力学と順動力学の両方の事前分布として活用するO2LaFを提案し、ラベルなし動画から転移可能な行動を学習する。
llm.problem: ビデオリポジトリから視覚的遷移を復元できる一方で、潜在行動学習は基盤となる動力学をゼロから学習することが多い課題がある。
llm.method: 1つの事前学習済みビデオDiTから逆・順動力学モデルを初期化し、情報アクセスを制御してコンパクトなボトルネックでエンドツーエンドに最適化する。
llm.result: ナビゲーションおよびロボットマニピュレーションにわたり、少ショット行動探索で新SOTAを達成しゼロショット行動転移を実現した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.26617.tldr_en: O$^{2}$LaF is introduced, a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences, and extends the framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance.
2611.26617.hf_summary_en: O2LaF repurposes a shared pretrained video model to learn inverse and forward latent action dynamics from unlabeled videos, achieving state-of-the-art few-shot action probing and zero-shot action transfer.

2611.26613.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
2611.26613.abstract: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

llm.title_ja: AgentRoboCritic：直接ロボット制御におけるフロンティアエージェントの能力の理解
llm.tldr_ja: 直接ロボット制御を行うフロンティア・マルチモーダル・エージェントの行動レベルの評価を行うフレームワークAgentRoboCriticを提案し、データセットとオープンソースの批評モデルを公開する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークはエピソードごとの成功率しか報告せず、エージェントがどのように成功しどこで失敗したかを示さない。
llm.method: ポリシーエージェントが各行動と共にローカルな意図を述べ、批評家がその結果や失敗モードを評価する意図に基づく批評フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 閉ループでの回復やゼロショット操作の有望な能力を示す一方、把持や位置合わせといった物理的実行のボトルネックを特定した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルエージェント

2611.26613.tldr_en: This paper introduces AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent.

2611.26600.title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
2611.26600.abstract: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

llm.title_ja: ロボット工学のための相補性ベースの接触モデルに関するチュートリアル
llm.tldr_ja: 剛体ダイナミクス、円錐最適化、摩擦接触を接続し、完全な導出と統一された表記法でロボット工学向けの相補性ベースの接触モデルを解説する。
llm.problem: 広く使われているシミュレータは、物理的仮定や数値解法に高度な背景知識を要するコーン相補性定式化に依存している。
llm.method: 剛体ダイナミクス、円錐最適化、摩擦接触を接続し、非侵入や摩擦散逸を符号化する相補性条件を完全な導出とともに解説する。
llm.result: 相補性ベースの接触モデルにおける定式化、ソルバーの選択、計算コスト、堅牢性、物理的忠実度のトレードオフを明確にした。

2611.26600.tldr_en: This tutorial explains how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes, and distinguishes equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep.

2611.26596.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
2611.26596.abstract: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

llm.title_ja: PGX：長期ヒューマノイド移動・操作のための物理的に接地された実行
llm.tldr_ja: 長期的な移動・操作タスクを3層に分解し、訓練不要の古典的コンポーネントに時間・精度制御をオフロードすることでタスク成功率を向上させるPGXを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットVLAモデルは多様な単一操作スキルを実行できるが、時間構造やスキル、精度が緊密に結合した長期移動・操作タスクには苦戦する。
llm.method: 述語ベースの状態マシン、VLAスキル、ワールド座標ロッキングの3層に長期移動・操作を分解する。
llm.result: Unitree G1ヒューマノイドを用いたシミュレーションと実世界の実証により、段階進行とタスク成功率の向上が示された。

2611.26596.tldr_en: The effectiveness of PGX is demonstrated with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates.

2611.26565.title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
2611.26565.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations. All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%. Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

llm.title_ja: PhyDEX：動的外発的器用さを通じた視覚言語行動モデルにおける物理的推論のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 動的外発的器用さを通じてVLAモデルの物理的推論能力を評価するスローイングベンチマークPhyDEXを提案し、既存モデルの性能限界と物理的盲点を明らかにする。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは把持と物体の接触を評価するが、環境との物理的相互作用を無視しており、ポリシーが物理を理解しているか不明確である。
llm.method: 質量・重心・摩擦の推論を必要とする、スローイングに基づく35K軌跡からなる自動生成ベンチマークPhyDEXを構築する。
llm.result: 代表的VLAの成功率は3%未満であり、事前学習済みモデルのロバスト性不足と物理的盲点が主なボトルネックであることを特定した。

2611.26565.tldr_en: This work introduces PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace, and reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success.

2611.26519.title: ACE-Brain-0.7: Learning Execution-Grounded Reasoning for Embodied Agents
2611.26519.abstract: Reliable reasoning for long-horizon embodied tasks requires predictions grounded in the observed execution state. We present ACE-Brain-0.7, a 9B vision--language model that combines spatial grounding, task understanding, and progress estimation. To train the model, we curate 3.7 million question--answer pairs, drawing execution supervision from egocentric human videos, robot episodes, and simulation. These questions span different stages of an execution and connect task-level judgments with observed progress and outcomes. We then fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this collection together with additional task, spatial-grounding, and progress-estimation data. Across six public task-reasoning benchmarks, ACE-Brain-0.7 achieves an average score of 76.5, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 72.7 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.5. Our model also leads the evaluated models in spatial grounding, averaging 75.90 across seven benchmarks and reaching 91.25 Acc@0.5 on RefCOCOg. Controlled evaluations further indicate that our task-only model makes more effective use of visual history and more accurately distinguishes execution states. Together, these results show that ACE-Brain-0.7 effectively combines spatial perception with temporal understanding, delivering strong execution-grounded reasoning and comparing favorably with closed-source models.

llm.title_ja: ACE-Brain-0.7：身体性エージェントのための実行接地型推論の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 空間接地、タスク理解、進捗推定を統合した9Bの視覚言語モデルACE-Brain-0.7を提案し、多様なタスク推論ベンチマークで高い性能を達成する。
llm.problem: 長期的な身体性タスクにおける信頼性の高い推論には、観測された実行状態に接地された予測が必要とされる課題がある。
llm.method: 人間の一次視点動画、ロボットエピソード、シミュレーションから収集した370万件のQ&Aペアを用いてQwen3.5-9Bをファインチューニングする。
llm.result: 6つの公開タスク推論ベンチマークで平均スコア76.5を達成し、既存のクローズドソースモデルを上回る性能を示した。

2611.26519.tldr_en: Results show that ACE-Brain-0.7 effectively combines spatial perception with temporal understanding, delivering strong execution-grounded reasoning and comparing favorably with closed-source models.

2611.26503.title: JARVIS: An Agent That Designs, Builds, and Tests Circuit Boards on Its Own
2611.26503.abstract: Power electronics is central to the energy transition, but developing new hardware still relies on human-led design, fabrication, testing, and iteration. We present JARVIS, an embodied AI agent that autonomously closes this loop for circuit boards. JARVIS maintains machine-specific capabilities and constraints, scans its workspace using a robot-mounted 3D scanner, and constructs an executable digital twin in which it rehearses robot motions, fabrication steps, and circuit behavior before consuming materials. A single text instruction initiates the physical experiment. Using unmodified desktop equipment, the agent coordinates a robot arm, a PCB printer that deposits conductive silver ink and solder paste, and a pick-and-place machine. It verifies progress using cameras and sensors, then tests the fabricated circuit with an OPAL-RT real-time simulator and an oscilloscope. Based on the measurements, JARVIS diagnoses deviations from the design and generates a revised design in KiCad for subsequent rehearsal. In a demonstration involving a 60 Hz notch filter for grid-connected converter sensing, JARVIS completed a first-run experiment in 2 h 39 min without human intervention, achieving 50.6 dB attenuation at 60 Hz. Its digital-twin rehearsal identified five issues before fabrication, including a test criterion that would have incorrectly rejected a functioning board. During execution, the agent also resolved encountered faults autonomously. These results demonstrate an integrated agent-driven workflow for physical design, fabrication, measurement, and iterative improvement of power-electronic circuitry. To our knowledge, JARVIS is the first system in power electronics in which an agent closes the physical design-build-test-learn loop for circuit boards.

llm.title_ja: JARVIS：自ら回路基板の設計、構築、テストを行うエージェント
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dスキャナとデジタルツインを用いたリハーサルを活用し、回路基板の設計・製造・測定・改善のループを自律的に完結させる身体性AIエージェントJARVISを提案する。
llm.problem: パワーエレクトロニクスのハードウェア開発は、依然として人間の主導による設計、製作、テスト、反復に依存している。
llm.method: ロボットアーム、PCBプリンタ、ピックアンドプレース機を調整し、デジタルツインで動作を予行演習した上で実機実験を行う。
llm.result: 人間介入なしで60Hzノッチフィルタ基板の製造とテストを2時間39分で完了し、設計上の問題を事前に特定・解決した。
keywords_ja: パワーエレクトロニクス

2611.26503.tldr_en: JARVIS is the first system in power electronics in which an agent closes the physical design-build-test-learn loop for circuit boards, demonstrating an integrated agent-driven workflow for physical design, fabrication, measurement, and iterative improvement of power-electronic circuitry.

2611.26485.title: An Open-Source ROS 2 Framework for Shared Control in Surgical Teleoperation: Integrating the Haply Inverse3 with the da Vinci Research Kit
2611.26485.abstract: Surgical teleoperation deprives surgeons of touch, forcing visual inference of tissue forces; the commercial platforms now restoring force feedback remain closed, preventing open research on haptic shared control. This paper provides a system contribution: it presents an open-source, ROS 2-native framework that integrates the compact, three-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) Haply Inverse3 haptic device with the da~Vinci Research Kit (dVRK). The framework includes a novel mapping strategy that combines 3-DOF translational device input with separately tracked VerseGrip orientation into 6-DOF patient-side manipulator commands. Two virtual-fixture-inspired guidance modes serve as reference implementations to evaluate the framework in a within-subjects user study on a teleoperated hot-wire benchmark task in simulation, and the architecture is further demonstrated on physical dVRK hardware. Relative to unassisted manual control, linear guidance significantly reduced both the number of wire contacts and the task completion time, whereas the progressive-stiffness guidance produced consistent but statistically non-significant trends in the same direction. Subjective ratings of workload, agency, and satisfaction showed favorable descriptive trends for the guidance modes. The results demonstrate the feasibility of haptic shared control with a compact device coupled to the dVRK and provide an openly available, reproducible platform for future research. They further suggest that simpler linear feedback may be more robust for inexperienced operators than more complex profiles.

llm.title_ja: 外科的遠隔操作における共有制御のためのオープンソースROS 2フレームワーク：Haply Inverse3とda Vinci Research Kitの統合
llm.tldr_ja: Haply Inverse3ハプティックデバイスとda Vinci Research Kitを統合したROS 2ネイティブのオープンソースフレームワークを提案し、触覚共有制御の有効性を実証する。
llm.problem: 商用の力覚提示プラットフォームはクローズドであり、触覚共有制御に関するオープンな研究が妨げられている。
llm.method: 3自由度のハプティックデバイス入力と追跡された方向を組み合わせて6自由度の操作コマンドを生成するマッピング戦略と案内モードを実装する。
llm.result: 直線案内により、未経験の操作者でもワイヤ接触回数と作業時間が大幅に削減されることを被験者実験で実証した。

2611.26485.tldr_en: An open-source, ROS 2-native framework that integrates the compact, three-degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) Haply Inverse3 haptic device with the da~Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) is presented and it is suggested that simpler linear feedback may be more robust for inexperienced operators than more complex profiles.

2611.26444.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
2611.26444.abstract: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.
2611.26444.hf_summary_en: A diagnostic benchmark of 180 simulated manipulation configurations evaluates whether embodied systems can combine history-based reasoning, precise execution, and closed-loop environmental feedback, revealing that single-view competence does not transfer to composed tasks.

llm.title_ja: Mind2Act World：ロボットマニプリレーションにおける身体性マインド、物理的行動、およびマインド・行動の合成のための診断ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 履歴ベースの推論、正確な実行、環境フィードバックによる合成能力を評価する診断ベンチマークMind2Act Worldを提案し、単一ビューの能力が合成タスクに直結しないことを明らかにする。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは推論と実行を単一のタスク内で評価するか別々に評価するため、失敗の原因がどこにあるのか分からない。
llm.method: 過去の観測に基づく意思決定、正確な実行、および両者を組み合わせた閉ループタスクからなる3つの視点を持つ180のシミュレーション環境を構築する。
llm.result: 単一ビューで優れた性能を持つシステムでも合成タスクでは大幅に成功率が低下し、連絡の維持や状態保持に課題があることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.26444.tldr_en: Evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks, pointing to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

2611.26438.title: Risk-Controlled Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.26438.abstract: Retrieval-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) models enable efficient test-time adaptation by leveraging expert demonstrations as additional context without updating model parameters. However, even when retrieved demonstrations are relevant to the current task, the VLA may fail to effectively utilize the retrieved information, ultimately leading to task failure. To address this challenge, we propose R2-VLA, a risk-controlled retrieval-augmented VLA framework that enables reliable test-time adaptation by satisfying a user-specified task success rate requirement with minimal expert assistance. Specifically, R2-VLA learns an uncertainty predictor that estimates the uncertainty of the VLA's predicted actions given the retrieved demonstrations, guiding when to act autonomously or request expert assistance. We further introduce a task-level risk-control procedure that calibrates the uncertainty threshold to satisfy a user-specified task-failure risk requirement. Moreover, R2-VLA continually incorporates expert corrections into its retrieval memory to improve future adaptation while preserving the prescribed task-level risk guarantee. Experiments across three VLA backbones and four LIBERO benchmark suites demonstrate that R2-VLA improves average task success by 9.2--11.2 percentage points, achieving the desired target with fewer expert requests. These results highlight the effectiveness of connecting the usefulness of retrieved demonstrations with task-level risk control to enable successful robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデルのためのリスク制御型テスト時適応
llm.tldr_ja: エキスパートのデモを活用してテスト時適応を行う際、ユーザ指定の成功率要件を満たすように不確実性を予測し自律行動と支援要請を切り替えるR2-VLAを提案する。
llm.problem: 検索拡張型VLAモデルはデモを活用してテスト時適応できるが、情報を有効に利用できずタスク失敗に至ることがある。
llm.method: 予測の不確実性を推定する不確実性予測器を学習し、ユーザ指定のリスク要件を満たすように閾値を較正するリスク制御手順を導入する。
llm.result: 4つのLIBEROベンチマークスイートにおいて平均タスク成功率を9.2〜11.2ポイント向上させ、少ないエキスパート要請で目標を達成した。

2611.26438.tldr_en: R2-VLA is proposed, a risk-controlled retrieval-augmented VLA framework that enables reliable test-time adaptation by satisfying a user-specified task success rate requirement with minimal expert assistance and introduces a task-level risk-control procedure that calibrates the uncertainty threshold to satisfy a user-specified task-failure risk requirement.

2611.26434.title: HumanCOIN: A 12,500-Hour Dataset for Human Intent in Egocentric Manipulation
2611.26434.abstract: First-person manipulation datasets treat the observation-action pair as the atomic unit and compress the generation and execution of an action into a policy network's weights, rendering the intent state behind the action unobservable. Human motor control research shows that intent mediates between observation and action and leaves observable traces along the intent pathway from decision to effect: gaze reaches the target before the hand, muscle load builds before contact, and cortical activity precedes the motor command. To record this pathway at scale, we present HumanCOIN, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies. At the output end, the L1 attention tier (10,000 h) infers gaze from headband camera video, exposing the operator's next object of attention and reach before the hand moves. Midway, the L2 exertion tier (2,000 h) records surface EMG from armbands, making load expectations readable before execution is complete. At the origin, the L3 cognition tier (500 h) records scalp EEG, giving early readouts of task decisions and monitoring. Each tier inherits all proxies from the tiers below. The dataset further provides multi-view RGB images, depth maps and point clouds, 6-DoF head and wrist pose, and step-level action and object annotations. The controlled L3 setting additionally measures gaze, hand pose and finger kinematics directly. Clock and calibration data are released with the dataset so that any read rate can be re-aligned. The three tiers cover three stations, from visual orienting to cortical preparation, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale. Project page: https://flagopen.github.io/HumanCOIN.

llm.title_ja: HumanCOIN：一人称視点操作における人間の意図に関する12,500時間のデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的指向、筋活動、皮質準備の3つの階層プロキシを通じて人間の意図を捉えた、12,500時間に及ぶ一人称視点操作データセットHumanCOINを構築する。
llm.problem: 一人称視点データセットは観察と行動のペアをアトミックな単位として扱い、行動の背後にある意図の状態を観測不能にする。
llm.method: アテンション（視線）、筋電図（筋負荷）、脳波（認知）の3階層のプロキシとマルチモーダルセンサデータを同期して大規模に記録する。
llm.result: 視覚的行動ペアの背後にあるプロセスをモデル化するための、視覚から皮質準備までをカバーする大規模データセットを公開した。

2611.26434.tldr_en: HumanCOIN is presented, a first-person manipulation dataset built around human intent: 12,500 hours across 38 scene classes with three tiers of proxies, making the process behind visual-action pairs available for modeling at dataset scale.

2611.26427.title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management
2611.26427.abstract: Long-term agents accumulate large external memory stores as interactions unfold, increasing the costs of storage, retrieval, and response generation. Efficiency is constrained by two coupled factors: a growing record count increases retrieval overhead, while longer retrieved contexts increase prefill computation and decoding-time attention costs. Existing methods prune or consolidate records, but pruning can discard useful evidence, whereas consolidation may produce fewer yet longer retrieval units. We introduce MemFolder, a structure-guided memory folding framework that sequentially reduces record count and context length. The framework comprises two core components that share memory groups, using cross-record structure to guide both evidence consolidation and compact representation. RecordFolder grounds entity mentions, progressively selects representative yet complementary anchors, and combines semantic and entity affinity with temporal chaining to consolidate compatible records into fewer retrieval units. ContextFolder encodes the original records within these groups into compact text and uses verification feedback to revise encodings when key facts cannot be recovered. Experiments on the three text-based memory benchmarks LoCoMo, PersonaMem, and LongMemEval and the two multimodal benchmarks M3-Bench-web and M3-Bench-robot demonstrate the strong performance of our methods. Notably, on Mem0, RecordFolder retains 99.0% of the original average performance across the three text-based benchmarks with 50% fewer records, exceeding the strongest baseline by 1.9 percentage points in performance retention. Combined with ContextFolder, existing record compression methods further shorten their output records while retaining most of their performance.

llm.title_ja: MemFolder：効率的なエージェント記憶管理のための構造誘導型メモリフォールディング
llm.tldr_ja: クロスレコード構造を利用して証拠の統合とコンパクトな表現を導出することで、レコード数とコンテキスト長を逐次削減するMemFolderを提案する。
llm.problem: 長期エージェントは外部記憶の蓄積に伴い、ストレージ、検索、応答生成のコストが増加する課題がある。
llm.method: エンティティ言及の接地や時間的連鎖を用いて互換性のあるレコードを統合するRecordFolderと、コンパクトなテキストにエンコードするContextFolderを組み合わせる。
llm.result: テキストおよびマルチモーダルなメモリベンチマークにおいて、レコード数を50%削減しつつ元の性能を99.0%保持することを実証した。

2611.26427.tldr_en: MemFolder is introduced, a structure-guided memory folding framework that sequentially reduces record count and context length and combined with ContextFolder, existing record compression methods further shorten their output records while retaining most of their performance.

2611.26420.title: Awaken-HI: Scaling Humanoid Intelligence with Whole-Body Human Experience
2611.26420.abstract: A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale. We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills. Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert. We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.

llm.title_ja: Awaken-HI：全身の人間の経験によるヒューマノイド知能のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 約50,000時間のステレオ動画と同期された全身の人間モーションデータを組み合わせたAwaken-Humanを構築し、共有行動エキスパートを通じてヒューマノイドの移動・操作を学習するAwaken-HIを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の一人称視点動画データセットは多くの活動をカバーするが、大規模な移動・操作の学習に必要な同期された全身モーションデータが不足している。
llm.method: 人間の軌跡によって共有行動エキスパートを直接監督するVLAモデルを構築し、プレトレーニングと適応を行う。
llm.result: T800での適応後、8つの個別タスクで平均成功率93.75%を達成し、既存モデルを上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.26420.tldr_en: It is shown that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert, and increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks.

2611.26405.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
2611.26405.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.
2611.26405.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Project page: https://tacinno.github.io

llm.title_ja: TacInno：視覚・行動を超えた接触ダイナミクスをVLAモデルに教える
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚と行動では説明できない接触ダイナミクスである「触覚イノベーション」を学習ターゲットとして分離し、VLAモデルに予測させるTacInnoを提案する。
llm.problem: 触覚入力を追加しても、変形などの触覚変化の多くが視覚と行動から予測可能なため、モデルが触覚入力をほとんど利用しない場合がある。
llm.method: 将来の触覚変化を離散コードに圧縮するTacInnoトークナイザを導入し、ポリシー側は推論時にモジュールを追加せずそのコードを予測するよう学習する。
llm.result: シミュレーションで平均成功率87.5%、実世界で70.5%を達成し、従来の触覚ベースラインを上回った。

2611.26405.tldr_en: TacInno is introduced, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target, and demonstrates the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

2611.26390.title: SpecFlow: Flow Matching in the Acceleration Spectrum for Multi-Agent Trajectory Forecasting
2611.26390.abstract: Multimodal trajectory forecasting must cover diverse future behaviors without sacrificing dynamical coherence. Most generative forecasters evolve frame-wise positions directly, leaving the relationships among position, velocity, and acceleration implicit. We present SpecFlow, a conditional flow-matching framework that treats the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) coefficients of future accelerations as its generative state. SpecFlow learns a transport from Gaussian noise to acceleration spectra and reconstructs velocity and position through fixed analytical integration initialized by the last observed state. A joint phase-space objective supervises all three kinematic levels. To represent destination uncertainty without future information, an endpoint predictor produces candidate destinations and confidence scores solely from observed context, and the highest-confidence candidate conditions the spectral denoiser. Alternating attention over trajectory hypotheses and agents captures multimodality and interaction. Under best-of-20 evaluation, SpecFlow achieves average minADE/minFDE of 0.15/0.22 on ETH/UCY, 0.69/0.86 at four seconds on NBA, and 7.38/11.57 on SDD. It establishes state-of-the-art results across all five ETH/UCY scenes and achieves the lowest four-second ADE on NBA with a tied-best FDE, while remaining competitive on SDD. Together, these results demonstrate that acceleration-spectrum flow matching provides an effective structured generative state across smooth pedestrian motion, coordinated multi-agent sports dynamics, and heterogeneous outdoor trajectories. Code will be made publicly available.

llm.title_ja: SpecFlow：マルチエージェント軌跡予測のための加速度スペクトルにおけるフローマッチング
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の加速度の離散コサイン変換係数を生成状態として扱い、ガウスノイズから加速度スペクトルへの輸送を学習する条件付きフローマッチングフレームワークSpecFlowを提案する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル軌跡予測は動的一貫性を犠牲にすることなく多様な将来の行動をカバーする必要があるが、位置を直接進化させる手法では関係性が暗黙的になる。
llm.method: 加速度スペクトルを生成状態とし、分析的積分により速度と位置を再構築する条件付きフローマッチングを構築する。
llm.result: 5つのETH/UCYシーンすべてでSOTAを達成し、歩行者からスポーツ、屋外軌跡まで効果的な構造化生成状態を提供することを示した。

2611.26390.tldr_en: Results demonstrate that acceleration-spectrum flow matching provides an effective structured generative state across smooth pedestrian motion, coordinated multi-agent sports dynamics, and heterogeneous outdoor trajectories.

2611.26389.title: ViDecide: Teaching Video Diffusion Models to Reason and Plan Step by Step
2611.26389.abstract: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.

llm.title_ja: ViDecide：ビデオ拡散モデルに段階的な推論と計画を教える
llm.tldr_ja: 状態遷移を因果的に予測し停止タイミングを決定する意思決定中心のフレームワークViDecideを提案し、ビデオ拡散モデルを信頼性の高い推論・計画者として機能させる。
llm.problem: 既存のビデオ生成モデルは、大規模な推論データや拡散RLで訓練された後でも、多段階の推論や計画において物理的・論理的制約に違反することが多い。
llm.method: 状態遷移を因果的に予測する意思決定中心の学習スケジュールと、失敗した決定のノイズを成功した継続にマッピングするCorrective Fine-tuningを導入する。
llm.result: 抽象ゲーム、計画タスク、ロボット計画の新しいベンチマークにおいて平均厳密成功率83.8%を達成し、従来法を大きく上回った。

2611.26389.tldr_en: This work presents ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule, and proposes Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization.
2611.26389.hf_summary_en: ViDecide trains video diffusion models to make causal state-transition and stopping decisions, using Corrective Fine-tuning to improve multi-step planning success without policy gradients.

2611.26385.title: Beyond the Sink Interpretation: Radial Attention in Flow-Based VLA Policies
2611.26385.abstract: Prior work calls the high attention on the first and last action tokens of a flow-based VLA policy a radial action sink, and uses these tokens to set the execution horizon. In language models, a sink is a token with high incoming attention, a small value, and little effect on the output. We test whether that profile holds, not the horizon rule, in one $π_{0.5}$ checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks. The two endpoints receive 5.4% of action-key mass, 1.4 percentage points above their uniform share, and rotary positional encoding produces this excess: directly in shallow layers and through upstream action-token RoPE deeper in the network. The endpoints do not fit the sink profile. Their value norms stay near the action-token mean in all 18 layers. On 250 paired episodes, masking them or zeroing their values changes success by less than 4 points, and replacing their value directions with those of another observation lowers it by 3.2 to 7.2 points across three donors, whereas the same replacement on two non-endpoint tokens in the executed prefix lowers it by 28.4 points. The token that does fit the sink profile on mass and value norm is the prefix BOS; on this checkpoint, zeroing its value raises success in two paired runs, by +13.2 points (95% CI [+7.0, +19.4]) and +6.0 points ([+0.2, +11.8]). Inside the action chunk, a relative-offset routing profile estimated on other tasks keeps 75% of action-token spread and keeps closed-loop success on three held-out tasks (42.7% against a 38.7% baseline), while uniform or shuffled routing drops success to 3-4%. High attention mass alone does not tell what a token does.

llm.title_ja: シンク解釈の向こう側：フローベースVLAポリシーにおける放射状アテンション
llm.tldr_ja: フローベースVLAポリシーのエンドポイントアクションが従来の「アテンションシンク」のプロファイルに当てはまらないことを示し、実際の値の寄与や相対オフセットルーティングの効果を検証する。
llm.problem: フローベースVLAポリシーの最初と最後のアクションストリームへの高いアテンションは放射状アクションシンクと呼ばれてきたが、そのプロファイルが実際に満たされているかは未検証であった。
llm.method: チェックポイントのエンドポイントトークンの値のノルム、マスクやゼロ化の影響、および相対オフセットルーティングプロファイルを実験的に分析する。
llm.result: エンドポイントはシンクプロファイルに適合せず、真のシンクはプレフィックスのBOSトークンであり、相対オフセットルーティングにより閉ループ成功率が維持されることを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル
フローベースポリシー

2611.26385.tldr_en: This work tests whether that profile holds, not the horizon rule, in one $\pi_{0.5}$ checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks, in which the high attention on the first and last action tokens of a flow-based VLA policy a radial action sink.

2611.26376.title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience
2611.26376.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.

llm.title_ja: アライメントが再利用を駆動する：異種経験からの汎化可能なロボット利用エージェントの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 異なるロボット embodiment やタスク設定のインタフェースや座標系を整列させることで、共有スキルセットを共同で洗練させるフレームワークUniCraftを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボット embodiment、タスク定式化、幾何学的規約、行動インタフェースの異質性が、ベンチマークやハードウェア間でのインタラクション経験を断片化している。
llm.method: 観測されたシーンジオメトリを統一座標系で表現し、感知・制御インタフェースを整列させ、デモやモデル重みの更新なしに共有スキルとポリシーを洗練する。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROなどの未見のシナリオやタスクにおいて、プールされたタスク成功率を大幅に向上させ、ゼロショット転移を実現した。

2611.26376.tldr_en: This work proposes UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings, which represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots.

2611.26350.title: PUPPET: Physical-Unified Platform for Presence, Embodiment, and Teleoperation
2611.26350.abstract: Remote access to robotics hardware does not by itself guarantee usable experimental data. A teleoperated trial can complete the task and still produce an incomplete or inconsistent record. PUPPET aims to solve this problem by presenting a cyber-physical framework that opens a physical robotics laboratory through a continuously synchronized VR replica of the robot, stranding environment, and task objects. In addition, PUPPET integrates a trial validation pipeline built into the experimental workflow. We evaluated PUPPET in a within-subject study with 30 participants, who performed the same table-to-shelf object-transfer task in person, through 2D teleoperation, and through PUPPET. VR reduced post-learning completion time by 27.7% over 2D (68.7,s vs. 95.0,s), statistically indistinguishable from in-person execution (72.1,s). It also produced more validation-ready (85.6% vs. 66.0%) and intervention-free (89.7% vs. 67.2%) trials. With PUPPET we show that modality shapes the remote task performance and the reusability of the resulting experimental record.

llm.title_ja: PUPPET：存在感、身体性、遠隔操作のための物理統合型プラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 同期されたVRレプリカを通じてロボット実験室を開放し、実験ワークフローに組み込まれた試行検証パイプラインを提供するサイバー物理フレームワークPUPPETを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットハードウェアへのリモートアクセス自体は、それだけでは有用な実験データを保証せず、不完全または一貫性のない記録を生むことがある。
llm.method: ロボットや環境、タスクオブジェクトの同期VRレプリカと、実験ワークフローに組み込まれた試行検証パイプラインを統合する。
llm.result: 30人の被験者を用いた実験により、VRが2D遠隔操作と比較して完了時間を短縮し、検証可能な試行を増やすことを実証した。
keywords_ja: サイバー物理システム

2611.26350.tldr_en: With PUPPET, modality shapes the remote task performance and the reusability of the resulting experimental record and it is shown that modality shapes the remote task performance and the reusability of the resulting experimental record.

2611.26341.title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
2611.26341.abstract: Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both. To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor. These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment. On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate. Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

llm.title_ja: オンデマンド推論：長期ロボット操作のための効率的なエージェント型ロボット制御
llm.tldr_ja: オンラインのタスク状態モニタを介して低レベルポリシーと高-level推論エージェントを調整し、イベント駆動型のエージェントレビューを行う枠組みRoCを提案する。
llm.problem: 大規模マルチモーダルモデルは長期ロボット操作を支援できるが、頻繁なモデル呼び出しにより高い遅延とトークンコストが発生する。
llm.method: 時間的視覚観測とインタフェースメモリを組み合わせて進捗推定と次タスク予測を行い、必要なときだけエージェントの介入を促す。
llm.result: RMBenchにおいて従来のエージェントベースラインと比較してタスク成功率を24.0ポイント向上させ、トークン消費量を65.3%削減した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルモデル

2611.26341.tldr_en: RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor, supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

2611.26313.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives
2611.26313.abstract: One fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) is enforcing temporal safety constraints, such as satisfying formal specifications. Existing methods often transform logic formulas into automata for state augmentation and reward shaping. However, this approach assumes that automaton construction is both feasible and tractable, which limits its applicability to small specifications and linear temporal logic (LTL). This paper proposes Actor-Predictor, a framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress without explicitly constructing an automaton. The predictor continuously estimates whether a partial trajectory will satisfy the formal specification in a later step, and its learned features are provided as auxiliary inputs to the actor, which is then optimized using GRPO and RWR. We show theoretically that, under sufficient predictive accuracy, the learned representation is equivalent to the automaton state. Experiments on grid world and robotic tasks in Isaac Lab demonstrate that Actor-Predictor outperforms automaton-based baselines on LTL-constrained tasks. It also performs well on non-regular formal specifications, such as $(a^n b^n)$, for which finite-automaton-based approaches are not applicable.

llm.title_ja: 形式仕様の目的に対する強化学習のためのActor-Predictorアーキテクチャ
llm.tldr_ja: オートマトンを明示的に構築することなく論理の進捗のサロゲート表現を学習するActor-Predictorフレームワークを提案し、LTL制約付きタスクでオートマトンベースの手法を上回る性能を示す。
llm.problem: 強化学習における時間的安全性制約の強制は、オートマトン構築の困難さにより小さな仕様やLTLに限定されるという課題がある。
llm.method: 明示的なオートマトン構築なしに、部分軌道が将来仕様を満たすかを継続的に予測しその特徴をアクターの補助入力とするフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: Isaac Labのグリッドワールドおよびロボットタスクの実験において、LTL制約タスクでオートマトンベースのベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2611.26313.tldr_en: Actor-Predictor is proposed, a framework that learns a surrogate representation of logic progress without explicitly constructing an automaton, and it is shown theoretically that, under sufficient predictive accuracy, the learned representation is equivalent to the automaton state.

2611.26302.title: Exposure-Aware Informative Path Planning Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
2611.26302.abstract: This paper addresses the finite-budget exposure-aware informative path planning (IPP) problem for a fleet of mobile sensing agents. The agents map an unknown scalar field while limiting exposure to high field intensity. Existing IPP methods optimize informativeness under motion or resource constraints, but do not address field exposure constraints. We formulate exposure-aware IPP (EA-IPP) as a scalarized bi-objective belief-state Markov decision process that trades the normalized Gaussian-process (GP) information gain against a normalized measurement-derived fleet exposure index. A parameter-shared proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework with decentralized actors and a centralized fleet critic is trained offline and evaluated on unseen fields. Across the radar, plume, and wildfire field families, the EA-IPP agent achieves the lowest GP reconstruction RMSE among the evaluated baselines while retaining D-optimal information within $10\%$ of the non-learning information baseline. The minimum field exposure is approximately $34.6\%$, $20.1\%$, and $27\%$ below the non-exposure-aware baseline for radar, plume, and wildfire, respectively.

llm.title_ja: 深層強化学習を用いた被曝考慮型情報的経路計画
llm.tldr_ja: 未知のスカラー場をマッピングしながら高強度場への露出を制限する露出考慮型情報的経路計画（EA-IPP）を、パラメータ共有型PPOフレームワークを用いて実現した。
llm.problem: 既存のIPP手法は運動やリソースの制約下での情報量を最適化するが、場への露出制約に対処していない。
llm.method: 正規化ガウス過程の情報利得と正規化計測由来の被曝指標をトレードオフするビオブジェクティブ信念状態MDPとして定式化し、PPOで学習する。
llm.result: GP再構成RMSEが最も低くなり、非露出考慮型ベースラインと比較して場への露出を大幅に削減した。

2611.26302.tldr_en: This paper addresses the finite-budget exposure-aware informative path planning (IPP) problem for a fleet of mobile sensing agents by forming exposure-aware IPP as a scalarized bi-objective belief-state Markov decision process that trades the normalized Gaussian-process information gain against a normalized measurement-derived fleet exposure index.

2611.26293.title: LocoMuJoCo: A Comprehensive Imitation Learning Benchmark for Whole-Body Control
2611.26293.abstract: LocoMuJoCo is an open-source benchmark for imitation learning (IL) and reinforcement learning (RL) on whole-body control. The library couples MuJoCo (CPU) with MJX and the MjWarp backend (GPU) under a single API, exposes 9 humanoid, 3 (musculo-)skeletal, and 4 quadruped embodiments, and ships a curated native motion-capture dataset for every humanoid, to which it can also retarget AMASS and LAFAN1. A modular plug-in architecture makes observations, rewards, control modes, terrains, and domain randomization fully interchangeable, while compact JAX implementations of many RL and IL algorithms provide JIT-compiled end-to-end training, and the companion loco-mujoco-real repository provides sim-to-real deployment. We describe the design, the SMPL-to-robot and robot-to-robot retargeting pipeline, and a usage example. LocoMuJoCo is released under MIT at https://github.com/robfiras/loco-mujoco.

llm.title_ja: LocoMuJoCo：全身制御のための包括的な模倣学習ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: MuJoCo、MJX、MjWarpバックエンドを単一APIで統合し、多数のロボット形態とモーションキャプチャデータセットを提供するオープンソースの模倣・強化学習ベンチマークLocoMuJoCoを提案する。
llm.problem: 全身制御の模倣学習および強化学習において、多様なバックエンドやロボット形態を統合し、シム・ツ・リアル展開まで一貫して扱える包括的なベンチマークが不足している。
llm.method: MuJoCo、MJX、MjWarpを単一APIで結合し、複数のヒューマノイドや四脚ロボットの形態と専用データセット、モジュール式プラグイン構造を提供する。
llm.result: JITコンパイルによるエンドツーエンドの訓練を可能にし、シム・ツ・リアル展開用のリポジトリも提供する。

2611.26293.tldr_en: The design, the SMPL-to-robot and robot-to-robot retargeting pipeline, and a usage example are described.

2611.26276.title: I See You: Initial Multi-Robot LiDAR Registration with Mutual-Observation Checks
2611.26276.abstract: Compared to single-robot deployments, multi-robot teams can significantly improve search-and-rescue (SAR) mission success by covering large areas in parallel. To collaborate effectively, these robots must be registered in a common reference frame. Standard registration methods typically rely on external infrastructure or significant map overlap, but real deployments require infrastructure-free, stationary initial alignment for immediate operation. While global LiDAR point cloud registration addresses this, existing single-scan methods often fail silently in aliased or degenerate environments. Approaches scaling beyond two agents also remain rarely evaluated in real-world scenarios. We propose a centralized, deployment-ready framework for pre-mission multi-robot registration. Our system performs pairwise coarse-to-fine alignment and actively rejects impossible pose hypotheses via deterministic plausibility checks. We validate the framework on a real-world custom dataset of four synchronized robots in various environments with ground truth. The checks reject more than a third of the incorrect pairwise registrations while falsely rejecting less than 1% of the correct ones, and reduce the number of team registrations with a wrong robot pose by 38%. Dataset and code are publicly available.
2611.26276.comment: Accepted final version. IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR), Incheon, South Korea, November 2026. Project page: https://tu-darmstadt-ros-pkg.github.io/i-see-you-registration

llm.title_ja: I See You：相互観測チェックによる初期マルチロボットLiDARレジストレーション
llm.tldr_ja: インフラストラクチャを必要とせず、決定論的妥当性チェックにより不可能なポーズ仮説を積極的に排除して初期アライメントを行う、展開可能なマルチロボット登録フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 現実の展開において、マルチロボットチームはインフラストラクチャなしで即座に動作するための静的な初期アライメントを必要とするが、既存の単一スキャン手法は失敗しやすい。
llm.method: ペアごとの粗いから細かいアライメントを実行し、決定論的な妥当性チェックによって不可能なポーズ仮説を積極的に排除する中央集権的フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 4台の同期ロボットによる現実世界のカスタムデータセットを用いた検証で、誤ったペア登録の3分の1以上を排除し、チーム登録のポーズ誤りを38%削減した。
keywords_ja: サーチアンドレスキュー

2611.26276.tldr_en: This work proposes a centralized, deployment-ready framework for pre-mission multi-robot registration that performs pairwise coarse-to-fine alignment and actively rejects impossible pose hypotheses via deterministic plausibility checks.

2611.26242.title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
2611.26242.abstract: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion at each update, integrated into a local trajectory, and advanced by consuming the current action. The corrected remainder is written back to the buffer, preserving motion corrections across successive updates. A bounded refresh rule normalizes speed and curvature variations within a newly decoded plan and assigns a short or long reuse budget according to the resulting plan-roughness score. The interface requires neither backbone features nor an additional learned driving policy. Over a 3 s horizon, independent real-request evaluation achieves average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) of 0.328/0.596 m on ORAD-3D and 0.266/0.526 m on RELLIS-3D, reducing FDE by 18.0% and 36.7% at request rates of 6.0% and 4.8%, respectively. These runs retain lower errors across four backbones and both datasets and reduce Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by factors of 16.6 and 20.8 under serial replay, while mechanism and motion-only controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the observed accuracy benefit. The source code and evaluation materials are publicly available at https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA.

llm.title_ja: FastRoverVLA：オフロード自動運転のための高速視覚・言語・行動実行
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚プラン生成とモーション条件付き実行を分離し、高価なマルチモーダル推論の頻度を抑えつつ正確な軌道追従を実現する学習不要のインターフェースFastRoverVLAを提案する。
llm.problem: オフロードVLAモデルは頻繁な軌道更新に依存するため、高価なマルチモーダル推論を繰り返し呼び出す必要があるという課題がある。
llm.method: 視覚的プラン生成とモーション条件付き実行を分離し、速度・曲率アクションバッファを用いた学習不要のインターフェースにより、プランを再利用・補正する。
llm.result: ORAD-3DおよびRELLIS-3Dデータセットにおいて、Qwen3-VLのリクエスト処理コストを大幅に削減しつつ、優れた位置誤差の低減を実現した。

2611.26242.tldr_en: Off-road vision-language-action models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference, so FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution.

2611.26239.title: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models to Stop Safely
2611.26239.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and (2) joint policy adaptation, which learns these targets alongside the original actions of retained tasks. This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills. Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance. On the evaluated LIBERO tasks, SAFI reduces aggregate target success after takeover to 1.3\%, with no recorded physical incidents or action saturation, while preserving high retained-task success.
2611.26239.comment: A two-stage pipeline that teaches VLAs to stop prohibited tasks safely while preserving permitted skills

llm.title_ja: ビジョン・ランゲージ・アクションモデルに安全な停止を教える
llm.tldr_ja: 禁止されたタスクの実行中に安全な代替応答を学習させる2段階のフレームワークState-Aware Fallback Imitation（SAFI）を提案し、物理的インシデントを回避しつつ許可されたスキルを維持する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルにおいて、実行途中の禁止された行動を停止させ、その結果生じる物理的応答を適切に制御することは依然として困難である。
llm.method: 静止アームコマンドと一貫したグリッパターゲットを割り当てる「フォールバックターゲット構築」と、それを元の行動と一緒に学習する「結合ポリシー適応」の2段階からなるSAFIを提案する。
llm.result: LIBEROおよびBadLIBEROタスクを用いた実験で、引き継ぎ後の目標成功率を1.3%まで低下させ、物理的インシデントなしで高精度な維持タスクの成功率を保持した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.26239.tldr_en: This work introduces State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response and demonstrates that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution.

2611.26218.title: MixReact: Physics-Based Reactive Humanoid Control from Multimodal Cues via a Discrete-Continuous Mixture of Transformers
2611.26218.abstract: Humanoid agents in everyday environments are expected to react to diverse cues as humans do, with semantically appropriate and physically executable behaviors. Existing cue-driven reaction generation methods support only a narrow range of cue modalities and are limited to purely kinematic generation, leaving the resulting reactions susceptible to physical artifacts. To this end, we present MixReact, the first unified framework for physics-based reactive humanoid control from text, audio, and video cues, integrating a Discrete--Continuous Mixture of Transformers (DisCo-MoT) for state prediction with a History-aware Action Transformer (HAT) for physical execution. DisCo-MoT couples a discrete masked-modeling branch with a continuous autoregressive diffusion branch via one-way mixture attention within a MoT architecture. Guidance from discrete context mitigates collapse into averaged behaviors in one-to-many reaction generation, while direct prediction in continuous state space bypasses the decoding bottleneck of discrete representations. HAT then maps the predicted next state and observed execution history to executable actions, enabling robust closed-loop control in physics-based simulation. Experiments across all three modalities demonstrate consistent improvements over the baselines in fidelity, diversity, and physical consistency, while ablations validate the complementary contributions of the components. Our code will be released to facilitate future research. Project page: https://binlee26.github.io/MixReact_Page/

llm.title_ja: MixReact：離散・連続混合Transformerによるマルチモーダルキューからの物理ベースの反応型ヒューマノイド制御
llm.tldr_ja: テキスト、音声、映像のキューから物理的に実行可能なヒューマノイドの反応行動を生成する初の統合フレームワークMixReactを提案し、忠実度や物理的整合性の向上を実証する。
llm.problem: 既存のキュー駆動型反応生成手法は、限られたキューモダリティにしか対応せず純粋な運動学的生成にとどまるため、物理的アーティファクトが生じやすい。
llm.method: 状態予測のためのDisCo-MoTと物理実行のためのHATを統合し、離散マスクモデリングと連続自己回帰拡散を1方向の混合アテンションで結びつける。
llm.result: 3つのモダリティすべてにおいて、ベースラインと比較して忠実度、多様性、物理的整合性が一貫して向上した。

2611.26218.tldr_en: MixReact is presented, the first unified framework for physics-based reactive humanoid control from text, audio, and video cues, integrating a Discrete--Continuous Mixture of Transformers (DisCo-MoT) for state prediction with a History-aware Action Transformer (HAT) for physical execution.

2611.26196.title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL
2611.26196.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.
2611.26196.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures. Code-as-policy robot-use agent post-training

llm.title_ja: EmbodyAgent：蒸留、SFT、RLによるポストトレーニング済み身体性VLMエージェント
llm.tldr_ja: ブラックボックス教師からのデータ合成、SFT、およびオンラインRLを組み合わせたエンドツーエンドのポストトレーニングフレームワークEmbodyAgentを提案し、LIBEROタスクでの把持や制御の性能を劇的に向上させる。
llm.problem: オープンウェイトのVLMを高性能な身体性エージェントにするためには、対話型ツール契約への対応や方策分布のシフトに対応する完全なポストトレーニングスタックが必要である。
llm.method: 教師モデルからのデータ合成パイプライン、説明とプログラムターゲットを蒸留するSFT、およびグループ相対優位性に基づくオンラインRLを統合する。
llm.result: LIBERO Spatialタスクにおいて、SFT後のテスト成功率が14/100、RL後には84/100に向上し、モデル呼び出し中央値も大幅に減少した。

2611.26196.tldr_en: EmbodyAgent is presented, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines that identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.

2611.26167.title: Planning to Stop: Factored Certification and Terminal Repair for Noncircular Robots
2611.26167.abstract: Tight-space navigation requires a robot to clear obstacles and stop inside its goal despite uncertainty. We present GeoDiff, a motion-program planner coupling original-goal stopped-set inclusion, witness-guided terminal repair, and factored proof compilation. An exact feasible-translation characterization guides repair; request-local reuse reduces repeated geometric work. We establish conditions for compiler equivalence and reach-and-stop soundness. Across 11,440 floorplan-derived jobs, GeoDiff certifies 61/139 tasks at 5-cm tolerance within 15 s, versus 44/139 for the stop-set baseline. The strongest observed external certificate adapter certifies 13/139 tasks from 119/139 native routes, separating route availability from certification. On tasks derived from public BARN maps, GeoDiff certifies 202/270 at 5-cm tolerance for a Jackal-shaped body, versus 3/270 for the portal baseline. Development analyses distinguish emitter savings from solver coverage, and 1,420 route-tracking episodes characterize the execution interface. These results show how terminal reasoning and proof reuse increase finite-budget certification coverage while preserving the original physical task and goal.

llm.title_ja: 停止の計画：非円形ロボットのための因子化された証明認証と終端修復
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実性下で狭い空間の障害物を回避し目標内で停止するためのモーションプログラムプランナーGeoDiffを提案し、従来のベースラインを大きく上回る認証成功率を示す。
llm.problem: 狭小空間のナビゲーションでは、ロボットが不確実性の中で障害物をかわし、目標地点内で確実に停止する必要がある。
llm.method: 元の目標停止セット包含、証人誘導型終端修復、因子化された証明コンパイルを組み合わせたモーションプログラムプランナーGeoDiffを提案する。
llm.result: フロアプラン由来の11,440件のジョブにおいて、GeoDiffは5cmの許容誤差で従来のベースラインよりも多くのタスクを迅速に認証した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.26167.tldr_en: GeoDiff, a motion-program planner coupling original-goal stopped-set inclusion, witness-guided terminal repair, and factored proof compilation is presented, showing how terminal reasoning and proof reuse increase finite-budget certification coverage while preserving the original physical task and goal.

2611.26165.title: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
2611.26165.abstract: Exocentric-to-egocentric (Exo2Ego) video generation transforms third-person recordings into first-person viewpoints, unlocking immersive AR/VR experiences and scalable demonstration synthesis for embodied robotics. Extending it to a streaming setting is expected to further enable live applications. However, existing methods suffer from degraded manipulation regions, overfitting and confinement to fixed-length clips with prohibitive latency. To address these limitations, we present StreamEgo, a real-time framework for unbounded, generalizable Exo2Ego video generation. To resolve intricate manipulation dynamics while supporting the streaming pipeline, a streaming dual-branch prior provides pixel-aligned guidance for translating appearance and skeletal kinematics. We also introduce a region-aware loss curriculum to improve generalization and stabilize multi-objective diffusion training. Furthermore, we distill the model into a chunk-wise autoregressive model, augmented with a region-aware corruption mechanism and a first-chunk curriculum, enabling high-quality, generalizable real-time streaming Exo2Ego generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

llm.title_ja: StreamEgo：ストリーミング型三人称から一人称への動画生成
llm.tldr_ja: 三人称視点から一人称視点への高品質な動画生成をリアルタイムのストリーミング環境で実現するフレームワークStreamEgoを提案し、単一H100 GPUで24.3 FPSを達成する。
llm.problem: 既存の手法は、細かな操作領域の劣化や過学習、固定長クリップへの限定、および処理遅延が大きいという問題がある。
llm.method: 外観と骨格の運動学をピクセル単位で誘導するストリーミングデュアルブランチプライアと、領域認識型損失カリキュラム、およびチャンク単位の自己回帰モデルへの蒸留を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 単一H100 GPU上で24.3 FPSという高品質かつ一般化可能なリアルタイムストリーミングExo2Ego動画生成を実現した。

2611.26165.tldr_en: This work distill the model into a chunk-wise autoregressive model, augmented with a region-aware corruption mechanism and a first-chunk curriculum, enabling high-quality, generalizable real-time streaming Exo2Ego generation at 24.3 FPS on a single H100 GPU.

2611.26161.title: One View, One Action: Spatially Generalizable VLAs through Observation-Aligned Experts and Cross Graph Consistency
2611.26161.abstract: Multi-view vision-language-action (VLA) models still face challenges in spatial generalization, particularly under changes in camera viewpoints and robot initial states. These models typically receive action supervision only in the robot base frame, requiring them to implicitly learn the spatial correspondence between observations from each view and base-frame actions. We propose One View, One Action (OVOA-VLA), which learns to predict actions in each view's camera frame, allowing the same physical motion to provide diverse, observation-aligned supervision across views. OVOA-VLA jointly trains a base-frame expert and view-specific action experts, whose robot-state inputs and action targets are expressed in their respective camera frames. Two complementary directed attention graphs model both directions of interaction between the base and view-specific experts, jointly leveraging view-specific action supervision to improve base-frame prediction. Cross Graph Consistency further encourages agreement between the two graphs' base-frame predictions for the same sample. With the same multi-view inputs, the model supports both full and base-only inference. Experiments across multiple simulation benchmarks demonstrate improved manipulation performance and robustness to camera-viewpoint and robot-initialization perturbations. Full and base-only inference achieve average success rates of 88.1% and 85.7% on LIBERO-Plus, respectively. In real-world evaluations, base-only inference raises the average success rates from $π_{0.5}$'s 28.3% to 58.3% across three tasks under spatial distribution shifts.

llm.title_ja: ワンビュー・ワンアクション：観測アラインされた専門家とクロスグラフ一貫性による空間一般化VLA
llm.tldr_ja: カメラ視点やロボット初期状態の変化に対する空間一般化能力を高めるため、各ビューのカメラ座標系で行動を予測・統合するOVOA-VLAを提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機実験で優れた成功率を実証する。
llm.problem: マルチビューVLAモデルは、カメラ視点やロボット初期状態の変化に対する空間一般化において、ベースフレームと各視点の対応付け学習に課題を抱えている。
llm.method: ベースフレーム専門家と各ビューのカメラ座標系で動作する視点固有の行動専門家を結合し、双方向の相互作用をモデル化する有向アテンショングラフとクロスグラフ一貫性を導入する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plusにおいて高い平均成功率を達成し、実機評価でも空間分布シフトに対して成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.26161.tldr_en: One View, One Action (OVOA-VLA), which learns to predict actions in each view's camera frame, allowing the same physical motion to provide diverse, observation-aligned supervision across views.

2611.26146.title: A Practical Proprioceptive Data Collection Utility for the Unitree GO1
2611.26146.abstract: The Unitree Go1 is a widely used platform for legged robotics research, yet collecting proprioceptive data from it is unnecessarily difficult: the Unitree SDK is sparsely documented, and ROS1 (Robot Operating System), the Go1's native middleware, is fully deprecated. We present an open-source graphical utility that enables researchers to reliably record proprioceptive data from the Go1, including joint states, IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) readings, foot force sensor data, and gyroscope measurements, without requiring ROS expertise. The tool provides a simple GUI (Graphical User Interface) for starting, stopping, and labeling recordings in real time. The contribution of this paper is the collection utility. We characterize the acquisition quality of 51 recordings collected with it, including the achieved sampling rate and repeated samples. As a secondary, deliberately modest check that the data is useful, we train a terrain classifier on it. The results are weak: a Temporal Convolutional Network reaches about 38% accuracy on held-out recordings across ten terrain classes (10% would be chance), and a window-level split that ignores recording boundaries inflates the same measurement to about 99%. We report this as a demonstration that the logged signals carry terrain information, not as a competitive classifier. The utility is designed to lower the barrier to collecting Go1 proprioceptive data without ROS.

llm.title_ja: Unitree GO1のための実用的な固有受容データ収集ユーティリティ
llm.tldr_ja: ROS不要でUnitree Go1から信頼性の高い固有受容データを記録できるオープンソースのGUIユーティリティを提案し、51件の記録データを用いた取得品質の検証と地形分類のデモを行う。
llm.problem: Unitree Go1での固有受容データ収集は、SDKのドキュメント不足やROS1のサポート終了により不必要に困難である。
llm.method: 関節状態、IMU、足部力センサー、ジャイロスコープのデータをROSなしでリアルタイムに記録・ラベル付けできるオープンソースのグラフィカルユーティリティを開発する。
llm.result: 51件の記録データの取得品質を評価し、取得したデータが地形情報を含んでいることを簡易的な地形分類モデルの訓練により示した。
llm.limitation: 地形分類器の性能は本質的な主目的ではなくデモ用であり、完全な分類器としては弱い。

2611.26146.tldr_en: An open-source graphical utility that enables researchers to reliably record proprioceptive data from the Go1, including joint states, IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit) readings, foot force sensor data, and gyroscope measurements, without requiring ROS expertise.

2611.26127.title: Spatially Conditioned Trajectory Diffusion
2611.26127.abstract: Multi-Robot Motion Planning (MRMP) requires trajectories that avoid environmental obstacles and collisions between robots in a shared workspace. Diffusion-based planners often address obstacle avoidance through sampling-time guidance, while some conditioned approaches aggregate map geometry into a global representation. We present Spatially Conditioned Trajectory Diffusion (SCTD), a map-conditioned trajectory generator for multi-robot planning. SCTD retains multiple position-aware occupancy tokens accessed through cross-attention throughout a temporal U-Net, with hard endpoint inpainting enforcing start and goal states. One model trained on single-robot demonstrations across procedural environments generates obstacle-aware trajectories without sampling-time obstacle-cost guidance. High-level Conflict-Based Search (CBS) coordinates these trajectories through constrained replanning, retaining inter-agent guidance during sampling and reusing the model across workspace layouts and team sizes. Experiments assess single-robot success and trajectory quality, generalization to unfamiliar layouts with added obstacles, and coordinated multi-robot planning.
