On 15,000 held-out tasks, SCTD achieves higher success than the evaluated guided diffusion baseline, with the largest gains on hard-detour tasks, while trajectory-quality comparisons show smoother trajectories. Conditioning ablations show higher success with spatial tokens than with a global map embedding, and map-replacement tests demonstrate dependence on the supplied geometry. The resulting multi-robot system achieves higher team success than the compared diffusion baselines, with experiments covering teams of up to 15 robots.

llm.title_ja: 空間条件付き軌道拡散
llm.tldr_ja: 複数ロボットの協調計画（MRMP）において、位置認識型占有トークンを用いて障害物を回避するマップ条件付き軌道生成器SCTDを提案し、高い成功率と滑らかな軌道を実現する。
llm.problem: マルチロボットモーションプランニング（MRMP）では、環境の障害物やロボット間の衝突を回避する軌道生成が必要となるが、既存の拡散プランナーはグローバルマップの扱いに課題がある。
llm.method: 時間的U-Netのクロスアテンションを介してアクセスされる複数の位置認識型占有トークンを保持し、ハードエンドポイントインパインティングで開始・目標状態を強制するSCTDを提案する。
llm.result: 15,000件のホールドアウトタスクにおいて、誘導付き拡散ベースラインよりも高い成功率と滑らかな軌道を実現し、最大15台のロボットチームの協調に成功した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.26127.tldr_en: Spatially Conditioned Trajectory Diffusion (SCTD), a map-conditioned trajectory generator for multi-robot planning, achieves higher success than the evaluated guided diffusion baseline, with the largest gains on hard-detour tasks, while trajectory-quality comparisons show smoother trajectories.

2611.26105.title: PhysVAM: Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
2611.26105.abstract: Predicting future scene or object states does not necessarily reveal how robot-object interactions will advance or hinder a task. This challenge is particularly pronounced in dynamic robotic manipulation, where objects continue moving during perception and execution. Effective action generation therefore requires not only modeling object dynamics but also anticipating how future interactions will shape task progress. To this end, we propose \textbf{PhysVAM}, a Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model that represents anticipated interactions through their effects on future task progress. This value-based formulation provides task-directed foresight without reconstructing future visual states. Conditioned on current observations and historical object and robot motion, PhysVAM jointly learns action generation and multi-horizon future-value prediction. The value branch learns horizon-specific latent representations through future task-value prediction from successful and failed trajectories. These future-value representations are integrated into the action policy through gated cross-attention, guiding action generation toward interactions that facilitate task success. Extensive simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate superior task success, with absolute success-rate improvements of 27.0 and 27.5 percentage points over the strongest baselines in simulation and real-world tasks, respectively. Project page: https://metarobo.github.io/physvam.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: PhysVAM：動的オブジェクト操作のための物理指向の将来価値行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 動的な物体操作において、将来のタスク進捗に対する影響を通じて予測された相互作用を表現する物理指向の将来価値行動モデル（PhysVAM）を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機で優れた成功率を達成する。
llm.problem: 動的なロボット操作において、将来のシーン状態を予測するだけではロボットと物体の相互作用がタスクをどのように進展・妨害するかを捉えられない。
llm.method: 将来のタスク進捗への効果を通じて予測された相互作用を表現し、行動生成とマルチホライズン将来価値予測を統合した価値ベースの定式化を行う。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機実験において、最強のベースラインと比較して絶対成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.26105.tldr_en: A Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model that represents anticipated interactions through their effects on future task progress through their effects on future task progress, and provides task-directed foresight without reconstructing future visual states.

2611.26103.title: UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation
2611.26103.abstract: Flow-matching robot policies usually use one prediction target throughout action generation, even though recovering actions from noise and polishing nearly clean actions bring different challenges. We systematically compare velocity prediction (V), endpoint prediction (X), and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction (X--V) across multiple robot policies, benchmarks, and inference budgets. On StarVLA and LiLa-WAM, X--V works best for few-step generation, while V gains more from iterative refinement. We further uncover their complementary strengths across noise levels: clean actions have concentrated covariance spectra, endpoint predictions stay more stable under high noise, and velocity predictions offer more accurate corrections near clean actions. Inspired by these findings, we introduce UniVEP, which learns both prediction targets together with consistency supervision and switches from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise drops. Each step only needs one network run, and joint training also boosts single-step endpoint generation. Tests on simulated and real-world manipulation show better success rates and efficiency. On RoboTwin, UniVEP hits 61.36% success with one StarVLA run, beating the best single-target baseline at sixteen runs (59.96%). With LiLa-WAM, two runs outperform the best sixteen-step single-target baseline and cut inference latency by 77.1%.

llm.title_ja: UniVEP：ロボット操作のための速度予測とエンドポイント予測の統合
llm.tldr_ja: ノイズからのアクション復元とクリーンなアクションの洗練におけるそれぞれの強みを活かし、速度予測とエンドポイント予測を統合したUniVEPを提案し、高効率かつ高成功率な操作を実現する。
llm.problem: フローマッチングロボットポリシーでは、ノイズからのアクション復元とクリーンなアクションの洗練で異なる課題があるにもかかわらず、一貫した予測ターゲットを使用している。
llm.method: エンドポイント予測と速度予測の両方を一貫性監視付きで同時に学習させ、ノイズの減少に応じてエンドポイント復元から速度洗練へ切り替えるUniVEPを提案する。
llm.result: RoboTwinシミュレーションおよび実機操作において、単一ターゲットのベースラインの複数ステップ推論を上回る成功率と大幅な推論レイテンシ削減を達成した。

2611.26103.tldr_en: Inspired by these findings, UniVEP is introduced, which learns both prediction targets together with consistency supervision and switches from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise drops, and each step only needs one network run, and joint training also boosts single-step endpoint generation.
2611.26103.hf_summary_en: UniVEP combines endpoint and velocity prediction with consistency supervision and switches from endpoint recovery to velocity refinement as noise decreases, improving success and efficiency in few-step robot action generation.

2611.26090.title: Dynamic Human-Robot Role Allocation through Entropy-Based Monitoring and LLM Reasoning
2611.26090.abstract: Role allocation strategies in human-robot collaboration typically assign tasks to both the human and the robot, limiting the user's ability to take initiative. Furthermore, allocation decisions may conflict with the user's intentions, and the rationale behind such allocations may remain unclear, potentially reducing both acceptance and collaboration fluency. The novelty of the proposed framework is that the human is left free to contribute to the task, while the robot is dynamically allocated activities through a cost-driven Behavior Tree architecture according to user-expressed preferences and behavior. Explicit preferences are extracted from natural language instructions using a large language model, whereas human activity is monitored online through a Shannon entropy-based analysis of hand-object interactions. Furthermore, the framework can recognize anomalies in human execution and autonomously trigger corrective robot actions. The approach was validated through a pilot study and a multi-subject experiment involving 14 participants. Results demonstrate the potential of such an allocation strategy for enabling intuitive and engaging collaboration without increasing the perceived workload.

llm.title_ja: エントロピーベースのモニタリングとLLM推論を通じた動的な人間とロボットの役割分担
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の自発性を制限せず、エントロピーベースの手のインタラクション監視と大規模言語モデルによる意図抽出を組み合わせてロボットの活動を動的に割り当てるフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 人間とロボットの協調における役割分担戦略は、人間の自発性を制限し、意図との衝突や分担の根拠の不透明さを招くことがある。
llm.method: 人間が自由にタスクに貢献できるようにしつつ、LLMで抽出した明示的選好とシャノンエントロピーに基づく手と物体の相互作用のオンライン監視を通じてコスト駆動型ビヘイビアツリーでロボットの活動を動的に割り当てる。
llm.result: 14人の参加者を対象とした実験により、認知的負荷を増加させることなく、直感的で魅力的な協調を実現できる可能性が示された。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボット協調

2611.26090.tldr_en: The novelty of the proposed framework is that the human is left free to contribute to the task, while the robot is dynamically allocated activities through a cost-driven Behavior Tree architecture according to user-expressed preferences and behavior.

2611.26083.title: Reference-Twist-Based Velocity-Domain Spatiotemporal Calibration for mmWave Radar, Event Camera, and IMU
2611.26083.abstract: Multi-sensor navigation requires a common spatial and temporal basis, but geometric calibration relies on targets, features, point clouds, or pose associations that are difficult to establish across mmWave radars, event cameras, and inertial measurement units (IMUs). These sensors nevertheless share rigid-body motion. This paper formulates reference-conditioned velocity-domain spatiotemporal calibration for a rigid suite of two mmWave radars, one event camera, and two IMUs. Given a trusted reference body twist, radar Doppler, event normal flow, and inertial measurements are regressed against the same motion to estimate relative rotations, lever arms, time offsets, and sensor-specific bias and scale without artificial targets, structure from motion, or cross-modal point-cloud registration. The reference is treated as a conditioning input rather than a sensor to be calibrated. We compare joint and reference- conditioned estimation, derive conditional identifiability and CRLB-level covariance and bias bounds, and state the operating conditions under which conditioning is informative. Indoor and forest recordings with axis-separated motion evaluate initial- ization, temporal alignment, motion degeneracy, reference-input sensitivity, and residual consistency. Because the reference does not add physical observability, the estimates remain conditional on reference accuracy, synchronization, motion excitation, and projection diversity.

llm.title_ja: リファレンス・ツイストに基づくミリ波レーダ、イベントカメラ、IMUのための速度ドメイン時空間キャリブレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 外部ターゲットや構造物なしで、信頼できるリファレンス・ボディ・ツイストを利用して複数の異種センサー間の相対回転や時間オフセットを推定する速度ドメイン時空間キャリブレーション手法を提案する。
llm.problem: ミリ波レーダ、イベントカメラ、IMUの間では、幾何学的キャリブレーションに必要なターゲットや点群の対応付けを確立することが困難である。
llm.method: 信頼できるリファレンス・ボディ・ツイストを与え、レーダのドップラー、イベント法線フロー、慣性計測を同じモーションに対して回帰させて相対回転や時間オフセット、バイアスを推定する。
llm.result: 屋内と森林の記録を用いた評価により、初期化、時間合わせ、運動退化、リファレンス入力の感度などを検証した。
llm.limitation: リファレンスは物理的観測可能性を追加しないため、推定値はリファレンスの精度、同期、運動励起などに条件付けられる。
keywords_ja: センサーキャリブレーション

2611.26074.title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
2611.26074.abstract: Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends. Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid. These schemes differ in how recurrent weights are trained. Ordered from most to least biologically faithful, they are: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture, where recurrent weights are kept frozen and only a linear readout is trained, the same network but with its synapses trained by reward-modulated spike timing dependent plasticity and eligibility propagation, and finally backpropagation through time as a non biological baseline for comparison. All schemes relied on distillation of a reinforcement learning expert policy with dataset aggregation. We show that e-prop reached 100% survival rate matching backpropagation through time, whereas both the fixed reservoir and the reward-modulated STDP, though the closest to biological cultures, plateaued at a much lower performance (~43.7% and ~11% survival). We explore in further detail which trends a real culture could and could not produce until now. Finally we demonstrate brief bipedal stepping on a full size humanoid H1-2.
2611.26074.journal_ref: IEEE-RAS 25th International Conference on Humanoid Robots, Dec 2026, San Francisco (CA, USA), United States

llm.title_ja: シミュレートされた生物学的可塑性ネットワークを用いた人型ロボットH1-2の制御
llm.tldr_ja: 生物学的にインスパイアされたスパイキングニューラルネットワークを異なる学習スキームで訓練し、H1-2人型ロボットを用いた二足歩行の制御を実証する。
llm.problem: 人工スパイキングニューラルネットワークを人型ロボットの歩行に向けて訓練しつつ、生物学的妥当性と堅牢なパフォーマンスを同時に維持できるかは未知数である。
llm.method: 固定リザーバー、報酬変調型STDP、バックプロパゲーション・スルー・タイムなど異なる学習スキームを持つ生物学的にインスパイアされたスパイキングネットワークを構成する。
llm.result: e-propがBPTTに匹敵する100%の生存率に到達した一方、固定リザーバーやSTDPは性能が頭打ちになることを示し、フルサイズH1-2での短い二足歩行を実証した。
keywords_ja: スパイキングニューラルネットワーク

2611.26074.tldr_en: It is shown that e-prop reached 100% survival rate matching backpropagation through time, whereas both the fixed reservoir and the reward-modulated STDP, though the closest to biological cultures, plateaued at a much lower performance.

2611.26054.title: Reference-Free Humanoid Skateboarding via Termination-Shaped Reinforcement Learning
2611.26054.abstract: Humanoid locomotion research has advanced rapidly on walking and running, but \emph {object-mediated} locomotion, in which a robot must coordinate its body with a passive external object, remains difficult. One challenging task is skateboarding, which requires simultaneous interaction with the ground and a passive but movable platform to achieve forward motion. Current methods for tackling skateboarding with humanoid robots either require human demonstrations or utilise analytic steering models that require system identification. In this paper, we introduce a deep reinforcement learning framework that does not rely on prior data such as demonstrations and enables robots such as the K1 humanoid to learn to skateboard using model-free learning. The method combines task rewards with exploit-blocking terminations. We introduce a number of constraints restricting behaviours such as losing the planted board foot, standing with both feet on the board, excessive twisting, separation from the board, and unstable board motion. Their changing prevalence during training produces an implicit progression from stance control towards sustained robot--board locomotion.
2611.26054.comment: 8 pages, 15 figures, Accepted at the 2026 IEEE-RAS 25th International Conference on Humanoid Robots (Humanoids 2026)

llm.title_ja: リファレンスフリーなヒューマノイドスケートボード：終端シェイピング強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 事前のデモンストレーションデータや解析的ステアリングモデルに依存せず、タスク報酬と悪用ブロック型の終了条件を組み合わせた深層強化学習により、ヒューマノイドロボットがスケートボードを学習するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットが受動的な外部オブジェクトと体を協調させるオブジェクト媒介型 locomotion、特にスケートボードは、従来の人間のデモンストレーションや解析的ステアリングモデルを必要とするため困難である。
llm.method: タスク報酬と、ボードからの足の離脱や過度のひねりなどを制限する悪用ブロック型の終了条件を組み合わせたモデルフリーの深層強化学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: K1ヒューマノイドロボットが事前のデモンストレーションなしで自立的にスケートボードを学習・持続できるようになることを示した。

2611.26054.tldr_en: A deep reinforcement learning framework is introduced that does not rely on prior data such as demonstrations and enables robots such as the K1 humanoid to learn to skateboard using model-free learning and combines task rewards with exploit-blocking terminations.

2611.26048.title: AGE-Capture: Autonomous, General, and Efficient UAV Capture for High-Fidelity Scene Reconstruction
2611.26048.abstract: High-fidelity scene reconstruction with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) requires more than identifying valuable viewpoints: the system must autonomously acquire informative observations and determine task completion under different sensing configurations and limited flight resources. We present AGE-Capture, an autonomous, sensor-adaptive, and efficient active-capture framework for real UAVs. Building on renderability, the framework uses a lightweight online state to evaluate the utility of candidate views, assess task progress, and guide flight execution. By decoupling geometric exploration from reconstruction observations and establishing a unified camera-ray interface, the framework allows different range sensors and RGB camera models to share a reconstruction-driven acquisition pipeline. Reconstruction-frontier viewpoints characterize residual acquisition value for region screening and autonomous termination; dynamics-aware hierarchical planning combined with asynchronous event-driven capture reduces unnecessary inter-region motion, time spent waiting for plans, and repeated observations. Across ten indoor and outdoor simulation scenes, AGE-Capture achieves a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) $3.30$--$3.53\,\mathrm{dB}$ higher than that of the online baselines while using $58.2\%$ of the common mission-time budget on average. Its mean peak GPU memory usage is $91.0\%$--$93.3\%$ lower than that of the same baselines. Experiments with different sensor configurations validate the adaptability of the shared acquisition pipeline, while flights in nine real-world scenes further demonstrate onboard closed-loop operation under practical computational and motion constraints.

llm.title_ja: AGE-Capture：高忠実度シーン再構築のための自立的、汎用的かつ効率的なUAVキャプチャ
llm.tldr_ja: 再構築のレンダラビリティを基に軽量なオンライン状態で視点の有用性を評価し、自律的なキャプチャと飛行実行を行うアクティブキャプチャフレームワークAGE-Captureを提案する。
llm.problem: 高忠実度シーン再構築のためのUAV運用では、有益な視点の特定だけでなく、限られた飛行リソース下での自律的な観測とタスク完了判定が必要である。
llm.method: レンダラビリティに基づく軽量なオンライン状態で候補視点の有用性を評価し、再構築フロンティアビューポイントと階層的計画を組み合わせて無駄な動きを削減する。
llm.result: 10のシミュレーションシーンで高いPSNRとミッション時間予算の削減を達成し、現実世界の9つのシーンでのオンボード閉ループ運用を実証した。

2611.26048.tldr_en: This work presents AGE-Capture, an autonomous, sensor-adaptive, and efficient active-capture framework for real UAVs, which uses a lightweight online state to evaluate the utility of candidate views, assess task progress, and guide flight execution.

2611.26046.title: Agentic Scaling of Embodied Tasks in Simulation for Synthetic Data Collection and Policy Evaluation
2611.26046.abstract: Scaling embodied interaction data requires a broad collection of usable tasks, yet specifying and validating each task instance remains costly. We present AgenticTask, an agent-based framework that expands existing task collections under human intent. Its central representation links interaction requirements to object and part bindings, scene and robot configurations, initial conditions, and completion criteria. A task-generation agent reuses interaction structure to construct supported variations and revises incompatible configurations using validation feedback. A task-execution agent uses the same bindings and geometric records to select robot-supported skills and check completion against the original task criteria. On RoboCasa, the framework builds the AgenticTask collection, saving 16,450 task instances from 20,323 construction attempts at a throughput of 166.97 saved instances per elapsed hour, with 62.26% of construction attempts passing the configured physical checks. The execution agent completes approximately 38% of evaluated tasks, with successful cases spanning object placement, articulated manipulation, and sequential arrangement. Diagnostic analysis identifies improvement priorities in construction reliability, action selection, task-robot compatibility, and runtime integration. Together, these results demonstrate task-collection expansion with measured construction productivity and concrete execution evidence, providing a foundation for subsequent interaction-data collection for embodied AI.

llm.title_ja: 合成データ収集とポリシー評価のためのシミュレーション内における身体性タスクのエージェント的スケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: AgenticTaskは、人間的意図のもとで既存のタスクコレクションを拡張し、検証フィードバックを用いてタスクバリエーションと設定を構築するエージェントベースのフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 身体性インタラクションデータのスケーリングには多様なタスクが必要だが、各インスタンスの指定と検証コストが高い。
llm.method: インタラクション要件と設定を結び付け、タスク生成・実行エージェントが連携してタスク構築と検証を行うフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: RoboCasa上で16,450個のタスクインスタンスを構築し、実行エージェントが評価タスクの約38%を完了した。
llm.limitation: 構築の信頼性、行動選択、タスクとロボットの適合性、ランタイム統合における改善優先度が診断分析により特定された。

2611.26046.tldr_en: Together, these results demonstrate task-collection expansion with measured construction productivity and concrete execution evidence, providing a foundation for subsequent interaction-data collection for embodied AI.

2611.26035.title: Fixing the Twin, Not the Detector: Sim-to-Real Roadside LiDAR Detection from Digital-Twin Data
2611.26035.abstract: Roadside LiDAR detectors are expensive to train on real labels, and digital twins promise to replace these labels, but a detector trained on a twin meets a different sensor, different objects and different annotation conventions on the real site. We describe the pipeline that placed first in the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge (IEEE BigData 2026 Cup, 0.5541 combined score) and fifth on its V2X-Real track (0.8102). Every detector is a CenterPoint model trained only on synthetic data, on a single 8 GB laptop GPU. Most of the gain came from correcting differences between the twin and the real site rather than from the detector. We align the twin's coordinates, point density and box convention with the test sensor, generate the pedestrians and riders that the twins lack, plus street clutter as unlabeled negatives, and rebuild twin objects at real size and real point density. A non-learned resampling to the per-cell point density of unlabeled real frames lifts LUMPI realism from 0.589 to 0.947, against 0.949 between real frames. Label-free post-processing then exploits what a fixed roadside sensor guarantees: static structures recur in every frame, and real objects have characteristic point statistics. Reporting the validation and test gain of each component side by side, we find that corrections of systematic sim-to-real differences transfer to the test set, typically keeping a quarter to three quarters of their validation gain, while choices that fit the few objects of a validation set do not.
2611.26035.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables. Accepted to the IEEE BigData 2026 Cup (UCF UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge); first place, LUMPI track. Code: https://github.com/dipper13579/urbantwin-sim2real-lidar

llm.title_ja: デジタルツインデータからのSim-to-Real路側LiDAR検出における、検出器ではなくツインの修正
llm.tldr_ja: 都市ツインと現実のサイト間の体系的な差異を修正することで、合成データのみで訓練されたLiDAR検出器のSim-to-Real転移性能を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 路側LiDAR検出器の現実のラベルによる訓練は高価であり、デジタルツインで代用すると現実のセンサーやオブジェクトとの間に差異が生じる。
llm.method: ツインの座標、点密度、ボックス規則をテストセンサーに合わせ、歩行者等の欠損要素の追加や非学習型リサンプリングによる現実的な調整を行う。
llm.result: LUMPIの現実らしさが0.589から0.947に向上し、UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR ChallengeのLUMPIトラックで1位を獲得した。

2611.26035.tldr_en: This work describes the pipeline that placed first in the LUMPI track of the UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, and reports that corrections of systematic sim-to-real differences transfer to the test set, typically keeping a quarter to three quarters of their validation gain, while choices that fit the few objects of a validation set do not.

2611.26031.title: Close&Safe: Maximal Task Preservation for Redundant Manipulators via C-Space Boundary Detour
2611.26031.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation such as wiping, polishing and surface inspection specifies the task as a continuous end-effector trajectory rather than a goal pose. When an obstacle absent from the planning model intersects it, conventional planners return a collision-free path that may differ from the nominal throughout, discarding trajectory that was never obstructed. We present Close&Safe (Close to the intended task, Safe from obstacles), which decouples tracking from avoidance: the nominal is followed exactly wherever it remains feasible, and avoidance acts only on the interval where it is not, so tracking is hindered as little as the obstacle allows. On that interval we sample the configuration-space obstacle boundary within a corridor around the nominal, connect the samples into a roadmap, and search it for the detour that deviates least before rejoining the nominal at the earliest feasible configuration. We evaluate across diverse simulated obstacle configurations, physical Franka experiments, and ablations of key algorithmic components. The results demonstrate collision-free trajectory repair with localized task modification, while recovering 52.4-78% in simulation and on hardware.

llm.title_ja: C空間境界デトュールを通じた冗長マニピュレータのための最大タスク温存型Close&Safe
llm.tldr_ja: Close&Safeは追従と回避を分離し、障害物が存在しない区間では意図された軌道を正確に追従しつつ、必要な区間でのみ最小限の迂回を行う。
llm.problem: 接触を伴うマニピュレーションでは軌道が指定されるが、未モデル化の障害物がある場合、従来プランナーは障害のない部分も含めて軌道を破棄してしまう。
llm.method: 公称軌道の周囲の構成空間障害物境界をサンプリングしてロードマップを構築し、最小限の逸脱で迂回して公称軌道に復帰するパスを探索する。
llm.result: 多様なシミュレーション環境および実機のFranka実験において、局所的なタスク修正による衝突フリーな軌道修復と52.4〜78%の復帰を実現した。
keywords_ja: 接触マニピュレーション

2611.26031.tldr_en: Close&Safe (Close to the intended task, Safe from obstacles), which decouples tracking from avoidance: the nominal is followed exactly wherever it remains feasible, and avoidance acts only on the interval where it is not, so tracking is hindered as little as the obstacle allows.

2611.25980.title: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
2611.25980.abstract: World models aim to predict environment dynamics under actions, enabling the prediction of action consequences without executing them in the real world. Yet despite producing increasingly realistic videos, current world models often fail to capture how small action changes affect future observations. This limits their use in tasks such as robotic policy evaluation and model-based planning, where nearly identical actions can lead to qualitatively different outcomes. To address this, we propose AFFECT, an auxiliary training objective for learning the distribution of visual changes induced by action perturbations. Specifically, we inject temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation. We then train the world model so that its generated videos respond to this noise as the recorded videos do, without requiring repeated executions from the same initial state. Across OGBench simulation and real-world DROID and ALOHA-2 setups, AFFECT makes world-model rollouts more faithful to real outcomes. On DROID, the Pearson correlation between policy success rates in the world model and on the real robot rises from 0.47 to 0.79, alongside up to 23% lower FVD. These gains carry over to planning, where selecting actions with AFFECT-trained world models improves task success by up to 8.3%.
2611.25980.hf_summary_en: AFFECT, an auxiliary objective that trains world models to match visual responses to temporally correlated action noise, improves rollout fidelity and planning success in simulated and real robotic tasks.

llm.title_ja: 行動が変化させるものの学習：動態に忠実な世界モデルのための行動効果マッチング
llm.tldr_ja: AFFECTは、時間的相関のある行動ノイズに対する視覚的変化の分布を学習する補助目的関数により、世界モデルのロールアウトの忠実度と計画の成功率を向上させる。
llm.problem: 現在の世界モデルは現実的なビデオを生成できるが、小さな行動の変化が将来の観測にどう影響するかを捉えきれず、ロボットのポリシー評価や計画への活用が制限される。
llm.method: タスク非依存のテレオペデータで訓練されたポリシーの行動に時間的相関ノイズを注入し、生成ビデオが記録ビデオと同様に応答するように世界モデルを訓練する。
llm.result: DROIDにおいて世界モデルの成功率と実機の相関が0.47から0.79に向上し、FVDが最大23%低下、計画成功率が最大8.3%向上した。

2611.25980.tldr_en: This work injects temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation, and trains the world model so that its generated videos respond to this noise as the recorded videos do, without requiring repeated executions from the same initial state.

2611.25958.title: Learning optimal gaits and styles for terrain-adaptive quadruped locomotion
2611.25958.abstract: Animals use many different gaits to locomote at different speeds across varying terrains. A longstanding question in biology and robotics is: which gait is best? This question is most often addressed from an energy-efficiency perspective on flat terrain, leaving open how the answer depends on terrain and on the criterion optimized. Here we show that gait optimality is determined jointly by terrain, performance metric, and velocity. We use deep reinforcement learning and networks of abstract oscillators, modeling spinal central pattern generators, to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits across diverse challenging terrains, together with the locomotion style (base height, foot ground clearance, foot offsets) that each requires. A second policy then selects among them to optimize a user-specified criterion such as cost of transport, base stability, or joint smoothness. Across these performance metrics and within this repertoire, every gait is optimal under at least one terrain-metric-velocity combination. The framework adapts zero-shot to gait couplings and styles never seen during training, to terrains far beyond the training distribution, and to larger quadrupeds five times the training mass. With a single additional pitch-tracking reward term, the same gait couplings also support bipedal-mode locomotion. Our method provides a general and systematic way to produce expressive locomotion and to select the gait best suited to a given terrain and criterion. Project page: https://guillaume10.github.io/terrain-gaits.

llm.title_ja: 地形適応型四足歩行のための最適歩容とスタイルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 地形、パフォーマンス指標、速度の組み合わせによって歩容の最適性が決まることを示し、深層強化学習と脊髄中央パターン生成器のモデルを用いて多様な最適歩容を獲得した。
llm.problem: 生物学やロボット工学において、平地でのエネルギー効率の観点から議論されることが多く、地形や最適化基準にどう依存するかは未解明であった。
llm.method: 深層強化学習と抽象オシレーターネットワークを用いて11種類の四足歩容とスタイルを学習し、性能指標に基づいて選択する第2のポリシーを導入した。
llm.result: 未知の地形や、訓練時の5倍の質量を持つ大型四足ロボットへゼロショット適応し、ピッチ追従報酬により二足歩行モードもサポートした。

2611.25958.tldr_en: This work uses deep reinforcement learning and networks of abstract oscillators, modeling spinal central pattern generators, to learn 11 quadrupedal gaits across diverse challenging terrains, and shows that gait optimality is determined jointly by terrain, performance metric, and velocity.

2611.25946.title: Point Dynamics as Proxy for Robotic World Models
2611.25946.abstract: Robotic world models predict future video frames from the current observation and a sequence of robot actions. While recent models follow the given actions closely, manipulated objects often collapse or move inconsistently with the action. We attribute this to the conditioning: an action, or a rendering of the robot, specifies where the robot goes but not how the scene responds, leaving a single video model to infer the interaction dynamics implicitly while also rendering appearance. We therefore separate dynamics prediction from visual rendering, with 3D point dynamics as the proxy between them. Specifically, we lift the first frame into 3D points, simulate how they respond to the robot's motion with a learned point dynamics model, and render the simulated points back into pixel-aligned videos that any video model can read. In controlled experiments on the DROID dataset with two video renderers of different architectures, this point dynamics proxy reduces object motion error by 8.6% and 6.2% without degrading image quality, and by 8.1% on a real bimanual robot. Moreover, the video follows the simulation: more accurate dynamics yield more accurate object motion, and editing the points steers the video. This suggests that advances in dynamics modeling can translate into more faithful robotic world models.

llm.title_ja: ロボット世界モデルのプロキシとしての点群ダイナミクス
llm.tldr_ja: 動態予測と視覚的レンダリングを分離し、3D点群ダイナミクスをプロキシとして用いることで、操作対象のオブジェクトが不自然に崩れたり動いたりする問題を軽減した。
llm.problem: 最近のロボット世界モデルは行動によく従うが、操作対象のオブジェクトが崩れたり行動と一致しない動きをする問題がある。
llm.method: 最初のフレームを3D点群に持ち上げ、学習済み点群ダイナミクスモデルでロボットの動きに対する応答をシミュレートし、それをピクセル整列ビデオにレンダリングする。
llm.result: DROIDデータセットおよび実機双腕ロボットにおいて、画質を落とすことなくオブジェクトの動作誤差を6.2%〜8.6%削減した。

2611.25946.tldr_en: This work lifts the first frame into 3D points, simulates how they respond to the robot's motion with a learned point dynamics model, and renders the simulated points back into pixel-aligned videos that any video model can read.

2611.25935.title: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
2611.25935.abstract: Facial deepfake detectors are usually trained on blending fakes, where a generated face is pasted back into a real frame. Recent generators synthesize the entire face and leave no traces of blending. On a benchmark of 19 datasets released from 2019 to 2026, the best prior facial deepfake detector reaches a mean AUROC of 96.2% on ten blending datasets, but none exceeds 78.1% on five datasets of entire face synthesis (EFS). AI-generated content (AIGC) detectors do not close this gap. We propose TwinD, a detector trained on FaceForensics++ fakes and two kinds of twins: fakes made from a real frame. A reconstruction twin is a real frame reconstructed by an autoencoder, with the real pixels put back in a random region. It targets the neural traces of a decoder. A blob twin blends an altered copy of a real frame with the frame itself, targeting blending artifacts. It needs no generator and no face-shaped mask. Together, these twins provide two complementary forensic cues that generalize to unseen manipulations. TwinDreaches a mean AUROC of 96.3%, 8.9 points above the prior state-of-the-art, with 98.1% on the blending datasets and 95.6% on the EFS datasets. Trained on twins alone, without a deepfake dataset, single models still reach 94.3% on average over three seeds. For reproducibility, the code, trained model, and training data are at: https://github.com/yermandy/TwinD

llm.title_ja: TwinD：ブレンドから顔全体合成へのディープフェイク検出の汎化
llm.tldr_ja: 現実のフレームから作られた2種類のツイン（再構成ツインとブロブツイン）を用いて検出器を訓練し、未見の操作手法に対するディープフェイク検出の汎化性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: 従来の顔ディープフェイク検出器はブレンド手法で訓練されており、顔全体を完全に合成する最新の生成手法に対して検出性能が大幅に低下する。
llm.method: デコーダーの神経痕跡をターゲットにした再構成ツインと、顔型マスクを不要とするブロブツインという2種類のツインを用いて検出器を訓練する。
llm.result: 平均AUROC 96.3%を達成し、従来最高手法を8.9ポイント上回り、顔全体合成データセットに対しても95.6%を記録した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2611.25935.tldr_en: TwinD is proposed, a detector trained on FaceForensics++ fakes and two kinds of twins: fakes made from a real frame and a reconstruction twin, which provide two complementary forensic cues that generalize to unseen manipulations.
2611.25935.hf_summary_en: TwinD, trained on reconstruction and blob twins derived from real frames, detects both blending and entire-face-synthesis deepfakes, improving AUROC over prior detectors.

2611.25927.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models
2611.25927.abstract: Latent world models predict the outcomes of action sequences, but comparing candidate plans through recursive rollout remains expensive at test time. We introduce Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search. Fast-JEPA reorganizes predictive computation to support effective action-sequence search at low planning cost. It constructs a goal-directed plan to guide search and directly predicts the outcomes of complete candidates for efficient comparison, avoiding recursive state rollout during refinement. Across PushT, Reacher, Cube, and TwoRoom, Fast-JEPA achieves 96.50% average success rate with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT. Search-budget sweeps show that its competitive success and low latency extend across candidate counts and refinement depths. We further introduce DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays. Fast-JEPA achieves average success rates of 73.83% on DynaGoal-Shift and 87.67% on DynaGoal-Deadline, demonstrating the practical value of low-latency predictive planning under changing control conditions and execution-time constraints. Our code is available at https://github.com/Sofilyzia/Fast-JEPA.

llm.title_ja: Fast-JEPA：潜在世界モデルにおける成功・レイテンシのフロンティアの向上
llm.tldr_ja: Fast-JEPAは、予測計算の再構成により、再帰的な状態ロールアウトを行わずに効率的な行動シーケンス探索を実現する潜在世界モデルの計画フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 潜在世界モデルは行動配列の結果を予測できるが、テスト時に再帰的ロールアウトによる候補プランの比較に高い計算コストがかかる。
llm.method: 目標指向の計画を構築して探索を誘導し、完全な候補の結果を直接予測して効率的に比較し、リファインメント時の再帰的状態ロールアウトを回避する。
llm.result: PushTやCubeなどの環境で平均96.50%の成功率を達成し、INTACTと比較して2.41倍高速な計画を実現した。

2611.25927.tldr_en: This work introduces Fast-JEPA, a latent world model planning framework that advances the success-latency Pareto frontier of predictive search and introduces DynaGoal, a benchmark for evaluating world-model planning under dynamic out-of-distribution conditions, execution deadlines, and controlled response delays.
2611.25927.hf_summary_en: Fast-JEPA is a latent world model planning framework that improves the success-latency trade-off of predictive search by predicting complete action-sequence outcomes and using goal-directed plans, with evaluation on manipulation and navigation tasks and a new dynamic planning benchmark.

2611.25904.title: Multiple-Camera Tracking of Rigid Objects
2611.25904.abstract: In this paper we describe a method for tracking rigid objects using one or several cameras. The tracking process consists of aligning a 3-D model representation of an object with image contours by measuring and minimizing the image error between predicted model points and image contours. The tracker behaves like a visual servo loop where the internal and external camera parameters are updated at each new image acquisition. We study in detail the Jacobian matrix associated with this minimization process in the presence of both point-to-point and point-to-contour matches. We establish the minimal number of matches that are needed as well as the singular configurations leading to a rank-defficient Jacobian matrix. We find a mathematical link between the point-to-point and point-to-contour cases. Based on this link we show that the latter has the same kind of singularities than the former. Moreover, we study multiple camera configurations which optimize the robustness of the method in the presence of single-camera singularities, bad, noisy, or missing data. Extensive experiments done with a complex ship part and with up to three cameras validate the method. In particular we show that the tracker may well be used as a camera calibration procedure.
2611.25904.journal_ref: International Journal of Robotics Research, 21(2), 97--113, February 2002

llm.title_ja: 複数カメラによる剛体追跡
llm.tldr_ja: 予測されたモデル点と画像輪郭間の画像誤差を測定・最小化することで、1台または複数のカメラを用いた剛体の追跡を行う手法を提案している。
llm.problem: 単一カメラでのオクルージョンやノイズ、特異点のある環境において、剛体をロバストに追跡することが困難である。
llm.method: 点対点および点対輪郭のマッチングが存在する場合のヤコビ行列を詳細に分析し、複数カメラの構成でロバスト性を最適化する。
llm.result: 複雑な船舶部品や最大3台のカメラを用いた広範な実験により、手法の有効性とカメラ校正手順としての利用可能性を実証した。

2611.25904.tldr_en: This paper defines multiple-camera configurations which optimize the robustness of the method in the presence of single-camera singularities, bad, noisy, or missing data, and finds a mathematical link between the point- to-point and point-to-contour cases.

2611.25866.title: From Sequence to Space: Explicit Spatial Belief with Vision-Language Distillation for Active Geo-Localization
2611.25866.abstract: Active geo-localization (AGL) asks an agent to navigate a small aerial search grid and reach a target specified by an aerial image, a ground-level photograph, or text. Existing methods align the goal modalities well, but they keep the navigation state inside a large sequential Transformer and train with a dense distance reward that uses the hidden goal location. This paper proposes EAGLE, an Explicit spatial-belief Agent for Geo-Localization and Exploration. Offline training jointly optimizes a teacher-conditioned Swin branch and a context-free Swin student from the same randomly masked partial mosaics. The teacher branch attends to frozen full-scene context extracted by Qwen2.5-VL-7B, both branches receive masked-cell aerial-feature reconstruction and uncertainty supervision, while the student additionally distills stop-gradient feature predictions from the teacher. After distillation, Qwen, its cached context, and the teacher-attention branch are discarded. The retained student predicts cell-level aerial-feature embeddings and predictive uncertainty from partial observations alone. These predictions are combined with the modality-aligned goal embedding and a trajectory-derived visitation mask to construct the spatial belief tensor. The student is then frozen while a compact CNN actor-critic is optimized with PPO. EAGLE achieves state-of-the-art average success rates of 78.1%, 76.4%, and 76.8% on MASA, xBD zero-shot transfer, and the MM-GAG zero-shot aerial-goal split, respectively, without using a VLM or cached visual tokens at inference. Code will be made publicly available.

llm.title_ja: シーケンスから空間へ：能動的ジオローカライゼーションのためのビジョン言語蒸留を用いた明示的空間信念
llm.tldr_ja: EAGLEは、オフラインでのビジョン言語モデルからの特徴蒸留と明示的な空間信念テンソルを用いて、推論時にVLMを使用せずに能動的ジオローカライゼーションを実現する。
llm.problem: 既存の能動的ジオローカライゼーション手法はナビゲーション状態を大規模なシーケンシャルTransformer内に保持し、隠れ目標位置を用いた密な距離報酬で訓練している。
llm.method: Qwen2.5-VL-7Bから抽出したフルシーンコンテキストを教師として学生ブランチに特徴を蒸留し、予測不確実性とモダリティ整合目標埋め込みから空間信念を構築する。
llm.result: MASAやxBDゼロショット転移などのベンチマークでSOTAの平均成功率（78.1%、76.4%、76.8%）を達成した。
keywords_ja: ジオローカライゼーション

2611.25866.tldr_en: This paper proposes EAGLE, an Explicit spatial-belief Agent for Geo-Localization and Exploration that achieves state-of-the-art average success rates of 78.1%, 76.4%, and 76.8% on MASA, xBD zero-shot transfer, and the MM-GAG zero-shot aerial-goal split, respectively, without using a VLM or cached visual tokens at inference.

2611.25854.title: Learning-Based System Identification for DVL-Constrained AUV Localization
2611.25854.abstract: Nowadays, most AUVs utilize Doppler velocity logs (DVLs) and inertial measurement units (IMUs) to achieve satisfactory dead-reckoning results. However, the DVL bottom lock may not be available in some scenarios, such as moving over a soft bottom or traveling further away from the seafloor beyond the DVL's range. As a result, the localization system solely reliant on the IMU data will experience significant drift. The relatively high cost of DVLs also inhibits multirobot or swarm operations. In this article, we present the results of using fully connected feedforward neural networks to predict vehicle velocity (surge, sway, and heave) for AUV localization. Approximation functions for the vehicle velocities are derived based on the generalized six degree-of-freedom dynamic equation and kinematics, proving that they are suitable for feedforward neural networks with measurable inputs. The neural networks are trained using field data collected using an AUV. An ablation study was conducted to investigate the impacts of hyperparameters, and the most effective models were selected using the Akaike information criterion. The selected neural network models are tested on three new sets of mission data collected on two different days. The quantitative results show that localization using vehicle velocities predicted by neural networks yields lower averaged root-mean-square distance errors and standard deviation compared to the DVL-aided dead-reckoning method. However, the extent of this improvement was found to depend on ocean current conditions. The promising results show that lightweight fully connected feedforward neural networks offer an attractive approach for inertial-based underwater localization when DVLs or their measurements are not available.

llm.title_ja: DVL制約下でのAUV位置推定に向けた学習ベースのシステム同定
llm.tldr_ja: 完全結合型フィードフォワードニューラルネットワークを用いてAUVの速度を予測し、DVLが利用できない状況下での慣性ベースの水中位置推定を実現する。
llm.problem: 軟弱な海底の移動時やDVLの範囲外ではドップラー対数速度計（DVL）が利用できず、IMUのみに依存した位置推定システムは大きなドリフトを発生させる。
llm.method: 6自由度の動力学方程式と運動学に基づき、ニューラルネットワークへの入力に適した速度の近似関数を導出し、実海域データで訓練する。
llm.result: 提案手法による位置推定は、DVL支援デッドレコニング法と比較して、平均二乗根距離誤差と標準偏差を低減できることを示した。
llm.limitation: 位置推定の精度の改善度は海流の条件に依存することが判明した。
keywords_ja: ニューラルネットワーク

2611.25854.tldr_en: The quantitative results show that localization using vehicle velocities predicted by neural networks yields lower averaged root-mean-square distance errors and standard deviation compared to the DVL-aided dead-reckoning method, however, the extent of this improvement was found to depend on ocean current conditions.

2611.25801.title: Fast and Accurate Body Estimation in Pixels, World Space and Scenes
2611.25801.abstract: We present FAB (Fast and Accurate Body estimation), a human body estimator that jointly improves inference efficiency and body-recovery fidelity. Rather than predicting only parametric mesh-model parameters, FAB directly predicts human skeleton joints and dense surface points. In images, it predicts dense 2D and 3D body points alongside a parametric Momentum Human Rig (MHR) head, then fits SMPL in one learned pass followed by two Gauss-Newton steps. Its ViT-L student, FAB-L, distilled from a fine-tuned SAM 3D Body, runs in real time for one person on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, from detection to a fitted body, at 4.6x the speed of SAM 3D Body's eager-PyTorch body-only path, while improving accuracy on most camera-space benchmarks. The same network predicts heel, toe, hand, and knee contacts, which connect the body to the scene. FAB also estimates world-space motion, fuses static-scene depth around the visible person, and aligns body and scene using predicted contacts. For human-to-humanoid real-to-sim transfer, an in-model G1 head and FAB-Retarget, a motion-level retargeter that reads dense points or the fitted mesh, map motion to a Unitree G1. FAB-Retarget produces references that follow the person more closely than specialized retargeters including SOMA, GMR, UMR, and OmniRetarget, and substantially more closely than Fast SAM 3D Body retargeted with our sequence IK. Project page: https://www.jinkuncao.com/FAB.
2611.25801.comment: 28 pages, 9 pages of main text. 16 figures

llm.title_ja: ピクセル、ワールド空間、シーンにおける高速かつ高精度な人体推定
llm.tldr_ja: FABは、パラメータ表現と高密度な3D点群を直接予測し、実時間での人体姿勢推定とシーンへの統合、ヒューマノイドへの動作転移を実現する。
llm.problem: 従来の人体推定手法はパラメータ化されたメッシュモデルパラメータのみを予測し、効率性と復元忠実度の両立が困難である。
llm.method: 画像内の高密度2D/3Dボディポイントと頭部モデルを予測し、SMPLフィッティングを行った上で、接触情報を用いてシーンとボディを整合させる。
llm.result: RT 4070 Ti SUPER上でSAM 3D Bodyの4.6倍の速度で動作し、多くのカメラ空間ベンチマークで精度を向上、Unitree G1への優れた動作転移を実現した。
keywords_ja: モーションリタイゲーション

2611.25798.title: Design and Validation of a Telescopic Chassis-Assisted Stair-Climbing Mechanism for Powered Wheelchairs
2611.25798.abstract: We propose a simple stair traversal mechanism that augments a four-wheel wheelchair with an auxiliary telescopic chassis actuator. The proposed mechanism provides the following key contributions during stair ascent: (A) enhanced safety by ensuring that either the front or rear wheels remain stationary at all times; (B) primary reliance of the required force and mechanical work on the telescopic chassis rather than the wheels; (C) insensitivity of the required force and mechanical work to stair inclination; and (D) reduced risk of wheel slip on steeper stairs. In addition, the telescopic chassis is expected to improve level-ground mobility by enabling tight turning with the shortest wheelbase and enhancing stability with the longest wheelbase.

llm.title_ja: 電動車椅子用伸縮式シャシ補助階段昇降機構の設計と検証
llm.tldr_ja: 補助的な伸縮式シャシアクチュエータを追加した四輪車椅子の階段昇降機構を提案し、安全性向上と車輪スリップのリスク軽減を実現する。
llm.problem: 従来の車椅子による階段昇降は安全性の確保や車輪の滑りリスクなどの課題がある。
llm.method: 前輪または後輪のどちらかを常に静止させ、必要な力や仕事を車輪ではなく伸縮式シャシに主に依存させる機構を設計・検証する。
llm.result: 階段昇降時の安全性を高め、階段の傾斜に依存せず、平地での小回りや安定性も向上させることが示された。

2611.25788.title: Collision-Free Is Not Enough: Passage-Conditioned Navigation for Wheeled-Legged Robots
2611.25788.abstract: A collision-free detour can still bring a legged robot to the next stair or ledge a few centimetres or degrees off, and a fixed locomotion skill, factory or learned, can stall or fall. Existing methods prevent this with a robot model or extensive trial and error, but on a new site with unknown skills neither is available, so they cannot be used. We find that a single 27-minute teaching session already supplies what these methods have to derive or learn: for every stair and ledge, one crossing the skill has completed. Our method, passage-conditioned navigation, makes the route remember how each transition was entered, not only where the path went. It stores each taught crossing as an event and, without training or a robot model, enforces it after every local replan: before each ledge, an entry gate makes the robot turn or back up and retry if it is more than 10 cm or 10° off the taught crossing. Under localization noise, with path, gait schedule, and sensing unchanged, this raises the share of disturbed ledge crossings that stay within these limits from 24.1% to 88.6%. In contact simulation with our learned policies, a robot pushed off course before stairs never falls in 180 climbs, against 9 falls when the stored direction is ignored; pushed 1.2 m away, it rejoins the route, ending on average 0.14 m from it (1.10 m without rejoining), and finishes as often as an undisturbed robot. This suits any robot with fixed skills that repeats a route over terrain transitions, as in inspection and patrol, where one wrong entry can end the task. We deployed it in competition on a real wheeled-legged robot: over 271 m of multi-obstacle terrain spanning 7.0 m of elevation, it completed all six runs, won third place at the 2026 Global Open-source AI Challenge, which drew 2,999 submissions, and was the only finalist in its task to finish fully autonomously.

llm.title_ja: 衝突フリーだけでは不十分：車輪脚ロボットのための通路条件付きナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 通路条件付きナビゲーションは、教示された各階段や段差の通過イベントを記憶し、局所再計画後に強制することで外乱に対するロバスト性を大幅に高める。
llm.problem: 衝突回避デトュールはロボットを数センチメートルずらしてしまい、固定された移動スキルではスタックや転倒を引き起こす。
llm.method: 27分の教示セッションで各段差の通過スキルをイベントとして記録し、訓練やロボットモデルなしで局所再計画後にそのエントリーゲートを強制する。
llm.result: 外乱を受けた段差通過の許容範囲内維持率が24.1%から88.6%に向上し、実機の車輪脚ロボットによるコンペティションで3位を獲得した。

2611.25788.tldr_en: This method, passage-conditioned navigation, makes the route remember how each transition was entered, not only where the path went, and suits any robot with fixed skills that repeats a route over terrain transitions, as in inspection and patrol.

2611.25778.title: ECHO: In-Context Behavior foundation model for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
2611.25778.abstract: Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions. Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution. Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage. Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates. Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control. Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

llm.title_ja: ECHO：ヒューマノイド全身制御のためのコンテキスト内行動基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ECHOは、事前学習による行動事前分布と、インタラクション履歴から動力学特有の構造化表現を学習する残差適応を分離し、テスト時のパラメータ更新なしで環境に適応する。
llm.problem: 従来のヒューマノイド行動基盤モデルは幅広いスキルを獲得するが、基底の動力学の違いを区別できず、環境特異的な精密実行が困難である。
llm.method: 混合・焼きなましサンプリングによる行動事前の事前学習と、インタラクション履歴に基づくコンテキスト表現・残差適応を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 多様な動作や物理条件でベースラインを上回り、Unitree G1でのアクロバットや地形インタラクション、ペイロード適応を含む全身遠隔操作を実現した。

2611.25778.tldr_en: ECHO is introduced, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution, and outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions.

2611.25777.title: Hindsight Self-Distillation: Teaching Robots to Act from the Present
2611.25777.abstract: A robot must choose an action before it can see the outcome. In a recorded demonstration, later camera frames show what happened after the robot moved. Hindsight Self-Distillation (HSD) uses these later frames to teach a policy what to extract from current images. During training, a teacher sees both the current and later frames, while a student sees the current frames. They share a visual encoder and an action predictor. Each branch summarizes its images with a small set of feature vectors. These visual summaries supply all visual input to the action predictor. The teacher learns from demonstrated actions. For each noisy action sequence, the student learns from either the demonstration or the teacher's denoising prediction. It also learns to match the teacher's visual summaries. We analyze which aspects of the teacher's predictions the student can recover from its inputs. At deployment, the student encodes the current images once and reuses its summaries at every denoising step. HSD achieves average success rates of 98.50\% on LIBERO and 92.31\% on RoboTwin 2.0.

llm.title_ja: 事後自己蒸留：現在から行動することをロボットに教える
llm.tldr_ja: Hindsight Self-Distillationは、デモンストレーションの後のフレームを用いて現在の画像から何を抽出すべきかをポリシーに教え、推論時の効率的な行動予測を実現する。
llm.problem: ロボットは結果を見る前に行動を選択しなければならないが、記録されたデモンストレーションでは後のフレームがその後の経過を示している。
llm.method: 現在と将来のフレームを見る教師と、現在のフレームのみを見る学生がビジュアルエンコーダと行動予測器を共有し、学生は教師の視覚的要約とノイズ除去予測を学習する。
llm.result: LIBEROで平均98.50%、RoboTwin 2.0で92.31%の成功率を達成した。

2611.25777.tldr_en: Hindsight Self-Distillation analyzes which aspects of the teacher's predictions the student can recover from its inputs and which aspects of the teacher's predictions the student can recover from its inputs.

2611.25747.title: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories
2611.25747.abstract: Promptable segmenters answer what a thing is. Dense prediction tasks also ask class-agnostic questions, such as what stands out or hides, how light is blocked, transmitted or reflected, and where structure lies. Robots, surveillance systems and image editors build on their answers. We study promptable concept maps (PCM), which extend SAM 3's promptable concept segmentation from noun instances to maps of concepts named by short noun phrases such as `"transparent object", with "none" as an answer. PCM-Bench groups the standard test sets of seven such tasks by the question they ask. On it, we find that SAM 3 sees more than it detects. Its semantic path responds to many of these concepts, yet a low image-level presence score can block every detection of its instance path. We present UNVEIL, which trains a copy of SAM 3's semantic path for these maps, with LoRA on copies of its last blocks. A separate presence decoder learns from verified negatives whether a concept occurs. With one text phrase per query, UNVEIL maps region concepts such as salient and camouflaged objects, shadows, transparent objects and mirrors. The same weights map thin structures such as edges and skeletons as well as object categories. Run next to SAM 3, it leaves SAM 3's own outputs unchanged. On each of the seven tasks, UNVEIL reaches the highest score among the compared promptable models, including SAM 3's official fine-tuning and pipelines built on multimodal LLMs. Code is available at https://github.com/yuhuan-wu/UNVEIL.

llm.title_ja: SAM 3は検出するもの以上を見る：カテゴリを超えたプロンプト可能コンセプトマップ
llm.tldr_ja: UNVEILは、SAM 3のセマンティックパスをコピーしてLoRAで訓練し、カテゴリを超えた透明オブジェクトや影などのプロンプト可能コンセプトマップを高精度に生成する。
llm.problem: プロンプト可能なセグメンターは物体インスタンスを答えるが、クラス非依存の質問（隠れているものや光の反射など）には対応しきれない。
llm.method: SAM 3のセマンティックパスのコピーを最後のブロックのLoRAで訓練し、検証済みネガティブから概念の発生を学習する独立した存在デコーダを導入する。
llm.result: 7つのタスクすべてにおいて、SAM 3の公式ファインチューニングやマルチモーダルLLMベースのパイプラインを上回る最高スコアを達成した。
keywords_ja: 画像セグメンテーション

2611.25747.tldr_en: UNVEIL is presented, which trains a copy of SAM 3's semantic path for these maps, with LoRA on copies of its last blocks, and reaches the highest score among the compared promptable models, including SAM 3's official fine-tuning and pipelines built on multimodal LLMs.

2611.25725.title: On the Hamel Coefficients and the Boltzmann-Hamel Equations for the Rigid Body
2611.25725.abstract: The Boltzmann-Hamel (BH) equations are central in the dynamics and control of nonholonomic systems described in terms of quasi-velocities. The rigid body is a classical example of such systems, and it is well-known that the BH-equations are the Newton-Euler (NE) equations when described in terms of rigid body twists as quasi-velocities. It is further known that the NE-equations are the Euler-Poincare, respectively, the reduced Euler-Lagrange equations on SE(3) when using body-fixed or spatial representation of rigid body twists. The connection between these equations are the Hamel coefficients, which are immediately identified as the structure constants of SE(3). However, an explicit coordinate-free derivation has not been presented in the literature. In this paper the Hamel coefficients for the rigid body are derived in a coordinate-free way without resorting to local coordinates describing the rigid body motion. The three most relevant choices of quasi-velocities (body-fixed, spatial, and hybrid representation of rigid body twists) are considered. The corresponding BH-equations are derived explicitly for the rotating and free floating body. Further, the Hamel equations for nonholonomically constrained rigid bodies are discussed, and demonstrated for the inhomogenous ball rolling on a plane.

llm.title_ja: 剛体のハメル係数とボルツマン・ハメル方程式について
llm.tldr_ja: 局座標を用いずに座標系フリーな方法で剛体のハメル係数を導出し、回転・浮遊・非ホロノミック拘束を持つ剛体に対するボルツマン・ハメル方程式を明示的に求めた。
llm.problem: 非ホロノミック系の動力学と制御において中心的なボルツマン・ハメル方程式の、剛体に対する座標系フリーな導出が文献に示されていなかった。
llm.method: 剛体ツイストの3つの表現（ボディ固定、空間、ハイブリッド）を考慮し、ローカル座標に頼らずにハメル係数を座標系フリーに導出する。
llm.result: 回転・浮遊する剛体および平面上の不均質な転がり球の例を用いて、ハメル方程式の妥当性を論証した。

2611.25725.tldr_en: The Hamel equations for nonholonomically constrained rigid bodies are discussed, and demonstrated for the inhomogenous ball rolling on a plane.

2611.25722.title: DACA: Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent for Zero-Shot 3D Visual Grounding
2611.25722.abstract: 3D visual grounding (3D-VG) is a task that bridges the natural language and 3D space, serving as a foundational capability for embodied intelligence and human-computer interaction. Although recent 3D-VG agents overcome the reliance on pre-processed 3D point clouds, they essentially employ a unidirectional, pipeline-style tool-calling architecture. This architecture separates semantic understanding from geometric reconstruction, leading to error accumulation and an inability to autonomously recover from failures. To address this flaw, this paper proposes the Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent (DACA), which reinterprets 3D-VG as a semantic-geometric dual-anchor collaborative reasoning paradigm. DACA comprises two complementary specialized tools: the semantic anchor tool holds the visual semantic features of the target and achieves efficient target tracking via optical flow and VLM local verification; the geometric anchor tool holds the 3D spatial geometric features of the target and performs global spatial reasoning via voxelization and multi-keypoint projection. The two components exchange information bidirectionally via a standardized tool call protocol, autonomously deciding on the next perception-action step to form a closed-loop optimization. Experiments on the ScanRefer and Nr3D benchmarks demonstrate that zero-shot DACA achieves an overall Acc@0.25 of 73.6\% on ScanRefer and 70.4\% overall accuracy on Nr3D, far surpassing the latest zero-shot 3D-VG methods. The code and models are available at https://github.com/liujia99/DACA

llm.title_ja: DACA：ゼロショット3Dビジュアルグラウンディングのためのデュアルアンカー協調エージェント
llm.tldr_ja: DACAは、視覚的意味特徴を持つセマンティックアンカーと3D空間幾何特徴を持つジオメトリックアンカーを双方向に連携させ、ゼロショットでの3Dビジュアルグラウンディングを実現する。
llm.problem: 近年の3Dビジュアルグラウンディングエージェントは単方向のツール呼び出しアーキテクチャを採用しており、意味理解と幾何再構成が分離して誤差が蓄積する。
llm.method: オプティカルフローやVLMによる意味アンカーツールと、ボクセル化やマルチキーポイント投影による幾何アンカーツールを標準プロトコルで双方向に連携させる。
llm.result: ScanReferで73.6%、Nr3Dで70.4%のAcc@0.25を達成し、最新のゼロショット3D-VG手法を大幅に上回った。
keywords_ja: 3Dビジュアルグラウンディング

2611.25722.tldr_en: The Dual-Anchor Collaborative Agent (DACA) is proposed, which reinterprets 3D-VG as a semantic-geometric dual-anchor collaborative reasoning paradigm, and achieves an overall Acc@0.25 of 73.6\% on ScanRefer and 70.4\% overall accuracy on Nr3D, far surpassing the latest zero-shot 3D-VG methods.

2611.25695.title: DMT-Attack: Diffusion-Prior Texture Search for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Policies
2611.25695.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely on visual feedback throughout manipulation, making them vulnerable to persistent texture attacks. However, optimized patterns can stand out from their surroundings, making an attack easier to notice and its carrier more likely to be inspected or removed. To address this limitation, our key insight is to search the structured image distribution of a diffusion model for natural-looking textures while using closed-loop feedback to identify task-disruptive candidates. Based on this idea, we propose DMT-Attack, a gradient-free gray-box attack that generates textures for ordinary scene objects such as tablecloths. A frozen text-conditioned diffusion model defines the search space, and an eight-expert latent proposal network is initialized from evaluated teacher latents and refined using rollout feedback. We evaluate DMT-Attack against pi_0.5 and OpenVLA-OFT across four LIBERO suites. DMT-Attack achieves a macro clean-conditioned attack success rate (cASR) of 57.9%, compared with 44.7% for UPA-RFAS and 19.7% for random natural textures. It also attains higher scene similarity and a lower clean-calibrated detector flag rate (45% versus 97.5-100% for optimized patch baselines). These results demonstrate that natural-looking textures can disrupt VLA visual feedback and closed-loop decision-making, motivating defenses that jointly assess visual appearance and task behavior.

llm.title_ja: DMT-Attack：閉ループビジョン言語アクションポリシーのための拡散事前学習テクスチャ探索
llm.tldr_ja: DMT-Attackは、拡散モデルの構造化画像分布を探索して自然に見えるテクスチャを生成し、閉ループフィードバックを用いてVLAポリシーを効果的に攪乱する。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーは視覚フィードバックに依存するため持続的なテクスチャ攻撃に脆弱だが、最適化されたパターンは周囲から浮いてしまい発見されやすい。
llm.method: 凍結されたテキスト条件付き拡散モデルを探索空間とし、ロールアウトフィードバックで洗練される8専門家の潜在提案ネットワークを用いる。
llm.result: LIBEROスイートにおいてマクロクリーン条件付き攻撃成功率57.9%を達成し、高いシーン類似度と低い検出器フラグ率を維持した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2611.25695.tldr_en: DMT-Attack is proposed, a gradient-free gray-box attack that generates textures for ordinary scene objects such as tablecloths that demonstrates that natural-looking textures can disrupt VLA visual feedback and closed-loop decision-making, motivating defenses that jointly assess visual appearance and task behavior.

2611.25683.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation
2611.25683.abstract: Changes in illumination can induce action drift in dexterous manipulation even when the physical state remains unchanged. Although existing vision--tactile--language--action (VTLA) policies incorporate tactile feedback, when and how touch refines actions under changing visual conditions remains challenging. We introduce \textbf{TipDex-VTLA}, a VTLA policy that combines estimated visual action reliability and tactile forecast verification to regulate execution-time refinement. Specifically, Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation (VASE) learns visual reliability from a frozen reference policy's action sensitivity to illumination perturbations. Tactile Anticipation and Correction during Execution (TACE) compares predicted and measured touch at matched times and combines the resulting discrepancy with visual reliability to gate bounded feature corrections for unexecuted actions. This effectively helps to refine actions under challenging unseen visual conditions. We evaluate TipDex-VTLA on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks and the UniVTAC simulation benchmark. TipDex-VTLA trained on data collected under normal visual conditions, achieves average full-task success rates of 87.5% (resp. 73.8%) under normal (resp. challenging unseen) lighting in real-world tasks, significantly outperforming some state-of-the-art methods. We will release the collected data and source code.

llm.title_ja: TipDex-VTLA：器用な操作における触覚を用いたアクション洗練のタイミング学習
llm.tldr_ja: TipDex-VTLAは、視覚的アクション信頼性と触覚予測の検証を組み合わせて、照明変化などの困難な視覚条件下での器用な操作を改善するVTLAポリシーである。
llm.problem: 照明の変化により、物理的状態が同じでも器用な操作でアクションのドリフトが発生する課題がある。
llm.method: 視覚的アクション信頼性推定と触覚予測・補正を組み合わせて、実行時のアクション修正を制御する。
llm.result: 実世界の器用な操作タスクにおいて、通常照明時で87.5%、未知の困難な照明時で73.8%の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2611.25683.tldr_en: TipDex-VTLA, a VTLA policy that combines estimated visual action reliability and tactile forecast verification to regulate execution-time refinement, achieves average full-task success rates and significantly outperforms some state-of-the-art methods.

2611.25679.title: LeCompass: Task-Level Execution through State-Indexed Interfaces
2611.25679.abstract: Action-conditioned joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) offer a foundation for predictive decision-making by modeling the consequences of actions in representation space. Yet evaluating local reachability in latent space does not by itself provide a task-level execution interface: intermediate targets must be generated, local inference has finite budgets, and execution requires spatial feedback and persistent interaction state. We introduce LeCompass, a state-indexed execution framework built around a frozen LeWorldModel (LeWM). A proposer supplies intermediate latent targets, while CompassFlow searches the source space of a learned trajectory prior to obtain effective action candidates under limited predictive-evaluation budgets. Patch-token readouts provide spatial feedback, while observation-based memory supports phase transitions and bounded recovery. State-indexed targets support cross-episode context-goal composition. On 1,000 official TEST full-episode Cube trials, the complete LeCompass execution system achieves 86.9% native 4-cm reach. Separate matched analyses show that predictive ranking raises success from 4.7% to 44.9% on TEST PushT and from 33.8% to 77.7% on TEST TwoRoom. These results demonstrate task-level execution with task-dependent roles for latent target proposal, predictive search, and observation-grounded control.

llm.title_ja: LeCompass：状態インデックス付きインターフェースによるタスクレベルの実行
llm.tldr_ja: LeCompassは、凍結されたLeWMを基盤に、中間目標の提案、予測探索、および観測に基づく制御を統合した状態インデックス付きの実行フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 潜在空間での局所的到達可能性の評価だけでは、中間目標の生成や永続的な相互作用状態を必要とするタスクレベルの実行インターフェースを提供できない。
llm.method: 凍結されたLeWorldModelを中心に据え、プロポーザとCompassFlowによる予測探索、状態インデックス付き目標を組み合わせる。
llm.result: TEST Cubeトライアルの4cm到達で86.9%の成功率を達成し、PushTやTwoRoomの予測ランキングで成功率が大幅に向上した。

2611.25679.tldr_en: LeCompass is introduced, a state-indexed execution framework built around a frozen LeWorldModel (LeWM), where a proposer supplies intermediate latent targets, while CompassFlow searches the source space of a learned trajectory prior to obtain effective action candidates under limited predictive-evaluation budgets.

2611.25667.title: CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control
2611.25667.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.

llm.title_ja: CauSyncVLA：非同期ロボット制御のための因果的潜在世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: CauSyncVLAは、因果的潜在世界モデルを用いて知覚メモリの予測と軌跡補正を実際のロボット実行に同期させ、推論効率と閉ループのロバスト性を向上させる非同期制御システムである。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーにおいて計算と実行のオーバーラップを行うと、知覚メモリが古くなり、連続するアクションチャンクが断絶する課題がある。
llm.method: 因果的潜在世界モデルにより遅延した視覚アンカーから現在の知覚メモリを予測し、予測的フローウォームスタートで単一ステップのフロー補正を行う。
llm.result: LIBERO-10において、5.04倍の推論スループットで93.8%の成功率を達成し、閉ループのロバスト性と動作の滑らかさを改善した。

2611.25667.tldr_en: CauSyncVLA is presented, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution, and Predictive Flow Warm-Starting aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training.

2611.25665.title: GNetSS: Towards Learning GNSS Corrections without Ground Truth
2611.25665.abstract: We present GNetSS, a self-supervised GNSS position correction framework that improves the robustness of single point positioning (SPP) without requiring ground-truth locations for training. GNetSS combines a transformer-based network with a deterministic differentiable positioning solver. The network predicts satellite-wise pseudorange corrections by modelling inter-satellite geometry and temporal context, while the solver converts these corrected measurements into receiver position corrections under GNSS geometry and optional motion constraints. Unlike supervised GNSS correction methods that rely on ground-truth, GNetSS derives its training signal directly from GNSS measurement consistency. Experimental results show that GNetSS improves robustness across open-sky, urban, and forested environments. The method is particularly effective at suppressing large-error outliers, reducing the maximum 3D positioning error by over 50% compared with SPP. These results demonstrate the potential of self-supervised pseudorange correction for scalable and robust GNSS positioning in real-world autonomy applications. Code and the in-house dataset will be released upon acceptance.
2611.25665.comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, Submitted to NAVIGATION, Journal of the Institute of Navigation. See navi.ion.org

llm.title_ja: GNetSS：グランドトラスなしのGNSS補正学習に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: GNetSSは、グランドトルースの位置情報を必要とせず、GNSSの測定矛盾から直接学習して単独測位のロバスト性を向上させる自己教師ありGNSS位置補正フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 従来の教師ありGNSS補正手法はグランドトルースに依存している。
llm.method: トランスフォーマーベースのネットワークと決定論的可微分測位ソルバーを組み合わせ、測定の一貫性から学習信号を導出する。
llm.result: オープン空、都市部、森林環境でロバスト性を改善し、最大3D測位誤差をSPPと比較して50%以上削減した。

2611.25665.tldr_en: GNetSS is a self-supervised GNSS position correction framework that improves the robustness of single point positioning (SPP) without requiring ground-truth locations for training, and is particularly effective at suppressing large-error outliers.

2611.25656.title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery
2611.25656.abstract: Tools with different shapes can have similar functions, but transferring manipulation skills across tools requires understanding how tool geometry relates to the specific task and adjusting the manipulation strategy accordingly. The key challenge is to discover the common affordances that contribute to task completion across different tools and verify whether they support new tools in performing similar work. We present A$^2$-VLA, a tool-adaptation framework that combines an embodied agent with a VLA policy. It treats tool affordances as hypotheses the agent can construct, test, and revise. Given teleoperated demonstrations with a few source tools, the agent reconstructs the scenes in simulation and autonomously determines task-relevant affordance features: functional regions and their key geometric properties. It develops affordance-extraction skills and refines both the features and skills through autonomous experiments in the reconstructed scenes. Validated extraction skills accumulate in a reusable skill library for unseen tools. Finally, A$^2$-VLA uses encoded functional-region features as conditioning inputs to a $π_{0.5}$ backbone during training and inference. Evaluation examines affordance reliability in reconstructed scenes and real-robot task success on unseen tools. Our method achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting based on affordances. On three real-robot tool-use tasks, A$^2$-VLA improves task success by 30.7 percentage points over $π_{0.5}$.

llm.title_ja: A$^2$-VLA：エージェント型アフォーダンス発見による新規ツールへのビジョン・言語・行動ポリシーの適応
llm.tldr_ja: A$^2$-VLAは、エージェントがタスク関連のアフォーダンス特徴を自律的に発見・検証し、新規ツールへのクロスツール操作適応を実現するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 異なる形状を持つツール間で操作スキルを転移するには、ツールの幾何学的形状がタスクとどのように関連するかを理解する必要がある。
llm.method: シミュレーション内での自律実験を通じてタスク関連のアフォーダンス特徴を構築、テスト、修正するエージェントとVLAポリシーを統合する。
llm.result: シミュレーションでのクロスツール軌跡再ターゲットで86.1%の成功率を達成し、3つの実機ツール使用タスクでpi_0.5を30.7ポイント上回った。

2611.25656.tldr_en: A$2-VLA is presented, a tool-adaptation framework that combines an embodied agent with a VLA policy that treats tool affordances as hypotheses the agent can construct, test, and revise and achieves 86.1% success in simulated cross-tool trajectory retargeting based on affordances.

2611.25637.title: Beyond Easy Clients: Difficulty- and Improvement-Aware Aggregation for Federated Reinforcement Learning in Robot Navigation
2611.25637.abstract: Federated reinforcement learning enables a fleet of robots to jointly learn a shared navigation policy without exchanging raw experience. In practice, however, the robots rarely operate in the same conditions: an open aisle is far easier to navigate than a cluttered room, and takes less learning to master. Standard federated aggregation rules ignore this. Uniform averaging weights every client equally, whether or not it is still learning, and weighting by episode return is worse, since easy environments permit high returns by construction. Both failures stem from what we call the \emph{plateau problem}: once a client masters its environment, its updates carry little new information even though its reported return remains high. We propose \emph{FedDIA}, which scores each client by how much its local training improves the global model it received, amplified by the difficulty of its environment. Difficulty is inferred from the model's own performance, without requiring any description of the environment. Both signals are measured against the global model, so they are comparable across clients. On a mapless navigation task with eight heterogeneous clients, FedDIA reaches a mean success rate of $75.5\%$ across training and held-out environments, against $68.7\%$ for the strongest federated baseline. Its advantage holds when the models are transferred to hand-authored warehouse and living-space layouts, or when one of the clients is defective.

llm.title_ja: 簡単なクライアントを超えて：ロボットナビゲーションにおける連合強化学習のための難易度および改善度を考慮した集約
llm.tldr_ja: FedDIAは、ロボットナビゲーションの連合強化学習において、環境の難易度とモデルの改善度に基づいてクライアントのアップデートをスコア付けし集約する手法である。
llm.problem: 標準的な連合集約ルールは、すでに簡単な環境をマスターしたクライアントの古いアップデートが混ざるプラトー問題に対処できない。
llm.method: モデル自身の性能から環境の難易度を推論し、グローバルモデルに対する局所的トレーニングの改善度と掛け合わせて各クライアントを評価する。
llm.result: 8つの異種クライアントを用いたマップなしナビゲーションタスクにおいて、平均成功率75.5%を達成しベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2611.25637.tldr_en: FedDIA is proposed, which scores each client by how much its local training improves the global model it received, amplified by the difficulty of its environment, which is inferred from the model's own performance, without requiring any description of the environment.

2611.25614.title: Don't Lose the Future: Latent-Aware 4-Bit Quantization of World Action Models
2611.25614.abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict how a scene will evolve and condition their actions on this predicted future. Deploying them on a robot's onboard computer calls for 4-bit weights, activations and key-value caches (W4A4KV4). Existing 4-bit quantizers for WAMs preserve the generated action, and estimate sensitivity one denoising step at a time. However, they fail to preserve the fidelity of the predicted future: once the action pathway is protected, the remaining action error enters mostly through a degraded future that none of them deliberately protects. We propose LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework that preserves the predicted future where it is written, stored and read. Specifically, we introduce a reader metric, which measures future error by its effect on the action, and a read count, which weights each rounding error by the number of denoising steps that read it. Together they give the allocation of precision over activations and caches a closed-form solution. We further develop gaze-guided refinement, which gives the tokens the action attends to a second 4-bit pass in the denoising loop and in the cache. All weights stay at 4 bits, with no high-precision branch and no per-task recalibration. On the LIBERO-Plus benchmark, LAQ reaches 76.4% and 83.3% average success on Fast-WAM and Cosmos-Policy, within 1.2 percentage points of the 16-bit models and all above the baselines with 16-bit KV caches. It compresses the model by 3.8x, reduces the peak GPU memory of the whole policy by 2.3x, and runs 1.66x faster than the 16-bit model. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, it reaches 47.0% average success over three tasks, against 52.0% for the 16-bit model and 30.0% higher than QuaRot.

llm.title_ja: 未来を見失うな：ワールドアクションモデルの潜在認識型4ビット量子化
llm.tldr_ja: LAQは、アクションに与える影響や参照回数に基づいて将来の予測精度を保持する、ワールドアクションモデル向けの潜在認識型4ビット量子化フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存の4ビット量子化器はアクション経路を保護する一方で、予測された未来の忠実度を損なう課題がある。
llm.method: 将来の予測誤差がアクションに与える影響を測定するリーダーメトリックと読込回数を用いて、精度割り当ての解を導出する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plusベンチマークで16ビットモデルに迫る性能を維持しながら、3.8倍の圧縮と2.3倍のピークGPUメモリ削減を実現した。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル

2611.25614.tldr_en: LAQ, a latent-aware quantization framework that preserves the predicted future where it is written, stored and read is proposed, which introduces a reader metric, which measures future error by its effect on the action, and a read count, which weights each rounding error by the number of denoising steps that read it.

2611.25604.title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
2611.25604.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce \textbf{Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD)}, a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a regularized approximation of local training geometry, producing scalable influence-based values for the policy. A controlled group-removal study establishes the directional fidelity of these values, while cross-planner analysis shows that the same candidate pool induces markedly different rankings across planner families. On DiffusionDrive, PAD improves EPDMS over real-only training by $3.5$ points on NavTest and $5.0$ points on NavHard. Policy-specific curation consistently outperforms real-only and full-pool training across diffusion-, regression-, and flow-matching-based planners while substantially reducing scene-level regressions. These results establish policy-aware data valuation as a basis for replacing indiscriminate data accumulation with targeted policy improvement, enabling more efficient and reliable scaling of autonomous-driving systems.

llm.title_ja: PAD：自動運転のためのポリシー認識型データ評価
llm.tldr_ja: PADは、シーンレベルのキャリブレーションフィードバックと射影ポリシー勾配を組み合わせることで、ターゲットの駆動ポリシーに特化したユーティリティを各デモンストレーションに割り当てるフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存のキュレーション方法は、下流のポリシーユーティリティを測定しない固有のサンプルプロパティに依存している。
llm.method: シーンレベルのキャリブレーションフィードバック、射影ポリシー勾配、局所的トレーニング幾何学の正則化近似を統合する。
llm.result: DiffusionDriveにおいて、NavTestで3.5ポイント、NavHardで5.0ポイントのEPDMS改善を達成し、データ選定効率を高めた。
keywords_ja: データキュレーション

2611.25604.tldr_en: Policy-aware data valuation is established as a basis for replacing indiscriminate data accumulation with targeted policy improvement, enabling more efficient and reliable scaling of autonomous-driving systems.
