2611.25595.title: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference
2611.25595.abstract: World action models (WAMs) couple generative video modeling with robotic action prediction but typically require large video and action transformers, limiting deployment efficiency. We present LoopedWAM, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert. To account for their asymmetric inference costs, the video and action experts can operate at different depths: visual features are computed once per query, whereas action computation repeats at every sampling step. We further propose elastic self-distillation, which trains a single elastic checkpoint, LoopedWAM-E, across action-depth and sampling-step budgets. With only 0.58B policy parameters and no robot pretraining, LoopedWAM achieves 96.1% success on LIBERO, 91.9% on RoboTwin 2.0, and 52.2% on RoboCasaGR1, while using $7.4\times$ less peak GPU memory than Fast-WAM under matched inference measurements. On LIBERO, LoopedWAM-E achieves 96.0% success in 27.6 ms or 95.2% in 24.7 ms on an H100, providing multiple accuracy-latency operating points from a single checkpoint; with two sampling steps and four action loops, it stays within 0.5 points of LoopedWAM on all three benchmarks. Ablations demonstrate that weight-shared depth preserves competitive performance, while aggressive action-depth reduction requires explicit budget-aware training. On a real AgileX PiPER arm, LoopedWAM succeeds in 71.3% of 80 trials across four tasks.

llm.title_ja: LoopedWAM：弾力的な推論のためのループ型ワールドアクションモデル
llm.tldr_ja: LoopedWAMは、共有される6ブロックのコアをリカレントに適用することで推論効率を高めた、コンパクトで弾力的なワールドアクションモデルである。
llm.problem: ワールドアクションモデルは大規模なビデオおよびアクション・トランスフォーマーを必要とし、デプロイ効率が制限される。
llm.method: 共有コアをリカレントに適用し、ビデオとアクションの専門家が異なる深さで動作する構造と、弾力的な自己蒸留を採用する。
llm.result: LIBEROで96.1%の成功率を達成しつつ、Fast-WAMと比較してピークGPUメモリを7.4倍削減した。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル

2611.25595.tldr_en: LoopedWAM is presented, a compact WAM that recurrently applies a shared six-block core in each expert, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert, which demonstrates that weight-shared depth preserves competitive performance, while aggressive action-depth reduction requires explicit budget-aware training.

2611.25594.title: Bradley-Terry Training Can Distort Outcome Probabilities of Initially Accurate Language World Models
2611.25594.abstract: Comparative feedback, in which a judge says which of two candidate outcomes is closer to what happened, is a practical way to train language world models that assign probabilities to an action's outcomes. We show that, fitted with a Bradley-Terry objective, it need not teach the true outcome probabilities and can distort accurate ones. On a simulated robot push with enumerated outcome distributions, this objective takes a model that is accurate on unseen layouts (hazard error 2.4 percentage points, pp) and moves 33 to 43 pp of its probability onto outcomes that none of a condition's enumerated branches produces. The cause is the objective, not the comparisons: its optimum, computed before training, predicts where the model ends up, and a likelihood that knows the judge's rule learns from the same comparisons without the shift. The shift is robust: it recurs on unseen conditions, under five candidate laws and a three-fold denser enumeration, and about 29 pp remain without the physically impossible events. Its cost is conditional: with those events it inflates hazard probabilities, and a threshold inherited from the pre-feedback model costs about 3 pp of utility per decision on trained and 1 to 2 pp on unseen conditions, through false rejects; without them the utility loss averages below 1 pp over six seeds, though a small regret in action choice remains. Audits of readout, response and decision trace the effect from probabilities to actions.

llm.title_ja: ブラッドリー・テリー学習は初期に正確な言語世界モデルの結果確率を歪める可能性がある
llm.tldr_ja: 比較フィードバックをブラッドリー・テリー目的関数で学習させると、真の結果確率を学習せず、正確な確率を物理的に不可能なイベントに歪めてしまうことを示した論文。
llm.problem: 比較フィードバックを用いた言語世界モデルの訓練において、ブラッドリー・テリー目的関数が正しい結果確率を歪めるリスクがある。
llm.method: シミュレートされたロボットプッシュ環境を用いて、学習前後の結果確率の分布やハザード確率の変化を分析する。
llm.result: 未知の環境において、初期に正確だったモデルの確率が不可能なイベントやハザード確率へ大きくシフトしてしまうことを確認した。
keywords_ja: ブラッドリー・テリー

2611.25594.tldr_en: It is shown thatComparative feedback, in which a judge says which of two candidate outcomes is closer to what happened, is a practical way to train language world models that assign probabilities to an action's outcomes and need not teach the true outcome probabilities and can distort accurate ones.

2611.25589.title: GraF-VTA: Neuro-Symbolic Trajectory Generation from Vision and Temporal Logic via Graph-Based Fusion
2611.25589.abstract: Robotic planning from visual observations and signal temporal logic (STL) requires grounding task requirements in scene evidence while adapting plans to execution feedback. We present GraF-VTA, a graph-based framework that extends Vision-TL-Action with structured task representations, causal observation history, and closed-loop trajectory generation. Bidirectional cross-attention fuses STL syntax tokens with visual features, while an optional frozen automaton embedding supplies complementary untimed task structure. A temporal pyramid preserves detailed current observations and compresses older frames to provide recent execution context. Conditioned on these features and robot state, a flow-matching model generates plans whose action prefixes are executed before replanning from refreshed observations. Across five simulation environments, the single-graph configuration achieves higher open-loop Success@$K$ than TeLoGraF and Vision-TL-Action on four environments at the reported budgets $K\geq16$. On Panda, matched-update ablations increase Success@256 from 53.91\% without observation history to 62.50\% with pyramid memory. In closed-loop Dubins evaluation, it reaches 64.06\% Success@1024, compared with 12.50\% for adapted S-MSP and 27.34\% for adapted Logic-VLA. These results support combining structured visual conditioning with observation history and replanning to improve coverage of STL-satisfying trajectories.

llm.title_ja: GraF-VTA：グラフベースの融合による視覚と時間論理からの神経・記号的軌跡生成
llm.tldr_ja: GraF-VTAは、双方向クロスアテンションを用いて信号時間論理（STL）の構文トークンと視覚特徴を融合し、構造化されたタスク表現と閉ループ軌跡生成を行うグラフベースのフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 視覚的観測と信号時間論理からのロボット計画には、シーンのエビデンスにタスク要件をグラウンディングさせつつ計画を適応させることが求められる。
llm.method: STL構文トークンと視覚特徴を双方向クロスアテンションで融合し、時間的ピラミッドで観測履歴を保持した上でフローマッチングモデルで計画を生成する。
llm.result: 5つのシミュレーション環境において、既存のTeLoGraFやVision-TL-Actionを上回るオープンループおよび閉ループの成功率を達成した。

2611.25589.tldr_en: GraF-VTA is presented, a graph-based framework that extends Vision-TL-Action with structured task representations, causal observation history, and closed-loop trajectory generation, and support combining structured visual conditioning with observation history and replanning to improve coverage of STL-satisfying trajectories.

2611.25587.title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation
2611.25587.abstract: Multimodal foundation models are advancing embodied navigation, but frequent inference incurs substantial computational cost. We present Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy. Retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback determine the cognitive horizon, or how many cached waypoints the robot executes before refreshing its prediction. At the policy's stop request, local visitation history guides a bounded correction with at most one extra movement and no additional model calls. CHAC reduces vision-language model calls by 33.4% on HM3D-OVON and 64.7% on R2R-CE, with success-rate decreases of 0.63 and 10.82 percentage points, respectively. Success rate and success weighted by path length improve per model call on both benchmarks. Across four physical navigation tasks with 40 runs per method, CHAC achieves 18 successes versus 14 for native execution, reducing model calls by 54.9% and GPU inference time by 49.7%.

llm.title_ja: 認知地平アクションチャンキング：身体化ナビゲーションのためのメモリガイド付き適応推論
llm.tldr_ja: CHACは、保持された視覚的コンテキストやコントローラーフィードバックに基づいてキャッシュされたウェイポイントの実行数を適応的に決定し、モデル呼び出し回数を削減するトレーニング不要のフレームワークである。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル基盤モデルによる身体化ナビゲーションは頻繁な推論による多大な計算コストを伴う。
llm.method: 視覚的コンテキスト、完了の手がかり、コントローラーのフィードバックから認知地平（キャッシュされたウェイポイントの実行数）を決定し、局所履歴で補正を行う。
llm.result: HM3D-OVONおよびR2R-CEにおいて、成功率の低下を抑えながらVLMの呼び出し回数をそれぞれ33.4%および64.7%削減した。
keywords_ja: 身体化ナビゲーション
アクションチャンキング

2611.25587.tldr_en: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking (CHAC), a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy, is presented, a training-free framework for memory-guided adaptive reasoning with a frozen navigation policy.

2611.25580.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash
2611.25580.abstract: Embodied agents are emerging as a promising paradigm for complex robotic tasks, leveraging Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and World Action Models (WAMs) to generate actions through Diffusion Transformer (DiT)-based iterative denoising. However, existing models often struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) environments. We observe that retrieving successful experiences and using them to warm-start denoising enables agents to better adapt to unfamiliar situations while reducing computational overhead. This creates a new opportunity to improve task accuracy and inference efficiency simultaneously, in contrast to conventional acceleration techniques that trade accuracy for computation. However, realizing this opportunity requires scaling experience banks, introducing substantial storage and search overhead that challenges the capacity, bandwidth, and power constraints of edge systems. We propose FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents. FlashX exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage. Proprioception-aware clustering further reduces search overhead and enables incremental experience acquisition without global reclustering. Evaluations across VLA and WAM workloads demonstrate up to 12.24\%p and 7.43\%p improvements in task success under dense and compute-efficient configurations, respectively. FlashX achieves 2.57$\times$ higher search throughput than the strongest prior NAND search architecture under pSLC sensing, with a further 9.7$\times$ search reduction through clustering. This delivers 1.29--3.95$\times$ end-to-end speedup and 1.12--2.34$\times$ energy efficiency improvement over SSD-based retrieval.

llm.title_ja: FlashX：CBAベースのNANDフラッシュを用いた身体化エージェント向けロボット経験再利用のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: FlashXは、CBAベースのNANDフラッシュアーキテクチャを活用して、精度と推論効率を同時に改善するスケーラブルな経験再利用システムである。
llm.problem: 身体化エージェントはOOD環境への一般化に苦戦し、経験の検索・保存にはエッジシステムのリソース制約という大きな課題がある。
llm.method: CBAの高帯域幅を活用した並列pSLCキー検索、インターリーブCompute-in-Flashエンジン、および固有受容を考慮したクラスタリングを導入する。
llm.result: VLAおよびWAMのワークロードにおいてタスク成功率を最大12.24ポイント改善し、従来比で2.57倍の検索スループットを達成した。
keywords_ja: ハードウェアアクセラレーション

2611.25580.tldr_en: This work proposes FlashX, a CMOS Directly Bonded to Array (CBA)-based NAND flash architecture for scalable experience reuse in embodied agents that exploits CBA's high internal bandwidth for parallel pSLC key search, employing interleaved Compute-in-Flash (CIF) engines to sustain sensing throughput while retaining dense TLC latent storage.

2611.25575.title: Trajectory-Calibrated Merging of Embodied Policies
2611.25575.abstract: Robot foundation models are increasingly adapted into task specialists to expand their embodied capabilities. Yet these capabilities remain fragmented across separate policies, and existing model-merging methods do not reliably preserve them during closed-loop execution: parameter-space alignment provides only an indirect proxy for behavior, while regression may fail to preserve behavior at states not covered by its calibration inputs. We present Trajectory-Calibrated Regression (TCR), an execution-aware, gradient-free framework that consolidates robot specialists into a single policy. Across two complementary timescales, TCR collects calibration inputs from expert rollouts spanning different stages of task execution and from intermediate states within iterative action generation. To account for representation shifts introduced by merging, TCR recomputes each block's input through the already merged blocks. It then uses each expert's computation within the block to form module inputs and fits merged weights to match the experts' linear outputs. A two-pass calibration procedure further refines the merged policy using separate rollout caches while retaining the frozen specialists as teachers. The resulting model preserves the original inference graph and requires neither expert routing nor additional gradient training. On LIBERO, TCR merges four $π_{0.5}$ specialists and achieves 77.83% success across 1,200 evaluation episodes, outperforming FeatCal, RegMean, and direct weight averaging by 9.50, 24.17, and 33.00 percentage points, respectively.

llm.title_ja: 身体化ポリシーの軌跡キャリブレーション型マージ
llm.tldr_ja: TCRは、専門家のロールアウトから収集したキャリブレーション入力とモジュール入力の再計算を用いて、複数のロボット専門家モデルを単一のポリシーに統合する実行アウェアなフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 複数のタスク専門家に適応されたロボット基盤モデルの機能は断片化されており、既存のマージ手法では閉ループ実行時の挙動を確実に保持できない。
llm.method: 専門家のロールアウトや中間状態からキャリブレーション入力を収集し、マージされたブロックを通じて各ブロックの入力を再計算して線形出力を一致させる。
llm.result: LIBEROにおいて4つのpi_0.5専門家をマージし、1,200のエピソード評価で77.83%の成功率を達成し既存手法を大きく上回った。

2611.25575.tldr_en: Trajectory-Calibrated Regression (TCR) is presented, an execution-aware, gradient-free framework that consolidates robot specialists into a single policy and requires neither expert routing nor additional gradient training.

2611.25558.title: Communication-Aware UAV Spatio-Temporal Relay Cooperation and Planning in Complex Urban Environments
2611.25558.abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly deployed in low-altitude urban airspace for delivery, emergency response, and other applications. However, UAV mobility across spatially heterogeneous urban communication environments can lead to time-varying communication outages, disrupting mission execution and compromising flight safety. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Spatio-Temporal Relay Cooperation and Planning (ST-RCP) framework that leverages delivery UAVs as opportunistic communication relays for disconnected UAVs without requiring additional communication infrastructure. The framework predicts communication blind-spot events over a finite planning horizon, constructs a helper-event compatibility graph, and jointly optimizes relay selection, obstacle-aware trajectory replanning, and communication-aware scheduling. Multiple planners are evaluated to investigate the trade-offs among communication coverage, computational cost, and energy consumption. Experiments based on real-world traffic scenarios compare the performance of ST-RCP against baseline methods. In the peak scenario, ST-RCP improves descent-phase communication coverage by 29.93% compared with the base-station baseline and by 27.38%, 22.02%, and 15.20% compared with configurations using one, two, and three dedicated relay UAVs, respectively. Process flexibility analysis demonstrates that predictive task-aware relaying expands the pool of feasible relay resources and improves communication continuity while maintaining the feasibility of delivery missions. These findings demonstrate the potential of trajectory-enabled UAV coordination to enhance the safety and resilience of urban aerial operations.

llm.title_ja: 通信を考慮した複雑な都市環境におけるUAV時空間中継協調と計画
llm.tldr_ja: ST-RCPは、配送用UAVを通信中継機として日和見的に活用することで時変の通信途絶に対処し、中継選択・軌跡再計画・通信スケジュールを共同最適化するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 都市環境におけるUAVの移動は時間変動する通信途絶を引き起こし、ミッション実行と飛行の安全性を損なう。
llm.method: 通信の死角イベントを予測し、ヘルパーイベント互換性グラフを構築して、中継選択、障害物を考慮した軌跡再計画、通信スケジュールを同時に最適化する。
llm.result: ピークシナリオにおいて、基地局ベースラインと比較して降下フェーズの通信カバレッジを29.93%改善した。

2611.25558.tldr_en: A Spatio-Temporal Relay Cooperation and Planning framework that leverages delivery UAVs as opportunistic communication relays for disconnected UAVs without requiring additional communication infrastructure is proposed.

2611.25553.title: TwoPass: Draft-Guided Few-Step Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation
2611.25553.abstract: Action-conditioned video prediction lets robots anticipate the visual consequences of their actions for planning and policy evaluation. Existing predictors denoise each future from noise without using their own estimate of it, which limits the quality of the predicted future, in particular of the manipulated objects, and requires many network calls. We present TwoPass, a self-conditioned training-and-inference framework that keeps the standard flow-matching objective. Self-Generated Draft Training supplies a detached clean-video estimate from the shared network as conditioning at the same noisy state. A Refinement-Only Late Adapter applies a dedicated residual transformation when a draft is present. At inference, Draft-Reuse Iterative Refinement obtains both a solver update and the next draft from each velocity prediction, requiring as few as 4 function evaluations (NFE) per video chunk. Training samples discrete solver-query noise levels and updates the pretrained backbone. Extensive experiments on Bridge and Language Table show that TwoPass achieves state-of-the-art results with 4 NFE, far fewer than the 50-59 calls of existing predictors. Code: https://github.com/PlantPotatoOnMoon/TwoPass.

llm.title_ja: TwoPass：ロボット操作のためのドラフト誘導型少数ステップビデオ予測
llm.tldr_ja: TwoPassは、自己生成されたドラフトを条件付けとして利用し、少数回の関数評価で高品質な将来のビデオ予測を実現する自己条件付けフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存の予測器は自身の推定を利用せずにノイズから将来をノイズ除去するため、品質が制限され、多くのネットワーク呼び出しが必要になる。
llm.method: 共有ネットワークからのクリーンビデオ推定をドラフトとして同じノイズ状態の条件付けに用いる自己生成ドラフトトレーニングと、洗練用のアダプターを導入する。
llm.result: BridgeおよびLanguage Tableでの実験において、わずか4回のNFEで既存手法と同等以上の最先端の結果を達成した。

2611.25553.tldr_en: TwoPass is presented, a self-conditioned training-and-inference framework that keeps the standard flow-matching objective and achieves state-of-the-art results with 4 NFE, far fewer than the 50-59 calls of existing predictors.

2611.25543.title: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds
2611.25543.abstract: Multimodal agents can now build interactive 3D worlds and games, yet these worlds, like those built by people, often contain glitches such as floating objects, walls that can be walked through, or objects that change when no one is looking. An automatic auditor could check such worlds at scale and provide rewards for agents that build them, but only if it is both accurate and cheap. Auditing requires three abilities, namely navigating to the objects that may contain a glitch, triggering glitches that appear only after a specific behavior, and recognizing what is wrong. Current auditors are either accurate but slow and expensive or cheap but unreliable. We study how much of the audit small models can take on. A 4B vision language model fine-tuned end to end on verified trajectories of a frontier teacher guided by Bayesian search learns to navigate and trigger, and six such explorers together match a frontier model on both, but recognition stays far behind. We therefore build an auditor in which a swarm of small explorers navigates and triggers, and a frontier model reviews what they record and report. On WorldAuditBench, our auditor succeeds on 55.9% of 213 tasks in Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js worlds, 13.6 points above the strongest auditor reported, at less than a quarter of its cost. It matches the frontier reviewer exploring on its own at 4.6 times lower cost and about half the latency. Without further training, it also answers embodied questions about real-world scans, matching the frontier reviewer exploring on its own and surpassing four other frontier models by 6.4 to 16.6 points.

llm.title_ja: 3Dワールドを監査するための効率的なマルチモーダルエージェント
llm.tldr_ja: 小型探索エージェントの群れがナビゲーションとトリガーを行い、フロンティアモデルがレビューを行うことで、低コストかつ高精度に3Dワールドの不具合を監査するシステムである。
llm.problem: インタラクティブな3Dワールドに含まれる不具合を自動監査する既存のエージェントは、正確だが遅くて高価であるか、安価だが信頼性が低いかのどちらかである。
llm.method: ベイジャン探索で訓練された小型ビジョン言語モデルの群れがナビゲーションや不具合の誘発を行い、フロンティアモデルがそれらをレビューする構成をとる。
llm.result: WorldAuditBenchにおいて213のタスク中55.9%で成功を収め、従来よりも低コストでフロンティアモデル単体に匹敵する性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダルエージェント

2611.25543.tldr_en: An auditor is built in which a swarm of small explorers navigates and triggers, and a frontier model reviews what they record and report, and matches the frontier reviewer exploring on its own at 4.6 times lower cost and about half the latency.

2611.25529.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach
2611.25529.abstract: Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do. We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy. The fine-tuned policy is then deployed on its own. On states where a World Action Model and a Vision-Language-Action model have stalled, naming the next step raises subgoal completion by 4.6x over the unchanged task instruction, and the frozen VLM supplies it from the same camera images the policy sees. After fine-tuning, unassisted success on long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, 9.8 points above fine-tuning on human demonstrations and 7.3 points above fine-tuning on self-collected successes at an equal data budget. With a coach that sees only camera images, it reaches 56.8%, above both baselines. The gain is obtained with the action backbone frozen: language coaching teaches the policy what should happen next, and the skills it already has do the rest.

llm.title_ja: CoachSI：言語コーチを用いたロボットポリシーの自己改善
llm.tldr_ja: CoachSIは、オフザコン的VLMを言語コーチとして用いてロボットの次のステップを指示し、成功した試行をリラベルしてポリシーを微調整することで長期的タスクの成功率を高める自己改善手法である。
llm.problem: 汎用ロボットポリシーは単一スキルはこなせるが、それらを長期的なタスクに合成すると失敗し、自身の経験のみからの自己改善では分布内にとどまってしまう。
llm.method: 凍結されたVLMがカメラ画像からロボットの次のステップを言語で指示し、成功したロールアウトをリラベルしてアクションバックボーンを固定したままポリシーを微調整する。
llm.result: 未知のシーンにおける長期的タスクでの未補助の成功率が47.4%から59.3%に向上し、人間デモによる微調整を9.8ポイント上回った。

2611.25529.tldr_en: CoachSI is presented, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action.

2611.25513.title: Mesh-Free Keypoint Learning for Category-Level 6D Object Pose Estimation
2611.25513.abstract: Category-level 6D pose estimation relates partial RGB-D observations of unseen instances to a canonical frame shared across a category. Object-aware reconstruction helps adaptive keypoints retain the geometry of the visible surface. Common reconstruction targets select observed points by their distance to a registered instance surface. We present MORSEPose, which derives this support directly from standard pose and metric-size annotations. We map observed 3D points to normalized object coordinates and retain those inside a tolerancedilated pose-and-size envelope. This construction is consistent across camera frames and metric scales. When the annotated extent bounds the object surface, the envelope conservatively contains the support of a conventional surface-distance selector. We integrate this target with multi-level RGB-D features, adaptive keypoints, and learnable category context. Experiments on REAL275 and HouseCat6D show that the envelope closely matches surface-based supervision at both point and task levels, remains stable under boundary perturbations and viewpoint changes, and supports competitive category-level pose accuracy across benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: カテゴリレベル6D物体姿勢推定のためのメッシュフリーキーポイント学習
llm.tldr_ja: MORSEPoseは、ポーズとメトリックサイズの注釈から直接サポートを導出し、マルチレベルRGB-D特徴と適応型キーポイントを統合してカテゴリレベルの6Dポーズ推定を行う手法である。
llm.problem: カテゴリレベルの6D姿勢推定において、一般的な再構築ターゲットは登録されたインスタンス表面までの距離に基づいて観測点を選択している。
llm.method: 観測された3D点を正規化オブジェクト座標にマッピングし、許容範囲のポーズ・サイズエンベロープ内にあるものを保持する。
llm.result: REAL275およびHouseCat6Dでの実験において、表面ベースの指導と同等の性能を維持しつつ、境界の摂動や視点の変化に対して安定した姿勢推定精度を示した。

2611.25513.tldr_en: MORSE-Pose, which derives this support directly from standard pose and metric-size annotations, is presented, which map observed 3D points to normalized object coordinates and retain those inside a tolerance-dilated pose-and-size envelope.

2611.25500.title: PRIO: Pre-trained Representation for Interactive Objects in 4D Worlds
2611.25500.abstract: 3D worlds can now be captured, reconstructed, and generated at scale, yet the objects in them stay still: a pressed pillow does not compress, and a pulled door does not swing. Bringing these objects into interactive 4D world models requires a representation of how they can move, deform, and respond physically to user actions in real time. We present PRIO, a pre-trained representation for interactive objects. Given static geometry, PRIO predicts an object-specific configuration space in a single forward pass. This space provides generalized coordinates for Lagrangian mechanics, allowing physical laws and user actions to govern motion. Configurations are linear in these coordinates, allowing the quantities needed by the dynamics to be precomputed. Dynamics then run at interactive rates without further network inference. Pre-trained on diverse 4D trajectories, PRIO learns priors over object configurations that generalize to unseen shapes. It supports meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians, bringing objects in reconstructed and generated scenes into interaction. We demonstrate its use in real-to-sim workflows and robot manipulation. In addition, compared with existing 4D generation methods, PRIO generates dynamics faster and follows user actions more faithfully.

llm.title_ja: PRIO：4Dワールド内のインタラクティブオブジェクトのための事前学習済み表現
llm.tldr_ja: PRIOは、単一のフォワードパスでオブジェクト固有の構成空間を予測し、ラグランジュ力学に基づくリアルタイムの物理的インタラクションを実現する事前学習済み表現である。
llm.problem: 3Dワールド内のオブジェクトは静止したままであり、ユーザーの操作に対して物理的に応答させるための動的表現が欠けている。
llm.method: 静的ジオメトリからオブジェクト固有の構成空間を予測し、構成が座標に対して線形である性質を利用して動力学を事前計算する。
llm.result: 多様な4D軌跡で事前学習され、未知の形状へ一般化しつつ、既存手法よりも高速かつ忠実に動力学を生成できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: インタラクティブオブジェクト
物理シミュレーション

2611.25500.tldr_en: Compared with existing 4D generation methods, PRIO generates dynamics faster and follows user actions more faithfully, and is demonstrated in real-to-sim workflows and robot manipulation.

2611.25480.title: Learning Ankle Exoskeleton Control for Reactive Standing Balance Through Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation
2611.25480.abstract: Deficits in reactive balance can increase fall risk among older adults and individuals with neuromuscular impairments, motivating the need for interventions that improve balance recovery. Wearable robotic exoskeletons offer a promising approach to addressing this need by augmenting balance control. However, developing controllers that deliver appropriately timed and scaled assistance remains challenging, as evaluating each candidate strategy requires repeated exposure to destabilizing perturbations. We propose a simulation-to-real framework that combines motion imitation and reinforcement learning to develop balance-assistive ankle exoskeleton control. A muscle-driven neuromusculoskeletal model was trained using a small set of motion-capture data from a single subject to reproduce kinematic and kinetic responses to backward-translation perturbations. This model served as a virtual human for training a reinforcement-learning exoskeleton controller. The resulting controller generated bilateral ankle assistance using only inertial sensor measurements, without explicit perturbation detection. We implemented the controller on-board a bilateral ankle exoskeleton and evaluated it in five healthy subjects whose data were not used for training. Assistance increased the perturbation magnitude that subjects could withstand without stepping by 11.8% and reduced peak center-of-mass displacement and velocity by 13.5% and 28.2%, respectively. Individual benefits varied with baseline recovery strategy and body mass. These results indicate that a single virtual human can yield transferable balance assistance, and that more diverse virtual humans could further improve its effectiveness.

llm.title_ja: 神経筋骨格シミュレーションを通じたリアクティブ起立バランスのための足首外骨格制御の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 単一被験者のモーションキャプチャデータから構築した神経筋骨格モデルを仮想人間として強化学習を行い、外乱に対する足首外骨格のバランス補助制御を開発した。
llm.problem: 適切なタイミングと規模の補助を行う外骨格コントローラの開発には、外乱への繰り返し曝露が必要であり困難である。
llm.method: モーション模倣と強化学習を組み合わせ、神経筋骨格シミュレーションを活用したシミュレーション・ツー・リアル（Sim2Real）のフレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 被験者がステップを踏まずに耐えられる外乱の大きさが11.8%増加し、質量中心の変位と速度のピークがそれぞれ13.5%および28.2%減少した。
llm.limitation: 個人の利益はベースラインの回復戦略や体重によって異なり、より多様な仮想人間モデルがさらなる改善をもたらす可能性がある。

2611.25480.tldr_en: A simulation-to-real framework that combines motion imitation and reinforcement learning to develop balance-assistive ankle exoskeleton control is proposed and results indicate that a single virtual human can yield transferable balance assistance, and that more diverse virtual humans could further improve its effectiveness.

2611.25474.title: TuringPAI: A Foundation for On-Device Physical AI
2611.25474.abstract: Physical AI requires models that understand spatial relationships and dynamic environments and translate observations into actions under limited onboard compute. We present TuringPAI, a family of models for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation. TuringPAI-VL is a 0.65B model built on HybridViT-MLQ, which combines convolutional local aggregation with Transformer-based global modeling. Multi-scale Latent Queries integrate spatial features and observation history within the same visual Transformer, providing a compact, structured interface to the language model. Training combines general vision-language data with geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision. TuringPAI-VL supports general multimodal understanding and improves quantitative geometric perception over Qwen2-VL-2B, while providing a shared initialization for the two downstream VLA models. For autonomous driving, TuringPAI-Drive maintains all evaluated ADE/FDE metrics within 1.2\% of a full-token HybridViT baseline using the MLQ interface and achieves comparable aggregate scores in an in-house simulation evaluation. Using XPeng Native Runtime (XNRT) on a single NVIDIA Orin-X SoC, TuringPAI-Drive generates trajectories at 12\,Hz in on-vehicle operation. For robotic manipulation, TuringPAI-Embodied achieves a 96.8\% average success rate across the four LIBERO suites. These results demonstrate a shared vision-language foundation for driving and robotic manipulation under practical on-device constraints.

llm.title_ja: TuringPAI：オンデバイス物理AIのための基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 空間関係と動的環境を理解し限られた車載計算量で行動に翻訳するオンデバイス物理AI向けモデルファミリ、TuringPAIを提案する。
llm.problem: 物理AIには空間関係や動的環境の理解が必要だが、限られた車載計算量の下で観測を行動に翻訳することが課題となっている。
llm.method: HybridViT-MLQをベースにした視覚言語モデルTuringPAI-VLと、自動運転向けのDrive、ロボット操作向けのEmbodiedからなるモデルファミリを構築した。
llm.result: TuringPAI-Driveは単一のNvidia Orin-X上で12Hzで軌道を生成し、TuringPAI-EmbodiedはLIBEROスイートで96.8%の平均成功率を達成した。

2611.25474.tldr_en: TuringPAI, a family of models for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation are presented.

2611.25469.title: A Wolf in Sheep's Pixels: Visual Camouflage Attacks via HDR Gain Maps
2611.25469.abstract: An image can pass automated safety checks while showing harmful content to its human viewer. We introduce DRJanus, a visual camouflage attack that exploits the gap between standard dynamic range (SDR) processing and high dynamic range (HDR) display. Automated systems often read only an image's SDR base, whereas HDR viewers reconstruct its appearance using an auxiliary gain map. DRJanus inverts this reconstruction to embed two independently chosen color images in a single JPEG, without querying or optimizing against the target model. It preserves the chosen SDR base exactly and reconstructs HDR targets at an average PSNR of 43.03 dB across 400 images. On a benchmark of 100 sexual-content images, DRJanus evades detection by all six tested commercial moderation services and nine vision-language models. Across five agents, each evaluated on 120 task cases per threat setting, attack success ranges from 31.67% to 100% for moderation evasion and from 95% to 100% for task manipulation. We also explore cross-view consistency checks as a mitigation. These findings expose a gap in visual trust: securing what a machine reads does not secure what a user sees. A demo is available at https://qshen0629.github.io/DRJanus/

llm.title_ja: 羊のピクセルを着た狼：HDRゲインマップを用いた視覚的迷彩攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: 標準ダイナミックレンジと高ダイナミックレンジ表示のギャップを利用し、自動安全チェックをすり抜けて人間には有害コンテンツを見せる視覚的迷彩攻撃を提案する。
llm.problem: 自動化されたシステムは画像の標準ダイナミックレンジベースのみを読み取るため、人間の閲覧者に有害なコンテンツを示しつつ安全チェックを通過させることが可能になる。
llm.method: 再構成を反転させて2つの独立したカラー画像を1つのJPEGに埋め込み、SDRベースを正確に保ちながらHDRターゲットを再構成するDRJanusを導入した。
llm.result: すべての商用モデレーションサービスおよび視覚言語モデルの検出を回避し、タスク操作において95%から100%の攻撃成功率を達成した。

2611.25469.tldr_en: DRJanus is introduced, a visual camouflage attack that exploits the gap between standard dynamic range (SDR) processing and high dynamic range (HDR) display and exposes a gap in visual trust: securing what a machine reads does not secure what a user sees.

2611.25462.title: Demonstration-Free Skill Composition for Navigation and Manipulation
2611.25462.abstract: Hierarchical reinforcement learning enables sequential tasks to be represented as compositions of separately trained skills. This paper evaluates demonstration-free hierarchical pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation, comparing their training requirements and task performance with flat reinforcement learning baselines. The evaluation concerns complete pipelines with task-specific observation, reward and control structures. In navigation, two parameterised skills are reused across unseen FourRooms layouts under manually specified high-level plans. In manipulation, reaching, grasp alignment and lifting are trained separately, with downstream skills initialised from states collected during predecessor rollouts. Across unseen navigation layouts, the hierarchical pipeline substantially outperforms the evaluated flat DQN baselines while requiring fewer training interactions. In manipulation, the hierarchical chain requires fewer training steps than flat SAC and exhibits lower observed variation across seeds. The frozen Pick and Lift skills are further reused for stacking by training an additional Place skill.
2611.25462.comment: 10 pages. Accepted at the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA 2026). Project page: https://madeleinenouri.github.io/acra-skill-composition

llm.title_ja: ナビゲーションとマニピュレーションのためのデモ不要なスキル合成
llm.tldr_ja: 階層型強化学習を用いて、手動指定の計画や事前訓練されたスキルを組み合わせることで、フラットな強化学習ベースラインよりも優れた性能を達成する。
llm.problem: 複雑なタスクを連続的に表現するためには個別に訓練されたスキルを効果的に組み合わせる必要があるが、そのための効果的な学習パイプラインの評価が求められている。
llm.method: ナビゲーション向けにパラメータ化されたスキルを再利用し、マニピュレーション向けに到達・把持・持ち上げを個別に訓練して接続するデモンストレーション不要の階層型パイプラインを評価した。
llm.result: 未知のナビゲーションレイアウトにおいて、より少ない学習インタラクションでフラットなDQNベースラインを大きく上回る性能を示した。

2611.25462.tldr_en: Evaluating demonstration-free hierarchical pipelines for MiniGrid navigation and robotic manipulation, comparing their training requirements and task performance with flat reinforcement learning baselines finds the hierarchical pipeline substantially outperforms the evaluated flat DQN baselines while requiring fewer training interactions.

2611.25461.title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action
2611.25461.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in real-world long-horizon manipulation, where memory plays a crucial role. However, existing memory-augmented VLAs either retrieve past observations without reasoning about what they imply, or reason over the full history in a shared context where it crowds out current perception. Cognitive science treats them as distinct systems: memory reconstructs past experience to decide what to do, while perception guides how to act. We therefore propose ActMem, an in-context memory framework that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone. Built on a vision-language model with native video understanding, ActMem infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT), which conditions a flow-matching action expert. Perception Attention further lets the expert attend directly to the current view. To keep inference fast under long histories, Efficient Memory CoT Inference reuses computation across consecutive decisions without changing the output. ActMem achieves 71.1% task success and 80.8% completion success on RoboMemArena, surpassing the strongest baseline by 7.5 and 8.7 percentage points, and 73.8% average success on MIKASA-Robo, the best among all compared methods. In the real world, it reaches 68.8% average success on exogenous, endogenous, and traceless memory tasks, 10.0 percentage points above the strongest memory-augmented VLA. Code and checkpoints will be released at https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem and https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem.
2611.25461.comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, 6 tables. Code and checkpoints: https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem

llm.title_ja: ActMem：潜在的メモリ推論からグラウンデッドなロボット行動へ
llm.tldr_ja: メモリ推論と知覚的グラウンディングを単一のビジョン言語バックボーン内で分離するコンテキスト内メモリフレームワークActMemを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のメモリ拡張VLAは過去の観測を推論なしで取得するか、共有コンテキスト内で全履歴を推論して現在の知覚を圧迫するという課題がある。
llm.method: タイムスタンプ付きのインタラクション履歴から現在のサブタスクを推論し、推論時に形成された隠れ状態を潜在的メモリ思考連鎖として保持して行動専門家に条件付けを行う。
llm.result: RoboMemArenaで71.1%のタスク成功率を達成し、最強のベースラインを7.5ポイント上回り、実世界でも平均68.8%の成功率を記録した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.25461.tldr_en: This work proposes ActMem, an in-context memory framework that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone and infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT).

2611.25460.title: LoongForge-Embodied: A Unified Framework for Training Heterogeneous Embodied Models
2611.25460.abstract: Training Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World-Action Models (WAMs) is computationally expensive, while their heterogeneous architectures and fragmented training stacks make system optimizations difficult to reuse across models. To address these challenges, we present LoongForge-Embodied, a native-PyTorch framework that unifies and accelerates the training of heterogeneous embodied models. At its core, LoongForge-Embodied introduces a common abstraction layer that decouples model-specific implementations from shared training infrastructure, enabling cross-model reuse without constraining individual architectures or execution requirements. Buildingon this unified infrastructure, the framework combines reusable acceleration mechanisms with model-specific and hardware-aware optimization strategies across computation, execution, memory, data I/O, and distributed communication, including FP8-based communication optimizations for DDP and FSDP. Beyond training acceleration, LoongForge-Embodied integrates a unified data infrastructure with a pipeline for synthesizing robot data from egocentric data, and an efficient evaluation framework that supports concurrency and optimized computation in simulator. Experiments across representative VLA and WAM models demonstrate 1.47x-4.38x end-to-end training throughput improvements over their corresponding open-source baselines, as well as 4.1x-23.2x faster evaluation under the same protocols.

llm.title_ja: LoongForge-Embodied：異種embodiedモデル訓練のための統一フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 異種embodiedモデルの訓練を統一し加速するネイティブPyTorchフレームワークLoongForge-Embodiedを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルや世界行動モデルの訓練は計算コストが高く、アーキテクチャが異なり訓練スタックが断片化しているためシステム最適化の再利用が困難である。
llm.method: モデル固有の実装を共有訓練インフラから切り離す共通抽象化層を導入し、計算・実行・メモリ・データI/O・分散通信にわたる最適化戦略を統合した。
llm.result: 代表的なVLAおよびWAMモデルにおいて、オープンソースのベースラインと比較して1.47倍から4.38倍のエンドツーエンド訓練スループットの向上を実現した。

2611.25460.tldr_en: LoongForge-Embodied is presented, a native-PyTorch framework that unifies and accelerates the training of heterogeneous embodied models and introduces a common abstraction layer that decouples model-specific implementations from shared training infrastructure, enabling cross-model reuse without constraining individual architectures or execution requirements.

2611.25445.title: Stereo Visual Odometry with In-the-Loop Geometric Feed-Forward Models Towards Dense Metric Mapping
2611.25445.abstract: We present a stereo visual odometry (SVO) framework that integrates geometric feed-forward models (GFMs) for dense depth prediction with factor-graph-based visual odometry to achieve accurate localisation and dense metric mapping. Our key idea is to exploit sparse but reliable metric geometry estimated from stereo and temporal multi-view observations to calibrate dense GFM predictions, while retaining the robustness and efficiency of model-based SVO. Rather than directly conditioning the GFM on potentially noisy stereo depth, optimised 3D landmarks are used to jointly estimate a scale-shift transformation over all keyframes within each local submap, yielding metrically consistent dense depth predictions. To balance accuracy and computational efficiency, we introduce a hierarchical factor-graph architecture. At the local level, sliding-window optimisation estimates high-frequency camera poses and multi-view-refined 3D landmarks. Dense predictions are generated only for selected keyframes and registered within each submap using SE(3) Generalised ICP. Consecutive submaps are further aligned in Sim(3) using their shared geometry, allowing residual scale inconsistencies to be corrected. These intra- and inter-submap constraints are incorporated into a global factor graph to produce a consistent trajectory and dense metric reconstruction. Extensive experiments on public and in-house datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive odometry accuracy against geometric and learning-based baselines while providing accurate dense metric reconstruction and improved robustness to failures in learned depth prediction.

llm.title_ja: 高密度な高精度マッピングに向けたインザループ幾何学的フィードフォワードモデルを持つステレオ視覚オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 高精度な位置合わせと高密度なメトリックマッピングを実現するため、高密度深度予測のための幾何学的フィードフォワードモデルを統合したステレオ視覚オドメトリフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ステレオおよび時間的マルチビュー観測から得られる信頼性の高いスパースな幾何学を利用して、学習ベースの深度予測の失敗に対する堅牢性を高める必要がある。
llm.method: 幾何学的フィードフォワードモデルとファクターグラフベースの視覚オドメトリを統合し、最適化された3Dランドマークを用いて全キーフレーム間のスケール・シフト変換を共同推定する。
llm.result: 公開データセットおよび自社データセットの実験において、幾何学的および学習ベースのベースラインと同等のオドメトリ精度を達成しつつ、正確な高密度メトリック再構成を実現した。
keywords_ja: ステレオ視覚オドメトリ

2611.25445.tldr_en: A stereo visual odometry framework that integrates geometric feed-forward models (GFMs) for dense depth prediction with factor-graph-based visual odometry to achieve accurate localisation and dense metric mapping and introduces a hierarchical factor-graph architecture.

2611.25417.title: MIR-Depth: Multi-Range Refinement for Single-View RGB-D Depth Completion of Transparent Objects
2611.25417.abstract: Recovering accurate visible-surface depth from a single RGB-D image and an object mask is essential for robotic grasping and manipulation of transparent objects. Specular reflections cause missing depth, while refraction corrupts nonzero returns with background depth, making raw measurements unreliable as surface anchors. Under a fixed sampling budget, refining an initial single-view prediction within a single search interval either misses large refraction offsets or sacrifices fine local resolution. To resolve this single-view trade-off, MIR-Depth constructs Coordinate-Aware Multi-Range Hypotheses: a 3D-aggregated global inverse-depth volume and depth-axis-filtered pixel-wise local volumes around a prior-guided initial depth. Selective Recurrent Refinement then introduces out-of-bounds lookup masking and validity-masked softmax fusion to iteratively update inverse depth from these volumes using a multi-scale ConvGRU. Finally, Spatially Gated Correction applies a learned per-pixel spatial gate to the full-resolution residual, preserving accurate initial geometry without imposing raw sensor readings as hard constraints. Experiments on TransCG, TODD, TRansPose, ClearPose, and HouseCat6D show that MIR-Depth achieves lower error than ReMake, DFNet, BP-Net, and PSD. Real-robot evaluations confirm accurate surface geometry for 6-DoF grasp pose prediction. Code and pretrained models will be publicly available.

llm.title_ja: MIR-Depth：透明物体単一視点RGB-D深度補完のためのマルチレンジ改良
llm.tldr_ja: 鏡面反射や屈折による深度の欠損や破損を解決するため、座標を考慮したマルチレンジ仮説と選択的再帰的改良を用いるMIR-Depthを提案する。
llm.problem: 透明物体の把持や操作において、鏡面反射や屈折により生じる未計測や背景深度による破損が表面アンカーとしての測定を信頼性のないものにしている。
llm.method: 3D集約大域的逆深度ボリュームと画素ごとの局所ボリュームを構築し、マルチスケールConvGRUを用いて逆深度を反復的に更新する選択的再帰的改良を導入した。
llm.result: TransCG等のデータセットにおいて既存手法よりも低い誤差を達成し、実機ロボット評価により6自由度把持姿勢予測のための正確な表面形状を確認した。

2611.25417.tldr_en: Experiments show that MIR-Depth achieves lower error than ReMake, DFNet, BP-Net, BP-Net, and PSD, and real-robot evaluations confirm accurate surface geometry for 6-DoF grasp pose prediction.

2611.25415.title: Stuck in Place: Stall Diagnosis and Remedies for JEPA Planners
2611.25415.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models plan from pixels with model predictive control, yet often fail on tasks their model should handle. Test-time adaptation attributes such failures to model error under distribution shift and updates the weights on the current episode, without checking this attribution against the planning loop itself. We follow the executed planning loop on pushing tasks. In most settings, with and without distribution shift, nearly all failures (at least 96%) are stalls, where the object stays in place while the model predicts progress. The warm-started gradient-descent (GD) planner then returns nearly the same plan, a fixed point where the agent mostly idles. We propose Unstick, which pairs on-policy fine-tuning before deployment with a fixed-weight loop breaker: a residual memory of the episode's prediction errors or random re-initialization at every replan. With GD, Unstick recovers most of the adaptation gain on pushing tasks with the memory, and with re-initialization most of it on shape shifts but much less on visual shifts. A large part of what limits these planners under GD is thus a fixed point of the planning loop, present with and without distribution shift, which a planner with fixed weights can break. Code is available at https://github.com/jhlee0619/unstick.

llm.title_ja: その場でのスタック：JEPAプランナーのためのストール診断と対策
llm.tldr_ja: JEPA世界モデルのプランナーがプッシュタスクで進行を予測しながら実際には物体が静止してしまう「ストール」現象を分析し、対策手法Unstickを提案する。
llm.problem: JEPA世界モデルはピクセルからモデル予測制御で計画を行うが、モデルが進捗を予測しているにもかかわらず物体が動かない失敗（ストール）が多く発生する。
llm.method: 勾配降下法プランナーにおける固定点を回避するため、展開前のオンポリシー微調整と、予測誤差の残差メモリや再初期化を組み合わせたUnstickを提案する。
llm.result: Unstickにより、メモリを用いることでプッシュタスクにおける適応ゲインの大部分を回復し、固定重みでもプランナーの固定点を打破できることを示した。

2611.25415.tldr_en: Unstick is proposed, which pairs on-policy fine-tuning before deployment with a fixed-weight loop breaker: a residual memory of the episode's prediction errors or random re-initialization at every replan.

2611.25413.title: WAMotor: Accelerating World Action Models via Speculative Inference under Dual Nonuniform Denoising Dynamics
2611.25413.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) unify world modeling and action generation for robotic control by integrating flow-matching velocities, yet suffer from high multi-step denoising latency. Recent studies have explored speculative inference to accelerate WAMs by drafting and verifying denoising steps in parallel. However, existing methods either require training task-specific draft models or overlook critical WAM denoising dynamics when reusing past velocities as drafts. We revisit the denoising dynamics of WAMs and identify a dual nonuniformity that breaks standard velocity-reuse assumptions: velocity smoothness is nonuniform as adjacent velocity residuals differ sharply at early and final steps, so reuse there yields large residuals, which nonuniform integration time steps further translate into local state errors that accumulate into the final action distribution. Accordingly, we formalize this by theoretically deriving a trajectory error tolerance bound that characterizes how velocity residuals and integration time steps affect the final action distribution. Based on this, we propose WAMotor, the first speculative inference method tailored to the dual nonuniformity in WAMs. It selects reliable anchor velocities by deferring speculation and employs time-step-aware verification that scales acceptance thresholds by integration time step size. WAMotor offers plug-and-play benefits, enabling seamless integration with prior WAMs. Extensive evaluations on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and LIBERO-Plus show that WAMotor achieves 2.86$\times$--4.28$\times$ end-to-end speedups while maintaining task success rates. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Overdue-Lin/WAMotor

llm.title_ja: WAMotor：二重非一様デノイジング動態下での推測推論による世界行動モデルの加速
llm.tldr_ja: 世界行動モデル（WAM）におけるマルチステップ・デノイジングのレイテンシを削減するため、二重非一様性に特化した初の推測推論手法WAMotorを提案する。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルはフローマッチング速度を統合してロボット制御を行うが、多段階のデノイジング遅延が大きいという課題がある。
llm.method: 速度の非一様平滑性に着目した理論的な軌道誤差許容境界を導出し、推測を遅らせて信頼できるアンカー速度を選択するタイムステップ認識検証を行うWAMotorを開発した。
llm.result: LIBERO等の評価において、タスク成功率を維持しながら2.86倍から4.28倍のエンドツーエンドの高速化を達成した。

2611.25413.tldr_en: This work revisits the denoising dynamics of WAMs and identifies a dual nonuniformity that breaks standard velocity-reuse assumptions, and proposes WAMotor, the first speculative inference method tailored to the dual nonuniformity in WAMs.

2611.25400.title: Dune: A Zeroth-Order Optimizer with Time-Conditioned Historical Error Regression for VLA Test-Time Adaptation
2611.25400.abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) enables Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to handle distribution shifts during deployment without source-domain retraining. However, backpropagation-based adaptation incurs heavy memory overhead on resource-constrained robots, whereas zeroth-order (ZO) methods suffer from high estimation variance under limited perturbation budgets. We observe that while ZO estimation enables low-memory adaptation with rapid initial gains, it often stalls or degrades over long-horizon updates due to noisy gradient estimates. To address these limitations, we propose Dune, a zeroth-order optimizer that stabilizes long-horizon adaptation by coupling online historical error prediction with current perturbation observations. Specifically, Dune learns a lightweight, time-conditioned error predictor from past optimization dynamics and fuses its predictions with instantaneous ZO estimates, achieving effective variance reduction without backpropagation or extra forward passes. Additionally, we theoretically characterize how estimation variance restricts convergence in high-dimensional, small-population regimes, motivating the use of historical statistics. Extensive experiments on LIBERO and real-world robots demonstrate that Dune achieves superior success rates under a low memory footprint, with ablations confirming improved closed-loop stability and post-disturbance recovery.

llm.title_ja: Dune：VLAテスト時適応のための時間条件付き履歴誤差回帰を持つゼロ次オプティマイザ
llm.tldr_ja: 限られた計算資源下でのVLAモデルのテスト時適応における分散を軽減するため、履歴誤差予測を組み合わせたゼロ次オプティマイザDuneを提案する。
llm.problem: 逆伝播ベースの適応は計算資源の限られたロボットで大きなメモリオーバーヘッドを発生させ、ゼロ次法は限られた摂動予算の下で高い推定分散に苦しむ。
llm.method: 過去の最適化ダイナミクスから軽量な時間条件付き誤差予測器を学習し、インスタントなゼロ次推定値と融合させることで逆伝播なしでの分散削減を実現した。
llm.result: LIBEROおよび実機ロボットの実験において、低いメモリフットワークで優れた成功率を達成し、閉ループ安定性と外乱からの回復力の向上が確認された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.25400.tldr_en: Dune is proposed, a zeroth-order optimizer that stabilizes long-horizon adaptation by coupling online historical error prediction with current perturbation observations and fuses its predictions with instantaneous ZO estimates, achieving effective variance reduction without backpropagation or extra forward passes.

2611.25398.title: RefreshGrad: An Online Adaptive Data-sampling Method for Diffusion-based Visuomotor Learning
2611.25398.abstract: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies from demonstrations typically samples trajectory segments uniformly or relies on static offline data curation before training. However, we find that demonstration data vary sharply in supervision value across temporal windows, and that each window's value to the policy evolves substantially during training rather than being fixed or captured by raw loss alone. Motivated by this finding, we propose RefreshGrad, an online adaptive data-sampling framework that periodically scores temporal windows from the evolving policy using five policy-native signals and dynamically adjusts their sampling weights during training. RefreshGrad focuses optimization on informative, learnable windows without altering the policy architecture, training objective, or inference cost. Across ten LIBERO-Plus manipulation tasks, RefreshGrad boosts average success from 60.7% (Uniform) and 68.2% (FAKTUAL) to 76.1% under visual perturbations, and from 57.4% and 73.3% to 81.3% in clean scenes.

llm.title_ja: RefreshGrad：拡散ベースの視覚運動学習のためのオンライン適応型データサンプリング手法
llm.tldr_ja: 学習中に時間的ウィンドウの価値が変化することに着目し、5つのポリシーネイティブな信号を用いてサンプリング重みを動的に調整するRefreshGradを提案する。
llm.problem: デモンストレーションからのVLAポリシーの訓練は一様なサンプリングや静的なオフラインデータキュレーションに依存しているが、データの監督価値は訓練中に進化する。
llm.method: 進化するポリシーから時間的ウィンドウのスコアを定期的に評価し、アーキテクチャや推論コストを変更することなく学習時のサンプリング重みを動的に調整するフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 10個のLIBERO-Plusタスクにおいて、視覚的外乱下での平均成功率を従来の均一サンプリングの60.7%から76.1%へと向上させた。

2611.25398.tldr_en: RefreshGrad, an online adaptive data-sampling framework that periodically scores temporal windows from the evolving policy using five policy-native signals and dynamically adjusts their sampling weights during training, is proposed.

2611.25373.title: Differentiable Hydrodynamics for Whole-Body MPC of Underwater Robots
2611.25373.abstract: Underwater vehicle-manipulator systems distribute actuation across thrusters and joint motors. Whole-body model predictive control (MPC), rather than separate vehicle and arm controllers, can coordinate both to extend the workspace and exploit the system's full kinematic capability. Doing so, however, requires a hydrodynamic model and derivatives throughout the prediction horizon. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) captures geometry-dependent forces and moments for such a model, but is too expensive to evaluate online. We present a differentiable analytical hydrodynamic model combining smooth spherical-harmonic force and moment fields with a coupled added-inertia matrix identified from CFD. It compactly represents velocity and acceleration-dependent loads and provides their derivatives in closed form. These derivatives are propagated through free-floating vehicle--manipulator dynamics for whole-body trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control, jointly optimizing thruster forces and joint torques for reaching and continuous tracking. Held-out CFD tests validate the principal translational-force and rotational-moment fields and the added-inertia response. The analytical Jacobians evaluate faster and avoid the step-size sensitivity of central finite differences. Closed-loop Stonefish experiments demonstrate whole-body MPC in an independent marine simulator. By making geometry-dependent hydrodynamics directly available to gradient-based control, the model incorporates water forces and their sensitivities into motion allocation between the vehicle and arm, rather than treating them only as disturbances.

llm.title_ja: 水中ロボットの全身MPCのための微分可能流体力学
llm.tldr_ja: 水中車両・マニピュレータシステムの協調制御を行うため、CFDから特定された追加慣性マトリクスと球面調和関数を組み合わせた微分可能解析的流体力学モデルを提案する。
llm.problem: 計算流体力学（CFD）は正確な力を捉えることができるが、オンライン評価にはコストが高すぎるため、予測ホライゾン全体にわたる微分可能な流体モデルが必要である。
llm.method: スムーズな球面調和力・モーメント場と追加慣性マトリクスを組み合わせた微分可能解析的流体力学モデルを構築し、全身軌道最適化とモデル予測制御（MPC）に組み込んだ。
llm.result: Stonefishを用いた閉ループ実験により、水中の力を外乱としてではなく勾配ベースの制御に直接取り入れ、車両とアーム間のモーション割り当てを実現できることを示した。

2611.25371.title: A Unified Framework for Image Manipulation Localization Under Multi-Type Weak Supervision
2611.25371.abstract: Existing weakly supervised image manipulation localization (IML) methods typically rely on annotation-specific training strategies, hindering the joint use of diverse annotations within a single model. This limits the scale of usable training data and constrains further progress. We propose UniIML, a teacher-student framework that maps diverse weak annotations into a unified representation to guide the Segment Anything Model (SAM) in generating multiple candidate masks. However, SAM is designed for general-purpose segmentation and has limited sensitivity to manipulation traces; its predicted quality scores alone may therefore fail to reliably identify the candidate that best delineates the manipulated region. We introduce Ordinal Safe Consensus (OSC), which first filters candidates using trusted weak-annotation constraints encoded in the unified representation. It then ranks the remaining candidates separately by consistency with weak annotations, SAM-predicted quality scores, and cross-view stability, aggregating these rankings for an initial selection. To assess how changes in the evaluation criteria affect candidate selection, OSC repeats ranking and selection while omitting one criterion at a time. The most frequently selected candidate is adopted as the final mask, and its relative selection frequency quantifies selection stability. We construct soft pseudo-labels from the selected candidate's predicted probabilities and estimate pixel-level supervision weights based on selection stability, pixel-level agreement among candidates, and predictive certainty. The student receives direct supervision in regions defined by weak annotations and learns from soft pseudo-labels elsewhere through reliability-weighted distillation, enabling unified training across weak annotation types. Experiments show that UniIML achieves superior average performance compared with state-of-the-art IML methods.

llm.title_ja: マルチタイプ弱教師あり学習に基づく画像操作局所化のための統合フレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な弱アノテーションを統合表現にマッピングし、Segment Anything Modelをガイドして複数の候補マスクを生成する教師・生徒フレームワークUniIMLを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の弱教師あり画像操作局所化手法は特定の注釈戦略に依存しており、単一モデル内で多様な注釈を共同利用することが妨げられている。
llm.method: 多様な弱注釈を統合表現にマッピングしてSAMをガイドし、順序付き安全コンソーシアム（OSC）を用いて信頼性に基づく擬似ラベルとピクセルレベルの監督重みを推定する。
llm.result: 要旨に記載なし
keywords_ja: コンピュータビジョン

2611.25371.tldr_en: The UniIML framework is proposed, a teacher-student framework that maps diverse weak annotations into a unified representation to guide the Segment Anything Model in generating multiple candidate masks, and achieves superior average performance compared with state-of-the-art IML methods.

2611.25366.title: Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies: Spatializing Latent Action Representations for Goal-Pose-Free Mobile Manipulation
2611.25366.abstract: The success of manipulation policies is closely tied to the spatial relationship between the robot and the target object, as well as the task being performed, making the ability to adjust the robot's pose critical for successful execution. When the robot starts away from the task, such adjustments require coordinating navigation with local manipulation. Jointly training these capabilities incurs substantial computational and data costs, while navigating toward a predefined goal pose limits the flexibility needed to adapt to task-specific manipulation requirements. To address these challenges, we propose Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies (M4M), a framework that learns manipulation-aware mobility directly from pretrained manipulation policies. By leveraging the hidden representations of the policy's action-generating network as dense supervision, together with a limited number of manipulation execution outcomes, we learn a spatially conditioned embedding that captures task-dependent manipulation success across candidate robot poses. From the robot's current stereo observations, this representation estimates manipulation success at unvisited poses without rolling out the manipulation policy at each location. It is further integrated into navigation policy training, while a learned handoff policy decides when to transition from navigation to manipulation, enabling the robot to move and manipulate in a unified, task-aware manner. Across eight articulated-object tasks in unseen RoboCasa kitchens, M4M achieves 47.0% mean task success, compared with 26.5% for the strongest baseline and 19.2% for direct manipulation execution, and refrigerator-closing experiments show consistent improvements across four frozen manipulation policies.

llm.title_ja: 移動と操作のポリシーからの学習：ゴールポーズフリーな移動マニピュレーションのための潜在的行動表現の空間化
llm.tldr_ja: 事前訓練されたマニピュレーションポリシーの隠れ表現を活用し、ロボットの姿勢に応じたタスク成功率を推定するM4Mフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 移動と局所的マニピュレーションの協調には多大な計算・データコストがかかり、事前定義されたゴールポーズへの移動は柔軟性を制限する。
llm.method: マニピュレーションポリシーの行動生成ネットワークの隠れ表現を密な監督として利用し、候補となるロボット姿勢にわたるタスク依存の成功率を捉える空間的条件付き埋め込みを学習する。
llm.result: 未知のRoboCasaのキッチンにおける8つの多関節オブジェクトタスクにおいて、平均タスク成功率47.0%を達成し、最強ベースラインの26.5%を上回った。
keywords_ja: 移動マニピュレーション

2611.25366.tldr_en: This work proposes Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies (M4M), a framework that learns manipulation-aware mobility directly from pretrained manipulation policies, and learns a spatially conditioned embedding that captures task-dependent manipulation success across candidate robot poses.

2611.25336.title: MoRE: Mixture-of-Experts for Multi-Physics Robotic World Models
2611.25336.abstract: A robotic world model should predict how objects evolve under robot actions and physical dynamics. While recent 3D world models have shown strong predictive capabilities, they still struggle with the heterogeneous dynamics arising from diverse object interactions. To address this in a unified framework, we decompose robotic interactions into distinct physical regimes and assign each to a specialized motion expert. We introduce MoRE, a 3D world model with a mixture of motion experts organized around rigid, deformable, and prehensile dynamics. This design enables a single model to capture diverse physical behaviors while preserving regime-specific priors. Trained on mixed simulation and real-world data, MoRE integrates with Model Predictive Control (MPC) to support diverse manipulation tasks. Experiments show that MoRE improves prediction accuracy across physics regimes, leading to stronger real-world MPC performance. Code, data, and project website are available at https://alwaysleepy.github.io/MoRE-WM-site/.

llm.title_ja: MoRE：マルチ物理ロボット世界モデルのためのMixture-of-Experts
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な物体の相互作用による異種動態に対処するため、剛体・変形可能・把持のダイナミクスごとに専門の動作エキスパートを割り当てた3D世界モデルMoREを提案する。
llm.problem: 近年の3D世界モデルは強力な予測能力を示しているものの、多様な物体の相互作用から生じる異種動態の扱いに苦慮している。
llm.method: ロボットの相互作用を異なる物理レジームに分解し、剛体、変形可能、把持のダイナミクスを専門とするエキスパートを組織したMoREを開発し、MPCと統合した。
llm.result: 物理レジーム全体で予測精度が向上し、実世界でのモデル予測制御（MPC）のパフォーマンスが向上した。

2611.25336.tldr_en: MoRE is introduced, a 3D world model with a mixture of motion experts organized around rigid, deformable, and prehensile dynamics that enables a single model to capture diverse physical behaviors while preserving regime-specific priors.

2611.25320.title: Improving Imitation Policies for Multi-Phase Tasks through Residual Learning Allocation
2611.25320.abstract: Residual reinforcement learning corrects an imitation-trained base policy using a limited budget of environment interaction. In a task with several phases, this budget must be divided among the phases, and the phase in which the base policy fails is not necessarily the phase in which a correction most improves task completion. We formalize this distinction through the completion gain: the change in full-task completion probability when, during a single phase, a state-feedback controller replaces selected components of the base policy's action. We decompose the completion gain into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and we estimate it from paired episodes. The positive estimates determine which action components the residual policy corrects and how training episodes are distributed across phases. In stochastic point-mass docking experiments, most failures occurred in the final docking phase, whereas the largest completion gain occurred in the preceding channel phase; gain-based allocation improved completion over allocation proportional to failure counts and, in a variant with a longer approach, over uniform allocation at half of the budget. In simulated bimanual robotic assembly, the completion-gain estimates were positive only for insertion and release, although few failures occurred during release; in a second assembly configuration, a residual policy trained in the release phase improved completion from held-out states at the start of release by 16.9%.

llm.title_ja: 残差学習割り当てを通じたマルチフェーズタスクのための模倣ポリシーの改善
llm.tldr_ja: マルチフェーズタスクにおいて、状態フィードバックコントローラによる模倣ポリシーの修正効果を完了利得として定式化し、学習エピソードの配分を決定する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 複数のフェーズを持つタスクでは環境相互作用の予算を分割する必要があるが、ベースラインポリシーが失敗するフェーズと修正が最も効果的なフェーズは必ずしも一致しない。
llm.method: 単一フェーズでの完了確率の変化を表す完了利得をペアのエピソードから推定し、正の推定値に基づいて残差ポリシーが修正するアクションコンポーネントとフェーズごとの予算配分を決定する。
llm.result: シミュレーション化された二腕ロボット組立において、リリースフェーズで訓練された残差ポリシーにより、リリース開始時の保持状態からの完了率が16.9%向上した。

2611.25320.tldr_en: The completion gain is decompose into the probability of reaching the phase and the conditional improvement in completion from the start of the phase, and it is estimated from paired episodes to determine which action components the residual policy corrects and how training episodes are distributed across phases.

2611.25254.title: Plan your Self-Adaptation! Ontology-Mediated Task and Architecture Co-adaptation Planning for Robots
2611.25254.abstract: Autonomous robots may need to adapt both their task plans and architectural configurations as operating conditions change. These decisions are interdependent: architectural configurations determine which actions a robot can perform, while task plans determine which capabilities are required. This paper presents PLANTA, an ontology-mediated approach to task and architecture co-adaptation that considers these dependencies during mission planning. PLANTA uses an ontology expressed in the Web Ontology Language to represent architectural alternatives and their associated functional and quality requirements, while the Planning Domain Definition Language defines task actions and mission goals. By automatically translating and integrating these models, PLANTA enables joint planning of task and reconfiguration actions. The approach uses satisficing planning and replans when changes during execution invalidate the current plan. PLANTA is evaluated in two robotic scenarios involving underwater inspection and ground navigation. The results support the feasibility of runtime co-adaptation and show lower planning time and memory consumption compared with optimal-policy generation in the evaluated navigation scenario, while producing plans of similar quality.

llm.title_ja: 自己適応を計画せよ！オントロジーを介したロボットのタスクとアーキテクチャの協調適応計画
llm.tldr_ja: 運転条件の変化に応じてタスク計画とアーキテクチャ構成を協調して適応させるオントロジーを介したアプローチPLANTAを提案する。
llm.problem: 自律型ロボットは環境変化に応じてタスク計画とアーキテクチャ構成の両方を適応させる必要があるが、これらの方策は相互依存している。
llm.method: Webオントロジー言語を用いてアーキテクチャの代替案を表現し、PDDLでタスクアクションとミッション目標を定義して、これらを統合して共同計画を行うPLANTAを開発した。
llm.result: 水中検査と地上ナビゲーションの2つのシナリオにおいてランタイムでの協調適応の実現可能性を実証し、最適なポリシー生成と比較して計画時間とメモリ消費量を削減した。

2611.25254.tldr_en: PANTA is evaluated in two robotic scenarios involving underwater inspection and ground navigation and shows the feasibility of runtime co-adaptation and lower planning time and memory consumption compared with optimal-policy generation in the evaluated navigation scenario, while producing plans of similar quality.

2611.25251.title: WEVO: World Model-Enabled VLA Optimization for Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
2611.25251.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) can improve vision-language-action (VLA) policies beyond imitation, but humanoid exploration is unsafe and simulator RL can exploit residual sim-to-real gaps. We present WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM). Simulated manipulation and locomotion play data improve contact-dynamics and viewpoint-change prediction. A VLA trained on synthetic demonstrations collects 20 autonomous real robot rollouts per task to align the WM with deployment observations. The VLA, whole-body controller (WBC), and video WM then form a closed-loop RL environment with dense progress rewards. Across three real robot tasks, play data improves every evaluated WM metric and downstream policy success; video WM RL raises mean success from 23.3% to 75.0%, compared with 48.3% for real robot RL. We therefore leverage the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement. Project website: https://qianzhong-chen.github.io/wevo.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: WEVO：全身ロコ・マニピュレーションのための世界モデル有効化VLA最適化
llm.tldr_ja: テレオペレーション不要で全身ヒューマノイドVLAをポストトレーニングする枠組みWEVOを提案し、ビデオ世界モデル内で強化学習を行う。
llm.problem: 強化学習はVLAポリシーを改善できるが、ヒューマノイドの探索は危険であり、シミュレータでの強化学習はシム・ツー・リアル・ギャップを悪化させる。
llm.method: VLA、全身コントローラ（WBC）、行動条件付きビデオ世界モデルを組み合わせて、高密度の進捗報酬を持つ閉ループ強化学習環境を構築した。
llm.result: 3つの実ロボットタスクにおいて、ビデオ世界モデル強化学習により平均成功率が23.3%から75.0%に向上し、実ロボットでの強化学習（48.3%）を上回った。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.25251.tldr_en: WEVO, a teleoperation-free framework for post-training a whole-body humanoid VLA in an action-conditioned video world model (WM), leverages the complementary strengths of both environments: simulation provides policy initialization and broad coverage, while the video WM offers a deployment-aligned environment for policy improvement.

2611.25249.title: A Synthetic Multi-Modal Testbed for Security Stress Testing of Agentic Counter-UAS Systems
2611.25249.abstract: Agentic cyber-physical systems rely on perception and state estimation to support autonomous decisions. Degraded, inconsistent, or manipulated sensor observations can therefore propagate through an autonomous pipeline and create security-relevant failures. This work presents a synthetic Counter-Unmanned Aircraft System (C-UAS) testbed developed in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking algorithms supporting agentic decision-making. A simplified quadrotor follows scripted trajectories while co-located virtual sensors generate synchronized RGB, RTX LiDAR, and illustrative IR-like observations. The testbed varies target range, motion, clutter, occlusion, and sensor availability, with future stress cases including sensor dropout, temporal misalignment, cross-modal disagreement, and false observations. As an initial exemplar, a nonlinear coordinated-turn Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is evaluated over a 20-s maneuvering trajectory using LiDAR target-centroid measurements. Position error and uncertainty are compared as LiDAR observations degrade and are lost. The framework provides a reproducible environment for studying how sensing degradation affects downstream autonomous estimation and resilience in agentic C-UAS systems.

llm.title_ja: エージェント型対UASシステムのエージェントセキュリティストレステストのための合成マルチモーダルテストベッド
llm.tldr_ja: 知覚および追跡アルゴリズムの再現可能なストレステストを行うため、NVIDIA Isaac Simで開発された合成カウンタUASテストベッドを提案する。
llm.problem: エージェント型サイバー物理システムは知覚や状態推定に依存しているため、劣化したセンサー観測が自律パイプラインを通じてセキュリティ上の失敗を引き起こす。
llm.method: NVIDIA Isaac Simにおいて、クアッドローターがスクリプト化された軌道に従いながら仮想センサーで同期されたRGBやLiDAR、IR風の観測を生成するテストベッドを構築した。
llm.result: LiDAR観測が劣化し失われるにつれて、非線形協調旋回拡張カルマンフィルタの位置誤差と不確実性がどのように変化するかを評価するための再現可能な環境を提供した。

2611.25249.tldr_en: This work presents a synthetic C-UAS testbed developed in NVIDIA Isaac Sim for repeatable stress testing of perception and tracking algorithms supporting agentic decision-making, and provides a reproducible environment for studying how sensing degradation affects downstream autonomous estimation and resilience in agentic C-UAS systems.

2611.25243.title: Verify2Act: Critic-Guided Latent World Models for Verifying Language-Conditioned Manipulation Plans
2611.25243.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons. We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification. A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed. V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. We deploy the full system on a low-cost robot arm, training the world model and critic only on data generated in a digital twin. Across six language-conditioned tasks, Verify2Act reaches 83.3\% task success, compared with 61.7\% for a latent world model without our architectural changes, 53.3\% for the VLM alone, and 46.7\% for a pixel-diffusion world model. It verified every plan it executed and incurred no planning-induced failures: all of its failed episodes were caused by low-level grasp or placement slips. In simulation, Verify2Act obtains the highest five-task chain success on CALVIN among the compared baselines with 30$\times$ fewer reflective VLM calls than pixel-diffusion verification, and the highest success on cluttered nut assembly.

llm.title_ja: Verify2Act: 言語条件付きマニプリケーション計画を検証するための批評家誘導型潜在世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: Verify2Actは、セマンティックな行動提案と潜在的物理検証を分離し、デジタルツインのデータで訓練された潜在世界モデルと批評家を用いて計画を検証するモジュール式フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 視覚言語モデル（VLM）は多段階のマニプリケーション計画を提案できるが、シーンの変化に関するグラウンドモデルを持たず、ピクセルレベルの世界モデルは低速でドリフトするという課題がある。
llm.method: VLMが計画を提案し、潜在世界モデル（V2A-WM）がDINOv2特徴空間で推論し、二重ヘッドの批評家が時間的整合性と目標達成度を検証するモジュール式フレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 6つの言語条件付きタスクにおいて83.3%のタスク成功率を達成し、ベースラインやVLM単体、ピクセル拡散世界モデルを上回った。
llm.limitation: 失敗したエピソードはすべて低レベルの把持や配置の滑りに起因していた。

2611.25243.tldr_en: Verify2Act is a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification, and obtains the highest five-task chain success on CALVIN among the compared baselines with 30$\times$ fewer reflective VLM calls than pixel-diffusion verification, and the highest success on cluttered nut assembly.

2611.25232.title: Ferrofluid Shape Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning
2611.25232.abstract: Ferrofluids are liquids containing magnetic nanoparticles, enabling shape control through external magnetic fields. This deformability supports their use as soft robotic bodies that can navigate confined spaces and manipulate objects. Their nonlinear continuum dynamics, however, make reliable control challenging. Existing work shows how spatial magnetic fields from electromagnet arrays can establish and maintain desired ferrofluid configurations. A complementary objective is to exploit the fluid's dynamics under limited actuation to reach prescribed shapes that may not be sustainable at equilibrium. Here, we use deep model-based reinforcement learning to control these transient shapes. Learning directly through physical interaction, our policies select current commands for a single fixed electromagnet based on visual observations, guiding the moving ferrofluid toward prescribed geometries. The learned policies repeatedly attain a variety of shapes spanning polygons, asterisks and pentominoes. These results demonstrate that learning directly from physical interaction enables reliable fluid shaping, opening new possibilities for controlling ferrofluid-based soft robots.

llm.title_ja: 深層強化学習による強磁性流体の形状制御
llm.tldr_ja: 深層モデルベース強化学習を用いて、視覚観測に基づき単一の固定電磁石の電流コマンドを選択し、動的な強磁性流体を所望の幾何学的形状へと導く手法を実証した。
llm.problem: 強磁性流体は柔らかいロボット本体として機能するが、その非線形な連続体力学のため信頼性の高い制御が難しい。
llm.method: 物理的な相互作用から直接学習を行う深層モデルベース強化学習を用いて、視覚観測に基づいて単一の固定電磁石の電流コマンドを選択する。
llm.result: 学習されたポリシーにより、多角形、アスタリスク、ペントミノなど多様な形状を繰り返し達成できることを示した。

2611.25232.tldr_en: This work uses deep model-based reinforcement learning to control ferrofluid shapes spanning polygons, asterisks and pentominoes through physical interaction, demonstrating that learning directly from physical interaction enables reliable fluid shaping.

2611.25215.title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
2611.25215.abstract: Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues. We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings. ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL). The VLM provides common-sense reasoning and semantic interpretation of the scene, assessing risks, interpreting signs, and producing semantic labels with associated navigation costs. An open-vocabulary segmentation module converts these labels into a dense, real-time risk map, which conditions two pre-trained RL policies responsible for agile locomotion and local navigation, effectively coupling high-level VLM reasoning with low-level physical control. Real-world experiments showed the system's ability to autonomously navigate a wide range of complex real-world environments. The robot completes kilometer-long hikes with minimal intervention, interprets signs to avoid danger, and evaluates its environment to identify safe areas on which to step. This work represents a step toward the reliable deployment of systems in unstructured environments. However, it also underscores the challenges that remain in VLM reliability and spatial reasoning, indicating that foundational models are a crucial component but not yet a complete solution for navigation in the wild.
2611.25215.comment: 42 pages, 6 figures, 15 supplementary figures. Author's version of the article published in Science Robotics. Project page: https://roam-hiking.github.io

llm.title_ja: 野外での脚型ロボットナビゲーションに向けた視覚言語推論と学習済み制御の架け橋
llm.tldr_ja: ROAMは、インターネット規模のデータで事前学習されたVLMの常識推論と、強化学習による頑健な移動・局所計画ポリシーを統合し、複雑な野外環境でのキロメートル単位の自律移動を実現する。
llm.problem: 多様な実環境での自律ナビゲーションには、多様な地形を処理する頑健な低レベル動作制御と、環境の手がかりを解釈する高レベル推論の両方が要求される。
llm.method: VLMのシーン解釈から得られるリスクマップに、強化学習で事前学習されたアジャイルな移動および局所ナビゲーションポリシーを条件付けして結合する。
llm.result: 最小限の介入でキロメートル単位のハイキングを完了し、危険を回避するための標識の解釈や安全な足場の評価が実環境で示された。
llm.limitation: VLMの信頼性と空間推論には依然として課題があり、野外ナビゲーションの完全な解決策には至っていない。
