2611.25215.tldr_en: ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings, and underscores the challenges that remain in VLM reliability and spatial reasoning.

2611.25202.title: Crisis Governance at the Joints. Mapping the Ethical and Societal Territory of Crisis Management Technologies: The Case of Human-Swarm Teaming
2611.25202.abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. This report maps the ethical and societal territory that HST opens up. It unpacks this territory with a 3i-framework, the Interface, where operators and swarms work together, the Infrastructure, where organisations distribute tasks, decisions and blame, and the Imaginary, where law, policy and shared societal assumptions define what a crisis is and which interventions it justifies. The central claim is that these concerns cannot be addressed one level at a time. Many of the most pressing problems, such as responsibility gaps and the erosion of meaningful human control, arise at the joints between levels, through four translations, habits harden, routines become stories, principles become procedures, and procedures become prompts. Drawing on a critical review of literature across philosophy of technology, political theory, moral psychology, philosophy of mind, AI ethics, and critical disaster and security studies, the report develops this framework, illustrates it with two worked examples, and derives design and governance implications and a set of questions for developers, emergency organisations and policymakers.

llm.title_ja: 関節部における危機ガバナンス：危機管理技術の倫理的・社会的領域のマッピング（ヒューマン・スウォーム・チーミングの事例）
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のオペレータとドローンスウォームが協調するヒューマン・スウォーム・チーミングを事例として、危機管理技術が直面する倫理的・社会的課題を3iフレームワークを用いてマッピングし分析する。
llm.problem: 危機や災害のガバナンスは人間よりも迅速に感知・行動する技術に依存しつつあるが、人間による制御や責任、監視、トリアージ等の疑問が生じている。
llm.method: 技術哲学、政治理論、AI倫理などの文献の批判的レビューに基づき、Interface、Infrastructure、Imaginaryからなる3iフレームワークを開発・適用する。
llm.result: 責任のギャップや意味ある人間制御の浸食などの問題が、各レベルの境界や翻訳の過程（習慣の硬直化等）で生じることを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: ヒューマン・スウォーム・チーミング

2611.25199.title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions
2611.25199.abstract: Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts. Test-time adaptation can alleviate this by correcting frozen policies at inference, but most methods ground their correction in a signal learned implicitly from robotic datasets, making it susceptible to the same shifts as the policy it corrects. Recent methods that instead exploit explicit spatial information are typically limited to coarse corrections, missing the nuanced, task-relevant motion most manipulation tasks require. We propose VG-Steer, which corrects existing policies by transferring the nuanced motion of successful in-distribution rollouts, captured along meaningful geometric axes, known here as object-relational distance pairs. VG-Steer leverages the semantic understanding of Large Vision Models (LVMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) reasoning, which combines the task-relevant entity pairs and their object-relational distance projections into a single tailored visual-geometric guidance signal. In a simulation benchmark, it efficiently corrects flow-matching policies under pose and task-goal shifts; on a real robot experiment, it widens the region of the workspace the frozen policy covers, more than doubling its success rate on cable placements one grid step outside the training positions, and steers a single-task policy toward objects it was never trained on while nearly eliminating object confusion. Project website: https://arthurfenderbucker.github.io/VG-Steer/

llm.title_ja: VG-Steer: コンテキスト内アラインされた抽象化に基づく視覚幾何学的ポリシー・ステアリング
llm.tldr_ja: VG-Steerは、成功したインディストリビューションの軌跡から抽出した意味のある幾何学的軸に沿った動きを転移させることで、既存のロボットポリシーを修正・適応させる手法である。
llm.problem: 一般化ロボットにおいて、限られた実世界データで分布外（OOD）設定に適応させることは、過学習や分布のずれによる破綻を招く主要なボトルネックとなっている。
llm.method: 大規模視覚モデル（LVM）やVLMの推論による意味的理解を活用し、タスク関連のエンティティペアとオブジェクト間距離投影を単一の視覚幾何学的ガイダンス信号に統合する。
llm.result: シミュレーションベンチマークでのフローマッチングポリシーの修正や、実ロボットのケーブル配置タスクでの成功率の2倍以上の向上を達成した。

2611.25199.tldr_en: VG-Steer is proposed, which corrects existing policies by transferring the nuanced motion of successful in-distribution rollouts, captured along meaningful geometric axes, known here as object-relational distance pairs, into a single tailored visual-geometric guidance signal.

2611.25197.title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger
2611.25197.abstract: Self-play reinforcement learning (RL) produces strong driving policies, but these policies are hard to verify or interpret. Differentiable model predictive control (DiffMPC) can enforce explicit constraints, but it is usually trained by imitating logged data or with costly RL. To add constraints to an already trained policy, we keep a PPO teacher's backbone and replace its action head with a DiffMPC that enforces road boundary half-planes and agent ellipses. We then distill the student with DAgger in the teacher's self-play simulator. Over 9 seeds, the constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and beats it on CARLA and on out-of-distribution Waymo scenes. For a stronger teacher, the student has fewer failures on nuPlan and Waymo, while staying level on CARLA. Its distillation takes no more than 30% of the teacher's training time.
2611.25197.comment: 18 pages, 10 main content pages, 3 figures, L4DC submission

llm.title_ja: セルフプレイRLから制約付き制御へ：DAggerを用いたDiffMPCスチューデントの蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: PPOティーチャーのバックボーンを維持しつつ行動ヘッドを微分可能モデル予測制御（DiffMPC）に置き換え、セルフプレイシミュレータ内でDAggerを用いてスチューデントモデルを効率的に蒸留する。
llm.problem: セルフプレイ強化学習（RL）は強力な駆動ポリシーを生み出すが、それらのポリシーは検証や解釈が難しく、DiffMPCにはコストがかかるかデータ模倣が必要である。
llm.method: PPOティーチャーのバックボーンを保持し、道路境界の半平面やエージェントの楕円を強制するDiffMPCで行動ヘッドを置換し、教師のセルフプレイシミュレータ内でDAggerにより蒸留する。
llm.result: nuPlanやCARLA、OODのWaymoシーンにおいて、ティーチャーと同等以上の性能を維持しつつ、ティーチャーの訓練時間の30%以下で蒸留を完了した。

2611.25197.tldr_en: A PPO teacher's backbone is kept and its action head replaced with a DiffMPC that enforces road boundary half-planes and agent ellipses, and the constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and beats it on CARLA and on out-of-distribution Waymo scenes.

2611.25179.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
2611.25179.abstract: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. Multi-view renderings are then used to verify whether the observed behavior satisfies the instruction. Across RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, and RoboDojo, 183 simulated test cases produced the predicted checker verdict. Visual verification and deduplication yielded 61 distinct defects across 49 tasks, including 40 phantom successes and 21 silent failures. Most defects in RoboCasa365 accepted incomplete executions, most in RoboDojo rejected valid executions, and both error types were common in RoboTwin 2.0. These findings suggest that validating success checkers requires testing both incomplete executions and valid alternatives to expert demonstrations, and motivate more rigorous evaluation protocols for future benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: 幻影の成功、沈黙の失敗：シミュレーションマニプリケーションベンチマークの成功チェッカーの監査
llm.tldr_ja: SimAuditは、タスク指示と成功チェッカーのコードを分析・検証することで、シミュレーションベンチマークにおけるチェッカーの不一致（幻影の成功や沈黙の失敗）を検出するLLMベースのパイプラインである。
llm.problem: シミュレーションマニプリケーションベンチマークで使用される手書きの成功チェッカーは、不完全な実行を合格させたり（幻影の成功）、有効な実行を不合格にしたり（沈黙の失敗）するという課題がある。
llm.method: 指示とチェッカーコードを分析して不一致シナリオを特定し、シミュレーションで再現した上でマルチビューレンダリングを用いて挙動を検証するLLMベースのパイプライン「SimAudit」を導入する。
llm.result: RoboCasa365などのベンチマークにおいて、40件の幻影の成功や21件の沈黙の失敗を含む61件の異なる欠陥を特定した。

2611.25179.tldr_en: SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions, is introduced, suggesting that validating success checkers requires testing both incomplete executions and valid alternatives to expert demonstrations, and motivating more rigorous evaluation protocols for future benchmarks.
2611.25179.hf_summary_en: An LLM-based pipeline audits simulated manipulation success checkers by recreating disagreement scenarios and visually verifying whether observed behavior satisfies task instructions, revealing phantom successes and silent failures.

2611.25151.title: Rate-distortion Assessment for Hierarchical Content Summarization
2611.25151.abstract: Powerful generative models including large language and vision models have demonstrated success across a wide range of content generation, editing and manipulation tasks via end-to-end prompt-based generation. However, current assessment of the quality of generative content manipulation remains subjective, limiting scientific understanding of model capabilities. Inspired by rate-distortion theory from Shannon information compression theory, in this work we formalize hierarchical content summarization as an information encoding problem. We design a principled framework to extract the semantic hierarchy of the source content to support quantitative characterization of the rate-distortion trade-off between compression efficiency (rate) against information loss (distortion) during generative content manipulation, which allows us to benchmark various models with respect to performance conditional on rate budget of interest. We demonstrate the use of the framework with empirical experiments on content summarization for long-context question-answering with state-of-the-art large language models, offering new insights into their efficiency and comprehension capabilities. We further demonstrate the use of the semantic hierarchy as guidance for performing effective retrieval augmented generation, showing improved rate-distortion characteristics against current baselines.

llm.title_ja: 階層的コンテンツ要約のためのレート歪み評価
llm.tldr_ja: シャノンの情報圧縮理論におけるレート歪み理論に着想を得て、階層的コンテンツ要約を情報符号化問題として定式化し、生成型コンテンツ操作の性能を定量的に評価するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 生成型コンテンツ操作の品質評価は主観的であり、モデル能力の科学的理解が制限されている。
llm.method: ソースコンテンツの意味的階層を抽出するフレームワークを設計し、圧縮効率（レート）と情報損失（歪み）のトレードオフを定量的に評価できるようにする。
llm.result: 最先端の大規模言語モデルを用いた長文コンテキストのQ&A実験を通じて、その効率性と理解能力に関する新たな洞察を提供した。

2611.25151.tldr_en: This work designs a principled framework to extract the semantic hierarchy of the source content to support quantitative characterization of the rate-distortion trade-off between compression efficiency against information loss during generative content manipulation, which allows us to benchmark various models with respect to performance conditional on rate budget of interest.

2611.25138.title: Old-School Planners Drive (Sometimes) Better Than Learned Ones
2611.25138.abstract: End-to-end driving models learn to plan from data, and hand-written planners are widely treated as a thing of the past. We test whether this is justified: we implement sixteen textbook planners, each combining a path source (reference line, A*, hybrid A*, RRT*) with a trajectory method (Frenet lattice, nonlinear optimization, $s$--$t$ search, dynamic window), and evaluate them on three benchmarks: open loop on nuScenes, closed loop on nuPlan with ground-truth perception, and photorealistic closed loop on HUGSIM. On HUGSIM, they replace only the planner of the end-to-end model UniAD and read its frozen perception, without an HD map or other privileged information. On nuScenes and nuPlan, the best textbook planners are competitive (L2 error of 0.735\,m against 0.947\,m for UniAD's planner; a nuPlan score of 79.3 against 76.1 for the rule-based PDM-Closed on Test14-hard with reactive agents). On HUGSIM, nine of the sixteen score above UniAD's learned planner on the same perception,. The best, a hybrid A* path followed by nonlinear trajectory optimization, raises HUGSIM's driving score (HD-Score) from 32.0 to 41.8. The gain is largest with standing and oncoming cars; against cars that steer at the ego, there is none. In 31 of the 182 runs in which UniAD's planner hits a car, the best textbook planner completes the route on the same perception: these crashes are due to the planner, not the perception.

llm.title_ja: 古典的プランナーは（時々）学習済みプランナーよりも上手に運転する
llm.tldr_ja: 16種類の教科書的な古典的プランナーを実装し、複数の自動運転ベンチマークで評価した結果、学習済みモデルと同等以上の性能を発揮し、プランナー起因の衝突を回避できることを示した。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンドの駆動モデルがデータから計画を学習する主流派において、手書きのプランナーは過去のものとして扱われているが、その正当性を検証する必要がある。
llm.method: 16種類の古典的プランナー（参照線やA*等と軌跡生成法を組み合わせたもの）を実装し、nuScenes、nuPlan、HUGSIMの3つのベンチマークで評価する。
llm.result: HUGSIMにおいて16種中9種がUniADの学習済みプランナーのスコアを上回り、最良のプランナーは駆動スコアを大幅に向上させ、プランナー起因の衝突を防いだ。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.25134.title: GEMS: Generation and Experience Memory for Subgoal-Guided Long-Horizon World Model Planning
2611.25134.abstract: Visual world models enable effective short-horizon goal-conditioned planning, such as reaching nearby targets and pushing objects over short distances, by predicting candidate action outcomes and comparing their representations with a goal representation. However, extending this approach to long-horizon tasks is challenging: prediction errors accumulate over extended rollouts, while latent-space similarity to distant goals provides limited guidance for ranking candidate outcomes. Existing methods address these limitations by introducing intermediate subgoals, either generated by learned models or selected from experience memory. Generated subgoals can contain hallucinations or be inaccurate in aspects such as object positions and timing. Memory-based approaches are constrained by experience coverage and may lack precise guidance for selecting appropriate intermediate states from stored observations. We introduce GEMS, which generates temporally structured subgoals to guide action search and state selection from Latent Experience Memory (LEM). A distance gate determines whether predicted outcomes are evaluated against the generated subgoal or the selected memory state. Experiments across six tasks and task suites spanning manipulation, navigation, and reaching demonstrate the effectiveness of GEMS for long-horizon planning. GEMS outperforms state-of-the-art world-model planning baselines across different manipulation settings, achieving success rates of 92.8% on Cube, 68.4% on Push-T, and 54.1% on Meta-World. It improves over the strongest evaluated baseline on these tasks by 24.0, 7.3, and 22.2 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate that generated subgoals and experience memory can jointly strengthen long-horizon planning with a frozen world model.

llm.title_ja: GEMS: サブゴール誘導型長期世界モデル計画のための生成・経験メモリ
llm.tldr_ja: GEMSは、一時的に構造化されたサブゴールを生成し、潜在経験メモリからの状態選択と組み合わせることで、凍結された世界モデルによる長期ホライズン計画の性能を向上させる手法である。
llm.problem: 視覚的世界モデルを用いた長期ホライズン計画では、予測誤差の蓄積や、遠隔目標に対する潜在空間の類似性による誘導の限界という課題がある。
llm.method: 行動探索と潜在経験メモリ（LEM）からの状態選択を誘導する時間的に構造化されたサブゴールを生成し、距離ゲートを用いて評価対象を切り替えるGEMSを導入する。
llm.result: CubeやPush-T、Meta-Worldなどのタスクにおいて最先端のベースラインを大きく上回る成功率を達成した。

2611.25134.tldr_en: GEMS is introduced, which generates temporally structured subgoals to guide action search and state selection from Latent Experience Memory (LEM) and improves over the strongest evaluated baseline on these tasks by 24.0, 7.3, and 22.2 percentage points, respectively.

2611.25119.title: Auditing Learned Dynamics in Weather Models
2611.25119.abstract: Learned weather models are experimentally accessible computational systems whose internal representations can be inspected and manipulated. Using sparse autoencoder features from GraphCast, DeepMind's autoregressive weather forecasting model, we test whether causal relevance requires physical semantics, a question that matters for auditing whether AI forecasters used in high-assurance settings rely on reliable mechanisms. We also look at whether physically associated latent directions can be steered to improve extreme-event forecasts, where interventions are applied to the model's internal activations during the rollout. We find that ablating a feature locked to GraphCast's computational mesh increases global geopotential height error despite lacking conventional physical semantics. Second, suppressing convection- and low-level-vorticity-associated features weakens predicted tropical-cyclone deepening (the fall in central pressure during intensification), while amplifying them reduces intensity error, with amplification of convection features through feature scaling achieving a median of 51\% error reduction over seven storms. Together, these results separate interpretable, physical association from causal utility and establish sparse features as experimental coordinates for auditing and intervening on learned weather dynamics.

llm.title_ja: 学習済み気象モデルにおける学習ダイナミクスの監査
llm.tldr_ja: DeepMindの気象予測モデルGraphCastのスパースオートエンコーダ特徴量を調査し、物理的意味論と因果的有用性の分離や、極端気象予測の改善に向けた内的活性化への介入を実証した。
llm.problem: 高信頼性設定で使用されるAI気象予報士が信頼できるメカニズムに依存しているかを監査するため、因果的関連性が物理的意味論を必要とするかという疑問がある。
llm.method: GraphCastのスパースオートエンコーダ特徴量を用いて、計算メッシュに固定された特徴のアブレーションや、対流・低レベル渦度関連特徴の抑制・増幅による介入実験を行う。
llm.result: 対流関連特徴の増幅により7つの台風の強度誤差の中央値51%削減を達成し、解釈可能な物理的関連性と因果的有用性を分離した。

2611.25119.tldr_en: Using sparse autoencoder features from GraphCast, DeepMind's autoregressive weather forecasting model, it is found that ablating a feature locked to GraphCast's computational mesh increases global geopotential height error despite lacking conventional physical semantics.

2611.25113.title: Do Deep Stereo Models Learn Shape Priors?
2611.25113.abstract: Localizing object boundaries is important for embodied visual systems, since small boundary errors can change the inferred geometry of physical surfaces. We study whether deep stereo models produce boundaries consistent with simple shape priors when local image and disparity cues are weak. We create a synthetic stereo dataset consisting of objects drawn from a highly constrained family of shapes, with randomized depth, slant, color and texture. Despite the simplicity of this shape space, we find that several state-of-the-art stereo models retain systematic boundary errors, even when finetuned or trained from scratch on the dataset. We then introduce a simple generative stereo model that jointly predicts disparity and a distance field representing object boundaries. The model improves boundary localization and produces contours that adhere more closely to the underlying shape space. These results expose limitations in the boundary predictions of current stereo architectures when local evidence is weak, and motivate further study of whether generative models can better combine regional grouping evidence with global geometric structure.

llm.title_ja: ディープステレオモデルは形状事前分布を学習しているのか？
llm.tldr_ja: 制約された形状ファミリの合成ステレオデータセットを用いて最新のディープステレオモデルを評価し、局所的証拠が弱い場合の境界予測の限界と、生成モデルによる改善の可能性を示した。
llm.problem: 埋め込み視覚システムにおいて物体の境界を正しくローカライズすることは重要であるが、小さな境界誤差が物理的表面の推論幾何学を変化させる。
llm.method: 制約された形状空間から描画されたオブジェクトを持つ合成ステレオデータセットを作成し、モデルの境界予測エラーを評価するとともに、距離場を共同予測する生成モデルを導入する。
llm.result: 既存のステレオモデルは局所的手がかりが弱い場合に体系的な境界誤差を示すことが分かり、提案する生成モデルにより境界のローカライズが改善された。

2611.25113.tldr_en: A simple generative stereo model is introduced that jointly predicts disparity and a distance field representing object boundaries that improves boundary localization and produces contours that adhere more closely to the underlying shape space.

2611.25105.title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation
2611.25105.abstract: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control: without attention, a four-arm relay falls from 95.0% to 39.0%, and without this supervision, Place Food falls from 78.0% to 47.0%.

llm.title_ja: MAWAM: 協調マニプリケーションのためのマルチエージェント・ワールド・アクションモデル
llm.tldr_ja: MAWAMは、クロスエージェント注意機構を用いて複数のロボットの将来の視覚表現と行動チャンクを同時にノイズ除去し、協調的なマニプリケーションを実現するモデルである。
llm.problem: ロボットチームの各動作はチームメイトの環境を変化させるため、協調マニプリケーションにはチームの行動と物理的な未来の共同予測が必要となる。
llm.method: 事前学習済みの単一ロボットのバックボーンをベースに、クロスエージェント注意機構を介して全ロボットの行動と将来ビューのトークンを共同でノイズ除去し、各ロボットの制御インターフェースを保持する。
llm.result: ランドリーバッグ収集などの3つの実ロボットタスクですべて最高成功率（平均67.8%）を達成し、MA-VLAを大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: 協調マニプリケーション

2611.25105.tldr_en: MAWAM is introduced, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample and shows that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control.

2611.25067.title: Mapping the Wind to Find the Source: Online Physics-Informed Gas Source Localization with Mobile Robots
2611.25067.abstract: Gas Source Localization (GSL) with mobile robots is challenging because wind and gas measurements are spatially sparse, noisy, and potentially affected by robot motion. Indoor airflow can vary substantially across space, while detailed environmental layouts, boundary conditions, or precomputed airflow fields are often unavailable. Moreover, hazardous sources must be localized as quickly as possible, making exhaustive exploration impractical. This paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for efficient GSL under spatially varying indoor airflow. As the robot navigates, it continuously collects wind and gas measurements and reconstructs the spatially varying airflow field online. The estimated wind field drives a forward dispersion model that predicts the gas pattern for each candidate source location. These predictions are compared with the measured gas pattern to update a probabilistic belief over the source location. As the wind field is reconstructed incrementally, the framework also accounts for the spatially non-uniform reliability of wind field estimation and its influence on the source estimation. The resulting belief map is then used for informative path planning to guide the robot toward informative regions. High-fidelity simulations provide a comprehensive evaluation of the individual components and their integrations within the complete system, while physical indoor experiments assess the system performance under realistic sensing, motion, and airflow conditions. The results demonstrate that incorporating lightweight physical knowledge significantly improves localization robustness under spatially complex airflow and enables more efficient exploration.

llm.title_ja: 風をマッピングして発生源を見つける：モバイルロボットを用いたオンライン物理情報に基づくガス源探索
llm.tldr_ja: 風とガスの測定値からオンラインで風向風速場を再構築し、前方拡散モデルと組み合わせることで、複雑な屋内気流下での迅速なガス源探索を実現する物理情報に基づく確率的フレームワークである。
llm.problem: モバイルロボットによるガス源探索（GSL）は、風やガスの測定値が空間的に疎であり、ノイズが多く、屋内の気流が空間的に大きく変動するため困難である。
llm.method: 移動しながら収集した風とガスの測定値から空間的に変動する気流場をオンラインで再構築し、それを拡散モデルに入力して発生源の確率的ビリーフを更新し、情報量に基づく経路計画を行う。
llm.result: 高忠度シミュレーションおよび実環境実験により、軽量な物理知識の統合が複雑な気流下での探索の頑健性と効率を大幅に向上させることを実証した。

2611.25067.tldr_en: This paper presents a lightweight physics-informed probabilistic framework for efficient GSL under spatially varying indoor airflow and demonstrates that incorporating lightweight physical knowledge significantly improves localization robustness under spatially complex airflow and enables more efficient exploration.

2611.25061.title: Infer3D: Inverse Generative Modeling Enables Robust 3D Reconstruction
2611.25061.abstract: Humans can understand the 3D structure of scenes even from highly unfamiliar or extreme viewpoints. Cognitive science suggests this generalization stems from a top-down generative inference strategy. In contrast, state-of-the-art 3D reconstruction neural networks typically rely on amortized, feedforward inference. While fast, this pattern-matching approach degrades when faced with out-of-distribution (OOD) scene conditions unseen during training. Inspired by the generative nature of human vision, we propose Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input. To prevent degenerate flat outputs, we couple the generative image prior with a frozen 3D lifting network that constrains the optimization space to a valid, multi-view-consistent 3D manifold. Across a variety of controlled synthetic and real-world tasks, Infer3D demonstrates superior OOD reconstruction accuracy compared to feedforward networks trained on equal or larger datasets. Furthermore, mirroring how human perception requires more time to process confusing stimuli, we introduce an adaptive inference strategy that expends more test-time compute on ambiguous OOD examples while efficiently routing in-distribution inputs. Project website: https://amanikiruga.github.io/infer3d-site/
2611.25061.comment: 23 pages, 12 figures, 15 tables. Includes references and appendices. Project page: https://amanikiruga.github.io/infer3d-site/

llm.title_ja: Infer3D: 逆生成モデリングによる頑健な3D再構成
llm.tldr_ja: Infer3Dは、生成モデルの潜在変数を逆推定し、凍結された3Dリフティングネットワークと組み合わせることで、未知の視点やOOD環境下でも頑健な3Dシーン再構成を実現するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 最先端の3D再構成ニューラルネットワークはフィードフォワード推論に依存しているため、訓練時に見ていないOODシーン条件に対して性能が低下する。
llm.method: 単眼入力を生成モデルの潜在変数に逆マッピングする逆生成モデリングフレームワークを採用し、マルチビュー一貫性のある3Dマニフォールドに最適化空間を制約する。
llm.result: 制御された合成および実世界タスクにおいて、同等以上のデータセットで訓練されたフィードフォワードネットワークよりも優れたOOD再構成精度を達成した。

2611.25061.tldr_en: This work proposes Infer3D, an inverse generative modeling framework that recovers the latent variables of a generative model to best match the monocular input and introduces an adaptive inference strategy that expends more test-time compute on ambiguous OOD examples while efficiently routing in-distribution inputs.

2611.24940.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
2611.24940.abstract: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: $Z$-sight: 視覚言語行動モデルと潜在世界モデルの統合
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚トークン空間で直接将来予測を行うことでピクセル生成や外部エンコーダを不要にし、ロボット制御の成功率を大幅に向上させる統合ロボット基盤モデルZ-sightを提案する。
llm.problem: ビデオベースの世界行動モデルは将来予測と制御の統合に有効である一方、ピクセル生成の重い計算コストを伴うという課題がある。
llm.method: VLMの知覚する視覚トークン空間で直接将来を予測し、フォーサイト専門家と連続行動専門家をMixture-of-Transformersで結合する。
llm.result: SIMPLEで81.9%、Unitree G1の6タスクで73.3%の成功率を達成し、既存のベースラインを大きく上回った。

2611.24940.tldr_en: A unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders.

2611.24938.title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models
2611.24938.abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet reconstruction-oriented visual representations do not explicitly emphasize the spatial relationships and object-state changes needed for manipulation. We introduce Phoenix, which learns representations of scene structure for world-action modeling. Specifically, Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge. Next, CS-VAE causally aggregates and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout. Finally, Phoenix jointly predicts these latents, complementary appearance latents, and robot actions, linking scene evolution with action generation. To study pretraining data efficiency, we curate approximately 39,000 hours of egocentric and robot manipulation data for representation learning and use the robot demonstration subset for WAM pretraining. Following benchmark-specific post-training, Phoenix achieves state-of-the-art performance across simulation and real-robot benchmarks spanning single-arm, bimanual, and dexterous manipulation. It demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations, achieving success rates of 94.8% on LIBERO-Plus and 72.4% on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, alongside strong cross-embodiment transfer and real-world manipulation performance on Bench2Dex and RoboDojo-RealWorld, respectively. Pretraining-scale analysis shows larger performance gains from data scaling than a video-VAE-only baseline, indicating stronger scaling benefits and more effective data utilization. Moreover, Phoenix maintains high success rates when adapted with limited downstream demonstrations, demonstrating strong few-shot adaptation. Our code, pretraining data, and models are available on the project page to help the community reproduce our results.

llm.title_ja: Phoenix: 汎化可能な世界行動モデルのためのシーン構造表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: シーン構造表現を学習し世界行動モデルに統合することで、シミュレーションおよび実機の様々なマニピュレーションタスクにおいて優れた汎化性能とロバスト性を実現するPhoenixを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来の再構築指向の視覚表現は、マニピュレーションに必要な空間関係や物体状態の変化を明示的に強調できていない。
llm.method: 幾何学的・時空間的知識の二重教師付き蒸留によりDINOv3のセマンティクスを拡張し、CS-VAEで生成用潜在変数に圧縮・統合する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plusで94.8%、RoboTwin 2.0で72.4%の成功率を達成し、少ショット適応や優れた実機性能を示した。

2611.24938.tldr_en: Phoenix Encoder enriches DINOv3's general visual semantics through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantic knowledge and compresses Phoenix Encoder features into generative latents while preserving scene information and spatial layout, and demonstrates strong robustness to perturbations.

2611.24926.title: Grana: Compositional Reward Modeling for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
2611.24926.abstract: Robot reward modeling faces two challenges: generalizing across tasks and accurately tracking progress in long-horizon manipulation. General-purpose reward models demonstrate broad task transfer, but transfer from short-task pretraining to long-horizon tasks remains underexplored. Long-horizon progress models often rely on task-specific subtask classifiers or fixed action vocabularies, limiting the reuse of learned progress knowledge when adapting to new tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce Grana, a vision-language robot reward model that learns to identify unfinished subtasks and estimate their continuous progress using open-vocabulary subtask descriptions. We train a language-conditioned model to estimate progress in short-horizon tasks and individual subtasks of long-horizon tasks. For long-horizon tasks, we combine the selected subtask's predicted progress with credit for preceding completed subtasks to estimate whole-task progress. General progress prediction requires training the model across diverse tasks with progress supervision that accounts for imperfect execution. Elapsed-time proxies can misrepresent progress when relative subtask durations vary, or failures reverse local progress. We therefore introduce an annotation protocol that converts sparse subtask boundaries and action-quality annotations into dense progress targets, without requiring annotators to assign numerical progress scores. Pretraining with this supervision on 200 diverse, mostly short-horizon manipulation tasks enables zero-shot reward prediction on unseen tasks and improves progress prediction after adaptation to multi-minute, long-horizon tasks. Experiments demonstrate (i) generalizable reward prediction, including adaptation to five long-horizon tasks, (ii) benefits from pretraining and composing subtask progress estimates, and (iii) improved downstream policy performance.

llm.title_ja: Grana: 長期ロボットマニピュレーションのための構成的報酬モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 未完了のサブタスクの特定とオープン語彙による連続進捗の推定を学習することで、未知のタスクへのゼロショット報酬予測と長時間の長期タスクへの適応を可能にするGranaを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボット報酬モデルは、多様なタスクへの汎化や長期マニピュレーションにおける進捗の正確な追跡が困難であるという課題がある。
llm.method: 多様な短時間タスクを用いて言語条件付きモデルを事前学習し、スパースなサブタスク境界から高密度な進捗ターゲットを構築する。
llm.result: 200の多様なタスクによる事前学習により、ゼロショット報酬予測を実現し、5つの長期タスクへの適応において優れた性能を示した。

2611.24926.tldr_en: Grana, a vision-language robot reward model that learns to identify unfinished subtasks and estimate their continuous progress using open-vocabulary subtask descriptions is introduced, and an annotation protocol that converts sparse subtask boundaries and action-quality annotations into dense progress targets, without requiring annotators to assign numerical progress scores is introduced.

2611.24925.title: Render the Robot, Generate the World: One Video World Model Across Embodiments
2611.24925.abstract: Predicting the consequences of an agent's actions requires modeling both the body's motion and the environment's response. Most video world models attempt to learn both from numerical actions, even though geometry and kinematics already specify the intended motion. We introduce Doppel, an embodiment-agnostic video world model conditioned on camera-aligned renderings of future body configurations and numerical action trajectories. By explicitly providing the intended motion, Doppel can focus on predicting object motion and interaction-driven changes in the environment. Rendered motion also provides a common visual interface across different embodiments and action spaces. To train on robot datasets without camera extrinsics, we recover camera poses and align rendered trajectories with recorded observations. We jointly train a single shared video backbone and conditioning adapter on eight datasets spanning eight robot and human embodiments, from single- and bimanual robot arms to a dexterous humanoid and human hands and bodies, using about 600 hours of video without embodiment labels. Across three robot-arm datasets, Doppel improves PSNR over action-only baselines by 1.00 dB on held-out trajectories and 1.20 dB under out-of-distribution evaluation, while predicting more consistent object motion. Training on all eight embodiments (Doppel-8) improves robot predictions over the three-robot model (Doppel-3) on four of six evaluation sets. Project page: https://doppelwm.github.io/.

llm.title_ja: ロボットのレンダリングと世界の生成: 複数身体に共通の単一ビデオ世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の身体構成のレンダリングと数値行動軌跡に条件付けられた身体非依存のビデオ世界モデルDoppelを提案し、多様なロボットおよび人間の身体において環境の変化を高精度に予測する。
llm.problem: 大半のビデオ世界モデルは、幾何学や運動学ですでに指定されている動作を数値行動のみから学習しようとしている。
llm.method: カメラ座標に合わせた将来の身体構成のレンダリングと数値行動軌跡を入力とし、共有ビデオバックボーンと条件付けアダプターを共同学習する。
llm.result: 3つのロボットアームデータセットにおいて、行動のみのベースラインと比較してPSNRを1.00 dB改善し、一貫性のある物体動作を予測できた。

2611.24925.tldr_en: Doppel, an embodiment-agnostic video world model conditioned on camera-aligned renderings of future body configurations and numerical action trajectories, is introduced, an embodiment-agnostic video world model conditioned on camera-aligned renderings of future body configurations and numerical action trajectories that improves robot predictions over the three-robot model.

2611.25005.title: Inhabitant: An Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Human-Scene Interaction with Spatial Control and Quantitative Feedback
2611.25005.abstract: Recent work on human-scene interaction (HSI) generation moves from single interactions to long-horizon interaction, where a language-model agent plans and executes a sequence of interactions in a 3D scene under one instruction. However, existing agents struggle in challenging everyday scenarios (e.g., picking up a toy and throwing it into a basket) because they lack spatial control over the motion and quantitative feedback on its execution, and they often fail to complete the interaction sequence. To address these gaps, we present Inhabitant, a training-free agent framework in which the agent specifies each motion through positions, paths and poses, measures how the executed interaction deviates from its intent, and revises the control specification accordingly. For an extensive evaluation in such scenarios, we build Inhabit, a benchmark of 75 household tasks in 31 furniture layouts of an apartment, in which every task chains one to three goals on movable objects and is carried out by the whole body, excluding fingers. On Inhabit, Inhabitant completes 98.7\% of the tasks with Claude Opus 5.5, and 93.3\% and 82.7\% with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon, respectively. Ablations confirm that without spatial control the agent fails most tasks, and without quantitative feedback its motion becomes less precise. Code is available on the project page.
2611.25005.hf_summary_en: Inhabitant enables a language-model agent to plan and execute long-horizon human-scene interactions by specifying motions spatially, measuring deviations, and revising control, achieving high task completion on the Inhabit benchmark.

llm.title_ja: Inhabitant: 空間制御と定量的フィードバックを備えた長期ヒューマン・シーンインタラクションのためのエージェントフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: Inhabitantは、言語モデルエージェントがモーションを空間的に指定し、意図からの偏差を測定・修正することで、3Dシーン内での長期的なヒューマン・シーンインタラクションを高精度に実行する訓練不要のエージェントフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存の言語モデルエージェントは、動作の空間制御や実行に対する定量的フィードバックが欠けているため、日常生活の複雑なシナリオにおけるインタラクション計画の実行に苦労している。
llm.method: エージェントが位置・経路・姿勢を通じて各モーションを指定し、実行されたインタラクションの意図からの偏差を測定して制御仕様を修正する訓練不要のフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 75の家庭内タスクからなるInhabitベンチマークにおいて、Claude Opus 5.5を用いて98.7%のタスクを完了した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマン・シーンインタラクション
言語モデルエージェント
定量的フィードバック

2611.25005.tldr_en: Inhabitant, a training-free agent framework in which the agent specifies each motion through positions, paths and poses, measures how the executed interaction deviates from its intent, and revises the control specification accordingly, is presented.

2611.24883.title: Teleoperated Haircutting with Delay Compensation and Passivity-Based Control for Unilateral Internet Teleoperation under Real Communication Uncertainties
2611.24883.abstract: Robotic haircutting requires accurate motion execution and reliable communication to safely reproduce the operator's commands. Internet-based teleoperation is a key enabling technology to remotely perform precise manipulation tasks such as haircutting. However, communication uncertainties, including variable transmission delays and packet jitter, degrade synchronization between the master and slave systems and affect tracking performance. This paper presents a unilateral Internet teleoperation framework for robotic haircutting that takes into account experimentally measured communication uncertainties. Three delay-compensation techniques, namely Zero-Order Hold (ZOH), First-Order Hold (FOH), and Low-Pass Filtering (LPF), are evaluated together with a classical proportional-derivative (PD) controller and a passivity-based synchronization controller. Unlike conventional studies based on synthetic delay models, the proposed framework is validated using communication data acquired from a real cloud-based teleoperation platform, where both packet delay and effective delay are characterized. The results demonstrate that combining delay-compensation techniques with passivity-based synchronization improves the robustness of unilateral Internet teleoperation under realistic communication uncertainties, providing a reliable control framework for robotic haircutting applications.

llm.title_ja: 実通信の不確実性下における遅延補償と受動性ベース制御を用いた片方向インターネット遠隔操作による遠隔理髪
llm.tldr_ja: 実際のクラウド型プラットフォームから得られた通信データに基づき、遅延補償技術と受動性ベースの同期制御を組み合わせることで、通信の不確実性下における片方向インターネット遠隔操作の堅牢性を向上させる。
llm.problem: インターネットを介した遠隔操作では、変動する伝送遅延やパケットジッターなどの通信の不確実性により同期性能や追従性能が低下する。
llm.method: ZOH、FOH、LPFの3つの遅延補償技術を、PDコントローラおよび受動性ベース同期コントローラと組み合わせて実証評価する。
llm.result: 遅延補償技術と受動性ベース同期の組み合わせにより、現実的な通信の不確実性下で片方向インターネット遠隔操作の堅牢性が向上した。
keywords_ja: インターネット遠隔操作

2611.24883.tldr_en: The results demonstrate that combining delay-compensation techniques with passivity-based synchronization improves the robustness of unilateral Internet teleoperation under realistic communication uncertainties, providing a reliable control framework for robotic haircutting applications.

2611.24876.title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation
2611.24876.abstract: Large-scale, multi-agent self-play trains robust driving policies effectively in simulation, but controlling these models to generate specific, safety-critical edge cases remains a key challenge. Existing goal-conditioned self-play frameworks rely primarily on static map-location goals and fail to reliably produce complex agent interactions such as aggressive tailgating or adversarial cut-offs. These agent interactions are necessary for rigorous autonomous vehicle (AV) testing. To address this, we present an extended multi-agent self-play framework that introduces agent-relative dynamic goals. By conditioning policies on this extended goal representation, our framework enables targeted, controllable scenario synthesis. We demonstrate that our approach successfully generates interactive driving behaviors that static-goal baselines cannot simulate, providing a flexible tool for long-tail scenario generation in AV testing.

llm.title_ja: 制御可能な自動運転シナリオ生成に向けたマルチエージェント自己対戦におけるインタラクション学習
llm.tldr_ja: エージェント相対的な動的目標を導入した拡張マルチエージェント自己対戦フレームワークにより、自動運転テストに必要な複雑なエージェントインタラクションをターゲット指向で生成する。
llm.problem: 従来の目標条件付き自己対戦フレームワークは静的な地図上の目標に依存しており、攻撃的な割り込みなどの複雑なエージェントインタラクションを確実に生成できない。
llm.method: ポリシーにエージェント相対的な動的目標を条件付けすることで、ターゲットを絞った制御可能なシナリオ合成を実現する。
llm.result: 静的目標ベースラインではシミュレートできなかったインタラクティブな駆動動作の生成に成功し、長期的なシナリオ生成を可能にした。

2611.24876.tldr_en: This work presents an extended multi-agent self-play framework that introduces agent-relative dynamic goals and generates interactive driving behaviors that static-goal baselines cannot simulate, providing a flexible tool for long-tail scenario generation in AV testing.

2611.24864.title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World
2611.24864.abstract: Underwater navigation requires translating visual spatial cues into motion, yet marine vision-language datasets rarely include paired robot trajectories. We present NereidVLA, a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned 3D navigation. We first train Sea2Know on approximately two million marine examples to learn target grounding, spatial relations, and scene structure without paired robot-motion supervision. We then adapt it using expert trajectories executed under simulated underwater vehicle dynamics. Given RGB histories and a language instruction, NereidVLA predicts discrete motion tokens that decode into local 3D trajectories for closed-loop tracking. Evaluation combines an independent six-dimensional underwater navigation understanding benchmark with offline prediction and closed-loop navigation. Under matched navigation training and execution settings, marine spatial pretraining increases simulation success from 72.4% to 84.4%. Without fine-tuning on the real test environment, NereidVLA achieves 78.75% success in laboratory-pool robot trials, compared with 47.50% for InternVLA-N1. These results show that marine spatial supervision can support downstream motion learning and physical underwater navigation.

llm.title_ja: NereidVLA: 水中世界の理解とナビゲーションの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 膨大な海洋データによる事前学習と専門家の軌跡を用いた適応により、言語指示に基づく3Dナビゲーションを実現するビジョン言語行動モデルNereidVLAを提案する。
llm.problem: 水中ナビゲーションには視覚的空間の手がかりを動作に翻訳することが求められるが、海洋用VLMデータセットにはペアとなるロボット軌跡がほとんど含まれていない。
llm.method: 約200万件の海洋データでターゲットグラウンディング等を学習するSea2Knowを事前学習し、シミュレーションでの専門家軌跡で適応させる。
llm.result: シミュレーションの成功率が72.4%から84.4%に向上し、実プールのロボット実験でも高い成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.24864.tldr_en: NereidVLA is presented, a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned 3D navigation and shows that marine spatial supervision can support downstream motion learning and physical underwater navigation.

2611.24858.title: Communications-free Collective Intelligence Via Allocentric Belief
2611.24858.abstract: A team of skilled card players share no information amongst each other, and yet still are able to coordinate their play by watching the same players and reading the same tells. Autonomous systems have failed to exploit this logic, relying instead on explicit communication or complex state estimation schemes that can fail when it matters most. Without it, decentralized agents diverge in their world beliefs, and coordination collapses. Here we show that anchoring all agents to a single shared external actor, a common witness whose reactions encode team state, produces spontaneous, communication-free coordination. An allocentric belief network trained on witness behavior allows each agent to independently reconstruct full team state, keeping group beliefs consistent with no inter-agent exchange. Across five competitive environments allocentric belief alignment outperforms egocentric approaches in collective performance, and even scales to sixty-agent teams where standard methods fail. These results establish a new principle for collective intelligence: in the absence of communication, a shared gaze replaces a shared channel.

llm.title_ja: 中心性信念を介した通信不要の集合知
llm.tldr_ja: 共通の観測対象の反応を通じてチーム状態を符号化・再構築する中心性信念ネットワークにより、明示的な通信を行わずに自律エージェント間の自発的な協調を実現する。
llm.problem: 自律システムは明示的な通信や複雑な状態推定に依存しているが、これらは重要な場面で失敗することがある。
llm.method: すべてのエージェントを単一の共有外部アクター（共通の証人）にアンカリングし、エージェントが独立してチーム状態を再構築する中心性信念ネットワークを構築する。
llm.result: 5つの競争環境において自己中心的なアプローチを上回る集団パフォーマンスを示し、60エージェントのチームにもスケーリングした。

2611.24858.tldr_en: It is shown that anchoring all agents to a single shared external actor, a common witness whose reactions encode team state, produces spontaneous, communication-free coordination, establishing a new principle for collective intelligence: in the absence of communication, a shared gaze replaces a shared channel.

2611.24840.title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
2611.24840.abstract: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning. However, existing evaluations focus on prediction fidelity and planning performance, and rarely verify that the predictions depend on the conditioning action. In this paper, we study action dependence in action-conditioned semantic forecasting, which predicts future semantic segmentation from past segmentations and the ego action. We compare a forecaster with feature-wise and input-level action conditioning against an identical model without action input, and measure action dependence with test-time action interventions scored by standard segmentation metrics. The evaluation is validated in a synthetic environment with known action-dependent dynamics and applied to Cityscapes and BDD100K, both within each dataset and across the two vehicle platforms. Experiments show that the executed action improves mid-term mIoU by at most 2.5 points on Cityscapes and 0.6 points on BDD100K, whereas a wrong action reduces it by up to 23.2 and 7.0 points, below the model without action input. On real data, feature-wise conditioning depends 1.6 times more on the action than input-level conditioning at similar accuracy, whereas both depend on it equally in the synthetic environment, where the history does not determine the action. These results show that an accuracy gain indicates that a driving world model uses its action, but not how strongly its forecasts depend on it. Code is available at https://github.com/binayksingh/does-action-matter.
2611.24840.comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 6 tables. Accepted at the WAM-AD Workshop, WACV 2027. Code: https://github.com/binayksingh/does-action-matter

llm.title_ja: 行動は重要か？自動運転向け世界モデルとしての行動条件付きセマンティック予測の検証
llm.tldr_ja: 行動条件付きセマンティック予測における予測の行動依存性をテスト時の行動介入を用いて評価し、予測精度の向上が必ずしも行動への強い依存を示すわけではないことを明らかにする。
llm.problem: 自動運転の世界モデルにおける既存の評価は予測の忠実度や計画性能に偏っており、予測が条件付けられた行動に依存しているかを十分に検証していない。
llm.method: 行動入力の有無による予測モデルの比較を行い、テスト時の行動介入に対するセグメンテーション指標の変化を測定する。
llm.result: 実行された行動によって中期のmIoUが向上する一方、誤った行動は予測精度を著しく低下させることが示された。

2611.24840.tldr_en: Results show that an accuracy gain indicates that a driving world model uses its action, but not how strongly its forecasts depend on it, in action-conditioned semantic forecasting, which predicts future semantic segmentation from past segmentations and the ego action.

2611.24836.title: DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play
2611.24836.abstract: Learning robot manipulation is constrained by the availability of action-labeled robot data, for both imitation and world models. Humans can demonstrate skills in seconds, but their demonstrations lack the required robot actions. We introduce DiWALI, a framework that learns and improves diffusion policies within a world model trained on human and robot play. DiWALI infers latent actions from consecutive frames using an inverse dynamics model, enabling world model training without action labels, and grounds them in robot commands through a decoder trained separately on robot play. Skill policies are trained over latent actions from action-free human demonstrations and improved with reinforcement learning in imagination. On the CALVIN benchmark, DiWALI policies trained solely from human demonstrations substantially outperform baselines trained with robot demonstrations. Incorporating human play into the world model training also yields stronger policies after fine-tuning than using the same amount of robot play alone. Experiments on a physical robot show that skills learned primarily from human demonstrations are further improved in imagination with a world model trained on human and robot play. Together, these results demonstrate that human experience can support both manipulation skill acquisition and subsequent policy improvement, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data. Videos, dataset and code are available at https://diwali.cs.uni-freiburg.de.

llm.title_ja: DiWALI: 人間とロボットのプレイデータからの潜在行動推論に基づく世界モデルにおける拡散ポリシー学習
llm.tldr_ja: 行動ラベルのない人間のデモンストレーションから逆ダイナミクスモデルで潜在行動を推論し、世界モデルと強化学習を用いてマニピュレーションスキルを学習・向上させるフレームワークDiWALIを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーションの学習は、模倣学習や世界モデルの学習に必要な行動ラベル付きロボットデータの不足によって制限されている。
llm.method: 連続フレームから逆ダイナミクスモデルで潜在行動を推論し、行動フリーの人間デモンストレーション上で拡散ポリシーを訓練・改善する。
llm.result: 人間デモンストレーションのみで訓練されたポリシーがロボットデモンストレーションを用いたベースラインを大幅に上回り、実機でも有効性を示した。

2611.24836.tldr_en: Experiments on a physical robot show that skills learned primarily from human demonstrations are further improved in imagination with a world model trained on human and robot play, demonstrating that human experience can support both manipulation skill acquisition and subsequent policy improvement, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data.

2611.24831.title: Overlooked and Underutilized: Prototypes are the Missing Piece in Tabular XAI
2611.24831.abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) is frequently applied to high-stakes tabular data, yet the field relies heavily on feature attribution methods. While these approaches offer technical transparency, evaluating dozens of isolated features demands excessive cognitive effort from non-expert users. In this paper, we argue that prototypes remain overlooked and underutilized, and should be integrated as a complementary, intuitive gateway to auditing complex machine learning models. Although entire exemplars function as an intuitive baseline for prototype-based explanations, we highlight prototypical parts as particularly valuable for tabular data. By grouping related features into bounded subspaces, prototypical parts technically embody human-understandable concepts, replacing isolated features with cohesive semantic units. We support this integration through two primary lenses. Cognitively, these parts align with Rosch's categorization theory and Kahneman's System 1 thinking to naturally reduce cognitive load for humans. Then, we introduce a Geometric Validity Triad to conceptualize why prototypes validate the data manifold - a critical dimension often neglected by existing methods. We contend that making tabular XAI genuinely comprehensible requires shifting toward composite explanation pipelines that pair intuitive similarity-based reasoning with rigorous feature-level auditing. The paper concludes by outlining open challenges of prototype-based methods and discussing potential solutions to guide future research.
2611.24831.comment: Accepted for publication in the Journal of Intelligent Information Systems (Springer Nature)

llm.title_ja: 見落とされ活用不足の要素: 表形式データXAIにおけるプロトタイプの欠如
llm.tldr_ja: 高リスクな表形式データの解釈可能性において、認知負荷を軽減しデータマニフォールドを検証するために、特徴量アトリビューションだけでなくプロトタイプや原型パーツを統合すべきであると論じる。
llm.problem: 説明可能AI（XAI）は表形式データにおいて特徴量アトリビューション手法に過度に依存しており、非専門家ユーザーに過剰な認知的努力を求めている。
llm.method: 認知のカテゴリー化理論やシステム1思考に基づき、関連する特徴量を意味的単位にグループ化する原型パーツと幾何学的妥当性の三つ組みを提案する。
llm.result: 直感的な類似性ベースの推論と厳密な特徴量レベルの監査を組み合わせた複合的な説明パイプラインの必要性を明らかにした。

2611.24831.tldr_en: It is contended that making tabular XAI genuinely comprehensible requires shifting toward composite explanation pipelines that pair intuitive similarity-based reasoning with rigorous feature-level auditing.

2611.24816.title: RoboMorpher: Scaling Robot Morphology Representations for Cross-Embodiment Action Prediction
2611.24816.abstract: Learning shared action representations is central to cross-embodiment manipulation. However, identical joint values can produce different spatial configurations across robots, limiting representations learned from joint values alone. We introduce RoboMorpher, a morphology-conditioned action tokenizer that jointly reconstructs joint angles and link poses to associate control coordinates with their kinematic effects. MorphGen supplies scalable kinematic supervision by generating serial-arm descriptions from survey-derived geometric priors. We pretrain RoboMorpher on 40 million morphology-state pairs and integrate the frozen tokenizer into a vision-language-action policy for discrete prediction and continuous refinement. We also introduce EmbodiBench, a ten-task benchmark with 30 generated URDFs per task. With downstream URDFs excluded from tokenizer pretraining, the policy achieves 56.40% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 23.27% on EmbodiBench, exceeding continuous joint-space control by 9.73 and 15.34 percentage points. Removing link-pose supervision reduces EmbodiBench success by 17.94 percentage points, supporting morphology-aware geometric supervision for joint-action representation learning.

llm.title_ja: RoboMorpher: 異種ロボット間行動予測のためのロボット形態表現のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 関節角度とリンク姿勢を共同で再構築することで制御座標と運動学的効果を関連付ける形態条件付き行動トークナイザRoboMorpherを提案し、異種ロボット間のマニピュレーション性能を向上させる。
llm.problem: 同一の関節値であってもロボット間で異なる空間的配置を生じるため、関節値のみから学習された表現では異種ロボット間での共有行動表現の学習が制限される。
llm.method: 幾何学的事前分布からシリアルアームの記述を生成するMorphGenを用いて、大規模な形態・状態ペアでRoboMorpherを事前学習する。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0で56.40%、EmbodiBenchで23.27%の成功率を達成し、連続関節空間制御を大きく上回った。

2611.24816.tldr_en: RoboMorpher, a morphology-conditioned action tokenizer that jointly reconstructs joint angles and link poses to associate control coordinates with their kinematic effects, and EmbodiBench, a ten-task benchmark with 30 generated URDFs per task, supporting morphology-aware geometric supervision for joint-action representation learning.

2611.24800.title: Planner-Controller Interaction for Ackermann Navigation: A Matched Simulation and Hardware Benchmark
2611.24800.abstract: Global planners and path-tracking controllers are often evaluated independently, although their interaction determines how a vehicle follows a planned path. Whether simulation accurately predicts the performance of specific planner-controller combinations on Ackermann-steered hardware remains uncertain. This study evaluated three geometric controllers (Regulated Pure Pursuit, Stanley, and Vector Pursuit) paired with two global planners (Hybrid A* and NavFn) on a 1/10-scale Quanser QCar and in a matched Gazebo simulation. Both environments used shared custom planning and control algorithms, matched route geometry and goals, ground-truth pose references, and a common evaluation pipeline. Five runs per configuration and environment yielded 60 benchmark runs. Controller rankings for tracking accuracy and command smoothness transferred consistently between environments, with Spearman correlations of 0.77-0.94. However, planner-dependent effects showed substantially weaker agreement. In simulation, planner selection changed the root-mean-square (RMS) angular acceleration of the commanded velocities by no more than 0.030 rad/s^2, whereas Hybrid A* increased it by 0.141-0.843 rad/s^2 on hardware, depending on the controller. These differences coincided with planner-dependent achieved speeds that the simulation's idealised longitudinal response did not reproduce. Mean controller computation times remained below 0.5 ms on the Jetson TX2. The findings demonstrate that agreement in controller rankings does not guarantee accurate prediction of planner-dependent performance for specific controller pairings on hardware, highlighting the importance of physical validation.
2611.24800.comment: 32 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables. Code: https://github.com/HWUD-AIMBeyonD/qcar and https://github.com/HWUD-AIMBeyonD/QCarSim

llm.title_ja: アッカーマン型ナビゲーションにおけるプランナーとコントローラーの相互作用: シミュレーションとハードウェアのマッチングベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 同一の環境設定を用いたシミュレーションと実機実験の比較を通じて、コントローラーの追従順位は一貫して転移する一方で、プランナーに起因する性能の違いは実機の物理的特性に大きく影響されることを示す。
llm.problem: グローバルプランナーとパストラッキングコントローラーは個別に評価されることが多く、シミュレーションがアッカーマン型実機の性能を正確に予測できるかは不確かである。
llm.method: 3種類の幾何学的コントローラーと2種類のグローバルプランナーを1/10スケールの実機とGazeboシミュレーションで組み合わせて評価する。
llm.result: コントローラーのランキングは環境間で一貫していたが、プランナー依存の挙動（角加速度等）にはシミュレーションと実機で大きな差異が見られた。

2611.24800.tldr_en: It is demonstrated that agreement in controller rankings does not guarantee accurate prediction of planner-dependent performance for specific controller pairings on hardware, highlighting the importance of physical validation.

2611.24789.title: HINT-WAM: Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models
2611.24789.abstract: World action models (WAMs) have shown promising generalization and data efficiency in robot manipulation by coupling action generation with predictions of future visual dynamics. Translating these capabilities into reliable task execution, however, remains a challenge for existing post-training methods. Offline supervised fine-tuning provides dense supervision on expert trajectories, but its flow-matching action expert is trained only on noised demonstration actions and never on the intermediate states produced by its own sampler; task-specific adaptation can also compromise pretrained capabilities. On-policy reinforcement learning trains on the policy's own behavior, yet sparse task rewards make exploration and credit assignment difficult, while dense reward shaping still provides scalar evaluations rather than direct action targets. We introduce \textbf{HINT-WAM}, the first on-policy self-distillation framework that supervises the action expert on its own sampling trajectories using hindsight, the future video of the demonstration, as privileged information available to the WAM itself. For each demonstration observation, the student generates its action through its own denoising trajectory, and at the states along this trajectory the same model acts as a teacher conditioned additionally on this hindsight, providing a conditional action distribution as a dense training target, while the student sees only deployment-time inputs and needs no environmental rewards or simulator interaction. To transfer this supervision to a flow-matching action expert, HINT-WAM distills the teacher into the student with an energy score, a distribution-level objective that matches the teacher's action distribution from the student's own samples rather than regressing its velocity field. The project web is available in https://tuandattt.github.io/hintwam/.

llm.title_ja: HINT-WAM: 世界行動モデルのための事後情報を用いた事後情報に基づく訓練
llm.tldr_ja: デモンストレーションの将来のビデオを特権情報として利用し、自身のサンプリング軌跡に沿った行動専門家を事後的に指導するオンプラシー自己蒸留フレームワークHINT-WAMを提案する。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデル（WAMs）の信頼性の高いタスク実行への翻訳は未だ困難であり、オフライン微調整の行動専門家は自身のサンプラによる中間状態で訓練されない。
llm.method: デモンストレーションの将来ビデオを条件付けられた教師モデルとして利用し、サンプリング軌跡に沿ったエネルギー・スコアベースの目的関数で行動専門家を蒸留する。
llm.result: 要旨に記載なし

2611.24789.tldr_en: HINT-WAM is introduced, the first on-policy self-distillation framework that supervises the action expert on its own sampling trajectories using hindsight, the future video of the demonstration, as privileged information available to the WAM itself.

2611.24778.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
2611.24778.abstract: World models operate in a world they cannot fully observe. When a hidden disturbance, such as a current pushing a boat, changes the outcome of an action, a counterfactual question follows: what would have happened under a different action, subject to the same disturbance? Its answer separates bad decisions from bad luck. We prove that world models trained on factual transitions cannot answer it on their own, whatever their data or capacity. For many physical systems, the observed outcome and a simple property of the dynamics suffice: natura non facit saltus, nature makes no leaps. When actions and disturbances act as separate forces, their interaction is second-order in time, so the counterfactual outcome is, to first order, the observed outcome plus the difference between the world model's predictions under the alternative and factual actions. This yields a counterfactual world model with no counterfactual data, extra parameters, or retraining. For transitions of duration $h$, we prove an $O(h^2)$ bound on the counterfactual error relative to the disturbance variance, establish a matching minimax lower bound from unpaired factual data, and characterize failures at discontinuities, coordinate folds, and disturbances that scale the command. We validate these predictions from pixels with JEPA world models on frozen DINOv2 and masked autoencoder (MAE) encoders. On four rendered simulators, our approach improves counterfactual $R^2$ from $38$--$46\%$ to $86$--$96\%$ with the same world models; on a fifth, an underwater vehicle, it reaches $90$--$94\%$ with sixteen times more factual data. Four further frozen encoders, DINOv3, SigLIP~2, CLIP and EVA-02, give $81$--$95\%$ on the same simulators. In hindsight planning, it finds the action that would have reached the goal in $35$--$69\%$ of events, against $14$--$23\%$ for an oracle planner that knows the simulator but not the outcome.

llm.title_ja: 反実仮想世界モデル: 「もし〜だったら」を推論するJEPA
llm.tldr_ja: 物理系の動的性質を利用し、反実仮想データや追加パラメータを必要とせずに、代替行動と事実行動の下での世界モデルの予測差から反実仮想の成果を正確に計算するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 世界モデルは観測できない隠れた外乱が存在する環境において、異なる行動をとった場合にどうなっていたかという反実仮想的な問いに単独で答えることができない。
llm.method: 物理系のダイナミクスの性質（自然は飛躍しない）を利用し、事実の遷移データから二次近似によって反実仮想的な成果を予測する。
llm.result: 4つのレンダリングシミュレータにおいて反実仮想のR2スコアを38〜46%から86〜96%に改善し、水中ビークルでも高い精度を達成した。
llm.limitation: 不連続点や座標の折り畳み、コマンドをスケーリングする外乱に対しては失敗することを特徴づけている

2611.24778.tldr_en: It is proved that world models trained on factual transitions cannot answer the counterfactual question "what would have happened under a different action, subject to the same disturbance" on their own, whatever their data or capacity.

2611.24771.title: Hierarchical Admittance-Impedance Control for Mobile Manipulator Load Transfer
2611.24771.abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical admittance-impedance controller that combines an inner Cartesian impedance controller, an outer 6D admittance supervisor, and workspace-aware mobile-base assistance for guided load transfer. The method is motivated by assistive tasks such as airport baggage handling, where a robot should support a payload while a human worker guides its motion through small physical forces. Following an interaction-role interpretation of admittance and impedance, the torque-controlled Franka Research 3 manipulator behaves as a Cartesian impedance at the robot-object interface, providing compliant load support around a commanded equilibrium pose. At the human-facing interaction level, the outer admittance supervisor converts measured human wrench input into smooth Cartesian reference motion. The workspace-aware assistance layer shares the admittance-generated translational motion between the manipulator and a velocity-controlled base when larger motion is required, while front-side load alignment keeps the carried object near the robot's frontal region for safer and more intuitive guidance. The system was implemented in ROS and validated through a suitcase transfer experiment, showing that the robot can support the load while allowing the human to guide the transfer with relatively little effort.
2611.24771.comment: Accepted at the International Symposium on Robotics Research (ISRR 2026); 5 figures

llm.title_ja: 移動マニピュレータの荷物運搬に向けた階層型アドミタンス・インピーダンス制御
llm.tldr_ja: 内部のデカルトインピーダンス制御、外部の6Dアドミタンス指導者、および作業空間を考慮した移動台車アシスタンスを組み合わせることで、人間の小さな物理的力によるスムーズな荷物運搬を実現する。
llm.problem: 空港の手荷物取扱などの作業において、ロボットが荷重を支えつつ人間が小さな物理的力で動作を誘導できる柔軟な制御が求められている。
llm.method: 内側にCartesianインピーダンスコントローラ、外側に6Dアドミタンススーパーバイザー、さらにマニピュレータと台車の間で移動を分担するワークスペース対応アシスタンス層を階層的に統合する。
llm.result: ROSを用いて実装され、スーツケースの運搬実験を通じて、人間が比較的少ない労力で荷物の運搬を誘導できることが実証された。

2611.24771.tldr_en: This paper presents a hierarchical admittance-impedance controller that combines an inner Cartesian impedance controller, an outer 6D admittance supervisor, and workspace-aware mobile-base assistance for guided load transfer that can support the load while allowing the human to guide the transfer with relatively little effort.

2611.24731.title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models
2611.24731.abstract: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting. Modeling these interactions involves capturing how hand actions change objects and how the resulting states persist over time. Yet systematic evaluation tailored to these hand-centric capabilities remains underdeveloped. To address this gap, we introduce HandWorldBench, a unified benchmark that systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human hands, simulated dexterous hands, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions: visual quality, hand fidelity, appearance consistency, instruction following, physical consistency, and temporal coherence. To construct the benchmark, we develop a data curation pipeline that extracts hand-object interaction clips and screens them for quality, yielding 20,500 high-quality egocentric clips from over 600 hours of footage. We then manually select 500 clips covering seven task families for evaluation. Benchmarking eleven models under a unified protocol reveals that stronger hand-pose control does not consistently translate into coherent object-state evolution and persistence or robust cross-embodiment performance, with several specialized hand-control models underperforming general-purpose text/image-to-video generators on dexterous-hand tasks.

llm.title_ja: HandWorldBench: 手を中心とした世界モデルのための統合ベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 手と物体の相互作用における世界モデルを視覚品質や物体の状態変化など6つの次元で体系的に評価する統合ベンチマークHandWorldBenchを提案する。
llm.problem: 手と物体の相互作用を伴う微細なタスクにおいて、手の行動が物体をどのように変化させるか等を系統的に評価するベンチマークが未発達である。
llm.method: 20,500件のエゴセントリッククリップから厳選した500件のクリップを用い、11のモデルを統一されたプロトコルで評価するパイプラインを構築する。
llm.result: より優れた手のポーズ制御が必ずしも物体の状態変化の一貫性やロバストなクロス身体性能につながらないことが明らかになった。

2611.24731.tldr_en: This work introduces HandWorldBench, a unified benchmark that systematically evaluates hand-centric world models across human hands, simulated dexterous hands, and real dexterous hands along six dimensions: visual quality, hand fidelity, appearance consistency, instruction following, physical consistency, and temporal coherence.

2611.24719.title: DRIFT: Detachable Reasoning for Runtime-Flexible and Efficient End-to-End Driving
2611.24719.abstract: The integration of vision-language models (VLMs) into end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving has demonstrated strong potential by providing scene description and reasoning capabilities. However, VLMs are computationally expensive, and switching language reasoning on and off at runtime without hurting closed-loop performance has not been demonstrated, which hinders practical adoption. To address these issues, we propose DRIFT, an E2E autonomous driving framework that integrates a lightweight language model (LM) for visual question answering and action commentary. By efficiently projecting intermediate driving representations into the language embedding space, we demonstrate that a compact LM (<150M parameters) can achieve strong scene description and action commentary. Furthermore, we introduce a runtime-flexible planning module that is trained on surrogate reasoning features distilled from the LM and can be conditioned on either the LM or the surrogate reasoning features at inference. This design enables bypassing the LM entirely when required by deployment constraints, without sacrificing driving performance. With only 255M parameters, DRIFT reaches up to a Driving Score (DS) of 97.03 and a Success Rate of 89.39% (mean over three runs) on Bench2Drive by interleaving its LM and surrogate reasoning at a chosen reasoning rate. This is on par with the strongest non-language models while being far more compact than existing VLM-based models. DRIFT further achieves competitive results on the real-world NAVSIM and AlpaSim benchmarks at significantly lower computational cost than existing VLM-based approaches. Project page: https://drift-e2e.github.io/
2611.24719.comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://drift-e2e.github.io/

llm.title_ja: DRIFT: ランタイム柔軟性と効率性を備えたエンドツーエンド自動運転のための分離可能推論
llm.tldr_ja: 軽量な言語モデルと蒸留された推論特徴量を組み合わせることで、配備の制約に応じて推論モジュールを動的にバイパスしつつ高い自動運転性能を維持するフレームワークDRIFTを提案する。
llm.problem: ビジョン言語モデル（VLM）は計算コストが高く、閉ループ性能を落とさずに実行時に言語推論のオン・オフを切り替えることができていない。
llm.method: 中間駆動表現を言語埋め込み空間に効率的に投影する小型言語モデルと、それから蒸留された代理推論特徴量で条件付け可能なランタイム柔軟な計画モジュールを統合する。
llm.result: Bench2Driveにおいて駆動スコア97.03を達成し、既存のVLMベースのアプローチと比較して大幅に低い計算コストで同等の性能を示した。

2611.24719.tldr_en: DRIFT is proposed, an E2E autonomous driving framework that integrates a lightweight language model (LM) for visual question answering and action commentary and introduces a runtime-flexible planning module that is trained on surrogate reasoning features distilled from the LM and can be conditioned on either the LM or the surrogate reasoning features at inference.

2611.24696.title: Improving Zero-shot 3D Semantic Mapping in Offroad with Geometric Priors
2611.24696.abstract: Semantic 3D mapping is a powerful representation that enables platform agnostic mobile robot navigation in challenging offroad conditions. Current vision foundation models can accurately predict semantics zero-shot on structured scenes but performance is compromised in natural environments. On the other hand, 3D point clouds encode valuable information for discriminating semantics in scenarios where vision foundation models fail. In this work, we propose fitting a sphericity-elevation distribution for each semantic class to act as geometric anchor. Only the points with the most confident vision foundation model predictions are considered when fitting to produce high quality geometric prior distributions. The geometric prior is fused with the vision foundation model prediction to produce the final semantic mapping. The proposed prior improves SAM3 baseline by +6.3 in mIoU and +8.9 in accuracy on the RELLIS-3D dataset, and by +1.7 in mIoU and +2.1 in accuracy on the WildScenes dataset. The source code will be made public upon paper acceptance.

llm.title_ja: 幾何学的事前分布を用いたオフロードにおけるゼロショット3Dセマンティックマッピングの改善
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚基礎モデルの予測信頼度の高い点からクラスごとの球形度-標高分布を幾何学的アンカーとしてフィッティングし、視覚予測と融合させることでオフロード環境でのセマンティックマッピングを改善する。
llm.problem: 現在の視覚基礎モデルは構造化されたシーンでは正確なゼロショットセマンティクスを予測できるが、自然環境やオフロードでは性能が低下する。
llm.method: 各セマンティッククラスの球形度-標高分布を幾何学的事前分布としてフィッティングし、視覚基礎モデルの予測と融合する。
llm.result: RELLIS-3DデータセットでmIoUが+6.3、精度が+8.9向上し、WildScenesデータセットでも性能向上が確認された。
keywords_ja: 3Dセマンティックマッピング

2611.24696.tldr_en: This work proposes fitting a sphericity-elevation distribution for each semantic class to act as geometric anchor, so that only the points with the most confident vision foundation model predictions are considered when fitting to produce high quality geometric prior distributions.

2611.24646.title: Conceptual full-vehicle modeling of a modular all-wheel-drive robotic ADS test platform as a foundation for a digital twin architecture
2611.24646.abstract: This paper presents the development of an initial full-vehicle simulation model of the PixKit modular electric test platform in IPG CarMaker. The objective is to create a physics-based and extendable model structure that can serve as a low-level foundation for future digital twin applications. The reference vehicle is a skateboard chassis combining unconventional vehicle characteristics such as four independent wheel-hub motors and rear axle steering capable of high steering angles. Since complete measurement data of the vehicle is not yet available, the model parameterization is based on a combination of manufacturer documentation, derived values and engineering assumptions. The modeling approach focuses on the system-level integration of the main vehicle subsystems rather than on a fully validated representation. The resulting model was assessed through basic driving scenarios with different steering inputs and configurations. The simulations showed stable model behavior and physically plausible interaction between the subsystems. The all-wheel-drive configuration produced symmetric wheel responses in longitudinal driving, while counter-phase rear axle steering increased the yaw response and reduced the simulated turning circle diameter compared with front axle steering only. The circular driving scenario further indicated bounded roll and slip behavior. Overall, the implemented CarMaker model provides a traceable and functional simulation basis for the PixKit vehicle. It can support future model refinement, calibration with real vehicle data and development with the goal of creating a validated digital twin architecture.
2611.24646.comment: 9 pages, 10 figures. Supplementary project files are available at https://git-ce.rwth-aachen.de/asil-lab-cologne/03_publications/02_pixkitcmdigtwin

llm.title_ja: デジタルツインアーキテクチャの基礎としてのモジュール式全輪駆動ロボットADSテストプラットフォームの概念的車両全体モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: IPG CarMakerを用いてモジュール式電動テストプラットフォームPixKitの物理ベースの拡張可能な車両全体シミュレーションモデルを開発し、デジタルツインの基礎を提供する。
llm.problem: 将来のデジタルツイン応用のための低レベル基盤となる、4輪独立インホイールモータや後輪操舵などの特殊な車両特性を統合した拡張可能な物理ベースモデルが求められている。
llm.method: メーカーのドキュメントや派生値、工学的仮定に基づいてIPG CarMaker内で主要車両サブシステムをシステムレベルで統合する。
llm.result: 基本走行シナリオにおけるシミュレーションにより、安定したモデル動作と、全輪駆動や後輪操舵による妥当な車両応答が確認された。
llm.limitation: 車両の完全な測定データがまだ利用可能ではないため、メーカー文書や仮定に基づいたパラメータ化となっている
keywords_ja: 車両シミュレーション
自動運転テストプラットフォーム

2611.24631.title: Hydrodynamics of robotic micro-swimmers in confinement
2611.24631.abstract: Inspired by seminal work by E.M. Purcell, we discuss the problem of predicting and optimizing the performance of autonomous robots swimming in confinement. Our approach is based on the explicit numerical resolution of the fluid flow induced by the swimmer, and it is validated experimentally on a cm-size prototype composed of a cargo head and a rotating propulsive tail. Using hydrodynamic scaling, we predict the performance of replicas of our prototype scaled down to mm- and sub-mm-size to test the feasibility of autonomous micro-robots navigating in narrow vessels. The main result of our theoretical, computational, and experimental analysis is that, while hydrodynamics seems to place no fundamental obstruction to the vision of autonomous micro-robots navigating in narrow lumens inside the human body, it does provide useful and strict guidelines for rational design at different length scales.

llm.title_ja: 狭隘空間におけるロボット型マイクロスイマーの流体力学
llm.tldr_ja: 自律型マイクロスイマーの性能予測と最適化を目的とし、流体流れの数値解法とcmサイズ試作機による実験的検証を行って設計指針を導出した。
llm.problem: 狭隘空間を遊泳する自律型ロボットの性能を予測し最適化する課題がある。
llm.method: 流体流れの明示的な数値解析と、貨物ヘッドと回転推進テールを持つcmサイズ試作機を用いた実験的検証。
llm.result: 流体力学は自律型マイクロスイマーの実現を妨げず、異なる長さスケールでの合理的設計のための明確な指針を与えることが分かった。

2611.24585.title: SHAPE: Discrete Supervision and Parallel Continuous Streams for Learning Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Human Data
2611.24585.abstract: Egocentric human recordings are far cheaper than dexterous robot demonstrations, promising stronger pretraining and direct skill learning without task-specific robot data. Yet humans and robots differ in morphology and kinematics, so human recordings lack the joint positions and actuator commands that supervise robot policies, providing only retargeted end-effector (EEF) actions. This raises two questions: how human data should supervise the policy, and how a dexterous robot should read out actions at deployment. We address both in SHAPE (Supervision from Human Action tokens with Parallel Executable streams), a vision-language-action (VLA) model whose backbone predicts discrete action tokens of EEF chunks as an auxiliary task, while a shared flow-matching expert outputs two executable streams, EEF and joint. On a bimanual robot with 22-DoF hands, a matched study shows that discrete supervision helps learn from human data, driving backbone gradients and shaping action-informative representations across domains. Under standard control pipelines at deployment, direct joint readout excels at fine-grained control with robot demonstrations, scoring 0.80 across six tasks against 0.63 for π0.5, whereas IK-based EEF readout excels at human-to-robot transfer. Pretrained with human data and discrete tokens, SHAPE learns new tasks from human demonstrations without task-specific robot data.

llm.title_ja: SHAPE：器用なマニピュレーション学習のための離散的指導と並列連続ストリーム
