llm.tldr_ja: 人間とロボットの形態差を克服するため、離散アクションと並列実行可能な連続ストリームを予測するVLAモデルSHAPEを提案した。
llm.problem: 人間のデモには関節位置やアクチュエータ指令が含まれず、形態やキネマティクスが異なるロボットポリシーの指導に利用するのが困難である。
llm.method: エンドエフェクタの離散アクションと関節・エンドエフェクタの連続ストリームを予測するVLAモデルSHAPEの提案。
llm.result: 離散的指導が人間データからの学習を促進し、タスク固有のロボットデータなしでの新規タスク学習を実現した。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2611.24585.tldr_en: Pretrained with human data and discrete tokens, SHAPE learns new tasks from human demonstrations without task-specific robot data, and shows that discrete supervision helps learn from human data, driving backbone gradients and shaping action-informative representations across domains.

2611.24579.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
2611.24579.abstract: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder. We introduce ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates native foundation model features between image observations. Given an anchor image, ALIVE uses subsequent events to transport and correct existing multi-layer features extracted by a frozen DINOv3 encoder. Its lightweight updater is trained end-to-end using only synthetic data, without downstream task supervision, and transfers directly to real-world event streams without any adaptation. Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric. On DSEC, when the anchor frame is 200,ms old, ALIVE improves over anchor-image predictions by 30.9,mAP in detection, 11.6,mIoU in segmentation, and 15.9% in depth AbsRel. Compared with image re-encoding, ALIVE reduces FLOPs by 82.4% and latency by a factor of 2.5.

llm.title_ja: ALIVE：イベントベースで基盤モデルの素性を活性化する
llm.tldr_ja: 画像観測間のビジュアル特徴量をインクリメンタルに更新するため、イベントデータを活用する軽量なアップデート手法ALIVEを提案した。
llm.problem: 画像観測の変化に伴い視覚基盤モデルの特徴量が陳腐化し、高価な画像エンコーダの再実行が必要になる。
llm.method: アンカー画像と後続のイベントを用いて、凍結されたDINOv3エンコーダの特徴量を転送・修正する軽量アップデータの導入。
llm.result: 合成データのみで学習しつつ実世界へ直接転移可能であり、既存のイベントベース手法を凌駕しつつ計算量を大幅に削減した。
keywords_ja: セマンティックセグメンテーション

2611.24579.tldr_en: Across three real-world datasets and five task-dataset settings spanning object detection, semantic segmentation, and depth estimation, ALIVE outperforms all evaluated event-based methods in every metric.

2611.24558.title: SCR: Detecting Backdoor-Poisoned Samples through Clean-Reference Residuals
2611.24558.abstract: Deep neural networks are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, in which adversaries manipulate model predictions by injecting poisoned samples into training data. Detecting these samples remains challenging because legitimate semantic variation can obscure poisoning-related signals in learned representations. Consequently, class-level statistics used by existing detectors may flag benign feature deviations while overlooking poisoned samples that blend into the class distribution. In this paper, we propose Semantic Counterfactual Residualization (SCR), which uses a small set of clean reference samples to account for benign variation through sample-specific feature reconstruction. SCR identifies poisoned samples by detecting coherent deviations from these clean baselines, without requiring prior knowledge of the attacks. We evaluate SCR through experiments covering twelve dirty-label and clean-label attacks across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet. With a small clean-reference set, SCR achieves attack-averaged true positive rates above 99.5\% and false positive rates below 2\% on each dataset, outperforming eight representative detection baselines in macro-TPR.

llm.title_ja: SCR：クリーン参照残差を用いたバックドア汚染サンプルの検出
llm.tldr_ja: 正規の意味的変動に起因する誤検知を防ぎつつバックドア汚染サンプルを検出するため、少数のクリーン参照サンプルを用いた残差手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 正当な意味的変動が学習表現中の汚染シグナルを隠すため、バックドア攻撃されたサンプルを高精度に検出することが困難である。
llm.method: 少数のクリーン参照サンプルを用いたサンプル固有の特徴再構成により、一貫した偏りを検出するSemantic Counterfactual Residualization（SCR）の提案。
llm.result: 各データセットで攻撃平均真陽性率99.5%超、偽陽性率2%未満を達成し、既存の検出ベースラインを大幅に上回った。

2611.24558.tldr_en: Semantic Counterfactual Residualization (SCR) is proposed, which uses a small set of clean reference samples to account for benign variation through sample-specific feature reconstruction through sample-specific feature reconstruction.

2611.24554.title: TinyARM-X: A Series of Open-Source, Configurable, and Transparent Torque-Controlled Desktop-Scale Robotic Manipulators
2611.24554.abstract: Visuomotor policies have demonstrated that imprecise low-cost robots can autonomously complete complex manipulation tasks. However, most inexpensive manipulators rely on compact and rigidly position-controlled servos for actuation, which complicate simulation, operation, and safety. This work introduces TinyARM-X, a framework for easily manufacturable, configurable, and torque-controllable low-cost (<350 USD) serial manipulators. By using a single hardware/software architecture, a <7 Degree of Freedom (DoF) TinyARM can be manually reconfigured to an operational >3 DoF robot within 10 min. Actuator modeling and dynamic compensation enable torque-controlled applications like mixed-reality impedance control teleoperation and simulator force feedback rendering. Experiments include mechanical benchmarking and real-world force-aware telemanipulation. The TinyARM-7 has a payload of 33.5 g, a max speed of 0.77 m/s, and a reach of 210 mm. Moreover, with dynamic compensation, the robot has a backdrive-breakaway force of 1.4 N and a backdrive-running force of 0.7 N. Additionally, Cartesian-Impedance Control (CIC) attains a translational stiffness of >15 N/m. Lastly, the TinyARM-X stack is open-sourced to disseminate accessible desktop-scale torque-controlled robotic manipulation to the community.
2611.24554.comment: 9 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to a robotics Journal. Reviews have not come in yet

llm.title_ja: TinyARM-X：オープンソースで設定可能かつ透明なトルク制御型デスクトップマニピュレータ
llm.tldr_ja: 低コストで容易に製造・設定可能なトルク制御型シリアルマニピュレータ群TinyARM-Xを開発し、そのハードウェアとソフトウエアを公開した。
llm.problem: 安価なマニピュレータの多くは位置制御サーボに依存しており、シミュレーション、動作、安全性が複雑化する。
llm.method: 単一のハードウェア・ソフトウェアアーキテクチャを用いた、低コストで手動再設定可能なトルク制御型マニピュレータフレームワークの構築。
llm.result: アクチュエータモデリングと動的補償により、インピーダンス制御テレオペレーションやシミュレータの力覚フィードバックを実現した。

2611.24554.tldr_en: TinyARM-X is introduced, a framework for easily manufacturable, configurable, and torque-controllable low-cost low-cost serial manipulators and the TinyARM-X stack is open-sourced to disseminate accessible desktop-scale torque-controlled robotic manipulation to the community.

2611.24512.title: Comparing Each Generation with Independent Siblings Gives Video World Model Post-Training a Proper Objective for Outcome Frequencies
2611.24512.abstract: Video world models are used as simulators, so when a first frame leaves several physical outcomes open, repeated generations should produce each outcome as often as it occurs in the data. Physics post-training scores every generation against the single recorded future of its history, which makes single videos more faithful, but the expected score is linear in the model distribution and is maximized by always producing the most likely outcome. The log-likelihood of the recorded outcome is maximized by the data distribution, and its gradient weights agreement with the record by the inverse of how often the model produces the generated outcome, a frequency that other generations of the same history with independent noise, its siblings, can estimate. To train with this weight from a finite group, we propose SibPO, which performs Sibling-paired Policy Optimization: siblings estimate a truncated inverse-frequency weight for agreement with the record, and a second term subtracts the same weight times the agreement with the siblings, which makes the expected objective a strictly proper divergence over outcome cells at every group size. On PisaBench, SibPO lowers the KS distance to simulated landing times by 9.1-10.2% relative to the strongest method outside its reward family on three of four video models without degrading single videos, and it lowers the error of estimated robot policy success rates by 13%.

llm.title_ja: 各世代と独立した兄弟の比較によるビデオ世界モデルの適切な事後学習目的関数の設計
llm.tldr_ja: ビデオ世界モデルの事後学習において結果の頻度を正しく評価するため、兄弟ペアリングポリシー最適化（SibPO）を提案した。
llm.problem: 物理事後学習において単一の記録された将来と生成結果を比較すると、モデルは常に最も確率の高い結果を出力するように偏る。
llm.method: 兄弟ペアを用いて切り捨て逆頻度重み付き合意を推定するSibling-paired Policy Optimization（SibPO）の提案。
llm.result: PisaBenchにおいて、単一動画の品質を損なうことなくシミュレートされた着陸時間のKS距離やロボットポリシー成功率の誤差を低減した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.24511.title: OmniFish: A Bioinspired, Modular, Reconfigurable Soft Robotic Fish Enabling Multi-Modal Swimming
2611.24511.abstract: In this work, we introduce OmniFish, a bioinspired modular soft robotic fish designed to emulate the full spectrum of body and/or caudal fin (BCF) locomotion modes within a single robotic platform. The design combines morphology averaging across representative fish species with a tendon-driven compliant segmented spine whose effective stiffness can be reconfigured through progressive mechanical jamming. By selectively constraining body segments, OmniFish shifts deformation from whole-body undulation to posterior body bending and localized tail oscillation, enabling bioinspired Anguilliform, Subcarangiform, Carangiform, Thunniform, and Ostraciiform swimming using a single tendon-driven actuator. The design was guided by morphometric analysis and evaluated through caudal-fin thrust characterization, numerical body-drag simulations, kinematic analysis, and swimming performance experiments. Kinematic analysis confirmed the intended robot transition from distributed body undulation to localized tail oscillation. Swimming experiments demonstrated distinct mode-dependent performance, with the Ostraciiform configuration achieving the highest straight-line velocity of 8.14 cm/s and the lowest cost of transport of 2.42 at 1.5 tail beats/s. These proof-of-concept results show that a mechanically simple stiffness-reconfigurable architecture can generate distinct BCF swimming modes and provide a versatile strategy for developing multimodal soft robotic fish.
2611.24511.comment: Under review at Bioinspiration & Biomimetics. 10 figures, 7 tables

llm.title_ja: OmniFish：多様な遊泳モードを実現する生体模倣型モジュール式再構成可能ソフトロボットフィッシュ
llm.tldr_ja: 単一の駆動機構で多様な遊泳モードを実現するため、剛性を再構成可能な腱駆動式セグメント脊椎を持つソフトロボットフィッシュを開発した。
llm.problem: 単一のロボットプラットフォームで多様な魚類の遊泳モードを包括的にエミュレートすることが困難である。
llm.method: 形態平均化と、機械的ジャミングにより有効剛性を変更できる腱駆動式コンプライアント脊椎を組み合わせた設計の採用。
llm.result: オストラシフォーム形態において最高直線速度8.14 cm/sを達成し、単一の単純な機構で多様な遊泳モードを生成できることを示した。

2611.24511.tldr_en: The proof-of-concept results show that a mechanically simple stiffness-reconfigurable architecture can generate distinct BCF swimming modes and provide a versatile strategy for developing multimodal soft robotic fish.

2611.24499.title: Single-Controller Teleoperation and Multimodal Dataset Generation for a Mobile Manipulator
2611.24499.abstract: Robot learning systems require synchronized, high-quality demonstrations that combine visual, proprioceptive, and action data. However, collecting such datasets with mobile manipulators is often slowed down by fragmented teleoperation interfaces and manual post-processing workflows. This paper presents an integrated framework for teleoperated multimodal data collection on a Clearpath Dingo-O mobile base equipped with a Kinova Gen3 Lite manipulator and an Intel RealSense RGB-D camera. The framework combines single-controller operation of the base, arm, and recording process with an automated ROS-based pipeline for data capture, image-quality filtering, temporal synchronization, visualization, and export to machine-learning-ready Zarr datasets. We validate the system on a pick-and-place mobile-manipulation task in which the robot transports a bottle between two surfaces. The results show that the unified controller supports complete task execution and recording without external commands, while the data pipeline produces synchronized datasets for short demonstrations and identifies corrupted visual frames. The proposed framework provides a practical basis for producing structured demonstrations for robot-learning research.

llm.title_ja: 移動マニピュレータのための単一コントローラ遠隔操作およびマルチモーダルデータセット生成
llm.tldr_ja: 移動マニピュレータのデータ収集を効率化するため、単一コントローラによる遠隔操作と自動ROSパイプラインを統合したフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 移動マニピュレータのデータ収集は、断片化された遠隔操作インタフェースや手動のポスト処理ワークフローによって遅延する。
llm.method: 移動ベース、アーム、記録プロセスの単一コントローラ操作と、データフィルタリングや同期を行うROSベースの自動パイプラインの統合。
llm.result: 統合コントローラにより外部コマンドなしでのタスク実行と記録が可能になり、機械学習用Zarrデータセットを構築できた。

2611.24499.tldr_en: An integrated framework for teleoperated multimodal data collection on a Clearpath Dingo-O mobile base equipped with a Kinova Gen3 Lite manipulator and an Intel RealSense RGB-D camera is presented.

2611.24494.title: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback
2611.24494.abstract: Vision-language-action policies control embodied agents through a perception-action loop grounded in physical interaction, where adversarial patches can corrupt action predictions and thereby alter subsequent observations. To mitigate these threats, many existing defenses rely on policy adaptation or auxiliary models, but require additional training or inference. We introduce RECLAIM, a training-free, inference-time defense that uses a frozen VLA's own attention response to local visual interventions to guide purification during closed-loop embodied manipulation. Our key insight is that attention changes induced by local edits provide feedback for choosing where and how to purify as the robot interacts with its environment. RECLAIM combines this feedback with robot geometry to refine patch localization and select local treatments, then revalidates them as the agent's embodied actions change the observed scene. We evaluate RECLAIM against patches generated by four adversarial attack methods across multiple manipulation task suites under frozen VLA control. Under adversarial patch attacks, RECLAIM succeeds in at least one rollout on 95% of the evaluated tasks and raises rollout success on LIBERO-Object from 0% without defense to 70.0%. Its mean decision time is only 548.9 ms per control step. These results highlight policy-guided visual purification as an effective approach to defending embodied agents against adversarial patches and recovering closed-loop task execution.

llm.title_ja: RECLAIM：身体化されたアテンションフィードバックに基づくロボット視覚情報活用型敵対的パッチ防御
llm.tldr_ja: 閉ループでのビ山タスクにおいて敵対的パッチからVLAポリシーを防護するため、凍結されたVLAのアテンションフィードバックを用いた防御手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 敵対的パッチが行動予測を改竄し、その後の観測を変化させることでVLAポリシーを誤動作させる脅威がある。
llm.method: 局所的な視覚的介入に対する凍結VLAの自己のアテンション応答を利用し、閉ループ操作中の浄化を誘導するRECLAIMの導入。
llm.result: LIBERO-Objectタスクでの成功率を0%から70%に向上させ、閉ループタスク実行の復旧に成功した。

2611.24494.tldr_en: RecLAIM is introduced, a training-free, inference-time defense that uses a frozen VLA's own attention response to local visual interventions to guide purification during closed-loop embodied manipulation.

2611.24482.title: Latent Action Policies from Suboptimal Data
2611.24482.abstract: Latent Action Models (LAMs) learn control representations from action-free video, but existing pipelines typically train latent policies with behavioral cloning, without an explicit policy improvement objective. Although offline RL offers a natural approach to policy improvement, standard methods do not transfer directly to learned latent action spaces. We find that the structure of learned latent actions makes naive offline RL unreliable: directly maximizing value over latent actions or fitting a unimodal policy can produce latent actions that cannot be realized by physical execution, while the latent representation can merge physical controls that receive different rewards. To understand when latent-space optimization remains valid, we derive conditions under which policy improvement transfers to decoded execution and under which latent and physical optima align. Building on these insights, we propose LAPIS for goal-conditioned latent policy improvement, grounding value-based policy improvement in observed state-latent transitions and using a conditional flow policy to capture their multimodal structure. LAPIS outperforms baselines on most tasks, with the clearest gains in visual manipulation, and remains effective even with only 1% action labels, where competing methods largely collapse.

llm.title_ja: サブオプティマルデータからの潜在行動ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 行動なし動画から制御表現を学ぶ潜在行動モデルに対し、状態-潜在遷移に基づく目標条件付き方策改善手法LAPISを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の潜在行動モデルは方策改善の目的関数を持たず、素朴なオフライン強化学習を適用すると物理的に実現不可能な行動が生成される。
llm.method: 観測された状態-潜在遷移に基づき、条件付きフロー方策を用いてマルチモーダル構造を捉えるLAPISの提案。
llm.result: 視覚的マニピュレーションタスクにおいて既存手法を凌駕し、行動ラベルが1%しかない状況でも有効性を示した。

2611.24482.tldr_en: This work derives conditions under which policy improvement transfers to decoded execution and under which latent and physical optima align, and proposes LAPIS for goal-conditioned latent policy improvement, grounding value-based policy improvement in observed state-latent transitions and using a conditional flow policy to capture their multimodal structure.

2611.24994.title: What the model knows but does not say: monitoring medical LLMs through verbalized thoughts
2611.24994.abstract: Efforts to keep clinical language models safe have concentrated on what enters and leaves the model, but a manipulated model can return an answer that looks entirely ordinary. Here we show that the model's own internal state, rendered in plain language, exposes manipulations the output conceals. Using a natural-language autoencoder, we translate the activations of a multimodal LLM (Gemma-3-27B) into text and let an input-blind judge read this verbalized internal state (the thoughts channel) and the model's answer separately. Across two clinical attack objectives (omitting a pathology, covertly recommending a drug), two input modalities, and two delivery mechanisms, the thoughts channel caught the injection significantly more often than the answer in all eight injected conditions (p<0.05), while both channels held near-zero false-positive rates on clean inputs; the omission result carried over to Llama-3.3-70B. The thoughts channel also registered unsafe clinical requests as harmful while the model was still reading them, before it decided whether to refuse. None of this requires retraining: an off-the-shelf verbalizer and a general-purpose judge are enough.

llm.title_ja: モデルが知っているが言わないこと：言語化された思考を通じた医療用LLMの監視
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダルLLMの内部活性化を自然言語オートエンコーダでテキストに翻訳し、出力とは別に監査することで、出力が隠蔽する悪意ある操作や有害なリクエストを効果的に検出できることを示した。
llm.problem: 臨床用言語モデルの安全性維持は入力と出力の監視に集中しているが、操作されたモデルは一見普通の回答を返すことができる。
llm.method: マルチモーダルLLMの活性化をテキスト（思考チャンネル）に翻訳し、出力から切り離された入力非依存のジャッジモデルに読ませて悪意や操作を検出する。
llm.result: すべての臨床攻撃条件下において、思考チャンネルは回答よりも有意に高い頻度でインジェクションや有害なリクエストを検出し、誤検知率も低く抑えられた。

2611.24994.tldr_en: This work shows that the model's own internal state, rendered in plain language, exposes manipulations the output conceals, and translates the activations of a multimodal LLM into text and lets an input-blind judge read this verbalized internal state and the model's answer separately.

2611.24470.title: When to Refine: Selective Search for Frozen Visual World Models
2611.24470.abstract: Planning with a visual world model requires deciding both which actions to execute and how long to search for them. We introduce Selective CEM Refinement (SCR), a learned rule for deciding whether to continue cross-entropy method (CEM) search with a frozen LeWorldModel. After five it- erations, the gate measures how far the mean first action chunk has moved, how much the mean terminal cost of elite plans has fallen, and how widely their first chunks vary. It returns the current plan for execution or continues the same search for ten more iterations. The gate requires no addi- tional world-model rollout. On 16 PushT scenes evaluated with two planning seeds, SCR succeeded in 25 of 32 trials, compared with 28 of 32 for fixed 15-iteration search (Fixed-15). All 25 SCR suc- cesses occurred in trials that Fixed-15 also solved, yield- ing 89.29% paired success retention. Across complete episodes, including replanning, SCR evaluated 23.81% fewer candidate plans and reduced mean controller time per eight-environment batch by 17.22%. Its observed suc- cess rate was 5.36 percentage points above an analytic mix- ture of the two fixed-depth controllers at the same expected candidate workload, although the difference changed sign across planning seeds. Compared with gating only at the initial solve under the same random-draw padding proto- col, gating again at replanning produced nine additional early exits. This reduced total candidate evaluations by 15.79%, while successes fell from 27 to 25.

llm.title_ja: いつ洗練すべきか：凍結視覚世界モデルのための選択的探索
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚世界モデルを用いた計画において計算コストを削減するため、探索を継続するか決定する学習済みルールSCRを提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚世界モデルを用いた計画では、どの行動を実行するか、そして探索をどれだけ継続すべきかを決定する必要がある。
llm.method: クロスエントロピー法（CEM）の探索途中において、平均行動チャンクの変化量やエリート計画のコスト低下等を測定して探索の継続・終了を判定するSCRの導入。
llm.result: 固定反復の探索と比較して、計画候補の評価回数を大幅に削減しつつ同等の成功率を維持した。

2611.24470.tldr_en: This work introduces Selective CEM Refinement (SCR), a learned rule for deciding whether to continue cross-entropy method (CEM) search with a frozen LeWorldModel, and measures how far the mean first action chunk has moved, how much the mean terminal cost of elite plans has fallen, and how widely their first chunks vary.

2611.24455.title: Homeward: No Place Like the Training View
2611.24455.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies implicitly assume that third-person cameras remain fixed at their data-collection poses; once a camera is bumped, remounted, or swapped at deployment, task success degrades precipitously even though the underlying task and robot remain unchanged. We present Homeward, a training-free, plug-and-play observation adapter that canonicalizes observations from an uncalibrated deployment camera back into the training view for frozen VLA policies. Our design stems from a closed-loop diagnostic paradox in simulation: while re-rendering perturbed views into the training camera with oracle geometry recovers much of the lost performance, substituting an off-the-shelf feed-forward 3D foundation model can leave the policy worse off than applying no correction at all. This degradation concentrates on the thin, articulated robot arm, which feed-forward depth prediction tears and scatters - yet the arm's exact 3D state is already known from robot kinematics. Homeward exploits this asymmetry: it estimates what is unknown - camera parameters and static scene depth - from the live RGB frame and a single training-view reference, and renders what is known - the moving robot links - directly from the kinematic model. Evaluated across $\sim$300,000 closed-loop episodes spanning four frozen VLAs, Homeward boosts success across all 1,599 camera variants of LIBERO-Plus from 62.5%, 76.5%, 68.0%, and 3.6% to 77.6%, 95.1%, 91.2%, and 26.4% for OpenVLA-OFT, $π_{0.5}$, $π_0$, and OpenVLA, respectively. Without any scene fine-tuning or deployment camera calibration, Homeward extends to 6-DoF random placements, focal-length changes, and, with per-step pose estimation, continuous intra-episode camera drift, while matching or surpassing a calibrated, scene-trained view-synthesis baseline on three of four policies on LIBERO-Plus.
2611.24455.comment: 22 pages, including supplementary material; author metadata simplified; paper content unchanged

llm.title_ja: Homeward：学習時の視点に勝る場所なし
llm.tldr_ja: デプロイ時のカメラ位置のずれによるVLAポリシーの性能低下を防ぐため、観測画像を学習時の視点に変換するアダプターHomewardを提案した。
llm.problem: デプロイ時にカメラが動かされると、背後のタスクやロボットが同じであってもVLAポリシーのタスク成功率が急激に低下する。
llm.method: ライブRGB画像と1枚の学習視点参照からカメラパラメータや静的背景深度を推定し、移動するロボットリンクは運動学モデルから直接描画するHomewardの提案。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plusの1,599種類のカメラバリエーションにおいて、追加のシーンファインチューニングなしで複数の凍結VLAの成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.24455.tldr_en: Homeward is a training-free, plug-and-play observation adapter that canonicalizes observations from an uncalibrated deployment camera back into the training view for frozen VLA policies, and exploits asymmetry in the kinematic model to renders what is known - the moving robot links - directly from the kinematic model.

2611.24424.title: Constructive Infinitely Differentiable Guidance Vector Fields for Robotic Control
2611.24424.abstract: Guidance vector fields (GVFs) are a popular framework for tasks such as robotic path-following and multi-robot motion coordination, but existing approaches may be non-differentiable or have large derivatives, limiting their use in controllers that require derivatives of the guidance signal, which is common when the GVF is used as an input in a cascaded controller. This paper proposes an infinitely differentiable constructive GVF. The resulting vector field depends on a smoothing parameter and is a generalization of [1], recovering the original GVF in the limit as this parameter approaches zero. It also admits a simple and efficient implementation that preserves smoothness under discretization and can reduce computation time by using substantially fewer curve samples while maintaining small path-following errors. We establish the main theoretical properties and demonstrate its practical advantages through numerical and real-world experiments.

llm.title_ja: ロボット制御のための構成的無限回微分可能な誘導ベクトル場
llm.tldr_ja: カスケードコントローラ等での利用に適した、滑らかさを保持する無限回微分可能な構成的誘導ベクトル場を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の誘導ベクトル場は非微分可能性や大きな導関数を持つため、微分信号を必要とするコントローラでの利用が制限される。
llm.method: 平滑化パラメータに依存し、極限で元のベクトル場を復元する、無限回微分可能な構成的誘導ベクトル場の提案。
llm.result: 離散化後も滑らかさを保持し、曲線サンプル数を大幅に削減しつつ小さな経路追従誤差を維持できることを数値・実機実験で示した。

2611.24424.tldr_en: An infinitely differentiable constructive GVF that preserves smoothness under discretization and can reduce computation time by using substantially fewer curve samples while maintaining small path-following errors is proposed.

2611.24376.title: Teaching VLMs What to Say, Not How to Reason: Rethinking Counterfactual Reasoning in Autonomous Driving
2611.24376.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving systems have been shown to suffer from shortcut learning and causal confusion, limiting their ability to generalize robustly under distribution shift. To mitigate these limitations, recent works based on Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have explored incorporating linguistic reasoning capabilities into driving decision-making, reporting improvements in driving performance. In particular, counterfactual (CF) reasoning has been proposed to enable self-reflective, high-level causal understanding. However, it remains unclear whether the language-based reasoning mitigates shortcut learning or merely shifts it from visual representations to linguistic patterns, creating an illusion of causal understanding. Moreover, existing approaches often conflate intervention-based reasoning with CF reasoning, leaving the effects of genuine CF reasoning unexplored. In this work, we examine what CF reasoning actually induces in VLM-based autonomous driving and observe that it shifts the action distribution toward more conservative behaviors while increasing uncertainty in reasoning and decision-making. This effect persists under reinforcement fine-tuning, suggesting that it is not merely a transient artifact. Furthermore, visual attention analysis shows that CF reasoning does not alter visual grounding, while causal intervention experiments reveal that masking causally relevant and non-causal factors in accident scenarios results in comparable decision change rates. Overall, these results suggest that CF reasoning does not induce genuine causal reasoning grounded in visual evidence. Instead, it acts as a linguistic shortcut that reshapes the action distribution, teaching models what to say but not how to reason, highlighting a gap between language-based reasoning and causal understanding in autonomous driving.
2611.24376.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Main Track (41 pages, 14 figures, 14 tables). Project page: https://ophd-hahao.github.io/projects/Rethink-CF/

llm.title_ja: VLMに「何を言うか」を教え、「推論の方法」は教えない：自動運転における反実仮想推論の再考
llm.tldr_ja: VLMベースの自動運転における反実仮想推論を検証し、それが真の因果推論ではなく行動分布を変化させる言語的ショートカットとして機能することを明らかにした。
llm.problem: VLMを用いたエンド端自動運転における反実仮想推論が、真の因果理解をもたらしているのか単なる言語的パターンへのシフトなのかが不明確である。
llm.method: 反実仮想推論がもたらす行動分布、視覚的グランディング、因果介入実験を通じた詳細な分析の実施。
llm.result: 反実仮想推論は視覚的証拠に裏付けられた真の因果推論を誘発せず、保守的な行動へバイアスをかける言語的ショートカットとして働くことを示した。

2611.24376.tldr_en: Examining what CF reasoning actually induces in VLM-based autonomous driving suggests that it acts as a linguistic shortcut that reshapes the action distribution, teaching models what to say but not how to reason, highlighting a gap between language-based reasoning and causal understanding in autonomous driving.

2611.24375.title: SearchDiffusion: Information-Guided Diffusion Planning for Object Search
2611.24375.abstract: Object search in unknown environments requires robots to gather useful observations while avoiding obstacles and accounting for limited sensor visibility. We present SearchDiffusion, a diffusion-based planner that generates position and heading trajectories using a learned dense utility map. The map represents geometric accessibility, useful visibility, and semantic progress. It conditions trajectory generation and provides an objective for sampling guidance. Sampled map hypotheses provide additional geometric context, while geometric and heading guidance, validity checks, and analytical selection support execution. Across 90 simulated tasks on 24 map layouts, SearchDiffusion achieved 95.6\% target detection at greater computational cost. Ablations show complementary benefits from utility and guidance, with limited additional detection benefit from runtime map hypotheses. In ten physical quadruped trials using OneMap relevance maps, eight were successful under operator assessment, without fine-tuning on real-robot data. These results support combining learned spatial utility with guided trajectory generation for object search under partial observability.

llm.title_ja: SearchDiffusion：物体探索のための情報誘導型拡散プランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 未知環境での物体探索を効率化するため、学習済み密集ユーティリティマップを用いた拡散ベースの軌道生成プランナーを提案した。
llm.problem: 未知環境での物体探索では、限られたセンサー視界を考慮しつつ障害物を避けながら有用な観測を収集する必要がある。
llm.method: 幾何学的アクセス可能性や有用な視覚性、セマンティックな進捗を表す学習済み密集ユーティリティマップを利用する拡散プランナーSearchDiffusionの提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションでの高い目標検出率を達成し、実機の四足ロボットを用いた実験でもファインチューニングなしで成功することを確認した。

2611.24375.tldr_en: The results support combining learned spatial utility with guided trajectory generation for object search under partial observability, and show complementary benefits from utility and guidance, with limited additional detection benefit from runtime map hypotheses.

2611.24360.title: Towards Pose-Robust Few-Shot Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.24360.abstract: Fine-tuning a vision-language-action (VLA) model on a few dozen demonstrations is the standard way to put a manipulation policy on a robot, yet the resulting policy silently assumes that the camera and the robot base stay exactly where they were during data collection: a bumped tripod or a base re-docked a few centimetres away makes it reach for the wrong place. We show that both failures are one phenomenon, a change of the camera-to-base extrinsic that the policy has memorised, and that the robot carries everything needed to undo it. We introduce WACO, a world-anchored canonicalization framework for VLA models: the arm, placed by forward kinematics at the measured joint angles, serves as a metric calibration target, and the static scene serves as the world anchor that tells a moved camera from a moved robot. From a single RGB-D frame, WACO estimates both shifts without ground-truth extrinsics or extra data, canonicalises the image to the calibration viewpoint and the state, action and start pose to the calibration base frame, and fine-tunes the unmodified policy under the artefacts of its own estimator. We also introduce LIBERO-PoseShift, the first benchmark for RGB VLAs with graded camera, base and compound shifts. Across LIBERO-PoseShift, the LIBERO-Plus camera track and four real-world tasks on a UR5e robot, WACO consistently outperforms the standard few-shot recipe and prior viewpoint-robust methods, raising shifted success by 13.2 points in simulation and by 36.7 points on the real robot, recovering 90% of the simulation gap to a ground-truth oracle and 87% of the real-robot gap, and establishing a new state of the art among methods that use no perturbed training data, with no test-time calibration. Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/WACO/.
2611.24360.comment: 17 pages, 13 figures, 17 tables (including supplementary material). Project page: https://peacelwh.github.io/WACO/

llm.title_ja: 姿勢ロバストな少数ショット視覚言語行動モデルに向けて
llm.tldr_ja: カメラやベースのわずかな位置ずれに対応するため、ロボットアームを較正ターゲットとしてワールドアンカー推定を行うWACOフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: カメラやベースがわずかにずれただけで、VLAポリシーは誤った位置に手を伸ばすなどの失敗を引き起こす。
llm.method: 順運動学で配置されたアームを較正ターゲットとし、静的シーンをワールドアンカーとして利用してずれを推定・正規化するWACOの提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機のUR5eロボットにおいて、追加の事前学習データなしで位置ずれに対する成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.24360.tldr_en: WACO is introduced, a world-anchored canonicalization framework for VLA models: the arm, placed by forward kinematics at the measured joint angles, serves as a metric calibration target, and the static scene serves as the world anchor that tells a moved camera from a moved robot.

2611.24327.title: Pixel2Perspective: A Benchmark for Multi-Modal and Multi-View Generalization in Vision-Language Models
2611.24327.abstract: Embodied AI systems, such as drones and autonomous vehicles, improve navigation by enhancing perception in environments containing unseen objects. While Visual Language Models (VLMs) offer strong image understanding, their real-world application is underexplored. For effective deployment, open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) models, leveraging models like CLIP to assign pixel-level labels from text, must be robust to outdoor conditions, adverse weather, and varying viewpoints. Despite their potential, these models encounter significant challenges in cross-domain generalization, hindering their practical use in embodied AI applications. In this work, we present Pixel2Perspective, a benchmark for multi-angle object localization and open-vocabulary segmentation across both aerial and ground perspectives. This benchmark supports thorough evaluation across different viewpoints and sensor modalities. We assess foundational models like CLIP and advanced OVSS models using a curated dataset that spans varied outdoor conditions, sim-to-real scenarios, and multiple sensors, including infrared, to support the development of robust and generalizable perception systems. We also present a novel framework, Multi-Source RGB-IR Uncertainty Quantification (MSRIQ), which jointly models aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties across RGB and infrared imagery. This approach supports robust evaluation of open-vocabulary segmentation models across diverse environmental conditions. Our work sets a robustness-driven benchmark, providing key insights and laying the foundation for future research in open-world embodied AI perception. The benchmark and project page are available at https://aniruddhsikdar1.github.io/publications/pixel2perspective/

llm.title_ja: Pixel2Perspective：視覚言語モデルにおけるマルチモーダル・マルチビュー汎化のためのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な視点やセンサー条件の下でオープンボキャブラリーセグメンテーションモデルを評価するため、新ベンチマークと不確実性定量化手法を提案した。
llm.problem: オープンボキャブラリーセグメンテーションモデルは、屋外の環境変化や多様な視点に対するドメイン汎化において大きな課題に直面している。
llm.method: 空撮と地上視点を網羅したマルチアングル物体局所化・セグメンテーションベンチマークと、RGB-IR統合の不確実性定量化フレームワークの提案。
llm.result: 環境条件が異なる状況下での頑健な評価基盤を提供し、ロボット知覚の汎化性能向上に向けた知見を提示した。
keywords_ja: オープンボキャブラリーセグメンテーション

2611.24327.tldr_en: This work presents Pixel2Perspective, a benchmark for multi-angle object localization and open-vocabulary segmentation across both aerial and ground perspectives, and presents a novel framework, Multi-Source RGB-IR Uncertainty Quantification (MSRIQ), which jointly models aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties across RGB and infrared imagery.

2611.24310.title: Proprioceptive Simultaneous Base and Terrain Elevation Estimation for Legged Robot Locomotion
2611.24310.abstract: Legged robots in visually degraded environments must rely exclusively on proprioceptive sensing, under which global position and yaw are unobservable. Vertical drift is particularly detrimental, as it corrupts the height reference required by swing-leg trajectories and can destabilize the robot. We treat the terrain itself as a persistent proprioceptive landmark: every footstep provides a height measurement that anchors the vertical axis. We propose Simultaneous Base and Elevation Estimation (SBEE), a real-time open-source framework in which a Left-Invariant Extended Kalman Filter (LI-EKF) for floating-base estimation and a grid-based elevation map are coupled in a bidirectional loop, mirroring SLAM with terrain elevation in place of landmarks. Stable foot contacts insert uncertainty-aware height samples into the map, and previously mapped cells are fed back as uncertainty-weighted vertical pseudo-measurements that act analogously to loop closures. Unlike contact-aided invariant filters, the LI-EKF consumes a kinematic velocity measurement instead of augmenting the state with a contact model per leg, so its state dimension is independent of the number of legs. We evaluate SBEE in MuJoCo on quadrupedal and bipedal platforms and on the ANYmal-D GrandTour dataset over 296 m of locomotion, reducing the absolute trajectory error by 22.1% relative to the best of three state-of-the-art proprioceptive estimators.

llm.title_ja: 脚式ロボットの移動に向けた固有感覚に基づくベースおよび地形標高の同時推定
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的劣化環境における脚式ロボットの垂直ドリフトを防ぐため、歩行接触をランドマークに見立てたLI-EKFと標高マップの統合手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚的劣化環境では固有感覚のみに頼らざるを得ず、特に垂直方向のドリフトがスイング脚の軌道を狂わせてロボットを不安定にする。
llm.method: 浮動ベース推定のための左不変拡張カルマンフィルター（LI-EKF）とグリッドベースの標高マップを双方向ループで結合したSBEEフレームワークの提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよびANYmal-Dデータセットを用いた評価において、既存の固有感覚推定位相と比較して絶対軌跡誤差を22.1%削減した。
keywords_ja: 拡張カルマンフィルター

2611.24310.tldr_en: Simultaneous Base and Elevation Estimation (SBEE) is proposed, a real-time open-source framework in which a Left-Invariant Extended Kalman Filter for floating-base estimation and a grid-based elevation map are coupled in a bidirectional loop, mirroring SLAM with terrain elevation in place of landmarks.

2611.24280.title: Remote Teleoperation of Endovascular Robots: A Network Emulation Framework for Systematic Performance Evaluation
2611.24280.abstract: Remote endovascular teleoperation requires network performance to be evaluated in relation to physical navigation and operator experience, while the effects of network degradation on the usability of remote endovascular systems remain insufficiently characterized from the perspective of clinical users. We developed a network emulation and benchmarking framework that combines an endovascular robot with data streaming. We conducted a user study involving eight clinicians from interventional neuroradiology and general interventional radiology and eight engineering students, who performed 480 navigation attempts across 15 network conditions. Communication performance and received video quality were assessed alongside navigation outcomes, confidence, workload and clinician rated acceptability. Under the most impaired combined condition, success was 78.1\%, compared with 93.8\% under the reference condition, and mean attempt time increased from 63.5 to 94.3\,s. At 5\% configured packet loss, 87.5\% of attempts succeeded, although all eight clinicians rated the condition unacceptable. Perceived video quality was associated with clinician confidence and acceptability, with mean within participant Spearman correlations of 0.72 and 0.78, respectively. Framework integration on a second robotic platform additionally supported successful remote navigation over a real network. Our framework provides a reusable basis that can help identify communication bottlenecks and assess their effects on navigation and clinician acceptance for endovascular intervention telesurgery tasks.

llm.title_ja: 血管内ロボットの遠隔操作：体系的性能評価のためのネットワークエミュレーションフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: ネットワーク劣化が血管内遠隔手術の操作性に与える影響を評価するため、血管内ロボットとデータストリーミングを統合したエミュレーションフレームワークを開発した。
llm.problem: ネットワーク劣化がリモート血管内システムの臨床的有用性に与える影響が十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: 血管内ロボットとデータストリーミングを組み合わせ、多様なネットワーク条件下で医師や学生によるユーザスタディを実施するフレームワークの構築。
llm.result: 通信障害の悪化に伴い成功率や作業時間が悪化し、動画品質の知覚が臨床医の信頼度や受容性と相関することを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: ネットワークエミュレーション

2611.24280.tldr_en: A network emulation and benchmarking framework that combines an endovascular robot with data streaming that provides a reusable basis that can help identify communication bottlenecks and assess their effects on navigation and clinician acceptance for endovascular intervention telesurgery tasks.

2611.24279.title: QDD-MM: A Simple and Compact Open-Source Muscle Module with Quasi-Direct-Drive Motor for Tendon-driven Robots
2611.24279.abstract: Tendon-driven robots, which actuate like biological muscles by using motors to wind wires, offer advantages such as variable stiffness and redundant actuation. Despite these advantages, musculoskeletal structures inherently involve a large number of diverse muscles, making it desirable to compactly modularize each muscle unit and flexibly accommodate diverse muscle arrangements. While various small muscle modules have been proposed to date, existing designs tend to be complex, difficult to maintain, and suffer from low backdrivability and limited actuation speed due to their high gear ratios. In this work, we propose QDD-MM, a muscle module that leverages recent advances in quasi-direct-drive motors to achieve a simpler and more compact structure with higher backdrivability and faster actuation than previous modules. By utilizing quasi-direct-drive motors, the module eliminates the need for dedicated force-sensing mechanisms, significantly simplifying the overall design, while also supporting flexible wire routing in multiple directions, various module-to-module connections, and even the use of the module body itself as a structural component. QDD-MM integrates these capabilities into a reusable muscle module, and its design is openly available at https://github.com/haraduka/qddmm. We developed tendon-driven robots with one joint and either two or three muscles, as well as a partial musculoskeletal humanoid, using the proposed QDD-MM and verified their effectiveness. We expect that this muscle module will democratize tendon-driven robotics and further accelerate progress in the field.
2611.24279.comment: Accepted to IEEE-RAS Humanoids 2026, website - https://haraduka.github.io/qddmm/, youtube - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=09xRhZO497k

llm.title_ja: QDD-MM：準ダイレクトドライブモーターを用いた腱駆動ロボット向けのシンプルでコンパクトなオープンソース筋モジュール
llm.tldr_ja: 腱駆動ロボットの構造を簡素化するため、準ダイレクトドライブモーターを活用した高バックドライブ性と小型化を両立する筋モジュールを開発した。
llm.problem: 従来の筋モジュールは構造が複雑でメンテナンスしづらく、高減速比のために高バックドライブ性と高速作動性が制限されていた。
llm.method: 準ダイレクトドライブモーターを採用し、力覚センサーなしで柔軟な配線やモジュール間接続を可能にしたQDD-MMの提案。
llm.result: 1関節ロボットや部分的な筋骨格ヒューマノイドの構築によりその有効性を検証し、オープンソースとして公開した。
keywords_ja: 準ダイレクトドライブ

2611.24273.title: Old Experience, New Lessons: Relabeling Autonomous Robot Rollouts in Interactive Imitation Learning
2611.24273.abstract: Interactive imitation learning enables robots to learn from human interventions during deployment. These interactions naturally produce sparse human corrections and abundant autonomous robot experience without human action labels. Yet existing methods either leave this experience unused for action supervision or imitate historical robot actions, which can reinforce suboptimal behavior. To address this limitation, we propose Set-valued Relabeling of Autonomous experience (SeRA), a framework that learns from autonomous robot experience through set-valued supervision of policy relabels. Later policy checkpoints relabel this experience, and agreement across checkpoints filters the relabels. Since agreement does not guarantee correctness, SeRA constructs desired action sets around accepted relabels. Following Set-Supervised Diffusion Policy (SDP), it trains an action-chunking diffusion policy to increase the probability of actions within these sets. A step-masked denoising loss combines accepted relabels with available human corrections in partially supervised chunks. Experiments across five simulated manipulation tasks in online and offline settings show that SeRA improves policy performance over SDP and outperforms baselines that imitate historical robot actions or exact relabels. On a real-robot tomato-picking task, SeRA achieves 80% success, compared with 40% for SDP, using the same human feedback and training budget. These results demonstrate that relabeled autonomous robot experience can complement human corrections to improve policy performance.

llm.title_ja: 過去の経験の新たな活用：インタラクティブ模倣学習における自律ロボット試行の再ラベリング
llm.tldr_ja: 自律ロボットの経験をセット値の監督により再ラベリングして活用するフレームワークSeRAを提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機タスクでポリシー性能の向上を示した。
llm.problem: 既存の手法は自律的な試行データを活用しないか、過去の最適でない行動をそのまま模倣してしまう。
llm.method: ポリシーのチェックポイント間で合意した再ラベリングを利用し、セット値の監督に基づく拡散ポリシーを学習する。
llm.result: トマト収穫の実機タスクで80%の成功率を達成し、ベースラインやSDPを大きく上回った。

2611.24273.tldr_en: Experiments show that SeRA improves policy performance over SDP and outperforms baselines that imitate historical robot actions or exact relabels and demonstrate that relabeled autonomous robot experience can complement human corrections to improve policy performance.

2611.24258.title: Towards Vacuum-Assisted Robotic Needle Interventions: From Fluid Aspiration to Tissue Biopsy
2611.24258.abstract: Robotic ultrasound-guided needle interventions have primarily focused on target localization and accurate needle placement, while the subsequent acquisition of diagnostic material remains comparatively underexplored. Moreover, pleural fluid aspiration and tissue biopsy are typically addressed as separate procedures, despite sharing common requirements for ultrasound guidance, safe access, and sample transport. This work presents a unified robotic framework for ultrasound-guided fluid and tissue extraction using a single vacuum-assisted end effector. The proposed system combines force controlled ultrasound scanning, semantic target identification, automated needle deployment, and procedure specific material acquisition. A coaxial needle assembly and shared pump assisted pathway enable direct pleural fluid aspiration, while controlled cannula actuation provides the additional cutting action required for solid-tissue acquisition. End-to-end evaluation using a Franka Emika Panda robot over 50 phantom trials achieved successful extraction in 23/25 pleural fluid aspiration trials (92\%) and 22/25 tissue acquisition trials (88\%). Following successful tissue-target access, acquisition and transport were completed in all 22 trials.
2611.24258.comment: 8 pages, 8 figures, Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

llm.title_ja: 真空補助型ロボット針治療に向けて：流体吸引から組織生検まで
llm.tldr_ja: 単一の真空補助エンドエフェクタを用いて超音波ガイド下での胸水吸引と組織生検を統合的に行うロボットフレームワークを提案し、ファントム実験で高い成功率を実証した。
llm.problem: 胸水吸引と組織生検は共通の要件を持つにもかかわらず、従来は別々の手技として扱われ、診断用材料の取得に関する研究は不十分であった。
llm.method: 力制御による超音波スキャン、意味的ターゲット識別、同軸針アセンブリ、制御されたカニューレ作動を単一システムに統合する。
llm.result: ファントムを用いた50回の試行で、胸水吸引は92%、組織生検は88%の成功率を達成した。

2611.24258.tldr_en: This work presents a unified robotic framework for ultrasound-guided fluid and tissue extraction using a single vacuum-assisted end effector that combines force controlled ultrasound scanning, semantic target identification, automated needle deployment, and procedure specific material acquisition.

2611.24247.title: Allocentric Memory, Egocentric Acting: A Dual-Frame VLA for Urban Aerial Navigation
2611.24247.abstract: Language-goal aerial navigation requires a UAV to reach a destination specified in natural language using observations collected during flight. A key challenge is linking changing egocentric perception with spatial evidence anchored to stable locations for long-range navigation. We propose CityNav-VLA, a dual-frame vision-language-action model for urban navigation integrating dynamic egocentric context with persistent allocentric spatial memory. The UAV incrementally accumulates visual observations on a fixed north-up map initialized with geographic and landmark priors, preserving evidence across viewpoint changes. A dynamic query conditioned on the instruction, current observations, UAV state, and motion history retrieves relevant memory evidence to predict a map-frame target. A deterministic controller converts this target into body-frame commands using the UAV's current pose, connecting global reasoning with egocentric execution. To reduce target fluctuations over long horizons, early goal commitment (EGC) fixes the execution target to the coordinate-wise median of the first $K$ predictions without extra trainable parameters. On Test Unseen, CityNav-VLA reduces NE by 21.2% and improves SR and SPL by 15.8% and 30.9%, respectively. It also reduces NE by 6.2% and improves SR and SPL by 5.6% and 23.2%, respectively, relative to the former SOTA after dataset refinement. Cumulative ablations show that navigation-map features yield the largest gains, while metric coordinates further improve endpoint accuracy. With a 4B-scale backbone, inference averages 0.68 s per decision with 8.6 GB peak memory on a single A100, presenting remarkable model efficiency.

llm.title_ja: アロセントリック・メモリとエゴセントリック・アクティング：都市部空中ナビゲーションのためのデュアルフレームVLA
llm.tldr_ja: 動的なエゴセントリック知覚と永続的なアロセントリック空間メモリを統合した都市部空中ナビゲーション用VLAモデルCityNav-VLAを提案し、ナビゲーション性能を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 言語目標に基づく空中ナビゲーションにおいて、変化する自己中心的な知覚と、安定した場所に関連付けられた空間的証拠をリンクさせることが困難である。
llm.method: 地理的・ランドマークの事前情報を持つ北上固定マップ上に視覚観測を蓄積し、動的クエリでメモリから証拠を検索して目標を予測するデュアルフレームVLAを構築する。
llm.result: Test Unseen環境において、ナビゲーション誤差（NE）を21.2%削減し、成功率（SR）とSPLをそれぞれ15.8%および30.9%向上させた。

2611.24247.tldr_en: CityNav-VLA is proposed, a dual-frame vision-language-action model for urban navigation integrating dynamic egocentric context with persistent allocentric spatial memory integrating dynamic egocentric context with persistent allocentric spatial memory.

2611.24244.title: CommDreamer: Radio-Geometric World Models for Mapless Cellular-Connected UAV Trajectory Planning
2611.24244.abstract: Reliable cellular connectivity and collision-free flight are essential for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) operations in low-altitude urban canyons, where dense 3D buildings obstruct flight clearance, shadow serving base stations, and create strong co-channel interference at street intersections. Existing planners either require prior 3D city meshes and channel knowledge maps unavailable onboard, or rely on model-free reinforcement learning with low sample efficiency and poor cross-city generalization. We propose CommDreamer, a mapless radio-geometric world model that fuses raw onboard 3D LiDAR scans, multicell cellular reports, and shift-invariant relative kinematics to jointly infer local obstacle clearance and directional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) dynamics. Using a categorical recurrent state-space model, CommDreamer compresses multimodal measurement histories into a coordinate-invariant latent belief, enabling the UAV to foresee deep shadow zones and train a lightweight online policy purely via multi-step latent imagination without prior maps or antenna patterns. Zero-shot evaluations across unseen urban morphologies in our open-source ray-tracing simulator, AeroCity-RT, show that CommDreamer converges within 150 episodes where model-free reinforcement learning fails to complete flights, achieving 100.0% mission success with zero collisions while lifting median route SINR to 8.02 dB and cutting effective SINR outage by over 50% relative to radio-blind world-model and reactive LiDAR baselines.

llm.title_ja: CommDreamer：マップレス携帯通信接続UAV軌道計画のための無線幾何学的世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: LiDARスキャンと無線レポートを統合したマップレスの無線幾何学的世界モデルCommDreamerを提案し、事前マップなしで高いミッション成功率と通信品質を実現した。
llm.problem: 都市の低空域におけるUAV運用において、既存のプランナーは事前の3D都市メッシュやチャンネルマップを必要とするか、サンプル効率が悪い。
llm.method: LiDARスキャンやマルチセル無線レポート、相対運動学を統合し、潜在的信念を通じて障害物クリアランスとSINRの動特性を予測する世界モデルを構築する。
llm.result: 未見の都市環境のシミュレーションにおいて、わずか150エピソードで収束し、衝突ゼロで100%のミッション成功率を達成した。

2611.24244.tldr_en: CommDreamer is proposed, a mapless radio-geometric world model that fuses raw onboard 3D LiDAR scans, multicell cellular reports, and shift-invariant relative kinematics to jointly infer local obstacle clearance and directional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) dynamics.

2611.24229.title: ProbeShare: Probing a Few, Sharing Across Many for Fast World-Model Planning
2611.24229.abstract: Visual planning with a frozen joint-embedding world model supports robotic reaching and object manipulation by evaluating candidate action sequences against an image goal before execution. Standard cross-entropy method (CEM) planners roll out every candidate independently through a billion-parameter predictor, even when nearby actions induce similar scene changes. This redundant computation grows with population size and search rounds, slowing closed-loop replanning. We observe that candidates within a planning step share an observation history and thus a common action-to-feature map. Based on this insight, we propose ProbeShare, which measures local responses with a few representative probes and reconstructs each candidate's feature grid through scene-conditioned, geometry-aware weighting. When promising candidates move beyond existing probe coverage, ProbeShare evaluates a new probe to rescore nearby candidates. Across four RoboCasa tasks, ProbeShare accelerates episode planning by 43.8--128.9 times over dense RoboJEPA and at least $14.2\times$ over competitive baselines, with greater mean goal progress in a matched-time comparison.

llm.title_ja: ProbeShare：高速な世界モデル計画のための少数のプローブと広範な共有
llm.tldr_ja: 候補間で共通の行動・特徴マップを利用して計算を効率化するビジュアル計画手法ProbeShareを提案し、従来手法に比べ数倍から数十倍の高速化を実現した。
llm.problem: 凍結された結合埋め込み世界モデルを用いたビジュアル計画において、すべての候補アクションを独立して評価すると計算コストが大きくなり、再計画が遅くなる。
llm.method: 少数の代表的なプローブで局所的応答を測定し、シーン条件付けされた幾何学的重み付けによって各候補の特徴グリッドを再構築する。
llm.result: 4つのRoboCasaタスクにおいて、エピソード計画の速度をDense RoboJEPAの43.8〜128.9倍に加速し、優れた目標達成度を維持した。

2611.24229.tldr_en: ProbeShare is proposed, which measures local responses with a few representative probes and reconstructs each candidate's feature grid through scene-conditioned, geometry-aware weighting and accelerates episode planning by 43.8--128.8 times over dense RoboJEPA and at least $14.2\times$ over competitive baselines, with greater mean goal progress in a matched-time comparison.

2611.24226.title: Neural Network-Based In-Contact Task Segmentation of Demonstrated Robot Motions via Hand Guiding
2611.24226.abstract: Intuitive robot programming approaches, such as Programming by Demonstration, enable non-experts to teach robots tasks through hand-guided demonstrations. However, for in-contact tasks requiring force control for parts of the motion, automated segmentation of motion types is crucial for improving usability. Considering the related work, this work proposes a neural network-based segmentation method categorizing motion into three fundamental types using input data of cartesian twists and wrenches at the end effector. We collect demonstration data using a 7-axis robot with a wrist-mounted force torque sensor and generate ground truth labeling by hand. While still in development, our research direction aims to enable non-experts to program in-contact tasks more intuitively.
2611.24226.comment: Extended abstract, accepted and presented at the 1st German Robotics Conference (GRC 2025), Nuremberg, 13-15 March 2025; no official proceedings, not peer-reviewed; see also https://eref.uni-bayreuth.de/id/eprint/94264

llm.title_ja: 手動誘導によるデモロボット動作の接触型タスクセグメンテーションのためのニューラルネットワーク手法
llm.tldr_ja: 手動誘導によるデモから力制御が必要な接触型タスクのモーションタイプを3種類に分類するニューラルネットワークベースのセグメンテーション手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 力制御を伴う接触型タスクにおいて、非専門家が直感的にプログラミングを行うためのモーションタイプの自動セグメンテーションが不可欠である。
llm.method: エンドエフェクタのデカルトツイストと力・トルクを入力データとして用いて、動作を3つの基礎的なタイプに分類するニューラルネットワークを構築する。
llm.result: 7軸ロボットと手首の力覚センサを用いてデモデータを収集し、グラウンド真実のラベリング手法を確立した。
llm.limitation: 現在開発中であり、公式なプロシーディングズのない拡張アブストラクトである。
keywords_ja: タスクセグメンテーション
プログラミング・バイ・デモンストレーション
ニューラルネットワーク
ロボットプログラミング

2611.24226.tldr_en: This work proposes a neural network-based segmentation method categorizing motion into three fundamental types using input data of cartesian twists and wrenches at the end effector, to enable non-experts to program in-contact tasks more intuitively.

2611.24222.title: Target-Consistent Action Guidance via Semi-Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Drifting World Models
2611.24222.abstract: Action-conditioned world models let robots imagine the outcomes of their actions for planning and offline policy evaluation, but these uses need many rollouts, which multi-step diffusion makes expensive. Drifting models move the iteration from inference to training and generate samples in one network pass. DriftWorld brought this paradigm to action-conditioned world models; to strengthen action following, it repels predictions from the current frame, a construction borrowed from classifier-free guidance. We show that this accentuation has a target bias: the push persists even when a prediction matches the recorded future, in kernel, balanced, and unbalanced Wasserstein drifting fields alike. We introduce Mass-Share Accentuation (MSA) to remove this bias. MSA treats the current frame as a counterfactual destination competing with the recorded future in a semi-relaxed optimal transport problem; subtracting the closed-form share of the correct future makes the guidance vanish at the target, and the remainder is shared by all predictions. We prove that the recorded future is the unique fixed point along the motion direction for collapsed predictions, and that the guidance fades with prediction error. On Push-T, Robomimic, and BridgeV2, where trained models under-react rather than overshoot, MSA improves action ranking, response slope, and moving-region error over latent-space baselines at no inference cost, though these benchmarks do not isolate bias removal as the cause.

llm.title_ja: ドリフトする世界モデルのための半不均衡最適輸送に基づくターゲット一貫性アクションガイダンス
llm.tldr_ja: アクション条件付き世界モデルにおけるターゲットバイアスを解消する質量共有アクセント（MSA）を提案し、推論コストを増やさずにアクションランキングや応答性を向上させた。
llm.problem: ドリフトするアクション条件付き世界モデルには、予測が記録された将来と一致してもし続けようとするターゲットバイアスが存在する。
llm.method: 現在のフレームを記録された将来と競合する反事実的な目的地として扱い、半緩和最適輸送問題において正しい将来の閉形式のシェアを差し引く。
llm.result: Push-TやRobomimic、BridgeV2において、推論コストなしでアクションランキング、応答スロープ、移動領域の誤差を改善した。
llm.limitation: ベンチマーク自体はバイアス除去の単独の効果を明確に分離しているわけではない。
keywords_ja: アクションガイダンス

2611.24222.tldr_en: It is proved that the recorded future is the unique fixed point along the motion direction for collapsed predictions, and that the guidance fades with prediction error, as well as improving action ranking, response slope, and moving-region error over latent-space baselines at no inference cost.

2611.24207.title: TapTacTouch: Shape Completion from Sparse Tactile Contacts with Geometric Priors
2611.24207.abstract: 3D object reconstruction is essential for robotic perception and manipulation, yet conventional approaches predominantly rely on visual observations that can be limited by occlusion or unavailable in visually constrained environments. In this work, we propose a vision-free, training-free, and category-agnostic framework for reconstructing 3D object meshes from sparse tactile contacts without relying on pretrained shape models. A 6-DoF robotic arm equipped with a 20-DoF multi-finger robotic hand collects tactile observations using 3x3 pressure sensor arrays mounted on the finger pads. The acquired tactile measurements are transformed into 3D contact constraints through robot kinematics and integrated into a multi-scale Gaussian Process Implicit Surface (GPIS). To address sparse and incomplete surface observations, the proposed method incorporates contact confidence weighting, weak pseudo-surface constraints, and an observation-driven geometric prior to preserve local surface geometry and provide structural guidance in unobserved regions. Real-world experiments on six objects achieve a Chamfer Distance (CD) of 1.610, an Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) of 7.738, and an F-Score of 95.00, with reconstruction completed in an average of 49.99 s per object. These results demonstrate that sparse tactile sensing can provide sufficient geometric information for continuous 3D object reconstruction without visual or semantic information.

llm.title_ja: TapTacTouch：幾何学的事前情報を用いたまばらな触覚接触からの形状補完
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの形状モデルに依存せず、まばらな触覚接触から3Dオブジェクトのメッシュを再構築するビジョン不要のフレームワークを提案し、実世界実験で精度を実証した。
llm.problem: 従来の3Dオブジェクト再構築は視覚観測に大きく依存しており、オクルージョンや視覚的に制約のある環境では制限が生じる。

2611.24192.title: TrajWAM: Trajectory-Conditioned Future Learning for Vision-Language Driving
2611.24192.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) connect future scene prediction with action planning for autonomous driving. Each driving record pairs an executed ego trajectory with its observed future, providing a factual outcome for learning this connection. We present TrajWAM, a trajectory-conditioned WAM that improves vision-language driving through auxiliary bird's-eye-view (BEV) future learning. An ego-trajectory query conditions DINOv3-aligned BEV predictions from shared planner representations. Training combines factual reconstruction under the executed trajectory with one-sided feature separation under an unlabeled perturbed trajectory. Together, these objectives train the shared planner to generate driving waypoints. Native inference directly generates waypoints and bypasses the auxiliary future-prediction branch. On all 220 Bench2Drive routes, TrajWAM achieves 91.53 Driving Score and 75.45% Success Rate, exceeding a schedule-matched planning-only fine-tuning baseline by 5.31 Driving Score points and eight successful routes.
2611.24192.comment: 22 pages, including supplementary material. Code and model weights: https://github.com/FangWD520/TrajWAM

llm.title_ja: TrajWAM：ビジョン言語自動運転のための軌道条件付き未来予測学習
llm.tldr_ja: 補助的な鳥瞰図（BEV）未来予測学習を通じてビジョン言語駆動を改善する軌道条件付き世界アクションモデル（WAM）TrajWAMを提案し、優れた運転スコアを達成した。
llm.problem: 自動運転において、将来のシーン予測とアクション計画を結びつける世界アクションモデルの学習において、正確な軌道と未来の観測を効果的に統合する必要がある。
llm.method: エゴ軌道クエリにより、共有プランナー表現からのDINOv3アラインされたBEV予測を条件付け、事実に基づく再構築と摂動軌道下での特徴分離を組み合わせて学習する。
llm.result: Bench2Driveの全220ルートにおいて、91.53の運転スコアと75.45%の成功率を達成し、ベースラインを大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: 世界アクションモデル

2611.24192.tldr_en: TrajWAM is presented, a trajectory-conditioned WAM that improves vision-language driving through auxiliary bird's-eye-view (BEV) future learning and combines factual reconstruction under the executed trajectory with one-sided feature separation under an unlabeled perturbed trajectory.

2611.24191.title: High-Precision Docking of Differential-Drive Mobile Robots Through LiDAR and Vision Collaboration
2611.24191.abstract: Precise docking requires a differential-drive robot to correct lateral offset through coupled rotation and translation within a short approach distance. We combine global navigation with terminal control using complementary LiDAR and visual observations. A line fitted to the cabinet front gives normal distance and heading. An AprilTag identifies the workstation; intersecting its center ray with the LiDAR plane determines tangential position. Taught observations define the docking reference and can cancel repeatable fixed biases under unchanged mounting and geometry. Lateral pre-alignment and continuous visual servoing coordinate the approach, with predictive stopping to account for low-speed actuation lag. Across two sessions using the same navigation and docking code at five workstations on Robot 2, all 111 tasks completed, including 101 on the first attempt. Relative to the taught observations, onboard longitudinal, lateral and heading residual root-mean-square values were 1.51 mm, 5.93 mm and 0.238 degrees, respectively. Joint acceptance within plus or minus 10 mm per position axis and plus or minus 1 degree heading was 96.4% (107/111), or 95.5% (106/111) with a plus or minus 0.5 degree heading limit.

llm.title_ja: LiDARとビジョンの協調による差動駆動型移動ロボットの高精度ドッキング
llm.tldr_ja: LiDARと視覚観測を補完的に用いてグローバルナビゲーションと端末制御を組み合わせたドッキング手法を提案し、実機での高精度な位置合わせを実証した。
llm.problem: 高精度なドッキングには、短いアプローチ距離内で結合された回転と並進を通じて、差動駆動ロボットが横方向のオフセットを修正する必要がある。
llm.method: キャビネット前面の直線フィッティングによる距離・方位推定と、AprilTagを用いた接線位置の特定を組み合わせ、予測停止を伴う視覚サーボを行う。
llm.result: 5つのワークステーションにおける111のタスクすべてを完了し（うち101回は1回目で成功）、高精度な位置・姿勢残差を達成した。

2611.24191.tldr_en: Across two sessions using the same navigation and docking code at five workstations on Robot 2, all 111 tasks completed, including 101 on the first attempt, across two sessions using the same navigation and docking code on Robot 2.

2611.24187.title: Worth Another Look:Constrained World-Model Planning for Visual Inspection
2611.24187.abstract: Visual inspection in field robotics and environmental monitoring must localize multiple targets under strict compute and sensing caps. Exhaustive sweeps waste calls on absent classes, while myopic and search-free policies stumble over heterogeneous tariff cliffs or discard viewport edits whose value emerges only after re-querying. We formulate inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules. Receding-horizon beam search with online replanning jointly schedules class queries, crops, enhancements, and termination (stop), paired with slack-aware shadow pricing and legal fallback at larger budgets. Across eight terrestrial, optical, and sonar benchmarks, multi-step lookahead outperforms static schedules and search-free offline RL under tight budgets -- gaining up to 28.4 AP percentage points over static priority on RUOD and 15.1 on ARIS -- while dynamic pricing lifts large-budget performance on all eight domains at 11 ms planning cost. Ultimately, pairing lightweight learned dynamics with exact symbolic constraints turns frozen detectors into adaptive, budget-aware inspection agents without retraining.

llm.title_ja: 再考の価値あり：視覚検査のための制約付き世界モデル計画
llm.tldr_ja: コンパクトな世界モデルと正確な記号的実行可能性を分離した神経記号的観察計画手法を提案し、厳しい計算・センシング制約下でのマルチターゲット視覚検査性能を向上させた。
llm.problem: フィールドロボティクスにおける視覚検査では、厳格な計算・センシングの制限下で複数のターゲットをローカライズする必要があり、従来の網羅的・近視的なポリシーでは非効率である。
llm.method: 凍結された検出器に対する神経記号的観察計画として定式化し、オンライン再計画を伴うリコーディングホライゾン・ビームサーチを用いる。
llm.result: 8つのベンチマークにおいて、マルチステップ先読みが静的スケジュールや強化学習を上回り、大幅な精度向上とコスト削減を達成した。

2611.24187.tldr_en: This work forms inspection over frozen detectors as neuro-symbolic observation planning under partial observability, decoupling a compact recurrent world model (WM) from exact symbolic feasibility and tariff rules.

2611.24182.title: ART: Bridging the Embodiment Gap in 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer
2611.24182.abstract: 3D affordance acts as a critical link between perception and action, providing priors for robotic manipulation. While existing approaches predominantly leverage human priors as direct references, they often overlook that affordance is not an object-intrinsic property but is inherently coupled with the agent's embodiment. Due to the structural and morphological disparities between human hands and robot end-effectors, directly applying human priors causes severe incompatibility for robotic execution. Motivated by this, we introduce a novel task setting, 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer, which addresses the affordance misalignment arising from distinct embodiment structures. To support this task, we construct the Human-Robot Paired Affordance Dataset (HPAD), the first large-scale 3D affordance benchmark in which every object is annotated with both human-prior and simulation-validated robot labels. HPAD covers 2,137 objects across 80 categories and 13 atomic action primitives, yielding over 27,000 object-action pairs. On top of HPAD, we propose the 3D Affordance tRansfer neTwork (ART). ART first filters geometric false positives in the human prior via a reliability gating stream, then reconstructs the prior into a robot-actionable distribution through hierarchical reconstruction and a graph-diffusion refinement that resolves the topological mismatch between human and robot affordances. Experiments on HPAD demonstrate the reliability of the proposed task and the superiority of ART. We further validate ART on a 6-DoF arm with a parallel-jaw gripper in a 2,400-execution benchmark across 12 objects and 4 action categories; ART attains the best success rate (86.5% over its 480 trials), confirming the practicality of the transfer paradigm. Project page: https://derek0907.github.io/ART/
2611.24182.comment: 15 pages, 14 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://derek0907.github.io/ART/

llm.title_ja: ART：3Dヒューマン・ロボット・アフォーダンス移転における身体性のギャップの架け橋
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のアフォーダンスをロボットの実行可能な分布に変換する新しいタスク設定と、大規模データセットHPADおよびARTフレームワークを提案し、実機での高い成功率を示した。

llm.method: 信頼性ゲーティングストリームによる幾何学的誤検知のフィルタリングと、階層的再構築・グラフ拡散洗練を行う3D Affordance tRansfer neTwork（ART）を提案する。
llm.result: 2,400実行のベンチマークにおいて86.5%の成功率を達成し、移転パラダイムの実用性を確認した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.24182.tldr_en: A novel task setting, 3D Human-to-Robot Affordance Transfer, is introduced, which addresses the affordance misalignment arising from distinct embodiment structures and first filters geometric false positives in the human prior via a reliability gating stream, then reconstructs the prior into a robot-actionable distribution through hierarchical reconstruction and a graph-diffusion refinement that resolves the topological mismatch between human and robot affordances.

2611.24178.title: Adaptive Action Horizon Selection via Flow-Field Uncertainty
2611.24178.abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimates are important for adaptive execution in vision-language-action (VLA) models. Existing approaches such as Adaptive Action Chunking (AAC) estimate action entropy from multiple sampled action chunks, introducing additional inference cost and capturing both uncertainty within an action trajectory and diversity across alternative strategies. We introduce Divergence-based Uncertainty-aware Adaptive Action Chunking (DUAC), a post-hoc method that extracts trajectory-conditioned predictive uncertainty from the vector field of a pretrained VLA. Building on a closed-form flow-posterior covariance formulation, DUAC derives action-level uncertainty scores from a single generated chunk using Jacobian-vector products, without retraining or multiple endpoint samples. DUAC strongly correlates with AAC, while capturing distinct information: AAC measures global dispersion across sampled chunks, whereas DUAC measures local uncertainty around the trajectory selected for execution. Consequently, DUAC is less sensitive to diversity among distinct but valid action strategies. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa, DUAC-based adaptive horizon selection performs favorably among the evaluated methods, combining strong task success with low uncertainty-estimation latency. These results establish the flow vector field as an efficient, trajectory-conditioned source of predictive uncertainty for robot decision making.

llm.title_ja: 流場不確実性に基づく適応型アクションホライズン選択
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みVLAのベクトル場から軌道条件付きの予測的不確実性を抽出する事後手法DUACを提案し、追加の推論コストなしで効率的な適応型アクション選択を実現した。

llm.method: 閉形式の流体後方共分散公式に基づき、ヤコビアン-ベクトル積を用いて単一の生成されたチャンクからアクションレベルの不確実性スコアを導出する。
llm.result: LIBEROやRoboCasaなどのタスクにおいて、強力なタスク成功率と低い不確実性推定レイテンシを両立した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル
アクションチャンキング

2611.24178.tldr_en: DUAC-based adaptive horizon selection performs favorably among the evaluated methods, combining strong task success with low uncertainty-estimation latency, and establishes the flow vector field as an efficient, trajectory-conditioned source of predictive uncertainty for robot decision making.

2611.24173.title: Dual-Actuation Emulation of Scaled Relative Orbital Dynamics on a Free-Flyer
2611.24173.abstract: Ground-based free-flyer testbeds reproduce the planar motion of a free-floating spacecraft using air bearings, but not the relative dynamics of spacecraft in orbit. We present a dual-actuation architecture that physically emulates Clohessy-Wiltshire dynamics on an open-source free-flyer. Two model predictive controllers run in parallel: one drives the solenoid thrusters with an orbital dynamics model, representing the spacecraft under test; the other drives bidirectional propellers that physically apply the orbital accelerations, continuously updating its reference to account for thruster-induced velocity changes. A dynamic similitude maps the orbital scenario onto the limited floor area and actuation rates of the testbed, letting the spacecraft controller run directly at orbital scale. We validate the architecture on hardware and against a high-fidelity orbital simulation, where the orbital accelerations instead arise naturally, both driven by the identical spacecraft controller. Their agreement indicates that the testbed reproduces the relative orbital motion the controller would encounter in flight.
2611.24173.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures. Presented at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Space Robotics (iSpaRo); to appear in IEEE Xplore

llm.title_ja: フリーフライヤーにおけるスケーリングされた相対軌道ダイナミクスの二重作動エミュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 空気軸受を用いた地上テストベッドで軌道上の相対運動を物理的にエミュレートする二重作動アーキテクチャを提案し、ハードウェアおよびシミュレーションで妥当性を検証した。
llm.problem: 地上ベースのフリーフライヤーテストベッドは平面運動を再現できるが、軌道上の宇宙船の相対ダイナミクスを再現できない。
llm.method: 軌道力学モデルでソレノイドスラスタを駆動するモデル予測制御と、軌道加速度を物理的に適用する双方向プロペラ駆動を並行して実行する。

2611.24171.title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
2611.24171.abstract: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

llm.title_ja: 物理誘導型探索蒸留による効率的な世界モデル計画
llm.tldr_ja: 未来表現と実行フィードバックを組み合わせた単一視点計画フレームワークPGSDを提案し、検索効率と道路遵守性を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 自動運転における世界モデルの未来予測において、候補がすべて道路境界に違反する場合、再ランキングだけでは実行可能な軌道を選択できない。
llm.method: 実行認識型選択、クリアランス認識型探索教師、未来条件付き修復学生の3つのコンポーネントからなる物理誘導型探索蒸留（PGSD）フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: NAVSIM v1で90.97 PDMSを達成し、既存の単一視点プランナーを凌駕するとともに、ナビゲーション性能を大幅に向上させた。

2611.24155.title: BEV-Diffusion: Camera-Only Traversability Navigation with BEV Memory and Efficient Cross-Robot Adaptation
2611.24155.abstract: Robot navigation requires both an understanding of the scene and an efficient adaptation to new robots, yet current methods rely on expensive LiDAR sensors, long mapping and modular pipelines. We present BEV-Diffusion, a camera-only model that learns a bird's-eye view (BEV) traversability map, its uncertainty and the path in a single network. A frozen DINOv2 backbone encodes consecutive RGB frames, which inverse perspective mapping and Bayesian fusion lift into the BEV, and a ranking loss keeps outdoor traversability graded rather than binary, separating asphalt from grass (median 0.94 vs. 0.75). On this map, a transformer denoiser generates polar waypoints in a few DDIM steps, and uncertainty-aware guidance refines the path and ends it where the map is no longer reliable. At deployment, a metric BEV memory keeps obstacles after they leave the camera view and warm starts each sample from the previous, ego-motion compensated path. Because the planner jointly learns the path, the map, and its uncertainty, it selects routes through terrain it can confidently traverse. In an unseen courtyard, a wheeled-legged robot autonomously traveled 120 m, completing 96% of the route without intervention, compared with 75-88% for the baselines. Even under low-light conditions after sunset, the proposed model completed the route without requiring any intervention. Retraining only the BEV head, about 3% of the parameters, adapts the model to a small legged robot in 2.3 min. Indoors, the memory gets this robot out of maze-like traps: it retains 62-66% of the nearby out-of-view obstacles, against at most 3% for the baselines, and the robot achieves 67-100% task progress, compared with 20-40% for the evaluated baselines.

llm.title_ja: BEV-Diffusion：BEVメモリと効率的なクロスロボット適応によるカメラのみの走行可能性ナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 高価なLiDARを使用せず、カメラ画像から鳥瞰図（BEV）の走行可能性マップと経路を単一ネットワークで学習するBEV-Diffusionを提案し、多様な環境で高い走破性を示した。
llm.problem: ロボットナビゲーションにはシーンの理解と新しいロボットへの迅速な適応が必要だが、従来手法は高価なLiDARや複雑なモジュールパイプラインに依存している。
llm.method: DINOv2バックボーンでエンコードされたRGBフレームをBEVに変換し、トランスフォーマーデノイザーで極座標のウェイポイントを生成するとともに、メッシュBEVメモリで障害物を保持する。
llm.result: 未見の中庭環境で120mの自動走行を96%の完了率で達成し、ヘッドの再学習だけでわずか2.3分で別の小型脚ロボットに適応できた。

2611.24155.tldr_en: BEV-Diffusion is presented, a camera-only model that learns a bird's-eye view (BEV) traversability map, its uncertainty and the path in a single network, and completes the route without requiring any intervention.

2611.24146.title: Assessing Vision-Language Models for Early Prediction of Unsafe Situations in Robotics
2611.24146.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) process visual information and textual instructions and, by using their ability to understand and reason about context, are well-suited for predicting robot failures before they occur. However, evidence supporting this remains limited. To address this, we present an empirical evaluation of VLMs for predicting robot failures. In particular, we experiment with Qwen, InternVL, and LLaVA-OneVision across three robotic case studies (HuRoN, Pal Robotics, and CrowdBot), analyzing both video and odometry data for early failure warning (i.e., before an unsafe situation occurs). Specifically, we evaluate their performance in classifying situations as safe, potentially unsafe, and unsafe, together with uncertainty quantified using various metrics, and study the relationship between uncertainty and performance. Our results showed that Qwen provides the strongest overall classification and prediction-reliability performance, while InternVL shows stronger early-warning capability in several configurations. The results further show that the effect of robot-state information and temporal history depends on the model and evaluation objective. Overall, our findings indicate that general-purpose VLMs can support early robot-safety monitoring, but the most suitable configuration depends on whether the priority is accurate assessment of safety-state, reliable confidence and uncertainty, or timely warning before unsafe events.
2611.24146.comment: Submitted to ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology (TOSEM)

llm.title_ja: ロボット工学における安全でない状況の早期予測に向けたビジョン言語モデルの評価
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの故障を事前に予測する汎用ビジョン言語モデル（VLM）の実証評価を行い、モデルごとの分類性能や早期警告能力の違いを明らかにした。

llm.method: Qwen、InternVL、LLaVA-OneVisionの3つのロボットケーススタディ（HuRoN、Pal Robotics、CrowdBot）におけるビデオおよびオドメトリデータの分類性能と不確実性を評価する。
