llm.result: Qwenが最も強力な全体的分類・予測信頼性を示し、InternVLがいくつかの構成で優れた早期警告能力を発揮することを確認した。

2611.24146.tldr_en: Overall, the findings indicate that general-purpose VLMs can support early robot-safety monitoring, but the most suitable configuration depends on whether the priority is accurate assessment of safety-state, reliable confidence and uncertainty, or timely warning before unsafe events.

2611.24142.title: BiPathCPG: A Novel Load-Sharing Design Architecture for Compound Planetary Gearboxes
2611.24142.abstract: Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD) actuators are widely used in legged robots due to their low reflected inertia, high backdrivability, and high torque density, commonly employing planetary or cycloidal gearboxes. Single-stage planetary gearboxes offer high efficiency but limited torque density; multi-stage designs improve torque density at the cost of efficiency; and cycloidal gearboxes provide high stiffness but suffer from torque ripple. Compound Planetary Gearboxes (CPG) offer a compromise, but conventional designs result in increased actuator width, mass, and reduced torsional stiffness in 3D-printed actuators. This paper proposes the BiPath Compound Planetary Gearbox (BiPathCPG), a novel architecture that introduces an idle second-stage sun gear and load-sharing second-stage planets within the otherwise unused space of a conventional CPG to simultaneously improve stiffness, reduce actuator width, and reduce mass. An optimization framework computes BiPathCPG parameters for a given motor and target gear ratio. The architecture is validated through a 3D-printed proof-of-concept actuator design, benchmarked against a conventional CPG using custom-built test rigs. The BiPathCPG achieves a torsional stiffness of 1394 Nm/rad, a 1.70x improvement over the conventional CPG, with a 32% reduction in backlash, 25 g lower mass, and approximately 6.4 mm reduction in axial width, while achieving a peak stall torque of 36.49 Nm.
2611.24142.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Project page: https://deepak-kapa.github.io/PancakeActuator/ Accepted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

llm.title_ja: BiPathCPG：複合遊星歯車装置のための新しい負荷共有設計アーキテクチャ
llm.tldr_ja: 脚ロボット向けに剛性を高めつつ幅と質量を削減する新しい複合遊星歯車アーキテクチャBiPathCPGを提案し、試作アクチュエータで性能を実証した。
llm.problem: 準ダイレクトドライブ（QDD）アクチュエータで用いられる従来の遊星歯車や複合遊星歯車は、トルク密度、サイズ、剛性のトレードオフに課題がある。
llm.method: 従来の複合遊星歯車の未利用スペースに、アイドル状態の第2ステージ太陽歯車と負荷分散プラネットを導入するBiPathCPGアーキテクチャを提案する。
llm.result: 従来設計比で1.70倍のねじり剛性（1394 Nm/rad）、32%のバックラッシ削減、25gの軽量化、約6.4mmの軸方向幅の削減を達成した。

2611.24138.title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot
2611.24138.abstract: Embodied models depend on real interaction data, yet collecting it on physical robots is slow and labor-intensive. Recent ego-to-robot pipelines retarget first-person view human videos to robot data via transferring hand and arm motion. They judge fidelity mainly by visual appearance. However, trajectories often fail in terms of physics: fingers hover beside objects, and grippers close on empty space. We argue that how the object moves and the contacts that drive the motion count. Thus, we present Ego2X, an object-centric framework that converts monocular egocentric video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Ego2X centers on CORE (Contact-centric Object-interaction REpresentation), which records each contact on the object by its surface anchor, as well as relative force, grasp mode, and interaction state. Throughout the pipeline, CORE corrects hand-object drift via object-relative constraints, steers inverse kinematics toward contacts the robot must realize, and preserves held objects during arm erasure and robot compositing. On HOT3D, contact-driven correction reduces in-contact hand depth error by 33.7%, while on EgoDex, contact-driven retargeting realizes 62.9% of annotated contacts, surpassing the official HuRo pipeline (27.9%). In RoboTwin 2.0, post-training X-VLA on Ego2X episodes alone, without simulator demonstrations, raises task success rate from 40.5% zero-shot to 67.0% across 200 paired scenes. We will publicly release our conversion pipeline and CORE-annotated dataset for dexterous hands and parallel grippers.

llm.title_ja: Ego2X：エゴセントリックな人間データからあらゆるロボットへの接触を考慮した移転
llm.tldr_ja: 単眼のエゴセントリック動画を器用な手や平行グリッパー向けの物理的に実行可能なロボットデータに変換するオブジェクト中心のフレームワークEgo2Xを提案した。
llm.problem: 身体化モデルは実インタラクションデータを必要とするが実ロボットでの収集は遅く、既存の視覚ベースの動画リターゲット手法は物理的な接触や動作の忠実度が不足している。
llm.method: オブジェクト上の接触を表面アンカーや相対力などで記録するCORE（Contact-centric Object-interaction REpresentation）を用いて、逆運動学やドリフトを補正する。
llm.result: HOT3Dで接触起因の深度誤差を33.7%削減し、RoboTwin 2.0においてシミュレータのデモなしでタスク成功率を40.5%から67.0%に向上させた。
keywords_ja: エゴセントリック動画
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.24138.tldr_en: Ego2X is presented, an object-centric framework that converts monocular egocentric video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers and will publicly release the conversion pipeline and CORE-annotated dataset for dexterous hands and parallel grippers.

2611.24115.title: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks
2611.24115.abstract: Long-horizon tasks in embodied and web environments involve extended decision sequences and delayed feedback, making accurate planning crucial for success. World models tackle this by learning latent dynamics for imagination-based planning. However, existing approaches merely rely on dense pixel-level observations, which forces the model to absorb redundant information while overlooking relations among task-relevant entities. Consequently, small errors may accumulate over long imagined rollouts and gradually corrupt the predictions. In this paper, we explore world models that imagine over sparse state abstractions, which poses two key challenges: 1) how to remove redundant information and form a compact state abstraction; 2) how to incorporate the relational structure to learn reliable long-horizon dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose Embodied Graph, a relational state abstraction that supports structured dynamics modeling and long-horizon imagination, and the Relational World Model (RWM), which performs imagination directly over graph states. RWM consists of (i) a Task-Aware Embodied Graph Constructor that filters redundant details and maintains graph memory through online updates, and (ii) an Embodied Graph Recurrent State Space Model that learns node-wise latent dynamics while capturing inter-node dependencies. The imagined graph states provide predictions of action consequences to guide decision-making. Experiments on Minecraft and Crafter demonstrate the effectiveness of RWM in embodied environments. Notably, in Minecraft, RWM is the only method that obtains diamonds within the given budget. Experiments on web interaction further illustrate the applicability of relational state prediction to the decision making process of web agents.

llm.title_ja: Embodied Graph：長期タスクのための関係型世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: スパースな状態抽象化上で想像を行う関係型世界モデル（RWM）を提案し、Minecraftやウェブ環境での長期タスク計画における有効性を示した。
llm.problem: 長期タスクにおける既存の世界モデルは高密度のピクセルレベルの観察に依存するため冗長な情報を取り込み、長期のロールアウトで誤差が蓄積する。
llm.method: 冗長な詳細をフィルタリングしてグラフメモリを維持するタスク対応エンボディドグラフコンストラクタと、ノードごとの潜在ダイナミクスを学習するリカレント状態空間モデルを構築する。
llm.result: Minecraftにおいて、与えられた予算内でダイヤを獲得できた唯一の手法となり、ウェブエージェントの意思決定への適用性も示した。

2611.24115.tldr_en: Embodied Graph is proposed, a relational state abstraction that supports structured dynamics modeling and long-horizon imagination, and the Relational World Model (RWM), which performs imagination directly over graph states.

2611.24108.title: Asymmetric Decomposition for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Unassigned Agents
2611.24108.abstract: Robots without assigned tasks may obstruct active robots, while routing them to designated parking locations can cause unnecessary travel. This article proposes flow-oracle conflict-based search (FOCBS) for Multi-Agent Path Finding with unassigned agents (MAPF-UA). FOCBS searches over assigned-agent paths using conflict-based search (CBS) and routes targetless unassigned agents through a min-cost flow oracle. When the selected assigned-agent paths leave unassigned agents no collision-free paths, flow-conflict branching converts min-cut blockers into assigned-agent constraints, which guide the search without excluding optimal solutions. A batched zero-cost warm start accelerates the oracle, and start-avoiding tie-breaking reduces unassigned-agent movement. For feasible instances on finite graphs, we prove termination and global minimization of assigned-agent sum of service time, measured by last-arrival times. Unassigned-agent movement is minimized conditional on the selected assigned-agent paths, without a global lexicographic optimality guarantee. Benchmark experiments show that FOCBS scales well with the number of unassigned agents, and ablation studies show that, compared with discarding non-completable assigned-agent paths, flow-conflict branching solves substantially more instances while retaining optimality. Simulation and physical-robot experiments demonstrate plan executability, with laboratory tests reducing fleet travel by 40.8% relative to the parking-based coordination baseline. The source code and related resources are available at https://github.com/Chin-hsi/focbs

llm.title_ja: 割り当てられていないエージェントを含むマルチエージェントパスファインディングのための非対称分解
llm.tldr_ja: 未割り当てエージェントを含むマルチエージェントパスファインディング（MAPF-UA）において、フローオラクルと競合ベース探索を組み合わせることで最適性を維持しつつ多数のインスタンスを効率的に解くFOCBSを提案する。
llm.problem: 未割り当てのエージェントがアクティブなエージェントの邪魔になり、従来の迂回誘導では不要な移動が発生する。
llm.method: CBSによる割り当て済みエージェントの経路探索と、最小費用流オラクルによる未割り当てエージェントの誘導を組み合わせる。
llm.result: ベンチマーク実験において、FOCBSは未割り当てエージェントの数に対して良好なスケーラビリティを示し、従来の手法と比較して大幅に多くのインスタンスを解きつつ最適性を維持した。
keywords_ja: マルチエージェントパスファインディング

2611.24108.tldr_en: benchmark experiments show that FOCBS scales well with the number of unassigned agents, and ablation studies show that, compared with discarding non-completable assigned-agent paths, flow-conflict branching solves substantially more instances while retaining optimality.

2611.24100.title: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots
2611.24100.abstract: Embodied robots increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to interpret user intent and coordinate with robot-specific action models for physical interaction. This multi-model pipeline creates a critical semantic boundary across mind, model collaboration, and motion: semantic consistency may break between what the large model understands, how the small action model translates that understanding into executable commands, and what physical actions the robot ultimately performs. As a security consequence, commercial robots may execute unintended physical actions even when user inputs contain no explicit action commands. To measure this problem, we develop TARS, a black-box framework that explores the command-reasoning-action pipeline and automatically discovers and validates unintended physical behaviors. We evaluate TARS on four commercial robots across 44 experimental settings, conducting 133,400 executions. TARS uncovers widespread cross-model action misalignment and achieves up to 94% verified action coverage.

llm.title_ja: 心、モデルの協調、動作の間の迷走：商用ロボットにおけるクロスモデルの動作不整合の理解と測定
llm.tldr_ja: 商用ロボットにおける大規模言語モデルとロボット固有の行動モデル間のセマンティックな不整合を自動的に発見・検証するブラックボックスフレームワーク「TARS」を開発し、広範なクロスモデル動作不整合を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルと小規模な行動モデルの間でセマンティックな一貫性が破綻し、意図しない物理的動作を引き起こすおそれがある。
llm.method: コマンド・推論・行動のパイプラインを探索し、意図しない物理的動作を自動的に発見・検証するブラックボックスフレームワークTARSの開発。
llm.result: 4種類の商用ロボットを用いた44の設定、133,400回の実行評価により、TARSは広範なクロスモデル動作不整合を検出し、最大94%の検証済み行動カバレッジを達成した。
keywords_ja: ブラックボックスフレームワーク

2611.24100.tldr_en: TARS is a black-box framework that explores the command-reasoning-action pipeline and automatically discovers and validates unintended physical behaviors and uncovers widespread cross-model action misalignment.

2611.24095.title: Object Pose: The Link between Weak Perspective, Paraperspective, and Full Perspective
2611.24095.abstract: Recently, DeMenthon and Davis [4,5] proposed a method for determining the pose of a 3-D object with respect to a camera from 3-D to 2-D point correspondences. The method consists of iteratively improving the pose computed with a weak perspective camera model to converge, at the limit, to a pose estimation computed with a perspective camera model. In this paper we give an algebraic derivation of DeMenthon and Davis' method and we show that it belongs to a larger class of methods where the perspective camera model is approximated either at zero order (weak perspective) or first order (paraperspective). We describe in detail an iterative paraperspective pose computation method for both non coplanar and coplanar object points. We analyse the convergence of these methods and we conclude that the iterative paraperspective method (proposed in this paper) has better convergence properties than the iterative weak perspective method. We introduce a simple way of taking into account the orthogonality constraint associated with the rotation matrix. We analyse the sensitivity to camera calibration errors and we define the optimal experimental setup with respect to imprecise camera calibration. We compare the results obtained with this method and with a non-linear optimization method.

llm.title_ja: 物体姿勢：弱透視、パラパースペクティブ、完全透視の間のつながり
llm.tldr_ja: 3次元から2次元への点対応を用いて3次元物体の姿勢を決定する手法について、DeMenthonとDavisの手法を代数的に導出し、ゼロ次または一次近似に基づくより広いクラスのメソッドに属することを示した。
llm.problem: カメラモデルの近似に基づく3次元物体の姿勢推定において、収束性や最適性の関係が十分に整理されていなかった。
llm.method: DeMenthonとDavisの手法の代数的な導出を行い、反復パラパースペクティブ姿勢計算手法の詳細な記述と収束性の解析を行う。
llm.result: 提案する反復パラパースペクティブ法は、従来の反復弱透視法よりも優れた収束特性を持つことを示した。
keywords_ja: パラパースペクティブ

2611.24095.tldr_en: An algebraic derivation of DeMenthon and Davis' method is given and it is shown that it belongs to a larger class of methods where the perspective camera model is approximated either at zero order (weak perspective) or first order (paraperspective).

2611.24083.title: VESPA: Verifiable Symbolic Policy Adaptation for Safe Reinforcement Learning
2611.24083.abstract: Safe reinforcement learning (RL) aims to prevent agents from taking actions that are dangerous or destructive to their environment. This is especially important for safety-critical domains, such as robotics or autonomous driving. Formal verification can be used to prove agent safety through safety constraints. However, in practice, many policies do violate safety constraints, and thus are verified to be unsafe. Since the goal is to obtain a safe policy, we would need to retrain a new policy from scratch and then verify it again until a candidate happens to pass. Both training and verification are usually not cheap, which makes this process inefficient. We introduce VESPA ($\textbf{VE}$rifiable $\textbf{S}$ymbolic $\textbf{P}$olicy $\textbf{A}$daptation), a framework for targeted fine-tuning of decision tree policies. We show that using counterexamples for policy adaptation can make existing unsafe policies safe, or at least make considerable progress towards safety. Targeted fine-tuning of the existing policy on those counterexamples enables it to learn how to avoid violating safety constraints. We thus use the result of a formal verification as a training signal for fine-tuning. On CartPole, VESPA raises the mean number of verified safe steps from 63.8 to at least 92.7, reaching after two iterations what the same loop without counterexamples reaches after ten. On MountainCarContinuous, VESPA turns an unsafe policy into a safe policy in 53 of 60 runs. We conclude that counterexamples from a verifier are an effective training signal, which can be utilized to systematically improve the safety of policies. Our implementation is available at: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/VESPA-Submission/

llm.title_ja: VESPA：安全な強化学習のための検証可能な記号的ポリシー適応
llm.tldr_ja: 安全な強化学習のために、形式検証器から得られる反例をトレーニング信号として決定木ポリシーをターゲット絞り込みで微調整し、効率的に安全性を向上させるフレームワーク「VESPA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 多くのポリシーは安全制約に違反するため検証で安全でないと判定され、ゼロからの再学習と再検証の繰り返しは効率が悪い。
llm.method: 形式検証器から得られた反例を用いた決定木ポリシーのターゲット微調整により、安全制約違反を回避する方法を学習させるフレームワークVESPAの導入。
llm.result: CartPoleおよびMountainCarContinuousのタスクにおいて、VESPAは反例を活用することで少ないイテレーションでポリシーを効果的に安全に修正できることを示した。

2611.24083.tldr_en: VESPA is introduced, a framework for targeted fine-tuning of decision tree policies, and it is shown that using counterexamples for policy adaptation can make existing unsafe policies safe, or at least make considerable progress towards safety.

2611.24077.title: AeroRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement for Aerial Vision-Language Navigation
2611.24077.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to follow natural-language instructions, yet still fail frequently in closed-loop flight. Correcting these failures requires repairs, i.e., actions that avoid them at the states the policy itself reaches, which human pilots cannot label at scale and rule-based planners cannot supply reliably. In this paper, we present AeroRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures. Our key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them. Judged in this way, its sampled actions and even rule-based proposals that hurt it when imitated directly become reliable supervision. Moreover, an episode terminates at its first failure, concealing subsequent failures until the earlier ones are repaired. AeroRSI thus renews its supervision in every round, anchoring the failures of the current policy, verifying repairs by its continuation, and distilling them while keeping its behavior elsewhere. On TravelUAV, three rounds raise the success rate of a supervised 2B-parameter policy from 46.4% to 67.5% and reduce collisions by half, surpassing the previous state of the art by 10.6 points from the same initialization without extra human labels or inference cost. Code and models are available at https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI.
2611.24077.comment: 8-page main paper with references and supplementary material (15 pages); 5 figures, 13 tables. Code: https://github.com/starsholic/AeroRSI Project page: https://starsholic.github.io/AeroRSI/

llm.title_ja: AeroRSI：空中視覚言語ナビゲーションのための再帰的自己改善
llm.tldr_ja: 無人航空機が自身の失敗から反復的に学習する再帰的自己改善フレームワーク「AeroRSI」を提案し、追加の人手によるラベルなしで成功率を大幅に向上させ衝突を半減させた。
llm.problem: 視覚言語行動モデルを用いた無人航空機の閉ループ飛行において頻繁に失敗が発生し、人間による大規模な修正データのラベル付けが困難である。
llm.method: 自身が失敗した状態から飛行を継続させて修正を評価し、信頼性の高い教師信号として活用する再帰的自己改善フレームワークAeroRSIの構築。
llm.result: TravelUAVを用いた実験で、3ラウンドの訓練により2Bパラメータポリシーの成功率を46.4%から67.5%に向上させ、衝突を半減させた。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2611.24077.tldr_en: AeroRSI is presented, a recursive self-improvement framework in which an aerial navigation policy iteratively learns from its own failures, and its key insight is that a failing policy should judge its own repairs by flying on from them.

2611.24076.title: Meaning Reaches Object Choice but Not Completion: Where Is a VLA Vulnerable to Landmark Synonyms?
2611.24076.abstract: VLA policies are fragile to rewording. Success rates alone cannot say whether a policy fails to choose the object or to complete the task, nor where in the policy to intervene. We study the released GR00T N1.7 on two LIBERO-Spatial tasks differing only in the landmark word telling which of two bowls to take. Synonyms absent from the training instructions send the policy to the bowl they name, unlike made-up words, yet complete 67.6% of one task's closed-loop episodes, against the original word's 100%. Before the connector between the vision-language model and the action generator, replacing only the landmark tokens' vectors with the other landmark's (pasting) sends nearly every episode to the other bowl. After the connector, pasting at the landmark, the remaining instruction, or the image tokens alone rarely moves the choice, but any two do. Hiding the landmark tokens from the action generator after the connector still lowers completion for the synonyms that fall short. Finetuning on diversified landmark words repairs that one task's completion for synonyms absent from finetuning; finetuning on the original instructions does not. Training only the connector on the diversified words suffices, as does copying the connector of a policy fully finetuned on them into one finetuned on the original instructions. An open-loop score on starting frames misses that weights outside the connector also carry part of the repair. For now, on this evidence, robustness to rewording should be judged in closed loop, with actions executed, intervening on both sides of the connector, scoring choice and completion separately.
2611.24076.comment: Accepted to the CoRL 2026 Workshop on The Action Gap (TAG 2026). OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=b7wZqqQzON

llm.title_ja: 意味はオブジェクト選択には到達するが完了には到達せず：VLAはランドマークの類義語に対してどこが脆弱か
llm.tldr_ja: VLAポリシーが類義語に対して持つ脆弱性を検証し、ビジョン言語モデルと行動ジェネレータを繋ぐコネクタの前後で介入や分析を行い、成功率や選択・完了の挙動を評価した。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーは言い換えに対して脆弱であるが、単なる成功率だけではオブジェクト選択の失敗かタスク完了の失敗かを切り分けられない。
llm.method: LIBERO-Spatialタスクを用いて、類義語の入力に対するコネクタの前後でのトークン置換や微調整による影響を閉ループで分析・評価する。
llm.result: コネクタの前後で介入を行い選択と完了を別個にスコアリングすることで、類義語に対する脆弱性の所在と改善に必要な微調整手法を明らかにした。

2611.24076.tldr_en: For now, robustness to rewording should be judged in closed loop, with actions executed, intervening on both sides of the connector, scoring choice and completion separately.

2611.24074.title: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
2611.24074.abstract: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. SemPhys inserts this prediction at its original position, scores the complete trajectory against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment. A paired anchoring loss stabilizes adaptation by keeping each generated reference close to its counterpart from the initial generator. On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

llm.title_ja: SemPhys：微分可能世界モデルによるヒューマノイドモーション生成のための意味的・物理的協調学習
llm.tldr_ja: ヒューマノイドの全身運動生成において、シミュレーション実行からの意味的フィードバックを用いてモーションジェネレータを訓練するフレームワーク「SemPhys」を提案し、指示取得の正確性を保持・向上させた。
llm.problem: 言語指示から生成された運動を追従コントローラで実行する際、接触制約下でのバランス維持により実行されたモーションが指示の意図から乖離してしまう。
llm.method: 微分可能世界モデルと固定追従コントローラを用いてシミュレーション上の実行結果を予測し、その完全な軌跡を指示に対してスコア付けして逆伝播させるSemPhysの導入。
llm.result: BONES-SEEDを用いた評価において、SemPhysは参照から実行への指示取得精度を大幅に保持し、評価手法の中で最も高い検索精度を達成した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.24074.tldr_en: This work introduces SemPhys, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions and largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

2611.24062.title: JEPA Dots: Dual-Latent World Model for Language-Guided Robot Control
2611.24062.abstract: Predictive world models for language-guided robot control face a fundamental conditioning challenge: instructions should influence action selection without altering the predicted consequences of fixed actions under identical observations. To address this challenge, we introduce JEPA Dots (Dynamics-Oriented Task Separation), a compact dual-latent framework that jointly learns visual dynamics and language-guided control through separate dynamics and task representations. Language-conditioned task features guide a flow-matching policy, while masked attention restricts world prediction to instruction-independent dynamics history and supplied actions. In closed-loop evaluation on 40 trained LIBERO tasks, JEPA Dots achieves 84.9% overall success with approximately 39.1M parameters, compared with the published 78.7% of NanoVLA-S with 161.0M parameters under a different evaluation protocol. In the reference experiment, JEPA Dots also improves overall success from 76.0% for our task-ID-conditioned adaptation baseline to 84.9%, with LIBERO-Goal success increasing from 67.1% to 88.5%. Instruction-switching experiments further confirm that task representations and policy outputs respond to language changes, while dynamics representations and world predictions remain invariant under fixed observations and supplied actions.

llm.title_ja: JEPA Dots：言語誘導型ロボット制御のための二重潜在世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的ダイナミクスと言語誘導型コントロールを分離して学習するコンパクトな二重潜在世界モデル「JEPA Dots」を提案し、複数のLIBEROタスクにおいて高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 言語誘導型ロボット制御のための予測世界モデルにおいて、指示が行動選択に影響を与えつつ、同一観測下での固定行動の予測結果を変化させないようにする条件付けの課題がある。
llm.method: 別々のダイナミクス表現とタスク表現を用いて視覚ダイナミクスと言語誘導制御を共同学習する二重潜在フレームワークJEPA Dotsの構築。
llm.result: 40のLIBEROタスクを用いた閉ループ評価において、JEPA Dotsは84.9%の全体的成功率を達成し、言語変更に対する不変性と適応性を確認した。

2611.24062.tldr_en: JEPA Dots (Dynamics-Oriented Task Separation), a compact dual-latent framework that jointly learns visual dynamics and language-guided control through separate dynamics and task representations, is introduced.

2611.24051.title: Attention Is Not Relevance: Challenging the Causality of Attention in Autonomous Driving
2611.24051.abstract: Attention has become one of the most widely adopted solutions for estimating the relevance of surrounding objects and interpreting an autonomous vehicle's driving decisions. However, its ability to capture the causal impact of individual input elements on an AI model's output has long been discussed in the literature, particularly in the Natural Language Processing (NLP) domain. This work brings this discussion into the autonomous driving domain by analyzing the accuracy of attention in estimating the impact of an input object on an autonomous vehicle's driving, i.e., its relevance. To this end, we compare different attention-based relevance estimation methods against a causal reference of object relevance obtained through counterfactual analysis. We perform our analysis on more than 80,000 synthetic driving scenes using an autonomous vehicle based on PlanT 2.0, a state-of-the-art Transformer-based model for object-level planning. Results show that attention provides a correlational rather than causal indication of object relevance. Attention-based relevance estimation methods do not consistently identify all relevant objects and tend to incorrectly classify as relevant objects with little or no impact on the vehicle's driving. In particular, results show that attention can effectively identify relevant objects in simple single-lane, straight-road scenarios, but its accuracy degrades in more complex settings, such as multi-lane roads and intersections. These findings highlight the limitations of attention as a proxy for object relevance, calling for novel methods able to accurately capture the causal impact of individual objects on the vehicle's driving and distinguish it from correlational associations.

llm.title_ja: アテンションは関連性ではない：自動運転におけるアテンションの因果関係への挑戦
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転の意思決定において、アテンションが周辺オブジェクトの関連性を推定する尺度として因果関係を示すものではなく、相関的な指標に留まることを反事実分析との比較により明らかにした。
llm.problem: アテンションはAIモデルの出力に対する個々の入力要素の因果的影響を捉える能力について長年議論されているが、自動運転分野での検証が必要である。
llm.method: 80,000以上の合成駆動シーンを用い、最先端のTransformerベースのモデルによるアテンションベースの関連性推定手法と、反事実分析による因果的基準とを比較する。
llm.result: アテンションはオブジェクトの関連性を因果的ではなく相関的にしか示さず、複雑なシナリオでは精度が低下することが示された。
keywords_ja: アテンションメカニズム

2611.24051.tldr_en: Results show that attention can effectively identify relevant objects in simple single-lane, straight-road scenarios, but its accuracy degrades in more complex settings, such as multi-lane roads and intersections, which highlights the limitations of attention as a proxy for object relevance.

2611.24011.title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
2611.24011.abstract: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two stages. The first, Cross-Morphology Policy Adaptation and Acceleration, adapts the arm-centric WAM to quadrupeds and distills the transferred policy into a student with one video and two action steps by on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). This student, however, is bounded by its teacher, which only imitates demonstrations. The second stage, Task-Specific Improvement and Merging, therefore tunes the teacher by reinforcement learning (RL) and merges the slow specialists into one few-step student by multi-teacher on-policy distillation (M-OPD). On QLM-Bench, ten simulated tasks with 1,000 demonstrations synthesized without teleoperation, the transferred policy reaches 77.0%, and the OPSD student keeps 76.7% while sampling 14 times faster. Task-specific RL and M-OPD lift it to 85.0%. We also deploy the OPSD student on a real Unitree Go2 Air. WAM-Policy thus achieves a stronger quadrupedal policy at a fraction of the inference cost.

llm.title_ja: WAM-Policy：四足歩行の移動とマニピュレーションのためのオンポリシー蒸留によるワールドアクションモデル
llm.tldr_ja: アーム用ワールドアクションモデルを強化学習とオンポリシー自己蒸留を活用して四足歩行による移動マニピュレーションポリシーへと適応させる「WAM-Policy」を提案し、実機での効率的な動作を実現した。
llm.problem: アームフリーの四足歩行ロボットによる移動マニピュレーション（ロコ・マニピュレーション）において、言語指示に従う既存のポリシーが存在しない。
llm.method: アーム中心のWAMを四足ロボットに適応させてオンポリシー自己蒸留を行う段階と、強化学習によるタスク特化型チューニングと複数教師からの蒸留を行う段階の2段階からなるWAM-Policyの提案。
llm.result: QLM-Benchのシミュレーションタスクにおいて85.0%の成功率を達成し、実機のUnitree Go2 Airロボットへのデプロイにも成功した。
keywords_ja: ワールドアクションモデル

2611.24011.tldr_en: WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two stages, tunes the teacher by reinforcement learning (RL) and merges the slow specialists into one few-step student by multi-teacher on-policy distillation (M-OPD).

2611.24010.title: HHW-Ego: DSLR-Quality Enhancement for Multi-Source Wearable Ego Imaging
2611.24010.abstract: Wearable ego-centric images are now in high demand for scenarios ranging from daily smart glass usage to embodied intelligence. But the image quality is far behind smart phone due to the lacking paired high-quality reference images and the dedicated enhancement systems. To solve this, a customized degradation pipeline is designed to generate paired samples matching wearable camera images, boosting the upper limit of enhancement performance. Besides a two-stage enhancement framework is further built: first, tuning an efficient model on the paired dataset to enhance real wearable images; second, using hyperspectral data to refine color temperature for better quality. Moreover we present HHW-Ego, a multi-source paired dataset integrating with Hyperspectral, High-dynamic range and Wearable Ego-centric data, which includes 5,000 image groups spanning indoor/outdoor and day/night scenes. On held-out paired data, Stage-1 fine-tuning improves PSNR, SSIM, Lab distance, and LPIPS for Real-ESRGAN and PFT-SR. On real wearable images, no-reference metrics, human preference, gamut analysis, and visual comparisons characterize the effects of Stage 2.

llm.title_ja: HHW-Ego：マルチソースウェアラブル一人称視点画像のためのDSLR品質向上
llm.tldr_ja: ウェアラブルカメラ画像の品質向上を目指し、カスタム劣化パイプラインと2段階のフレームワークを設計するとともに、ハイパースペクトル等のデータを含むマルチソースペアデータセット「HHW-Ego」を構築した。
llm.problem: ウェアラブルな一人称視点画像は、ペアとなる高品質な参照画像の不足と専用の画質改善システムの欠如により、スマートフォン等の品質に大きく劣っている。
llm.method: ウェアラブルカメラ画像に一致するペアサンプルを生成するカスタム劣化パイプラインの設計と、実画像を改善して色温度を調整する2段階の画質改善フレームワークの構築。
llm.result: 保持されたペアデータおよび実際のウェアラブル画像を用いた評価において、PSNRやSSIMなどの指標や視覚的品質の改善を確認した。

2611.24010.tldr_en: A customized degradation pipeline is designed to generate paired samples matching wearable camera images, boosting the upper limit of enhancement performance, and a two-stage enhancement framework is further built, tuning an efficient model on the paired dataset to enhance real wearable images.

2611.24008.title: Modelling the human-exoskeleton interaction interface - Benchmarking MuJoCo's deformable model
2611.24008.abstract: The human-exoskeleton interaction interface, consisting of the exoskeleton attachment and the underlying human soft tissue, can affect the transfer of assistance. MuJoCo's \textit{flexcomp} has been previously used to model the soft tissue, but its accuracy has not been benchmarked against a finite element model. We benchmarked the \textit{flexcomp} Saint Venant-Kirchhoff (StVK) and Stable Neo-Hookean (SNH) models against COMSOL's Yeoh model in three cases: \textit{case 1}) spherical indentation, \textit{case 2}) compression, and \textit{case 3}) compression of a thigh. We compared force and strain energy as a function of indentation depth, hysteresis and computation time. MuJoCo's models capture force trends with a correlation of 0.97-0.99, but showed a stiffer response, which could be attributed to the volumetric locking of the linear finite elements. The MuJoCo models systematically underestimated hysteresis as MuJoCo's Rayleigh damping could not substitute a viscoelastic model. Moreover, MuJoCo's computational advantage was speed dependent: it was 2-2.5 times faster for spherical indentation, but COMSOL was faster for the other cases, which have more degrees of freedom and contacts. Although MuJoCo's \textit{flexcomp} offers a combination of soft-tissue modelling and multibody dynamics, the limitations regarding the stiffening and hysteresis should be addressed to be used for the analysis of the human-exoskeleton interaction interface.

llm.title_ja: 人間と外骨格の相互作用インターフェースのモデリング - MuJoCoの変形モデルのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: MuJoCoの柔軟体モデル（flexcomp）を有限要素モデルと比較し、球体圧迫や大腿部圧縮などのケースを通じて力やひずみエネルギーの傾向をベンチマーク評価した。
llm.problem: 外骨格のアタッチメントと人間の軟部組織を含む相互作用インターフェースが補助の伝達に影響を与えるが、MuJoCoの軟部組織モデルの精度が十分に検証されていなかった。
llm.method: MuJoCoのStVKモデルおよびSNHモデルをCOMSOLのYeohモデルと比較し、インデント深さに対する力やひずみエネルギー、ヒステリシス、計算時間を評価する。
llm.result: MuJoCoのモデルは0.97〜0.99の相関で力の傾向を捉えるものの、硬めの応答を示し、ヒステリシスを過小評価することが示された。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.23974.title: LaST1.0: A Unified Latent World-Action Model with Control-Centric SpatioTemporal Reasoning
2611.23974.abstract: World-Action Models couple action learning with future prediction, enabling robotic policies to capture environmental dynamics for robust control. However, prevailing methods take a reconstruction-oriented approach to model future videos, allocating substantial capacity to appearance details that are incidental to control. In this work, we reformulate world modeling for manipulation as control-centric future prediction in latent space, and present LaST1.0, a unified latent World-Action Model. Rather than modeling an observation-complete video future, LaST1.0 predicts compact, geometry-aware latent targets derived from future wrist views, focusing the supervision on the evolving robot-object interactions required for fine-grained manipulation. To better support this control-centric paradigm, LaST1.0 revisits the visual input interface and attention mechanism of its unified architecture. It adopts a vision-encoder-free design with a lightweight patch embedder, exposing fine-grained visual cues directly to the backbone, and introduces LaST-Attention for structured spatiotemporal interactions across modalities. Evaluations across two robot embodiments, five challenging manipulation tasks, and three simulation benchmarks---RLBench, LIBERO, and LIBERO-Plus---demonstrate that LaST1.0 achieves state-of-the-art success rates and generalizes to novel scenarios. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of control-centric latent world modeling for robust manipulation.

llm.title_ja: LaST1.0：制御中心の時空間推論を備えた統合潜在型ワールド・アクションモデル
llm.tldr_ja: 詳細な外見よりもロボットと物体の相互作用に焦点を当てた制御中心の潜在空間における将来予測を行う、統合型潜在ワールド・アクションモデル「LaST1.0」を提案し、優れた成功率と汎化性能を実現した。
llm.problem: 従来の世界モデルは将来の動画の再構築を重視するあまり、制御に直接関係のない外観の詳細に多くの容量を割いてしまっている。
llm.method: 手首視点からの幾何学的認識が可能なコンパクトな潜在ターゲットを予測し、軽量パッチ埋め込みとLaST-Attentionを導入した制御中心の潜在ワールド・アクションモデルLaST1.0の提案。
llm.result: RLBench、LIBEROなどの複数のシミュレーションベンチマークにおいて、最先端の成功率を達成し、新しいシナリオへの汎化性能を示した。

2611.23974.tldr_en: This work reformulates world modeling for manipulation as control-centric future prediction in latent space, and presents LaST1.0, a unified latent World-Action Model that achieves state-of-the-art success rates and generalizes to novel scenarios.

2611.23970.title: TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting
2611.23970.abstract: Forecasting future hand movements from egocentric videos plays an important role in understanding human intentions and hand-object interactions. However, different manipulation intentions can lead to substantially different hand trajectories even when interacting with the same object. Existing methods have not sufficiently explored the intrinsic relationships between articulated hand movements and object semantics to capture such operation-dependent motion patterns. Therefore, we propose TOMAS, a topology-aware operation modeling and adaptive staging framework for egocentric hand forecasting. Specifically, we develop a topology-aware hand-object reasoning mechanism that associates hand skeletal structures and articulation dynamics with object semantics and spatial relationships to jointly infer potential interaction targets and latent manipulation operations. The resulting object-operation representations provide interaction conditions for future hand trajectory prediction, with supervision adapted to the annotations available in each dataset. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive staging mechanism that organizes future hand movements into ordered latent stages with learnable temporal boundaries. Stage-specific geometric subgoals are then incorporated to guide trajectory refinement according to the underlying manipulation patterns. Experimental results on multiple publicly available benchmarks demonstrate that TOMAS achieves state-of-the-art performance in multi-dimensional and multi-target hand motion forecasting.

llm.title_ja: TOMAS：一人称視点の手の動き予測のための位相認識型オペレーションモデリングと適応型ステージング
llm.tldr_ja: 手の骨格構造や関節ダイナミクスと物体の意味情報を結びつけて将来の手の動きを予測する位相認識型オペレーションモデリングおよび適応型ステージングフレームワーク「TOMAS」を提案し、最先端の性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 同じ物体と相互作用する場合でも異なる操作意図によって手の軌跡が大きく異なるが、既存手法では関節運動と物体セマンティクスとの関係性が十分に探求されていない。
llm.method: 手と物体の関係を推論して操作ターゲットと潜在操作を特定し、適応型ステージング機構によって順序付けられた潜在ステージに将来の手の動きを整理して軌跡を洗練させるTOMASの構築。
llm.result: 複数の公開ベンチマークにおいて、多次元かつ多ターゲットの手の動作予測において最先端のパフォーマンスを達成した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンセントリック

2611.23970.tldr_en: TOMAS is proposed, a topology-aware operation modeling and adaptive staging framework for egocentric hand forecasting that achieves state-of-the-art performance in multi-dimensional and multi-target hand motion forecasting.

2611.23963.title: CoRA-VTLA: Contact-Guided Attention and Queryable Response Memory for Tactile Post-Training
2611.23963.abstract: In precision manipulation, small errors in alignment or force can cause jamming or deformation, making contact feedback essential for adapting pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models to these tasks. A single tactile observation leaves the response to recent actions ambiguous. Direct tactile fusion during post-training can also disperse the action expert's visual attention and reduce the share it allocates to contact regions. To address these challenges, CoRA-VTLA augments pretrained VLAs with lightweight tactile modules. A queryable action-response memory retrieves recent contact responses so that the action expert can combine them with immediate tactile feedback. Contact-guided gaze supervision concentrates the visual attention of the tactile semantic token on image regions corresponding to fingertip contact. CoRA-VTLA achieves 73.33% mean success across three MuJoCo tasks, compared with 50% for direct tactile fusion with the same sensor inputs. It also achieves 67% success on an optical-tactile task from the public UniVTAC benchmark and 66.7% mean success across three real-robot tasks. These results show that tactile post-training helps pretrained VLAs adjust to changing contact.

llm.title_ja: CoRA-VTLA：触覚ポストトレーニングのための接触誘導型アテンションとクエリ可能応答メモリ
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みの視覚言語行動（VLA）モデルに軽量な触覚モジュールや接触誘導型アテンションを組み込むことで、精密な接触タスクへの適応力を高めた「CoRA-VTLA」を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実機タスクで高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 精密なマニピュレーションにおいて、単一の触覚観測では行動への応答が曖昧になり、直接的な触覚融合は視覚アテンションを分散させてしまう。
llm.method: 最近の接触応答を検索するクエリ可能アクション応答メモリと、指先の接触領域に対応する画像領域に視覚アテンションを集中させる接触誘導型視線指導をVLAに追加するCoRA-VTLAの提案。
llm.result: MuJoCoタスク、UniVTACベンチマーク、および実機ロボットタスクにおいて、直接的な触覚融合手法を上回る優れた平均成功率を達成した。

2611.23963.tldr_en: Results show that tactile post-training helps pretrained VLAs adjust to changing contact, and augments pretrained VLAs with lightweight tactile modules with CoRA-VTLA.

2611.23961.title: 3DTouch: A Tactile-aware VLA Model with 3D Geometric Relations for Dexterous Manipulation
2611.23961.abstract: In contact-rich dexterous manipulation, occlusion by the fingers and interacting objects obscures local geometry, preventing visual observations from fully capturing contact locations. Visually similar scenes may also differ subtly in the relative positions of interacting objects, leading to different contact states. We propose 3DTouch, a tactile-geometric conditioning approach for vision-language-action (VLA) models. 3DTouch constructs a shared 3D visuo-tactile representation by expressing RGB-D scene points and dense five-finger tactile measurements in the robot-base frame, preserving each taxel's spatial location and force vector. Hand-object and object-object relations derived from hand landmarks and pose-aligned reconstructed surfaces explicitly describe the relative arrangement of interacting entities. Together, these representations condition the VLA action expert on spatially localized contact forces and relative surface geometry, providing explicit cues for contact adjustment and object alignment. We evaluate 3DTouch on five real-world contact-rich dexterous manipulation tasks using a UR7e robot arm equipped with an XHand dexterous hand. 3DTouch improves the average success rate by 42 percentage points over the corresponding VLA baseline and by 20 percentage points over the strongest evaluated alternative. Ablation studies reveal the complementary benefits of scene geometry and spatial tactile feedback, with further gains from shared spatial grounding and explicit geometric relations.

llm.title_ja: 3DTouch：器用なマニピュレーションのための3D幾何学的関係を持つ触覚認識型VLAモデル
llm.tldr_ja: RGB-Dシーンポイントと高密度な触覚計測を統合し、手と物体の空間的な幾何学的関係を考慮してVLAモデルの行動エキスパートを条件付けするアプローチ「3DTouch」を提案し、実機での器用なマニピュレーションの成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 接触を伴う器用なマニピュレーションにおいて、指やオブジェクトによるオクルージョンが局所的なジオメトリを隠し、視覚観測だけでは接触位置を完全に捉えられない。
llm.method: RGB-D点群と五指の触覚計測値をロボットベース座標系で共有3D視覚触覚表現として構築し、相対的な配置関係を用いてVLAを条件付けする3DTouchの提案。
llm.result: UR7eロボットアームとXHandを用いた5つの実世界でのタスクにおいて、平均成功率をベースラインと比較して大幅に向上させた。

2611.23961.tldr_en: 3DTouch, a tactile-geometric conditioning approach for vision-language-action (VLA) models, constructs a shared 3D visuo-tactile representation by expressing RGB-D scene points and dense five-finger tactile measurements in the robot-base frame, preserving each taxel's spatial location and force vector.

2611.23939.title: Effects of Locomotion and Viewpoint Control on Immersive Robot Telepresence for Navigation and Inspection
2611.23939.abstract: In many robot telepresence interfaces, movement and viewing are managed through handheld inputs. This can divide attention between steering, looking, and inspection. We compared joystick versus omnidirectional treadmill locomotion and joystick-based versus head-guided camera control in a within-subject 2x2 study in which 17 participants used a virtual reality headset to guide a quadruped robot through a physical maze while locating marked wall symbols and capturing them as visual evidence. Mixed-effects analyses showed that head-guided camera control was associated with faster completion, lower wall-contact cost, lower workload, and more favorable presence, usability, technology acceptance, and flow than joystick-based camera control. The strongest overall objective performance was observed in the joystick locomotion plus head-guided camera condition, whereas the omnidirectional treadmill plus head-guided camera condition emerged as the strongest experiential compromise. Exploratory camera analyses showed that head-guided camera control reduced switching, increased reliance on the pan-tilt view, and supported a more stable viewing strategy across the maze. These strategy differences were consistent with the performance advantage, especially for wall-contact duration. Targets captured remained near ceiling and simulator sickness remained low across all conditions. Overall, the results indicate that viewpoint control was the stronger differentiator in this combined navigation and inspection task, while locomotion still shaped the objective and experiential tradeoff.

llm.title_ja: ナビゲーションと検査のための没入型ロボット遠隔プレゼンスにおける移動方式と視点制御の影響
llm.tldr_ja: 仮想現実ヘッドセットを用いて四足ロボットを迷路で誘導する実験を通じて、視点制御方式と移動方式が遠隔操作のパフォーマンスや作業負荷、臨場感に与える影響を評価した。
llm.problem: 多くのロボット遠隔プレゼンスインターフェースでは移動と視野の管理がハンドヘルド入力で行われ、ステアリングと検査の間で注意が分散してしまう。
llm.method: ジョイスティックと全方向トレッドミルによる移動方式、およびジョイスティックと頭部誘導によるカメラ制御を組み合わせた2x2の被験者内実験による評価。
llm.result: 頭部誘導によるカメラ制御が完了時間の短縮や壁との接触コストの低減、作業負荷の軽減などの優れた性能と主観的評価をもたらしたことを示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.23939.tldr_en: Overall, the results indicate that viewpoint control was the stronger differentiator in this combined navigation and inspection task, while locomotion still shaped the objective and experiential tradeoff.

2611.23935.title: Facet-SLAM: Real-Time Triangle Splatting SLAM
2611.23935.abstract: Dense SLAM systems based on 3D Gaussian splatting build maps that render photorealistically, but their surface geometry is poor, and obtaining a mesh requires extraction or fusion stages. Triangle splatting avoids this with surface primitives whose vertices can be triangulated directly into a connected mesh, yet SLAM with this representation has so far relied on photometric tracking, which is too slow for localization at sensor rate. We present Facet-SLAM, the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras. Fast geometric registration is the natural alternative, but it is not sufficient alone, since the mapper's optimization displaces triangles from the observed surface and makes them unreliable registration targets. We therefore separate the two roles: the tracker sets each triangle's centroid from fused depth and registers frames to these centroids by GICP, while the mapper is restricted to non-translating updates via a change of variables. Our system achieves competitive tracking accuracy at around 100 FPS on a desktop GPU and runs at sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin. Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm. We will release the implementation at https://github.com/edward62740/Facet-SLAM.

llm.title_ja: Facet-SLAM：リアルタイム三角形スプラッティングSLAM
llm.tldr_ja: RGB-Dカメラ向けの最初のリアルタイム三角形スプラッティングSLAMシステム「Facet-SLAM」を提案し、幾何学的登録と非移動更新を分離することで、高速で精度の高い表面メッシュ構築と位置合わせを実現した。
llm.problem: 3DガウシアンスプラッティングベースのDense SLAMは表面ジオメトリが粗く、三角形スプラッティングを用いたSLAMはフォトメトリックトラッキングの処理速度がセンサーレートに対して遅すぎる。
llm.method: トラッカーが深さから各三角形の重心を設定してGICPでフレームを登録し、マッパーは変数の変更により非移動更新に制限するFacet-SLAMシステムの構築。
llm.result: デスクトップGPUで約100 FPS、Jetson AGX Orin上でセンサーレートでの動作を達成し、従来の手法と比較して20倍以上高速で表面精度を向上させた。
keywords_ja: 三角形スプラッティング

2611.23935.tldr_en: Facet-SLAM is presented, the first real-time triangle splatting SLAM system for RGB-D cameras, which is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm.

2611.23932.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate
2611.23932.abstract: Diverse, semantically synchronized, and low-latency facial expressions are essential for human-robot interaction. While large language models (LLMs) have endowed anthropomorphic robots with fluent speech, facial expression still struggles to follow the conversation. Motivated by this gap, we present Emo-H2A (hidden-to-actuation), a paradigm that drives a facial robot directly from LLM hidden states during autoregressive decoding. Without a separate emotion label, expression stays continuous and context-sensitive, and the face moves with the unfolding reply. We instantiate this paradigm as EmoManifold, a training-free method that extracts a valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinate from each hidden state, projects it, and drives the face at token granularity. The readout is checked on six language models, and the same projection drives our 29-degree-of-freedom (DoF) facial robot. When driven by this projection, the face shifts its expression in the matching direction on 87.5% of within-reply valence transitions, whereas holding a single label for the whole reply leaves directional tracking near the 50% chance level, and first moves in 0.96s rather than waiting 10-26s for the reply to finish and a turn-level label to return.

llm.title_ja: Emo-H2A：トークンレートでのLLM隠れ状態からの顔面ロボットの直接駆動
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデルの自己回帰デコード中の隠れ状態から感情座標を抽出し、追加の感情ラベルなしで顔面ロボットの表情を連続的かつ文脈に即してリアルタイムに駆動する「Emo-H2A」パラダイムを提案した。
llm.problem: 大規模言語モデルが流暢な音声を実現する一方、顔面ロボットの表情生成は会話の流れに追従することが困難であった。
llm.method: 各隠れ状態からVAD（Valence-Arousal-Dominance）座標を抽出し、それを投影してトークン粒度で顔面を駆動するトレーニング不要の手法「EmoManifold」の導入。
llm.result: 29自由度の顔面ロボットを用いた実験において、返答内のvalence遷移の87.5%で表情を一致する方向にシフトさせることができることを示した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマンロボットインタラクション

2611.23932.tldr_en: Emo-H2A (hidden-to-actuation), a paradigm that drives a facial robot directly from LLM hidden states during autoregressive decoding, and instantiate this paradigm as EmoManifold, a training-free method that extracts a valence-arousal-dominance coordinate from each hidden state, projects it, and drives the face at token granularity.

2611.23930.title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments
2611.23930.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are expected to achieve semantic reasoning, intelligent decision-making, and long-horizon navigation under strict onboard constraints. While recent foundation-model-driven approaches have shown promising progress toward this goal, existing methods remain limited by challenges in 3D data availability, trajectory feasibility, long-horizon reasoning, and computational efficiency in complex environments. To bridge these gaps, we propose VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation (VLN) framework for aerial robots. VLN-AR decouples multimodal reasoning and low-level control, enabling structured prediction of 3D pose commands and navigation intentions that are translated into dynamically feasible actions. To mitigate data scarcity and domain gaps, we introduce a fully automated 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based pipeline to generate scalable photorealistic UAV navigation data. A progressive three-stage training strategy further enhances grounding, scene reasoning, and complex navigation. In addition, a lightweight cognitive agent improves long-horizon reasoning via memory-aware task decomposition. Finally, we design onboard optimization techniques, including token sparsification and model lightweighting, achieving 7.1x-9.4x speedup while maintaining high navigation performance on resource-limited UAV platforms. Experiments show great improvements over existing methods in both simulation and real-world UAV navigation. Project website: https://wyz000.github.io/VLN-AR/

llm.title_ja: 複雑な環境における空中ロボットのための階層型オンボード視覚言語ナビゲーションフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: 空中ロボット向けにマルチモーダル推論と低レベル制御を分離した階層型視覚言語ナビゲーションフレームワーク「VLN-AR」を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実世界のUAV環境で優れた性能と高速化を達成した。
llm.problem: ファウンデーションモデルベースのUAVナビゲーション手法は、3Dデータの可用性、軌跡の実行可能性、長期推論、計算効率の面で制限がある。
llm.method: 3DGSベースのフォトリアルなUAVナビゲーションデータ生成パイプライン、3段階の訓練戦略、メモリ認識型タスク分解を行う軽量認知エージェント、およびオンボード最適化を統合したVLN-ARの提案。
llm.result: リソースが限られたUAVプラットフォーム上で高いナビゲーション性能を維持しながら7.1倍〜9.4倍の高速化を達成し、従来手法を大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション
階層型フレームワーク
3Dガウシアンスプラッティング

2611.23930.tldr_en: VLN-AR is proposed, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation (VLN) framework for aerial robots that decouples multimodal reasoning and low-level control, enabling structured prediction of 3D pose commands and navigation intentions that are translated into dynamically feasible actions.

2611.23926.title: GTI: Grounding Task Intent Throughout Long-Horizon VLA Manipulation
2611.23926.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models generate local actions from visual observations, language, and robot state, but long-horizon manipulation requires the global task intent to remain grounded in the currently executable context. We propose GTI (Grounding Task Intent), which uses the current observation and execution history to localize the active subtask and its execution phase. For the same local subtask, GTI generates two phase-dependent visual targets: an interaction/contact state and a local completion state. The local language instruction and the corresponding phase-specific visual target jointly condition the VLA, specifying both what to do now and what state should be reached at the current phase. During execution, anomaly monitoring and local recovery re-establish an intent-consistent execution context through rollback, re-observation, and phase re-evaluation after persistent deviation. We evaluate GTI on RoboCasa365, VLA-Arena Horizon-Long, and real-world PiPER tasks. Relative to matched Global-FT baselines, GR00T success on seen composite RoboCasa365 tasks increases from 14.6%/12.1% to 31.8%/20.4% under ID/OOD evaluation. On VLA-Arena, GTI+$π_{0.5}$ reaches 47.6% overall success versus 45.2% for an adapted ForeAct baseline, with gains of 5.2/6.0 percentage points on the harder L1/L2 tasks. In the three real-robot task experiments, mean full-task success increases from 21.7% to 59.2%. The results indicate that persistent semantic intent localization and phase-conditioned visual grounding improve multi-stage execution, while failure-triggered local recovery provides additional deployment-time support.

llm.title_ja: GTI: 長期VLAマニピュレーションを通じたタスク意図のグラウンディング
llm.tldr_ja: 長期的なマニピュレーションを改善するため、現在の観測と実行履歴を用いてアクティブなサブタスクと実行フェーズを特定するGTIを提案する。
llm.problem: 長期マニピュレーションでは、グローバルなタスク意図が実行中の文脈に正しくグラウンディングし続ける必要があるという課題。
llm.method: 現在の観測と実行履歴を利用してアクティブなサブタスクとフェーズを特定し、フェーズ依存の視覚的ターゲットを生成してVLAを条件付けする。
llm.result: RoboCasa365、VLA-Arena、および実機のPiPERタスクにおいて、ベースラインと比較して成功率が大幅に向上した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2611.23926.tldr_en: The results indicate that persistent semantic intent localization and phase-conditioned visual grounding improve multi-stage execution, while failure-triggered local recovery provides additional deployment-time support.

2611.23917.title: Vanguard: Knowing When to Trust the Draft in Speculative Vision-Language Agents
2611.23917.abstract: Vision-language agents that browse websites, operate phones and act in homes reason before every action, so every step waits for a large model, a latency and cost that stand in the way of deployment. Step-level speculation lets a small model draft each step and calls the large model only on rejected drafts, but its outcome rests on the judge, and a judge that reads only a step's text cannot tell whether the step fits the screen it acts on. We find that a few samples of a small model can contain a correct step about as often as the large model gets the step right, and not always on the same steps: checked against the screen, small drafts can be not only cheaper but better. We present Vanguard, a training-free judge that leaves the draft and target models unchanged: a general decision model, with the screenshot in view, gives each candidate step a probability of being right in one forward pass; the best candidate is kept if it clears a threshold, and otherwise the large model writes the step. On web, mobile and embodied agents, a 2B draft judged by Vanguard is at least as accurate as its 8B target and significantly more accurate on Mind2Web and EB-ALFRED, while the target writes only a minority of the steps; it completes far more closed-loop episodes, and with a 27B target from another family it is both faster and more accurate. Vanguard is the most accurate judge we compare on the agent tasks; it relies on the screenshot on web and mobile tasks, its calibrated threshold transfers to unseen websites, and across model families its gain over the target grows with the draft's pass@4 relative to the target's accuracy. Vanguard composes with token-level speculative decoding and matches trained process reward models on mathematics, turning speculation from a way to save the large model's work into one that can improve on it.

llm.title_ja: Vanguard: 推論型ビジョン言語エージェントにおけるドラフト信頼性の判断
llm.tldr_ja: スクリーンショットを入力として、小モデルのドラフトステップの成否を1回の順伝播で判定する学習不要の判定器Vanguardを提案する。
llm.problem: ステップごとの推論を行うビジョン言語エージェントにおいて、大規模モデルの利用は遅延とコストの大きな障壁となること。
llm.method: スクリーンショットを入力とし、各候補ステップが正しい確率を1回の順伝播で出力する学習不要の判定器Vanguardを設計する。
llm.result: Web、モバイル、および身体性エージェントにおいて、大規模モデルと同等以上の精度を達成しつつ、ターゲットモデルの呼び出しを少数に抑えた。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語エージェント

2611.23917.tldr_en: V Vanguard is the most accurate judge the authors compare on the agent tasks; it relies on the screenshot on web and mobile tasks, its calibrated threshold transfers to unseen websites, and across model families its gain over the target grows with the draft's pass@4 relative to the target's accuracy.

2611.23916.title: ReLoco: Unified Humanoid Locomotion and Fall Recovery via Behavior-Conditioned Motion Priors
2611.23916.abstract: Humanoid robots must recover from falls and resume commanded motion to sustain locomotion. Learning these behaviors in one policy requires supervision that accommodates both upright movement and ground-contact recovery. We present ReLoco, a framework that uses behavior-conditioned adversarial motion priors to learn locomotion, get-up from arbitrary fallen postures, and command resumption within one proprioceptive policy. During training, robot posture selects the expert pool and conditions a shared discriminator with two behavior-specific outputs. Task rewards and shared regularization support command tracking and recovery, while temporary assistance facilitates exploration. A simulation-based refinement stage supplies robot-executed motion references for this supervision. Ablations examine conditional supervision, output separation, and reference quality under matched settings. At a common training iteration, the full policy achieves $96.80\%$ independent get-up success and $96.96\%$ push-recovery success, including command resumption. Its torso planar velocity root-mean-square error is $0.1266$~m/s, $14.7\%$ lower than the conditional single-output variant, with similar joint-angle discrepancy measured by dynamic time warping. Deployment on the 64.5-kg Tiangong~3.0 humanoid demonstrates walking, running, get-up, and locomotion resumption after falls using one proprioceptive actor, without controller switching or on-robot policy fine-tuning.

llm.title_ja: ReLoco: 動作条件付きモーションプライアによるヒューマノイドの統合型歩行と転倒からの復帰
llm.tldr_ja: 姿勢選択型の敵対的モーションプライアを用い、歩行、任意の姿勢からの起き上がり、コマンド再開を単一の固有受容ポリシーで実現するReLocoを提案する。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドロボットが転倒からの復帰と指令された移動の再開を単一のポリシーで学習することの難しさ。
llm.method: ロボットの姿勢に応じてエキスパートプールを選択し、共有の識別子を条件付ける動作条件付き敵対的モーションプライアフレームワークを用いる。
llm.result: Tiangong 3.0ヒューマノイドの実機において、コントローラの切り替えなしで歩行、走行、起き上がり、転倒からの復帰を実現した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.23916.tldr_en: ReLoco is presented, a framework that uses behavior-conditioned adversarial motion priors to learn locomotion, get-up from arbitrary fallen postures, and command resumption within one proprioceptive policy.

2611.23911.title: Scalable Iterative Multi-Agent Path Finding under Turn Constraints
2611.23911.abstract: Large-scale multi-mobile-robot systems require fast and reliable path planning under realistic motion constraints. Multi-Agent Path Finding with turn actions (MAPF$_T$) explicitly models orientation changes and turn-induced delays, but these constraints increase the computational burden of search-based methods. Priority-inheritance-based planning offers a highly scalable alternative, yet directly extending it to MAPF$_T$ is nontrivial because turn actions break the immediate node-vacation assumption underlying conventional priority inheritance. To address this challenge, this paper proposes PIBT$^*_T$, an efficient iterative solver for MAPF$_T$. PIBT$^*_T$ advances scalable multi-agent coordination by preserving the lightweight single-timestep planning mechanism of Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT), while introducing dedicated mechanisms to handle turn-induced dependencies, local deadlocks, livelock, and inefficient repeated pushing. Experiments on standard MAPF benchmarks show that PIBT$^*_T$ achieves high success rates and strong scalability, solving instances with up to 1000 agents within seconds. For realistic engineering environments, Action Dependency Graph (ADG)-based execution simulation and a flexible manufacturing system case study show that turn-aware planning better reflects robot execution and reduces actual makespan compared with classical MAPF planning. Experiments with TurtleBot4 robots further validate the practical feasibility of the proposed method.

llm.title_ja: 回転制約を考慮したスケーラブルな反復型マルチエージェント経路計画
llm.tldr_ja: 回転動作による遅延と依存関係を効率的に処理し、最大1000エージェントの問題を数秒で解く反復型ソルバーPIBT*_Tを提案する。
llm.problem: 回転動作を明示的にモデル化したマルチエージェント経路計画（MAPF_T）において、制約により探索ベースの手法では計算負担が増大する課題。
llm.method: PIBTの軽量な単一タイムステップ計画メカニズムを維持しつつ、回転起因の依存関係や局所的デッドロックに対処するPIBT*_Tを提案する。
llm.result: 標準的なMAPFベンチマークにおいて高い成功率と拡張性を示し、最大1000エージェントの問題を数秒で解き、TurtleBot4での実機検証も行った。

2611.23911.tldr_en: PIBT$^*_T$ advances scalable multi-agent coordination by preserving the lightweight single-timestep planning mechanism of Priority Inheritance with Backtracking (PIBT), while introducing dedicated mechanisms to handle turn-induced dependencies, local deadlocks, livelock, and inefficient repeated pushing.

2611.23894.title: Navigating Robots from Unknown and Uncalibrated Exocentric Cameras via Map Estimation
2611.23894.abstract: Exocentric cameras, mounted on walls or ceilings in indoor environments, offer wider vantage points and are less easily occluded than robot-mounted cameras, making them an appealing alternative for perception in robot navigation algorithms. Previous methods that use such cameras, however, require their pose and intrinsics to be known before deployment, demanding calibration that is time-consuming, requires specialized personnel, and must be repeated whenever a camera moves or a new room is navigated. We propose Robot-centric Obstacle Maps from Unknown and uncalibrated eXocentric cameras (ROMUX), an agent that navigates a robot toward point goals while avoiding obstacles using exocentric cameras that are both uncalibrated, meaning the system does not require their pose or intrinsic information as input, and unknown, meaning it is not fit to a specific camera during training and does not require pre-deployment fine-tuning. We train a cross-view transformer on large-scale simulation data to predict metric robot-centric obstacle maps from exocentric images, without conditioning image tokens on camera information. A small policy trained with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) then navigates on the predicted maps toward a goal coordinate relative to the robot. We benchmark our agent in simulation with cameras randomized per episode, and it matches the success rates of a PPO policy that navigates from a robot-mounted camera. Further, ROMUX works with one camera or multiple cameras with partial views and has been transferred zero-shot to a real robot using a camera at varying positions and orientations across various room layouts.

llm.title_ja: マップ推定を用いた未知かつ未較正の外部カメラからのロボットナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 未較正かつ未知の外部カメラ画像からメートル単位の障害物マップを予測し、ゼロショットでロボットを誘導するROMUXを提案する。
llm.problem: 外部カメラを用いたロボットナビゲーションにおいて、事前のカメラ較正や姿勢情報の入力が不可欠であり、変更のたびに再設定が必要になる課題。
llm.method: 大規模シミュレーションデータでクロスビューtransformerを訓練して外部カメラ画像からロボット中心の障害物マップを予測し、PPOでナビゲーションを行う。
llm.result: シミュレーションでロボット搭載カメラと同等の成功率を達成し、異なる部屋レイアウトの実機環境へゼロショットで移行できることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2611.23894.tldr_en: ROMUX is proposed, an agent that navigates a robot toward point goals while avoiding obstacles using exocentric cameras that are both uncalibrated, meaning the system does not require their pose or intrinsic information as input, and unknown, meaning it is not fit to a specific camera during training and does not require pre-deployment fine-tuning.

2611.23871.title: HOForce: Motion and Force Reconstruction of Hand-Object Interaction Using a Single-View RGB-D Video
2611.23871.abstract: Reconstructing hand-object interactions is an important task, and achieving it with a single camera makes large-scale capture practical but challenging due to heavy occlusions. We introduce HOForce to track hands and objects, and further recover interaction forces from single-view RGB-D video and known object properties. For two-hand manipulation, we jointly model fingertip forces of both hands and the contact forces between objects when two objects are presented. The reconstructed forces also improve motion tracking by giving pose constraints in the occluded regions. HOForce recovers hand and object motion more accurately on DexYCB and TACO and produces less hand-object penetration than interaction baselines on DexYCB. On our dataset of fingertip forces recorded with tactile sensors, HOForce reduces normal-force MAE by 24.5% relative to the strongest baseline. The recovered forces reproduce object motion in MuJoCo and transfer to other engines after adaptation.

llm.title_ja: HOForce: 単眼RGB-Dビデオを用いた手とオブジェクトのインタラクションのモーションおよび力再構築
llm.tldr_ja: 単眼RGB-Dビデオと既知のオブジェクト特性から、手とオブジェクトのモーション追跡と相互作用力の復元を同時に行うHOForceを提案する。
llm.problem: 単一カメラによる手とオブジェクトのインタラクション再構築は大規模キャプチャに実用的だが、激しいオクルージョンにより困難を伴うこと。
llm.method: 両手の指先力や物体間の接触力を共同でモデル化し、オクルージョン領域でのポーズ制約を与えることでモーション追跡を改善する。
llm.result: DexYCBおよびTACOデータセットでより正確にモーションを復元し、触覚センサで記録された指先力の法線力MAEを24.5%削減した。
keywords_ja: 手と物体のインタラクション

2611.23871.tldr_en: This work introduces HOForce to track hands and objects, and further recover interaction forces from single-view RGB-D video and known object properties, and jointly model fingertip forces of both hands and the contact forces between objects when two objects are presented.

2611.23867.title: Control-Aware Separating Hyperplanes for Control Barrier Functions in Planar Navigation
2611.23867.abstract: Separating hyperplanes are widely used in Control Barrier Function (CBF)-based collision avoidance, yet their orientations strongly govern control intervention-the deviation of the applied control from the robot's nominal command. Existing methods typically select hyperplane orientations from geometry alone. Jointly optimizing orientations and control yields a continuous, non-convex problem in which local nonlinear solvers suffer from initialization sensitivity, local minima, and unpredictable latency, while discretized orientation grids scale exponentially with obstacle count. For planar navigation of a polygonal robot among polygonal obstacles, we present a solver-free, control-aware separating hyperplane selection method that directly computes a global optimum of this joint problem at each step whenever it is feasible. Exploiting the geometry of Minkowski difference polygons, we reduce this continuous non-convex optimization to evaluating a polynomial-size set of candidate control interventions via closed-form algebraic checks, selecting the feasible candidate of minimum norm. Across 250 simulated navigation scenarios, our method reduces cumulative intervention cost by 3.6% at the median and 27.3% at the 90th percentile compared to a local nonlinear solver, and completion time by 0.6% and 5.6%, respectively. In scalability benchmarks, it achieves a 6.1x per-step speedup at 16 simultaneous obstacles.

llm.title_ja: 平面ナビゲーションにおける制御バリア関数に向けた制御考慮型分離超平面
llm.tldr_ja: ミンコフスキー差の幾何学を利用して非凸最適化を閉形式の代数的チェックに帰着させ、各ステップで大域的最適解を高速に計算する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 制御バリア関数に基づく衝突回避において、分離超平面の向きの選択が制御介入を強く左右するが、その共同最適化は非凸でソルバーの初期値依存や高計算量の課題があること。
llm.method: 多角形ロボットと多角形障害物の平面ナビゲーションにおいて、最小ノルムを持つ実行可能な候補を選択するソルバー不要の制御考慮型分離超平面選択手法を提案する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて、局所非nonlinearソルバーと比較して累積介入コストと完了時間を大幅に削減し、高速化を実現した。

2611.23867.tldr_en: This work presents a solver-free, control-aware separating hyperplane selection method that directly computes a global optimum of this joint problem at each step whenever it is feasible, and achieves a 6.1x per-step speedup at 16 simultaneous obstacles.

2611.23858.title: LAGR: Language-Aware Grasp Re-Ranking for Task Oriented Grasping
2611.23858.abstract: Grasping is a fundamental capability for robotic manipulation, with the appropriate grasp depending on the downstream task. For example, a hammer should be held by its handle for hammering but by its head when it is handed over. Selecting such a grasp requires consideration of two criteria: physical feasibility on the object and suitability for the task. Developing such an approach requires dense grasp labels with both feasibility and task scores on real observations, but existing task-oriented grasping datasets are small, synthetic, or costly to annotate. To address this gap, we construct a dataset of 2.68 million scored 5-DoF grasp annotations over 100,911 image-task pairs from $17$ object categories. Additionally, we introduce LAGR, a task-oriented grasp detection method that explicitly addresses both these challenges. Given vision-language inputs, LAGR first generates task-independent grasp proposals along with a physical feasibility score, and then scores the generated grasps with a language-conditioned re-ranker that reasons over all proposals jointly. Experiments show that LAGR outperforms the next best method by 9.3 percentage points. We further validate LAGR on real objects by executing task-oriented grasps with a Franka Research 3 robot.
2611.23858.comment: Manav Kulshrestha and Shreyans Jain contributed equally to this work

llm.title_ja: LAGR: タスク指向把持のための言語認識型把持再ランキング
llm.tldr_ja: ビジョン言語入力を受け取り、物理的妥当性とタスク適合性を考慮して把持候補を再ランキングするタスク指向把持検出手法LAGRを提案する。
llm.problem: タスク指向の把持には物理的妥当性とタスク適合性の両方の考慮が必要だが、既存のデータセットは小規模、合成的、または高コストであるという課題。
llm.method: 268万件のスコア付き把持アノテーションデータセットを構築し、タスク非依存の把持候補生成と、言語条件付きリランカーによるスコア付けを行うLAGRを提案する。
llm.result: 次の最適手法を9.3ポイント上回り、Franka Research 3ロボットを用いた実世界でのタスク指向把持実験により有効性を検証した。

2611.23858.tldr_en: This work introduces LAGR, a task-oriented grasp detection method that explicitly addresses both physical feasibility on the object and suitability for the task, and validates LAGR on real objects by executing task-oriented grasps with a Franka Research 3 robot.

2611.23855.title: RoboBuilder: Agentic Robot Co-Design with Real-world Video Feedback in the Loop
2611.23855.abstract: Can AI agents design robots that work in the real world? We introduce RoboBuilder, a benchmark in which coding agents co-design a robot's hardware and program from standard parts, motors and a custom 3D-printed part, and every design that passes in simulation is built and tested on a physical course. Simulation alone is not enough: under public part data, none of 15 initial passing designs crossed the real course, so an agent learns the simulator from measurements it requests and videos of real runs. Across four frontier coding agents, ten obstacles at three difficulty levels, 16,427 simulations of 12,774 distinct robots and 135 physical robots built in an estimated 240 hours, agents solve nearly all easy obstacles and invent mechanisms our search baselines do not reach, but falter at harder levels, when one robot must cross every obstacle, and in the real world, where 66% of simulated passes hold across all levels. Closing the loop helps: shown a video of its real failure, an agent redesigns the robot, sometimes correcting its simulator, and removes 72% of level-1 and level-2 failures. RoboBuilder measures progress toward agents that engineer real machines. Project Page: https://ghadinehme.com/robobuilder.github.io/

llm.title_ja: RoboBuilder: 実世界からのビデオフィードバックをループに組み込んだ自律型ロボット共同設計
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーションでの設計を実世界コースで実際に組み立ててテストし、失敗動画のフィードバックを基にエージェントが再設計を行うベンチマークRoboBuilderを提案する。
llm.problem: AIエージェントが実世界で動作するロボットを設計できるかという問いに対し、シミュレーション単体では実世界の環境に適応できないという課題。
llm.method: 標準パーツや3Dプリントパーツからロボットのハードウェアとプログラムをコーディングエージェントが共同設計し、実機での失敗動画をフィードバックして再設計を行う。
llm.result: 4つのフロンティアコーディングエージェントを用いて多数のシミュレーションと実機製作を行い、失敗動画の提示によりレベル1および2の失敗の72%を除去できた。
keywords_ja: 実世界フィードバック

2611.23855.tldr_en: This work introduces RoboBuilder, a benchmark in which coding agents co-design a robot's hardware and program from standard parts, motors and a custom 3D-printed part, and every design that passes in simulation is built and tested on a physical course.

2611.23843.title: RePlan-VLA: Progress-Aware Replanning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.23843.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose robotic manipulation, yet their performance often degrades on long-horizon tasks that require multiple interdependent manipulations. Instead of burdening the VLA policies with long-horizon reasoning, memory, action generation, progress tracking, and error recovery, we argue for leveraging their short-horizon manipulation capabilities within an execution-aware framework. To this end, we introduce \textnormal{\textbf{RePlan-VLA}}, a VLA-agnostic framework that translates a VLA's short-horizon capabilities into reliable long-horizon execution. RePlan-VLA explicitly monitors the robot's motion for progress evaluation, and adaptively revises the future plan based on observed outcomes. We preserve the underlying VLA policy entirely, requiring no additional fine-tuning. Experiments on RoboCasa365 and CALVIN benchmarks show an improvement of 21.9% and 10.4% in success rate over the next strongest baseline. We also validate our approach for real-world deployment on a Franka Research 3 robot.
2611.23843.comment: Apoorva Vashisth and Manav Kulshrestha contributed equally to this work. Prof. Zachary Kingston and Prof. Aniket Bera jointly advised this work

llm.title_ja: RePlan-VLA: 長期ビジョン言語アクションモデルのための進捗認識型再計画
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの動作から進捗を明示的にモニタリングし、観測された結果に基づいて将来の計画を適応的に修正するVLA非依存のフレームワークRePlan-VLAを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルに長期的な推論やエラー回復を直接負担させると、複数の相互依存するマニピュレーションを含む長期タスクで性能が低下する課題。
llm.method: VLAのポリシー自体は微調整せずそのまま維持し、実行状況を監視して進捗評価と将来の計画の適応的修正を行う実行認識型フレームワークを導入する。
llm.result: RoboCasa365およびCALVINベンチマークで次位のベースラインより成功率が大幅に向上し、Frankaロボットによる実機展開も検証した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2611.23843.tldr_en: RePlan-VLA is introduced, a VLA-agnostic framework that translates a VLA's short-horizon capabilities into reliable long-horizon execution and preserves the underlying VLA policy entirely.

2611.23830.title: Estimation-Aware Reachability
2611.23830.abstract: Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability computes the states from which a system can be kept safe under worst-case disturbances, but it assumes the state is known exactly, whereas real robots act on noisy estimates whose uncertainty evolves with their motion. We extend Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability to the robot's belief, estimate and uncertainty, treating unexpected measurements as a bounded adversary and enlarging the unsafe set by the current uncertainty, so that certified states are safe with a prescribed probability. The formulation is compatible with existing solvers. In simulation, the resulting safety filters nearly eliminate the collisions of certaintyequivalent HJ and are less conservative than equally safe uncertainty-padding baselines. The implementation code is available at https://github.com/HimanshuPaudel/Estimation-Aware-Reachability

llm.title_ja: 推定認識型到達可能性
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実性の進化を伴うロボットの信念や推定値に対し、予期せぬ測定を制限付きの敵対者として扱い安全領域を拡張する拡張ハミルトン・ジャコビ到達可能性を提案する。
llm.problem: ハミルトン・ジャコビ到達可能性は状態が正確に知られていると仮定するが、実際のロボットは運動に伴って不確実性が変化するノイズの多い推定値に基づいて動作する点。
llm.method: ロボットの信念、推定値、不確実性に拡張し、現在の不確実性によって安全でない集合を拡大することで規定の確率で安全性を保証する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて、提案する安全性フィルタが確実性同等HJの衝突をほぼ排除し、保守性を抑えられることを示した。

2611.23830.tldr_en: This work extends Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability to the robot's belief, estimate and uncertainty, treating unexpected measurements as a bounded adversary and enlarging the unsafe set by the current uncertainty, so that certified states are safe with a prescribed probability.

2611.23825.title: Learning Martial Arts Motion Skills for Animating Opponents in VR Sparring Games
2611.23825.abstract: Animating virtual opponents is an important yet challenging task in game development. In martial arts games, opponent motions must not only be physically plausible but also exhibit appropriate technique, timing, transitions, and target-directed intent. Traditional game animations often rely on handcrafted clips, state machine transitions, and procedural adjustments, which can be labor-intensive and may limit the behavioral diversity of non-player characters. This paper presents a martial arts motion skills learning framework for character animation in virtual sparring games. Inspired by Tang Soo Do, we collected a martial arts motion capture dataset containing isolated attacking and defending techniques, technique combinations and transitions, and contextual sparring variations. We first pretrained a reusable repertoire of martial arts motion skills from the captured data using reinforcement learning (RL) with adversarial style rewards, and then adapted these skills with task-specific rewards for target-directed striking and threat-aware evasion. We evaluated the motions generated by the learned policy through a user study, in which participants assessed their physical plausibility, smoothness, and martial arts form. To demonstrate their applicability to interactive gameplay, we developed a VR sparring prototype for Meta Quest headsets. The prototype combines policy-generated motion clips with lightweight state-based control to support interactive opponent behavior. Together, these findings support the feasibility of using a learned martial arts skill repertoire as a motion foundation for animating opponents in VR sparring games.

llm.title_ja: VRスパーリングゲームにおける対戦相手アニメーションのための武術モーションスキルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 敵対的スタイル報酬を用いた強化学習により再利用可能な武術スキルレパートリーを事前学習し、タスク特化型報酬で適応させるフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: VRゲーム内の仮想対戦相手のモーションは、物理的に自然でありながら適切な技術や意図を持つ必要があるが、手動のクリップや状態機械では行動の多様性が制限されること。
llm.method: 唐手道に着想を得たモーションキャプチャデータから強化学習を用いて武術モーションスキルを事前学習し、ターゲット指向の攻撃や回避へ適応させる。
llm.result: ユーザー調査により物理的妥当性、滑らかさ、武術の形式が評価され、Meta Questヘッドセット向けのVRスパーリングプロトタイプを通じて対戦相手の動作として実証された。
keywords_ja: キャラクターアニメーション

2611.23825.tldr_en: The feasibility of using a learned martial arts skill repertoire as a motion foundation for animating opponents in VR sparring games is supported.

2611.23816.title: RoboDx: Repair and Diagnosis of Faults in Robot Software
2611.23816.abstract: A patch to a robot's navigation software can pass every unit test and still drive the robot off its path. Checking how the repaired robot drives catches such patches. It does not show that the agent found everything that was wrong. We introduce RoboDx, a generator of repair tasks for simulated robot navigation software with known injected faults.
