A hidden verifier marks a repair as verified only if the robot then drives correctly in hidden scenarios, which the agent never sees. A second track hides the code and asks the agent to pick the cause from a list of hypotheses. A task with two faults can contain a quiet fault, a fault that makes no hidden scenario fail unless the other fault is also present. On our set of 100 tasks, RoboDx-Hard-100, almost every repair by Claude Opus 5.5 with standard coding tools is verified. We analyse 94 of the tasks, 44 with one fault and 50 with two. On the 50 two-fault tasks, only 17 of Opus's 49 verified repairs remove both injected edits. Most faults left behind are configuration constants whose correct value the task's documentation does not state. Opus names both faults on 10/50 of these tasks when it cannot see the code. We then give four current models the same measurements of each faulty robot, picked so that, in the simulator, only the true cause produces all of them. The models name the cause on at most 38 of 94 tasks. They are right on almost all when they also get the simulator's output for every hypothesis. Their own predictions of that output give no detectable gain. On 97 tasks from real bug-fix pull requests, Claude Haiku 5.5, the weakest model on the generated tasks, scores lowest, and the other three models are not ordered.

llm.title_ja: RoboDx: ロボットソフトウェアの不具合の修復と診断
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーションされたロボットナビゲーションソフトウェア向けに既知の注入故障を含む修復タスクを生成するRoboDxを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットのナビゲーションソフトウェアのパッチは単体テストをすべて通過してもロボットを誤作動させることがあるが、何が問題であったかを網羅的に示すのは難しいこと。
llm.method: 隠しシナリオでロボットが正しく走行するかどうかで修復を検証するロボットナビゲーション用修復タスクジェネレータ「RoboDx」を構築し、LLMによる診断能力を分析する。
llm.result: RoboDx-Hard-100のタスクにおいて、Claude Opusなどによる修復や原因特定の傾向を分析し、現実のバグ修正プルリクエストにおけるモデル性能を評価した。
keywords_ja: ロボットソフトウェア

2611.23816.tldr_en: RoboDx, a generator of repair tasks for simulated robot navigation software with known injected faults, is introduced, and a hidden verifier marks a repair as verified only if the robot then drives correctly in hidden scenarios, which the agent never sees.

2611.23804.title: TacPilot: Does Touch Need to Be Everywhere?
2611.23804.abstract: Tactile feedback helps visual manipulation policies respond to local contact, but changes in tactile observations do not always require corrective motion, and sustained corrections do not always require new tactile features. We introduce TacPilot, a tactile residual framework that separates representation updates from action intervention around a frozen visual policy. TacPilot uses a perception gate to determine when tactile features need refreshing and updates only affected regions while reusing unchanged features. A separate intervention gate determines whether bounded Cartesian and gripper residuals modify the nominal visual action. This separation allows tactile perception and action correction to follow different spatial and temporal demands during manipulation. In offline expert-trajectory replay, local feature reuse reduces encoded regions by 56.4% relative to periodic full encoding, with essentially unchanged action predictions. In an exploratory simulation evaluation spanning two cylinder sizes, TacPilot succeeds in 26 of 30 trials (86.7%). We further validate TacPilot on OpenArm v2 equipped with Paxini tactile sensors across four contact-rich manipulation tasks.

llm.title_ja: TacPilot: 触覚はあらゆる場所に必要なのか？
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された視覚ポリシーの周囲で表現の更新とアクション介入を分離し、必要な部分だけ触覚特徴を更新する触覚残差フレームワークTacPilotを提案する。
llm.problem: 視覚マニピュレーションポリシーにおいて触覚フィードバックは有効だが、触覚情報の変化が常に補正動作を必要とするわけではないという課題。
llm.method: 触覚特徴のリフレッシュ要件を判断する知覚ゲートと、デカルトおよびグリッパーの残差が視覚アクションを修正するかを判断する介入ゲートを備えたTacPilotを提案する。
llm.result: オフラインの専門家軌跡リプレイにおいて符号化領域を大幅に削減しつつアクション予測を維持し、シミュレーションおよびOpenArm v2の実機4タスクで有効性を検証した。

2611.23804.tldr_en: TacPilot, a tactile residual framework that separates representation updates from action intervention around a frozen visual policy, is introduced and validated on OpenArm v2 equipped with Paxini tactile sensors across four contact-rich manipulation tasks.

2611.23803.title: CoT-WAM: Collaborative Training of Vision-Language Models and World-Action Models via Plan Latents
2611.23803.abstract: General robot manipulation requires both semantic competence and physical foresight. World action models (WAMs) acquire an understanding of and predictive capability over the physical world by jointly modeling visual foresight and action distributions. However, existing WAMs still lack semantic competence: they have limited ability to perform open-world scene understanding, semantic reasoning, and long-horizon planning. Although vision-language models (VLMs) provide these capabilities, effectively integrating their semantic priors into WAM prediction and control remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose CoT-WAM, a jointly trained WAM-VLM framework. CoT-WAM uses a learnable embedding to exchange information between the VLM and the WAM, which is supervised by textual and goal-image signals during training to encode rich intent information. A tailored two-stage training strategy enables joint optimization and more effective collaboration between the VLM and WAM. We evaluate CoT-WAM on six benchmarks covering control performance, zero-shot generalization, and long-horizon planning. CoT-WAM achieves SOTA performance on LIBERO, CALVIN, and RoboCasa-Kitchen, and demonstrates stronger zero-shot generalization on LIBERO-Plus and LIBERO-Pro without fine-tuning. On RoboCasa365, it further improves long-horizon planning over baselines with and without external planners. Real-world experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in practical deployments. Code is available at: https://github.com/jhz1192/CoT-WAM.git
2611.23803.tldr_en: CoT-WAM is proposed, a jointly trained WAM-VLM framework that uses a learnable embedding to exchange information between the VLM and the WAM, which is supervised by textual and goal-image signals during training to encode rich intent information.

llm.title_ja: CoT-WAM: プラン潜在表現を通じたビジョン・言語モデルとワールド・アクションモデルの協調訓練
llm.tldr_ja: CoT-WAMは、学習可能な埋め込みを用いてVLMとWAMの間で情報を交換し、テキストおよび目標画像信号で教師あり学習を行うことで、セマンティック能力と物理的予測力を統合したフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存のワールドアクションモデル（WAM）は、オープンワールドのシーン理解や長期的計画を行うためのセマンティックな能力が不足している。
llm.method: VLMとWAMの間で情報を交換するための学習可能な埋め込みを使用し、訓練中にテキストおよび目標画像信号によって指導する2段階の訓練戦略を提案する。
llm.result: LIBERO、CALVIN、RoboCasa-KitchenなどのベンチマークでSOTAを達成し、ゼロショット汎化性能と長期計画能力の向上が実証された。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語モデル

2611.23774.title: Improve How You Improve: Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Multi-Object Navigation
2611.23774.abstract: To advance the development of embodied general navigation, zero-shot open-vocabulary multi-object navigation has attracted increasing attention, aiming to enable robots to efficiently search multiple objects in unseen environments without training. For this task, the key lies in improving navigation policies from earlier searches to locate subsequent goals more efficiently. Recent methods automate this process through trajectory reflection and rule revision, enabling policy self-improvement. However, the mechanisms for diagnosing problems and generating revisions are typically designed by humans and remain fixed across iterations. Consequently, the system's capacity for continued self-improvement remains constrained, even as its navigation policy evolves. To this end, we propose RPSI-Nav, a Recursive Policy Self-Improvement framework for zero-shot multi-object navigation that revises both the navigation program and its revision mechanism. RPSI-Nav diagnoses search behavior, requests diagnostic views when existing observations cannot distinguish competing causes, and generates targeted navigation revisions. Feedback from subsequent goal searches is linked to the rules that produced these revisions, guiding changes to diagnosis, observation acquisition, and revision planning. The updated improver governs subsequent navigation improvements, forming a recursive loop in which RPSI-Nav revises its own improvement process. Across goals, the robot conditionally inherits accepted program updates and spatial memory, enabling search experience to improve both future navigation and adaptation. Benchmark experiments and qualitative real-robot evaluations validate RPSI-Nav's effectiveness.

llm.title_ja: 改善方法の改善: ゼロショットオープンボキャブラリーマルチオブジェクトナビゲーションのための再帰的ポリシー自己改善
llm.tldr_ja: 検索行動の診断や観察の要求、ターゲットを絞ったナビゲーションの修正を行い、改善プロセス自体を再帰的に更新するフレームワークRPSI-Navを提案する。
llm.problem: ゼロショットのオープンボキャブラリーマルチオブジェクトナビゲーションにおいて、ポリシー自己改善のための問題診断や修正の仕組みが人間によって固定設計されているため、自己改善能力が制限されること。
llm.method: ナビゲーションプログラムだけでなくその修正メカニズム自体を改訂し、診断・観察取得・修正計画を変更する再帰的ループを形成するRPSI-Navを提案する。
llm.result: ベンチマーク実験および定性的な実機評価を通じて、RPSI-Navの有効性が検証された。
keywords_ja: マルチオブジェクトナビゲーション

2611.23774.tldr_en: RPSI-Nav is proposed, a Recursive Policy Self-Improvement framework for zero-shot multi-object navigation that revises both the navigation program and its revision mechanism, enabling search experience to improve both future navigation and adaptation.

2611.23746.title: ZERITH V2.5: From Predictive Power to Policy Learnability
2611.23746.abstract: When humans learn to manipulate an unfamiliar object, they may already be able to anticipate how its state will change while still being unable to control it skillfully. This gap between prediction and control motivates us to study how the priors acquired by video generation models can be used effectively by an action policy. We present ZERITH V2.5, a video-action model (VAM) in which the action policy reads intermediate features of a video generation model, and use it to study, under fixed demonstrations and a fixed total number of updates, what kind of predictive training improves subsequent action learning. We find that the way video predictive training is supervised affects subsequent action learning. In our experiments, adapting at many noise levels yields a large gain, while adapting only at the noise level used at deployment yields none. Weight-transfer experiments further show that the gain stays with the adapted weights when they remain in the video generation model and disappears when they are used only to initialize the action policy. Initial loss and gradient measurements at the start of joint training indicate that target-domain predictive training gives the video model a better starting state, making subsequent joint learning of prediction and action easier. Under matched data and training budgets, predictive adaptation improves control. We evaluate the complete policy on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, Meta-World MT50, and real-robot tasks.
2611.23746.comment: 50 pages, 17 figures, 22 tables. Project page: https://www.zerith.com/blog/zerith-2-5/

llm.title_ja: ZERITH V2.5: 予測能力からポリシー学習可能性へ
llm.tldr_ja: 行動ポリシーがビデオ生成モデルの中間特徴を読み込むビデオ行動モデル（VAM）「ZERITH V2.5」を提案し、予測的訓練がアクション学習に与える影響を調査する。
llm.problem: 未知の物体の操作を学ぶ際、状態変化の予測と巧みな制御の間にはギャップがあり、ビデオ生成モデルの事前学習がアクションポリシーにどう活用できるかという課題。
llm.method: ビデオ生成モデルの中間特徴量をアクションポリシーが読み取るVAMを構築し、多様なノイズレベルでの適応や重み転移実験を通じて予測的訓練の効果を検証する。
llm.result: ターゲットドメインでの予測的訓練がビデオモデルの初期状態を改善し、予測と行動の共同学習を容易にすることを示し、LIBEROや実機タスクで評価した。

2611.23746.tldr_en: It is found that the way video predictive training is supervised affects subsequent action learning, and initial loss and gradient measurements at the start of joint training indicate that target-domain predictive training gives the video model a better starting state, making subsequent joint learning of prediction and action easier.

2611.23731.title: RecallFlow: Episodic Memory as the Source Distribution of Generative Robot Policies
2611.23731.abstract: Diffusion and flow-matching policies have become a standard choice for visuomotor imitation learning, owing to their ability to model multimodal action distributions. In memory-dependent manipulation, the robot must act on information that is no longer visible. Existing methods feed the observation history to the policy as an additional condition, while action generation still starts from Gaussian noise. However, the policy must then pick out the relevant target from a long and redundant history, leading to spurious correlations and unreliable decisions as the memory load grows. Additionally, the initial noise carries no information about what the robot has seen, leaving generation without guidance toward the remembered target. To address these issues, we propose RecallFlow, a flow-policy framework that builds the source distribution from episodic memory. Recall-Relocalization relates the memory to the current view through a few recall slots, so that the source reflects where the remembered targets are now. Recall Anchors then turns each slot into a Gaussian component of the source, enabling generation to start close to the intended action instead of from noise. The transport network then completes the action from the current observation alone, keeping inference nearly as cheap as a memoryless policy. We further build a suite of memory-dependent tasks grouped by memory load and compare all policies under a matched protocol. Extensive experiments show that RecallFlow achieves a state-of-the-art average success rate of 80.4% on the public MIKASA-Robo memory benchmark, and outperforms the strongest baseline by 20.3 points on our suite and by 18.8 points on four real-robot tasks.

llm.title_ja: RecallFlow: 生成ロボットポリシーのソース分布としてのエピソード記憶
llm.tldr_ja: エピソード記憶からソース分布を構築し、記憶されたターゲットに近い位置から行動生成を開始するフローポリシーフレームワークRecallFlowを提案する。
llm.problem: 記憶依存のマニピュレーションにおいて、過去の長い観察履歴を条件としてガウス雑音からアクション生成を行うと、スプリアス相関や信頼性の低い決定につながる課題。
llm.method: 記憶と現在のビューをリコールスロットで結びつけてソースに反映させ、各スロットをガウス成分に変換して生成が目的のアクションの近くから開始できるようにする。
llm.result: MIKASA-RoboメモリベンチマークでSOTAの成功率を達成し、提案するタスクスイートや4つの実機タスクでベースラインを大きく上回った。

2611.23731.tldr_en: Recursion and flow-matching policies have become a standard choice for visuomotor imitation learning, owing to their ability to model multimodal action distributions, but this work proposes RecallFlow, a flow-policy framework that builds the source distribution from episodic memory.

2611.23719.title: Improving While Deployed: Learning Proactive End-to-End Driving from Imperfect Human Takeover Data
2611.23719.abstract: Once deployed on vehicles, end-to-end driving models continuously encounter challenging scenarios, generating valuable human takeover data that capture both model outputs and human behaviors. However, human interventions are often imperfect, as drivers may intervene too late or unnecessarily. Consequently, direct imitation can reinforce late responses or discourage otherwise appropriate maneuvers. To address this challenge, we propose an offline post-training framework that transforms imperfect takeover data into proactive supervision. We first construct diverse trajectory candidates by augmenting the plans of the deployed model and shifting recorded human corrective maneuvers earlier in time. We then train a scene-conditioned trajectory scorer to rank these candidates using expert demonstrations and unpaired preference signals from takeover logs. Using this scorer, we selectively replace pre-takeover training targets with higher-scoring candidates while retaining the original targets in normal driving scenarios. Finally, we distill the resulting targets into the driving model without changing its inference architecture. In closed-loop evaluations using real-world scenarios reconstructed with 4D Gaussian splatting, our method achieves the highest overall success rate, outperforming the deployed model, direct imitation learning and trajectory post-optimization. These results highlight a practical path toward efficient updates of deployed driving models using existing fleet logs.

llm.title_ja: 展開中の改善: 不完全な人間のテイクオーバーデータからのプロアクティブなエンド端運転の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 不完全な人間のテイクオーバーデータをプロアクティブな教師信号に変換し、既存のフリートログから効率的に運転モデルを更新するオフライン後訓練フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンドの自動運転モデルが展開後に直面する、人間の不完全なテイクオーバー（介入の遅れや不必要な介入）を直接模倣すると不適切な学習を引き起こす課題。
llm.method: モデルの計画を拡張し人間の修正を前方にシフトして多様な軌跡候補を作成し、スコアラーを用いて高スコアの候補を選択的に置き換えてモデルに蒸留する。
llm.result: 4Dガウススプラッティングで再構築した実世界シナリオを用いた閉ループ評価において、最高の全体的成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習
テイクオーバーデータ

2611.23719.tldr_en: This work proposes an offline post-training framework that transforms imperfect takeover data into proactive supervision of deployed driving models using existing fleet logs and achieves the highest overall success rate, outperforming the deployed model, direct imitation learning and trajectory post-optimization.

2611.23714.title: ExecGap: Exploiting Command-Execution Gap for Patch Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.23714.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have become a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation and show strong promise for real-world deployment, making adversarial robustness critical for reliable robot operation. Existing adversarial attacks on VLA-controlled robots mainly optimize prediction-level discrepancies or rollout-level deviations to disrupt manipulation. However, they rarely account for the fact that VLA-predicted commands are not executed directly, but must be realized through downstream control and robot embodiment. In this paper, we propose ExecGap, an adversarial patch attack framework that exploits this command-execution gap to expose embodiment-specific execution vulnerabilities. Specifically, ExecGap biases VLA-predicted task-space commands toward low-executability directions, which are estimated from kinematic inefficiency and dynamic weak actuation. This induces execution degradation, where the predicted command becomes difficult to realize effectively, thereby impairing task completion. Extensive simulation experiments across multiple VLA policies show that ExecGap induces larger command-execution mismatch and weaker realized execution than existing patch attacks. Real-robot experiments further validate that the deployed patch can induce execution degradation on physical platforms.

llm.title_ja: ExecGap: ビジョン言語アクションモデルに対するパッチ攻撃のためのコマンド実行ギャップの悪用
llm.tldr_ja: VLA予測のタスク空間コマンドを低実行可能性の方向にバイアスさせ、実行 degradation（劣化）を引き起こす敵対的パッチ攻撃フレームワークExecGapを提案する。
llm.problem: VLAモデルに対する既存の敵対的攻撃は予測レベルの不一致やロールアウトの偏りを主に最適化し、下流の制御やロボットの身体性を通じた実行ギャップを考慮していないこと。
llm.method: 運動学的非効率性と動的弱駆動から推定される低実行可能性の方向にタスク空間コマンドをバイアスさせる敵対的パッチ攻撃フレームワークExecGapを提案する。
llm.result: 複数のVLAポリシーを用いたシミュレーションおよび実機実験において、既存のパッチ攻撃よりも大きなコマンド実行の不一致と実行劣化を誘発できることを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2611.23714.tldr_en: ExecGap is proposed, an adversarial patch attack framework that exploits this command-execution gap to expose embodiment-specific execution vulnerabilities in VLA-predicted task-space commands and induces execution degradation, where the predicted command becomes difficult to realize effectively, thereby impairing task completion.

2611.23685.title: Measuring the Conservatism of Latent Safety Filters for World Models
2611.23685.abstract: A latent safety filter decides from the latent of a world model whether a planned action is safe. Conformal calibration sets the threshold of the filter so that it accepts an unsafe action only with a small probability. However, the filter can still be conservative and refuse many safe actions, depending on the latent. To measure the conservatism that a latent forces on the filter, we group similar latents and actions into cells. A filter that gives one decision per cell can refuse the unsafe transitions of a cell only by refusing the safe ones in it as well. We call the share of safe transitions that lie in such cells the overlap. We prove that the overlap is the minimum share of safe transitions that such a filter has to refuse in order to accept no unsafe transition in the data. Both the overlap and the conformal calibration can be applied to any latent. We use this to compare three existing designs, in which the safety labels train a classifier on top of the world model, the world model itself, or a separate encoder beside it. In a visual navigation task, the separate encoder has the lowest overlap, and at the same conformal level its filter refuses the fewest safe actions and lets the planner reach the most goals of the three.

llm.title_ja: 世界モデルのための潜在安全性フィルターの保守性の測定
llm.tldr_ja: 潜在安全性フィルターの保守性を測るため、類似した潜在表現と行動をセルにグループ化し、安全な遷移のうちフィルターが拒否せざるを得ない割合である「オーバーラップ」を証明・定義した。
llm.problem: 潜在安全性フィルターが保守的になりすぎて、潜在表現に応じて多くの安全な行動を拒否してしまう問題がある。
llm.method: 類似した潜在表現と行動をセルにグループ化し、安全な遷移のうち拒否が避けられない割合をオーバーラップとして定義・証明した。
llm.result: ビジュアルナビゲーションタスクにおいて、別個のエンコーダーを用いた設計が最もオーバーラップが低く、安全な行動の拒否が最も少なかった。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルナビゲーション

2611.23685.tldr_en: It is proved that the overlap is the minimum share of safe transitions that a latent safety filter has to refuse in order to accept no unsafe transition in the data.

2611.23676.title: Finetuning VLAs for Dexterous Manipulation: The Right Checkpoint Is All You Need
2611.23676.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models have demonstrated strong manipulation capabilities. A limitation of VLA models is that most manipulation datasets focus on parallel-jaw gripper systems, making transfer to multi-finger hands challenging, particularly as teleoperation datasets are harder to collect with multi-fingered robots. In this work, we study how to best adapt VLAs to dexterous hands by pairing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with diffusion-steering reinforcement learning (DSRL). Using $π_{0.5}$ and a LEAP hand, we evaluate five fine-tuning recipes across two simulation tasks using only a handful of demonstrations. Our empirical analysis yields three key insights: (1) SFT success is poorly correlated with post-DSRL success, meaning the best SFT checkpoint is rarely the most effective to steer; (2) freezing the vision-language model (VLM) and tuning only the action expert produces the most steerable policy for both training and out-of-distribution placements; and (3) low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is the least steerable approach. Consequently, we recommend an adaptation recipe that freezes the VLM, fully trains the action expert, and eschews SFT rollout success as a checkpoint selection metric.
2611.23676.comment: Accepted to the Workshop on Dexterous Manipulation at CoRL 2026

llm.title_ja: 器用なマニピュレーションのためのVLAファインチューニング：適切なチェックポイントの選択がすべて
llm.tldr_ja: VLAモデルを器用な手に適応させるため教師あり微調整と拡散ステアリング強化学習を組み合わせ、VLMを凍結して行動エキスパートのみを調整するのが最も操縦しやすい方針であることを示した。
llm.problem: ほとんどのマニピュレーションデータセットは平行爪グリッパーを対象としており、多指ハンドへの転移が困難である。
llm.method: 教師あり微調整と拡散ステアリング強化学習を組み合わせ、5つの微調整手法をシミュレーションタスクで評価した。
llm.result: VLMを凍結し行動エキスパートのみをトレーニングすることが最も操縦しやすいポリシーを生み出し、SFTの成功率はDSRL後の成功率と相関が低いことが分かった。
keywords_ja: 器用なマニピュレーション

2611.23676.tldr_en: This work studies how to best adapt VLAs to dexterous hands by pairing supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with diffusion-steering reinforcement learning (DSRL) and recommends an adaptation recipe that freezes the VLM, fully trains the action expert, and eschews SFT rollout success as a checkpoint selection metric.

2611.23670.title: EyeDiT: Anatomy-Grounded Multi-Modal Eye Generation and Simulation
2611.23670.abstract: Synthetic eye data are critical for rapid development of eye tracking (ET) in AR/VR applications. However, existing synthetic eye generators are largely image-centric and lack a high-quality underlying 3D anatomy of the eye, which limits their control mainly to the gaze and provides no anatomical labels. To address this problem, we propose EyeDiT, an anatomy-grounded, multi-modal 3D eye generation and simulation model trained with optical coherence tomography (OCT), labeled anatomy point clouds and near-eye images. Our pipeline first trains a Multi-Modal Anatomy Variational Autoencoder (VAE), which encodes an anatomy-aware latent representation from all input modalities. Then, our Eye Latent DiT is trained to generate latent samples conditioned on the optical axis, the pupil position and radius, and the subject identity. Together with Gaussian decoders for novel-view simulation, our model enables control over the pupil, subject identity and viewpoint for data synthesis. We show that our model outperforms previous eye image synthesis models in novel-view synthesis (24.9 against 21.8 dB PSNR from a single view), and that a public ET neural network trained on our synthetic data shows a smaller sim-to-real gap than when trained on data from other generators (3.5$^\circ$ vs. 8.4$^\circ$ gaze error), approaches a network trained on real data, and further improves ET performance when combined with real data (2.3$^\circ$ vs. 2.6$^\circ$). More information is available on the project page: https://lyhan12.github.io/eyedit

llm.title_ja: EyeDiT：解剖学的根拠に基づくマルチモーダル眼球生成とシミュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: AR/VRのアイトラッキング開発に向け、OCTや解剖学点群、近眼画像を用いて眼球の3D解剖学的構造を考慮したマルチモーダル眼球生成・シミュレーションモデルEyeDiTを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の合成眼球ジェネレーターは画像中心であり、高品質な3D解剖学構造を欠いているため制御が視線に限定され解剖学的ラベルがない。
llm.method: マルチモーダル解剖学VAEと眼球潜在DiTを訓練し、光学軸、瞳孔位置、被験者IDに基づき新規視点画像を生成するモデルを構築した。
llm.result: 新規視点合成において従来モデルを上回り、合成データで訓練したETニューラルネットワークは現実データとのシムリアルギャップが小さくなった。
keywords_ja: 変分オートエンコーダー

2611.23670.tldr_en: EyeDiT is proposed, an anatomy-grounded, multi-modal 3D eye generation and simulation model trained with optical coherence tomography (OCT), labeled anatomy point clouds and near-eye images, which outperforms previous eye image synthesis models in novel-view synthesis and improves ET performance when combined with real data.

2611.23661.title: LightSEAD: Lightweight SE(3)-Aware Keypoint Detector through Selective Knowledge Distillation
2611.23661.abstract: The pursuit of improved performance in deep learning has often been accompanied by increasing architectural complexity and computational demands. We explore an alternative direction: achieving more with less through structured supervision. We introduce LightSEAD, a lightweight SE(3)-aware keypoint detector initialised with calibrated Harris pseudo-labels and enriched through viewpoint-aware and appearance-aware supervision and selective knowledge distillation. LightSEAD comprises only six convolutional layers and 84,289 learnable parameters, achieving competitive repeatability across HPatches, KITTI 06 and 4Seasons while demonstrating its downstream applicability to relative pose estimation on MegaDepth-1500. Further optimised for mixed-precision inference, LightSEAD Coarse achieves approximately 909 FPS on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 and 139 FPS on a Jetson Orin Nano Super.

llm.title_ja: LightSEAD：選択的知識蒸留による軽量なSE(3)認識型特徴点検出器
llm.tldr_ja: キャリブレーションされたハリス疑似ラベルと選択的知識蒸留を用いて、わずか6つの畳み込み層で構成される軽量かつ高精度なSE(3)認識型特徴点検出器LightSEADを開発した。
llm.problem: ディープラーニングの性能追求は、アーキテクチャの複雑化と計算要求の増大を伴うことが多い。
llm.method: キャリブレーション済みハリス疑似ラベルによる初期化、視点・外観認識型監視、選択的知識蒸留を用いてモデルを構築した。
llm.result: HPatchesなどで競争力のある繰り返し精度を示し、NVIDIA RTX 4090で約909 FPS、Jetson Orin Nanoで139 FPSを達成した。

2611.23661.tldr_en: LightSEAD is introduced, a lightweight SE(3)-aware keypoint detector initialised with calibrated Harris pseudo-labels and enriched through viewpoint-aware and appearance-aware supervision and selective knowledge distillation, achieving competitive repeatability across HPatches, KITTI 06 and 4Seasons.

2611.23654.title: Radar-Native Control Barrier Functions: Doppler Range Rate as a Measured Barrier Derivative
2611.23654.abstract: Safe control around dynamic obstacles requires information about both distance and relative motion. Range-based filters commonly reconstruct the required range rate from successive range measurements or from obstacle-state estimators, which can introduce estimator delay or sensitivity to range noise when obstacle motion changes. A frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar measures radial relative velocity directly through Doppler. We use this measurement as the derivative of an ego-centered range control barrier function (CBF) and obtain a closed-form filter on the robot's forward velocity. A measurement margin constructed from sensor error bounds accounts for errors in range, Doppler, ego velocity, and bearing. In 508 paired encounters within the platform's retreat capability, direct Doppler produces two buffer incursions, compared with 15 for a constant-acceleration and 25 for a constant-velocity Kalman filter. On a Unitree Go1, the controller stops at $0.777 \pm 0.015$ m against the predicted $0.758$ m and reacts to a farther approaching object while a nearer static return remains. The guarantee covers the longitudinal range channel under bounded measurement errors and continuously available detections. Direct Doppler removes the need to reconstruct range rate in the safety loop, reducing the delay between a change in obstacle motion and its effect on the safety command.

llm.title_ja: レーダーネイティブ制御バリア関数：測定されたバリア微分としてのドップラーレンジレート
llm.tldr_ja: FMCWレーダーのドップラー速度を自己中心型レンジ制御バリア関数の微分として直接利用し、ロボットの前進速度に対する閉形式の安全フィルターを構築した。
llm.problem: 範囲ベースのフィルターは、障害物の運動変化に対して遅延やノイズ感度を引き起こすレンジレートの再構築を必要とする。
llm.method: FMCWレーダーのドップラーによるラジアル相対速度測定値を制御バリア関数の微分として使用し、閉形式のフィルターを導出した。
llm.result: ユニットリーGo1の実機実験において、従来のカルマンフィルターを用いた手法に比べてバッファ侵入回数を大幅に削減し、安全性を維持して停止した。

2611.23628.title: LoRN: Low-Rank Noise Steering for Generative Robot Policies
2611.23628.abstract: Noise steering improves pretrained generative robot policies by learning to select their initial noise without updating model weights. We find that actions in the evaluated world-action models are more sensitive to video noise than action noise, making video noise an expressive input for steering. However, the noise-steering methods we evaluate, in their published forms, struggle to scale to the high-dimensional noise inputs of large policy classes such as world-action models. We introduce Low-Rank Noise Steering (LoRN), a reinforcement learning method that scales noise steering to world-action models. A small steering actor selects a direction through a fixed low-rank random projection, while our norm-controlled construction keeps the resulting noise near the typical scale of a Gaussian sample. This separates the actor's control dimension from the full noise dimension, enabling steering of both video and action inputs. Across three world-action models and ten model-task pairs, video steering improves average success by 26.2 percentage points over the base policy, compared with 7.1 points for DSRL action steering. For smaller action policies, the same construction achieves comparable final success while generally improving early-training success. Steering actors trained in simulation also transfer to three physical bimanual manipulation tasks across two base policies, without additional real-world training.

llm.title_ja: LoRN：生成ロボットポリシーのための低ランクノイズステアリング
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模な世界行動モデルの高次元ノイズ入力に対応するため、固定された低ランクランダム投影を用いて効率的にノイズを制御する強化学習手法LoRNを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のノイズステアリング手法は、世界行動モデルのような大規模ポリシーの高次元ノイズ入力へのスケーリングに苦労する。
llm.method: 小さなステアリングアクターが固定された低ランクランダム投影を介して方向を選択し、ノルム制御された構築によりガウスサンプルの規模を維持する強化学習手法を開発した。
llm.result: 3つの世界行動モデルと10のタスクペアにおいて、動画ステアリングはベースポリシーと比較して平均成功率を大幅に向上させ、実機へのゼロショット移転も成功した。
keywords_ja: 両腕マニピュレーション

2611.23628.tldr_en: Low-Rank Noise Steering (LoRN), a reinforcement learning method that scales noise steering to world-action models and transfers to three physical bimanual manipulation tasks across two base policies, without additional real-world training is introduced.

2611.23620.title: How Uncertain Is My Action? Self-Correcting Visual Planning with Frozen World Models
2611.23620.abstract: A frozen latent world model combined with sampling-based model predictive control is a visual planner. At deployment, the executed action can depart from the commanded one, and the frozen model has no way to notice. We show that the model can be run in reverse: for any hypothesized actuation shift, it predicts what it should have observed under that shift, and comparing this prediction with what was actually observed quantifies the shift and lets the planner correct itself. Unlike the residual energy, which mixes the shift with the model's own error, the score keeps only the part of the residual that a shift can produce. This shift score detects the shift with a locally optimal test, estimates it with Cramer-Rao error bars, names the dominant generator, and compensates the planner once an alarm fires. On PushT, TwoRoom and OGBench-Cube with a frozen latent world model, measured detection follows the prediction to within 0.05 AUROC. Self-correction raises success from 0.650 to 0.862 on PushT and from 0.378 to 0.432 on the harder Cube task, levels with an oracle that is told the true shift at the same block, better than five common test-time adaptation methods. On a real robotic arm, the score identifies a base-joint offset that no joint encoder registers and reduces the reach error from 36 mm to 3-5 mm, and under shifts drawn at random and sealed before the session, estimates recover 92-94% of the error reduction achieved with the true shift. The broader implication is that a frozen world model can act as a filter by predicting the future, testing action-interface uncertainty and validity, and finally correcting failures.

llm.title_ja: 私の行動はどれほど不確かか：凍結された世界モデルによる自己修正型ビジュアルプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された潜在世界モデルを逆方向に実行し、予測と実際の観測の残差からアクチュエーションのズレを定量化して自己修正を行うビジュアルプランナーを提案した。
llm.problem: デプロイ時に実行された行動が指令された行動から乖離した場合、凍結された世界モデルにはそれを知る方法がない。
llm.method: 仮定されたアクチュエーションのズレのもとで観測されるべき内容を逆予測し、実際の観測と比較してズレを検出・補正するスコアを導出した。
llm.result: PushTやロボットアームの実機実験において、ベース関節のオフセットを特定して到達誤差を大幅に削減し、優れた適応性能を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジュアルプランニング

2611.23620.tldr_en: The model can be run in reverse: for any hypothesized actuation shift, it predicts what it should have observed under that shift, and comparing this prediction with what was actually observed quantifies the shift and lets the planner correct itself.

2611.23589.title: Recoverability, Not Invariance: Certified Safety for Robots at the Limits of Performance
2611.23589.abstract: Safety certification in robotics typically rests on forward invariance of the deployed controller, a property that demands high-fidelity models at the edge of the operating envelope, exactly where models are least reliable and robots perform best. As a result, many of the behaviors we most want robots to run, from learned policies to aggressive maneuvers at the limits of traction, cannot be certified at all. We introduce recoverability, a contraction-theoretic safety concept that resolves this tension by certifying a robot's ability to reengage a trusted recovery mode rather than the invariance of a deployed behavior. We prove that switching to the recovery mode from anywhere inside a certified tube guarantees exponential convergence, even under disturbances and model error. To decide when to switch, we derive the contraction insertion gradient, the first-order effect of a recovery insertion on the certificate, and embed it in a switching-time program in which feasibility alone guarantees safety and optimality only shapes performance. To supply the certificates, we develop sequential convex synthesis that monotonically grows the certified tube toward the exact viability kernel. We validate our approach in simulated quadrotor flight through uncertain obstacles, where it outperforms invariance-based safety filters, and in hardware deployments aboard a full-scale IndyNXT autonomous racecar, where it repeatedly recovers the car from an aggressive raceline at the limits of handling in the rain. Recoverability provides a certified exit strategy, extending formal safety guarantees to aggressive, learned, and experimental behaviors without requiring their invariance.

llm.title_ja: 不変性ではなく回復可能性：限界性能におけるロボットの証明された安全性
llm.tldr_ja: 展開されたコントローラーの前進不変性ではなく、信頼できる回復モードへ再係合する能力（回復可能性）を証明することで、極限状態でのロボットの安全性を保証する枠組みを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の安全性証明は前進不変性に基づくため、モデルが最も信頼できずロボットが高性能を発揮する限界領域では証明不能になる。
llm.method: 回復モードへの切り替え時に収束を保証する収縮理論に基づく安全性概念を導入し、順次凸合成により証明されたチューブを拡大した。
llm.result: シミュレーションでのクアッドローター飛行および実物のインディNXT自動運転レーシングカーにおいて、限界状況からの回復に成功した。

2611.23589.tldr_en: Recoverability provides a certified exit strategy, extending formal safety guarantees to aggressive, learned, and experimental behaviors without requiring their invariance.

2611.23585.title: SPICE: Stochastic Policy for Interaction in Cluttered Environments
2611.23585.abstract: Agricultural tasks such as harvesting and pruning require robots to reach through dense foliage, where contact is often unavoidable and vision is obstructed. Intermittent contact creates an imbalance between free-space and contact-rich observations, complicating the learning of contact-responsive behaviours. We present SPICE, a tactileconditioned diffusion policy for reaching targets in dense plant canopies using tactile sensing as the sole environmental feedback. SPICE exhibits three behaviours: moving through compliant foliage, manoeuvring around partially obstructing stems, and manipulating branches that block the target path. To the best of our knowledge, SPICE is the first tactile-conditioned diffusion policy for target reaching through physically cluttered plant canopies. Across over 180 real-robot trials, SPICE was evaluated against tactile-conditioned, image-conditioned, and reactive-control baselines. Spatial tactile information and explicit contact conditioning proved important, with SPICE achieving 95% branch-manoeuvring success versus 45% for the strongest tactile baseline. SPICE also achieved branch manipulation beyond the reactive controller and remained effective under visual occlusion, where the image-conditioned DP failed. Zero-shot transfer across 40 trials on unseen tomato and lime plants achieved 87.5% success rate. These results demonstrate the potential of tactile-conditioned generative policies for interaction in visually occluded plant environments.

llm.title_ja: SPICE：密集環境における相互作用のための確率的ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 触覚センシングを唯一の環境フィードバックとして利用し、視覚が遮蔽された高密度の植物群の中でもターゲットに到達できる触覚条件付き拡散ポリシーSPICEを提案した。
llm.problem: 農業タスクでは密集した葉をかき分ける必要があり、接触が避けられず視覚が妨げられ、接触応答行動の学習が困難になる。
llm.method: 空間的触覚情報と明示的な接触条件付けを組み込んだ触覚条件付き拡散ポリシーを構築し、180回以上の実機トライアルで評価した。
llm.result: 枝の操りにおいて強力な触覚ベースラインを大きく上回る成功率を達成し、視覚的遮蔽下や未知の植物へのゼロショット移転でも有効性を示した。

2611.23585.tldr_en: SPICE is the first tactile-conditioned diffusion policy for target reaching through physically cluttered plant canopies using tactile sensing as the sole environmental feedback and demonstrates the potential of tactile-conditioned generative policies for interaction in visually occluded plant environments.

2611.23578.title: DOCK: Dual-Stream-Inspired Self-Supervised Object-Centric Representations Grounded in Robot Kinematics
2611.23578.abstract: Latent-space planners select actions by comparing the embedding of a predicted future image with that of a goal image. This assumes that distance in the embedding reflects how far the scene is from the goal. We profile this assumption with simulator-executed futures, which removes prediction error. For six frozen DINO and V-JEPA encoders, feature distance barely tracks the object's distance to its goal: the rank correlation is at most 0.11, against 0.87 for object-mask centroids. It is dominated by background and robot patches, and frozen-feature readouts capture the arm far better than the object. Inspired by the ventral (what) and dorsal (where/how) visual streams, we propose DOCK, which learns an object representation whose changes agree with measured physical motion. A grasped object moves with the gripper, so forward kinematics on the joint angles gives a proxy for the object's displacement without annotation. From 9,951 held-object transport trajectories in 21 simulated kitchen scenes, we mine 404K displacement pairs and train three components: an object token pooled from patch features (what), a spatial ruler that makes differences of readout coordinates equal to measured displacements (where), and a dynamics predictor over object tokens (how). Used as a planning cost, the learned representation places the object in 15 of 21 tasks, as many as an oracle that reads the true object position, while mask geometry reaches 10 and frozen feature distance 9. It still solves the most tasks when the unseen robot arm is visible, and its ranking transfers to held-out layouts with unseen object instances and categories without any adaptation.

llm.title_ja: DOCK：ロボットの運動学に根ざした、二重経路に着想を得た自己教師あり物体中心表現
llm.tldr_ja: 腹側・背側視覚経路に着想を得て、把持された物体の移動と順運動学の一致を利用することで、物体の物理的変位を捉える自己教師あり物体中心表現DOCKを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の潜在空間プランナーの埋め込み表現の距離は、物体の目標までの距離を十分に追跡できず、背景やロボットに支配されている。
llm.method: キッチン環境での把持物体輸送軌跡から変位ペアをマイニングし、物体トークン（何）、空間ルーラー（どこ）、動力学予測器（どうやって）の3コンポーネントを訓練した。
llm.result: プランニングのコストとして使用した場合、オラクルと同等のタスク解決数を達成し、未知のレイアウトや物体カテゴリにも適応なしで転移可能であった。
keywords_ja: 潜在空間プランニング

2611.23578.tldr_en: Inspired by the ventral (what) and dorsal (where/how) visual streams, DOCK is proposed, which learns an object representation whose changes agree with measured physical motion.

2611.23575.title: LuxTac: A Flexible, Scalable, and Open-Source Optical Taxel Array with Distributed Three-Axis Force Sensing for Tactile Robot Learning
2611.23575.abstract: Low-cost tactile arrays have made touch a practical input for robot learning, but piezoresistive designs sense only pressure, while camera-based sensors that also resolve shear are too bulky to tile over a gripper. To solve this problem, we present LuxTac, a flexible, scalable optical taxel array, about 3.5 mm thick and built from off-the-shelf parts. Each taxel is a digital RGBC light-to-digital converter under a translucent white silicone layer capped by an opaque black film, so the back-scattered LED light falls monotonically with local indentation depth. The same board accepts two interchangeable gel cartridges: a plain one for normal sensing, and one with colored walls that encodes the local shear in the color of the returned light, with no camera, magnets, or bump overlay, making LuxTac, to our knowledge, the first optical taxel array to resolve shear at individual taxels. Characterized with an automated CNC indenter and a six-axis force/torque sensor, the normal cartridge responds linearly to force ($R^2$ = 0.999) from 104 mN to at least 5.8 N, with 2.0% repeatability, 5.9% hysteresis, and a taxel-to-taxel variation of 6-10% after normalization. With the shear cartridge, per-taxel models estimate the three-axis force at every taxel; across three indenter shapes and nine held-out sessions, the summed estimates reach $R^2$ = 0.96/0.96/0.92 in x/y/z, each taxel's estimate 0.92/0.93/0.94, and the median shear-direction error is 4.8 degrees. Adding LuxTac pressure readings to an Action Chunking Transformer policy substantially improves peg-in-hole success over a vision-only baseline. Design files, code, and videos are available at https://luxtac.github.io.
2611.23575.comment: 11 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Project page: https://luxtac.github.io

llm.title_ja: LuxTac：ロボット学習のための分散型3軸力センシングを備えた柔軟で拡張性のあるオープンソース光学式タクセルアレイ
llm.tldr_ja: 安価で柔軟かつ拡張性のある光学式タクセルアレイLuxTacを開発し、各タクセルで法線力と個別のせん断力を同時に解像できるようにした。
llm.problem: 従来の感圧アレイは圧力しか感知できず、せん断力を解決できるカメラベースのセンサーはかさばりすぎてグリッパーにタイル貼りできない。
llm.method: デジタルRGBC光コンバーターと半透明シリコン層を組み合わせ、通常センシング用とせん断エンコード用の2種類のゲルカートリッジを採用した。
llm.result: CNCインデンターによる評価で線形応答を示し、Action Chunking Transformerポリシーに組み込むことでペグインホールタスクの成功率が大幅に向上した。
keywords_ja: 光学式タクセルアレイ

2611.23575.tldr_en: Low-cost tactile arrays have made touch a practical input for robot learning, but piezoresistive designs sense only pressure, while camera-based sensors that also resolve shear are too bulky to tile over a gripper, so LuxTac, a flexible, scalable optical taxel array, is presented.

2611.23567.title: Panini- Feasible Grammar For Robot Designs
2611.23567.abstract: Symbolic methods make robot designs interpretable but often overlook continuous geometry; learned methods handle geometry but offer less transparent structure. We introduce a typed production grammar that uses case-role relations, parameter inheritance, and specificity-based rule arbitration to generate both manipulation skills and robot morphologies. A geometric realization map translates grammar composition into transformations in SE(3), behaving as a monoid homomorphism when inheritance is inactive and exhibiting a measurable defect when inheritance is enabled. The grammar provides a compact representation, and its arbitration decisions can be recovered from geometric containment (agreement 0.905 +/- 0.062 across 10 seeds, versus 0.611 +/- 0.090 for a Euclidean control). We also introduce PANINI, a cross-entropy search method over grammar-based morphology representations. Across 30 methods and 24 seeds, PANINI achieves the best mean rank but is not statistically distinguishable from strong generic optimizers. Its main demonstrated advantage is therefore structural rather than optimization performance: grammar-generated designs are legal by construction, and coordinated limb placement produces 95% jointly feasible edits, compared with 55% for range-constrained resampling and none for flat parameterization in 6,000 draws. These results show how typed grammars can make robot generation more interpretable and geometrically coordinated, without implying that every feasible design will locomote or that grammar-based search universally outperforms generic optimizers.

llm.title_ja: Panini：ロボット設計のための実現可能な文法
llm.tldr_ja: 格役割関係やパラメータ継承を用いた型付き生成文法を用いることで、解釈可能で幾何学的に協調したマニピュレーションスキルとロボット形態を同時に生成する手法PANINIを提案した。
llm.problem: 記号的手法は解釈可能だが連続的幾何学を無視し、学習手法は幾何学を扱うが構造の透明性が低い。
llm.method: 文法構成をSE(3)の変換に翻訳する幾何学的実現マップを定義し、文法ベースの形態表現に対するクロスエントロピー探索手法PANINIを開発した。
llm.result: 文法によって生成された設計は構築上適法であり、協調的な肢の配置により高い割合で関節的に実現可能な編集を達成した。
llm.limitation: すべての実現可能な設計が歩行できることや、文法ベースの検索が普遍的に汎用オプティマイザーを上回ることを意味するものではない

2611.23567.tldr_en: These results show how typed grammars can make robot generation more interpretable and geometrically coordinated, without implying that every feasible design will locomote or that grammar-based search universally outperforms generic optimizers.

2611.23563.title: Learning the Dynamics of Deformable Linear Objects Through Coupled Oscillators for Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
2611.23563.abstract: Many learning-based approaches for deformable linear objects (DLOs) rely on simplified deformation models that neglect dynamic effects and the mechanical response of the objects, limiting their applicability to lightweight, compliant objects and slow motions. Inspired by recent advances in learning physically structured dynamics with coupled oscillator networks (CONs), we propose $Φ$-CON for learning force-driven DLO dynamics. The model combines a floating-base coupled oscillator network (FBCON), whose latent potential energy depends only on the DLO's shape, with a learned affine diffeomorphism $Φ$ between observed positions along the DLO and latent coordinates. Its shape dynamics are stable by construction, and its Lagrangian structure yields explicit expressions for kinetic and potential energy. We exploit this structure to design a model-based proportional-derivative (PD) controller that compensates for the learned potential forces, thereby establishing closed-loop stability guarantees and ensuring convergence. We evaluate the approach on four simulated DLOs and a real bimanual robot setup. In simulation, $Φ$-CON achieves prediction accuracy comparable to neural ordinary differential equation (NODE) models and Lagrangian neural networks (LNNs), with $97.2\%$ and $90.2\%$ fewer parameters, respectively. Relative to a model-free PD baseline, the proposed controller reduces mean endpoint regulation error by $97.5$-$99.7\%$ in simulation and achieves a mean per-target reduction of $27.9\%$ across both endpoints in real-world experiments, demonstrating the importance of explicitly accounting for the mechanical response of stiff and heavy objects.

llm.title_ja: 結合オシレーターを通じた変形可能線状物の動力学学習と両腕ロボットマニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 自由浮動型結合オシレーターネットワークと学習されたアフィン同相写像を組み合わせた力駆動型DLO動力学学習モデルΦ-CONを提案し、両腕ロボットによる制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 変形可能線状物（DLO）の多くの学習手法は、動的効果や力学的応答を無視した単純化された変形モデルに依存している。
llm.method: 位置と潜在座標間のアフィン同相写像を持つ自由浮動型結合オシレーターネットワーク（FBCON）を構築し、モデルベースのPDコントローラーを設計した。
llm.result: シミュレーションでモデルパラメータ数を大幅に削減しつつ同等の予測精度を実現し、実機両腕ロボット実験でもエンドポイントの平均制御誤差を大幅に削減した。
keywords_ja: 両腕マニピュレーション

2611.23563.tldr_en: This work proposes a model-based proportional-derivative (PD) controller that compensates for the learned potential forces, thereby establishing closed-loop stability guarantees and ensuring convergence and evaluates the approach on four simulated DLOs and a real bimanual robot setup.

2611.23531.title: RESCUE Jumper: A Centimeter-Scale Rolling and Jumping Robot for Search and Rescue
2611.23531.abstract: Centimeter-scale robots are promising for urban search and rescue because they can enter confined spaces that are inaccessible or unsafe for humans. However, their small size limits obstacle traversal after deployment. This paper presents the RESCUE Jumper, a 125 g mobile robot with a 6.2 cm width and 6.2 cm diameter wheels that combines ground rolling with jumping to traverse steps and gaps that exceeds its rolling capability. The RESCUE Jumper uses its two actuators for both rolling mode and jumping by reversing the direction of wheel motion. Forward wheel motion enables rolling, while reverse wheel motion winds a spring steel tail to store elastic potential energy and release it for jumping. The RESCUE Jumper varies tail winding speed to control jump direction, transitioning from backward to forward jumps as winding speed increases from 0.75 rad/s to 8.73 rad/s. The launch angle of the jumps ranges from 45 degree to -11 degree with respect to the vertical axis, reaching a maximum height of 9.2 cm and a maximum lateral displacement of 11.2 cm. We model the winding speed-dependent jumping behavior in three phases: tail release to determine the contact point and robot orientation, tail straightening until liftoff, and ballistic flight to predict jump height and lateral displacement. Finally, qualitative tests highlight the robot's locomotion in cluttered, real-world environments. The model and experiments presented in this work can inform future designs of space-constrained jump mechanisms in centimeter-scale robots for search and rescue and inspection in unstructured environments.

llm.title_ja: RESCUE Jumper：捜索救助のためのセンチメートルスケール走行・跳躍ロボット
llm.tldr_ja: 車輪の回転方向を反転させることで地上走行とバネ弾性エネルギーを利用した跳躍を切り替え、閉ざされた狭い空間や段差を乗り越えるセンチメートルスケールのロボットを開発した。
llm.problem: センチメートルスケールのロボットは狭い空間に入れる一方で、展開後の障害物乗り越え能力がその小型ゆえに制限される。
llm.method: 車輪の正転で走行を行い、逆転でゼンマイばねのテールを巻き上げて弾性位置エネルギーを蓄積し跳躍する機構と、3フェーズの跳躍挙動モデルを構築した。
llm.result: 最大高さ9.2 cm、最大横方向変位11.2 cmの跳躍を達成し、実際の散らばった環境での移動性能を定性的に示した。
keywords_ja: センチメートルスケール

2611.23517.title: RageVLA: Augmentation-Trained Perception and Action for State-of-the-Art Robustness on LIBERO
2611.23517.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models look saturated on LIBERO, yet most of them fall apart on LIBERO-PRO as soon as an object moves or the instruction asks for something new. We argue that what is missing is not scale but decoupling. In these policies, what to do is tied to where things were during training, to the scene around them and to the wording of the instruction. We cut these ties in two places. In the data, LIBERO demonstrations are re-arranged by general rules: every object and fixture is moved and rotated, tasks are carried into other environments and onto other surfaces, and every instruction is paraphrased. In the policy, a perception engine on frozen DINOv3 features, trained on this augmented data, hands the action model the scene in decoupled form: a list of objects with their positions, and a compact code of what the gripper is looking at, next to image and instruction embeddings from TinyCLIP. A flow-matching diffusion transformer, trained from scratch, acts on this view. We call this combination of Robust Augmentation and Grounded Encoding RageVLA. With 0.21 billion parameters, RageVLA sets a new state of the art on LIBERO-PRO among VLA policies, scoring 0.72 against 0.53 for the best published model, and a larger variant reaches 0.73. Two further tests on LIBERO-Object show that the policy acts on what it perceives. When the object positions it is given are shuffled while the camera images stay correct, its success falls from 0.965 to 0.215. When the target object is displaced by 28 cm, it still succeeds in 0.865 of the episodes, where $π_{0.5}$, run through the same harness, succeeds in 0.105.

llm.title_ja: RageVLA：LIBEROにおける最先端の頑健性を実現した拡張訓練済み知覚・行動モデル
llm.tldr_ja: データとポリシーの結合を切り離すデータ拡張と、凍結されたDINOv3特徴量に基づく知覚エンジンを用いたフローマッチング拡散TransformerポリシーRageVLAを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のVLAモデルはLIBEROで飽和しているように見えるが、LIBERO-PROで物体が動いたり指示が変わるとすぐに破綻する。
llm.method: オブジェクトや環境を規則的に再配置・回転させ、指示をパラフレーズした拡張データで凍結DINOv3特徴量上の知覚エンジンを訓練し、フローマッチング拡散Transformerを組み合わせた。
llm.result: LIBERO-PROにおいて従来のVLAポリシーを大きく上回る最高性能を達成し、物体の位置が変化しても頑健に行動できることを示した。

2611.23517.tldr_en: With 0.21 billion parameters, RageVLA sets a new state of the art on LIBERO-PRO among VLA policies, scoring 0.72 against 0.53 for the best published model, and a larger variant reaches 0.73.

2611.23502.title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems
2611.23502.abstract: We introduce TAG (Testbed for Autonomous Games), a compact, low-cost robotic platform for studying learning and control in physically coupled dynamical systems. TAG combines an actively tilted and steered ball-in-maze board with a top-mounted rotary inverted pendulum. The pendulum's reaction torque and vibration disturb the board and marble, while the board's tilt, driven by the maze-solving policy, simultaneously disturbs the pendulum's balance. The main challenge in learning control policies for each subsystem is accounting for the impact of one subsystem's dynamics on the other's learning process. To address this challenge, we present complementary reinforcement learning paradigms, leveraging model-based and model-free approaches to learn the control policies for the maze and pendulum, respectively. Our key finding is that introducing the pendulum causes an immediate, sharp drop in the maze policy's success rate, but the policy adapts online and recovers to its pre-coupling performance within a small number of learning episodes. Experimental results show that both policies, trained independently, successfully control the maze board and the pendulum despite their physical coupling.

llm.title_ja: 物理的に結合された動力学系における学習と制御
llm.tldr_ja: 迷路ボードとロータリー逆立ち振子を物理的に結合させた低コストロボットプラットフォームTAGを開発し、モデルベースとモデルフリーの強化学習を用いてそれぞれの制御ポリシーを学習した。
llm.problem: 一方のサブシステムの動力が他方の学習プロセスに与える影響を考慮して制御ポリシーを学習することが課題となる。
llm.method: 迷路と振子に対してそれぞれモデルベースおよびモデルフリーの強化学習パラダイムを適用し、オンライン適応による性能回復を検証した。
llm.result: 物理的結合によって一時的な成功率の急落が見られたものの、ポリシーがオンラインで適応し、短期間のエピソードで結合前の性能まで回復することを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットプラットフォーム

2611.23502.tldr_en: A key finding is that introducing the pendulum causes an immediate, sharp drop in the maze policy's success rate, but the policy adapts online and recovers to its pre-coupling performance within a small number of learning episodes.

2611.23499.title: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
2611.23499.abstract: Autoregressive vision-language-action (VLA) models predict discrete action tokens with the next-token objective of their vision-language backbone, so the action tokenizer defines the interface between the policy and the robot. In bimanual manipulation, the two arms share a repertoire of movements yet coordinate through complementary roles, and an action representation should capture both. However, most existing tokenizers encode both arms as a single concatenated action vector, in which motion patterns common to the two arms are not shared and cross-arm dependencies remain entangled within each token. The policy must therefore learn both aspects implicitly. We propose Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization (BiCAT), which shares one motion representation across arms while conditioning each arm's tokens on its partner through symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder. The policy then predicts all tokens of each arm in parallel, generating the left arm first and the right arm conditioned on it. Across ten RoboTwin 2.0 tasks and six real-world tasks on three embodiments, BiCAT achieves the highest success among the compared tokenizers. In simulation, it improves mean success by 17.6 percentage points over the strongest of eight baselines, with the largest gains on tasks that require close coordination between the arms, while requiring only 40.5 ms per action chunk. These results suggest that the action tokenizer is a natural place to model bimanual coordination.

llm.title_ja: BiCAT：両腕協調行動トークン化
llm.tldr_ja: 両腕間で1つの運動表現を共有しつつ、対称的なクロスアーム注意機構と共同デコーダーによりパートナー条件付けを行う両腕協調行動トークン化手法BiCATを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の多くのトークン化手法は両腕を単一の連結ベクトルとしてエンコードするため、両腕共通の運動パターンが共有されずクロスアーム依存関係が絡み合う。
llm.method: 対称的なクロスアーム注意機構を用いて一方のアームのトークンをもう一方に条件付けし、左腕を先に生成してから右腕を生成する並列予測構造を導入した。
llm.result: 10のRoboTwinタスクと3つの身体形状における6つの実世界タスクにおいて最高の成功率を達成し、特に密接な協調を要するタスクで大きな改善を示した。
keywords_ja: 両腕マニピュレーション
ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.23499.tldr_en: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization (BiCAT), which shares one motion representation across arms while conditioning each arm's tokens on its partner through symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder, and suggests that the action tokenizer is a natural place to model bimanual coordination.
2611.23499.hf_summary_en: BiCAT shares a motion representation across arms and conditions each arm's tokens on its partner via symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder, enabling parallel arm token prediction and improving bimanual manipulation success.

2611.23491.title: GRID-UAV: Geometry and Ray-depth Integrated Decision-making for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
2611.23491.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) encode images with 2D encoders that capture little 3D structure. A common approach is to feed the policy estimated depth, but a UAV chooses its own altitude, must judge distances tens of meters away, where monocular depth is less reliable, and must relate its forward and downward views. On long aerial routes, adding depth features directly brings no significant gain (42.5% vs. 42.6% success), so we study how 3D information should be given to the policy. Analyzing flight failures, we find that two forms of 3D grounding fail in opposite ways: explicit 3D lifting of depth collides less on the way but more often fails to finish at the target, while implicit alignment with a 3D geometry model finishes more often but collides more. We propose GRID, which combines both: (1) it lifts monocular depth into ray-corrected 3D positions in the UAV's frame for both cameras, and (2) during training only, it aligns its visual features with a frozen multi-view geometry model, at no inference cost. GRID adding explicit lifting to implicit alignment significantly increases how often the policy reaches the target ($61.5\% \rightarrow 69.5\%$, $p<0.001$), and adding implicit alignment to explicit lifting significantly increases how often it completes the task once there ($57.7\% \rightarrow 61.4\%$, $p<0.05$). On TravelUAV (3,005 test episodes), GRID achieves the best success rate on every split, with relative gains over the state of the art of 9.5% (seen), 17.1% (unseen objects) and 25.4% (unseen map).

llm.title_ja: GRID-UAV：無人航空機のための幾何学およびレイ深度統合型意思決定
llm.tldr_ja: 単眼深度をレイ補正された3D位置に持ち上げ、訓練時のみ凍結された多視点幾何学モデルに視覚特徴を整合させることで、UAVの目標到達性とタスク完了率を向上させるGRIDを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAは2Dエンコーダーを使用するため3D構造を捉えにくく、UAVの長期空中ルートにおいて単眼深度の信頼性が低下する。
llm.method: 単眼深度をUAVフレームのレイ補正3D位置に変換する明示的リフティングと、訓練時に多視点幾何学モデルと整合させる暗黙的アライメントを組み合わせた。
llm.result: TravelUAVのテストにおいて、既存の最先端手法と比較して既知、未知オブジェクト、未知マップのすべてのスプリットで優れた成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.23491.tldr_en: GRID is proposed, which combines GRID, which lifts monocular depth into ray-corrected 3D positions in the UAV's frame for both cameras, and during training only, it aligns its visual features with a frozen multi-view geometry model, at no inference cost.

2611.23441.title: Hebbian self-organization of monosynaptic reflexes in a biologically realistic multiarticular limb
2611.23441.abstract: Spinal monosynaptic reflexes depend on patterns of connectivity between muscle spindle afferents and motoneurons that should reflect musculoskeletal dynamics. One possibility is that the details of these circuits are specified genetically, but this requires an unlikely coevolution of musculoskeletal and neural elements. Here we show how biomechanical structure can determine the connectivity of self-organized spinal circuits. Using a neuromechanical model combining a multi-joint limb, proprioceptive feedback, and Hebbian plasticity driven by motor babbling, we find that biologically realistic connectivity emerges spontaneously when babbling is neither too sparse nor too frequent. This results in strong homonymous projections, weaker heteronymous projections among functional synergists, and very weak connections among antagonists. This outcome also depends on musculoskeletal morphometry. Heteronymous synergies form when proximal muscles are strongest---the characteristic gradient of mammalian limbs--whereas excessively strong biarticular muscles lead to unphysiological antagonist coupling. The mechanisms differ: homonymous connections arise from direct sensorimotor correlation during fusimotor coactivation by beta motoneurons, while heteronymous connections depend on multi-joint dynamics that emerge only after homonymous reflexes stabilize and increasing muscle strength generates multisegmental motion. Overall, this study provides a mechanistic basis for fetal sensorimotor development and generates testable predictions about the consequences of naturally occurring and experimentally induced variations.

llm.title_ja: 生物学的に現実的な多関節肢における単シナプス反射のヘッブ型自己組織化
llm.tldr_ja: 多関節肢、固有受容感覚フィードバック、運動バブリングによるヘッブ可塑性を組み合わせた神経力学モデルを用い、生物学的に現実的な脊髄反射回路の結合が自発的に生じることを示した。
llm.problem: 脊髄単シナプス反射の接続パターンがどのように筋骨格系ダイナミクスを反映して形成されるかという疑問がある。
llm.method: 多関節肢とプロプリオセプション、ヘッブ則に基づく神経力学モデルを構築し、運動バブリングの頻度や筋形態計測の影響を検証した。
llm.result: 適切なバブリング条件下で同名突起や相乗筋間の異名突起などの現実的な接続が自発的に現れ、発生学的発達の機構的基礎を提供した。

2611.23441.tldr_en: This study provides a mechanistic basis for fetal sensorimotor development and generates testable predictions about the consequences of naturally occurring and experimentally induced variations.

2611.23228.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
2611.23228.abstract: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively. We present Spool, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's state without replaying frames through the backbone. Removal is exact within each layer; as with key-value eviction in attention, expired frames can retain residual influence through the cached inputs computed by earlier layers. We design a dedicated data structure and GPU kernels to achieve low caching and composition overhead. Across five open-source hybrid VLMs and four video reasoning benchmarks, Spool achieves the lowest p95 time-to-first-token in all 20 model-benchmark tests, reducing it by a geometric mean of $6.6\times$ over the faster of two recent vLLM baselines, while improving accuracy by 2.3 percentage points on average.

llm.title_ja: Spool: ハイブリッド視覚言語モデルのための低遅延ストリーミング推論
llm.tldr_ja: Spoolは、ハイブリッド視覚言語モデルにおいて過去フレームの状態変換をキャッシュし効率的に合成することで、バックボーンの再処理なしに期限切れフレームを正確に削除し、時間対初トークン遅延を大幅に削減するトレーニング不要のフレームワークである。
llm.problem: ハイブリッドVLMにおいてスライディングウィンドウを維持すると、過去の全フレームを共有状態に圧縮するため、古いフレームを失効させる際にモデル全体を再実行する必要がありコストが高い。
llm.method: リカレント更新が入力依存係数を持つ状態に対してアフィンであることに着目し、フレームごとの状態変換をキャッシュしてウィンドウの進行に合わせて効率的に合成するトレーニング不要のフレームワークSpoolを提案する。
llm.result: 5つのオープンソースハイブリッドVLMと4つの動画推論ベンチマークにおいて、すべての20モデル・ベンチマークテストで最も低いp95初トークン時間を達成し、最近のvLLMベースラインより幾何平均で6.6倍削減しつつ精度を平均2.3ポイント改善した。

2611.23228.tldr_en: Spool is presented, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's state without replaying frames through the backbone.

2611.23364.title: Neural Circuit Architectural Priors for Rat Locomotion
2611.23364.abstract: Animals generate behavior through continuous interactions between their neural circuits, bodies, and environment. Embodied simulations study these interactions by testing neural circuit models in biologically realistic settings. Recent efforts have simulated diverse animals, and emerging work on biologically grounded neural architectures has begun to integrate circuit connectivity and single-unit dynamics from experimental data into artificial neural networks, introducing stronger inductive biases and closer mechanistic alignment with biology. How can we develop embodied simulations that enable the study of increasingly complex bodies and neural circuits? In this work, we address the challenge through coordinated advances in the simulated body, neural architecture, and training infrastructure. We introduce Rat v2, an efficient and flexible biomechanical body for simulating rat behavior. To control this body, we develop Rat NCAP, a biologically grounded neural architecture for locomotion based on mammalian spinal circuits that incorporates cell-type-specific connectivity and a novel flexor-extensor neuromechanical interface. To optimize circuit parameters, we develop GPU-accelerated simulation and training infrastructure. The model learns to locomote at different speeds and transition between gaits without imitation learning, producing locomotion statistics, kinematics, and cell-type-specific neural activity consistent with experimental data. Analyses reveal that the neuromechanical interface substantially affects trainability and gait quality, and in silico cell-type ablations reproduce known gait phenotypes and predict gait changes under graded perturbations. Together, these findings support the view that embodied simulations at an intermediate level of abstraction can simultaneously reproduce complex behavior and yield mechanistic insights into the neural circuits that generate it.
2611.23364.comment: NeurIPS 2026. 10 pages main text, 41 pages total, 7 figures in main text. Code and videos: https://rat-ncap.github.io/

llm.title_ja: ラットの移動のための神経回路アーキテクチャ上の事前知識
llm.tldr_ja: 哺乳類の脊髄回路に基づく生物学的ニューラル回路アーキテクチャ（Rat NCAP）と効率的な生体力学ボディ（Rat v2）を組み合わせ、模倣学習なしで多様な速度での移動や歩容移行を実現した。
llm.problem: 複雑化する身体や神経回路を研究するための、より強い帰納バイアスを持つ統合的な体と神経回路のシミュレーション開発が求められている。
llm.method: 効率的な生体力学ボディRat v2と、細胞特異的接続性や屈筋・伸筋の神経筋インターフェースを持つ神経回路アーキテクチャRat NCAPを開発・訓練した。
llm.result: 模倣学習なしで移動や歩容移行を学習し、得られた移動統計や神経活動が実験データと一致することを確認した。
keywords_ja: 歩行シミュレーション

2611.23364.tldr_en: Rat v2 is introduced, an efficient and flexible biomechanical body for simulating rat behavior that incorporates cell-type-specific connectivity and a novel flexor-extensor neuromechanical interface that supports the view that embodied simulations at an intermediate level of abstraction can simultaneously reproduce complex behavior and yield mechanistic insights into the neural circuits that generate it.

2611.23215.title: Feedback-Linearised Trajectory Tracking via Model-Informed Robust Geometric DDPC
2611.23215.abstract: Data-driven predictive control (DDPC) predicts system responses from recorded trajectories, but nonlinear dynamics can limit the accuracy of fixed linear predictors. This paper studies geometric robust DDPC for trajectory tracking of a fully actuated manipulator using model-based feedback linearisation. A mechanical model maps virtual acceleration commands into joint torques, while recorded data capture residual dynamics arising from imperfect model parameters. The controller minimises worst-case prediction error over an open Grassmannian ball centred at the fitted trajectory subspace. Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed method with double-integrator model predictive control (MPC) and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control (DeePC). Results show improved tracking over double-integrator MPC despite increased torque effort, while performance relative to DeePC depends on the reference trajectory.
2611.23215.comment: This manuscript has been submitted to the 9th Annual Learning for Dynamics & Control Conference, taking place in Stockholm, Sweden, in June 2027

llm.title_ja: モデル情報に基づくロバスト幾何学的DDPCによるフィードバック線形化軌道追従
llm.tldr_ja: モデルベースのフィードバック線形化とデータ駆動型予測制御を組み合わせた幾何学的ロバストDDPCにより、不完全なモデルパラメータに起因する残差ダイナミクスを捉えつつ完全駆動マニピュレータの軌道追従精度を向上させる。
llm.problem: データ駆動型予測制御は記録された軌道からシステム応答を予測するが、非線形ダイナミクスが固定線形予測器の精度を制限する。
llm.method: モデルベースのフィードバック線形化を用いて仮想加速度指令を関節トルクに変換し、記録されたデータで不完全なモデルパラメータによる残差ダイナミクスを捉えつつ、適合された軌道部分空間を中心とするグラスマン球上で最悪ケースの予測誤差を最小化する幾何学的なロバストDDPCを提案する。
llm.result: 重力下での平面2Rマニピュレータのシミュレーションにおいて、提案手法は二重積分器モデル予測制御と比較してトルク努力の増加にもかかわらず追従性能が向上し、DeePCに対する性能は参照軌道に依存することが示された。
keywords_ja: データ駆動型予測制御
フィードバック線形化

2611.23215.tldr_en: Simulations on a planar 2R manipulator under gravity compare the proposed DDPC method with double-integrator model predictive control and direct regularised data-enabled predictive control, showing improved tracking over double-integrator MPC despite increased torque effort, while performance relative to DeePC depends on the reference trajectory.

2611.23211.title: Multimodal Masked Diffusion Autoencoder for Modeling Impaired Driving
2611.23211.abstract: Human cognitive state (e.g., distraction, stress), gaze, and behavior interact with the driving environment in subtle ways that AI could use to assist drivers, but ground-truth labels for human cognitive state levels are costly to obtain at scale. We propose a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder, ID-MAE, that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory. To probe the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference, we introduce DIVERT, a driving-simulator dataset containing 103 hours of driving data (n = 109) with ten impairment inductions spanning cognitive, visual, and emotional states, recorded with gaze, vehicle state, and scene video. We demonstrate how ID-MAE affords significant improvements in impairment inference results on both the DIVERT dataset and existing datasets, and enables strong results in additional tasks, such as trajectory and gaze prediction. For location-matched pairs, our model achieves a paired AUC of 0.706 for impairment detection on DIVERT, compared to 0.590 without reconstruction loss, improving over existing baselines. We probe the design space in terms of input modalities, masking scheme, positional encoding, attention mechanism, and decoding. We also investigate the interaction between various impairments in training and inference, demonstrating that visually demanding distractions are separable from cognitive distractions. Code and data will be available upon acceptance.
2611.23211.comment: Equal contribution: John Gideon and Anshul Gupta. 8 pages, 6 figures

llm.title_ja: 運転の不全状態をモデリングするためのマルチモーダルマスク拡散オートエンコーダ
llm.tldr_ja: 自己教師あり学習の目的関数として障害予測に加えてマスクされた視線や軌道を再構築するマルチモーダルマスク拡散オートエンコーダID-MAEを提案し、多様な運転障害の推論性能を大幅に向上させる。
llm.problem: AIがドライバを支援するために人間の認知的状態や行動と運転環境の相互作用を利用できる可能性があるが、人間の認知的状態レベルのグランドトルク正解ラベルを大規模に取得するのはコストがかかる。
llm.method: 障害予測をマスクされたトークンとして予測するだけでなく、マスクされた視線や軌道を再構築する自己教師ありの自己符号化目的関数を追加したマルチモーダルマスク拡散オートエンコーダID-MAEを提案し、103時間の多様な障害誘導を含む運転シミュレータデータセットDIVERTを構築する。
llm.result: DIVERTデータセットを用いた位置一致ペアの障害検出において、再構築損失なしの場合のAUC 0.590に対してペアのAUC 0.706を達成し、既存のベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2611.23211.tldr_en: This work proposes a multimodal masked-diffusion autoencoder that adds a self-supervised objective to impairment prediction: alongside predicting the impairment label as a masked token, it reconstructs masked gaze and trajectory, and investigates the effects of different modalities and types of impairments on model inference.

2611.23198.title: Learned versus Kinematic Trajectory Prediction under Reduced Observation Frequency
2611.23198.abstract: Trajectory prediction models for automated driving are usually trained on data with a fixed sampling frequency, while positions received via vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication arrive at 1-10 Hz. We study whether a learned predictor that uses only the observation history keeps its advantage over constant velocity (CV) and constant acceleration (CA) models when the history frequency drops. On the Argoverse 2 motion forecasting dataset, the 5 s history of the focal agent was downsampled from 10 Hz to 5, 2, and 1 Hz, and the 6 s future was predicted without maps or neighboring agents. An LSTM-based recurrent neural network (RNN) trained for each frequency was compared with the same network trained at 10 Hz and applied to sparse histories after linear interpolation. Hypotheses and thresholds were fixed before training, the main RNNs were trained with ten seeds each, and results on 24,984 test scenarios have bootstrap confidence intervals over scenarios and seeds. The average displacement error of the frequency-specific RNN grew by 3.1% at 5 Hz, 10.1% at 2 Hz, and 20.3% at 1 Hz. Contrary to our hypothesis, its advantage over the better kinematic model did not vanish on straight motion and was 24-30% on both straight motion and turns at every frequency, while for pedestrians CV was more accurate. The 10 Hz model with interpolation was at most 1.3% less accurate than the frequency-specific model down to 2 Hz but 11.5% less accurate at 1 Hz. Each hypothesis was only partly supported.
2611.23198.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Code and per-scenario results: https://github.com/nleaxy/learned-vs-kinematic-trajectory-prediction

llm.title_ja: 観測周波数を下げた場合の学習済み軌道予測と運動学に基づく軌道予測の比較
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転向け軌道予測モデルにおいて、観測履歴の周波数を10 Hzから1 Hzまで下げた際、学習済みLSTMベースのRNNは運動学モデル（CV/CA）に対する優位性を維持し続け、直線運動や旋回において24-30%の優位性を示すことを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 自動運転用の軌道予測モデルは通常固定サンプリング周波数で訓練されるが、V2X通信で受信される位置情報は1-10 Hzで変動するため、周波数が低下した際に学習済み予測器が定速・定加速度モデルに対する優位性を保持できるかは不明である。
llm.method: Argoverse 2モーション予測データセットを用い、焦点エージェントの5秒間の履歴を10 Hzから5、2、1 Hzにダウンサンプルし、マップや周辺エージェントなしで6秒間の未来を予測するLSTMベースのリカレントニューラルネットワークを各周波数で訓練して比較する。
llm.result: 周波数特化型RNNの平均変位誤差は、5 Hzで3.1%、2 Hzで10.1%、1 Hzで20.3%増加し、予測に反して直線運動や旋回において運動学モデルに対する24-30%の優位性は消失しなかった。
keywords_ja: リカレントニューラルネットワーク

2611.23198.tldr_en: This work studies whether a learned predictor that uses only the observation history keeps its advantage over constant velocity (CV) and constant acceleration (CA) models when the history frequency drops, and results show that for pedestrians CV was more accurate than CA.

2611.23192.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
2611.23192.abstract: Goal recognition is the task of inferring an agent's intended goal from its observed behavior. Most existing work focuses on high-level symbolic recognition, abstracting away the continuous motion through which agents reach their goal. Methods that do reason over continuous trajectories rely on an explicit dynamics model that is hard to acquire and rarely transfers across settings. Neither approach explicitly learns how agents move toward each candidate goal, limiting accuracy on ambiguous trajectory prefixes where such knowledge is most needed. We present WoRD (Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion), which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations. At each step, WoRD runs one warm-started denoising chain per candidate goal, steers each chain toward the observed trajectory through a closed-form log-likelihood gradient, and reweights the resulting samples by Bayes' rule into a calibrated posterior over goals. We evaluate WoRD on simulated robot settings, pedestrian trajectories, and vehicle trajectories using four metrics targeting distinct failure modes. Across all three settings, the same inference procedure preserves calibrated multimodal beliefs through ambiguous prefixes where filter- and classifier-based observers collapse to a single mode or grow overconfident.
2611.23192.comment: Accepted at the 40th Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

llm.title_ja: WoRD: オンライン目標認識のための拡散ベース事後分布推論
llm.tldr_ja: WoRDは、学習済み軌道事前分布を利用し、ウォームスタートした拡散デノイジングチェーンと閉形式の対数尤度勾配によって部分観測からエージェントの意図する目標を推論する手法であり、曖昧な軌道プレフィックスにおいても較正されたマルチモーダルな信念を維持する。
llm.problem: 既存の目標認識手法は高次元の連続運動を抽象化した高レベルな記号的認識に依存するか、設定間で転移しにくい明示的なダイナミクスモデルを必要としており、曖昧な軌道プレフィックスにおける正確性が低い。
llm.method: 学習済み軌道事前分布を用いて部分観測からエージェントの目標を推論するWoRDを提案し、各ステップで候補目標ごとにウォームスタートしたデノイジングチェーンを実行し、閉形式の対数尤度勾配で誘導してベイズの定理により再重み付けする。
llm.result: シミュレーションロボット環境、歩行者、車両の軌道の3つの設定において、フィルタや分類器ベースのオブザーバーが単一モードに収束したり過信したりする曖昧なプレフィックスでも、較正されたマルチモーダルな信念を維持できることを示した。

2611.23192.tldr_en: Waypoint Recognition with Diffusion is presented, which uses a learned trajectory prior to infer the agent's goal from partial observations and preserves calibrated multimodal beliefs through ambiguous prefixes where filter- and classifier-based observers collapse to a single mode or grow overconfident.

2611.23174.title: Inference after coding agents
2611.23174.abstract: Empirical research is changing rapidly as AI coding agents are becoming increasingly proficient in every step of it, from writing code to manipulating data. We argue that while the potential of coding agents for science is vast, their use in hypothesis testing poses a substantial threat to classical inference, as these agents enable a supercharged form of selective inference. In particular, we argue that coding agents carrying out empirical research introduce a new type of post-selection inference that combines human-like, open-ended search over an implicit space of estimators with programmatic replayability of both the selection and the estimation process. Indeed, we find that on simulated data with zero effects, four frontier agents report significant p-values between 54% and 98% of the time when asked to produce a compelling finding. We propose a simple procedure for detecting and correcting these distortions. After an agent has completed its analysis, we reset and replay it on subsamples of the data to estimate the agent's relative probability of selecting that analysis when it looks statistically favorable. For agents with stable selection behavior, the resulting corrected test is asymptotically valid and consistent conditional on selection. Importantly, the correction is learned from the black-box agent's actual choices rather than a model of how it searches, so it remains valid even as AI technology continues to evolve rapidly. In simulations, the correction robustly lowers the high false rejection rates to near the nominal 5%. We illustrate the method on applications from two published papers.

llm.title_ja: コーディングエージェント実行後の統計的推論
llm.tldr_ja: AIコーディングエージェントが科学的探求やデータ操作を行う際に、暗黙的な推定器空間のオープンエンドな探索と選択・推定プロセスのプログラム的再現性を組み合わせることで選択的推論の歪みをもたらすことを示し、検出・修正のためのシンプルな手順を提案する。
llm.problem: AIコーディングエージェントがコード記述からデータ操作まで科学的研究のあらゆるステップで熟練度を増すにつれ、仮説検定において超充電された形式の選択的推論を引き起こし、古典的推論に対する大きな脅威となる。
llm.method: エージェントの分析完了後にデータをサブサンプル上でリセットおよび再実行し、統計的に有利に見える場合にその分析を選択する相対確率を推定するシンプルでデータ駆動型の修正手順を提案する。
llm.result: 効果がゼロのシミュレーションデータにおいて、4つの最先端エージェントが説得力のある発見を生み出すよう求められた際に54%から98%の確率で有意なp値を報告し、提案手法が過剰な偽棄却率を公称5%近くまで堅牢に引き下げることをシミュレーションで示した。
keywords_ja: コーディングエージェント

2611.23174.tldr_en: It is argued that coding agents carrying out empirical research introduce a new type of post-selection inference that combines human-like, open-ended search over an implicit space of estimators with programmatic replayability of both the selection and the estimation process.
