2611.23149.title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling
2611.23149.abstract: The agents in a heterogeneous team can cooperate to accomplish tasks that exceed their individual capabilities. The team trajectories for a cooperative task can be generated by a generative model, provided that the model has been trained on demonstrations of the agents cooperating. Yet, demonstrations of cooperation are costly and may not exist for tasks that the team has never performed. The conditions under which the agents can combine their capabilities, however, are physical properties of the team and are known before any demonstration is collected. We encode the conditions as constraints on the team trajectories, and we enforce the constraints while sampling from generative models trained on demonstrations of each agent alone. We prove that the proposed method can generate every team trajectory that satisfies the constraints, although the demonstrations contain no cooperation. Hence the constraints determine which team trajectories can be generated, and the demonstrations determine how likely each team trajectory is. Numerical results on two cooperative tasks show the effectiveness of the method, which generates cooperative team trajectories that satisfy the constraints and requires no retraining when agents join or leave the team. Finally, we implement the method on a multi-robot testbed.

llm.title_ja: バリア誘導型拡散サンプリングによる異種ロボットチームの能力合成
llm.tldr_ja: 協調のデモンストレーションが存在しないタスクにおいても、異種ロボットの物理的制約をチーム軌道に対する制約としてエンコードし、各エージェント単体のデモンストレーションで訓練された生成モデルからのサンプリング時に適用することで、協力的なチーム軌道を生成する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 異種チームのエージェントは個々の能力を超えるタスクを遂行するために協調できるが、協調のデモンストレーションはコストが高く、チームが一度も実行したことのないタスクでは存在しない場合がある。
llm.method: エージェントが能力を組み合わせる条件を物理的制約としてエンコードし、各エージェント単体のデモンストレーションで訓練された生成モデルからのサンプリング時にその制約を強制するバリア誘導型拡散サンプリング手法を提案する。
llm.result: 2つの協調タスクにおける数値結果から、制約を満たす協力的なチーム軌道を生成でき、エージェントの参加や離脱時に再訓練を必要としないことが示され、マルチロボットテストベッドに実装された。
keywords_ja: 制約付きサンプリング

2611.23149.tldr_en: Numerical results on two cooperative tasks show the effectiveness of the method, which generates cooperative team trajectories that satisfy the constraints and requires no retraining when agents join or leave the team.

2611.23143.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
2611.23143.abstract: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. Given a monocular video and initial 2D TCP queries, the tracker directly recovers metric TCP poses in SE(3) and gripper states alongside scene geometry and camera parameters. The generator samples local features from the same 4D representation along the recovered TCP tracks, then combines them with robot observations and language instructions to predict future TCP states. Our new cross-embodiment augmentation pipeline converts existing RGB videos into demonstrations for alternative embodiments by retargeting the recovered motion and synthesizing the corresponding observations, without recorded source-robot states. Experiments show that the tracker achieves absolute trajectory errors of 7.60 and 16.07 mm on DROID and RoboLab and adapts to a new embodiment with only ten demonstrations. The generator achieves 69.19% mean success on RoboTwin and outperforms well-established policy models on two real-world tasks, while joint training on source and augmented demonstrations improves target-robot success by 41.5% over augmented-only training.

llm.title_ja: TCP4D: ロボットマニピュレーションのための統合型ツール中心点追跡・生成モデル
llm.tldr_ja: モノクロ動画と初期の2D TCPクエリからSE(3)の指標的TCPポーズやグリッパー状態を直接復元し、同じ4Dシーン表現から将来のTCP軌道を予測する統一モデルTCP4Dを提案し、クロスロボット拡張パイプラインにより少量のデモンストレーションでの適応を実現する。
llm.problem: ロボットマニピュレーション動画は豊富な視覚体験を提供するが、RGB観測からロボットの行動やグリッパー状態のアノテーションを復元することは依然として困難である。
llm.method: 一般化されたツール中心点（TCP）ポーズを行動空間とし、共有される4Dシーン表現を用いて観測されたTCP運動の追跡と将来のTCP軌道の生成を同時に行う統一モデルTCP4Dを構築し、既存のRGB動画を代替ロボットのデモンストレーションに変換するクロスembodiment拡張パイプラインを提案する。
llm.result: DROIDおよびRoboLabにおいて絶対軌道誤差7.60および16.07 mmを達成し、わずか10個のデモンストレーションで新しいロボット形態に適応し、RoboTwinで69.19%の平均成功率を達成した。

2611.23143.tldr_en: TC4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories, is presented, which outperforms well-established policy models on two real-world tasks and joint training on source and augmented demonstrations improves target-robot success by 41.5% over augmented-only training.

2611.23120.title: Pressure Drop: Gravity Vector Estimation from a Distributed Barometric Pressure Sensor Array
2611.23120.abstract: While gravity is often used in mobile robotics as a global constraint for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms, most estimation methods rely on indirect observation of the gravity vector. In this paper, we propose the use of altimeter measurements to directly observe the direction of the gravity vector. We provide a theoretical evaluation of the estimation noise and validate it through extensive experimental data, along with an evaluation of the impact of intersensor distance on our gravity vector estimates. Experimental results demonstrate that a median error of $0.87^\circ$ on the tilt estimation can be achieved with our system in semi-static scenarios. Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential of this approach by comparing it with state-of-the-art methods based on Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs). We highlight that we achieve similar performance to that of IMU-based systems in highly dynamic scenarios and even outperform in specific cases of accelerometer measurement saturation. Finally, an additional experiment shows the potential use within a robotic system through the integration into an Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm.
2611.23120.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027

llm.title_ja: 圧力降下: 分散型気圧センサーアレイによる重力ベクトル推定
llm.tldr_ja: モバイルロボティクスのSLAMにおけるグローバル制約として、従来の慣性計測装置（IMU）の代わりに高度計（気圧センサー）の測定値を用いて重力ベクトルの方向を直接観測する手法を提案し、半静的シナリオで中央値0.87度の傾斜推定誤差を達成する。
llm.problem: モバイルロボティクスにおいて重力はSLAMアルゴリズムのグローバル制約としてよく使用されるが、ほとんどの推定手法は重力ベクトルの間接的な観測に依存している。
llm.method: 分散型気圧センサーアレイ（高度計測定値）を使用して重力ベクトルの方向を直接観測し、推定ノイズの理論的評価とセンサー間距離が重力ベクトル推定に与える影響の実験的評価を行う。
llm.result: 半静的シナリオにおいてシステムは0.87度の傾斜推定誤差の中央値を達成し、高度に動的なシナリオではIMUベースのシステムと同等の性能を発揮し、加速度計の測定飽和の特定ケースではそれを上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン
モバイルロボティクス

2611.23118.title: Auditing a Learned Simulator for Legged Robots: The Robotic World Model on ANYmal D
2611.23118.abstract: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions. They are usually trained and checked one step ahead, although a policy uses them for a hundred steps or more. We audit one published system end to end, without a GPU: the dynamics model of the Robotic World Model (RWM) for the ANYmal D quadruped, and the uncertainty estimate of its follow-up, RWM-U. We rebuilt the model to match the released code's outputs, losses and gradients exactly, measured 101 trained simulators, 200 compressed copies and 38 simulators of three other architectures, and trained policies inside simulators that we tested in a hand-built MuJoCo model of the robot. Training on the model's own rollouts beat one-step training at 368 steps on all ten held-out episodes (registered), although one-step training was better one step ahead. One-step checks therefore misjudge design choices: pruning 30% of the weights kept 90% of the model's skill one step ahead and 39% at 2 s. Ensemble disagreement ranked rollout error well (Spearman +0.90 at 100 steps), yet covered 4.6% of outcomes at one sigma, against 68% for a calibrated estimate, as each network's own variance collapses under the implemented loss. Two checks that need no recorded future ranked some pools of simulators well, but neither was shown better than 8-step error in a primary test. At the robot level, accuracy has not predicted walking: all 18 fine-tuned copies we tested predicted better than the released model one and eight steps ahead, yet 13 gave failing policies, and registered tests of whether any check ranks simulators by their policies were not settled. In a secondary test, running the authors' policy inside each simulator ranked them well. We also report nine of our own claims that we withdrew. Scope: one robot, one gait, simulated data, no hardware.
2611.23118.comment: 39 pages, 13 figures, 20 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/joyjeet-singh/rwm and https://github.com/joyjeet-singh/rwm-robot-level. Extends arXiv:2611.02699 with robot-level experiments

llm.title_ja: 学習済みシミュレータの監査: ANYmal Dにおけるロボット世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: ANYmal D四足歩行ロボットのロボット世界モデル（RWM）およびRWM-Uのエンドツーエンドの監査を実施し、1ステップのチェックでは設計選択やポリシーの歩行性能を正確に判断できず、モデル自身のロールアウトを用いた訓練が有効であることを示した。
llm.problem: 四足歩行ロボットは学習済みシミュレータ内で歩行を学習できるが、ポリシーが100ステップ以上実行するのに対し、シミュレータは通常1ステップ先のみで訓練・検証されている。
llm.method: ANYmal D用ロボット世界モデル（RWM）のダイナミクスモデルと不確実性推定をGPUなしでエンドツーエンドに再構築し、101個の訓練済みシミュレータ、200個の圧縮コピー、他の3つのアーキテクチャのシミュレータを測定し、MuJoCoモデル内でポリシーを訓練して評価する。
llm.result: モデル自身のロールアウトで訓練したモデルは、すべての10個の保持エピソードで1ステップ訓練を上回ったが、18個の微調整モデルのうち13個が失敗するポリシーを生み出し、1ステップの精度では実際の歩行性能を予測できなかった。

2611.23118.tldr_en: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions, but accuracy has not predicted walking: all 18 fine-tuned copies tested predicted better than the released model one and eight steps ahead, yet 13 gave failing policies, and registered tests of whether any check ranks simulators by their policies were not settled.

2611.23111.title: Event-Based Dynamic Lip Region Estimation During Speech
2611.23111.abstract: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and low power consumption, making them promising for speech-related applications. These include automatic lip reading, audiovisual speech analysis, and human-robot interaction, particularly in challenging environments characterized by low illumination or high dynamic range. Event-based lip reading, speaker recognition, and voice activity detection, however, mostly operate on a cropped region of interest (ROI), by hand or by the dataset, and no event-based method supplies that ROI as a spatial region; existing event-based face analysis gives the mouth as landmarks, which presents a mismatch between application and localization. The present work predicts a dense heatmap over the lip region from the full event "frame". Events are encoded as a polarity-separated voxel grid and processed at every location by a two-pathway continuous-time recurrent network (CT-RNN) with learned, log-space bounded time constants acting on the real elapsed time of each bin: a stateless fast pathway and a stateful slow pathway, utilised for refining and anchoring the prediction. The model reaches 69.5% on lips on four unseen speakers and switches target only 2.1 times per second, against 8.9 and 11.0 for convolutional baselines with more parameters. Adding a spatial encoder improves precision but fails on a new face scale. On a real event sensor, trained only on simulated events, the proposed model reaches 58.0% on lips against 43.2% for the CNN, with fewer than half its target switches.

llm.title_ja: イベントベースの音声中動的唇領域推定
llm.tldr_ja: イベントカメラを用いて、実時間を処理する状態なしの高速経路と状態ありの低速経路を持つ2経路連続時間リカレントネットワークにより、完全なイベントフレームから唇領域の密なヒートマップを直接予測する。
llm.problem: イベントベースの読唇術や音声解析は、手動またはデータセットによる切り抜かれた関心領域（ROI）に依存しており、既存の顔面解析手法にはアプリケーションと局所化の間にミスマッチが存在する。
llm.method: イベントを極性分離ボクセルグリッドとしてエンコードし、実時間に基づいて学習されたログ空間バウンド時定数を持つ2経路の連続時間リカレントネットワーク（高速な状態なし経路とアンカリング用の低速な状態あり経路）で処理し、唇領域の密なヒートマップを予測する。
llm.result: 4人の未見の話者に対して69.5%の精度を達成し、より多くのパラメータを持つCNNベースラインと比較してターゲットスイッチ数を大幅に削減し、シミュレーションイベントのみで訓練して実センサー上で58.0%を達成した。
keywords_ja: リカレントニューラルネットワーク

2611.23111.tldr_en: This work predicts a dense heatmap over the lip region from the full event"frame", encoded as a polarity-separated voxel grid and processed at every location by a two-pathway continuous-time recurrent network (CT-RNN) with learned, log-space bounded time constants acting on the real elapsed time of each bin.

2611.23102.title: CADENCE: Learning Acyclic Gaits for Model-Based Quadruped Locomotion
2611.23102.abstract: Model-based quadruped controllers usually step on a cyclic gait, which lifts the legs in a fixed order on a fixed period, wherever the safe footholds are. We present CADENCE, a learned step planner with a small action space. Every 40 ms, it picks one of at most 65 discrete choices: no step, or one leg's step to a safe foothold. It also predicts a swing time. We train CADENCE by reinforcement learning on top of a convex model predictive controller (MPC). Nothing prescribes a gait: there is no gait schedule, and the reward has no gait term, only a cost per step. The one structural constraint is that at most two legs may swing at once. The policy we analyzed developed an acyclic gait, with no fixed period or stepping order, yet it still paired diagonal legs. An inverse footstep model (IFM), fitted on a controller's logged steps, turns each foothold into a command. With only the IFM refitted, on fewer than 20,000 steps, CADENCE ran frozen on OCS2's nonlinear MPC. In simulated trials on a range of terrains (26% to 49% voids) and speeds (0.1 m/s and 0.2 m/s), it succeeded in 85.1% (mean of five seeds), against 67.8% for OCS2-Trot, 65.5% for OCS2-Single, and 39.6% in a static walk ablation of CADENCE. At 49% voids, it succeeded in 72.9%, against 43.0% for OCS2-Trot.

llm.title_ja: CADENCE: モデルベース四足歩行のための非周期的歩行の学習
llm.tldr_ja: CADENCEは、凸モデル予測制御の上に強化学習を用いて小さなアクション空間で安全な足場とスイング時間を計画する学習済みステッププランナーであり、固定された順序のない非周期的歩行を発展させて多様な不整地で高い走破性を達成する。
llm.problem: モデルベースの四足歩行コントローラは通常、安全な足場がどこであれ固定の順序と周期で足を上げる周期的歩行に依存している。
llm.method: 凸モデル予測制御の上に強化学習を用いて学習され、各ステップのコストのみを与えて歩行スケジュールや歩行項の報酬なしで、最大2本の足が同時にスイングできる制約の下で非周期的歩行を学習するステッププランナーCADENCEを提案する。
llm.result: 26%から49%の空隙を持つ様々な地形と速度でのシミュレーション試行において、CADENCEは平均85.1%の成功率を達成し、従来のOCS2-Trot（67.8%）やOCS2-Single（65.5%）を上回った。

2611.23102.tldr_en: CADENCE, a learned step planner with a small action space, is presented, a learned step planner with a small action space that developed an acyclic gait, with no fixed period or stepping order, yet it still paired diagonal legs.

2611.23070.title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home
2611.23070.abstract: Household robots often need to operate appliances, and smart appliances offer both control panels and device APIs. Existing embodied AI simulation environments, however, model appliances solely as physical objects. We introduce PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol~\footnote{https://csa-iot.org/all-solutions/matter/}, the industry standard for smart-home devices. PAIR provides 84 smart-device assets whose functional control panels and APIs act on a shared device state, with ambient conditions that evolve in response to both. From a survey of 1,443 requests, we construct a benchmark of 40 tasks that all require object manipulation yet remain solvable without API access, with 340 human demonstrations for policy training. Whether run alone, with a high-level planner, or with an API-enabled planner, two fine-tuned VLA policies complete none of the 120 evaluation episodes. Robots rarely get far enough to use the API: even with oracle plans and API access, over 90\% of failed rollouts stall at navigating, grasping, or operating a door. With a perfect oracle in place of the robot's body, the best planner still gets through only 57.3\% of its plan. When choosing between pressing a button and calling an API, several planners go by whether they can read the panel, not by API latency.\footnote{We will release our code and data upon publication.}

llm.title_ja: PAIR: 家庭用ロボットをスマートホームに統合する
llm.tldr_ja: Matterプロトコルに準拠したスマートホームシミュレーション環境PAIRを導入し、84のスマートデバイスアセットと40のタスクベンチマークを用いて評価した結果、既存のVLAポリシーや高レベルプランナーはナビゲーションや把持、扉の操作などの物理的操作の失敗によりタスクを完遂できないことを示した。
llm.problem: 家庭用ロボットは家電を操作する必要があり、スマート家電はコントロールパネルとデバイスAPIの両方を提供しているが、既存のembodied AIシミュレーション環境は家電を単なる物理オブジェクトとしてモデル化している。
llm.method: 業界標準のMatterプロトコルに準拠し、物理状態と機能コントロールパネル・APIを共有する84のスマートデバイスアセットと40のタスクからなるシミュレーション環境PAIRを構築し、2つの微調整されたVLAポリシーと各種プランナーを評価する。
llm.result: 微調整されたVLAポリシーは120の評価エピソードのいずれも完遂できず、失敗したロールアウトの90%以上がナビゲーション、把持、扉の操作などの物理的動作で停滞することが判明した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーション環境
ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.23070.tldr_en: PAIR is introduced, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol that provides 84 smart-device assets whose functional control panels and APIs act on a shared device state, with ambient conditions that evolve in response to both.

2611.23056.title: RFW-S: Everyday Deformable Objects with Independent Simulation Verification
2611.23056.abstract: Large-scale robotic simulation requires diverse deformable objects with executable physical properties and realistic interaction behaviors. However, existing 3D asset collections primarily emphasize visual diversity, while scalable physical construction and verification remain challenging. We introduce RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families: soft solids, cloth sheets, shells, garments, and bags. We develop an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration. To ensure physical reliability, we introduce an independent simulation verification framework that evaluates object behaviors under interactions distinct from those used for parameter calibration. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of independent verification and characterize deformable responses under different physical configurations. We further evaluate robotic grasping in terms of both task success and object integrity, and demonstrate the physical realism of our simulated objects through sim-to-real replay of fragile-object manipulation. RFW-S provides a scalable foundation for physically grounded simulation and embodied robotic learning.

llm.title_ja: RFW-S: 独立したシミュレーション検証を備えた日常的な変形可能オブジェクトデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: RFW-Sは、485の日常カテゴリにわたる83,365個のシミュレーション検証済み変形可能オブジェクトアセットの大規模データセットであり、参照誘導型3D生成と独立したシミュレーション検証フレームワークを通じて物理的リアリズムを提供する。
llm.problem: 大規模ロボットシミュレーションには実行可能な物理的特性と現実的な相互作用動作を持つ多様な変形可能オブジェクトが必要だが、既存の3Dアセットコレクションは視覚的多様性に偏っており、スケーラブルな物理構築と検証は困難である。
llm.method: 参照誘導型3D生成、構造を意識した物理モデリング、LLM支援によるパラメータ推定・較正を統合した自動パイプラインを開発し、パラメータ較正とは異なる相互作用下でオブジェクトの挙動を評価する独立したシミュレーション検証フレームワークを導入する。
llm.result: 独立したシミュレーション検証の有効性を実証し、異なる物理設定下での変形応答を特徴付け、把持の成功率とオブジェクトの完全性に関してロボット把持を評価し、壊れやすいオブジェクトのマニピュレーションのシム・ハード実演を通じて物理的リアリズムを示した。
keywords_ja: 変形可能オブジェクト
シミュレーション検証

2611.23056.tldr_en: This work introduces RFW-S, a large-scale dataset of 83,365 simulation-verified assets spanning 485 everyday categories across five structural families, and develops an automated pipeline integrating reference-guided 3D generation, structure-aware physical modeling, and LLM-assisted parameter estimation and calibration.

2611.23050.title: Magflow: Differentiable Simulation of Industrial-Grade 6D Magnetic Levitation
2611.23050.abstract: Magnetic levitation with six-degrees-of-freedom enables frictionless transport and micrometer-scale positioning in principle, but low-level control is inherently challenging due to its complex and unstable dynamics. Industrial systems typically rely on deep hardware-software co-design, where mover and stator geometries are jointly designed to enable a compact, hand-crafted approximation of the electromagnetic force computation, thereby keeping control computationally tractable at kilohertz rates. However, this approach imposes overly conservative constraints on the operating workspace and the range of supported mover topologies. Instead of reducing the underlying physics to a hand-crafted approximation, we compute the physics directly. We introduce Magflow, a fully differentiable, GPU-parallel simulator for 6D magnetic levitation. It is used to train the first neural controller for an industrial-grade 6D magnetic levitation system that is learned purely from simulated physics. We show that the learned neural controller transfers zero-shot from simulation to real hardware while satisfying hard real-time constraints at 4 kHz. The learned controller achieves qualitatively new behaviors and even levitates a mover topology for which no hand-crafted solution exists. These results demonstrate that co-design is not a physical necessity for 6D magnetic levitation control. More broadly, control learning from simulated physics can find solutions beyond the reach of control engineering in demanding industrial domains. Source code and demonstration videos are publicly available at https://sites.google.com/view/magflow.
2611.23050.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L). Project page: https://sites.google.com/view/magflow

llm.title_ja: Magflow: 工業用グレードの6軸磁気浮上の微分可能シミュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: Magflowは、複雑な電磁気力を直接計算する完全微分可能なGPU並列6軸磁気浮上シミュレータであり、シミュレーション上の物理のみから学習された初の神経コントローラがゼロショットで実機に転移し、ハードリアルタイム制約を満たして動作することを示した。
llm.problem: 6軸磁気浮上は摩擦のない搬送やミクロン単位の位置決めを可能にするが、その複雑で不安定なダイナミクスにより、従来の工業システムは手作業による近似計算を用いた深いハードウェア・ソフトウェアの共同設計に依存しており、動作ワークスペースやトポロジーに過度に保守的な制約を課している。
llm.method: 物理の近似を避け、電磁気力の計算を直接行う完全微分可能なGPU並列6軸磁気浮上シミュレータMagflowを開発し、シミュレーション上の物理のみから4 kHzのハードリアルタイム制約を満たす神経コントローラを訓練する。
llm.result: 学習された神経コントローラはシミュレーションから実ハードウェアへゼロショットで転移し、手作業による解が存在しないムーバートポロジーをも浮上させ、共同設計が物理的必然ではないことを実証した。
keywords_ja: 微分可能シミュレーション

2611.23050.tldr_en: Magflow, a fully differentiable, GPU-parallel simulator for 6D magnetic levitation, is introduced and used to train the first neural controller for an industrial-grade 6D magnetic levitation system that is learned purely from simulated physics.

2611.23021.title: Satisfiability Modulo Theories for Robust Synthesis of Signal Temporal Logic Specifications
2611.23021.abstract: Signal Temporal Logic is a popular framework for describing a robotic system's goals. Once described using a temporal logic framework, synthesis turns the goals into actual steps for the robots to follow. Currently, the state of the art for sound and complete synthesis is using Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), which struggles on long time horizons and large environments, preventing the construction of guaranteed safe plans for long deployments. This paper introduces a new synthesis method using Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) which scales better for long deployments and adapts to environmental changes more quickly. We do this by introducing an encoding method for STL into SMT constraints, and an encoding method for discrete-time dynamical systems modeled as a transition system. We then conduct an empirical comparison of our SMT based methods against the state of the art MILP based methods. Results show that for this class of problems, SMT is an effective encoding strategy that performs the best on long time horizon tasks.

llm.title_ja: シグナル一時論理仕様のロバスト合成のための充足可能モジュロ理論
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットの目標記述フレームワークであるシグナル一時論理（STL）の制約および離散時間動的システムをSMT制約にエンコードする新しい手法を提案し、長期的な展開におけるスケーラビリティと環境変化への適応性をMILPベースの手法と比較して検証した。
llm.problem: 健全で完全な合成の現状の最先端手法である混合整数線形計画法（MILP）は、長時間のホライズンや大規模な環境において苦戦し、長期間の展開に向けた保証付きの安全なプランの構築を妨げている。
llm.method: STL仕様および遷移系としてモデル化された離散時間動的システムをSMT制約にエンコードする新しい手法を提案し、最先端のMILPベースの手法と実証的に比較する。
llm.result: このクラスの問題において、SMTは効果的なエンコード戦略であり、長時間のホライズンを持つタスクで最も優れた性能を発揮することが示された。
keywords_ja: 充足可能モジュロ理論

2611.23021.tldr_en: This paper introduces a new synthesis method using Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) which scales better for long deployments and adapts to environmental changes more quickly and conducts an empirical comparison of the SMT based methods against the state of the art MILP based methods.

2611.22998.title: Residual-Guided Lightweight Reinforcement Learning for Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection with a Frozen World Model
2611.22998.abstract: In automated driving, world models provide future scene predictions for evaluating candidate trajectories, but fixed selection rules may not capture scene-dependent trade-offs. We propose a residual-guided reinforcement learning (RL) framework for lightweight trajectory selection with a frozen world model and a fixed candidate bank. The framework uses proximal policy optimization (PPO) to fine-tune a joint policy over candidate selection and bounded trajectory residuals. A context-conditioned ranking network learns candidate preferences from feedback obtained by evaluating local perturbations of the selected trajectories. At inference, the selector combines learned preference and predicted risk ranks using fixed weights and returns the selected candidate trajectory without modification. Fine-tuning updates 16,106 parameters across the actor and critic, while the deployed selector retains only the 11,725-parameter ranking network, with the residual branch and critic used exclusively during training. In open-loop evaluation on the nuScenes validation set, the method reduces average Euclidean trajectory error (L2) by 3.99% relative to the RiskWorld model baseline without RL-based selection. Under matched budgets for feedback accesses and actor updates, residual exploration reduces L2 by 0.83% relative to the categorical PPO variant trained without residuals. The method also maintains lower L2 than RiskWorld when risk features are removed or shuffled.

llm.title_ja: 残差誘導型軽量強化学習による凍結された世界モデルを用いたリスク考慮型軌道選択
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された世界モデルと固定された候補バンクを用い、PPOで候補選択と軌道残差を共同ファインチューニングする残差誘導型強化学習フレームワークを提案し、nuScenes検証セットにおいて平均ユークリッド軌道誤差を削減する。
llm.problem: 自動運転において世界モデルは候補軌道を評価するための将来のシーン予測を提供するが、固定された選択ルールではシーンに依存するトレードオフを捉えられない場合がある。
llm.method: PPOを用いて候補選択と有界な軌道残差にわたる結合ポリシーをファインチューニングする残差誘導型強化学習フレームワークを提案し、選択された軌道の局所的摂動の評価フィードバックから候補の好みを学習する文脈条件付きランキングネットワークを使用する。
llm.result: nuScenes検証セットのオープンループ評価において、リスクワールドモデルのベースラインと比較して平均ユークリッド軌道誤差（L2）を3.99%削減し、残差を使用せずに訓練されたカテゴリカルPPOと比較してL2を0.83%削減した。

2611.22998.tldr_en: A residual-guided reinforcement learning (RL) framework for lightweight trajectory selection with a frozen world model and a fixed candidate bank and a context-conditioned ranking network to fine-tune a joint policy over candidate selection and bounded trajectory residuals.

2611.22994.title: Making Future-Predictive Representations Actionable
2611.22994.abstract: Recent world action models (WAMs) drop future prediction at inference, assuming that representations learned through auxiliary future supervision still benefit action generation. However, our layerwise analysis of Fast-WAM reveals a depth-dependent mismatch: while probes decode future state transitions more accurately from deeper visual layers, the gradients and visual focuses of the future and action objectives increasingly diverge with depth, leaving much of this predictive information unused by the action pathway. To address this issue, we introduce RelayWAM, which adds an explicit transition space between the video and action backbones. Conditioned on the task instruction, robot state, and current action estimate, recurrent transition layers extract step-relevant predictive cues across depth and relay them directly into the action attention, without generating future frames at inference. Experiments show that RelayWAM substantially amplifies the benefit of future supervision, translating into stronger generalization under distribution shifts in both simulation and real-world robot tasks. On LIBERO-Plus, RelayWAM achieves 72.03% mean success, compared to 56.42% without future supervision and 51.50% for Fast-WAM.
2611.22994.comment: 15 pages, 6 main figures, including supplementary material

llm.title_ja: 将来予測表現の行動可能性の向上
llm.tldr_ja: Fast-WAMの深さによるミスマッチを解消するため、ビデオと行動のバックボーン間に明示的な遷移空間を追加し将来フレームの生成なしにステップ関連の予測的手がかり行動注意に中継するRelayWAMを提案し、シミュレーションおよび実ロボットタスクで汎化性能を向上させる。
llm.problem: 最近の世界行動モデル（WAMs）は推論時に将来予測を省略し、補助的な将来教師信号を通じて学習された表現が行動生成に役立つと仮定しているが、深さとともに将来の目的と行動の目的の勾配や視覚的焦点が乖離していく。
llm.method: タスク指示、ロボット状態、現在の行動推定に条件付けられ、将来フレームを生成することなくリカレント遷移層を通じてステップ関連の予測的手がかりを抽出して行動注意に直接中継するRelayWAMを提案する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plusにおいて、将来教師信号なしの場合の56.42%およびFast-WAMの51.50%と比較して、RelayWAMは72.03%の平均成功率を達成し、シミュレーションおよび実世界ロボットタスクの分布シフト下でより強力な汎化を実現した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22994.tldr_en: Experiments show that RelayWAM substantially amplifies the benefit of future supervision, translating into stronger generalization under distribution shifts in both simulation and real-world robot tasks.

2611.22990.title: Physics-Informed Tactile-based Shape Estimation of Deformable Linear Objects
2611.22990.abstract: Accurate shape estimation of Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) is a fundamental challenge in robotic manipulation, often hindered by visual occlusions and the high-dimensional configuration space of flexible materials. While Force/Torque (F/T) and vision-centric methods have been proposed, they frequently struggle with grasp-site ambiguities and environmental interference. In this letter, we investigate the hypothesis that global shape estimation can be achieved through tactile sensing and proprioception, without any visual perception. We contend that dense, high-resolution tactile imprints capture critical boundary conditions and contact gradients that are sufficient to resolve the high-dimensional configuration of the DLO. To prove this, we introduce a Physics-Informed Vision Transformer (ViT) framework that maps tactile images to a 3D vertex chain. By leveraging self-attention mechanisms and a physics-weighted loss function, our model enforces structural priors to ensure that the predicted geometry adheres to the object's physical manifold. Experimental results demonstrate that our tactile-based approach achieves superior reconstruction accuracy across Euclidean and Chamfer metrics. Furthermore, we demonstrate the efficiency of this modality, achieving model transfer to novel DLO materials and geometries. Our findings suggest that tactile feedback provides a robust and computationally efficient alternative for DLO state estimation in visually degraded or occluded environments.

llm.title_ja: 物理情報に基づく触覚を用いた変形可能線状物の形状推定
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚情報を用いず、高解像度な触覚インプリントとプロプリオセプションのみから物理情報に基づくVision Transformerを用いて変形可能線状物（DLO）の3D頂点チェーンを再構成する手法を提案し、優れた再構築精度とモデル転移性を実証する。
llm.problem: 変形可能線状物（DLO）の正確な形状推定は、視覚的オクルージョンや柔軟な材料の高次元構成空間によって妨げられることが多く、従来のF/Tや視覚中心の手法は把持部位の曖昧さや環境干渉に苦しむことが多い。
llm.method: 触覚画像から3D頂点チェーンへマッピングする物理情報に基づくVision Transformer（ViT）フレームワークを導入し、自己注意力機構と物理重み付き損失関数により予測幾何学がオブジェクトの物理多様体に適合するよう構造的事前知識を強制する。
llm.result: ユークリッドおよびチャムファー指標において優れた再構築精度を達成し、新しいDLOの材料や幾何形状へのモデル転移を実証し、視覚的劣化やオクルージョン環境におけるDLO状態推定の代替手段として触覚フィードバックの有効性を示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・トランスフォーマー
物理情報に基づく学習

2611.22954.title: Sim2CBF: From Forward Simulations to Implicit Control Barrier Function Safety Filtering without Model Derivatives
2611.22954.abstract: Failure avoidance in complex robot-environment interactions is challenging because the underlying dynamics are difficult to model accurately, and available predictive models may not provide reliable derivatives. We present Sim2CBF, a failure-avoidance framework that solves the Control Barrier Function (CBF)-Safety Filter (SF) optimization problem using only forward-model evaluations, thereby avoiding differentiation of the predictive model. Specifically, we approximate the CBF constraint using finite differences and local linear interpolation over sampled control inputs while preserving failure-avoidance guarantees. The underlying CBF is implicit and constructed from backup-policy rollouts, enabling the use of expressive predictive models such as physics-based simulators and learned world models. Compared with purely sampling-based SFs, our formulation requires fewer control samples and yields less conservative behavior than direct nominal-backup blending. We evaluate Sim2CBF in simulation, hardware box-toppling, and vision-based control tasks, demonstrating its applicability to contact-rich and learned dynamics, as well as its adaptability to changes in the predictive model.

llm.title_ja: Sim2CBF: 順方向シミュレーションからモデル微分を必要としない暗黙的コントロールバリア関数安全性フィルタリングへ
llm.tldr_ja: Sim2CBFは、予測モデルの微分を回避し、順方向モデルの評価と有限差分・局所線形補間のみを用いてコントロールバリア関数（CBF）の安全性フィルタ最適化問題を解くフレームワークであり、接触の多いダイナミクスや学習済み世界モデルへの適用性を示す。
llm.problem: 複雑なロボットと環境の相互作用における失敗回避は、基礎となるダイナミクスの正確なモデリングが難しく、利用可能な予測モデルが信頼性の高い微分を提供しないため困難である。
llm.method: 予測モデルの微分を回避し、順方向モデルの評価のみを用いて、制御入力のサンプリングに対する有限差分と局所線形補間によりCBF制約を近似するSim2CBFフレームワークを提案し、バックアップポリシーのロールアウトから暗黙的なCBFを構築する。
llm.result: シミュレーション、ハードウェアのボックストップリング、視覚ベースの制御タスクにおいてSim2CBFを評価し、接触の多いダイナミクスや学習済みダイナミクスへの適用性、および予測モデルの変化に対する適応性を示した。
keywords_ja: コントロールバリア関数
微分可能シミュレーション

2611.22954.tldr_en: Sim2CBF is presented, a failure-avoidance framework that solves the Control Barrier Function-Safety Filter optimization problem using only forward-model evaluations, thereby avoiding differentiation of the predictive model.

2611.22927.title: Sideslip-Conditioned Drift Trajectory Planning with Flow Matching and Control Barrier Functions
2611.22927.abstract: Drifting, the deliberate control of a vehicle at large sideslip angles, is relevant to both motorsport and recovery from unexpected oversteer. Existing autonomous drifting methods typically determine drift intensity through predefined reference trajectories, optimization objectives, or learned policy rewards, rather than accepting a desired sideslip angle as an explicit input. We propose, to the best of our knowledge, the first generative drift trajectory planner explicitly conditioned on a requested peak sideslip angle. A conditional flow matching model is trained on demonstrated drift laps with hindsight-derived sideslip labels and refined through reinforcement fine-tuning. A control barrier function (CBF) correction is then applied to satisfy model-based road, tire friction, and actuator constraints at the planning waypoints. In closed-loop experiments in the racing simulator Assetto Corsa, a nonlinear model predictive controller tracks the generated plans for six requested sideslip angles from 20 deg to 45 deg, with 30 laps (approximately 75 km) per request. The median peak sideslip angle measured across drift-corner passes follows the requested angle, with a mean absolute error of 1.2 deg across the six conditions. Ablation experiments show that reinforcement fine-tuning improves conditioning accuracy, while CBF correction substantially reduces off-road and spin events.
2611.22927.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Under review. Demonstration video: https://youtu.be/nskukDD1MFg

llm.title_ja: 流動マッチングと制御バリア関数を用いた横滑り角条件付きドリフト軌道計画
llm.tldr_ja: 所望のピーク横滑り角を明示的に入力として受け取る、初の生成的ドリフト軌道計画手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の自律ドリフト手法は、所望の横滑り角を明示的入力とせず、事前定義された参照軌道等を使用している。
llm.method: 条件付き流動マッチングモデルの訓練と強化学習によるファインチューニング、および制御バリア関数による補正を適用する。
llm.result: 実機シミュレーションにおいて、測定されたピーク横滑り角の中央値は要求角度によく追従し、平均絶対誤差は1.2度となった。

2611.22927.tldr_en: This work proposes, to the best of its knowledge, the first generative drift trajectory planner explicitly conditioned on a requested peak sideslip angle, and shows that reinforcement fine-tuning improves conditioning accuracy, while CBF correction substantially reduces off-road and spin events.

2611.22908.title: Arboreus: A Realistic Boreal Forest Simulator with Topographic Terrain and Satellite-Informed Parametric Tree Distributions
2611.22908.abstract: This work presents Arboreus, a realistic Boreal forest simulator, developed to support statistical validation of robotic autonomy algorithms in Boreal forest environments. Arboreus presents an automated methodology for synthesizing large-scale, data-informed, plausible forest worlds from parametric trees, height-variant terrain, and satellite-informed tree density distributions. The parametric generation of dominant Boreal tree species such as Birch, Spruce, and Pine is guided by trunk, canopy, and foliage parameters, extracted from growth studies in the Nordic areas. Tree distribution in an area of interest is guided by the Copernicus satellite dataset, which provides tree cover density and dominant species type at up to 10m raster resolution. The forest floor generation is guided by topographic data from the Swedish cadastral agency to produce realistic data-informed terrains. Given coordinates and extents of forested areas of interest, Arboreus synthesizes data-informed plausible forests, while offering flexibility to inject user observations of real forests (detail, age, dimensionality and tree count), which is critical for realistic synthetic data generation and for the testing of feature-sensitive autonomy algorithms. The applicability of Arboreus for benchmarking and validation of robot autonomy for different robot mobilities is demonstrated in Gazebosim, Unreal Engine, and Isaac Sim physics engines. The applicability of Arboreus as a source of synthetic forest data and its potential to support downstream forest resource mapping research (volume estimation, tree instance segmentation and stem attribute estimation) is also demonstrated. Arboreus has been open-sourced along with a dataset comprising 25 Boreal forest worlds of size 1000m2 corresponding to three real forest sites.

llm.title_ja: Arboreus: 地形と衛星情報に基づくパラメータ化された樹木分布を持つ現実的なタイガ林シミュレータ
llm.tldr_ja: タイガ林環境におけるロボットの自律アルゴリズムの統計的検証を支援するため、現実的なタイガ林シミュレータ「Arboreus」を開発した。
llm.problem: タイガ林環境におけるロボットの自律アルゴリズムを検証するための、現実的なシミュレーション環境が不足している。
llm.method: パラメータ化された樹木、高低差のある地形、衛星情報の樹木密度分布を組み合わせて、大規模な森林ワールドを自動合成する手法を提案する。
llm.result: Gazebo、Unreal Engine、Isaac Simの各物理エンジンにおいて、ロボットの機動性ベンチマークと検証への応用可能性を示した。

2611.22883.title: Fly as Instructed: Refining World-Action Policies for UAV Vision-Language Navigation
2611.22883.abstract: Natural language-guided UAV navigation enables intuitive human-robot interaction and flexible autonomous flight in complex environments. However, reliable navigation requires accurate instruction following, continuous task progress tracking, and safe obstacle avoidance, which remain challenging for existing world-action models that primarily focus on action prediction. To address these limitations, we propose a world-action learning framework that integrates three complementary mechanisms: a language-conditioned action interface with targeted post-training for instruction-responsive motion, recurrent instruction-consumption prediction to track task progress and determine termination, and Gaussian-scene post-training to enhance obstacle avoidance through trajectory imitation and differentiable geometric feedback. Closed-loop evaluations and ablation studies demonstrate improvements in sequential task completion, safe goal reaching, and timely termination. Furthermore, direct one-step denoising reduces inference overhead, and real-world indoor and outdoor flights validate the framework's effectiveness.

llm.title_ja: 指示通りに飛ぶ：UAV視覚言語ナビゲーションのための世界行動ポリシーの洗練
llm.tldr_ja: 指示への応答性、タスク進捗の追跡、障害物回避を統合したUAVの言語誘導型ナビゲーションのための世界行動学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存の世界行動モデルはアクション予測に主眼を置いており、正確な指示追従やタスク進捗の追跡、安全な障害物回避の両立が困難である。
llm.method: 言語条件付きアクションインターフェース、再帰的指示消費予測、ガウスシーン事後訓練を統合したフレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 閉ループ評価とアブレーション実験により、逐次タスクの完了、安全な目標到達、タイムリーな終了の改善が示された。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション

2611.22883.tldr_en: A world-action learning framework that integrates three complementary mechanisms: a language-conditioned action interface with targeted post-training for instruction-responsive motion, recurrent instruction-consumption prediction to track task progress and determine termination, and Gaussian-scene post-training to enhance obstacle avoidance through trajectory imitation and differentiable geometric feedback is proposed.

2611.22880.title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
2611.22880.abstract: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations. However, most world VLA models generate future frames at the pixel level with plenty of dense visual tokens. Although such generated futures can be visually plausible, they preserve many driving-irrelevant appearance details, i.e., only a small portion of the tokens directly encode critical planning-relevant factors, such as agent geometry, motion dynamics, and interactions. This introduces a significant performance bottleneck. An important question thus arises: what world state should a world VLA model reason over to support planning beyond pixel-level prediction? We argue that planning-oriented world modeling should focus on a compact and structured agent-centric latent state that captures the interactions between objects in the driving scene over time. As such, we introduce AgentWorld, an agent-centric VLA world model that uses discrete agent tokens jointly for reasoning and trajectory planning. Each token is dynamically grounded to a surrounding agent associated with its object's state, such as semantic identity, 3D geometry, motion, and interaction context. AgentWorld learns these tokens through three key processes: explicit geometric grounding, reasoning-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and agent-oriented reinforcement learning. Extensive open-loop and closed-loop experiments under diverse driving scenarios show that AgentWorld enhances planning capabilities, fully exploits visual evidence and agent dynamics, and yields interpretable agent-centric world states.

llm.title_ja: 自動運転のためのエージェント中心型視覚言語行動世界モデルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: シーン内のオブジェクト間の相互作用を捉えるコンパクトで構造化されたエージェント中心の潜在状態に焦点を当てた、自動運転向けVLA世界モデル「AgentWorld」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のワールドVLAモデルはピクセルレベルで未来のフレームを生成するため、駆動に関係のない詳細が多く含まれパフォーマンスのボトルネックとなっている。
llm.method: 明示的な幾何学的接地、推論指向の教師あり微調整、エージェント指向の強化学習を通じて離散エージェントトークンを学習するAgentWorldを導入する。
llm.result: 多様な運転シナリオにおけるオープンループおよびクローズドリープ実験により、計画能力の向上と解釈可能な世界状態の実現が示された。

2611.22880.tldr_en: This work argues that planning-oriented world modeling should focus on a compact and structured agent-centric latent state that captures the interactions between objects in the driving scene over time, and introduces AgentWorld, an agent-centric VLA world model that uses discrete agent tokens jointly for reasoning and trajectory planning.

2611.22878.title: Outcome-Balanced PPO and Policy-Induced Flow Rectification for Flow-Based VLA Policies
2611.22878.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables post-training of flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies by optimizing expected task return through environment interaction. However, this optimization raises two challenges: policy updates can alter the velocity-field geometry underlying the score approximation used for stochastic transitions, and sparse multi-task rollouts can yield uneven learning signals across tasks and advantage signs. We introduce an RL framework that combines Outcome-Balanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with policy-induced flow rectification. Outcome-Balanced PPO reweights positive advantages using task success-rate estimates and rescales positive and negative advantages while preserving their signs. Policy-induced rectification periodically fits a linear-bridge flow to ODE endpoint pairs generated by the current policy, refreshing the representation used in subsequent stochastic optimization. We evaluate the framework on simulated manipulation benchmarks and additionally study a component combination in a Real2Sim2Real task, examining task performance, optimization behavior, and flow consistency. The proposed framework improves success rates over the evaluated baselines across the simulated benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: 結果バランス型PPOとフローベースVLAポリシーのためのポリシー誘導型フロー整流
llm.tldr_ja: 結果バランス型PPOとポリシー誘導型フロー整流を組み合わせた、フローベースVLAポリシーの強化学習によるポストトレーニングフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: フローベースVLAポリシーの強化学習におけるポリシー更新が速度場のジオメトリを変化させる点や、スパースなマルチタスクロールアウトが不均一な学習信号を生む点が課題である。
llm.method: タスク成功率推定を用いて正のアドバンテージを再重み付けし符号を保持しつつスケーリングするOutcome-Balanced PPOと、線形ブリッジフローを定期的にフィッティングする手法を組み合わせる。
llm.result: シミュレーションされたマニピュレーションベンチマークにおいて、評価されたベースラインと比較して成功率が向上した。

2611.22878.tldr_en: This work introduces an RL framework that combines Outcome-Balanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with policy-induced flow rectification, which improves success rates over the evaluated baselines across the simulated benchmarks.

2611.22855.title: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation
2611.22855.abstract: Language-conditioned traffic simulation enables scalable test scenarios steered by natural language. The goal is to control selected agents while surrounding traffic reacts to their observed behaviour. For example, a vehicle instructed to cut in late should cause the following vehicle to brake only when the manoeuvre becomes observable. Yet simulators can leak private instructions across agents, causing surrounding vehicles to react before the instructed behaviour becomes observable. Such premature reactions defuse desired events and alter the ensuing closed-loop scenario. Existing benchmarks measure what agents do, not what they could have known, leaving this failure unmeasured. We formalise it as intent leakage and address it through evaluation, data and modelling. Our paired intervention test holds an instructed agent's executed trajectory fixed while varying its private instruction, isolating leakage-induced changes in surrounding agents. We also construct WOMD-PACT, an automatically generated, verifiable dataset of 531,099 WOMD scenes with timed behaviour tags with reaction episodes identified through a counterfactual ghost test and grounded private instructions. Finally, we introduce CaFe, a dual-stream diffusion-forcing simulator fine-tuned in closed loop that restricts inter-agent interactions to public beliefs, preserving legitimate anticipation without leaking private intent. Our evaluation reveals that existing conditioning designs displace 23-83% of nearby uninstructed agents through private-intent leakage, even when the instructed agent's executed motion is held fixed. CaFe eliminates measurable leakage while maintaining comparable WOSAC realism (0.763), demonstrating that causal faithfulness can be enforced without sacrificing measured simulation realism.

llm.title_ja: CaFe: 因果的に忠実な条件付き交通シナリオ生成
llm.tldr_ja: 意図の漏洩を防ぎつつ、言語指示による交通シナリオを生成する因果的に忠実な二重ストリーム拡散フォールティングシミュレータ「CaFe」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のシミュレータではプライベートな指示がエージェント間で漏洩し、意図された行動が観測可能になる前に周囲の車両が反応してしまう問題がある。
llm.method: 対抗ゴーストテストを通じて反応エピソードを特定するデータセットWOMD-PACTの構築と、エージェント間相互作用を公開信念に制限するデュアルストリーム拡散フォールティングシミュレータCaFeを導入する。
llm.result: 提案手法は測定可能な漏洩を完全に排除しつつ、同等のWOSACリアリズムを維持できることが示された。

2611.22855.tldr_en: CaFe is introduced, a dual-stream diffusion-forcing simulator fine-tuned in closed loop that restricts inter-agent interactions to public beliefs, preserving legitimate anticipation without leaking private intent, demonstrating that causal faithfulness can be enforced without sacrificing measured simulation realism.

2611.22852.title: Technical Report of Mobile Manipulator Robot for Industrial Environments
2611.22852.abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' mobile manipulator robot, developed at the Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Department of Electrical Engineering, Shahid Beheshti University. Hereafter, this platform is referred to as the @Work Robot. The robot targets industrial tasks, with an emphasis on improving efficiency in repetitive or hazardous work environments. It uses a 4-wheel Mecanum drive for omnidirectional movement and a 5-degree-of-freedom manipulator arm with a 3D-printed gripper for object handling and navigation. The electronics consist of custom PCB boards built around ESP32 microcontrollers, together with an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX that handles high-level processing and real-time system control. On the software side, Hector SLAM provides mapping and localization, A* handles path planning, and YOLO performs real-time object detection. These modules draw on fused sensor data to deliver robust navigation and reliable collision avoidance. Overall, the system shows effective hardware-software integration, with consistent performance in autonomous navigation, object handling, and task execution in industrial-like settings.
2611.22852.comment: 25 pages, 22 figures, 4 tables. Technical report of Team Auriga's 2025 mobile manipulator (@Work) platform (Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Shahid Beheshti University)

llm.title_ja: 産業環境向けモバイルマニピュレータロボットの技術報告
llm.tldr_ja: 反復的または危険な作業環境における効率向上を目的として開発された、Auriga Roboticsのモバイルマニピュレータロボットの設計と実装について報告する。
llm.problem: 産業における反復的または危険な環境での作業効率化が求められている。
llm.method: 4輪メカナム駆動による全方向移動、5自由度のマニピュレータアーム、NVIDIA Jetson Orin NXを用いたハードウェア・ソフトウェア統合システムを設計・実装する。
llm.result: 産業用環境に似た設定において、自律ナビゲーション、オブジェクトハンドリング、タスク実行で一貫した性能を示した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレータ

2611.22852.tldr_en: The @Work team and their robot, developed at Shahid Beheshti University Faculty of Electrical Engineering's Robotics and Intelligent Automation Lab for RoboCup 2024 competitions, is designed for industrial tasks, optimizing efficiency in repetitive or hazardous environments.

2611.22850.title: Pelorus: Resource-Aware Lidar-Inertial Odometry
2611.22850.abstract: Lidar-inertial odometry (LIO) has an efficiency problem. High-resolution lidars produce millions of points per second that must be processed online on the resource-constrained hardware of robots, cars, or drones, yet most LIO methods neither bound their memory nor report their compute footprint. We introduce Pelorus, a resource-aware LIO with a fixed-capacity multiresolution map of voxelized normal distributions and an iterated equivariant state estimator. A relevance-based eviction keeps the map memory bounded, and a maturity-weighted map update suppresses inconsistent observations. The pipeline runs in parallel on CPUs and GPUs. On five sequences from three public datasets, Pelorus achieves the lowest relative pose error in seven of ten metrics with a small, bounded memory footprint and, with GPU offloading, the lowest CPU load of all compared methods. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, it processes a 128-beam lidar at 10 Hz. Pelorus is open source with CUDA, Vulkan, and Metal backends.

llm.title_ja: Pelorus: リソース考慮型LiDAR-慣性オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 固定容量のマルチ解像度マップと反復的等変状態推定器を用いた、リソース考慮型のLiDAR-慣性オドメトリ「Pelorus」を提案する。
llm.problem: 高解像度LiDARの膨大なポイントクラウドをロボット等のリソース制限されたハードウェア上でオンライン処理する際、多くのLIO手法はメモリや計算量を制限できていない。
llm.method: 関連性に基づく退避によるマップメモリの制限、成熟度加重マップ更新、CPUとGPUでの並列処理パイプラインを実装する。
llm.result: 公開データセットでの評価において、小さな制限されたメモリフットプリントで最も低い相対姿勢誤差と低いCPU負荷を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットナビゲーション

2611.22850.tldr_en: Pelorus is a resource-aware LIO with a fixed-capacity multiresolution map of voxelized normal distributions and an iterated equivariant state estimator, which achieves the lowest relative pose error in seven of ten metrics with a small, bounded memory footprint and, with GPU offloading, the lowest CPU load of all compared methods.

2611.22831.title: Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Balance on Dynamically Responsive Supports
2611.22831.abstract: Conventional balance formulations often assume a rigid, stationary support, decoupling body stabilization from support motion. This assumption becomes inadequate on mechanically responsive supports, creating a coupled control challenge: corrective body motions intended to restore equilibrium can also excite support motion. We formulate sustained balance as a coupled regulation problem that coordinates equilibrium restoration with suppression of motion induced by the robot's own corrections. We introduce LISST (Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Stabilization), a learning framework that accounts for how earlier actions shape the conditions for subsequent corrections. It uses recent observations to support immediate adjustments and longer histories to characterize persistent motion, with physical supervision relating the learned representation to robot-support behavior. To evaluate corrective actions, LISST uses coupled dynamics to assess both imbalance and the direction of motion. A Lyapunov-inspired criterion measures progress over finite windows, accommodating the transients required to restore balance. This physical evaluation guides joint-level policy learning through backpropagation through differentiable model rollouts. Privileged guidance focuses training on difficult states reached by the deployment policy and is transferred through distillation. The resulting policy operates using only onboard proprioception. Real-world experiments demonstrate that LISST maintains balance while limiting residual oscillations during continuous interaction with a dynamically responsive support. Video: youtu.be/iGHU7S4wPyw.

llm.title_ja: リアプノフに着想を得た動的応答性支持面上の持続的バランス
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット自身の補正による支持面の動きの誘発と姿勢の復元を協調させる、リアプノフに着想を得た持続的安定化学習フレームワーク「LISST」を提案する。
llm.problem: 機械的に応答する支持面上では、姿勢を復元しようとする身体の補正動作が支持面の動きを励起してしまうという結合された制御課題が生じる。
llm.method: 結合されたダイナミクスを用いて不均衡と運動方向を評価し、リアプノフに着想を得た基準で有限ウィンドウにわたる進捗を測定する学習フレームワークを導入する。
llm.result: 実世界実験により、動的応答性支持面との継続的な相互作用において、残留振動を抑えつつバランスを維持できることが示された。

2611.22831.tldr_en: This work forms sustained balance as a coupled regulation problem that coordinates equilibrium restoration with suppression of motion induced by the robot's own corrections, introducing LISST (Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Stabilization), a learning framework that accounts for how earlier actions shape the conditions for subsequent corrections.

2611.22829.title: Kolibri: Color Finds the Place, Refinement Sets the Pose for RGB-D Localization in Colored Point Clouds
2611.22829.abstract: An agent or robot in a scanned building must locate its camera in rooms that no model saw during training. Point cloud registration methods can align each RGB-D frame with the building's colored point cloud, accurately but at a high cost. We observe that geometric refinement brings nearby initial poses to the same final pose, so the learned component only needs to find the place. Kolibri does this with a graph network of 55,712 parameters that describes 10 cm cubes of points, called cells, by their color, local shape and neighbors. With the same refinement, it matches GeDi on 96 unseen ScanNet rooms (81.4% against 80.3% within 5 cm and 5°) and on a held-out test of 10 further rooms, in 82 ms per frame on an RTX 2080 Ti. The saved time allows for search without a room label. In one point cloud of 100 rooms, Kolibri loses 1.3 points against knowing the room, while retrieving the room first loses 56.0. In a hospital emergency department scene from a real scan, it localizes 86.5% of the frames rendered from the scan in 384 ms each, where GeDi needs 91 minutes per frame on cubes of the scan for a similar recall. The method needs colors that agree between the frame and the point cloud. On gray frames and across cameras with different color responses, point cloud registration methods keep the lead.

llm.title_ja: Kolibri: 色による場所の特定と幾何学的洗練によるRGB-Dカラー点群ローカリゼーション
llm.tldr_ja: 色、局所形状、隣接関係を用いて点群のキューブを記述するグラフネットワークにより、高速かつ正確なRGB-Dローカリゼーションを実現する「Kolibri」を提案する。
llm.problem: 未知の部屋でエージェントやロボットがカメラ位置を特定する際、点群登録手法は高精度だが計算コストが非常に高い。
llm.method: 幾何学的洗練が近くの初期姿勢を同じ最終姿勢に収束させることに着目し、グラフネットワークを用いて色の情報から場所を効率的に見つける。
llm.result: 未見の ScanNet ルームにおいてGeDiと同等の高精度を維持しつつ、1フレームあたり82msという高速なローカリゼーションを実現した。

2611.22829.tldr_en: It is observed that geometric refinement brings nearby initial poses to the same final pose, so the learned component only needs to find the place, so the learned component only needs to find the place.

2611.22820.title: Pixel is All You Need
2611.22820.abstract: Text, images, audio, touch, and even robot actions can, in principle, all be rendered onto a single canvas, suggesting an ambitious goal of unifying all modalities within vision. Language provides the natural first test. To subsume it, a visual model must reason directly over text in pixels. Across a wide range of image, video, and unified multimodal generators, however, we find that their visual generation modules cannot perform symbolic reasoning over text on the canvas. They succeed only when an underlying text module or prompt rewriter already supplies the answer, effectively reducing the generator to a mere renderer, a limitation that post-training does little to resolve. To test whether this failure stems from pixels themselves or from current training paradigms, we train a family of purely pixel-space generative models from scratch without any text pathway. With images as their sole input and output, these models read questions, write intermediate steps, and produce answers directly on the canvas. Remarkably, they exhibit hallmark behaviors of large language models. Performance improves predictably with scale following a power law. Writing intermediate steps frame by frame substantially outperforms single-frame answering, echoing chain-of-thought, while reinforcement-learning post-training further strengthens reasoning. Moreover, sharing one canvas allows the same model to reason across modalities, a capability that text-only language models lack. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of these phenomena in purely pixel-space generative models free of text tokens.
2611.22820.comment: 20 pages, 6 figures, 7 tables, including references and appendices

llm.title_ja: ピクセルこそがすべて：テキストパスを持たない純粋なピクセル空間生成モデルの系統的研究
llm.tldr_ja: テキストパスを一切持たず、画像を入力・出力として推論・生成を行う純粋なピクセル空間生成モデルの系統的研究を行い、大規模言語モデルの特徴を示すことを明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存の視覚生成モデルの視覚生成モジュールは、テキストモジュールやプロンプトラライタに依存しており、ピクセル上で直接シンボリックな推論を行うことができない。
llm.method: テキストパスを一切使用せず、画像を唯一の入力および出力として、質問の読み取り、中間ステップの書き込み、回答の生成をキャンバス上で行うモデルファミリーをゼロから訓練する。
llm.result: スケーリング則に従った性能向上を示し、フレーム単位で中間ステップを書くことが思考の連鎖（CoT）の役割を果たし推論能力が強化されることを確認した。

2611.22820.tldr_en: This is the first systematic study of these phenomena in purely pixel-space generative models free of text tokens, and sharing one canvas allows the same model to reason across modalities, a capability that text-only language models lack.

2611.22797.title: Zero-Shot Compositional Generalization for Embodied Manipulation
2611.22797.abstract: Robot demonstrations are collected on different embodiments, leaving many robot-skill combinations unobserved. Pooling these data shares visual knowledge, while joint labels remain tied to the demonstrating kinematic chain. We propose a geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills. The central insight is that a demonstrated command provides a tool-space target for every robot that can realize it. Calibrated forward kinematics supplies this supervision to foreign native action interfaces without their joint labels for that skill. Native reconstruction retains demonstrated configurations, and positive reachability checks select targets for cross-robot supervision. A visual policy learns to predict shared actions and executes through the target robot's native decoder. During policy learning, one prediction receives geometric supervision through both source and foreign native realizations. Matched supervision controls, repeated policy training and evaluations across three backbones and two simulators demonstrate improved transfer to missing robot-task combinations.

llm.title_ja: embodiedマニピュレーションのためのゼロショット構成的汎化
llm.tldr_ja: 異なるロボットのデモンストレーションデータを活用し、馴染みのあるロボットとスキルをゼロショットで構成するための幾何学的に監督された学習フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットのデモンストレーションは多様なロボット形態で収集されるため、多くのロボットとスキルの組み合わせが未観測のまま残されている。
llm.method: 較正された順運動学を用いて、動作コマンドを任意の実現可能なロボットのツール空間ターゲットに変換し、結合ラベルなしで外部のネイティブアクションインターフェースを監督する。
llm.result: 3つのバックボーンと2つのシミュレータを用いた実験により、未観測のロボット・タスクの組み合わせへの転移性能の向上が示された。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22797.tldr_en: A geometry-supervised training framework for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills for zero-shot composition of familiar robots and skills is proposed.

2611.22769.title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty
2611.22769.abstract: Forces and torques drive human motion, central to biomechanics, robotics, and physics-aware animation, yet they are often absent from learning-based motion pipelines for body reconstruction and generation. Some motion datasets provide force annotations, but the paired motion sequences are incompatible with the parametric body models used in modern learning pipelines. In addition, existing datasets typically obtain joint torques through inverse dynamics, which is inherently sensitive to the quality of the input kinematics; however, they do not quantify the reliability of these torque estimates. We close this gap with ForceBody, the first dataset to bring ground truth force supervision into a parametric body representation, shipped with per-sample torque uncertainty. ForceBody pairs the SKEL body model with ground reaction forces and inverse-dynamics joint torques across 10,386 motion trials (9.7M frames, 26.9 hours) from 140 subjects. Each torque label is paired with a per-frame, per-joint uncertainty annotation obtained by Monte Carlo sampling through the inverse dynamics pipeline. We benchmark six architectures (MLP, Conv1D, LSTM, GRU, Mamba2, Transformer) on ground reaction force and joint torque prediction from SKEL motion. As one example use of the released uncertainty, finetuning a Transformer with per-sample uncertainty weighting reduces the MAE of joint torque estimation by 5%. Code and data are at https://github.com/DominoAI-Lab/ForceBody-NeurIPS-ED-2026.
2611.22769.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations & Datasets Track

llm.title_ja: ForceBody: トルク不確実性を伴う力ペアのパラメータ化された身体動作データセット
llm.tldr_ja: 地上反力と逆動力学による関節トルクのグランド真値監督信号を、サンプルごとのトルク不確実性とともにパラメータ化された身体表現に統合した最初のデータセット「ForceBody」を構築した。
llm.problem: 現代の学習ベースの身体再構築パイプラインでは、人間の動作駆動に不可欠な力やトルクの情報が欠落しており、既存の推定値には信頼性の定量化がない。
llm.method: SKEL身体モデルと地上反力、逆動力学関節トルクをペアにし、モンテカルロサンプリングを介してフレーム毎・関節毎の不確実性注釈を付与した10,386件の動作トライアルを収集・公開する。
llm.result: 6つのアーキテクチャのベンチマークを実施し、不確実性を用いた重み付けファインチューニングにより関節トルク推定のMAEが5%減少した。

2611.22769.tldr_en: ForceBody is the first dataset to bring ground truth force supervision into a parametric body representation, shipped with per-sample torque uncertainty, and benchmark six architectures on ground reaction force and joint torque prediction from SKEL motion.

2611.22767.title: Levio: Smart Actuated Back-Exoskeleton via Retrofit of a Commercial Passive Device
2611.22767.abstract: Passive back exoskeletons show promising benefits for reducing occupational musculoskeletal disorders. However, their assistance cannot be modulated towards the task requirements. Active exoskeletons offer opportunities for pose-specific assistance, but, developing these systems from scratch for research can be time consuming. Therefore, here, we present an accelerated design pipeline that retrofits a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) passive back exoskeleton, Laevo Flex, with COTS actuation (CubeMars AK10-9) and sensing (IMUs and load-cell) paradigms. Levio was able to provide assistance based on the user's pose. Nine participants performed stoop lifting with the original Laevo and the retrofit Levio system, in transparent and assisted modes. Compared to Laevo, Levio modulated the assistance provided between the bending and lifting phases of the stoop task. The passive assistance offered by Laevo was $25.2 \pm 4.3$ Nm and $30.6 \pm 9.5$ Nm respectively during the bending and lifting phases of the stoop tasks. Levio reduced the resistive torque during bending to $17.9 \pm 4.6$ Nm and offered increased assistance of $37.7 \pm 6.4$ Nm during lifting. Moreover, participants reported higher usability scores and lowest mean global discomfort score while using the Levio when compared to Laevo. These benefits demonstrates retrofitting passive exoskeletons is a viable direction for rapid prototyping of wearable exoskeletons for lifting.

llm.title_ja: Levio: 市販の受動型デバイスのレトロフィットによるスマート駆動型背部外骨格
llm.tldr_ja: 市販の受動型背部外骨格に市販の駆動源とセンシング機能を後付け（レトロフィット）することで、作業者の姿勢に応じた補助を提供するスマート外骨格「Levio」を開発した。
llm.problem: 受動型背部外骨格は作業者の筋骨格系障害軽減に有効だが、タスクの要件に合わせて補助力を変調させることができず、能動型をゼロから開発するのは時間がかかる。
llm.method: 市販の受動型背部外骨格 Laevo Flex に、アクチュエータとIMU・ロードセルをレトロフィットし、屈曲時と持ち上げ時で補助力を動的に変化させる。
llm.result: 9名の被験者による実験で、Levioは従来のLaevoと比較して持ち上げ時に大きな補助力を提供し、ユーザビリティスコアの向上と不快感の軽減を示した。
keywords_ja: ウェアラブルロボット

2611.22767.tldr_en: An accelerated design pipeline is presented that retrofits a Commercial Off-The-Shelf passive back exoskeleton, Laevo Flex, with COTS actuation (CubeMars AK10-9) and sensing (IMUs and load-cell) paradigms and demonstrates retrofitting passive exoskeletons is a viable direction for rapid prototyping of wearable exoskeletons for lifting.

2611.22761.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots
2611.22761.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) in embodied robots create security dependencies beyond inference. We investigate a network-exposed configuration attack on the Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to replace personality settings and the cloud LLM's system prompt through a management interface, without adversarial conversational input. Eleven prompt-injection attempts across five categories were reported as resisted, whereas both configuration-layer attack paths produced observable behavioural changes on physical hardware. We demonstrate local and network-adjacent access, mapping the weakness to CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for a Critical Function) and CWE-1327 (Binding to an Unrestricted IP Address), with a reported CVSS v3.1 score of 6.5 (Medium). A configuration endpoint also accepts cross-origin requests without a CORS preflight (CWE-352; 6.5 Medium), while the persistent-memory sink stores content without enforcing its stated restrictions. A source review of 59 public repositories identifies missing authentication in 10 of 11 source-verifiable genuine applications, or 11 of 11 including a framework-default case. These findings indicate recurrence within the sampled repositories, not prevalence in commercial products. We characterise a deployment gap between developer-oriented network assumptions and consumer-facing embodied AI security: inference-layer refusal cannot prevent unauthorised changes to model instructions. Potential consequences include surveillance through onboard cameras and microphones and social engineering of nearby users. Proof-of-concept code, evidence and the survey are available at https://bit.ly/reachypi.

llm.title_ja: LLM制御型ソーシャルロボットに対するネットワーク露出型設定攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: LLMを搭載した実ロボットにおいて、認証の欠如や制限のないIPアドレスバインディングに起因する、ネットワークを介した設定変更攻撃の脆弱性を調査し実証した。
llm.problem: embodiedロボットにおけるLLMの採用は、推論にとどまらずセキュリティ上の依存関係や脆弱性をもたらすが、その影響は十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite を対象に、管理インターフェースを介したパーソナリティ設定やクラウドLLMのシステムプロンプトの不正置換を試みる。
llm.result: 設定レイヤーの攻撃パスにより物理ハードウェア上で動作の変更が観測され、公開リポジトリの多くに認証の欠如が存在することが確認された。

2611.22761.tldr_en: A deployment gap between developer-oriented network assumptions and consumer-facing embodied AI security: inference-layer refusal cannot prevent unauthorised changes to model instructions is characterised.

2611.22743.title: Stochastic Diversity Windows: Diagnosing Noise Influence in Robotic Diffusion Sampling
2611.22743.abstract: Diffusion models are increasingly adopted in robotics and control due to their capability to express multiple feasible solutions to a given task. However, the role of stochasticity in the diffusion model-sampler across denoising remains poorly understood. We introduce a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic that tests how changing the sampled noise affects the final output. Across five model-sampler configurations spanning three robotics benchmarks, diverse architectures, domains, and conditioning mechanisms, we reveal highly varied temporal sensitivity profiles, where noise-induced deviations can amplify, partially contract, or undergo near-total attenuation downstream. From these profiles, we define stochastic diversity windows (SDWs): compact intervals that identify where sampler stochasticity has the strongest measured influence on the final output. Guided by these windows, we apply two heuristic interventions: targeted stochastic amplification, which increases sample diversity exploration of the solution space, and an SDW-hybrid sampler, which replaces DDPM steps with DDIM skips in low-impact regions, resulting in network evaluation reductions of up to 40-60% and wall-clock time by up to 85%, with no consistent changes detected in feasibility, cost, or diversity across held-out tasks.

llm.title_ja: 確率的多様性ウィンドウ：ロボット拡散サンプリングにおけるノイズ影響の診断
llm.tldr_ja: 拡散モデルサンプラにおけるサンプリングされたノイズの影響を診断するためのタイムステップごとの反事実的診断手法と、サンプルの多様性と効率を向上させる手法を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボット工学や制御において広く採用されている拡散モデルにおいて、デノイジング中のサンプリング確率性の役割については十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: ノイズによる偏差が増幅、部分的に収縮、または減衰する時間的感度プロファイル（確率的多様性ウィンドウ：SDW）を定義し、それに基づいたターゲットを絞った確率的増幅とSDWハイブリッドサンプラを適用する。
llm.result: ネットワーク評価回数を最大40〜60%、壁時計時間を最大85%削減しつつ、タスクの実行可能性や多様性を維持できることを示した。

2611.22743.tldr_en: A per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic is introduced that tests how changing the sampled noise affects the final output of the diffusion model-sampler across denoising, revealing highly varied temporal sensitivity profiles, where noise-induced deviations can amplify, partially contract, or undergo near-total attenuation downstream.

2611.22738.title: Can Activation Steering Substitute for Prompt-Based Affective Priming in LLM Digital Twins?
2611.22738.abstract: Affective priming -- asking participants to write about a recalled event, such as a time they felt grateful or lacked control, and then measuring the induced state and its spillover onto related judgments -- is a standard way to manipulate emotion in the social sciences, and it also shifts the responses of LLM-based digital twins. The writing task, however, requires generating a full text. We test whether activation steering can replace it. Using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on 100 personas in two domains (gratitude, lack of control), we compare a real-prompt path replicating the original Twin-2K-500 Mega Study (J2) with an injection path that skips the writing and adds a mean-difference direction, extracted from human writing, to the residual stream at varying strengths. The real-prompt effects fall between the original human and digital-twin effects in 5 of 6 comparisons. Injection shifts the manipulation check in a dose-dependent way and matches the real-prompt effect at one strength in the gratitude domain (beta ~ 2.7), but overshoots beyond it, on the proximal measure as well, and asymmetrically across the two directions. A structure-matched No-Injection baseline separates two sources of difference: omitting the writing task raises the proximal measure in both domains, whereas the injected direction itself moves a distal measure in the lack-of-control domain. Substitution is therefore measure-dependent: validity established for one way of inducing a state does not carry over uniformly to another.
2611.22738.comment: Code, generation logs and analysis scripts: https://github.com/JunyiTim/twin-activation-injection

llm.title_ja: 活性化ステアリングはLLMデジタルツインにおけるプロンプトベースの感情プライミングの代わりになるか
llm.tldr_ja: LLMベースのデジタルツインにおいて、長文の記述を伴う感情プライミングの代わりに、活性化ステアリング（表現のベクトル加算）が感情操作の代替手段として機能するかを検証した。
llm.problem: 社会科学の標準的な手法である感情プライミングはLLMの応答を変化させるが、記述タスクのために完全なテキスト生成を必要とする。
llm.method: Llama-3.1-8B-Instructを用い、記述タスクをスキップして人間の書き込みから抽出した平均差分方向のベクトルを残留ストリームに加算する注入パスと、実際のプロンプトパスとを比較する。
llm.result: 注入は用量依存的に感情操作のチェックを変化させるが、過剰補正やドメイン間の非対称性が見られ、代替の有効性は測定方法に依存することが示された。

2611.22738.tldr_en: This work compares a real-prompt path replicating the original Twin-2K-500 Mega Study with an injection path that skips the writing and adds a mean-difference direction, extracted from human writing, to the residual stream at varying strengths, and finds the real-prompt effects fall between the original human and digital-twin effects in 5 of 6 comparisons.

2611.22736.title: RefCloth: Transferable Adversarial Tablecloths for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.22736.abstract: Closed-loop vision-language-action (VLA) policies rely continuously on multi-view cameras, yet existing visual attacks typically hijack sensor streams with 2D patches or alter target object meshes that require retraining when manipulation objects change. We introduce RefCloth, a framework that optimizes one persistent adversarial tablecloth on a frozen source policy and deploys it zero-shot across unseen tasks and target models without modifying task objects or cameras. Throughout manipulation, static third-person and moving wrist views observe this shared world-bound texture under evolving occlusions. To generalize across shifting surface views while bridging the gap between differentiable and native renderers, RefCloth combines bounded texture parameterization with shared surface UV transformations and a same-path clean reference that removes static rendering offsets at initialization. Across four LIBERO suites in native simulation, one frozen texture transfers from OpenVLA-OFT to $π_0$ and $π_{0.5}$, reducing success relative to an unoptimized cloth by 62.50 and 43.75 percentage points on average and far exceeding amplitude- and variation-matched random controls. Dual-view audits and target closed-loop camera interventions show that moving wrist exposure drives over twice the standalone drop of the main view with strong synergy, while ablations confirm the roles of UV diversification and path calibration.

llm.title_ja: RefCloth: 視覚言語行動モデルのための転移可能な敵対的テーブルクロス
llm.tldr_ja: タスクオブジェクトやカメラを変更することなく、未見のタスクやターゲットモデルへゼロショットでデプロイ可能な、固定された単一の敵対的テーブルクロス最適化フレームワーク「RefCloth」を提案する。
llm.problem: 閉ループVLAポリシーはマルチビューカメラに依存しているが、既存の視覚的攻撃は2Dパッチやターゲットオブジェクトのメッシュ変更を必要とし、変更のたびに再学習が必要となる。
llm.method: 境界付きテクスチャパラメータ化、共有表面UV変換、初期化時の静的レンダリングオフセットを除外するクリーンリファレンスを組み合わせることで、多様な表面ビューへの汎化を図る。
llm.result: LIBEROスイートのシミュレーションにおいて、最適化されていないクロスと比較して成功率を大幅に低下させ、敵対的攻撃としての有効性を示した。

2611.22736.tldr_en: RefCloth is introduced, a framework that optimizes one persistent adversarial tablecloth on a frozen source policy and deploys it zero-shot across unseen tasks and target models without modifying task objects or cameras.

2611.22722.title: Practice in Text, Act in Pixels: Correcting Where Perception Fails
2611.22722.abstract: GUI agents can learn cheaply from a text view of an interface and act on screenshots through a vision-language screen reader. Yet on a simulated mobile platform with a low-cost reader, policies that complete most tasks in text fail on many of the same tasks on screenshots. We ask where a small budget of real screenshots is best spent to close this gap. We find that the reader's misreads are systematic and recur on the same interface elements. Noise matched to the reader's error rates, a natural sim-to-real remedy, misses this structure, and in a pre-specified comparison it did not beat training the policy directly on screenshots. We therefore correct the misreads at their source with reader alignment, which fine-tunes the reader on screenshots paired with their text views. The reader learns to output each screen's text view, as in text practice, and the policy stays unchanged. Spent on the reader, the screenshot budget gives 80.9% full-task success on new task instances, against 55.6% when spent on training the policy. Given the same labeled screenshots, adapting the reader also beats adapting the policy, and a single aligned reader improves every text-trained policy we tried without retraining any of them.
2611.22722.comment: 25 pages, 8 figures, 19 tables. Code: https://github.com/Carlxuzhl/practice-in-text ; aligned reader: https://huggingface.co/xuzhl/practice-in-text-aligned-reader

llm.title_ja: テキストで練習し、ピクセルで行動する：知覚が失敗する箇所の修正
llm.tldr_ja: スクリーンショットとテキストビューのペアを用いてGUIエージェントのテキストリーダーを微調整することで、スクリーンショット上でのタスク成功率を効率的に向上させる手法を提案する。
llm.problem: GUIエージェントはテキストビューで安価に学習しスクリーンショットで行動できるが、低コストのスクリーンリーダーを使用したポリシーはスクリーンショット上で失敗しやすい。
llm.method: スクリーンショットとそのテキストビューのペアでリーダーを微調整する「リーダーアライメント」により、ポリシー自体を変更せずにリーダー側の誤読を修正する。
llm.result: 限られたスクリーンショットの予算をリーダーの適応に費やすことで、新しいタスクインスタンスで80.9%のフルタスク成功率を達成し、ポリシーの直接訓練を上回った。
keywords_ja: リーダーアライメント

2611.22722.tldr_en: It is found that the reader's misreads are systematic and recur on the same interface elements, and a natural sim-to-real remedy, misses this structure, and in a pre-specified comparison it did not beat training the policy directly on screenshots.

2611.22713.title: Body Schema Policy: Body as the Vision-Action Interface for Efficient Robot Loco-Manipulation
2611.22713.abstract: Currently, robots can learn whole-body loco-manipulation through scale: the strongest policies have billions of parameters and still need task-specific fine-tuning. Humans have limited processing capacity, yet learn and act efficiently through a body schema that organizes what they see and how they move. We introduce Body Schema Policy (BSP), an imitation learning policy that builds such a schema into the vision-action interface. Its latent body schema places joint and link tokens on the robot's kinematic tree, where learned screw motions carry features between links. Through body-queried vision, each body part retrieves its own visual evidence, which conditions the denoising of its actions. With this inductive bias, BSP returns an action chunk faster than any policy we compare. Compact, body-specific visual readouts also emerge without spatial supervision: manipulation commands depend strongly on task objects, while locomotion commands respond more broadly to the scene. On nine simulated Unitree G1 whole-body tasks, BSP matches the $Ψ_0$ humanoid foundation model with $75\times$ fewer parameters and nearly doubles Diffusion Policy's success. The same holds on a real G1 and a Fetch mobile manipulator.

llm.title_ja: ボディスキーマポリシー：効率的なロボットの全身ロコ・マニピュレーションのためのビジョン・アクションインターフェースとしての身体
llm.tldr_ja: 関節やリンクのトークンを運動学的ツリー上に配置する潜在的ボディスキーマをビジョン・アクションインターフェースに組み込んだ模倣学習ポリシー「BSP」を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットの全身ロコ・マニピュレーションの学習には大規模なパラメータが必要であり、タスク特有の微調整が依然として必要である。
llm.method: 身体固有の視覚的読出しを用いて自身の視覚的証拠を取得し、アクションのデノイジングを条件付けるボディスキーマポリシー（BSP）を構築する。
llm.result: 9つのシミュレーションされた全身タスクにおいて、パラメータ数が75倍少ないにもかかわらず、ヒューマノイド基礎モデル $Ψ_0$ に匹敵し、Diffusion Policyの成功率をほぼ倍増させた。
keywords_ja: ロコ・マニピュレーション

2611.22713.tldr_en: Body Schema Policy (BSP), an imitation learning policy that builds such a body schema into the vision-action interface, and matches the $\Psi_0$ humanoid foundation model with $75\times$ fewer parameters and nearly doubles Diffusion Policy's success.

2611.22695.title: Learning Accurate End-Effector Trajectory Tracking with Inertial Feedback for a Quadruped Manipulator
2611.22695.abstract: Accurate end-effector trajectory tracking on quadruped manipulators is challenging because uncertainties in actuators, foot-ground contact, and geometric errors are propagated through the leg-arm kinematic chain. Detecting such errors requires sensing beyond joint encoders that can capture the effects of these uncertainties on the robot's motion, since joint encoders only provide measurements at the actuated joints and cannot fully observe mechanical errors such as backlash, dimensional inaccuracies, or structural deformation. This work addresses these challenges using a reinforcement learning framework with end-effector (EE) inertial feedback, targeting local high-accuracy manipulation while maintaining a nominal body pose and support configuration without intentional body motion or foot repositioning. The learned policy uses EE inertial measurements to compensate for tracking errors induced by uncertainties throughout the leg-arm system that cannot be fully inferred from proprioception alone. Simulation and real-world experiments on continuous EE trajectory tracking show overall improvements relative to nominal and proprioception-only baselines.
