In real-world experiments, the proposed policy reduces the MoCap-based RMSE by 17.3% and 28.0% relative to the nominal baseline under the two in-distribution (ID) command conditions, respectively, and by an additional 12.6% and 15.9% relative to the proprioception-only baseline. Furthermore, the trajectory-wise RMSE between FK-reconstructed and motion-capture-measured end-effector positions averaged 12.61+-2.15mm (mean+-standard deviation) across 24 controller-trajectory combinations, revealing a substantial discrepancy between nominal kinematic reconstruction and measured end-effector motion.

llm.title_ja: 四脚マニピュレータのための慣性フィードバックを用いた高精度エンドエフェクタ軌道追従の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 四脚マニピュレータの不確かさに起因する追従誤差を補償するため、エンドエフェクタの慣性フィードバックを用いた強化学習フレームワークを提案し、シミュレーションと実機実験で追従精度の向上の改善を示した。
llm.problem: アクチュエータや接地の不確かさ、幾何学誤差が運動連鎖を伝播し、高精度な軌道追従が困難であること。
llm.method: エンドエフェクタの慣性測定値を用いて関節固有受容感覚だけでは推論できない誤差を補償する強化学習フレームワークの適用。
llm.result: 実機実験において、2つのIDコマンド条件下で名目ベースラインと比較してMoCapベースのRMSEをそれぞれ17.3%および28.0%削減した。

2611.22695.tldr_en: This work uses a reinforcement learning framework with end-effector (EE) inertial feedback, targeting local high-accuracy manipulation while maintaining a nominal body pose and support configuration without intentional body motion or foot repositioning, to compensate for tracking errors induced by uncertainties throughout the leg-arm system.

2611.22691.title: Making the World React Realistically: A Closed-Loop Interactive World Model for Autonomous Driving
2611.22691.abstract: World models (WMs) generate driving scenarios beyond recorded logs, enabling the training and evaluation of autonomous driving systems in unseen interactions. However, existing WMs struggle to ensure both behavioral realism and visual fidelity, since they overlook the relationship between vehicle interactions and the ego visual observations. We propose a closed-loop interactive WM that couples behavior modeling and visual rendering. First, imitation-learned background-vehicle (BV) policies are fine-tuned with multi-agent reinforcement learning in the closed loop against an end-to-end ego planner that reacts to the rendered images, so that their interaction behaviors match those in real logs. Second, the viewpoints exposed by these interactions guide a per-Gaussian diagnosis of each 3D Gaussian vehicle asset, which attenuates view-dependent colors on under-observed Gaussians and fills never-observed surfaces with generated Gaussians, while preserving the observed appearance. Third, signal lights are rendered according to the driving intentions of the vehicles, by an editor that learns the light states unobserved for a vehicle through counterfactual fine-tuning with a light-state classifier. On long-tail closed-loop scenarios, our method reduces the divergence from real-world interaction behaviors by 85% and improves novel-view vehicle PSNR by 2.0dB over the state-of-the-art WM. The significance of BV light signaling in WMs is shown, as the rendered signal lights conveying BV driving intentions indirectly impact ego driving behaviors in a quarter of the scenarios.

llm.title_ja: 世界を現実的に反応させる：自動運転のための閉ループ対話型世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 行動モデリングと視覚的レンダリングを結合した閉ループ対話型世界モデルを提案し、長期的な閉ループシナリオにおいて現実世界の相互作用行動からの乖離を85%削減し、新視点車両のPSNRを向上させた。
llm.problem: 既存の世界モデルは、車両の相互作用とエゴの視覚的観測の関係を無視しているため、行動のリアリズムと視覚的忠実度の両立に苦労していること。
llm.method: 模倣学習された背景車両ポリシーを強化学習で微調整し、3Dガウス車両アセットの診断および信号灯のレンダリングと統合する。
llm.result: 長期的な閉ループシナリオにおいて、現実の相互作用行動からの乖離を85%削減し、新視点車両のPSNRを2.0dB改善した。

2611.22691.tldr_en: A closed-loop interactive WM that couples behavior modeling and visual rendering is proposed, which reduces the divergence from real-world interaction behaviors by 85% and improves novel-view vehicle PSNR by 2.0dB over the state-of-the-art WM.

2611.22666.title: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.22666.abstract: Our aim is to accelerate autoregressive vision-language-action models (VLAs), which generate robot actions one token at a time. Speculative decoding makes this possible: a lightweight draft model proposes several tokens at once, and the VLA verifies them in a single pass, accepting only those that match its own predictions, so decoding remains lossless. The speedup, however, is limited in robot control, where many different tokens encode nearly the same motion and a draft close to the correct action is still rejected. To address this, our approach, VSpark, is built upon three design choices: (i) rollouts collected with calibrated action noise, which expose the draft to a wider range of robot states; (ii) feature alignment, which trains the draft to match the VLA's hidden features rather than its output tokens alone; and (iii) continuation reuse, which keeps the predictions the VLA has already computed along rejected drafts as candidates for the next verification step, instead of discarding them. On four VLAs with different action tokenizers and four manipulation benchmarks, VSpark achieves 1.28x to 2.10x speedup while keeping the VLA's decoding lossless.

llm.title_ja: VSpark：自己回帰型ビジョン・言語・アクションモデルのための推測デコーディング
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット制御における推測デコーディングの制限を克服するため、較正されたノイズによるロールアウト、特徴アライメント、継続の再利用を導入し、VLAモデルのデコーディングをロスレスのまま1.28倍から2.10倍に高速化した。
llm.problem: ロボット制御では異なるトークンがほぼ同じ動作をエンコードするため、推測デコーディングのスピードアップが制限されること。
llm.method: 較正された行動ノイズを用いたロールアウト、特徴アライメント、および拒否されたドラフトの予測を維持する継続再利用を組み合わせたVSparkの導入。
llm.result: 4つの異なるVLAと4つのマニピュレータベンチマークにおいて、VLAのデコーディングをロスレスに維持したまま1.28倍から2.10倍の高速化を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクション

2611.22666.tldr_en: The aim is to accelerate autoregressive vision-language-action models (VLAs), which generate robot actions one token at a time, by building upon three design choices: rollouts collected with calibrated action noise, feature alignment, and continuation reuse, which keeps the predictions the VLA has already computed along rejected drafts as candidates for the next verification step, instead of discarding them.
2611.22666.hf_summary_en: VSpark accelerates autoregressive vision-language-action models by improving speculative decoding with calibrated action-noise rollouts, hidden-feature alignment, and reuse of rejected-draft continuations, achieving lossless 1.28x–2.10x speedups across multiple robot manipulation tasks.

2611.22654.title: Risk Density RRT$^*$: Planning in the Space of Probability
2611.22654.abstract: Planning under uncertainty is a fundamental problem in robotics. While much of the literature seeks minimum-cost paths subject to probabilistic constraints, this paper instead considers collision probability, or risk classically defined as probability times severity, directly as the planning objective. We propose Risk Density RRT$^*$ (RD-RRT$^*$), an extension of RRT$^*$ for high-level planning in environments with deterministic and uncertain obstacles. RD-RRT$^*$ builds on Risk Density, a functional that evaluates a continuous path as a whole and provides a tractable approximation of its collision probability. The framework also supports severity-weighted risk and a hybrid variant that adds a path-length penalty, balancing risk and geometric efficiency while regularizing exploration in low-density regions. We validate the method across a wide range of scenarios. The results show that RD-RRT$^*$ consistently finds paths with lower estimated collision probability by optimizing a global risk-based objective. We further demonstrate the fidelity of the underlying approximation through Monte Carlo simulations. Finally, we discuss how the topological structure induced by Risk Density may provide a useful representation of the environment and offer insights into risk-aware planning.
2611.22654.comment: Accepted for publication in The International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR)

llm.title_ja: リスク密度RRT$^*$：確率空間における計画
llm.tldr_ja: 衝突確率やリスクを直接計画の目的関数として考慮するRRT$^*$の拡張であるRisk Density RRT$^*$（RD-RRT$^*$）を提案し、決定的および不確実な障害物がある環境で一貫して低い衝突確率の経路を発見することを示した。
llm.problem: 不確実性下での計画において、従来の多くは確率的制約の下で最小コスト経路を探索することであること。
llm.method: 連続パス全体を評価し衝突確率の近似を提供するRisk Densityを利用したRRT$^*$の拡張（RD-RRT$^*$）の提案。
llm.result: 大半のシナリオで、大域的なリスクベースの目的関数を最適化することにより、推定衝突確率が低い経路を一貫して発見した。

2611.22654.tldr_en: RRT-RRT is proposed, an extension of RRT that builds on Risk Density, a functional that evaluates a continuous path as a whole and provides a tractable approximation of its collision probability, and shows that RD-RRT consistently finds paths with lower estimated collision probability by optimizing a global risk-based objective.

2611.22625.title: VLM-guided Grounding Expert for Generalised Referring Expression Comprehension
2611.22625.abstract: Generalised referring expression comprehension (GREC) aims to identify and localise the zero, one or multiple objects referred to by a language expression. In robotic manipulation, grounding also needs to remain accurate when requests for the same objects are paraphrased or embedded in additional context in robotics. However, grounding expert models are sensitive to instruction variation, while generative vision--language models (VLMs) struggle with complete target recovery and rejection of absent targets. These complementary limitations motivate combining the contextual representations of VLMs with the direct spatial prediction capabilities of grounding experts. We therefore introduce VLM-guided Grounding Expert (VGE), which combines a frozen VLM with a trainable grounding expert through layerwise joint attention and text-conditioned instance scoring. These interfaces leverage multimodal understanding of the VLM to guide object-query refinement and candidate selection while retaining direct bounding-box prediction. Across three datasets, VGE achieves the highest averaged F1 score among the evaluated methods on all five test splits, with differences of at most 1.2 percentage points across instruction conditions within each split. On the dataset with robotic scenes, VGE also achieves the highest F1 across instruction variants and no-target, single-target and multiple-target cases. VGE provides a $5.3$--$13.0\times$ inference speedup over the baseline with the same VLM base model. These results support combining VLM context with specialised spatial prediction to address both grounding challenges, with particularly strong performance in robotic scenes. Code will be released upon publication.

llm.title_ja: 一般化された指示表現理解のためのVLM誘導型グラウンディング専門家
llm.tldr_ja: VLMの文脈理解とグラウンディング専門家の直接的な空間予測能力を組み合わせたVGEを提案し、3つのデータセットですべてのテスト分割において最も高い平均F1スコアを達成した。
llm.problem: グラウンディング専門家モデルは指示の変動に敏感であり、生成型VLMは完全なターゲットの回収や不在ターゲットの拒否に苦労すること。
llm.method: 凍結されたVLMと訓練可能なグラウンディング専門家を、層ごとの結合アテンションとテキスト条件付きインスタンススコアリングによって組み合わせるVGEの導入。
llm.result: 3つのデータセットにおいて、すべてのテスト分割で最も高い平均F1スコアを達成し、ベースラインと比較して5.3〜13.0倍の推論高速化を実現した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22625.tldr_en: VLM-guided Grounding Expert (VGE), which combines a frozen VLM with a trainable grounding expert through layerwise joint attention and text-conditioned instance scoring, supports combining VLM context with specialised spatial prediction to address both grounding challenges, with particularly strong performance in robotic scenes.

2611.22609.title: Task Convergent Flow Matching for Generative Robotics
2611.22609.abstract: Successful manipulation requires the manipulated objects to progress toward a desired task outcome. Generative policies can produce plausible robot motions without ensuring this progress, allowing successive action chunks to stall or undo earlier changes to the scene. We introduce a task-centric inference-time refinement framework for flow matching policies that evaluates candidate action chunks through parallel physics-based rollouts and searches for motions satisfying sufficient conditions for task convergence. Task-level performance funnels bound temporary regressions while requiring net progress over each chunk. We establish sufficient conditions under which repeated funnel satisfaction yields convergence throughout execution, and use interval-wise Lipschitz bounds to verify continuous-time funnel satisfaction from sampled rollouts. To accommodate contact-rich hybrid dynamics, we refine the flow's source seeds using derivative-free Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES), constrained to radial quantile bands of the source distribution to help retain the learned motion prior. This formulation supports both Euclidean and pose-valued Riemannian Flow Matching (RMFM) policies. On PushT and three-cube stacking, refinement raises success from 31.3% to 88.5% and from 77.0% to 86.0%. On PushT, whose coverage score responds continuously to the motion of the block, a learned funnel lowers the average maximum loss of achieved progress by 19% relative to constraining the endpoint of each chunk alone, at a similar success rate. With the radial band, 11.3% of the executed motion windows are out of distribution, a rate within the range of held-out demonstrations, compared with 34.1% for an unconstrained search.

llm.title_ja: 生成ロボティクスに向けたタスク収束型フローマッチング
llm.tldr_ja: タスクの進行を保証するための推論時リファインメントフレームワークを提案し、PushTおよび3キューブ積み上げにおいて成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 生成ポリシーは適切なロボット動作を生成できるものの、タスクの進行を保証せず、シーンの変更を停滞させたり台無しにしたりすること。
llm.method: 並列物理ベースのロールアウトを通じて候補行動チャンクを評価し、タスク収束のための十分条件を満たす動きを探索するタスク中心の推論時リファインメントフレームワークの導入。
llm.result: PushTおよび3キューブ積み上げにおいて、リファインメントにより成功率がそれぞれ31.3%から88.5%へ、77.0%から86.0%へ向上した。
keywords_ja: 推論時リファインメント

2611.22609.tldr_en: A task-centric inference-time refinement framework for flow matching policies that evaluates candidate action chunks through parallel physics-based rollouts and searches for motions satisfying sufficient conditions for task convergence is introduced.

2611.22592.title: Distilling World Action Models for Efficient Bimanual Manipulation via Anchored Path Matching
2611.22592.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly generate future video and robot actions through iterative denoising. Few-step distillation reduces the number of model evaluations, but its coarse updates can move the student away from the teacher's trajectory. We propose Anchored Path Matching (APM), which supervises endpoint and short-transition predictions from states reached by the student. From each state, we continue the teacher to zero noise and use its endpoint and first intermediate state as targets. Modality-routed adapters learn to match both targets from the same starting state. When the two gradients conflict, anchor-priority updates preserve the endpoint gradient and remove the opposing component of the local gradient within each modality. One checkpoint supports 1-, 2-, and 4-step joint generation. The sampling budget can be chosen at deployment without retraining or teacher queries. On RoboTwin 2.0, we train only on Clean demonstrations and evaluate directly on the domain-randomized Random setting. At one step, APM improves closed-loop success over continued base distillation at matched inference budgets by 2.0 percentage points on Clean and 1.4 on Random. Video peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) rises from 30.169 to 32.317 dB, with gains in structural similarity (SSIM) and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS). On two real-robot tasks, APM improves success over the one-step teacher and reduces control-cycle latency by $21.3\times$ relative to the eight-step teacher.Project page: https://jialonglong.github.io/Anchored-Path-Matching/.

llm.title_ja: アンカードパスマッチングによる効率的な両手操作のための世界アクションモデルの蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: エンドポイントと短い遷移の予測を教師から監督するアンカードパスマッチング（APM）を提案し、ロボットの閉ループ成功率を向上させつつ制御サイクルの遅延を削減した。
llm.problem: 世界アクションモデル（WAMs）の数ステップの蒸留では、粗い更新によってスチューデントが教師の軌道から外れてしまうこと。
llm.method: スチューデントが到達した状態からのエンドポイントと最初の中間状態をターゲットとし、モダリティルーテッドアダプターとアンカー優先更新を用いたAPMの提案。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0において、1ステップでの閉ループ成功率が改善し、2実機タスクにおいて1ステップ教師を上回り、8ステップ教師に比べ遅延を21.3倍削減した。
keywords_ja: 世界アクションモデル

2611.22592.tldr_en: Anchored Path Matching (APM), which supervises endpoint and short-transition predictions from states reached by the student and improves success over the one-step teacher and reduces control-cycle latency by $21.3\times relative to the eight-step teacher.

2611.22584.title: InteractVLA: Turning VLAs into Interactive Tools for Agentic Robotic Manipulation
2611.22584.abstract: Existing agentic manipulation systems treat pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies as opaque, language-only primitives: when a policy call fails under unfamiliar instructions or scene perturbations, the agent cannot steer its behavior and is forced into futile retries or costly manual takeover. We present InteractVLA, a framework that turns pretrained flow-based VLAs into geometrically steerable and inspectable tools through a bidirectional geometric interface with vision-language agents. In the forward direction, test-time geometric guidance translates an agent-specified end-effector target into input gradients through the action expert via a differentiable command-to-pose mapping, while soft-time target alignment treats arrival time as a latent execution index to match the target pose without distorting the policy's approach motion. In the reverse direction, action-informed agentic refinement exposes generated action chunks and calibrated camera reprojections back to the agent, allowing it to diagnose spatial discrepancies, revise targets for subsequent VLA calls, or locally adjust motion segments on top of the guided trajectory. Making the VLA controllable not only boosts online agentic tool use, but also unlocks effective recursive self-improvement (RSI), achieving state-of-the-art performance of 99.4\% on LIBERO-Plus, 48.62\% on RoboDojo, and 89.4\% on RoboCasa365. Project page: https://lingwupro.github.io/InteractVLA/.

llm.title_ja: InteractVLA：VLAをエージェント型ロボット操作のための対話型ツールに変える
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みのフローベースVLAを、視覚言語エージェントとの双方向幾何学的インターフェースを通じて幾何学的に誘導・検査可能なツールに変換するフレームワークInteractVLAを提案し、多様なベンチマークで最先端の性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 既存のエージェント型操作システムは、事前学習済みVLAポリシーを不透明な言語専用プリミティブとして扱い、未知の指示等で失敗した際にエージェントが行動を制御できないこと。
llm.method: 微分可能なコマンドからポーズへのマッピングを通じたテスト時の幾何学的誘導と、生成された行動チャンクをエージェントに公開する行動情報に基づくエージェント的洗練の組み合わせ。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plusで99.4%、RoboDojoで48.62%、RoboCasa365で89.4%という最先端の性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語エージェント

2611.22584.tldr_en: InteractVLA is presented, a framework that turns pretrained flow-based VLAs into geometrically steerable and inspectable tools through a bidirectional geometric interface with vision-language agents and unlocks effective recursive self-improvement (RSI).

2611.23347.title: SurgCBVR: A Multi-Domain Benchmark for Content-Based Surgical Video-to-Video Retrieval
2611.23347.abstract: Hospitals record thousands of hours of surgical video annually, yet these archives remain difficult to search by content. Surgeons cannot readily retrieve similar operations, complications, or workflow events. Existing surgical computer vision primarily produces labels rather than retrieving relevant videos. We introduce SurgCBVR, the first benchmark for content-based video-to-video retrieval in surgery. It integrates eight public datasets across four domains-ophthalmic, laparoscopic, robotic-assisted, and colonoscopy-covering six procedure types, 679 cases, and 76,489 clips (106 hours). SurgCBVR comprises two tiers: Scene, retrieving the same operative state across cases and sites, and Workflow, retrieving and localizing phase transitions and deviations. Scene includes 74,765 clips spanning 40 classes, three temporal granularities, and three playback speeds; Workflow contains 1,724 transition clips. Fixed clip lengths and frame counts, together with phase-classifier oracle and duration-only baselines, help assess label and timing shortcuts. We evaluate six generic and surgical foundation models, two video retrieval methods, and contrastive heads trained on SurgCBVR, using within-dataset, cross-dataset, and pooled-gallery retrieval restricted to the same procedure type. Frozen representations barely outperform a timing-only baseline, transition retrieval approaches chance, and trained heads lose up to half their accuracy across datasets. These findings expose substantial limitations in current video representations and establish SurgCBVR as a benchmark for advancing surgery-aware retrieval.

llm.title_ja: SurgCBVR：コンテンツベースの手術ビデオ対ビデオ検索のためのマルチドメインベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: コンテンツベースの手術ビデオ検索の初のベンチマークであるSurgCBVRを提案し、複数ドメインのデータセット統合と評価を通じて現状のビデオ表現の限界を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 病院の膨大な手術ビデオアーカイブは内容による検索が困難であり、既存のコンピュータビジョン手法はラベル付けに偏っている。
llm.method: 4ドメインの8つの公開データセットを統合し、シーンとワークフローの2つの階層を持つ初の検索ベンチマークSurgCBVRを構築した。
llm.result: 凍結された表現はタイミングのみのベースラインを辛うじて上回る程度であり、訓練済みヘッドはデータセット間で精度が最大半分低下した。
llm.limitation: 現在のビデオ表現には大幅な限界があり、手術認識型検索の高度化に向けた課題が浮き彫りになった。

2611.23347.tldr_en: This work introduces SurgCBVR, the first benchmark for content-based video-to-video retrieval in surgery, and establishes SurgCBVR as a benchmark for advancing surgery-aware retrieval.

2611.22543.title: JointGV: Structure-Aware Correction of Visual World Models with Parallel Graph Dynamics for Long-Horizon Modeling
2611.22543.abstract: Visual world models predict future visual states conditioned on actions, but recursive errors in entity poses and spatial relations limit their long-horizon prediction for robot planning and control. We ask whether a separately predicted relational state can correct this drift without restructuring the visual model. This is challenging because graph nodes and visual states share neither elements nor a feature space. We propose Joint Graph--Visual Dynamics Correction (JointGV), a plug-in based on a cross-granularity dynamics hypothesis: despite their different representations, graph-node and visual-state changes describe the same physical transition. JointGV rolls out a task-conditioned scene graph alongside the visual world model, couples their predicted changes, and combines the resulting graph-motion context with graph-predicted node positions to compute a bounded residual. Graph-learning and correction gradients do not propagate into the original visual dynamics. We attach JointGV to DINO-WM (spatial tokens) and DreamerV3 (a global latent state), evaluating both on DMC Cheetah Run and Walker Walk across three seeds and extending the evaluation to contact-rich manipulation with DMC Finger Turn Hard. Across 32-step rollouts, JointGV improves structural and visual-prediction accuracy, reducing joint-position error by 11--28\%. For spatial tokens, learned graph--visual change coupling gives lower error than broadcasting the same mean graph-motion context to every token, particularly when non-adjacent parts appear close together in the image. On real-robot inverted-pendulum sequences, JointGV reduces DINO-WM's 32-step pole-angle error from $12.56^\circ$ to $6.69^\circ$ and improves DreamerV3 and LeWorldModel as well. In simulated inverted-pendulum control, an actor trained with JointGV-corrected rollouts completes 46 of 50 episodes, compared with none using the original rollouts.

llm.title_ja: 長期モデリングのための並列グラフダイナミクスを用いた視覚的世界モデルの構造認識型補正
llm.tldr_ja: グラフノードと視覚的状態の変化が同じ物理的遷移を記述するという仮説に基づき、視覚的世界モデルとタスク条件付きシーングラフを結合するJointGVを提案し、長期予測誤差を削減した。
llm.problem: 視覚的世界モデルは将来の視覚状態を予測するが、エンティティのポーズや空間関係における再帰的エラーがロボット計画・制御の長期予測を制限すること。
llm.method: ビジュアルワールドモデルと並行してタスク条件付きシーングラフを展開し、予測された変化を結合して有界残差を計算するJointGVの導入。
llm.result: 32ステップの展開において、構造的および視覚的予測精度が向上し、関節位置誤差が11〜28%減少し、実機の振り子実験でも角度誤差を大幅に削減した。

2611.22543.tldr_en: Joint Graph--Visual Dynamics Correction (JointGV), a plug-in based on a cross-granularity dynamics hypothesis: despite their different representations, graph-node and visual-state changes describe the same physical transition.

2611.22532.title: DGF-Asym: Adaptive Peer Weighting for Collective Estimation under Noisy and Faulty Sensing
2611.22532.abstract: Collective estimation under unreliable sensing requires robots to adaptively balance personal observations and social information from peers. We propose DGF-Asym, a decentralized collective estimation method extending the DeGroot-Friedkin model with asymmetric peer weighting based on retrospective predictive performance. The method supports consensus formation without prior sensor-noise statistics or explicit fault models while keeping inter-robot communication asynchronous. We evaluate DGF-Asym in simulated collective navigation under noisy observations and time-varying sensor faults. Compared with three baselines, it produces more stable estimates and more reliably sustains the decision criterion, at the cost of longer decision times. However, overall performance depends on fault ratio, group size, and influence-threshold selection. Our results demonstrate the potential of adaptive peer weighting for stable model-free collective estimation under unreliable sensing.

llm.title_ja: DGF-Asym：ノイズと故障のあるセンシング下での集合推定のための適応型ピア重み付け
llm.tldr_ja: DeGroot-Friedkinモデルを拡張し、過去の予測性能に基づく非対称なピア重み付けを用いた分散型集合推定手法DGF-Asymを提案し、シミュレーションにより安定した推定的特徴を確認した。
llm.problem: 信頼性の低いセンシング下での集合推定において、ロボットが個人の観察と他者からの社会的高情報を適応的にバランスさせる必要があること。
llm.method: 過去の予測性能に基づく非対称なピア重み付けを用いてDeGroot-Friedkinモデルを拡張したDGF-Asymの提案。
llm.result: 3つのベースラインと比較して、より安定した推定量生成と決定基準のより確実な維持を達成したが、決定時間が長くなるトレードオフがあった。

2611.22532.tldr_en: DGF-Asym is proposed, a decentralized collective estimation method extending the DeGroot-Friedkin model with asymmetric peer weighting based on retrospective predictive performance that supports consensus formation without prior sensor-noise statistics or explicit fault models while keeping inter-robot communication asynchronous.

2611.22518.title: The Multivariate Feedback Particle Filter for State-dependent Multiplicative Noises and Its Application to Attitude and Pose Estimations
2611.22518.abstract: Nonlinear filtering with state-dependent multiplicative measurement noise poses a notable challenge for spacecraft attitude determination and robotic pose estimation. This work develops the FPF-DM, a decomposition scheme for feedback particle filters tailored to this family of filtering problems. Extending prior decomposition techniques for additive noise and polynomial measurement models, the proposed method resolves the key difficulty that state-dependent multiplicative noise breaks the polynomial assumption and prevents Hermite spectral backward recursion for the weighted Poisson's equation. By measure transformation and importance reweighting, we incorporate the inverse measurement covariance into particle weights and rescale the feedback gain to restore the polynomial-form Poisson's equation, with the decomposition generalized to non-uniformly weighted mixtures for closed-form gain computation. This general FPF-DM is instantiated on quaternion and dual-quaternion manifolds for attitude tracking and point-cloud registration. Simulations on 4D attitude tracking and 8D point-cloud registration verify that the instantiated filters using only 10 particles achieve superior accuracy and computational performance relative to baseline filters.

llm.title_ja: 状態依存の乗法ノイズに対する多変量フィードバック粒子フィルタとその姿勢およびポーズ推定への応用
llm.tldr_ja: 状態依存の乗法測定ノイズを持つ非線形フィルタリングの困難を解決するため、フィードバック粒子フィルタの分解スキームFPF-DMを開発し、シミュレーションにより優れた精度と計算性能を確認した。
llm.problem: 状態依存の乗法測定ノイズを持つ非線形フィルタリングが、宇宙機の姿勢決定やロボットのポーズ推定において大きな課題となっていること。
llm.method: 測定共分散を粒子ウェイトに組み込みフィードバックゲインを再スケーリングすることで多項式形式のポアソン方程式を復元するFPF-DM分解スキームの開発。
llm.result: わずか10個の粒子を用いた4次元姿勢追跡および8D点群登録のシミュレーションにおいて、ベースラインフィルタと比較して優れた精度と計算性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 非線形フィルタリング

2611.22518.tldr_en: This work develops the FPF-DM, a decomposition scheme for feedback particle filters tailored to this family of filtering problems, which is instantiated on quaternion and dual-quaternion manifolds for attitude tracking and point-cloud registration.

2611.22491.title: Progress Predicts Policy
2611.22491.abstract: A task specifies how the world should change, while a policy specifies what the robot should do. We introduce Progress Predicts Policy (PPP), which learns a language-conditioned scalar field through the commands induced by its differential. We obtain action conditioning by composing a latent progress field with a shared world model and read its action gradient at a fixed reference command. Continuous commands scale this gradient by a learned positive gain, while discrete commands use finite differences of the same scalar. This yields a hybrid policy without a separate action head or iterative search. Fitting demonstration progress values alone does not ensure that action gradients align with expert commands. PPP trains the induced commands by imitation and uses double backpropagation for the continuous gradient readout to shape the field's local control geometry. Demonstration timing calibrates field values on observed states without additional annotation. The continuous readout remains learnable without progress labels but these timing-derived targets support progress monitoring during execution. Experiments in simulated and real robot manipulation show that PPP outperforms behavioral cloning under a shared architecture.

llm.title_ja: 進捗がポリシーを予測する
llm.tldr_ja: 微分によって誘導されるコマンドを通じて言語条件付きスカラー場を学習するProgress Predicts Policy（PPP）を提案し、シミュレーションおよび実ロボットのマニピュレーションにおいて行動クローンよりも優れた性能を示すことを確認した。
llm.problem: タスクは世界の変化を指定するのに対し、ポリシーはロボットの動作を指定するという不一致があること。
llm.method: 潜在的進捗場を共有世界モデルと構成し、固定基準コマンドでその行動勾配を読み取ることで、別のアクションヘッドなしでハイブリッドポリシーを学習するPPPの提案。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実ロボットのマニピュレーション実験において、PPPが共有アーキテクチャ下の行動クローンを上回ることを示した。

2611.22491.tldr_en: Progress Predicts Policy is introduced, which learns a language-conditioned scalar field through the commands induced by its differential through the commands induced by its differential, and outperforms behavioral cloning under a shared architecture.

2611.22483.title: Manufacturing Differential Sparsity: Planner-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient World Model Planning
2611.22483.abstract: JEPA-style latent world models let embodied agents plan toward new goals with model predictive control, but they are still too slow for real-life embodied control: sampling-based MPC repeats predictor inference tens of thousands of times per plan, and even on high-end GPUs one planning step can take tens of seconds. We observe substantial latent locality in this repeated-inference workload: the predictor maps close actions to close latents, and inside a quantized predictor this closeness takes a form that hardware can exploit, differential bit-level sparsity. Unlike an input stream, whose temporal similarity is given, a planner itself decides which candidates it evaluates together, so the planner can choose its own references and, with reference forest sampling, manufacture more sparsity: it couples the sampled action sequences of each group to a shared root, with competitive planning quality. We build the accelerator on the insights of the rich line of bit-level sparsity accelerators and design it and the planner tightly coupled as a single co-design: the planner increases sparsity and exposes structure for hardware scheduling, and the bit-exact hardware effectively uses the sparsity that the planner creates. On three JEPA world models, our co-design is 1.28-1.80x faster than a dense accelerator and uses 38-52% less energy, and it is 1.22-1.58x faster than prior bit-sparse design and uses 16-36% less energy, with the same area. To our knowledge, our planner is the first planner that manufactures differential bit-level sparsity across its candidates and exposes its structure for hardware scheduling, and our co-design is the first algorithm-hardware co-design for JEPA-style world-model planning.

llm.title_ja: 差分スパース性の製造：効率的な世界モデル計画のためのプランナー・ハードウェア共同設計
llm.tldr_ja: JEPAスタイル世界モデルのサンプリングベースMPCにおける推論負荷を軽減するため、プランナー側で差分ビットレベルのスパース性を自ら作り出し専用ハードウェアで処理するアルゴリズム・ハードウェア共同設計を提案し、高速化と省電力化を実現した。
llm.problem: JEPAスタイルの潜在世界モデルを用いたサンプリングベースのMPCは、実生活での組込み制御を行うには推論が数十万回繰り返され、処理が非常に遅いこと。
llm.method: プランナーがサンプリングされた行動配列を共通のルートに結合して自らスパース性を生み出し、ビット正確なハードウェアスケジューリングと密に結合させた共同設計の導入。
llm.result: 3つのJEPA世界モデルにおいて、高密度アクセラレータと比較して1.28〜1.80倍高速で、38〜52%少ないエネルギー消費を達成した。
keywords_ja: ハードウェアアクセラレータ

2611.22483.tldr_en: This planner is the first planner that manufactures differential bit-level sparsity across its candidates and exposes its structure for hardware scheduling, and its co-design is the first algorithm-hardware co-design for JEPA-style world-model planning.

2611.22453.title: VoxelSBFL: Voxel-Level Spectrum-Based Failure Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.22453.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models integrate visual perception, language understanding, and action generation to control robots. Testing these systems produces trajectories and task outcomes, but existing approaches provide limited guidance on using these recorded trajectories to assess subsequent executions or inform policy repair. We conjecture that, for a given policy and task, traversing certain workspace regions is associated with a higher likelihood of failure. To investigate this conjecture, we propose VoxelSBFL, a black-box adaptation of Spectrum-Based Fault Localization (SBFL) in which workspace voxels replace program elements as units of analysis. Recorded tool-center-point (TCP) trajectories provide binary voxel coverage, which is combined with execution outcomes to construct suspiciousness maps using established SBFL formulas. These maps identify failure-associated regions and score unseen trajectories without requiring internal model access. We evaluate 34 spectrum-based techniques across four VLA models using 96,000 Pick-Up trajectories in simulation and compare the leading techniques against eight action- and trajectory-based metrics. VoxelSBFL obtains an overall macro ROC-AUC of 0.704, significantly outperforming state-of-the art baselines. Sensitivity analyses show that performance varies with spatial granularity and training-set size. These findings support spatial spectra for VLA execution assessment and motivate future research on runtime monitoring, self-healing and targeted policy improvement.

llm.title_ja: VoxelSBFL：ビジョン・言語・アクションモデルのためのボクセルレベルスペクトルベース故障予測
llm.tldr_ja: プログラム要素の代わりにワークスペースボクセルを分析単位とするスペクトルベース故障局所化（SBFL）のブラックボックス適応手法VoxelSBFLを提案し、シミュレーションでの検証を通じて優れた故障予測性能を示した。
llm.problem: VLAモデルのテストでは軌道とタスク結果が生成されるが、これらを用いて後続の実行を評価したりポリシー修正に役立てたりするための既存アプローチのガイダンスが限られていること。
llm.method: ツールセンターポイント（TCP）軌道によるバイナリボクセルカバレッジと実行結果を組み合わせ、既存のSBFL式を用いて不審さマップを構築するVoxelSBFLの提案。
llm.result: 34のスペクトルベース手法を4つのVLAモデルの96,000件のピックアップ軌道で評価し、全体で0.704のマクロROC-AUCを達成して既存の最先端ベースラインを大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: スペクトルベース故障局所化

2611.22453.tldr_en: VoxelSBFL is proposed, a black-box adaptation of Spectrum-Based Fault Localization (SBFL) in which workspace voxels replace program elements as units of analysis and obtains an overall macro ROC-AUC of 0.704, significantly outperforming state-of-the art baselines.

2611.22447.title: COAST: Safe Flight Corridor Planner for Fast and Robust Snap Minimized Trajectories
2611.22447.abstract: Current B-Spline trajectory planners face a critical trade-off: they either sacrifice computational speed to maintain strict Safe Flight Corridor (SFC) guarantees, or they abandon hard safety bounds in favor of soft-constraint penalties to achieve real-time performance. We present COAST (Corridor-Optimized Aerially-Safe Trajectories), a B-Spline based, online trajectory planner capable of formulating snap minimized trajectories with SFC guarantees. COAST divides the problem into two stages: an A* based front-end that generates geometrically simple SFCs (represented as a chain of rectangular prisms), and a quadratic programming back-end for control point optimization. To handle the non-convexity of SFC intersections, we leverage the finite support property of B-Splines, to ensure the spline never exits SFC boundaries. The control point optimization incorporates MINVO transforms for kinodynamic bounding, allowing COAST to design non-conservative, dynamically feasible trajectories, while a snap minimization matrix calculation provides flight smoothness. This formulation provides a formal geometric containment guarantee, while ensuring mean trajectory computation times under 5 ms for real-time deployment. We validate our results through high-fidelity simulation experiments. The source code can be found at: https://github.com/byu-magicc/Minimum-Snap-Trajectories
2611.22447.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference (ACC 2027)

llm.title_ja: COAST：高速かつ頑健なスナップ最小化軌道のための安全飛行回廊プランナー
llm.tldr_ja: 安全飛行回廊（SFC）の保証を維持しつつリアルタイム性能を実現するオンラインBスプライン軌道プランナーCOASTを提案し、高品質なシミュレーション実験で有効性を検証した。
llm.problem: 現在のBスプライン軌道プランナーは、厳格な安全飛行回廊（SFC）の保証を維持するために計算速度を犠牲にするか、リアルタイム性能のために安全境界を放棄するという重大なトレードオフがあること。
llm.method: 幾何学的に単純なSFCを生成するA*ベースのフロントエンドと、Bスプラインの有限サポート特性を利用して制御点を最適化する二次計画法バックエンドによる2段階アプローチの採用。
llm.result: 形式的な幾何学的包含保証を提供しながら、リアルタイム展開のために5ms未満の平均軌道計算時間を達成した。

2611.22447.tldr_en: COAST (Corridor-Optimized Aerially-Safe Trajectories), a B-Spline based, online trajectory planner capable of formulating snap minimized trajectories with SFC guarantees, which provides a formal geometric containment guarantee, while ensuring mean trajectory computation times under 5 ms for real-time deployment.

2611.22445.title: Autonomous Track Racing with a Commercially Available Humanoid: System Design and Real-World Deployment
2611.22445.abstract: Learning-based methods now let humanoids run robustly, and they have begun to compete in athletic events. Yet few reports describe a complete autonomous humanoid running system in an actual race, where the robot must follow a lane at a new venue, pace itself within hardware limits, and finish without intervention. We report such a system deployed on the Unitree G1, a commercially available general-purpose humanoid, in the 100 m, 400 m, and 1500 m events of the World Humanoid Robot Games 2026. The system integrates vision-based lane perception, path tracking, and a running policy trained by reinforcement learning with a human motion prior. To address the challenges of humanoid running, we stabilize head-camera images against body motion and use IMU-assisted leg odometry to bridge flight phases. To manage motor heating, we penalize hip-pitch torque during training, add heat-dissipation plates, and apply temperature-based speed limiting with event-specific pacing. The robot placed 13th of 74 in the 100 m, 10th of 44 in the 400 m first round before falling in the semifinal, and seventh of 35 in the 1500 m. In this deployment, thermal margin set the pace in every event, and the semifinal fall followed a lane-detection error.
2611.22445.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Practice. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

llm.title_ja: 市販の人型ロボットによる自律型トラックレース：システム設計と実世界展開
llm.tldr_ja: 市販の汎用人型ロボットUnitree G1に、視覚ベースのレーン認識、パタートラッキング、強化学習による走行ポリシーを統合したシステムを実装し、実際のレース競技（100m、400m、1500m）で完走および成果を収めた。
llm.problem: 新しい会場でのレーン追従、ハードウェア制限内でのペース配分、介入なしでの完走を必要とする実際のレースにおいて、完全な自律型人型ロボットの走行システムの報告が少ないこと。
llm.method: ヘッドカメラ画像の安定化、IMU補助型レッグオドメトリ、訓練中のヒップピッチトルクのペナルティ付与、放熱プレートや温度ベースの速度制限の統合。
llm.result: 100mで74人中13位、400mで44人中10位、1500mで35人中7位を記録した。
llm.limitation: 熱的マージンが各イベントでのペースを制限し、準決勝での転倒はレーン検出エラーに起因した。

2611.22445.tldr_en: A complete autonomous humanoid running system trained by reinforcement learning with a human motion prior deployed on the Unitree G1 in the 100 m, 400 m, and 1500 m events of the World Humanoid Robot Games 2026, where thermal margin set the pace in every event.

2611.22407.title: ROSMonitoring in Action: Runtime Monitoring and Enforcement for ROS 2 Actions
2611.22407.abstract: Robotic applications often rely on long-running operations, such as navigation, manipulation, and inspection, which in ROS~2 are commonly implemented as actions. Unlike topics and services, actions involve a structured lifecycle comprising goal submission and acceptance, feedback, status updates, result retrieval, and cancellation. Existing versions of ROSMonitoring support topics and services, but do not reconstruct this lifecycle or expose action-level events to a runtime-verification oracle. In this paper, we extend ROSMonitoring with runtime monitoring and enforcement for ROS~2 actions. Actions are declared directly in the monitoring configuration and automatically instrumented through the underlying ROS~2 communication endpoints. The generated monitor reconstructs action-level events, correlates them through goal identifiers, maintains the state of active goals, and translates violations into protocol-aware enforcement operations. These include goal rejection, cancellation, message suppression, and protocol-compliant responses generated directly by the monitor when the original communication cannot be forwarded. We evaluate the implementation through controlled stress tests that vary the number of action invocations, workload size, and clientâserver topology. The results show approximately linear growth in monitoring cost with repeated action invocations under a fixed workload, while larger action workloads and a greater number of configured clientâserver pairs introduce additional overhead. These results characterise the scaling behaviour of the current implementation under the tested sequential workloads while highlighting the main performance limitations of the current synchronous implementation.

llm.title_ja: アクション中のROSMonitoring：ROS 2アクションのためのランタイム監視と強制
llm.tldr_ja: ROS 2のアクションのライフサイクル全体（目標の送信、受付、フィードバック、状態更新、結果取得、キャンセル）を追跡・検証できるようにROSMonitoringを拡張し、制御されたストレステストを通じてスケーリング挙動を評価した。
llm.problem: ROS 2におけるナビゲーションやマニピュレーションなどの長期実行操作がアクションとして実装されているが、既存のROSMonitoringはトピックやサービスのみをサポートしアクションのライフサイクルを公開していないこと。
llm.method: モニタリング設定でアクションを直接宣言し、基盤となるROS 2通信エンドポイントを介して自動的にインストルメント化する仕組みの拡張。
llm.result: 固定ワークロードの下で反復的なアクション呼び出しに対して監視コストがほぼ線形に増加することを示した。
llm.limitation: 現在の同期的実装における主要なパフォーマンスの制限を明らかにしている
keywords_ja: ロボットミドルウェア

2611.22407.tldr_en: ROSMonitoring is extended with runtime monitoring and enforcement for ROS~2 actions, which includes goal rejection, cancellation, message suppression, and protocol-compliant responses generated directly by the monitor when the original communication cannot be forwarded.
2611.22407.venue: Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science

2611.22403.title: BehaVerify: A Formal Verification Tool for Behavior Trees
2611.22403.abstract: This paper presents BehaVerify, a verification toolbox for behavior trees (BTs) and Neuro-Symbolic BTs. BTs are a graphical language for planning and sequencing behaviors - similar to extended state machines - and are increasingly used in safety-critical domains. BehaVerify enables users to specify a BT using a Domain Specific Language (DSL) with formal syntax and semantics. This language further includes Linear Temporal Logic and Computation Tree Logic specifications. BehaVerify uses an efficient encoding into nuXmv, called fastforwarding, to quickly verify if a specification holds over the BT. Additionally, BehaVerify can generate implementations of the BT in Python and Haskell. Through Python, BehaVerify has been integrated with PyTrees and Robot Operating System (ROS) and has been deployed to several autonomous robotic systems, including for verifying runtime monitors. While prior works have developed the underlying theory, this manuscript focuses on the toolbox usage, functionality and implementation. BehaVerify is open source: https://github.com/verivital/behaverify

llm.title_ja: BehaVerify：ビヘイビアツリーのための形式的検証ツール
llm.tldr_ja: ビヘイビアツリー（BT）および神経記号的BTのための検証ツールボックスBehaVerifyを提示し、nuXmvへの効率的なエンコーディングを用いて仕様がBT上で成立するかを迅速に検証できるようにした。
llm.problem: ビヘイビアツリーは安全性がクリティカルなドメインでますます使用されているが、その形式的な検証手法やツールボックスのサポートが不十分であること。
llm.method: 形式的な構文と意味論を持つドメイン固有言語（DSL）を通じてBTを指定し、nuXmvへの高速フォワーディングエンコーディングを用いて検証を行う仕組みの提供。
llm.result: PythonおよびROSとの統合により、ランタイムモニタの検証をはじめとするいくつかの自律ロボットシステムに展開された。
keywords_ja: ロボットソフトウェア

2611.22403.tldr_en: BehaVerify is a verification toolbox for behavior trees (BTs) and Neuro-Symbolic BTs that enables users to specify a BT using a Domain Specific Language (DSL) with formal syntax and semantics.
2611.22403.venue: Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science

2611.22399.title: Plenty to FRET About: From Hazard Analysis to Formal Requirements for Robot-Assisted Dressing
2611.22399.abstract: Understanding requirements for systems involving humans and robots is essential for providing robust evidence that such systems behave correctly. Requirements formalisation approaches such as the Formal Requirements Elicitation Tool (FRET) can support the transition from unstructured natural language to formal representations suitable for verification. In this paper, we formalise 146 hazard-derived natural-language requirements for a Robot-Assisted Dressing (RAD) case study, previously classified using a taxonomy of Human-Robot Teamwork (HRT) requirements. Through an iterative process involving domain-expert clarification, these were represented by 117 unique FRETISH requirements. Formalisation exposed ambiguities, temporal and probabilistic assumptions, and cases where source requirements needed to be decomposed or could be consolidated because they expressed the same formal behaviour. Temporal analysis showed that 70.1% of the unique FRETISH requirements use either immediate-response or ordering constraints (immediately or before), while formalisation also exposed relationships between requirements across HRT taxonomy categories. We further analyse the formal semantics and realisability of the resulting requirements. The results show that HRT classification and formalisation provide complementary views: the taxonomy captures the teamwork concern represented by a requirement, while FRETISH makes the required behaviour explicit. We report practical lessons and limitations of applying FRET to HRT requirements and identify directions for further work.
2611.22399.tldr_en: This paper formalises 146 hazard-derived natural-language requirements for a Robot-Assisted Dressing case study, previously classified using a taxonomy of Human-Robot Teamwork requirements, and shows that HRT classification and formalisation provide complementary views.
2611.22399.venue: Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science

llm.title_ja: ロボット支援着衣のためのハザード分析から形式要件への展開
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット支援着衣の事例研究において、ハザードから導出された146件の自然言語要件をFRETを用いて形式化し、HRT分類と形式化が補完的な視点を提供することを示した。
llm.problem: 人間とロボットの協調システムにおける要件の曖昧さや検証の困難さ
llm.method: FRETを用いた自然言語要件の形式化とドメイン専門家による反復的な明確化
llm.result: 146件の要件が117件のFRETISH要件に変換され、即時応答や順序制約の傾向が明らかになった
llm.limitation: FRETをHRT要件に適用する際の現実的な教訓や限界の報告に留まる

2611.22397.title: SkiNet-Sim: Simulating Petri Nets with Data for the Verification and Validation of Controllers for Autonomous Systems
2611.22397.abstract: A large amount of high-level Petri net formalisms has been investigated and deployed in academic settings over the past decades, but these deployments fail to reach practical applications, despite the strong guarantees they can bring to stakeholders. In particular, the lack of direct benefits from end-users reduces the appeal of Petri nets, both due to the overly simple classical Petri net formalism, and the overly specialized high-level formalisms, on top of state-space explosion issues. In this work, we investigate how a middle-ground could be reached, by separating the implementation-specific aspects of software or hardware behaviors, from the classical Petri net semantics. The goal is to benefit from the sought-after aspects of Petri nets, namely their simple firing semantic and model-checking capabilities, while still being able to augment their behavior to best reflect the modelled system. We present a formal model of Interpreted Petri nets with data-aware transitions and tokens. We illustrate this formalism by modelling the executive layer of a robotic system, and provide a lightweight tool to augment classical Petri nets for general purpose applications, as well as data-aware state-space exploration for model-checking. Their specialization in the context of autonomous robotics is showcased, with a complete industrial inspection mission use-case, to compare simulation and model-checking results between the classical and the new data-aware Petri net semantic.

llm.title_ja: SkiNet-Sim：自律システムコントローラの検証および妥当性確認のためのデータ付きペトリネットのシミュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: ソフトウェアやハードウェアの動作の特定の実装側面を古典的ペトリネットの意味論から分離した、データアウェアな遷移とトークンを持つ解釈ペトリネットの形式モデルを提案し、産業検査ミッションのユースケースで検証した。
llm.problem: 高度なペトリネット形式主義は学術界で研究されてきたが、過度にシンプルな古典的ペトリネットや特殊すぎる高利用形式主義、状態爆発問題のため、実用的なアプリケーションに届かないこと。
llm.method: 実装固有の側面を分離し、単純な発火意味論とモデル検査機能を活用しつつシステムを反映できるように拡張した、データアウェアな解釈ペトリネットモデル（SkiNet-Sim）の導入。
llm.result: 完全な産業検査ミッションのユースケースを用いて、古典的ペトリネットと新しいデータアウェアな意味論の間でシミュレーションとモデル検査の結果を比較・実証した。

2611.22397.tldr_en: This work presents a formal model of Interpreted Petri nets with data-aware transitions and tokens, and illustrates this formalism by modelling the executive layer of a robotic system, and provides a lightweight tool to augment classical Petri nets for general purpose applications, as well as data-aware state-space exploration for model-checking.
2611.22397.venue: Electronic Proceedings in Theoretical Computer Science

2611.22395.title: CoBoVLA: Decoupling Language from Action with Discrete Codes for Robust and Interpretable Robot Manipulation
2611.22395.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models achieve high success rates on the LIBERO benchmark but remain sensitive to paraphrasing. Existing VLAs ranging from 0.6B to 7.5B parameters experience a 22-52 point performance drop on LIBERO-Para while SmolVLA exhibits an even larger decline, from 83\% to 8\%. Because most VLAs jointly learn language understanding and action generation, it is difficult to determine whether a failure originates from misunderstanding an instruction or executing it incorrectly. To address these challenges, we introduce CoBoVLA, or CodeBookVLA, a 250M-parameter VLA that decouples language understanding, planning, and control through learned discrete interpretable codes. A text encoder maps the instructions to shared step codes, which a visual planner then converts into action code sequences executed by a language-independent actor. This design improves robustness to instruction paraphrasing while allowing failures to be traced to individual stages. It also enables efficient real-time control on resource-constrained hardware by encoding instructions only once and using compact discrete representations to keep each component lightweight. CoBoVLA achieves 91.4\% success on LIBERO-Goal, compared with 82.8\% for SmolVLA, under a matched protocol, with 17 ms per control step latency. On LIBERO-Para, it achieves 81.1\% across 4,092 unseen paraphrases and 78.5\% on matched episodes, compared with 36.5\% for SmolVLA LoRA fine-tuned on paraphrases. Without two-step demonstrations, CoBoVLA completes 48.8\% of 160 free-form two-step tasks. Finally, success reaches 91\% when instructions are correctly encoded but falls to 27.2\% otherwise, identifying language understanding as the main source of remaining failures. Together, these results demonstrate that decoupling language understanding and control can improve instruction robustness while making VLA failures easier to diagnose.
2611.22395.comment: 16 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables, and supplemental material included

llm.title_ja: CoBoVLA: 離散コードによる言語と動作の分離によるロバストで解釈可能なロボットマニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: CoBoVLAは、言語理解、計画、制御を学習された離散的かつ解釈可能なコードによって分離し、指示のパラフレーズに対する頑健性と制御の効率性を向上させた2.5億パラメータのVLAモデルである。
llm.problem: VLAモデルは指示のパラフレーズに敏感であり、言語理解の失敗と動作実行の失敗の切り分けが困難である。
llm.method: テキストエンコーダ、視覚プランナー、言語非依存のアクターを離散コードで結合して言語・計画・制御を分離するCoBoVLAを提案する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Goalで91.4%の成功率を達成し、パラフレーズされたLIBERO-Paraでも81.1%の高い頑健性を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22395.tldr_en: CoBoVLA, a 250M-parameter VLA that decouples language understanding, planning, and control through learned discrete interpretable codes, is introduced, demonstrating that decoupling language understanding and control can improve instruction robustness while making VLA failures easier to diagnose.

2611.22388.title: Hidden Variables Behind Real-Robot Data Quality: Lessons from Hundreds of Thousands of Hours
2611.22388.abstract: As real-robot data collection scales, collection-system design shapes both operator efficiency and the behaviors learned by robot policies. Workspace limitations, control-interface friction, and latency can introduce pauses, detours, and corrective motions into otherwise successful demonstrations. We investigate these effects across embodiment, teleoperation control, and data consistency, combining a kinematic study of 25 dual-arm robots, controlled teleoperation experiments, and real-robot evaluation of fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ policies. The embodiment study shows that positional reachability overstates orientation-aware task coverage and that modest shoulder motion can substantially expand the effective workspace. Teleoperation experiments show that parallelizing body-part control reduces task completion time by 43-53%, while compliant control improves success and reduces peak contact forces on constrained and contact-rich tasks. Policy-learning experiments show that demonstrations must capture the visual information underlying action choices: active-search demonstrations improve arm-selection accuracy from chance (50%) to 100%. Calibration experiments reveal that mixed-calibration training data remain usable in our tested configurations when an inference-aligned subset is retained, whereas inference-time miscalibration causes all 30 trials to fail. Policies also retain approximately 90% of the extra path length in detour-contaminated demonstrations, showing how inefficient operator motions persist in learned behavior. Together, these findings connect collection-system design to demonstration quality and downstream policy execution. They motivate evaluating effective workspace, control efficiency, observation completeness, calibration alignment, and motion quality before scaling collection, and addressing system-induced compensations at their source.

llm.title_ja: 実ロボットデータ品質の裏に隠された変数：何十万時間からの教訓
llm.tldr_ja: 実ロボットのデータ収集システム設計がデモの質とポリシーの挙動に与える影響を、二腕ロボットの運動学調査や制御実験、π0.5ポリシー評価を通じて明らかにした。
llm.problem: ワークスペースの制限や操作インターフェースの摩擦、遅延が、デモに不要な停止や迂回、不自然な動作を引き起こす。
llm.method: 25台の二腕ロボットの運動学的研究、制御された遠隔操作実験、および微調整されたπ0.5ポリシーの実ロボット評価を組み合わせた。
llm.result: ボディパーツ制御の並列化によりタスク完了時間が43〜53%短縮され、コンプライアント制御により接触の多いタスクの成功率が向上した。

2611.22388.tldr_en: Together, these findings connect collection-system design to demonstration quality and downstream policy execution, and motivate evaluating effective workspace, control efficiency, observation completeness, calibration alignment, and motion quality before scaling collection, and addressing system-induced compensations at their source.

2611.22385.title: DGV-DLIVO: Degeneracy-Guided Visual Fusion for Direct LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry in Degenerate Tunnel Environments
2611.22385.abstract: Reliable localization in long underground infrastructures remains a major challenge for autonomous inspection robots. In hydropower spillway tunnels and drainage galleries, repetitive geometric structures provide insufficient constraints along the tunnel axis, while weak texture and illumination variations further degrade visual estimation. Under this coupled degradation, existing LiDAR-inertial and visual-inertial odometry systems may lose the ability to recover continuous longitudinal motion. This paper presents DGV-DLIVO, a degeneracy-guided visual fusion for direct LiDAR-inertial-visual odometry for extreme tunnel environments. Instead of treating vision as a general complementary sensor, the proposed method exploits the LiDAR-degenerate direction as an active guidance signal to determine informative visual regions, establish LiDAR-anchored visual associations, and perform subspace-selective fusion. The visual constraints are introduced only into the deficient motion subspace, while unreliable LiDAR information in the same direction is adaptively suppressed and reliable geometric constraints are preserved. Real-world experiments in hydropower tunnels demonstrate that representative state-of-the-art LIO, LIVO, and VIO methods suffer from stagnation, oscillation, severe under-travel, curved drift, or divergence, whereas DGV-DLIVO maintains continuous and directionally consistent tunnel-axis motion estimation under both cart-mounted and handheld acquisition. It achieves a 91.4% progress ratio over the 40m tunnel sequence and significantly improves longitudinal recovery and trajectory stability. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of degeneracy-guided adaptive fusion for robotic inspection in severely degraded underground environments. The source code and a supplementary video are publicly available at https://github.com/0RayZhang0/DGV-DLIVO.

llm.title_ja: DGV-DLIVO：変性トンネル環境における直接LiDAR慣性視覚オドメトリのための変性誘導型視覚融合
llm.tldr_ja: トンネルなどの極限環境における安定した自己位置推定のため、LiDARの変性方向を能動的なガイダンス信号として利用し、視覚情報を適応的に融合するDGV-DLIVOを提案する。
llm.problem: 長大な地下インフラなどの繰り返し構造や低テクスチャ環境では、既存のLIOやVIOシステムは連続的な運動推定が困難になる。
llm.method: LiDARの変性方向を能動的なガイダンス信号として活用し、情報量豊かな視覚領域の特定、LiDARアンカー型視覚関連付け、および部分空間選択的融合を行う。
llm.result: 水力発電所トンネルの実世界実験において、既存手法が発散や停止を起こす中、DGV-DLIVOはトンネル軸に沿った連続的かつ方向一貫性のある運動推定を維持した。

2611.22374.title: AutoE2E: Don't speak - Language free end-to-end autonomy A Real-Time Driving Model for L2++ ADAS and L4 Robotaxis
2611.22374.abstract: AutoE2E is an open-source end-to-end driving model developed by the Autoware Foundation Robotaxi Working Group. It introduces a temporal bird's-eye-view (BEV) architecture that combines multi-camera perception, HD-map information and route conditioning to predict future vehicle motion. The evaluated model uses a pretrained camera-BEV backbone, temporal feature fusion and a lightweight recurrent trajectory planner. It contains approximately 79.9 million parameters, of which approximately 1.45 million are trainable in the evaluated configuration. The v1.0 release provides model checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and DataModelConsole, a dashboard for visualizing and inspecting model experiments. On the KITScenes validation benchmark, the fine-tuned checkpoint achieves an average displacement error (ADE) of 0.745 m and a final displacement error (FDE) of 2.020 m at a three-second prediction horizon. The paper also reports preliminary real-vehicle research conducted with the Technical University of Munich's EDGAR platform, alongside ongoing collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology. AutoE2E v1.0 is an early open research release. Its quantitative evaluation is open-loop, and the model has not yet demonstrated validated closed-loop autonomous driving. The release is intended to provide the autonomous-driving community with an inspectable baseline for further research, experimentation and collaborative development.
2611.22374.comment: 22 pages, 17 figures, 6 tables. Code, model checkpoints and evaluation pipeline released at https://github.com/autowarefoundation/auto_e2e(v1.0 tag, Apache-2.0)

llm.title_ja: AutoE2E：話さない - 音声フリーのエンドツーエンド自律性：L2++ ADASおよびL4ロボタクシー向けリアルタイム運転モデル
llm.tldr_ja: AutoE2Eは、マルチカメラ知覚、HDマップ、ルート条件付けを統合し、将来の車両運動を予測するオープンソースのテンポラルBEVベースエンドツーエンド運転モデルである。
llm.problem: エンドツーエンドの自動運転モデルにおいて、効果的なマルチカメラ知覚、HDマップ情報、ルート条件付けを統合したオープンソースの頑健なベースラインが不足している。
llm.method: プレトレーニングされたカメラBEVバックボーン、テンポラル特徴融合、軽量なリカレント軌道プランナーを組み合わせたテンポラルBEVアーキテクチャを採用する。
llm.result: KITScenes検証ベンチマークにおいて、微調整されたチェックポイントは3秒の予測ホライズンでADE 0.745m、FDE 2.020mを達成した。
llm.limitation: 定量評価はオープンループであり、検証済みのクローズドロープ自動運転はまだ実証されていない。

2611.22374.tldr_en: The AutoE2E v1.0 release provides model checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and DataModelConsole, a dashboard for visualizing and inspecting model experiments to provide the autonomous-driving community with an inspectable baseline for further research, experimentation and collaborative development.

2611.22368.title: Seeing What Still Holds: How Waiting Control Changes Cooperative Recovery
2611.22368.abstract: Changing the holding reference during a fixed-duration wait can reverse the ranking of visual recovery methods. We introduce AuditEmbodied, a paired execution and trajectory evaluation framework that independently varies holding references and waiting duration while keeping recovery executors frozen. A 960-execution factorial on 20 initialization seeds compares CAD-feedback and landmark-based recovery from identical post-wait physical states within each holding and waiting condition. Protected completion requires successful recovery under the declared execution constraints. At a 1 s wait with registered wrist references, their protected completion counts change from 6/40 versus 19/40 under registered holding to 34/40 versus 22/40 under position-only holding. Trajectory analysis localizes the main separation to grasp formation: small observation-time target residuals precede large tracking errors. Joint diagnostics and controlled interventions characterize persistent tracking constraints. On fresh seeds, gradual position reanchoring improves CAD recovery's long-wait completion by 42.5 percentage points and reduces mean complete recovery time by 6.06 s relative to registered holding. Additional evaluations with pretrained policies, handover, and a mass-matched geometry characterize holding-reference sensitivity across executors and physical regimes. These findings establish holding reference as an explicit evaluation condition for comparing visual recovery performance.

llm.title_ja: 何が保持されているかを見る：待機制御が協調的回復をどのように変えるか
llm.tldr_ja: 固定待機中の保持参照の変更が視覚的回復手法の優劣を逆転させることを示し、保持参照を評価の明示的な条件として確立するAuditEmbodiedフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 固定持続時間の待機中に保持参照を変更すると、視覚的回復手法のランキングが変わり、把持形成におけるトラッキング制約が大きくなる。
llm.method: 保持参照と待機時間を独立して変化させながら回復実行者を固定するペア実行および軌道評価フレームワーク「AuditEmbodied」を導入する。
llm.result: 段階的な位置再アンカーにより、CADリカバリーの長期待機完了率が42.5パーセントポイント向上し、平均完全回復時間が短縮された。

2611.22368.tldr_en: AuditEmbodied is introduced, a paired execution and trajectory evaluation framework that independently varies holding references and waiting duration while keeping recovery executors frozen, and holding reference is established as an explicit evaluation condition for comparing visual recovery performance.

2611.22367.title: FailureGen: Scalable Robot Failure Data Generation with World Models
2611.22367.abstract: Robot failures are difficult to collect at scale, limiting the range of failure scenarios represented in robot learning datasets. We present FailureGen, a method for generating synthetic videos with temporal event annotations by reusing action trajectories from recorded failures. The method comprises four stages: (1) fine-tuning an action-conditioned Cosmos world model on successful and failed real executions; (2) annotating source recordings to identify failure-associated donor segments and compatible successful hosts; (3) transferring donor motion into host contexts, with optional spatial offsets, to generate continuous video rollouts; and (4) annotating and filtering the generated samples according to observed events and visual quality. We study two implementations with different tasks and robot configurations, with visual failure detection serving as one downstream application. In a preliminary comparison, a detector trained on real and generated data achieves an average precision of 0.51, compared with 0.41 using real data alone, and detects 33 of 36 failure intervals, compared with 28 of 36. By reusing observed failures in additional contexts, FailureGen expands the data available for studying robot failures and developing downstream learning methods.

llm.title_ja: FailureGen: 世界モデルを用いたスケーラブルなロボット失敗データ生成
llm.tldr_ja: FailureGenは、記録された失敗の動作軌跡を再利用し、時間的イベント注釈付きの合成ビデオを生成することで、ロボット学習用の失敗データを大規模に拡張する手法である。
llm.problem: ロボットの失敗事例は大規模収集が難しいため、ロボット学習用データセットにおける失敗シナリオの多様性が制限されている。
llm.method: 成功および失敗の実際の実行データで行動条件付きCosmos世界モデルを微調整し、失敗に関連するセグメントを成功ホストの文脈に転送してビデオを生成・フィルタリングする。
llm.result: 実データと生成データの両方で訓練された検出器は、実データのみの場合の0.41に対して0.51の平均適合率を達成し、36中33件の失敗区間を検出した。

2611.22367.tldr_en: FailureGen, a method for generating synthetic videos with temporal event annotations by reusing action trajectories from recorded failures by expanding the data available for studying robot failures and developing downstream learning methods is presented.

2611.22356.title: SR-VLA: Stall-Reduced VLA Execution via Predicted-Input Lookahead and Selective KV Cache Repair
2611.22356.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk. Asynchronous early inference can hide latency, but its results may be inconsistent with the arriving actual inputs. Unconditional reuse risks acting on mismatched inputs, whereas full recomputation discards useful precomputation. We propose SR-VLA, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair. During current chunk execution, a lightweight action-conditioned predictor generates next-boundary visual observations and proprioceptive state. These predictions, together with the task instruction, drive the frozen VLA to precompute a speculative KV cache and action chunk. After real inputs are available to VLA, predicted--real differences and task conditions determine whether to accept the action chunk or trigger selective KV repair. On LIBERO, SR-VLA achieves $2.67\times$ and $1.27\times$ query speedups over the respective synchronous $π_{0.5}$ and OpenVLA-OFT baselines, while maintaining competitive average task success rates. Under target-motion perturbation, success remains baseline-comparable, with $1.52\times$--$1.93\times$ query speedup.

llm.title_ja: SR-VLA: 予測入力ルックヘッドと選択的KVキャッシュ修復によるストール削減型VLA実行
llm.tldr_ja: SR-VLAは、予測入力ルックヘッドと選択的KVキャッシュ修復を組み合わせることで、VLAポリシーの推論遅延による制御ストールを削減する。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーは推論が次のアクションチャンクをブロックする際に制御ストールを引き起こし、非同期早期推論は実際の入力と不整合を起こすリスクがある。
llm.method: 軽量な行動条件付き予測子で次の境界の視覚・固有状態を予測し、凍結されたVLAに推測的KVキャッシュとアクションチャンクを事前計算させて差異に応じて選択的修復を行う。
llm.result: LIBEROにおいて、同期型π0.5およびOpenVLA-OFTベースラインと比較して、競合するタスク成功率を維持しながら2.67倍および1.27倍のクエリ高速化を達成した。

2611.22356.tldr_en: SR-VLA is proposed, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair with selective KV cache repair, combining predicted-input lookahead with selective KV cache repair forVision-language-action policies incur control stalls when inference blocks the next action chunk.

2611.22321.title: Beyond Episodic Recall: Experience-to-Knowledge Evolution for Lifelong Embodied Navigation
2611.22321.abstract: Lifelong embodied navigation requires agents to accumulate experience through continuous interaction and reuse it for subsequent goal searches. Existing memory-enhanced methods typically retain historical observations or construct structured scene representations. However, storing observations or high-dimensional semantic embeddings incurs growing storage costs. Meanwhile, structured representations support retrieval and semantic reasoning but do not explicitly evolve accumulated experience into environment-specific knowledge. To address these limitations, we propose Experience-Evolving Memory (EvoNav), a novel two-timescale memory framework. It organizes semantic observations, spatial relations, and task-feedback cues into sparse experience atoms. During online operation, experience atoms continually consolidate repeated observations and form dynamic links based on transitions. At the slower timescale, EvoNav distills accumulated category co-occurrences and feedback signals into environment-specific structural knowledge without relying on predefined object--room relations. For each new goal, EvoNav combines direct goal evidence from experience atoms with learned structural knowledge to guide goal-directed search on the current traversability map. Experiments on single-goal, sequential multi-floor, and multimodal navigation demonstrate effective experience reuse and improved path efficiency with compact persistent memory, together with successful transfer to a real robot.

llm.title_ja: エピソード記憶を超えて：生涯にわたる身体化ナビゲーションのための経験から知識への進化
llm.tldr_ja: EvoNavは、連続的な相互作用から得た経験をスパースな経験原子と環境固有の構造的知識に階層的に統合し、コンパクトな記憶で効率的なゴール探索を実現する記憶フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存の記憶を用いた手法は過去の観察や高次元埋め込みを保存するためストレージコストが増大し、構造化表現も経験を環境固有の知識へと明示的に進化させない。
llm.method: 観察、空間関係、タスクフィードバックをスパースな経験原子に組織化し、低速なタイムスケールで環境固有の構造的知識に蒸留する二重タイムスケール記憶フレームワークを提案する。
llm.result: 単一ゴール、連続的マルチフロア、マルチモーダルナビゲーションの実験において、コンパクトな永続メモリによる効果的な経験の再利用と経路効率の向上が実証された。

2611.22321.tldr_en: Experience-Evolving Memory (EvoNav), a novel two-timescale memory framework that organizes semantic observations, spatial relations, and task-feedback cues into sparse experience atoms into environment-specific structural knowledge without relying on predefined object--room relations.

2611.22314.title: Inertial Video World Models
2611.22314.abstract: The physical world has inertia: it evolves from what already exists rather than being recreated at every instant. However, many existing video world models lack an explicit mechanism for inertial state evolution, leaving the continuity of motion and structure implicit in video prediction. During autoregressive rollouts, repeated reconstruction can accumulate errors and destabilize the predicted dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce InertialWorld, an Inertial Video World Model that makes inertia a structural prior for autoregressive prediction: existing scene evidence is carried across time rather than reconstructed at every step. Central to this formulation is Inertial Memory, which turns memory from passive predictive context into an evolving video state with two complementary views: a dense Eulerian grid preserves scene-aligned evidence, while persistent Lagrangian carriers bind local content to learned canonical coordinates. At each step, the model transports the carrier content according to action-conditioned motion, predicts the complete next video state from the transported carriers and dense grid, and uses a learned gate to combine transported and newly predicted content into the memory for the next step. Extensive experiments across multiple domains, including robot manipulation, 3D game simulation, and open-world navigation, demonstrate that InertialWorld achieves competitive autoregressive prediction performance against strong video world model baselines. Codes link: https://github.com/YuanGao-YG/InertialWorld

llm.title_ja: 慣性ビデオ世界モデル
llm.tldr_ja: InertialWorldは、慣性を構造的な事前知識として組み込み、既存のシーン証拠を時間的により一貫して伝送することで、自己回帰的なビデオ予測の誤差蓄積と不安定性を防ぐ世界モデルである。
llm.problem: 多くのビデオ世界モデルは明示的な慣性状態の進化メカニズムを欠いており、自己回帰的ロールアウト時に繰り返しの再構築によって誤差が蓄積し動的挙動が不安定になる。
llm.method: 密なオイラーグリッドと永続的なラグランジュキャリアという相補的な2つのビューを持つ慣性メモリを導入し、アクション条件付きの運動に従ってキャリア内容を輸送して次のビデオ状態を予測する。
llm.result: ロボットマニピュレーション、3Dゲームシミュレーション、オープンワールドナビゲーションを含む複数のドメインで、強力なビデオ世界モデルベースラインと同等の自己回帰予測性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: 物理シミュレーション

2611.22314.tldr_en: Extensive experiments across multiple domains, including robot manipulation, 3D game simulation, and open-world navigation, demonstrate that InertialWorld achieves competitive autoregressive prediction performance against strong video world model baselines.

2611.22310.title: EviDARL: Evidence-Centric Dual-Agent Reasoning via Alternating Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Table Question Answering
2611.22310.abstract: Despite advances in LLM-based table reasoning, most studies focus on single-table settings. Multi-table QA requires multi-hop reasoning over complex table relationships and evidence dispersed across long contexts, often without verifiable intermediate traces. To address these challenges, we introduce EviDA, an evidence-centric dual-agent framework comprising an Evidence Construction Agent and a Reasoning and Answering Agent. The Evidence Construction Agent generates and executes table-manipulation programs over complete tables to produce question-specific evidence and verifiable intermediate traces, simplifying subsequent reasoning. The Reasoning and Answering Agent then performs multi-hop reasoning over this evidence to derive final answers. We further introduce EviDARL, which combines agent-specific fine-grained rewards with parameter-efficient alternating reinforcement learning to improve collaboration between the agents. By optimizing each agent in turn while holding the other fixed, EviDARL enables bidirectional adaptation between evidence construction and answer reasoning. Experiments on MMQA and TQA-Bench demonstrate that EviDARL substantially outperforms competitive open-model and multi-table reasoning baselines under constrained model and training budgets.

llm.title_ja: EviDARL: 交互強化学習による証拠中心型二重エージェント推論を用いたマルチテーブル質問応答
llm.tldr_ja: EviDARLは、証拠構築エージェントと推論・回答エージェントを交互強化学習で協調させ、複雑なマルチテーブル質問応答における多段階推論性能を向上させるフレームワークである。
llm.problem: マルチテーブルQAでは、複雑なテーブル関係や長文脈に分散した証拠にわたる多段階推論が必要であるが、検証可能な中間トレースが不足していることが多い。
llm.method: テーブル操作プログラムを実行して質問固有の証拠を生成する証拠構築エージェントと、それに基づいて多段階推論を行う推論・回答エージェントを、エージェント固有の報酬を用いた交互強化学習で最適化する。
llm.result: MMQAおよびTQA-Benchの実験において、制約されたモデル・訓練予算の下で、競合するオープンモデルやマルチTable推論ベースラインを大きく上回る性能を達成した。

2611.22310.tldr_en: EviDA, an evidence-centric dual-agent framework comprising an Evidence Construction Agent and a Reasoning and Answering Agent, and EviDARL, which combines agent-specific fine-grained rewards with parameter-efficient alternating reinforcement learning to improve collaboration between the agents, are introduced.

2611.22302.title: Where Do Human-to-Robot Transfer Gains Come From?
2611.22302.abstract: Human data can support robot policy pretraining, but gains attributed to a data recipe may also reflect subset size, training variability, or downstream adaptation. In an HPT implementation on a 20-task MetaWorld suite with three training blocks, a constrained random 5,000-recording subset matches most of the task-informed subset's gain over the 40,000-recording pool at 20,000 updates (3.69 of 4.29 percentage points), leaving equal-size selection differences of 0.60 points at 5,000 recordings and 0.45 points at 1,250 recordings, with wide paired intervals. Across 12 comparisons, task orderings repeat across seeds for several contrasts, but a fixed predictor built from the other two seeds trails the mean or difficulty reference in at least one held-out fold for every comparison. Neither mechanism probe shows its predicted positive interaction: task-slot mismatch yields an interaction of $-0.0347$ points after adaptation, and in a six-task observation experiment the observation-by-pretraining interaction changes sign between seeds ($-18.29$ and $+1.04$ points) while full-state pretraining gains are positive in both ($+6.37$ and $+2.31$ points). This retrospective study shows how equal-size and capacity controls, seed-level reporting, and targeted interventions change the interpretation of apparent transfer gains.

llm.title_ja: ヒューマン・ロボット間転移の利得はどこから来るのか？
llm.tldr_ja: 人間データの事前学習における性能向上要因を検証し、サブセットサイズや訓練のばらつき、下流の適応が転移利得の解釈に与える影響を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 人間データによるロボットポリシーの事前学習の利得は、データレシピだけでなく、サブセットサイズや訓練のばらつき、下流の適応を反映している可能性がある。
llm.method: 20タスクのMetaWorldスイートを用いたHPT実装において、制約されたランダムサブセットやタスク順序、観察と事前学習の相互作用などを体系的に比較・検証した。
llm.result: 制約されたランダムサブセットがタスク情報付きサブセットの利得の大部分を一致させ、同サイズや容量の制御、シード別の報告が転移利得の解釈を変えることを示した。

2611.22302.tldr_en: This retrospective study shows how equal-size and capacity controls, seed-level reporting, and targeted interventions change the interpretation of apparent transfer gains.

2611.22297.title: FIRE-Drive: Feasibility-Informed Risk Evaluation for End-to-End Diffusion Planning
2611.22297.abstract: Diffusion-based end-to-end autonomous driving models have shown strong potential in generating multimodal planning trajectories. However, their performance still depends heavily on trajectory initialization, mode evaluation, and supervision quality. Weakly constrained noisy initialization may introduce infeasible proposals and increase the burden of denoising. Moreover, selecting the optimal mode remains challenging when candidate trajectories are geometrically similar but differ in safety, interaction risk, and progress. To address these issues, we propose FIRE-Drive, a feasibility-informed risk evaluation framework for end-to-end autonomous driving. FIRE-Drive improves diffusion-based planning through dynamic feasible anchor initialization, candidate-specific bird's-eye-view risk evidence, and compact high-quality candidate supervision with lightweight refinement. This design aligns the initial support, risk-aware scoring, and multimodal supervision of trajectory modes under a unified planning objective. It enables the diffusion decoder to focus on refining plausible trajectories while the scorer distinguishes modes using local risk evidence. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 show that FIRE-Drive achieves a Predictive Driver Model Score of 91.5 with a ResNet34 backbone. Additional closed-loop evaluation on 220 Bench2Drive routes yields a Driving Score of 71.43 and a Success Rate of 42.73%. Component ablations and a scorer comparison under matched candidate inputs support the contributions of feasible initialization, auxiliary supervision, and risk-informed selection. Our code is available at https://github.com/Latte00/FIRE-drive.

llm.title_ja: FIRE-Drive: エンドツーエンド拡散計画のための実現可能性情報に基づくリスク評価
llm.tldr_ja: FIRE-Driveは、動的な実現可能アンカー初期化、リスク認識スコアリング、および軽量な改良を統合し、拡散ベースのエンドツーエンド自動運転の計画性能を向上させる。
llm.problem: 拡散ベースのエンドツーエンド自動運転モデルは、初期化、モード評価、および教師データの品質に依存しており、非現実的な軌道の提案やリスク評価の課題がある。
llm.method: 動的な実現可能アンカー初期化、候補固有のBEVリスク証拠、軽量な改良を伴うコンパクトな高品質候補教師データを統合した計画フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: NAVSIM v1においてResNet34バックボーンを用いて91.5の予測ドライバーモデルスコアを達成し、Bench2Driveルートのクローズドループ評価でも高い成功率を記録した。
keywords_ja: クローズドループ評価

2611.22297.tldr_en: FIRE-Drive improves diffusion-based planning through dynamic feasible anchor initialization, candidate-specific bird's-eye-view risk evidence, and compact high-quality candidate supervision with lightweight refinement, and aligns the initial support, risk-aware scoring, and multimodal supervision of trajectory modes under a unified planning objective.

2611.22295.title: Similar Is Not Useful: Selecting In-Context Demonstrations by Closed-Loop Utility
2611.22295.abstract: Retrieval-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies fill their context with the demonstrations whose frames look most like the current observation under frozen DINOv2 embeddings. We ask whether visual similarity selects the demonstrations that make the policy succeed. For a frozen retrieval-augmented VLA (RICL on $π_0$-FAST, LIBERO), we make the demonstration pool swappable at run time and score each demonstration's utility by regressing the closed-loop success of 60 fixed-size pools on their membership. On initial states disjoint from those used for scoring, pools of the five highest-utility demonstrations succeed on 66.4% of 760 paired episodes across 19 tasks, pools of the five most similar on 55.7%, and random pools on 55.5%. Utility beats similarity by 10.8 points ($p=3.2\times10^{-6}$; positive on 15 of 18 untied tasks), including on 12 tasks the policy was never primed on, and similarity-selected pools do no better than random ($+0.1$ points). Within a task, a pool's visual similarity to the test scenes tracks its success at Spearman 0.10; across tasks, similarity separates tasks whose scenes differ and falls to chance when two tasks share a scene. The gain comes from on-task closed-loop evidence: best-of-ten direct search over pools recovers two-thirds of it with 100 rollouts. Against the shipped 20-demonstration pool, utility-curated pools of five lead by 7.0 points over 560 paired episodes from two evaluation runs ($p=0.006$), and utility-ordered retrieval inside the full pool leads by 4.5 points ($p=0.055$).

llm.title_ja: 類似していることは有用ではない：クローズドループの有用性によるインコンテキストデモの選択
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的類似性ベースのデモ検索が必ずしもポリシーの成功に結びつかないことを示し、クローズドループの有用性に基づいてデモを選択・順序付けすることで成功率が大幅に向上することを実証した。
llm.problem: 検索拡張VLAポリシーは、DINOv2埋め込みで現在の観察に最も似たフレームを持つデモを取得しているが、視覚的類似性がポリシーを成功させるデモを選べているかは不明である。
llm.method: 固定サイズプールのクローズドループ成功率の回帰分析により各デモの有用性をスコアリングし、類似性ベースの選択と比較評価を行った。
llm.result: 有用性に基づき選択されたデモプールは760のペアエピソードで66.4%の成功率を達成し、類似性ベース（55.7%）やランダム（55.5%）を大きく上回った。
keywords_ja: インコンテキスト学習
ロボットマニピュレーション
