2611.22295.tldr_en: This work makes the demonstration pool swappable at run time and scores each demonstration's utility by regressing the closed-loop success of 60 fixed-size pools on their membership, asking whether visual similarity selects the demonstrations that make the policy succeed.

2611.22294.title: Perception into Imagination: Executable Memory for World Models
2611.22294.abstract: Physical agents must use what they previously saw or touched after visibility or contact is lost. Their actions change the implications of these remembered facts. We introduce executable perceptual memory (EPM), a world-model framework that advances explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during imagination. Its evolving read-out informs reward prediction, value estimation and policy learning. We align reward inputs with the transitions that produced them and supervise the reward head on open-loop rollouts of recorded actions. On Memory Maze $13\times13$, EPM reaches 30.37 return at 1M interactions, compared with 23.37 when the same evolving read-out informs only policy and value on a common perceptual front end: a gain of 7.00 [3.80, 10.21]. The complete method also improves control on $9\times9$ and in MiniWorld. Probes of remembered, out-of-view arrivals show stronger reward anticipation in both visual implementations. Concentration, tactile recovery and real tactile frames demonstrate complementary roles of remembered facts in imagined-policy training, motion-dependent decisions and sensory-content retention. EPM connects persistent perception to the predicted consequences and learning signals of a world model for Physical AI.

llm.title_ja: 知覚から想像へ：世界モデルのための実行可能な記憶
llm.tldr_ja: EPM（実行可能知覚記憶）は、物理エージェントの想像中に明示的な知覚状態を神経潜在力学とともに進化させ、報酬予測やポリシー学習を向上させる世界モデルフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 物理エージェントは視界や接触が失われた後も過去の知覚情報を使用する必要があり、その行動によって記憶された事実の意味合いが変化する課題がある。
llm.method: 遷移と整合させた報酬入力を通じて知覚的記憶（EPM）を神経潜在力学と並行して進化させ、オープンロールアウトで報酬ヘッドを監督する。
llm.result: Memory Maze 13x13において、ポリシーと価値のみに情報を伝達するベースラインの23.37に対して30.37のリターンを達成し、制御性能が大幅に向上した。

2611.22294.tldr_en: This work introduces executable perceptual memory (EPM), a world-model framework that advances explicit perceptual state alongside neural latent dynamics during imagination, and connects persistent perception to the predicted consequences and learning signals of a world model for Physical AI.

2611.22291.title: When the World Is the Test Suite: Agentic Intelligence for the Physical World
2611.22291.abstract: Coding agents built to repair software now write, test, and repair programs for robots, laboratories, and industrial controllers. Unlike in software engineering, no test suite comes with the code. Whether a program works must be established by running it on a robot, in a physics simulator, or through the policies it helps to train, and such evidence is costly to obtain and can itself be wrong. As these agents take on more physical tasks, how their programs are judged matters as much as how they are written. This paper examines this emerging area, agentic intelligence for the physical world, by treating the world as the program's test suite. We organize the discussion around three questions: how agents write programs for the physical world, how these programs are tested, and how agents learn from the results. We first trace how language models for robots and software engineering agents came together, ask which software testing practices carry over to physical tests, and describe each program by where it sits relative to the actuator and by what judges it. For writing, we cover programs that act as robot policies and programs that support policy learning by producing rewards, tasks, and training worlds. For testing, we examine what physical trials cost, what traces, learned judges, simulators, and formal checks can establish in their place, and what safety requires beyond task success. For learning, we discuss how tested programs are retained as experience, in skill libraries and in model weights. Finally, we turn to benchmarks and evaluation practice and outline open challenges. Writing programs is becoming cheap, while trustworthy evidence about what they do remains costly. Progress will therefore depend on a physical counterpart of continuous integration: verification cheap enough to run often, reliable enough to trust under search, and maintained alongside the experience it validates.

llm.title_ja: 世界がテストスイートであるとき：物理世界の エージェント型インテリジェンス
llm.tldr_ja: ソフトウェアテストのプラクティスを物理世界に応用し、ロボットやシミュレータ、ポリシーを実行してプログラムを記述・テスト・学習する「物理世界のエージェント型インテリジェンス」という新興分野を体系的に考察する。
llm.problem: ソフトウェアエンジニアリングとは異なり物理世界には標準的なテストスイートが存在せず、プログラムの正当性をロボットやシミュレータ上で検証する証拠の取得にコストがかかる。
llm.method: エージェントが物理世界向けのプログラムをどのように書き、どのようにテストされ、結果からどう学ぶかという3つの問いを中心に文献と動向を網羅的に分析する。
llm.result: プログラムの自動記述が容易になる一方で信頼性の高い検証証拠を得るコストが高いため、物理版の継続的インテグレーション（検証）の重要性を浮き彫りにした。
keywords_ja: エージェント型インテリジェンス

2611.22291.tldr_en: This paper examines this emerging area, agentic intelligence for the physical world, by treating the world as the program's test suite, and describes each program by where it sits relative to the actuator and by what judges it.

2611.22275.title: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
2611.22275.abstract: Collaboration promises to extend humanoid capabilities beyond what individual robots can achieve. However, realizing this potential requires coordinated whole-body interactions, coherent long-horizon planning, and precise synchronization across robots. We introduce Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation. At the low level, we develop a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone. At the high level, we train a vision-language planner and design a speech-based leader-follower coordination mechanism to synchronize decentralized execution without network communication. Trained with two identical humanoids, our system scales to teams of up to ten robots and generalizes to heterogeneous teams without retraining. To benchmark these capabilities, we introduce HH-Bench, comprising 12 tasks involving teams of 2 to 10 humanoids, including heterogeneous teams. Systematic evaluations show that Heave-Ho consistently outperforms baseline methods, while real-world experiments demonstrate robust decentralized collaboration across challenging tasks.
2611.22275.comment: 18 pages, 10 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://heaveho-humanoid.github.io/
2611.22275.hf_summary_en: A decentralized framework enables teams of humanoids to coordinate whole-body loco-manipulation over long horizons using low-level multi-agent post-training and a high-level vision-language planner with speech-based leader-follower synchronization.

llm.title_ja: Heave-Ho: 分散型長期マルチヒューマノイド協調
llm.tldr_ja: Heave-Hoは、低レベルのマルチエージェント事後訓練と高レベルの言語プランナー・音声同期を組み合わせ、ネットワーク通信なしで長時間の協調作業を行う分散型ヒューマノイド協調フレームワークである。
llm.problem: ヒューマノイドの協調には、協調された全身インタラクション、一貫した長期計画、およびロボット間の正確な同期が求められる。
llm.method: 基礎追従モデルを物理的に結合した相互作用に適応させるマルチエージェント事後訓練と、音声ベースのリーダー・フォロワー同期を備えたビジョン言語プランナーを組み合わせる。
llm.result: 10台までのロボットチームへ拡張可能であり、HH-Benchを用いた評価および実世界実験において、挑戦的なタスクで堅牢な分散協調を実証した。

2611.22275.tldr_en: This work introduces Heave-Ho, a decentralized framework for long-horizon collaborative multi-humanoid loco-manipulation, and develops a multi-agent post-training framework that adapts a humanoid foundation tracking model to physically coupled interactions between humanoids, enabling coordinated decentralized control from local observations alone.

2611.22258.title: ALERT: Extending Humanoid Motion Trackers with a General and Lightweight Human Avoidance Pipeline
2611.22258.abstract: Whole-body motion tracking has enabled humanoid dancing, athletic motions, and teleoperation, providing a foundation for capability demonstrations and manipulation data collection. However, existing tracking policies lack awareness of nearby humans and proactive avoidance capabilities, while motion substitution and local constraint-based corrections may compromise reference motion integrity and tracking continuity. We propose ALERT, a general lightweight pipeline for extending motion tracking to shared human-robot environments. Through lightweight adaptation, it integrates human perception and proactive avoidance into pretrained tracking policies, balancing avoidance demands with reference motion tracking while preserving existing motion capabilities. Simulation and real-world experiments across tracking backbones demonstrate reliable collision-free execution through localized human avoidance, preserving whole-body coordination and enabling rapid recovery of reference tracking, while retaining the ability of pretrained policies to track unseen motions.

llm.title_ja: ALERT: 汎用かつ軽量な人間回避パイプラインによるヒューマノイドモーショントラッカーの拡張
llm.tldr_ja: ALERTは、事前学習済みの追跡ポリシーに人間の知覚と能動的回避を軽量に適応させ、参照モーションの追跡と安全な人間回避を両立させるパイプラインである。
llm.problem: 既存の追跡ポリシーは周辺の人間に対する認識や能動的回避能力を欠いており、モーションの置換などは追跡の連続性を損なうおそれがある。
llm.method: 軽量な適応を通じて、人間の知覚と能動的回避機能を既存の事前学習済み追跡ポリシーに統合し、回避要求と参照モーション追跡のバランスを取る。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界実験において、全身の協調性を維持しながら局所的な人間回避による信頼性の高い衝突回避動作を実現した。

2611.22258.tldr_en: ALERT, a general lightweight pipeline for extending motion tracking to shared human-robot environments, integrates human perception and proactive avoidance into pretrained tracking policies, balancing avoidance demands with reference motion tracking while preserving existing motion capabilities.

2611.22244.title: PhyVGGT: Feed-Forward Articulated Object Reconstruction from Monocular Videos
2611.22244.abstract: Reconstructing an articulated object with its 3D movable parts, joint parameters and unseen articulation states from an uncalibrated monocular video is essential for robot manipulation and interactive digital twins. Existing per-scene optimisation methods require minutes to hours and external depth or camera poses, whereas feed-forward 3D foundation models reconstruct dense point maps in one pass without segmenting movable parts or inferring joints. Even on these monocular point maps, regressing or fitting continuous joints directly fails on casual videos, since cross-frame attention blurs moving part boundaries in deep layers, underestimates motion along the viewing ray and leaves continuous axes ill-conditioned under small opening angles. To address these challenges, we propose PhyVGGT, a single-pass framework on a frozen 3D foundation model that anchors moving-part matching and closed-form joint estimation to the undistorted geometry of the stationary base. First, our Part and Motion Decoder fuses intermediate per-frame tokens with global tokens and references part queries to a static-base query to segment 3D parts, align point maps on the static base and predict learned Bingham priors. Second, our Kinematic Inference Layer fits an orthogonal Manhattan frame to static surface normals, selects the joint axis in closed form under a Bingham posterior combining pairwise motion scatter with the learned priors, and solves a linear system for the hinge pivot to drive unseen states. Trained solely on synthetic data, PhyVGGT achieves state-of-the-art monocular performance across five benchmarks, outperforming FAMOS and monocular ArtiPoint, surpassing posed RGB-D ArtiPoint in median error, and running in 6.8 s per 48-frame video against hours of per-scene optimisation in Articulat3D. Project page: https://phyvggt.github.io.
2611.22244.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables. Project page: https://phyvggt.github.io

llm.title_ja: PhyVGGT: 単眼ビデオからのフィードフォワード関節付オブジェクト再構築
llm.tldr_ja: PhyVGGTは、凍結された3D基盤モデル上で静止ベースに対する幾何学的制約と運動デコーダを活用し、単眼ビデオから関節付オブジェクトを高速かつ高精度に再構築する単一パスフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 既存のシーンごとの最適化手法は数分から数時間を要し、単眼点群からの直接的な関節パラメータの回帰は動きの境界のぼやけや視線方向の運動過小評価を引き起こす。
llm.method: 静止ベースのクエリを参照して3Dパーツをセグメント化するパート・運動デコーダーと、直交マンハッタンフレームをあてはめて閉じた形式で関節軸を推論する運動推論レイヤーを組み合わせる。
llm.result: 5つのベンチマークで最先端の単眼性能を達成し、ビデオあたり6.8秒で動作して既存の最適化手法や従来手法を大きく上回る精度を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22244.tldr_en: PhyVGGT achieves state-of-the-art monocular performance across five benchmarks, outperforming FAMOS and monocular ArtiPoint, surpassing posed RGB-D ArtiPoint in median error, and running in 6.8 s per 48-frame video against hours of per-scene optimisation in Articulat3D.

2611.22231.title: From Temperature-Limited to Battery-Limited Legged Locomotion
2611.22231.abstract: On legged robots, sustained locomotion often ends in thermal shutdown rather than battery depletion: the heat of walking concentrates in a few joint motors, which overheat long before the battery is empty. We train thermally aware locomotion policies by reinforcement learning without ever observing temperature, and demonstrate this on a Unitree Go2 quadruped. We first identify a coupled 13-node lumped RC thermal network, fitted on two runs of a single robot and calibrated against the measured electrical power, that predicts all twelve motor temperatures with a mean RMSE below 1 $^\circ$C across different robot instances, gaits, payloads, and speeds. Under a sustained gait, the temperatures the motors will settle at follow directly from the gait-averaged squared torques and joint speeds. Our core contribution is a reward that drives down the hottest predicted asymptotes: thermal time constants exceed the credit-assignment horizon of reinforcement learning by orders of magnitude, but predicted asymptotes respond to torque and joint speed within a single gait cycle, so the policy learns to lower and spread heat with no temperature input. On the robot, the policy turns sustained locomotion from temperature-limited to battery-limited: with a 5 kg payload at 1 m/s, a learned baseline reaches thermal shutdown after 19 minutes (1.1 km), whereas our policy runs the battery down after 174 minutes (10.0 km) with its hottest motor 14 $^\circ$C below the shutdown threshold in a 26 $^\circ$C room; on an unloaded factory circuit with stairs and ramps, the baseline overheats after 25 laps (6.2 km), while our policy completes 47 (11.2 km) on one battery with 22 $^\circ$C of margin.
2611.22231.comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Supplementary video in the ancillary files. Dataset: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24274994

llm.title_ja: 温度制限からバッテリー制限へ：脚式移動の熱制約克服
llm.tldr_ja: モータ温度を直接観測せず強化学習により熱的に配慮した移動ポリシーを学習させることで、四脚ロボットの持続走行における熱的シャットダウンを回避しバッテリー限界まで稼働させることに成功した。
llm.problem: 脚式ロボットの持続的な移動は、バッテリ消耗ではなく関節モータの過熱による熱的シャットダウンで終了することが多い。
llm.method: ガイト平均の二乗トルクと関節速度からモータ温度を予測する熱ネットワークを構築し、予測された最も高い非対称な熱的漸近値を下げるような報酬設計を用いて強化学習を行う。
llm.result: Unitree Go2において、ベースラインが19分で過熱停止するところ、提案ポリシーはバッテリーを174分間（10km）まで稼働させることができた。

2611.22224.title: TRIDENT: Efficient Triple-Task Learning of Dehazing, Depth, and Uncertainty Estimation for Underwater 3-D Robot Visual Perception
2611.22224.abstract: Underwater visual systems often suffer from blurry textures and low color contrast due to the inevitable light propagation. These issues can significantly degrade the perception of stable robotic operations. In this paper, we introduce a novel learning-based sensing system that tackles the multidimensional vision tasks in underwater; concretely, we deal with image enhancement, depth estimation, and uncertainty for 3-D visual systems. Also, we propose a TRIDENT model in a fast and lightweight manner; TRIDENT consists of three parallelized decoders and one backbone structure for efficient feature sharing. In addition, it is designed to be trained to express complex parameterization. In experimental evaluation on several standard datasets, we demonstrate that TRIDENT significantly outperforms other existing methods on image enhancement and depth estimation. Despite performing three tasks, our model has better efficiency than the others for both memory size and inference time. Finally, our joint learning approach demonstrates robustness in feature matching and seamlessly extends from 2-D to 3-D vision tasks. Supplements are available at https://sites.google.com/view/underwater-trident/home

llm.title_ja: TRIDENT: 水中3次元ロボット視覚認識のための鮮明化・深度・不確実性推定の効率的な3タスク学習
llm.tldr_ja: TRIDENTは、水中環境における画像鮮明化、深度推定、不確実性推定の3つのビジョンタスクを並列デコーダーと特徴共有により高速かつ効率的に処理する学習ベースのセンシングシステムである。
llm.problem: 水中の視覚システムは光の伝播によるぼやけたテクスチャや低コントラストに悩み、ロボットの安定した運用における知覚を著しく低下させる。
llm.method: 効率的な特徴共有のための1つのバックボーン構造と、並列化された3つのデコーダーで構成される軽量なTRIDENTモデルを設計・訓練する。
llm.result: 複数の標準データセットでの評価において、画像鮮明化と深度推定で既存手法を大幅に上回り、複数タスクを実行しながらメモリサイズと推論時間の両方で優れた効率を示した。

badges.venue: IEEE Sensors Journal, vol. 25, no. 1, pp 2025

2611.22224.tldr_en: A novel learning-based sensing system that tackles the multidimensional vision tasks in underwater, which significantly outperforms other existing methods on image enhancement and depth estimation and has better efficiency than the others for both memory size and inference time.

2611.22212.title: Joint-ID: Transformer-based Joint Image Enhancement and Depth Estimation for Underwater Environments
2611.22212.abstract: Underwater imaging is a challenging task due to factors such as scattering, absorption, and turbulence, which degrade image quality and limit visibility. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for enhancing underwater images that leverages the benefits of joint learning for simultaneous image enhancement and depth estimation. We introduce Joint-ID, a transformer-based neural network that can obtain high-perceptual image quality and depth information from raw underwater images. Our approach formulates a multi-modal objective function that addresses invalid depth, lack of sharpness, and image degradation based on color and local texture. We design an end-to-end training pipeline that enables joint restoration and depth estimation in a shared hierarchical feature space. Additionally, we propose a synthetic dataset with various distortions and scene depths for multi-task learning. We evaluate Joint-ID on synthetic and standard datasets, as well as real underwater images with diverse spectra and harsh turbidity, demonstrating its effectiveness for underwater image enhancement and depth estimation. Furthermore, we demonstrate the ability of Joint-ID to perform feature matching and saliency detection for visually guided underwater robots. Our proposed method has the potential to improve the visual perception of underwater environments and benefit applications such as oceanography and underwater robotics. Supplements are available at: https://sites.google.com/view/joint-id/home

llm.title_ja: Joint-ID: 水中環境向けのTransformerベースの画像強調と深度推定の統合
llm.tldr_ja: 水中環境における散乱や吸収などの課題に対処するため、高画質な画像と深度情報を同時に取得するTransformerベースのニューラルネットワーク「Joint-ID」を提案する。
llm.problem: 水中画像は散乱、吸収、乱流により画質が低下し視認性が制限される課題がある。
llm.method: 共有階層的特徴空間で同時復元と深度推定を行うトランスフォーマーベースのネットワークJoint-IDを提案する。
llm.result: 合成データセットおよび標準データセット、実世界の水中画像において画像強調と深度推定の有効性を示した。

badges.venue: IEEE Sensors Journal, vol. 24, no. 3, pp 2024

2611.22212.tldr_en: This article introduces Joint-ID, a transformer-based neural network that can obtain high-perceptual image quality and depth information from raw underwater images and formulates a multimodal objective function that addresses invalid depth, lack of sharpness, and image degradation based on color and local texture.

2611.22195.title: Haptic Probing for Subsurface-Aware Force Distribution on Layered Soft Tissue
2611.22195.abstract: Force-regulated contact with layered soft tissue fails most often where the subsurface composition changes: controllers infer the substrate from the loading signal alone, so the estimate guiding them lags the change---more acutely, we argue, over compliant than over bone-backed tissue. We remove that lag with a separate haptic channel. Under a light preload, a brief low-amplitude excitation lets the local dynamic admittance discriminate muscle from bone-backed tissue relative to a per-subject baseline, before task force is applied---active haptic sensing used to commit a control decision rather than to characterise tissue. A force- and tactile-driven distribution law then consumes that regime throughout execution: an instantaneous allocation equalises pressure across the engaged fingertips, while the regime sets the admissible pressure and hence the area the hand must recruit to deliver the target force---making patch area a controlled variable rather than a by-product. Probing, switches and recruitment are priced in a partitioned passivity budget, so safety monitoring cannot suppress the probe and a refused recruitment forfeits force tracking rather than the pressure bound. We report force tracking and pressure uniformity over curved, migrating contact on three human subjects, with regime labels from anatomical landmarks.

llm.title_ja: 積層軟組織における下層認識型力分布のための触覚プロービング
llm.tldr_ja: 下層の組成変化による力制御の遅れを解消するため、タスク力適用前に低振幅励振による動的アドミタンスを用いて組織を識別する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 下層組織が変化する積層軟組織との力制御において、推定の遅れにより追従が失敗しやすい。
llm.method: 軽量なプレロード下での低振幅励振により筋肉と骨の裏打ちされた組織を識別し、パッチ面積を制御変数とする力・触覚駆動の分配則を適用する。
llm.result: 3名の被験者を対象とした曲面や移動する接触における力追従と圧力の均一性を報告した。

2611.22180.title: CueClash: Frontier Vision-Language Models Judge 3-D Relations Close to the Picture Plane
2611.22180.abstract: A vision-language model (VLM) can judge 3-D relations from the picture or from the ground layout. In photographs the two usually agree. We separate them with CueClash, rendered scenes in which the 2-D cue for each of five relations is right on exactly half the statements. The shortcut gap is accuracy when the cue is right minus accuracy when it is wrong. For Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.6 Flash at low reasoning effort it is +18 to +37 percentage points. It is +7 to +29 without two relations whose cue-wrong items are confounded with borderline cases or occlusion. Given ground coordinates and each relation's definition, they answer 99 to 100% correctly. Pixel measurements with camera depths remove most of the gap for objects fitting through openings. The failure lies in the step from the picture to the layout. The maps that the models draw of the scene from above mostly keep the depth order but, like the picture, shorten depth. GPT-5.5's maps stay close to a copy of the picture. Opus 5.5's and Gemini's maps undo about 0.6 of this shortening. Gemini's then shrink all depths by a further uniform factor. Opus 5.5 follows the picture mainly on fits, and its maps correct depth about as much as human observers of real scenes do. The three models also lose accuracy on CV-Bench photographs where a reliable 2-D cue misleads. In two open models the layout information reaches the language model, but their maps lose much of it.

llm.title_ja: CueClash: 画像平面付近の3次元関係を判断する最先端の視覚言語モデル
llm.tldr_ja: VLMが写真から3次元関係を判断する際の手がかりの衝突を調査するベンチマーク「CueClash」を提案し、モデルが写真からレイアウトへの変換ステップで失敗する傾向を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 視覚言語モデル（VLM）は写真や地面のレイアウトから3次元関係を判断する際に誤りを起こしやすい。
llm.method: 2次元の手がかりが対立するレンダリングシーンを用いたCueClashベンチマークにより、Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-5.5、Gemini 3.6 Flashなどの推論能力を評価した。
llm.result: モデルは写真からレイアウトへのステップで精度が低下し、生成されるマップは深度を短縮化する傾向があることが示された。

2611.22180.tldr_en: A vision-language model (VLM) that can judge 3-D relations from the picture or from the ground layout loses accuracy on CV-Bench photographs where a reliable 2-D cue misleads, and in two open models the layout information reaches the language model, but their maps lose much of it.

2611.22174.title: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
2611.22174.abstract: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We study this capability as reconfigurability, the ability to realize new behaviors by cost-efficiently restructuring existing components and relations under sparse governing information, where task specifications provide high-level goals and procedure specifications expose a limited set of reusable factors, leaving the concrete bindings and compositions required for execution underdetermined. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and materializes executable skill sequences by composing stored transitions to realize task-specific changes. RecPo maintains a procedure knowledge base of skill-induced transitions, with each view exposing a reusable factor and preserving local skill connectivity. At deployment, it interprets task specifications through the same views and resolves the resulting compositional queries over the stored relations to bind skills for execution. On long-horizon tasks in an extended Franka Kitchen benchmark, RecPo achieves 91.9% ordered completion with 1.0 ms of task inference per episode across varying procedure support and task-record sparsity. Real-robot studies further demonstrate adaptation through local memory edits without task-specific retraining.

llm.title_ja: 構成的ロボットスキル適応のための手続き的知識の再構成
llm.tldr_ja: 既存の手続き的知識を再構成することで、スパースな情報から新しいタスク目標へとコスト効率よくロボットスキルを適応させるフレームワーク「RecPo」を提案する。
llm.problem: 汎用行動モデルの新しい目標やスキルインターフェースへの適応において、既存のコンピテンスを再構成することが求められる。
llm.method: 複数の手続きビューを通じてスキルをタスク非依存に表現し、保存された遷移を組み合わせて実行可能なスキル配列を生成するRecPoを提案する。
llm.result: 拡張されたFranka Kitchenベンチマークにおいて91.9%の順序付き完了率を達成し、実機でのタスク非依存な適応を示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22174.tldr_en: RecPo is proposed, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and materializes executable skill sequences by composing stored transitions to realize task-specific changes.

2611.22151.title: EgoHandWAM: Probing the Role of Hand Motion in Egocentric World Action Modeling
2611.22151.abstract: How much does hand motion tell us about what a first-person camera will see next? EgoHandWAM forecasts three-dimensional wrist and fingertip trajectories and a future visual feature from the current image and recent hand states. We train on 751,065 EgoDex windows using a frozen DINOv2 encoder. On held-out development sessions, the action-only model reduces two-second wrist endpoint error from 60.26 to 56.48~mm relative to a stationary forecast. It still underestimates long reaches. Adding future-feature supervision gives nearly identical trajectory accuracy. With the recorded hand history, the visual head reduces smooth L1 error by 1.32\% relative to copying the current feature. Shuffling histories across sessions erases this gain. In a separate four-task probe, adding recorded future displacements to observed context and future tracking-validity masks reduces visual-feature error by 3.93\%. Masks alone give little improvement. A trajectory predicted from the same observations adds little. On two simulated RoboTwin tasks, substituting aligned human examples for an auxiliary batch of robot examples gives no consistent increase in task success across three training seeds.

llm.title_ja: EgoHandWAM: 独白型一人称視点世界行動モデリングにおける手の動きの役割の検証
llm.tldr_ja: 一人称視点カメラの将来の映像予測において手の動きが果たす役割を調査するため、手首・指先の軌跡と視覚特徴を予測するEgoHandWAMを提案する。
llm.problem: 一人称視点カメラの将来像予測において、手の動きがどれほど情報を与えるのかが十分に解明されていない。
llm.method: 凍結されたDINOv2エンコーダを用いて手首や指先の3D軌跡と将来の視覚特徴を予測するEgoHandWAMを訓練し、多様なプローブを用いて検証した。
llm.result: 行動のみのモデルにより静止予測と比較して手首のエンドポイント誤差が削減され、過去の手の履歴の活用が視覚特徴の予測誤差を低減することを示した。

2611.22151.tldr_en: EgoHandWAM forecasts three-dimensional wrist and fingertip trajectories and a future visual feature from the current image and recent hand states and finds that adding future-feature supervision gives nearly identical trajectory accuracy.

2611.22146.title: HandUMI: A Modular Hand-Worn Parallel-Jaw Interface for Robot-Free Bimanual Data Capture
2611.22146.abstract: HandUMI captures robot-free bimanual demonstrations with a hand-worn parallel-jaw interface. Swappable fingertips match the robot's installed gripper; Quest/PICO controllers track hands and encoders measure aperture. Robot-agnostic recordings are retargeted by inverse kinematics to seven simulated bimanual arms (median position error $\leq 1.2$ mm; $\leq 4.7$% of episodes rejected). On bimanual towel folding, 562 robot-free demonstrations train policies on real PiPER arms: ACT succeeds in 12/20 attempts and fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ in 7/20; ACT on the first 101 and base $π_{0.5}$ each succeed in 0/20. Hardware and software are open source (Apache-2.0), and a pair costs USD 557 with Quest 3S, excluding the optional ZED Mini and host computer. Project website: https://murobotics.ai/research/handumi.

llm.title_ja: HandUMI: ロボット不要の双腕データ収集に向けたモジュール式ハンド装着型平行グリッパーインターフェース
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットを使用せずに双腕のデモデータを低コストで収集するため、交換可能な指先とトラッキングコントローラーを備えたハンド装着型インターフェース「HandUMI」を提案する。
llm.problem: ロボットを使用しない双腕デモデータの収集はコストがかかり、既存のインターフェースでは柔軟性が不足している。
llm.method: ハンド装着型の平行グリッパーインターフェース「HandUMI」を開発し、逆運動学を介してシミュレーションおよび実機の双腕アームにデータを適用する。
llm.result: 双腕タオル畳みタスクにおいてロボット不要のデモからポリシーを訓練し、ACTや微調整されたπ0.5の有効性を実証した。
keywords_ja: 双腕マニピュレーション

2611.22146.tldr_en: HandUMI captures robot-free bimanual demonstrations with a hand-worn parallel-jaw interface that trains policies on real PiPER arms and retargeted by inverse kinematics to seven simulated bimanual arms.

2611.22138.title: RoboTeam: Benchmarking Vision-Based Multi-Agent Control of Many Robot Arms in Real Time
2611.22138.abstract: Multimodal agents can now control robot arms by calling tools and writing code. Existing benchmarks fall short in three ways: most test one or two arms on short tasks, many pause the world while the agent thinks, and many give it ground-truth object positions. We present RoboTeam, a simulated benchmark where agents control 4 to 16 robot arms in real time from camera images alone. Its 36 tasks are long jobs that the arms must do together, such as passing timbers or building a picture from hundreds of cubes. We start from the most flexible agent system, the adaptive system, where one agent decides when to fork delegates. With it, gpt-6.1-sol and opus-5.5 complete 28 and 27 tasks, and four other models at most 3. But at a high price: a typical task takes gpt-6.1-sol 3.5 hours and 218 million input tokens, and a third of its steps fail at least once and must be retried. We then compare it with three fixed systems: single-agent, hierarchical, and decentralized. All four complete a similar number of tasks but differ in time and tokens. The hierarchical and decentralized systems are faster but use up to 1.9 times the tokens, and the single agent uses fewer tokens but takes 1.6 times as long, so the adaptive system lies between them. Even so, no model or system is yet fast, cheap, and reliable at once. RoboTeam measures these limits where earlier benchmarks cannot: long multi-arm jobs, camera images only, and a world that never pauses.

llm.title_ja: RoboTeam: カメラ画像のみによる多数のロボットアームのリアルタイム視覚ベースマルチエージェント制御のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: カメラ画像のみを用いてリアルタイムで多数のロボットアームを協調制御する能力を評価するシミュレーションベンチマーク「RoboTeam」を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは1〜2本のアームの短いタスクのテストに偏っており、リアルタイム性や完全なカメラ画像のみの入力を十分に扱えていない。
llm.method: 4〜16台のロボットアームを同時に制御する36の長期タスクからなるシミュレーションベンチマーク「RoboTeam」を構築し、適応型および固定型のマルチエージェントシステムを評価した。
llm.result: 適応型システムによりGPT-6.1-solやOpus-5.5が多くのタスクを完了できる一方で、膨大なトークン消費や処理時間などの課題が明らかになった。
keywords_ja: マルチエージェント制御

2611.22138.tldr_en: RoboTeam is presented, a simulated benchmark where agents control 4 to 16 robot arms in real time from camera images alone, where earlier benchmarks cannot: long multi-arm jobs, camera images only, and a world that never pauses.

2611.22132.title: DailyBrick: Language-Guided Synthesis of Brick Assembly Instructions
2611.22132.abstract: Generating a LEGO model from a user request is more than a plausible 3D shape generation. LEGO models require physical support per brick, and each brick should be placed unblocked. Current methods address this issue by training an expert large language model. We reduce the problem of generating extremely long context on all brick connections to that of writing a program that builds LEGO models like a human, considering each intermediate step could be executed. We introduce DailyBrick , a multi-stage agentic system that produces a LEGO model together with a brick-by-brick assembly instruction for human building and robot assembly. We design a multi-stage harness with roles to help LLMs generate more effectively. A versioned construction SDK compiles multi-level decisions, from semantic subparts to individual bricks, into canonical operations. An external Meta-Reviewer agent replays and inspects the generated package, verifies the model and its construction process, identifies failures, traces them to the responsible stage, and routes them to bounded repairs or to editable candidates for later skill or tool updates. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DailyBrick generates LEGO models based on simple user requests better than recent agentic systems, and show its utility in downstream applications such as robot manipulations on model assembly from instructions and brick sets (https://SpatialAgent.github.io/DailyBrick/).

llm.title_ja: DailyBrick: 言語指示に基づくブロック組み立て手順の合成
llm.tldr_ja: ユーザーの指示から物理的支援や干渉を考慮したLEGOモデルと人間・ロボット向けの組み立て手順を生成するマルチステージエージェントシステム「DailyBrick」を提案する。
llm.problem: ユーザーのリクエストからLEGOモデルを生成するには、物理的サポートや未ブロック状態の配置を考慮する必要がある。
llm.method: 役割を持つマルチステージハーネス、セマンティックなサブパーツから個々のブロックまでを統合するSDK、および生成パッケージを検証するメタレビュワーエージェントからなるDailyBrickを提案する。
llm.result: DailyBrickは単純なユーザーリクエストから優れたLEGOモデルを生成し、指示やパーツセットを用いたロボット組み立てなどの下流タスクでの有用性を示した。
keywords_ja: エージェントシステム
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22132.tldr_en: DailyBrick is introduced, a multi-stage agentic system that produces a LEGO model together with a brick-by-brick assembly instruction for human building and robot assembly, and a multi-stage harness with roles to help LLMs generate more effectively.

2611.22122.title: Low-speed Limit Cycle Walking of Planar X-shaped Bipedal Robot with Special Properties
2611.22122.abstract: This paper proposes a novel planar semicircular-footed X-shaped bipedal robot in which the center of mass of each leg link is at the same position as the hip joint, and discusses a method for generating a stable limit cycle gait on level ground. First, we outline the assumptions of the robot model with four degrees of freedom, and develop the mathematical equations of motion and collision. Second, we set the relative hip-joint angle as a control output and design a control system to follow it to the desired trajectory specified as a fifth-order function of time. Third, we mathematically show that there are special properties: the angular velocity of the swing leg does not change before and after the collision, and the time-integral of the control input becomes zero in a steady gait. We also mathematically show that the model has the feature that approximate linearization is effective and the antigravity effect of semicircular feet can be utilized. Through numerical simulations, we verify the validity of the theoretical results, and analyze some fundamental gait properties such as convergence speed and mechanical energy restoration.
2611.22122.comment: 6 pages, 7 figures. Published in the Proceedings of IEEE ICARM 2023. This author version corrects bibliographic information and minor typographical errors in a table and figure labels; the scientific content remains unchanged

llm.title_ja: 特殊な特性を持つ平面X字型二足歩行ロボットの低速リミットサイクル歩行
llm.tldr_ja: 各脚リンクの重心が股関節と同じ位置にある新しい平面半円足型X字型二足歩行ロボットを提案し、平地での安定したリミットサイクル歩行の生成方法を論じる。
llm.problem: 二足歩行ロボットの安定した低速歩行の実現と歩行特性の解析が求められている。
llm.method: 4自由度のロボットモデルの運動方程式と衝突方程式を導出し、相対股関節角度を制御出力とする制御システムを設計して数学的特性を証明した。
llm.result: 数値シミュレーションを通じて理論的結果の妥当性を検証し、収束速度や機械的エネルギー復元などの基本的な歩行特性を明らかにした。

2611.22122.venue: International Conference on Advanced Robotics and Mechatronics

2611.22109.title: VTT: Reading Vehicle Size and Powertrain Type from Motion Trajectory Across Unseen Car Models
2611.22109.abstract: Vehicle size and powertrain information can enrich trajectory data for traffic analysis and simulation. We present VTT, a dataset and benchmark for identifying these attributes from motion and controller area network (CAN) signals across unseen car models. The dataset contains 9,062 drives, about 3,950 h, from 1,431 vehicles and 174 car models. It provides three footprint-based size classes, powertrain labels, and evaluation on unseen car models and unseen drivers. Using 60-s windows, we compare four sequence architectures, statistical features and physical features proposed by large language models. Training with auxiliary physical targets, data augmentation and task-specific weighting raises drive-level macro-F1 to 92.6-93.0% for battery-electric versus combustion vehicles and from 62.9% to 67.1% for size classification. On public logs from 4,061 additional drivers, the full-input model identifies powertrain correctly for 86 of 88 car models; size accuracy is 63.2%, close to the internal vehicle-level result of 63.5%. Physical-feature analysis links powertrain recognition to deceleration behaviour and size recognition to steering response. Errors near size-class boundaries and limited gains from longer observations highlight the importance of label resolution and training-fleet coverage for cross-model generalisation.

llm.title_ja: VTT: 未知の車種にわたる運動軌跡からの車両サイズとパワートレインタイプの読み取り
llm.tldr_ja: 交通解析やシミュレーションの軌跡データを豊かにするため、運動およびCAN信号から車両サイズとパワートレインを識別するデータセットとベンチマーク「VTT」を提案する。
llm.problem: 交通解析において、未知の車種の車両サイズやパワートレイン情報を運動データから正確に識別する必要がある。
llm.method: 1,431台の車両による9,062件のドライブデータを含むVTTデータセットを構築し、大規模言語モデルが提案する物理的特徴量を用いたシーケンスアーキテクチャを比較評価した。
llm.result: 補助的な物理ターゲットを用いた学習により、電気自動車と内燃機関車の識別におけるマクロF1スコアが向上し、未知の車種への汎化性能を示した。

2611.22109.tldr_en: VTT, a dataset and benchmark for identifying these attributes from motion and controller area network (CAN) signals across unseen car models, is presented and four sequence architectures, statistical features and physical features proposed by large language models are compared.

2611.22080.title: CRA: Continuous Risk Assessment for Safety-critical Visual Navigation
2611.22080.abstract: Traditional safety-critical control methods often rely on predefined constraints that separate states into safe and unsafe regions. While recent studies have extended geometric safety toward semantic safety, real-world safety is rarely purely binary. The risk associated with an object or human can vary continuously with its physical properties, like motion, and interaction context; for example, a person carrying a heavy object or a hot object moving at high speed may require a different safety response from an ordinary static obstacle. In this paper, we propose a vision-based continuous risk assessment framework for safety-critical visual navigation. Our method uses RGB and LiDAR observations to estimate four risk factors (kinetic, potential, contact-severity, and thermal) and combines them into a continuous risk score for each assessed object or person. These estimates are integrated into a Poisson safety function with a Laplace guidance field as a safety filter, enabling online monitoring and intervention in open-world robot navigation. We demonstrate the proposed method in a simulated restaurant scene.

llm.title_ja: CRA: 安全性クリティカルな視覚ナビゲーションのための継続的リスク評価
llm.tldr_ja: 実世界の安全性を連続的に評価するため、RGBとLiDARの観測から4つのリスクファクターを推定し安全フィルタとして統合するフレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 従来の安全性制御は二値的な制約に依存しており、移動体や人の物理的性質やインタラクション文脈に応じた連続的なリスクに対応できない。
llm.method: RGBとLiDARの観測から運動エネルギー、位置エネルギー、接触の厳しさ、熱的リスクの4つを推定し、ラプラス誘導場を持つポアソン安全性関数に統合する。
llm.result: シミュレートされたレストランシーンにおいて、オープンワールドでのロボットナビゲーションにおけるオンライン監視と介入の実証を行った。

2611.22080.tldr_en: A vision-based continuous risk assessment framework for safety-critical visual navigation that uses RGB and LiDAR observations to estimate four risk factors and combines them into a continuous risk score for each assessed object or person, enabling online monitoring and intervention in open-world robot navigation.

2611.22077.title: ReLAP: Latent Action Pretraining through Recurrent Video Prediction in JEPA Space
2611.22077.abstract: Videos provide a rich source of physical interaction for learning robot behavior without action annotations, yet effective latent actions must capture not only local transitions but also how those transitions evolve over time. We introduce ReLAP, a latent-action pretraining framework that couples local transition learning with recurrent multi-step prediction in a frozen JEPA representation space. A shared inverse dynamics model infers compact continuous latent actions from adjacent observations, while a latent world model recurrently predicts the future JEPA features. Because each predicted feature becomes the context for the next transition, errors at later steps backpropagate through the rollout to earlier latent actions, encouraging temporally coherent dynamics beyond pairwise reconstruction. We transfer this representation to a vision-language model using two complementary objectives: latent distillation from the frozen inverse teacher and recurrent future-feature prediction through the frozen latent world model. The resulting policy is then adapted to robot demonstrations with action flow matching. At deployment, the explicit latent-action and world-model branches are removed, and the fine-tuned VLM predicts physical actions directly, reducing inference complexity. With only 11M pretraining samples and 1.06B trainable parameters, ReLAP achieves 97.9% on standard LIBERO and 70.0% over zero-shot LIBERO-Plus perturbations. On the LARY latent-action benchmark, ReLAP ranks second in both mean regression error and mean classification accuracy among the compared methods. These results demonstrate that recurrent action-free latent action pretraining can learn compact, temporally structured, and transferable representations for downstream robot control.

llm.title_ja: ReLAP: JEPA空間におけるリカレント動画予測を通じた潜在行動事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: 行動アノテーションなしでロボットの行動を学習するため、JEPA表現空間における局所遷移学習とリカレント多ステップ予測を組み合わせた潜在行動事前学習フレームワーク「ReLAP」を提案する。
llm.problem: 行動注釈なしで動画からロボット行動を学習する際、局所的遷移だけでなく時間的な変化を捉える効果的な潜在行動が必要となる。
llm.method: 逆ダイナミクスモデルで連続的な潜在行動を推論し、凍結されたJEPA表現空間で潜在世界モデルを用いて将来の特徴をリカレントに予測するReLAPを提案する。
llm.result: 標準LIBEROで97.9%を達成し、コンパクトで時間的に構造化された表現学習によりダウンストリームのロボット制御性能を向上させた。

2611.22077.tldr_en: ReLAP, a latent-action pretraining framework that couples local transition learning with recurrent multi-step prediction in a frozen JEPA representation space, is introduced, demonstrating that recurrent action-free latent action pretraining can learn compact, temporally structured, and transferable representations for downstream robot control.

2611.22047.title: SE(3)-LIVOM: Adaptive Multi-LiDAR-Inertial-Visual Odometry and Mapping
2611.22047.abstract: This paper presents SE(3)-LIVOM, the overall winner of the COMFORT Challenge at IROS 2026. The challenge asks for the trajectory of a legged robot in the GrandTour dataset, whose scenes include collapsed buildings, construction sites and snowfields. SE(3)-LIVOM runs in real time on two LiDARs, one camera and an IMU. Its frontend extends SE(3)-LIO to multiple LiDARs and a camera. Adaptive downsampling keeps the time per scan near 35 ms within and across scenes. An online backend corrects drift with a plane bundle adjustment over submaps and an incremental pose graph. With a single configuration for all scenes, the system reaches an average ATE of 1.40 cm on the six test scenes. The code is available at https://github.com/url-kaist/se3-livom-comfort.
2611.22047.comment: 3 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Overall winner of the COMFORT Challenge, IROS 2026 Workshop on Data in Field Robotics. Code: https://github.com/url-kaist/se3-livom-comfort

llm.title_ja: SE(3)-LIVOM: 適応型マルチLiDAR・慣性・ビジュアルオドメトリおよびマッピング
llm.tldr_ja: 崩壊した建物や工事現場などの過酷な環境下で脚ロボットの軌跡を高精度に推定し、COMFORTチャレンジで優勝を果たしたリアルタイムのマルチLiDAR・慣性・ビジュアルオドメトリシステム「SE(3)-LIVOM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 崩壊建物や雪原などの過酷な環境において、脚ロボットの正確な軌跡をリアルタイムで推定することが課題である。
llm.method: 2つのLiDAR、1台のカメラ、IMUを使用し、適応型ダウンサンプリングと平面バンドル調整・インクリメンタルポーズグラフによるバックエンドを持つSE(3)-LIVOMを構築した。
llm.result: グランドツアーデータセットのテストシーンにおいて平均ATE 1.40 cmを達成し、チャレンジで総合優勝を果たした。
keywords_ja: ビジュアル慣性オドメトリ

2611.22001.title: DreamFAR: Real-Time and Long-Horizon Interaction with Diverse Objects
2611.22001.abstract: World models have shown great potential in serving as a simulator for robot manipulation. However, existing models are either fit to a single environment or lack ability to simulate long-horizon contact-rich events. We present DreamFAR, a world model whose dynamics model is trained from scratch on a large robot-native teleoperation dataset, with no internet-video pretraining. We present an architecture and learning recipe designed for training on robot-native data. DreamFAR is significantly smaller than the high-performance video generation models, yet shows better understanding of contact and causality, and runs 10 FPS on a commercial GPU. Experimentally, DreamFAR significantly outperforms existing models in predicting the long-horizon future. We further demonstrate various applications where DreamFAR can be used, including policy evaluation and mixed-data co-training. Project page: https://www.yimingdou.com/DreamFAR/

llm.title_ja: DreamFAR: 多様なオブジェクトとのリアルタイムかつ長期的なインタラクション
llm.tldr_ja: ロボット操作のためのシミュレータとして機能する世界モデル「DreamFAR」を提案し、大規模なロボットネイティブのテレオペレーションデータからゼロから訓練する。
llm.problem: 既存の世界モデルは単一の環境に特化しているか、長期的な接触を伴うイベントのシミュレーション能力が不足している。
llm.method: インターネット動画の事前学習を行わず、ロボットネイティブなテレオペレーションデータからゼロからダイナミクスモデルを訓練するアーキテクチャと学習レシピを設計した。
llm.result: 既存モデルを大きく上回る長期将来予測性能を示し、商用GPU上で10 FPSで動作しつつポリシー評価や混合データ共同訓練に活用できることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.22001.tldr_en: DreamFAR is a world model whose dynamics model is trained from scratch on a large robot-native teleoperation dataset, with no internet-video pretraining, and significantly outperforms existing models in predicting the long-horizon future.

2611.21958.title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
2611.21958.abstract: Weight-space programming is a process where a large language model reads and writes the weights of a neural network directly, guided by a natural language specification, without an optimiser or gradient descent. This study applies it to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator. GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (also 5.2) edited the network for our research tractor using a small budget of simulated evaluations to repair a network trained for another tractor and write a controller into a network with zero weights. We compared them with an evolution strategy, gradient descent and pure pursuit in simulation and on the real tractor. Both models read the network and analysed the closed loop with control theory correctly, and Fable's repair without simulation succeeded only occasionally. With simulated feedback, both models repaired the trained network in single sessions and wrote a working controller from zero weights, whereas from zero the evolution strategy found none. The controllers written from zero were sparse and in a classical cascaded structure; one model edited the trained network while the other replaced it. Gradient descent reached higher accuracy with far more simulation, and all language model controllers steered the real tractor without intervention, with errors of the same order as pure pursuit. Language models can program the weights of a neural controller directly, much as control engineers design one. We call this Weight-Space Engineering.
2611.21958.comment: 20 pages, 8 figures, 8 tables (1 in the appendices); includes a field test on a real tractor

llm.title_ja: トラクタ誘導コントローラーのための重み空間プログラミング：大規模言語モデルによる実トラクタを操舵するニューラルネットワーク重みの直接記述
llm.tldr_ja: 最適化や勾配降下法を用いず、大規模言語モデルが自然言語の仕様に基づいてニューラルネットワークの重みを直接読み書きする「重み空間プログラミング」を自動トラクタ誘導に応用する。
llm.problem: トラクタの仕様変更などに対応してステアリングコントローラーを適応させる際、従来の最適化手法には手間がかかる。
llm.method: 大規模言語モデル（GPT-6 AstraやClaude Fable 5.1など）を用いて、シミュレーション評価の予算内で既存ネットワークの修復やゼロからのコントローラー重みの直接編集を行う。
llm.result: 言語モデルが制御理論的に正しいネットワーク解析を行い、シミュレーションと実機の両方において介入なしで実トラクタを正常に操舵するコントローラーを作成できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: 重み空間プログラミング
ニューラルネットワーク

2611.21958.tldr_en: Weight-space programming is applied to automatic tractor guidance, where a 253-parameter neural network steers along paths of lines and arcs and must be adapted when the machine changes, such as a slower steering actuator.

2611.21945.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Wheelchair Configuration Classification in Accessible Automated Vehicle Applications
2611.21945.abstract: Making automated vehicles accessible requires consideration of vulnerable road users, including wheelchair users. To offer a more tailored experience that supports independence for this group, vehicle design needs to accommodate the wide range of wheelchair configurations. However, wheelchairs are individualized, varying in frame geometry, propulsion, and visual appearance. Moreover, occupants or accessories may obscure visual cues. Existing mobility-aid datasets only label the presence of a wheelchair, rather than describing its specific configuration. To fill this gap, this paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), comprising 467 face-blurred images across 192 capture groups solely for evaluation. Each image is annotated with (i) a two-class label of manual or powered, (ii) a chair subtype, (iii) occupancy, viewpoint, setting, lighting, occlusion, propulsion, and control, with a 273-image validation split and 194-image test split. Three convolutional neural network backbones and a frozen vision-language probe are trained on an external image dataset and evaluated on WCID to measure cross-dataset generalization, while also testing robustness using Gaussian blur. Convolutional models do well on clean images, but performance drops under strong blur, leaving a gap before deployment. Code, split assignments, labels, trained weights, and the face-blurred images is available at: https://github.com/Mi3-Lab/MAID

llm.title_ja: アクセシブルな自動運転車両アプリケーションにおける車椅子構成分類のためのディープラーニングモデルのベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転車が車椅子ユーザーに合わせたサポートを提供するため、車椅子の構成や種類を分類する新しい画像データセット「WCID」を構築し、ディープラーニングモデルを評価する。
llm.problem: 既存の移動補助具データセットは車椅子の存在を示すのみで、個別の構成や形状のバリエーションを記述していない。
llm.method: 467枚の顔をぼかした画像を含む車椅子構成画像データセット（WCID）を構築し、CNNおよび凍結されたVLMプローブを評価してクロスデータセット汎化性とガウスぼかしに対する堅牢性を検証した。
llm.result: クリーンな画像ではCNNが優れた性能を示したが、強いぼかしに対しては性能が低下し、デプロイに向けた課題が残ることを明らかにした。

2611.21945.tldr_en: This paper introduces the Wheelchair Configuration Image Dataset (WCID), comprising 467 face-blurred images across 192 capture groups solely for evaluation, and introduces convolutional neural network backbones and a frozen vision-language probe to measure cross-dataset generalization.

2611.21938.title: HubEgo-100K: In-the-Wild Egocentric Video of Skilled Work for Robot Learning
2611.21938.abstract: Robot policies trained by imitation generalize poorly outside the environments and objects seen in training. Published data-scaling studies find that generalization grows with the diversity of training environments and objects rather than with more demonstrations per environment. Robot data is costly to collect across many environments, whereas egocentric human video can be recorded in the wild at scale; existing egocentric video, however, mostly shows daily-life activity and contains little skilled work in real workplaces. We present HubEgo-100K, a dataset built for diversity. This version of the paper covers the first release, v1.0: 10,124 hours of 1080p egocentric video with synchronized 100 Hz inertial (IMU) data from one head-mounted phone camera. In v1.0, 12,227 contributors record their own unscripted work in 15,548 environments (each one contributor's own setting of one type, such as their kitchen or workshop) across 11 setting types, 30 work categories, 56 task types and 35 action families, with 83% of hours in workplace settings. The release comprises 72,754 episodes with machine-generated action and language annotations, in LeRobot and MCAP formats under CC BY 4.0. We measure diversity along each axis, show that inside v1.0, with episodes in random order, new contributors and words keep appearing, and relate the measurements to published evidence on six data properties tied to policy performance, including hand visibility and inertial sensing. We also document collection, curation, privacy measures and data format, and provide a datasheet. Later versions of this paper will add benchmarks and cover further releases toward 100,000 hours.

llm.title_ja: HubEgo-100K: ロボット学習に向けた熟練作業の実環境一人称視点動画
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットポリシーの汎化性能を高めるため、頭部マウントカメラによる10,124時間の同期IMUデータを含む大規模な実環境一人称視点動画データセット「HubEgo-100K」を提案する。
llm.problem: 模倣学習で訓練されたロボットポリシーは訓練環境外での汎化性能が低く、多様な実環境での熟練作業データが不足している。
llm.method: 12,227人のコントリビューターによる15,548の多様な環境で収集された10,124時間の1080p一人称視点動画と100 HzのIMUデータを収集・アノテーションして公開する。
llm.result: 多様な作業カテゴリーやアクションファミリを含む大規模なデータセットを構築し、LeRobotおよびMCAPフォーマットで提供した。

2611.21938.tldr_en: This version of the paper covers the first release of HubEgo-100K, a dataset built for diversity that measures diversity along each axis, relates the measurements to published evidence on six data properties tied to policy performance, including hand visibility and inertial sensing.

2611.21919.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
2611.21919.abstract: Learning from human demonstrations has enabled robots to acquire a wide range of manipulation skills, but learned policies typically execute far slower than ordinary humans. This speed gap is mainly due to lack of an interface for collecting demonstration data at high speed, and the difficulty in training policies that can robustly execute high-speed motions. In this paper, we present ALOHA Lightning (Flash ALOHA), a system for learning fast and precise robotic manipulation. Our system uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories. We also present a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action smoothing and aligns the visual data distribution between data collection and deployment with masking. Given 50 demonstrations for each task, ALOHA Lightning autonomously completes bimanual tasks such as ball tossing and catching, folding shorts, battery insertion, and bussing tables for over 80% success rates while close to human speed. Project website: https://flash-aloha.github.io/

llm.title_ja: ALOHA Lightning: 高速かつ精密なマニピュレーションの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 人間のデモデータ収集速度の限界と高速動作ポリシー訓練の難しさを克服し、人間並みの高速で精密な双腕マニピュレーションを実現するシステム「ALOHA Lightning」を提案する。
llm.problem: 学習済みポリシーは人間並みの速度で実行できず、その原因は高速データ収集インターフェースの欠如と高速モーション訓練の難しさにある。
llm.method: バックドライブ可能な双腕プラットフォームを用いた運動学的教授（キネステティック・ティーチング）により高速デモを収集し、テスト時のアクション平滑化やマスク処理による視覚データ分布の整合を行う学習パイプラインを提案する。
llm.result: ボールの投げ渡しや衣類の折り畳み、配膳などの双腕タスクにおいて、50回のデモで人間並みの速度と80%以上の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.21919.tldr_en: This paper uses kinesthetic teaching to intuitively collect near-human-speed demonstrations on a backdrivable bimanual platform, yielding natural and fast trajectories and presents a learning pipeline that enables smooth high-speed execution through test-time action smoothing and aligns the visual data distribution between data collection and deployment with masking.
2611.21919.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation

2611.21908.title: From Human Videos to Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Data: Confidence-Guided RL Refinement of Video Priors
2611.21908.abstract: Collecting demonstrations for bimanual dexterous manipulation is costly, motivating the use of human videos as a source of robot training data. However, uncertainty in video-derived motion estimates and differences between human and robot embodiments make direct motion transfer challenging. In this work, we introduce PriDex, a framework that transforms human-video Priors into executable robot Dexterous manipulation demonstrations through reinforcement learning in simulation. PriDex preserves task-relevant interaction structure while allowing embodiment-specific behavior to be regenerated for the robot. Human-object interactions provide affordance cues for selecting task-relevant, robot-specific grasps from geometry-based candidates. For motion refinement, object trajectories provide a task-level reference, while relative bimanual wrist trajectories offer complementary guidance for coordinated motion. Since object-motion estimates can become unreliable under occlusion or visual ambiguity, PriDex uses object-motion confidence to adaptively balance these two priors, emphasizing object-level guidance when confidence is high and increasing the contribution of wrist-level guidance as confidence decreases. Reinforcement learning refines these video-derived priors under the robot's kinematic and physical constraints, and the resulting policies are rolled out to generate robot demonstrations for training a vision-based diffusion policy. We evaluate PriDex on four bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks, including pouring, sweeping into a dustpan, bottle-cap unscrewing, and plate cleaning, assessing both simulation-based robot data generation and downstream visuomotor policy learning.

llm.title_ja: 人間の動画から双腕器用マニピュレーションデータへ：動画事前学習の信頼性誘導強化学習リファインメント
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の動画をロボット訓練データに変換する際の不確実性と構造差を克服するため、強化学習を用いて動画事前学習を洗練させるフレームワーク「PriDex」を提案する。
llm.problem: 双腕器用マニピュレーションのデモ収集はコストがかかり、動画からの動作推定の不確実性や人間とロボットの身体性の違いにより直接的な動作転移が困難である。
llm.method: 対象物の軌跡と手首の軌跡を補完的に用い、オブジェクトの動きの信頼性に基づいて適応的にバランスを取りながら強化学習で事前学習を洗練させるPriDexを提案する。
llm.result: 液体の注ぎ込みやごみ箱への掃き込みなど4つの双腕器用マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、シミュレーションデータ生成と視覚運動ポリシー学習の有効性を評価した。
keywords_ja: 双腕マニピュレーション

2611.21908.tldr_en: This work introduces PriDex, a framework that transforms human-video Priors into executable robot Dexterous manipulation demonstrations through reinforcement learning in simulation, which preserves task-relevant interaction structure while allowing embodiment-specific behavior to be regenerated for the robot.

2611.21905.title: Agile Monoped Hopping on Complex and Discrete Terrain via Kinodynamic Planning with Distilled MPPI Steering
2611.21905.abstract: This paper presents FlowRRT, a kinodynamic planner for agile monoped hopping on discrete terrain. Steering for kinodynamic RRT on complex dynamical systems currently relies on motion primitives or closed-loop policies, limiting the diversity of motions or the planning speed. Distilling a trajectory optimizer avoids both, but existing methods regress a single solution per query, which fails on monoped hopping, where the feasible action set is narrow and disconnected. Our key insight is to treat steering as set-valued and predict the distribution of feasible actions instead. A multi-start MPPI expert collects the entire feasible set of each query offline, and conditional flow matching distills it into a generative sampler. With this sampler, FlowRRT coordinates successive jumps over long horizons and finds non-greedy maneuvers that are hard for reactive policies to discover. Benchmarks across different terrains show higher success rates and substantially shorter planning times than sampling-based baselines. On terrains with inclined platforms, FlowRRT reaches $80\%$ success within $1$~s, versus $24$~s for RL-RRT and $77$~s for SST. Sim-to-sim tracking in MuJoCo confirms accurate execution under full-order dynamics.

llm.title_ja: 蒸留されたMPPIステアリングを用いた運動学的計画による複雑かつ離散的な地形でのアジャイルな単脚ホッピング
llm.tldr_ja: 離散的な地形におけるアジャイルな単脚ホッピングを実現するため、条件付きフローマッチングを用いて実行可能なアクションの分布を予測する運動学的プランナー「FlowRRT」を提案する。
llm.problem: 複雑な力学系における運動学的RRTのステアリングは動作プリミティブや反応型ポリシーに依存しており、動作の多様性や計画速度が制限される。
llm.method: マルチスタートMPPIエキスパートにより各クエリの実行可能な集合をオフラインで収集し、条件付きフローマッチングによって生成サンプラーへと蒸留するFlowRRTを提案する。
llm.result: 傾斜プラットフォームなどの複雑な地形において、ベースライン手法と比較して高い成功率と大幅に短い計画時間を達成した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.21905.tldr_en: FlowRRT is presented, a kinodynamic planner for agile monoped hopping on discrete terrain to treat steering as set-valued and predict the distribution of feasible actions instead, which shows higher success rates and substantially shorter planning times than sampling-based baselines.

2611.21885.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
2611.21885.abstract: A language model is trained once and frozen. Making it better takes another training run, or a prompt, a harness or extra computation at inference that is gone once the task ends. We show a third way: to our knowledge for the first time, a language model rewrites its own weights by its own reasoning and becomes better, with no gradients and no training. We call this self-rewriting: the model is its own optimizer. In earlier work, a frontier model edited a much smaller one; here an open 27B model, given its weights, its graded answers and the ability to run itself, diagnoses its own failure and rewrites the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on problems it never saw. It keeps getting better: it tests its edits on practice problems and submits only what works, each edit improving on the last, and over eight consecutive sessions its accuracy only rises. It repairs a damaged copy of itself, like a broken robot that fixes itself without being rebuilt: the copy solves almost nothing, yet with no retraining and without ever reading the original weights, the model brings it back to over 80% of the original accuracy on image tasks it never saw. And the ability emerges with scale: in one model family, the smaller models make no edit or break themselves, and only the largest improves and repairs itself. Unlike test-time scaling, self-rewriting writes its gain into the weights, at no cost per answer; unlike training, it runs only forward passes, as serving does. The wall between training and inference is a limit of our tools, not a property of intelligence. We believe self-rewriting is a necessary step toward recursive self-improvement: a model that, like a human, does not separate training from inference could keep upgrading itself for life, with no larger model, no harness or prompt engineering, and no pre- or post-training.
2611.21885.tldr_en: Self-rewriting is a necessary step toward recursive self-improvement: a model that, like a human, does not separate training from inference could keep upgrading itself for life, with no larger model, no harness or prompt engineering, and no pre- or post-training.

llm.title_ja: 言語モデルは自身の重みを書き換えることができる
llm.tldr_ja: 言語モデルが勾配や再学習なしに自身の推論によって自身の重みを書き換え、未見の問題に対する精度を向上させることができる自己書き換え手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 言語モデルの性能向上には追加の学習やプロンプト、推論時の追加計算が必要であり、学習と推論の壁が存在している。
llm.method: オープンな27Bモデルに自身の重み、採点済みの回答、および自身を実行する能力を与え、自己の失敗を診断して重みを書き換える自己書き換え機構を導入した。
llm.result: 未見の問題に対する精度が6.6ポイント向上し、破損した自己のコピーを修復して元の精度を80%以上に回復させることができた。

2611.21851.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
2611.21851.abstract: Autonomous driving requires anticipating how traffic will evolve while responding quickly to new observations. Video foundation models offer the first ability, but repeated history encoding and iterative video generation make them costly to use for driving. We present AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning. Because its video backbone is causal, AR-WAM updates its visual context incrementally, reusing past computation and conditioning future prediction on observed motion. We further hypothesize that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation. AR-WAM therefore obtains these features in one forward pass and uses them to condition trajectory generation, and reinforcement learning then improves the policy through direct optimization of driving rewards. With a single front camera, AR-WAM achieves 91.5 PDMS after supervised training and 94.0 after reinforcement learning on NAVSIM-v1, outperforming the compared strong end-to-end world-action models. In a dynamic setting of continuous driving, supervised AR-WAM keeps its visual history across decisions and outperforms strong world-action baselines.

llm.title_ja: AR-WAM：自動運転のための効率的なストリーミング世界行動モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転向けに、因果的な動画バックボーンを用いて視覚コンテキストを段階的に更新し、強化学習でポリシーを改善する効率的なストリーミング世界行動モデル「AR-WAM」を提案する。
llm.problem: 動画基盤モデルは歴史符号化の繰り返しや反復的な動画生成のため、運転用途ではコストが高い。
llm.method: 自己回帰的な時間的モデリングと1パスの将来条件付けを組み合わせ、強化学習により駆動報酬を最適化する。
llm.result: NAVSIM-v1での強化学習後に94.0 PDMSを達成し、既存の強力なエンドツーエンド世界行動モデルを上回った。
keywords_ja: エンドツーエンド学習

2611.21851.tldr_en: This work presents AR-WAM, an efficient streaming world-action model that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning, and hypothesizes that future features computed from recent observations can improve generalization in dynamic traffic without iterative video generation.

2611.21846.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection
2611.21846.abstract: Deepfake detectors often perform well on the dataset they are trained on, but their performance drops when tested on videos from different datasets. In this paper, we study whether a predictive video model can provide a signal that generalizes better across datasets. Instead of relying only on generator-specific artifacts, as many existing detectors do, we use a model trained to predict natural video and measure the difference between what it predicts and what it observes in a video. Using V-JEPA 2.1, we keep the encoder frozen and adapt the predictor using rank-16 LoRA. We define the difference between the predictor output and the frozen encoder target as the prediction residual. We hypothesize that manipulated clips produce, on average, larger prediction residuals than authentic clips, and use this as our consistency-margin prior. We process these residuals using a lightweight Latent Consistency Head (LCH), which separates residual magnitude from direction for training and classification. To test whether the direction of the consistency margin affects cross-dataset generalization, we compare standard and reversed margin objectives while keeping the remaining training setup fixed. We match the two settings on FF++ validation performance before evaluating them on unseen data. The reversed-margin setting exhibits a larger cross dataset generalization gap on average, providing evidence that the direction of the consistency margin affects cross-dataset transfer. Our complete model adds only 8.25M trainable parameters, which is 2.47% of the total 334M parameters. Trained only on FF++, it achieves an AUC of 90.5 on Celeb-DFv2 and performs well across several other cross-dataset benchmarks. Our ablations show that separating residual magnitude from direction, reducing dataset-specific variation, and using a low-rank projection improve cross-dataset generalization in our experiments.

llm.title_ja: 世界モデルはディープフェイク動画を予測できるか：ディープフェイク検出のための整合性マージン事前分布
llm.tldr_ja: 自然動画の予測モデルを用いて観察値との差分（予測残差）を測定し、整合性マージン事前分布と軽量なヘッドを活用することで、データセット横断的な汎化性能を高めたディープフェイク検出手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のディープフェイク検出器は、異なるデータセットの動画に対してテストすると性能が低下する。
llm.method: V-JEPA 2.1のエンコーダを凍結しLoRAで予測器を適応させ、予測残差の大きさ・方向を分離する軽量ヘッドで処理する。
llm.result: FF++のみで学習し、Celeb-DFv2で90.5のAUCを達成し、他のデータセット横断ベンチマークでも良好に機能した。
keywords_ja: ディープフェイク検出

2611.21846.tldr_en: These ablations show that separating residual magnitude from direction, reducing dataset-specific variation, and using a low-rank projection improve cross-dataset generalization in the authors' experiments.

2611.21811.title: ARC-2: Continuous Compliance Through Delta Management
2611.21811.abstract: ARC 1 introduced a three-layer governance architecture for autonomous systems comprising model safety validation, cognitive certification (CRAB), and operational authorization (LEA). However, it did not address how compliance should be maintained after deployment. This paper introduces Delta Management, a continuous governance framework that measures deviations between a system's current operational state and its certified baseline, defined as a region rather than a fixed point. Compliance is assessed through continuous monitoring instead of static certification. Four extensions are proposed. First, CRAB evaluation incorporates the worst verified behavioral deviations, with isolated outliers quarantined pending confirmation to prevent unjustified restrictions. Second, a layered trigger taxonomy distinguishes hard safety violations, critical single-dimension failures, correlated multi-system degradation, and risk-weighted composite indicators, each triggering proportionate responses. Third, a graduated safe transition protocol separates withdrawal of operational authorization from physical shutdown, consistent with established safety standards and EU AI Act requirements. Fourth, environmental delta is introduced as a distinct baseline validity condition: environmental drift beyond the certified Operational Design Domain (ODD) triggers recertification or ODD revision rather than automatic authority contraction. Together, these extensions transform ARC from a deployment-time certification architecture into a continuous framework for monitoring, evaluating, and enforcing compliance throughout the operational lifecycle of autonomous systems. The framework addresses the continuous compliance obligations established by EU AI Act Article 72(2).
2611.21811.comment: 22 pages. Conceptual framework for continuous compliance monitoring, behavioral drift detection, and operational authorization of autonomous robotic systems. Extends ARC-1 (arXiv:2609.12932)

llm.title_ja: ARC-2：デルタ管理による継続的コンプライアンス
llm.tldr_ja: 自律システムの運用ライフサイクル全体にわたって、システムの状態と認証済みベースライン間の偏差を監視・評価してコンプライアンスを維持する「デルタ管理」フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: ARC 1の3層ガバナンスアーキテクチャは、デプロイ後のコンプライアンス維持方法に対処していなかった。
llm.method: 最悪の行動偏差の組み込み、階層型トリガー分類、段階的安全移行プロトコル、環境デルタの導入によりARCを拡張する。
llm.result: 自律システムの運用ライフサイクル全体を通じてコンプライアンスを監視・評価・強制する継続的フレームワークを構築した。

2611.21811.tldr_en: Delta Management is introduced, a continuous governance framework that measures deviations between a system's current operational state and its certified baseline, defined as a region rather than a fixed point, to address the continuous compliance obligations established by EU AI Act Article 72(2).

2611.21806.title: A Probabilistic Lateral Motion Prediction Model with Improved Response Fidelity for Vehicle-in-the-Loop Simulation
2611.21806.abstract: Vehicle-in-the-loop (VIL) simulation requires a lateral dynamics model that accurately reproduces vehicle responses and reliably generates horizontal lateral-position and heading commands through recursive integration. This paper presents a probabilistic lateral motion prediction model with improved response fidelity. A two-degree-of-freedom vehicle model provides the physical prior, while a recurrent neural network learns correlated residual corrections to lateral acceleration and yaw rate. To maintain prediction fidelity during recursive motion generation, multistep rollout training feeds corrected responses into subsequent states and histories and directly penalizes accumulated lateral-velocity error. A conditional Gaussian characterizes response uncertainty, which is propagated to lateral-response, position, and heading predictions through augmented-state linearization. Evaluation results demonstrate improved lateral-response and integrated-motion prediction. Compared with the Deep Dynamics lateral adaptation, the proposed model reduces mean lateral-position root-mean-square error (RMSE) from 0.596 m to 0.483 m, an improvement of 19.0%, while reducing mean lateral-velocity RMSE from 0.0469 m/s to 0.0441 m/s. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining physical priors, probabilistic residual learning, and multistep rollout training for response-faithful lateral motion prediction.

llm.title_ja: 車両インザループシミュレーションのための応答忠実度を向上させた確率的横方向運動予測モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 物理事前分布とリカレントニューラルネットワークによる相関残差補正、および多ステップロールアウト学習を組み合わせた確率的横方向運動予測モデルを提案し、予測のRMSEを削減した。
llm.problem: 車両インザループシミュレーションでは、再帰的統合を通じて車両応答を正確に再現する横方向ダイナミクスモデルが必要とされる。
llm.method: 2自由度車両モデルの物理事前分布とRNNによる残差補正を組み合わせ、多ステップロールアウトで学習する。
llm.result: 平均横方向位置RMSEを0.596mから0.483mへ19.0%改善し、予測精度を高めた。

2611.21806.tldr_en: A probabilistic lateral motion prediction model with improved response fidelity is presented, which combines physical priors, probabilistic residual learning, and multistep rollout training for response-faithful lateral motion prediction.

2611.21795.title: The Impact of Scenario Representation in Scenario-based Optimization Certification
2611.21795.abstract: Scenario-based optimization provides finite-sample guarantees for decisions constructed from sampled uncertainty, but its certification procedures can be sensitive to how those samples are represented. We investigate this sensitivity under lossless scenario regrouping, which preserves the sampled information, feasible region, optimizer, and primitive violation probability. For an equal-allocation support-subsample certificate, we derive the distortion factor \(k^2(1-ε)^{k-1}\), establish certification reversals between equivalent representations, and provide sufficient conditions for acceptance dominance under nested coarsening. We further apply nondegeneracy-free Wait-and-Judge theory to coordinatewise scenario envelopes, enabling stronger certification directly from the primitive observations. In paired scenario-MPC experiments, exact regrouping increases certification availability from 318 to 471 of 480 attempts without changing the samples, numerical proposals, or requiring any reduction in witness cardinality. Primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping. These results demonstrate that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk.

llm.title_ja: シナリオベース最適化認証におけるシナリオ表現の影響
llm.tldr_ja: 損失のないシナリオ再グループ化を通じてシナリオベース最適化における認証の感度を調査し、証明書の勘定方法によって見かけ上のサンプル効率の向上が生じることを示した。
llm.problem: シナリオベース最適化は有限サンプル保証を提供するが、その認証手順はサンプルの表現方法に敏感である場合がある。
llm.method: 同等な表現間の認証逆転を導出し、等配分サポートサブサンプル証明書の歪み因子と受容優位性の十分条件を分析する。
llm.result: 厳密な再グループ化により、サンプルや数値提案を変更することなく、試行の認証可用性が大幅に向上した。
keywords_ja: シナリオベース最適化

2611.21795.tldr_en: It is shown that apparent scenario sample-efficiency gains can arise from certificate accounting rather than additional information or reduced decision risk, and primitive Wait-and-Judge certification accepts the same 471 attempts without regrouping.

2611.21789.title: ASTRA: ASV Simulator for Transferable Realistic Autonomy
2611.21789.abstract: Autonomy development for marine autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) remains challenging because field testing is costly and difficult to reproduce. Existing marine simulation tools provide mature capabilities in vessel dynamics, robotics integration, and visual rendering, but these strengths are emphasized differently across platforms. This paper presents ASTRA, an ASV simulation framework built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim that combines marine vehicle dynamics, photorealistic perception, and Robot Operating System (ROS 2) autonomy interfaces within a common environment. ASTRA incorporates a Fossen-style marine dynamics model together with geometry-based buoyancy and programmable spectral wave disturbances, enabling non-planar hydrostatic and wave-induced motion. The simulator reproduces the sensor configuration of a physical BlueBoat testbed, including GPS, IMU, LiDAR, and RGB-D sensing exposed through ROS 2. This allows localization, perception, planning, and control software to be developed against interfaces consistent with the physical platform. The BlueBoat's existing ROS 2 localization and perception modules were ported directly into ASTRA, while targeted zero-propulsion experiments were used to verify the implemented wave-body coupling. The simulated roll response was consistent with the expected non-oscillatory hydrostatic behavior, and heave remained highly coherent with the generated wave field, with approximately unity gain at the dominant wave frequency in the tested sea states. ASTRA is intended as an open-source testbed for marine autonomy development, simulation-based benchmarking, and sim-to-real experimentation.
2611.21789.comment: 7 pages, 3 figures, accepted to OCEANS 2026 Monterey

llm.title_ja: ASTRA：移行可能な現実的自律性のためのASVシミュレータ
llm.tldr_ja: NVIDIA Isaac Simをベースに、船舶の動力学、フォトリアルな知覚、ROS 2インターフェースを統合したオープンソースの海上水上艇シミュレーションフレームワーク「ASTRA」を提案する。
llm.problem: 海上自律水上艇の開発において、フィールドテストはコストが高く再現が困難である。
llm.method: Fossenスタイルの船舶動力学モデルに、幾何学的浮力とプログラム可能な波浪外乱を組み合わせ、ROS 2経由でセンサー構成を再現する。
llm.result: シミュレーション上のロール応答やヒーブが実際の挙動とよく一致し、シム・トゥ・リアル実験のテストベッドとして機能することを確認した。

2611.21789.tldr_en: ASTRA is an ASV simulation framework built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim that combines marine vehicle dynamics, photorealistic perception, and Robot Operating System (ROS 2) autonomy interfaces within a common environment, intended as an open-source testbed for marine autonomy development, simulation-based benchmarking, and sim-to-real experimentation.

2611.21783.title: Better Calibrated, Better Planned: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-ASV Informative Path Planning for Oil Spill Monitoring
2611.21783.abstract: Monitoring oil spills with fleets of Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) requires mapping a heterogeneous pollutant field from sparse, noisy measurements under tight time and energy budgets. Informative Path Planning (IPP) addresses this problem by coupling a reconstruction model, which infers the field and its uncertainty, with a planner that decides where to sample next. Prior work has focused on planning strategies and has largely relied on Gaussian Processes (GPs), leaving the calibration of the model's uncertainty underexplored. We study how uncertainty calibration conditions multi-vehicle IPP with a fleet of ASVs that coordinates online through a shared uncertainty map. We introduce Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) as an uncertainty-calibrated information model. We benchmark EDL, Monte Carlo Dropout and Deep Ensembles against a GP in closed loop with five planners on physics-based oil spill simulations. Across 60 maps, the choice of model dominates the outcome, explaining 80\% of the variance of the final reconstruction error, against 1\% for the planner among the deep models. EDL achieves the lowest error and the highest IoU under every planner, is the best calibrated model and runs at 3.9 ms per step. With 50 cells per vehicle it reconstructs the spill better than MC Dropout and Deep Ensembles with 150. Deep Ensembles become more confident as their error grows, whereas EDL is unaffected. Robustness of the information model to the data its own planner collects is therefore a requirement of uncertainty-aware IPP.
2611.21783.comment: 11 pages, 7 figures, Submitted to IEEE Internet of Things Journal

llm.title_ja: より良く校正され、より良く計画される：油流出モニタリングのための不確実性を考慮したマルチASV情報的経路計画
llm.tldr_ja: 不確実性校正がマルチ車両の情報的経路計画（IPP）に与える影響を調査し、証拠的ディープラーニング（EDL）が従来のガウス過程やアンサンブル手法よりも優れた再構成性能と校正を示すことを実証した。
llm.problem: 複数の自律水上艇による油流出のモニタリングでは、限られた予算下でスパースでノイズの多い測定から不確実性を伴う異種汚染物質フィールドをマッピングする必要がある。
llm.method: 証拠的ディープラーニング（EDL）を不確実性校正情報モデルとして導入し、複数のプランナーと組み合わせて物理ベースの油流出シミュレーションで検証する。
llm.result: EDLは全てのプランナーにおいて最も低い誤差と高いIoUを達成し、最も優れた校正性能と処理速度を示した。

2611.21782.title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models
2611.21782.abstract: Interactive video world models serve as simulators for embodied agents: from a starting image and an action trajectory, they generate the views the agent would see. The starting image fixes how high the camera is, for example 0.15 m for a floor robot or 2.2 m for an overhead camera, and a faithful simulator must keep this height as the camera moves. We show that six recent open-weight models fail to do so: as motion replaces the starting view with generated content, they move the camera toward human eye level, a failure we call camera-height regression.
