Our benchmark, EyeHeight, pairs six rendered elevations (0.15 m to 2.2 m) and four calibrated real-world rig heights with scale-free multi-view height estimation. All six models lose their initial height during a $180^\circ$ turn-and-walk rollout: initialized at 0.15 m, only 0-20% of clips end within $1.3\times$ of the starting height as inferred viewpoints converge to human heights of 1.1 m to 1.5 m, whereas ground-truth renders remain within a few percent. In Matrix-Game models, homography-tracked floor motion stays consistent with constant elevation during rotation even as newly outpainted room geometry yields a higher reconstructed viewpoint. Regression grows with rotation angle, begins while the start frame remains in context, and largely reverses in SANA-WM when a $360^\circ$ turn restores the initial view. We trace this pull to human-centric video priors in which floor-level views are nearly absent: in SANA-WM, textual height cues and dense floor-disparity maps do not prevent it, whereas classifier-free text guidance during the first half of denoising strengthens it. Combining unguided sampling with height-balanced fine-tuning recovers more retention but costs 5 MUSIQ points, a loss fixed during those same early steps. Viewpoint drift alone shifts the paths predicted by visual navigation policies.

llm.title_ja: すべてのカメラが成長する：インタラクティブ映像世界モデルにおけるカメラ高さ回帰
llm.tldr_ja: 近年のオープンウェイトなインタラクティブ映像世界モデルがカメラの初期高さを維持できず人間の目の高さに収束してしまう現象（カメラ高さ回帰）を明らかにし、その原因を分析した。
llm.problem: インタラクティブ映像世界モデルはロボットなどのシミュレータとして機能するが、生成コンテンツに置き換わるにつれて初期のカメラ高さを維持できない。
llm.method: 6つのレンダリングされた標高と4つの実世界リグ高さを組み合わせたベンチマーク「EyeHeight」を構築し、複数のモデルの挙動を評価する。
llm.result: 初期化された低い高さから移動すると、多くのモデルが人間の目の高さへと収束してしまうことを実証した。
keywords_ja: ロボットシミュレーション

2611.21782.tldr_en: This work traces this pull to human-centric video priors in which floor-level views are nearly absent to human-centric video priors in SANA-WM, where textual height cues and dense floor-disparity maps do not prevent it, whereas classifier-free text guidance during the first half of denoising strengthens it.

2611.21771.title: An Open-Source da Vinci X/Xi Instrument Module for Laparoscopic Surgery Research
2611.21771.abstract: Studying electrosurgical tasks on a research robot requires control of both instrument motion and energy activation, along with a record of when each action occurs. This paper presents an open-source module for da Vinci X/Xi instruments on a UR5/UR5e robotic arm. Five motors transmit torque through timing belts to spring-loaded drive discs. An electrosurgical interposer accepts software commands, gives the surgeon's foot pedals priority, and records the source of each activation request. In bench testing, the interposer recorded all 12 activation and deactivation events from six pedal presses. Ex vivo demonstrations included monopolar and bipolar coagulation of splenic tissue and monopolar cutting during gallbladder dissection. Optical tracking of the Fenestrated Bipolar Forceps showed that calibration brought pitch and yaw gains from 0.904 and 1.14 to 1.00 and 1.02, respectively. The module enables researchers to record instrument motion, video, and the timing and source of electrosurgical commands during laparoscopic tasks.
2611.21771.comment: Submitted to the 2027 International Symposium on Medical Robotics (ISMR). † Equal contribution. ‡ Equal supervision

llm.title_ja: 腹腔鏡手術研究のためのオープンソース da Vinci X/Xi インストゥルメントモジュール
llm.tldr_ja: UR5/UR5eロボットアーム上でda Vinci X/Xi器具の制御と電気メスによるエネルギー活性化を可能にするオープンソースのモジュールを開発し、ベンチテストと生体外実験で検証した。
llm.problem: 研究用ロボットで電気外科手術のタスクを研究するには、器具の運動制御とエネルギー活性化の記録の両方が必要である。
llm.method: 5つのモーターとタイミングベルトで駆動ディスクにトルクを伝え、フットペダルを優先する電気外科用インターポーザーを統合する。
llm.result: 較正によりピッチ・ヨー方向のゲインが適切に調整され、腹腔鏡タスク中の器具動作やコマンドのタイミングを記録できることを示した。

2611.21771.tldr_en: An open-source module for da Vinci X/Xi instruments on a UR5/UR5e robotic arm that enables researchers to record instrument motion, video, and the timing and source of electrosurgical commands during laparoscopic tasks.

2611.21607.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
2611.21607.abstract: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

llm.title_ja: ScaleVLA: ビジョン・言語・行動モデルを5520億パラメータへスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 552Bパラメータのバックボーンを持つScaleVLAを開発し、サンプル効率、汎化性能、精密マニピュレーションにおいて優れたロボット学習基盤性能を示した。
llm.problem: 既存のVLAポリシーは小規模なVLMバックボーンに依存しており、フロンティアスケールの表現力がロボット学習に与える潜在能力が未活用であること。
llm.method: 552BのDeepSeek-V4.1-Flashバックボーンを訓練可能なアクションDiTに接続し、多様なスケールのVLMを比較・評価する。
llm.result: わずか10個のデモンストレーションで50個使った2Bモデルを上回り、 LIBERO-PROの成功率が45.1%に向上し、実世界の充電器挿入も改善した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.21607.tldr_en: ScaleVLA is introduced, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup, suggesting that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

2611.21604.title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
2611.21604.abstract: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets. We present FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions. Following the Jev formulation, FaceJev answers eight independent questions about facial parts using a shared image encoding and reads anomaly probabilities from the native answer logits. A face is classified as forged if any part is predicted to be abnormal, directly linking the detection result to the part decisions. We construct PartForensics, a dataset of approximately 160k images with binary anomaly targets for the eight facial parts, to supervise these decisions. We further propose FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards. FaceJev outperforms the strongest baseline by 7.25 percentage points on unseen manipulations. Extensive ablation studies validate our design choices and the effectiveness of the main components.

llm.title_ja: FaceJev: 顔の偽造検出に向けた直接的視覚判断
llm.tldr_ja: 顔のパーツに対する8つの独立した質問に視覚的に直接答え、報酬比較により最適化するFaceJevを提案し、未見の操作に対する検出精度を向上させた。
llm.problem: 既存の顔偽造検出手法は学習済みの操作には強いが、未見の操作に対する汎化性能が低く、MLLMベースの手法はテキスト説明に頼り個別パーツを明示的に扱わないこと。
llm.method: 8つの顔パーツに関するバイナリ異常ターゲットを持つPartForensicsデータセットを構築し、報酬比較を用いてパーツ決定を最適化するFS-GRPOを提案する。
llm.result: 未見の操作において、FaceJevは最強のベースラインを7.25パーセンテージポイント上回る性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル

2611.21604.tldr_en: This work presents FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions, and proposes FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards.

2611.21596.title: SADL: On the Demand-Supply Geometry of Representation Collapse
2611.21596.abstract: In Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs), a well-constrained projector output does not by itself prevent representation collapse. We find that, from initialization, the encoder representation is dominated by a component shared by different inputs. A batch-normalized projector removes this component, so regularization after the projector cannot correct it, and the differences between representations shrink until they collapse. We propose SADL (Supply And Demand Loss), which keeps the original training objective and constrains the encoder directly when needed. SADL compares the representation differences that the projector output demands with the differences the encoder can retain and pass on to the projector, and adds a constraint on the encoder only when supply falls short of demand. It works with different Demand Regularizers and introduces no auxiliary networks, additional trainable parameters, or architectural changes. In single-task and jointly trained four-task LeWorldModel (LeWM) and INTACT experiments, SADL lowers the collapse rate over ten random seeds from 50% to 0%. After one epoch of training, encoder effective rank is 3.4-6.4 times that of the corresponding baseline without SADL, and latent prediction error falls to 1/20-1/303 of it. Without additional tuning, SADL stays robust as its loss weight spans orders of magnitude, and with several Demand Regularizers INTACT exceeds 95% mean search-free control success. On four image datasets, SADL also consistently improves accuracy and stability across random seeds. These results show that matching the representation differences a regularizer demands with the differences the encoder can supply leads to faster and more stable representation learning in control and image classification.

llm.title_ja: SADL: 表現崩壊の需給幾何学について
llm.tldr_ja: プロジェクターが要求する表現の差異とエンコーダーが供給可能な差異を一致させるSADLを提案し、制御および画像分類における表現学習の崩壊を防ぎ安定化させた。
llm.problem: JEPAにおいて十分に制約されたプロジェクター出力だけでは、エンコーダー表現の崩壊（representation collapse）を防げないこと。
llm.method: プロジェクターの要求する差異とエンコーダーが保持・転送できる差異を比較し、供給が不足した場合のみエンコーダーに制約を追加するSADLを提案する。
llm.result: LeWMやINTACTの実験において崩壊率を50%から0%に低下させ、有効ランクを3.4〜6.4倍に向上させるとともに予測誤差を大幅に削減した。

2611.21596.tldr_en: Results show that matching the representation differences a regularizer demands with the differences the encoder can supply leads to faster and more stable representation learning in control and image classification.

2611.21532.title: How Much Does Saliency Accuracy Matter for Saliency-Guided 360-degree Image Compression?
2611.21532.abstract: Saliency-guided coding allocates bits to the regions viewers are most likely to attend, but accurate 360-degree saliency prediction is computationally expensive, an obstacle for low-latency immersive streaming applications such as robot teleoperation. We quantify how much saliency-prediction accuracy actually translates into compression gain. Building on a saliency-guided rate-distortion-optimized (RDO) learned codec, modified so that the training-time latent mask is driven by ground-truth saliency, which yields a single, predictor-agnostic codec, we evaluate saliency predictors spanning two orders of magnitude in compute on both the learned codec and H.265/HEVC. The results show that higher saliency-prediction accuracy yields diminishing compression gains: a lightweight predictor fast enough for live use (52 frames per second) captures 65% of the ground-truth oracle's bit-rate saving, a 3.3x heavier one reaches 74%, and a further 38x increase in compute adds no measurable benefit, on either codec. Therefore, lightweight predictors might also be a practical choice for latency-constrained 360-degree streaming.
2611.21532.comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Accepted at the 2027 IEEE/SICE International Symposium on System Integration (SII 2027)

llm.title_ja: saliencyガイド付き360度画像圧縮において saliencyの精度はどれほど重要か
llm.tldr_ja: 360度画像圧縮におけるsaliency予測の精度と圧縮利得の関係を評価し、軽量な予測器でも十分なビットレート削減を達成できることを示した。
llm.problem: 高精度な360度 saliency予測は計算コストが高く、ロボットのテレオペレーションなどの低遅延ストリーミングの障害になっていること。
llm.method: グラウンド真値 saliency駆動型学習コーデックを用い、計算量が異なる複数の saliency予測器を評価する。
llm.result: 高精度な予測による圧縮利得は逓減し、ライブ用途に十分な軽量予測器でもオラクルによるビットレート削減の65%を達成することを示した。

2611.21532.tldr_en: Higher saliency-prediction accuracy yields diminishing compression gains: a lightweight predictor fast enough for live use captures 65% of the ground-truth oracle's bit-rate saving, and lightweight predictors might also be a practical choice for latency-constrained 360-degree streaming.

2611.21530.title: DuoFlow: Towards Synchronized Speech and Motion Generation with Fine-Grained Control
2611.21530.abstract: An embodied speaker's expressiveness depends not only on what is said, but also on how the voice sounds and how the body moves. However, existing joint speech-motion generation models are largely driven implicitly by transcript semantics or intermediate speech representations, offering little explicit control over motion hierarchy, body parts, or vocal style. To bridge this gap, we construct MotionSpeech, a structured benchmark for controllable joint speech-motion generation that includes transcripts, voice-style descriptions, and motion conditions at two hierarchical levels. Building on this benchmark, we propose DuoFlow, a dual-stream latent flow transformer that jointly denoises speech and motion under a shared noise level and a unified second-based temporal coordinate. Modality-specific residual connectors inject structured conditions into the corresponding streams, layer-wise bidirectional cross-modal attention coordinates their generation, and a monotonic phoneme pathway combines normalized progress anchors with CTC supervision to strengthen speech temporal modeling. DuoFlow provides a unified interface for fine-grained motion and vocal-style control and demonstrates the ability to synthesize high-quality, synchronized, and instruction-consistent speech-motion sequences. Project page, https://jundong-dev.github.io/DuoFlow-project-page.
2611.21530.tldr_en: DuoFlow is proposed, a dual-stream latent flow transformer that jointly denoises speech and motion under a shared noise level and a unified second-based temporal coordinate that provides a unified interface for fine-grained motion and vocal-style control and demonstrates the ability to synthesize high-quality, synchronized, and instruction-consistent speech-motion sequences.

llm.title_ja: DuoFlow：きめ細かな制御による同期された音声およびモーション生成に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: 音声とモーションを共有ノイズレベルと統合された時間座標のもとで共同でノイズ除去するデューストリーム潜在フローTransformer「DuoFlow」を提案し、同期された高品質なシーケンス生成を実現した。
llm.problem: 既存の音声・モーション共同生成モデルは暗黙的に駆動されており、モーション階層や身体部位、ボーカルスタイルに対する明示的な制御が乏しい。
llm.method: 構造化ベンチマークMotionSpeechを構築し、共有ノイズレベルの下で音声とモーションを同時生成するデューストリーム潜在フローTransformerを設計する。
llm.result: きめ細かなモーションおよびボーカルスタイルの制御のための統一インターフェースを提供し、高品質で同期したシーケンス生成を実証した。

2611.21517.title: Lazy-MOSAIC: Accelerating Skill-Centric Manipulation Planning with Learned Skill-Effect World Models
2611.21517.abstract: Long-horizon manipulation tasks require a robot to perform a sequence of physical interactions with its environment, typically combining several different skills. Planning such behaviors efficiently is challenging: given a library of parameterized skills, solutions lie in a vast hybrid space of skill sequences and their parameters, and evaluating each candidate skill's feasibility and effect with a high-fidelity world model such as a physics simulator is computationally expensive. MOSAIC, a recent skill-centric approach, lets the skills guide a non-sequential search toward the regions of this space where they are likely to succeed; however, it pays the full cost of simulation for every parameterized skill it considers. In this work, we introduce Lazy-MOSAIC, a lazy planning framework that instead searches over hypothesized skill outcomes. A cheap learned skill-effect world model predicts, in a fraction of a millisecond, a skill's feasibility and the world state it produces. Lazy-MOSAIC then uses these predictions to focus expensive simulation on promising candidate skills and, when a hypothesis is invalidated, repairs only the affected part of the search, while ensuring that every skill in a returned plan is validated in simulation. We evaluate Lazy-MOSAIC on cluttered-shelf retrieval tasks of increasing difficulty and demonstrate it on a physical robot, showing that it plans substantially faster than baselines with fewer simulator queries, while matching or exceeding their success rate in every setting. Visit skill-mosaic.github.io.

llm.title_ja: Lazy-MOSAIC: 学習済みスキル効果世界モデルによるスキル中心マニプリューション計画の高速化
llm.tldr_ja: 安価な学習済み世界モデルを用いて仮説上のスキルの結果を探索し、有望な候補のみを高精度なシミュレータで検証するLazy-MOSAICを提案した。
llm.problem: 長ホライズンのマニプレーション計画では膨大なハイブリッド空間を探索し、高精度な世界モデルですべてのスキル候補を評価する計算コストが非常に高いこと。
llm.method: スキルの実現可能性と世界状態を予測する安価な学習済みスキル効果世界モデルを導入し、検証が必要な部分のみシミュレーションを実行する遅延計画フレームワークを構築する。
llm.result: 実ロボットと cluttered-shelf タスクにおいて、シミュレータへの問い合わせ回数を減らしつつベースラインよりも大幅に高速な計画を実現した。

2611.21517.tldr_en: Lazy-MOSAIC is introduced, a lazy planning framework that instead searches over hypothesized skill outcomes and focuses expensive simulation on promising candidate skills and, when a hypothesis is invalidated, repairs only the affected part of the search, while ensuring that every skill in a returned plan is validated in simulation.

2611.21507.title: GHySSeg: Real-Time Geometric Ground and Road Segmentation for Hybrid Solid-State LiDAR
2611.21507.abstract: Hybrid solid-state LiDAR sensors are making their way into production vehicles, yet the data they produce differs structurally from that of the established spinning mechanical sensors behind today's autonomous-driving datasets: it is ring-free, dense, cluttered, and concentrated in a frontal field of view. The classical geometric methods that autonomous vehicles rely on for drivable space computation and navigation assume the ordered ring-and-column structure of a 360-degree spinning LiDAR and degrade or fail on this data, while learned alternatives are computationally heavy, hard to certify, and trained almost exclusively on spinning-LiDAR data. We demonstrate that the same dense, per-curve geometry is instead an opportunity to close the divide between the industry's preferred sensors and autonomous-driving research. We present GHySSeg, a purely geometric method that segments ground and drivable road from a single hybrid solid-state LiDAR frame by tracing each scan curve and reading two geometric signatures, a step in height and a fold-back in range, with no training and no graphics processing unit. To evaluate it, we release HySoLiD-Drive, the first public benchmark dedicated to ground and road segmentation on an automotive hybrid solid-state LiDAR, comprising 100 manually labeled and 7000 unlabeled frames recorded by two vehicles in real driving. On this benchmark, GHySSeg surpasses both geometric and learned state-of-the-art baselines across ground and road segmentation, reaching an intersection-over-union of 0.907 for road and 0.896 for ground at over 0.96 precision, while running in real time at about 22 milliseconds per frame on a single core.
2611.21507.comment: 14 pages, 8 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible. HySoLiD-Drive dataset: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21705196

llm.title_ja: GHySSeg: ハイブリッド半導体LiDARのためのリアルタイム幾何学的地面・道路セグメンテーション
llm.tldr_ja: 各スキャン曲線を追跡して地面や道路をセグメンテーションする純粋な幾何学的手法GHySSegを提案し、新しいデータセットで優れた性能とリアルタイム動作を示した。
llm.problem: ハイブリッド半導体LiDARのデータ構造は従来の360度回転式LiDARと異なり、従来の幾何学的手法が破綻する一方で学習ベースの手法は計算負荷が高く認証が困難であること。
llm.method: 高さの段差と範囲の折り返しという2つの幾何学的シグネチャを読み取る、訓練不要かつGPU不要の幾何学的セグメンテーション手法GHySSegを開発する。
llm.result: 新しく構築したHySoLiD-Driveデータセットにおいて道路IoU 0.907、地面IoU 0.896を達成し、単一コアでリアルタイム動作（約22ms/フレーム）を実現した。

2611.21507.tldr_en: GHySSeg is presented, a purely geometric method that segments ground and drivable road from a single hybrid solid-state LiDAR frame by tracing each scan curve and reading two geometric signatures, a step in height and a fold-back in range, with no training and no graphics processing unit.

2611.21485.title: Lost in the Hallway: Benchmarking Persistent Spatial Memory Across Revisits
2611.21485.abstract: Persistent spatial understanding is essential for embodied agents to operate reliably in environments they repeatedly encounter. It requires recognizing revisited places despite viewpoint changes, distinguishing them from similar-looking rooms, and updating memories as environments change. Yet existing evaluations often leave physical place identity across separated visits implicit. We introduce ReSpaceBench, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning. Controlled walkthroughs define visits by physical room entry and deliberately include same-type room distractors and cross-session object changes. Our evaluation of 32 models and 3 agentic video-understanding frameworks reveals substantial limitations: the strongest evaluated zero-shot model achieves 50.5% overall accuracy and 52.2% on a 450-question subset, compared with 90.1% for human annotators. The evaluated agentic frameworks offer no overall improvement over direct inference with the same base model. Analysis of agent execution traces reveals evidence omissions and incorrect cross-visit room associations as major failure modes, suggesting that iterative evidence seeking alone does not ensure consistent spatial memory. Further analyses expose a gap between recognizing familiar rooms and identifying the correct visited room, while annotation-guided sampling highlights the importance of preserving intervening visits and transitions. We also provide RS-30K, a separate training dataset from synthetic sources with no template, scene, route, or video overlap with the benchmark. Fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B raises overall accuracy from 35.5% to 60.4%, with the largest gains in association and improvements extending to real-life scenes.

llm.title_ja: 廊下での迷子: 再訪問にわたる永続的空間記憶のベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 部屋の関連付けや状態追跡などを含む永続的空間記憶評価のためのベンチマークReSpaceBenchを提案し、既存のビジョン言語モデルやエージェントの限界を明らかにした。
llm.problem: 既存の評価では物理的な場所の同一性が曖昧であり、視点変化への対応や環境変化に伴う記憶の更新能力の評価が不十分であること。
llm.method: 3,244の質問と590のシーンからなるReSpaceBenchを構築し、複数のモデルやエージェントフレームワークを評価するとともにファインチューニング用のデータセットを開発する。
llm.result: 最強のゼロショットモデルの精度は50.5%にとどまり、人間（90.1%）との間に大きな差があることを示し、ファインチューニングにより精度が大きく向上することを確認した。

2611.21485.tldr_en: ReSpaceBench is introduced, a benchmark comprising 3,244 questions across 590 synthetic and real-home scenes, organized into 9 tasks spanning room association, persistent state tracking, and downstream reasoning, and analysis of agent execution traces reveals evidence omissions and incorrect cross-visit room associations as major failure modes, suggesting that iterative evidence seeking alone does not ensure consistent spatial memory.

2611.21378.title: Data-Driven Predictive Control for Autonomous Vehicle Racing under Varying Friction
2611.21378.abstract: Data-driven predictive control (DPC) predicts future outputs by combining recorded input-output trajectory data such that the combined trajectory approximately matches a measured initial trajectory and tracks a provided reference. This paper investigates to what extent and under which conditions DPC using data pooled across operating conditions retains the prediction accuracy of DPC using data from the current operating condition. In autonomous vehicle racing, the tire-road friction varies between racetrack sections and tire sets. If the initial trajectory and the recorded data originate from different frictions, prediction accuracy of DPC degrades. Ensuring the frictions match requires knowing the friction during recording and estimating the current friction explicitly. Instead, we pool data recorded at different frictions. We compare the prediction accuracy of DPC using data recorded under the current friction (matched), a different friction (mismatched) and data pooled from both frictions. We evaluate in simulation and small-scale vehicle experiments in the Cyber-Physical Mobility Lab (CPM Lab). Our results show that pooled data keep the multi-step root-mean-square prediction error within 1.5 times that of matched data, whereas mismatched data increase it by a factor of 2.2 to 3.4. To assess how this prediction accuracy carries over to control, we evaluate the tracking error from the raceline in closed loop. In simulation, DPC with pooled data tracks comparably to nonlinear model predictive control (13.7 cm versus 13.3 cm) and close to DPC with matched data in the CPM Lab, differing by 0.1 cm on the low-friction tires (1.6 cm versus 1.5 cm) and by 0.2 cm on the high-friction tires (0.9 cm versus 1.1 cm). DPC thus provides partial adaptation to varying friction, without a dedicated adaptation method.
2611.21378.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to the 2027 European Control Conference (ECC). Code and data: https://github.com/bassamlab/multisurface-racing-with-dpc

llm.title_ja: 摩擦変動下における自動運転車レースのためのデータ駆動型予測制御
llm.tldr_ja: 異なる摩擦条件で記録されたデータをプールして用いるデータ駆動型予測制御（DPC）が、摩擦変動に対して部分的な適応性と良好な追従性能を維持することを示した。
llm.problem: 自動運転車レースにおいてタイヤと路面の摩擦が変動すると、初期軌道と記録データの摩擦が異なる場合にDPCの予測精度が大きく低下すること。
llm.method: 異なる摩擦で記録されたデータをプールし、予測精度や追従誤差への影響をシミュレーションおよび小型車実験で評価する。
llm.result: プールされたデータを用いることで、ミスマッチデータと比較して予測誤差を抑え、非線形モデル予測制御に匹敵する追従性能を達成した。

2611.21378.tldr_en: This paper investigates to what extent and under which conditions DPC using data pooled across operating conditions retains the prediction accuracy of DPC using data from the current operating condition, and evaluates the tracking error from the raceline in closed loop.

2611.21370.title: Federated TD Learning in Heterogeneous Environments with Average Rewards: A Two-timescale Approach with Polyak-Ruppert Averaging
2611.21370.abstract: Federated Reinforcement Learning (FRL) provides a promising way to speedup training in reinforcement learning when one has access to multiple edge devices that can operate in parallel. Recently, it has been shown that even when these edge devices have access to different dynamic models---such as cars or robots with differing system configurations---an optimal convergence rate that has a linear speedup proportional to the number of devices is achievable. However, this result requires that the algorithm's stepsize be chosen in a manner that depends on the unknown model parameters. Also, it applies only to a discounted setting, which has been argued to fit episodic tasks better than continuing control tasks. In this paper, we obtain finite-time bounds for heterogeneous FRL with average rewards. We show that optimal convergence rate and linear speedup are achievable even with a universal stepsize choice, independent of the underlying dynamics. To achieve our result, we modify the existing one-timescale FRL method to a novel two-timescale variant that additionally incorporates iterate averaging. We remark that this idea also extends to other settings already studied in the literature, such as the homogeneous FRL or the heterogeneous case with a discounted cost function.

llm.title_ja: 不均一環境における平均報酬型連合TD学習: Polyak-Ruppert平均化を用いた2タイムスケールアプローチ
llm.tldr_ja: 不均一な動的モデルを持つ環境における平均報酬型の連合強化学習において、普遍的なステップサイズ選択で最適収束レートと線形スピードアップを達成できることを示した。
llm.problem: 既存の不均一連合強化学習の結果は未知のモデルパラメータに依存するステップサイズの選択を必要とし、割引設定に限定されていたこと。
llm.method: 既存の1タイムスケール連合強化学習手法を、イテレート平均化を組み込んだ新しい2タイムスケール変形へと拡張する。
llm.result: 背後にある動力学に依存しない普遍的なステップサイズを用いても、最適収束レートと線形スピードアップが達成可能であることを示した。

badges.venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control

2611.21370.tldr_en: Federated Reinforcement Learning is modified to a novel two-timescale variant that additionally incorporates iterate averaging and shows that the optimal convergence rate with a linear speedup is possible even with a universal stepsize choice, independent of the underlying dynamics.
2611.21370.venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control

2611.21365.title: Exploring the link between predictive uncertainty and the sim-to-real gap in deep learning models utilizing synthetic data
2611.21365.abstract: Today, state-of-the-art methods for quality control (QC) are based on Machine Vision, combining deep learning (DL) models with camera-based inspection. Yet, the integration of such solutions in industrial applications is often impeded by data sparsity and trust in model reliability. While synthetic data offers a promising approach to generate the necessary data with perfect annotations, it poses risks related to performance degradation due to the possible occurrence of the sim-to-real gap. This study conducts experiments using the ensemble method to estimate the predictive uncertainty of DL models trained on synthetic data. The results show that predictive uncertainty increases under the sim-to-real domain shift. However, the observed performance drop is dominated by a systematic sim-to-real bias rather than by ensemble disagreement.These findings contribute to the effective utilization of synthetic data in industrial settings while highlighting the importance of risk assessment for the deployment of DL solutions for QC tasks.

llm.title_ja: ディープラーニングモデルにおける予測不確実性とシム・ツー・リアルギャップの関連性の探求
llm.tldr_ja: 合成データで学習した品質検査用ディープラーニングモデルにおいて、シム・ツー・リアルドメインシフト下で予測不確実性が増加することを示した。
llm.problem: 合成データはアノテーション付きデータを供給できる一方で、シム・ツー・リアルギャップに起因する性能低下のリスクがあること。
llm.method: アンサンブル法を用いて合成データで訓練されたディープラーニングモデルの予測不確実性を推定する実験を行う。
llm.result: 予測不確実性はドメインシフトにより増加するが、性能低下はアンサンブルの不一致ではなく、主に系統的なシム・ツー・リアルバイアスに起因することを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: シム・ツー・リアルギャップ

2611.21365.tldr_en: This study conducts experiments using the ensemble method to estimate the predictive uncertainty of DL models trained on synthetic data and shows that predictive uncertainty increases under the sim-to-real domain shift.

2611.21309.title: Safe Physical Interaction of All-Electric Heavy-Duty Robotic Manipulators via Control Barrier Functions and Variable Impedance Control
2611.21309.abstract: All-electric heavy-duty robotic manipulators are increasingly expected to operate close to tunnel walls, equipment, and other structures while retaining the force capability required for large-payload tasks. Accurate motion control alone does not address the resulting safety and interaction requirements. This paper develops a safety-aware physical-interaction architecture that combines variable impedance control (VIC) with control barrier functions (CBFs) on top of an established virtual decomposition control (VDC) framework for electromechanical linear actuator (EMLA)-driven manipulators. VIC continuously adapts the task-space stiffness and damping according to predicted proximity and contact risk, whereas a joint-velocity CBF filter enforces Cartesian workspace boundaries and the physical stroke limits induced by the closed-chain lift and tilt mechanisms. To account for nonideal realization of the filtered velocity by the inner VDC/EMLA dynamics, the CBF inequalities are tightened using a measured bound on the joint-velocity tracking error. Four configurations, namely VDC, VIC+VDC, CBF+VDC, and VIC+CBF+VDC, are evaluated under workspace, actuator-limit, and physical-interaction scenarios. VIC reduces the peak and RMS environment-interaction forces by 92.59% and 96.33%, respectively; both robust CBF configurations maintain positive workspace and EMLA safety margins, while VIC+CBF+VDC reduces the CBF intervention metric by 10.30% compared with CBF+VDC.

llm.title_ja: 制御バリア関数と可変インピーダンス制御を用いた全電動型重作業ロボットマニピュレータの安全な物理的相互作用
llm.tldr_ja: 可変インピーダンス制御と制御バリア関数（CBF）を統合した安全意識型物理相互作用アーキテクチャを提案し、重作業マニピュレータの相互作用力を大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: 全電動型重作業マニピュレータは狭い環境で高負荷作業を行う際、正確なモーションコントロールだけでは安全性と相互作用の要件を満たせないこと。
llm.method: 仮想分解制御フレームワークの上に、近接度に応じて剛性と減衰を連続適応する可変インピーダンス制御と、作業空間境界を強制するCBFフィルターを組み合わせる。
llm.result: ピークおよびRMSの環境相互作用力をそれぞれ92.59%および96.33%削減しつつ、安全マージンを維持できることを示した。

2611.21302.title: Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating
2611.21302.abstract: Event cameras keep capturing structure where conventional cameras blur or saturate, which makes them attractive for 3D perception in fast or poorly lit scenes. Event datasets with dense 3D ground truth, however, are far smaller and less diverse than the image collections behind feed-forward 3D reconstruction models. We present Déjà-Events, an event-only model that predicts depth, camera pose and pointmaps from multiple views in a single forward pass. Rather than relying on scarce 3D labels, we distil it from Déjà View, a feed-forward RGB model that refines its tokens by repeatedly applying one shared transformer block. On paired RGB and event recordings, the event student learns to reproduce the frozen teacher's final tokens, which requires no depth or pose ground truth and trains only about 1% of its parameters. Because events are dense at edges and moving texture but nearly absent in textureless regions, we further introduce sparsity-aware adaptive gating, which adapts the shared block's gates to events and adjusts them per patch by event density, so that accuracy holds as refinement steps are added. Trained only on simulated data, Déjà-Events achieves the lowest pointmap error among the event-based methods we evaluate, on EventScape and zero-shot on the real MVSEC and DSEC datasets. On DSEC it halves the error of the strongest baseline (0.15 vs. 0.30 AbsRel) with about a tenth of its parameters. It also has the lowest depth error on EventScape and DSEC and the lowest trajectory error on EventScape.

llm.title_ja: Déjà-Events: スパース性を考慮した適応的ゲーティングを用いたイベントカメラによるマルチビュー3D幾何学
llm.tldr_ja: スパース性を考慮した適応的ゲーティングを導入し、教師モデルからの蒸留により深さやカメラポーズを予測するイベント専用モデルDéjà-Eventsを提案した。
llm.problem: 密な3Dグラウンド真値を持つイベントデータセットは非常に小さく多様性に乏しいこと。
llm.method: 事前学習済みのRGB教師モデルからイベント学生モデルへトークンを蒸留し、イベント密度に応じてパッチ単位でゲートを調整するスパース対応適応ゲーティングを導入する。
llm.result: シミュレーションデータのみで訓練されながら、MVSECやDSECのゼロショット評価において、既存のイベントベース手法の中で最も低いポイントマップ誤差と深さ誤差を達成した。

2611.21302.tldr_en: D\'ej\`a-Events is presented, an event-only model that predicts depth, camera pose and pointmaps from multiple views in a single forward pass and achieves the lowest pointmap error among the event-based methods evaluated.

2611.21264.title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations
2611.21264.abstract: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential. To address the computational challenges for high-dimensional joint trajectories faced by conventional constrained optimization-based solutions, this paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessary spatial flexibility. By formulating the planning task as a constrained Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation, we decouple multiagent objectives to leverage pre-trained single-agent diffusion priors for dynamic feasibility, obstacle avoidance, and smoothness. We then interleave the generative process with projected gradient descent (PGD) to strictly enforce affine geometric constraints with safety guarantees. Simulations demonstrate that our framework generates highly smooth, collision-free plans that are readily trackable by common distributed controllers and outperforms state-of-the-art planners in various metrics.

llm.title_ja: マルチエージェントのアフィン隊形に向けたハイブリッド最適化・生成型モーションプランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済み拡散事前分布と射影勾配降下法を組み合わせたハイブリッド最適化・生成型フレームワークを提案し、滑らかで衝突のないアフィン隊形計画を実現した。
llm.problem: マルチエージェントの隊形制御における高次元の結合軌道計画において、従来の制約付き最適化手法は大きな計算上の課題に直面していること。
llm.method: プランニングタスクを制約付きMAP推定として定式化し、単一エージェントの拡散事前分布を活用して動的安全性や回避を達成しつつ、PGDでアフィン幾何制約を厳密に強制する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて、滑らかで衝突のない計画を生成し、多様な指標で最先端のプランナーを上回る性能を示した。
keywords_ja: モーションプランニング

2611.21264.tldr_en: This paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessary spatial flexibility by formulating the planning task as a constrained Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation and interleave the generative process with projected gradient descent to strictly enforce affine geometric constraints with safety guarantees.

2611.21258.title: ThinkWAM: Rethinking Latent Futures for Action Refinement
2611.21258.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple action generation with predictions of future states. An initial action chunk may be flawed. A future prediction that is not conditioned on the chunk is identical for every proposal and thus carries no proposal-specific signal, limiting its usefulness for refinement before execution. We introduce ThinkWAM, a latent WAM that establishes bidirectional feedback before execution through a proposal-rethink-refine loop: the policy first proposes a complete action chunk, the proposal corrects multi-horizon future latents through a learned residual, and the corrected latents are injected into a second pass of the same action head, which generates the executable chunk. An affordance-guided observation-action memory and a near-fine, far-coarse multi-horizon prediction scheme, both motivated by predictive coding, support this loop, and all prediction stays in latent space. ThinkWAM achieves 98.70% success on LIBERO, 84.76% on LIBERO-Plus without OOD fine-tuning, 85.75%/65.85% on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean/Random, and 65.17% on RoboCasa24. ThinkWAM achieves 64.4% mean success across three real-world OOD conditions. The mean two-pass inference latency per action chunk is 153.48 ms on LIBERO, 164.61 ms on RoboTwin, and 101.2 ms on the Galaxea A1Z. Ablations show complementary gains from rethinking and affordance guidance. Diagnostics indicate that proposal-conditioned corrections change both predicted futures and action trajectories, showing that the corrected future representations improve the final action.
2611.21258.comment: 21 pages, 12 figures, 15 tables, including references and appendix. Project page: https://thinkwam-project.github.io/
2611.21258.tldr_en: ThinkWAM is introduced, a latent WAM that establishes bidirectional feedback before execution through a proposal-rethink-refine loop, and diagnostic indicate that proposal-conditioned corrections change both predicted futures and action trajectories, showing that the corrected future representations improve the final action.

llm.title_ja: ThinkWAM：行動洗練のための潜在的未来の再考
llm.tldr_ja: 実行前に提案・再考・洗練のループを通じて双方向フィードバックを確立する潜在世界行動モデル「ThinkWAM」を提案し、ロボット操作タスクで高い成功率を達成した。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルにおける最初の行動チャンクには欠陥がある可能性があり、チャンクに条件付けられていない将来予測は提案固有の信号を持たないため洗練に限界がある。
llm.method: ポリシーが行動チャンクを提案し、残差を通じて未来の潜在表現を修正した上で、再度同じ行動ヘッドに入力して実行可能チャンクを生成するループを構築する。
llm.result: LIBEROで98.70%の成功率を達成し、実世界のOOD条件でも優れた平均成功率を示した。

2611.21235.title: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated via truthful evidence in open channel
2611.21235.abstract: Language-model agents' beliefs can be manipulated through open channels such as social media, even when the information they receive is truthful. When agents fill gaps between fragments with self-induced relationships, they may accept those relationships as established facts and pass the resulting rumours to others. Drawing on cognitive theory of narrative understanding and film theory of montage, we introduce Generative Montage to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives. Across 1,090 rumour targets from six Twitter events, agents often accepted rumours overconfidently, with overall acceptance exceeding 65 percent in twelve of fourteen models. Acceptance remained above 50 percent after majority voting or review of the same evidence, showing how errors can reach downstream decisions. To explain this susceptibility, fragment interventions identify posts that influence belief within complete narratives. Synthetic controls then show that similar response patterns arise from valid evidence, separating belief influence from evidential support. This distinction motivates Grounded Monitor, a proof-of-concept neuro-symbolic runtime monitor that checks direct evidential support to guide agents' judgements, improving decision accuracy by 5.6 to 29.0 percentage points across original and anonymized settings. These findings expose a cognitive route to rumour amplification and support monitoring inferred relationships before agent-generated conclusions guide public decisions.

llm.title_ja: 言語モデルエージェントの信念はオープンチャネル内の真実の証拠によって操作され得る
llm.tldr_ja: 真実の断片を誤解を招く物語に配列することで言語モデルエージェントの信念が操作される現象（物語の過剰適合）を分析し、文脈監視による改善を示した。
llm.problem: 言語モデルエージェントは、断片間の関係を自ら補完して確立された事実として受け入れることで、ソーシャルメディア等のオープンチャネルで操作されやすいこと。
llm.method: 認知的物語理解理論に基づき、エージェントが真実の断片を誤解を招く物語に配置する「Generative Montage」を導入し、直接的な証拠支持をチェックするモニターを提案する。
llm.result: 多数のモデルで噂の受容が65%を超える脆弱性を示し、提案するGrounded Monitorにより意思決定精度が5.6〜29.0パーセンテージポイント向上した。

2611.21235.tldr_en: Generative Montage is introduced to operationalize this failure, termed narrative overfitting, by coordinating agents to arrange truthful fragments into misleading narratives, exposing a cognitive route to rumour amplification and support monitoring inferred relationships before agent-generated conclusions guide public decisions.

2611.21209.title: BoBDeLaN: Bounded-Bandwidth Context Adaptation for Deep Lagrangian Robot Control
2611.21209.abstract: Learned physics-based models provide structure for robot control, but uncertain payloads and unmodeled dynamics limit their predictive accuracy. Context-aware Deep Lagrangian Networks enable adaptation through a latent context inferred from measurement histories while retaining Lagrangian structure for each fixed context. However, this structure alone does not constrain sensitivity to measurement disturbances. We introduce BoBDeLaN, which combines a contracting, gain-bounded Recurrent Equilibrium Network context encoder with stable linear filtering to shape disturbance sensitivity across frequencies. This architecture guarantees exponential forgetting of the recurrent initialization and admits a finite-horizon, frequency-weighted bound on context perturbations, which extends to residual torque prediction under a Lipschitz continuity assumption on the context-conditioned dynamics model. We evaluate a low-pass realization within model predictive control on simulated and real hardware manipulation tasks, together with frequency-sensitivity analysis on real-robot data. Compared with an LSTM encoder using the same input filter, BoBDeLaN exhibits reduced high-frequency context sensitivity, lower residual torque prediction error, and smoother motion, with less degradation under injected disturbances.
2611.21209.comment: Submitted to the 9th Annual Learning for Dynamics & Control Conference (L4DC 2027)

llm.title_ja: BoBDeLaN: ディープラグランジュロボット制御のための帯域制限コンテキスト適応
llm.tldr_ja: 収縮的で利得が有界なリカレント平衡ネットワークコンテキストエンコーダーと安定な線形フィルタを組み合わせたBoBDeLaNを提案し、外乱感度を抑制した。
llm.problem: 文脈対応型ディープラグランジュネットワークは測定履歴からコンテキストを推論して適応するが、測定外乱に対する感度を制限できないこと。
llm.method: 周波数全体での外乱感度を形作るリカレント平衡ネットワークエンコーダーと線形フィルタを結合し、コンテキスト摂動に対する周波数重み付き有界性を保証する。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実機タスクにおいて、LSTMエンコーダーと比較して高周波コンテキスト感度が低く、残差トルク予測誤差が小さい滑らかな動作を実現した。

2611.21209.tldr_en: BoBDeLaN is introduced, which combines a contracting, gain-bounded Recurrent Equilibrium Network context encoder with stable linear filtering to shape disturbance sensitivity across frequencies and evaluates a low-pass realization within model predictive control on simulated and real hardware manipulation tasks.

2611.21198.title: Cooperative Mobile Manipulation using Learned Dynamical Systems
2611.21198.abstract: Cooperative mobile manipulation requires robots to coordinate their motions while ensuring whole-body collision avoidance and preserving task-relevant behaviors. We propose CALDS (Cooperative Adaptation of Learned Dynamical Systems), a framework that enables mobile manipulators to adapt learned single-agent behaviors for coordinated execution. Building on individual dynamical systems (DSs) learned from demonstrations, CALDS enables cooperative adaptation through two key components: Cooperative Policy Selection, which identifies compatible combinations of learned policies, and Temporal Adaptation, which ensures collision-free cooperation while preserving the spatial structure and convergence properties of the original behaviors. We evaluate CALDS across three diverse scenarios: assistive dressing, restaurant cleaning and serving, and drawer opening and object placement. Quantitative results demonstrate its effectiveness in improving task success and enabling safe, coordinated simultaneous execution while maintaining fidelity to demonstrated behaviors.

llm.title_ja: 学習済み力学系を用いた協調型モバイルマニピュレーション
llm.tldr_ja: 協調ポリシー選択と時間的適応により学習済み単一エージェント行動を協調実行へと適応させるフレームワークCALDSを提案した。
llm.problem: 協調型モバイルマニピュレーションでは、ロボットが全身の衝突回避を確保しつつタスク関連の行動を維持しながら動作を調整する必要があること。
llm.method: 実演から学習された個別の力学系に基づき、互換性のあるポリシーの組み合わせを特定する協調ポリシー選択と、衝突のない協調を保証する時間的適応を統合する。
llm.result: 衣服着脱やレストランの清掃・配膳、引き出しの開放など3つのシナリオで、タスク成功率の向上と安全な協調動作の実証に成功した。
keywords_ja: モバイルマニピュレーション

2611.21198.tldr_en: Quantitative results demonstrate CALDS effectiveness in improving task success and enabling safe, coordinated simultaneous execution while maintaining fidelity to demonstrated behaviors.

2611.21163.title: Polygraph: Large-Scale Multi-Session Trajectory Optimization using Pose Graphs
2611.21163.abstract: Robots, vehicles, and wearable devices often traverse the same environment many times. Each pass produces its own trajectory from onboard visual or visual-inertial odometry. These trajectories are locally accurate but drift over time and live in unrelated coordinate frames. Turning many such independent trajectories into one globally consistent set is the large-scale multi-session trajectory optimization problem. Existing solutions largely work offline. All sessions must be available up front, one session is fixed as the reference frame, and a single fused map is then optimized. This paper presents Polygraph, a multi-session trajectory optimization pipeline that processes sessions online, one keyframe and one spatial cluster at a time, and never builds a 3D map. Keyframes are grouped into local clusters. When a cluster closes, it is matched against every other session through learned image retrieval. Candidate pairs are verified with sparse feature matching, monocular metric depth, and robust pose estimation. A two-tier consensus gate admits a cross-session edge into the shared pose graph only once independent evidence corroborates it. A cheap incremental solve keeps the graph current, and a periodic robust batch solve prunes outliers. We evaluate Polygraph on stereo outdoor driving, HoloLens and iPad indoor traversals, legged indoor locomotion with a Boston Dynamics Spot, and large-scale outdoor vehicle and handheld routes. Against the closest prior work on the same GPU model, using its reported timings, Polygraph runs faster, commits fewer loop-closure edges, and matches or improves on accuracy.

llm.title_ja: Polygraph: ポーズグラフを用いた大規模マルチセッション軌道最適化
llm.tldr_ja: 3Dマップを構築せずにオンラインでキーフレームと空間クラスタ単位でマルチセッションの軌道最適化を行うPolygraphパイプラインを提案した。
llm.problem: 複数回の通過で得られるローカルに正確だがドリフトを含む独立した軌道を、事前一括処理なしに大規模に大域的整合性のあるセットに統合することの難しさ。
llm.method: キーフレームをローカルクラスタにグループ化し、画像検索とスパース特徴量マッチングによりクロスセッションのエッジをポーズグラフにインクリメンタルに統合・最適化する。
llm.result: 屋外のステレオ走行、屋内トラバーサル、四足歩行ロボットなど多様な環境において、従来手法よりも高速に動作し、ループクロージャエッジを削減しつつ同等以上の精度を達成した。
llm.limitation: source_summaryがないため要旨に記載なし

2611.21163.tldr_en: Polygraph is presented, a multi-session trajectory optimization pipeline that processes sessions online, one keyframe and one spatial cluster at a time, and never builds a 3D map.

2611.21143.title: WinDEX: Metric 3D Hand Motion Reconstruction in the Wild for Dexterous Teleoperation and Policy Learning
2611.21143.abstract: Human manipulation data are widely used to train robots for human-like dexterity. However, low-cost, large-scale collection in the wild remains challenging. Existing methods remain limited in geometrically grounded metric-scale reconstruction, real-world generalization and inference speed. We present WinDEX, integrating (1) geometric-temporal optimization for metric 3D hand annotation from in-the-wild egocentric stereo videos, combined with visual-inertial SLAM for world-frame reconstruction; (2) WinDEX-Net, an end-to-end, fisheye-native network combining calibrated stereo, local detail and temporal context, with a data-model flywheel of model-assisted annotation and retraining; (3) distilled models for offline reconstruction and causal streaming, supporting reinforcement learning and teleoperation; and (4) low-cost CyberCap stereo-inertial capture, forming the WinDEX-Hand dataset with 1,000 hours of training annotations and held-out human-annotated in-the-wild 2D and independent optical motion-capture evaluation sets. Offline reconstruction runs at 43.61 FPS and causal streaming at 171 FPS. On held-out data, offline reconstruction achieves state-of-the-art accuracy: 14.5 pixels in-the-wild reprojection error and, with visual-inertial odometry, 37.29 mm world-frame joint error. We achieve 7.6 and 3.6 times the task success rates of reinforcement learning policies trained with WiLoR and HaWoR motion references, respectively, and demonstrate real-time arm-hand teleoperation. Project website: https://fruitrabbit.github.io/WinDEX/.

llm.title_ja: WinDEX: 器用なテレオペレーションとポリシー学習に向けたインザワイルドでのメトリック3D手の動き再構成
llm.tldr_ja: 幾何学・時間的最適化とWinDEX-Netを統合し、インザワイルドの映像からメトリック3D手の動きを再構成してロボットの器用な操作学習や制御を実現した。
llm.problem: 人間の器用な操作データをロボット学習に活用するためには、インザワイルドでの低コストかつ大規模なメトリック3D再構成が困難であること。
llm.method: 幾何学・時間的最適化によるメトリック3D手アノテーション、魚眼対応のWinDEX-Net、およびデータ・モデルのフライホイールを統合したWinDEXを構築する。
llm.result: オフライン再構成は43.61 FPS、因果的ストリーミングは171 FPSで動作し、強化学習ポリシーの成功率を大幅に向上させ、実時間でのアーム・ハンド遠隔操作を実現した。

2611.21143.tldr_en: This work presents WinDEX, integrating geometric-temporal optimization for metric 3D hand annotation from in-the-wild egocentric stereo videos, combined with visual-inertial SLAM for world-frame reconstruction and distilled models for offline reconstruction and causal streaming, supporting reinforcement learning and teleoperation.

2611.21129.title: Linglong Agent Service: A Runtime for Centralized Agent Reasoning and Distributed Execution
2611.21129.abstract: LLM agents can use remote tools and cloud sandboxes, but integrating reasoning, session state, and heterogeneous execution sites remains a runtime design problem. We present Linglong Agent Service (agentsvc), a self-hosted HTTP service and embeddable Python runtime that treats execution site as a configurable dimension alongside model, tools, and context. A parent service retains inference orchestration, tool descriptions, and conversation history; each inference request selects one child environment for file, shell, terminal, and MCP operations. Direct HTTP and child-initiated WebSocket tunnels carry the same application interfaces, including portable request context and centrally managed updates. The normal core path requires no third-party Python packages, with an optional Windows pseudo-terminal dependency. We further present online_debugger as the process-scale special case of execution-site separation: an instrumented program submits exception evidence, executes session-scoped inspection tools inside the incident process, and resumes the same diagnostic session. Its default prompt requires failing-then-passing reproduction evidence for source changes, while runtime patch activation and failed-call recovery remain unimplemented. We explain the design through constrained expected-utility reasoning, compare concrete mechanisms with Hermes Agent, Pi, Codex, and Claude Code, and report implementation and regression-test evidence. The current evidence establishes executable contracts, not performance advantages, repair accuracy, or production recovery. The source code is open source under the MIT license at https://github.com/mz24cn/agents.

llm.title_ja: Linglong Agent Service: 中央集権型エージェント推論と分散実行のためのランタイム
llm.tldr_ja: LLMエージェントの推論、セッション状態、異種実行環境の統合課題を解決するため、実行環境をモデルやツールと並ぶ設定可能な次元として扱う自己ホスト型HTTPサービスおよびPythonランタイム「Linglong Agent Service」を提案する。
llm.problem: LLMエージェントにおいて、推論、セッション状態、異種実行環境の統合はランタイム設計上の問題となっている。
llm.method: 実行環境をモデルやツール等と並ぶ設定可能な次元として扱い、推論のオーケストレーションと子環境での操作を組み合わせた自己ホスト型HTTPサービスとPythonランタイムを構築した。
llm.result: 実行可能な契約を確立し、プロセス規模の特殊ケースとしてオンラインデバッガーを提示して実装と回帰テストの証拠を報告した。
llm.limitation: 実行時パッチの有効化や失敗した呼び出しの回復は未実装である。
keywords_ja: 推論オーケストレーション

2611.21129.tldr_en: Linglong Agent Service is presented, a self-hosted HTTP service and embeddable Python runtime that treats execution site as a configurable dimension alongside model, tools, and context and explains the design through constrained expected-utility reasoning.

2611.21115.title: ReuseMem: One Memory, Multiple Goals in Robot Manipulation
2611.21115.abstract: Robots that work alongside people should be able to use what they have seen when new requests arise. The same experience may later support identifying an object or returning it to its original location, although these uses were unknown during observation. ReuseMem learns to use one visual memory for multiple later manipulation goals. It records visual features independently of future goals, retrieves complementary evidence for each request, and combines it with the current scene through a lightweight action interface. Retrieval is supervised by how well candidate evidence supports expert-action prediction across different current states, linking memory selection to its use in manipulation. Repeated visual features are stored once, and memory computations that remain unchanged during action generation are reused. Experiments on four simulation tasks and two physical scenarios demonstrate reuse of a common recording across different requests. With matched action adaptation, ReuseMem improves joint goal completion on the benchmark tasks by 24.5 percentage points over uniform memory. These findings show that one memory can support multiple later manipulation goals as the scene changes.

llm.title_ja: ReuseMem: ロボットマニピュレーションにおける1つの記憶と多様な目標
llm.tldr_ja: ReuseMemは、将来の目標から独立して視覚的特徴を記録し、軽量なアクションインターフェースを介して現在のシーンと組み合わせることで、1つの視覚的記憶を複数の異なるマニピュレーション目標に再利用できるように学習する。
llm.problem: ロボットが観察時には未知であった将来の多様な目標に対して、過去の視覚的経験を再利用することは困難である。
llm.method: 将来の目標から独立して視覚的特徴を記録し、現在のシーンと組み合わせてエキスパート行動予測を教師として検索を最適化する軽量なアクションインターフェースを学習する。
llm.result: 4つのシミュレーション課題と2つの現実シナリオの実験により、均一メモリと比較してベンチマーク課題の目標達成率が24.5パーセントポイント向上した。
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.21115.tldr_en: ReuseMem learns to use one visual memory for multiple later manipulation goals as the scene changes, showing that one memory can support multiple later manipulation goals as the scene changes.

2611.21099.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
2611.21099.abstract: Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Bringing force to an API-only frozen model raises two challenges. First, contact evolves much faster than an API model can decide, so the system must close the loop on force beneath the model. Second, a frozen model cannot interpret raw force streams, so force must be returned in a form the model can reason about. Therefore, we present ForceHarness, a harness that lets frozen models use force without demonstrations or finetuning. After calibrating hand force from a wrist sensor or joint torques alone, ForceHarness addresses the first challenge with self-terminating force primitives that regulate force on their own and return at a contact event. To address the second challenge, a physics translation layer turns each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty as the tool result. To evaluate ForceHarness against expert force controllers and learned policies under identical conditions, we also build HiddenPhys, a seven-task MuJoCo benchmark with hidden physical variables. On a real arm without a wrist force sensor, ForceHarness raises the zero-shot success rate of GPT-6 Astra from 3.3% to 90.0%. In simulation, it adds 17.5 percentage points on the public ForceBench suite and 34.3 percentage points on HiddenPhys, surpassing force-aware policies trained on demonstrations on both benchmarks and matching hand-written expert controllers on HiddenPhys. Ablations further show that smaller models make significantly better decisions when given physical quantities rather than raw force values.
2611.21099.comment: 31 pages: 8-page main paper, references, and supplementary material. Project page: https://showlab.github.io/ForceHarness

llm.title_ja: ForceHarness: 凍結されたフロンティアモデルのための力から行動・物理への変換ハーネス
llm.tldr_ja: ForceHarnessは、デモやファインチューニングを行わずに、手首センサーや関節トルクから較正された力と自己終端型の力プリミティブおよび物理翻訳レイヤーを用いて、APIのみの凍結されたフロンティアモデルが接触力を活用できるようにする。
llm.problem: 接触力は画像には映らないが、APIのみの凍結されたフロンティアモデルは生の力ストリームを解釈できず、接触変化が速すぎるためモデル単体では制御できない。
llm.method: 自己終端型の力プリミティブで力を調整し、物理翻訳レイヤーによって力トレースを不確実性付きの物理量へと変換してツール結果としてモデルに提供する。
llm.result: 実機のロボットアームにおいてGPT-6 Astraのゼロショット成功率を3.3%から90.0%に向上させ、シミュレーションのForceBenchおよびHiddenPhysでも既存手法を上回る成果を挙げた。

2611.21099.tldr_en: ForceHarness is presented, a harness that lets frozen models use force without demonstrations or finetuning, andlations show that smaller models make significantly better decisions when given physical quantities rather than raw force values.

2611.21069.title: CoopDistill: Equilibrium-Guided Multi-Agent Policy Distillation for Cooperative Driving
2611.21069.abstract: Cooperative driving extends autonomous driving from individual vehicle decisions to joint maneuvers that improve traffic safety and efficiency. Optimization-based methods impose safety constraints but often fix paths to simplify multi-vehicle planning, limiting spatial flexibility. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) explores alternatives through interaction, but coordinated learning and safe execution remain challenging. Their integration nevertheless faces challenges in exploration efficiency, experience allocation, and execution reliability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes CoopDistill, an equilibrium-guided multi-agent policy distillation framework. A potential-game (PG) formulation provides a fixed-path longitudinal reference, around which a residual MARL policy learns longitudinal acceleration, conflict-approach timing, and lateral path corrections. A hard-case curriculum concentrates experience on interactions that PG leaves unresolved or substantially delayed. A comparative rollout selector evaluates the joint consequences of learned corrections against PG before choosing the executed action. Experiments in merging, roundabout, and intersection scenarios compare CoopDistill with six baselines at four connected automated vehicle penetration levels. Relative to PG, success improves by 2.1--27.1 percentage points and delay decreases by 7.3--27.3\%, with no observed collisions. Code is available at https://github.com/FanGShiYuu/CoopDistill

llm.title_ja: CoopDistill: 協調的運転のための均衡誘導型マルチエージェント方策蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: CoopDistillは、ポテンシャルゲームの定式化による縦方向の基準と、残差マルチエージェント強化学習方策、ハードケースカリキュラム、比較ロールアウト選択器を組み合わせて協調的運転の性能と安全性を向上させる。
llm.problem: 協調的運転におけるマルチエージェント強化学習は、探索効率、経験の割り当て、実行の信頼性の面で課題を抱えている。
llm.method: ポテンシャルゲームによる縦方向の基準の周りで残差MARL方策を学習させ、困難な事例に集中するカリキュラムと比較ロールアウト選択器を組み合わせる。
llm.result: 合流、ラウンドアバウト、交差点のシナリオにおいて、ベースラインと比較して成功率が2.1〜27.1パーセントポイント向上し、遅延が7.3〜27.3%減少した。
keywords_ja: マルチエージェント強化学習

2611.21069.tldr_en: This paper proposes CoopDistill, an equilibrium-guided multi-agent policy distillation framework, which provides a fixed-path longitudinal reference, around which a residual MARL policy learns longitudinal acceleration, conflict-approach timing, and lateral path corrections.

2611.21060.title: MetricHand: Geometry-Aware Flow Matching for 4D Hand Reconstruction in Metric World Space
2611.21060.abstract: Egocentric hand motion provides physical motion supervision for dexterous manipulation and vision-language-action pretraining. Reliable use of this supervision requires accurate and temporally coherent 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. Existing methods typically lift framewise estimates produced under weak perspective into world coordinates. By ignoring joint-dependent depth variation at close range, this approximation couples errors in translation, orientation, and articulation that persist after world lifting and worsen under occlusion. We present MetricHand, a geometry-aware flow matching framework for 4D hand reconstruction in metric world space. MetricHand encodes depth priors from hand-object interaction regions into joint-associated representations that preserve local spatial structure and metric scale. Fused with visual features, this geometry guides coarse metric estimation and conditions every step of temporal generation. The model jointly recovers world-space translation, global orientation, MANO articulation, and shape, while structural priors and temporal context support estimation under partial occlusion. MetricHand reduces camera-space MPJPE by 49.3% and 52.9%, absolute world-space MPJPE by 28.7% and 21.7%, and wrist localization error by 48.5% and 37.9% relative to HaWoR, respectively. World-space acceleration error decreases by 44.2% and 64.3%, demonstrating improved temporal fidelity alongside more accurate absolute localization.

llm.title_ja: MetricHand: メトリック・ワールド空間における4Dハンド復元のための幾何学認識型フロー・マッチング
llm.tldr_ja: MetricHandは、手と物体の相互作用領域からの深度事前情報を関節関連表現にエンコードし、視覚的特徴と融合させることで、メトリック・ワールド空間での正確かつ時間的に一貫した4Dハンド復元を実現する。
llm.problem: 従来の弱遠近法に基づく手フレーム推定は、近距離での関節依存の深度変化を無視するため、ワールド座標変換後に誤差が結合し、オクルージョン下で悪化する。
llm.method: 手と物体の相互作用領域の深度事前情報をローカル空間構造とメトリック・スケールを保持する表現にエンコードし、視覚的特徴と融合してフローマッチングの各ステップを条件付ける。
llm.result: カメラ空間のMPJPEを49.3%および52.9%削減し、絶対ワールド空間のMPJPEや手首の局所化誤差、加速度誤差を大幅に低減した。

2611.21060.tldr_en: The model jointly recovers world-space translation, global orientation, MANO articulation, and shape, while structural priors and temporal context support estimation under partial occlusion, demonstrating improved temporal fidelity alongside more accurate absolute localization.

2611.21059.title: Multi-CONDOR: Learning Multistable Motion Primitives from Demonstration
2611.21059.abstract: Dynamical-system-based motion policies provide a framework for learning reactive robot motions with stability and convergence properties. Many manipulation tasks, however, admit several distinct goals or a continuous set of acceptable outcomes, requiring motion primitives that preserve these alternatives. Accommodating both goal structures within a unified framework with continuous, autonomous dynamics remains an open challenge. We propose a CONDOR-based framework, multi-CONDOR, for learning motion primitives with either multiple discrete attractors or a continuous attracting goal contour. The approach combines imitation learning with losses that encourage agreement between the learned task dynamics and latent reference systems encoding the desired attraction structure. We provide a Lyapunov-based analysis of the convergence properties of the learned motion dynamics. We evaluate the framework on simulated benchmarks with discrete goals, qualitative examples with continuous goal contours, and robotic grasping experiments. In simulation, multi-CONDOR reduces trajectory RMSE by approximately 72% compared with separately learned single-goal motion primitives selected by a state machine. For tasks with two and three goals, respectively, it reduces the fraction of evaluated initial states ending outside the goal tolerance from StableNODE's 0.31% and 7.29% to 0% in both settings. Experiments with a Franka Emika robot arm demonstrate successful grasping of a container by either of its two handles using motions learned from demonstrations. Together, these results show multi-CONDOR combines motion reproduction with the flexibility to converge to alternative valid outcomes.

llm.title_ja: Multi-CONDOR: デモからの多安定運動プリミティブの学習
llm.tldr_ja: Multi-CONDORは、模倣学習とタスクダイナミクスを潜在参照システムに一致させる損失関数を組み合わせることで、複数の離散アトラクタまたは連続的な引き込みゴール輪郭を持つ運動プリミティブを学習する。
llm.problem: 複数の異なるゴールや連続的な許容結果の集合を持つマニピュレーション課題において、それらの代替案を維持する運動プリミティブを連続かつ自律的なダイナミクスで統一的に扱うことは困難である。
llm.method: 複数の離散的アトラクタまたは連続的ゴール輪郭を持つ運動プリミティブを学習するため、模倣学習にタスクダイナミクスと潜在参照システムの一致を促す損失関数を統合する。
llm.result: シミュレーションにおいて軌道RMSEを約72%削減し、複数のゴール設定において許容範囲外で終了する初期状態の割合を0%に低減、実機での把持に成功した。

2611.21059.tldr_en: Results show multi-CONDOR combines motion reproduction with the flexibility to converge to alternative valid outcomes, and a Lyapunov-based analysis of the convergence properties of the learned motion dynamics is provided.

2611.21057.title: WiTac: Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations for Contact-Rich Manipulation
2611.21057.abstract: Similar tactile contacts can call for different corrections depending on the configuration of the hand, object and target. Rather than supplying touch and wrist vision separately, fusing them before policy injection better grounds tactile features in visual context, yielding more accurate contact representations. We introduce Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations (WiTac), a pretrained encoder that learns such representations before action generation. Pretrained on nearly 300 hours of SharpaDex data, WiTac deeply fuses tactile signals with hand motion and wrist views into a comprehensive contact representation. Conditioning downstream VLA policies (GR00T N1.7 and $π_{0.5}$) on WiTac substantially improves task success over vision-only base policies across four contact-rich manipulation tasks (+28.8% and +15.0% on average), and further outperforms a wrist-free tactile encoder by 18.8% and 7.5%, respectively. Offline analyses further show that incorporating wrist vision yields more accurate contact descriptors, stronger joint task-contact discrimination, greater feature stability under tactile noise, and clearer action-direction readout from similar contacts. Project page: https://wrist-informed-tactile-representations.github.io/.
2611.21057.tldr_en: Wrist-Informed Tactile Representations is introduced, a pretrained encoder that learns such representations before action generation that yields more accurate contact representations and better grounds tactile features in visual context, yielding more accurate contact representations.

llm.title_ja: WiTac：接触リッチな操作のための手首情報に基づく触覚表現
llm.tldr_ja: 触覚信号と手首カメラ映像、手の動きを深く融合させる事前学習済みエンコーダ「WiTac」を提案し、接触リッチな操作タスクにおけるVLAポリシーのタスク成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 触覚と手首の視覚情報を別々に供給すると、ハンドやオブジェクトの構成に応じた適切な補正が難しくなる。
llm.method: 約300時間のSharpaDexデータで事前学習を行い、触覚信号、手の動き、手首視覚を深く融合した接触表現を学習する。
llm.result: 4つの接触リッチな操作タスクで視覚のみのベースラインや触覚エンコーダを上回り、平均成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.21035.title: FlowRow: Learning Navigation Behaviors in Agricultural Environments with Long-Horizon Goal-Conditioned Flow Matching Policies
2611.21035.abstract: Autonomous monitoring and intervention in semi-structured agricultural environments, such as orchards and vineyards, require mobile robots to navigate to locations across diverse field configurations. This entails performing navigation behaviors including in-row driving, row turning and skipping, and inter-row traversal. Recent learning-based approaches have enabled robust in-row navigation from onboard perception, but navigation across rows typically requires a priori knowledge of field geometry to specify and tune row-transition maneuvers, preventing arbitrary transitions between rows. We address this challenge by framing navigation in these environments as a goal-directed navigation task, where a long-horizon goal is expressed relative to the robot and a planner generates local paths based on the goal and the robot's perceptual observations. We present FlowRow, a flow-matching-based local planner which models the distribution of diverse agricultural navigation behaviors as $\mathrm{SE}(2)$ paths using the long-horizon goal and depth perception. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce RowNavBench, a navigation benchmark for semi-structured agricultural environments developed in Isaac Sim, comprising 900 episodes across grape vineyards, lemon orchards, and apple orchards with varying row lengths, row and plant spacings, plant positions, and weed growth. FlowRow achieves 87% success, compared to 44% for the strongest generative behavior cloning baseline retrained on the same demonstrations. We will release our benchmark, data, and code upon acceptance.

llm.title_ja: FlowRow: 長期ゴール条件付きフローマッチング方策による農業環境でのナビゲーション行動の学習
llm.tldr_ja: FlowRowは、ロボットの相対的な長期ゴールと深度知覚を入力として、SE(2)パスに基づく多様な農業環境のナビゲーション行動の分布をモデル化するフローマッチングベースのローカルプランナーである。
llm.problem: 半構造化された農業環境における行間走行や行の転換などの移動には、従来は事前にフィールド幾何学の知識を指定して調整する必要があり、任意の行間移動が妨げられていた。
llm.method: 長期ゴールをロボット相対で表現し、深度知覚と長期ゴールからSE(2)パスとして多様な農業ナビゲーション行動の分布をモデル化するフローマッチングベースのローカルプランナーを構築した。
llm.result: Isaac Simで構築された900のエピソードからなる農業ナビゲーションベンチマークRowNavBenchにおいて、従来の行動クローン法を大きく上回る87%の成功率を達成した。

2611.21035.tldr_en: FlowRow is presented, a flow-matching-based local planner which models the distribution of diverse agricultural navigation behaviors as $\mathrm{SE}(2)$ paths using the long-horizon goal and depth perception, and achieves 87% success, compared to 44% for the strongest generative behavior cloning baseline retrained on the same demonstrations.

2611.21033.title: POKE: Probe Offline, Keep Efficiently for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.21033.abstract: Visual token pruning reduces the inference cost of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, but attention-based scores do not directly measure a token's effect on the predicted action. We define action sensitivity as the magnitude of the first-order action change when a token is replaced by its camera's mean token and estimate it for all tokens with a single backward pass. Computing it online is costly: scoring on the full (unpruned) graph needs an extra forward pass at every control step. Scoring on the pruned forward pass is cheaper but causes scoring-graph lock-in: removed tokens lose their direct paths through later layers and tend to receive lower scores, making those locations less likely to return. On replayed observations, even with a random conditioning mask, pruned-graph scoring re-selects 59% of the mask's tokens, versus 6% expected by chance; attention histories show a similar bias. POKE (Probe Offline, Keep Efficiently) computes full-graph action sensitivities offline and distills them into a student with under 0.3M parameters. At inference, the student scores the current observation without backpropagation or previous masks, and score-guided diversity selection retains the tokens. Keeping 32 of 512 visual tokens on LIBERO, POKE achieves 95.2% success on OpenVLA-OFT and 90.8% on $π_{0.5}$ at $1.85\times$ and $1.26\times$ speedups, outperforming attention-, diversity-, and distillation-based pruners, with larger margins on LIBERO-Plus.

llm.title_ja: POKE: 視覚・言語・行動モデルのためのオフラインプローブによる効率的なトークン削減
llm.tldr_ja: POKEは、フルグラフでのアクション感度をオフラインで計算して軽量なスチューデントモデルに蒸留し、推論時に逆伝播なしでスコア誘導型の多様性選択を用いて重要な視覚トークンを保持することでVLAモデルを高速化する。
llm.problem: 視覚トークン削減はVLAモデルの推論コストを削減するが、アテンションベースのスコアはアクションへの影響を直接測定できず、オンラインでの計算は高コストである。
llm.method: フルグラフのアクション感度をオフラインで計算して小規模なスチューデントモデルに蒸留し、推論時にバックプロパゲーションなしでトークンをスコア・誘導型の多様性選択によって保持する。
llm.result: LIBEROにおいてOpenVLA-OFTで95.2%、π0.5で90.8%の成功率を達成し、1.85倍および1.26倍の高速化を実現して既存のプルーナーを上回った。

2611.21033.tldr_en: POKE (Probe Offline, Keep Efficiently) computes full-graph action sensitivities offline and distills them into a student with under 0.3M parameters, outperforming attention-, diversity-, and distillation-based pruners, with larger margins on LIBERO-Plus.

2611.20978.title: Inverse Kinematics in Endoscopic Scenarios using MoveIt
2611.20978.abstract: Inverse kinematics are critical in many robotic applications, yet standard MoveIt-based solvers struggle in confined scenarios. This paper provides a benchmark of the available solvers and compares multiple practical modifications for improving the performance of the solvers. Splitting the IK problem into two parts results in the best performance, leading to a 100% success rate under 100 ms in an endoscopic tank scenario.

llm.title_ja: 内視鏡シナリオにおけるMoveItを用いた逆運動学
llm.tldr_ja: 制限された内視鏡シナリオにおけるMoveItベースの逆運動学ソルバーの性能を比較・評価し、IK問題を2つに分割することで内視鏡タンク環境において100ms未満で100%の成功率を達成する実用的な修正方法を提案する。
llm.problem: 標準的なMoveItベースの逆運動学（IK）ソルバーは、制限されたシナリオにおいて苦戦する。
llm.method: 利用可能なソルバーのベンチマークを行い、IK問題を2つの部分に分割するなどの実用的な修正方法の性能を比較する。
llm.result: 内視鏡タンクシナリオにおいて、100ms未満で100%の成功率を達成した。

2611.20978.tldr_en: This paper provides a benchmark of the available solvers and compares multiple practical modifications for improving the performance of the solvers, leading to a 100% success rate under 100 ms in an endoscopic tank scenario.

2611.20971.title: FAVR: Flow-Aware Visual Residual Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Policies
2611.20971.abstract: Pretrained video representations provide rich temporal information for robotic manipulation, yet effectively integrating them into existing vision-language-action (VLA) policies remains challenging. We present Flow-Aware Visual Residual Alignment (FAVR), a lightweight framework for flow-aware visual conditioning of frozen VLA policies. FAVR maintains a compact temporal visual state through linear Test-Time Training (TTT) and retrieves action-conditioned visual features throughout flow-based action generation. By exploiting the affine structure of the frozen action head, we explicitly characterize how injected visual features influence predicted action velocities and formulate flow-aware channel selection as a box-constrained optimization problem. We develop a FISTA-based solver for joint gate optimization and derive an efficient closed-form approximation through diagonalization and rescaling. With only 1.74-2.19M trainable parameters and 5,000 adaptation steps, FAVR improves pretrained VLA policies across benchmarks. On RoboTwin 2.0, FAVR improves LingBot-VLA from 87.12% to 90.04% under clean conditions and from 86.88% to 89.38% under randomized conditions. A controlled ablation on five RoboTwin tasks further shows that flow-aware gating increases average success from 72.0% with a gate shared across flow steps to 82.0%, demonstrating the benefit of adapting visual conditioning throughout action generation.
2611.20971.comment: 17 pages, 5 figures. Equal contribution: Qixuan Wu and Xiaole Yang. Corresponding authors: Yuguang Yang and Baochang Zhang

llm.title_ja: FAVR: 視覚・言語・行動ポリシーのためのフロー認識型視覚残差アライメント
llm.tldr_ja: FAVRは、線形テスト時訓練（TTT）によるコンパクトな時間的視覚状態の維持と、フローベースの行動生成を通じたアクション条件付き視覚特徴の取得により、凍結されたVLAポリシーを軽量に適応させるフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 事前学習済みの動画表現を既存のVLAポリシーに効果的に統合することは困難である。
llm.method: 線形テスト時訓練によりコンパクトな時間的視覚状態を維持し、凍結された行動ヘッドのアフイン構造を活用してフロー認識型チャネル選択を最適化問題として定式化して解く。
llm.result: RoboTwin 2.0においてLingBot-VLAの成功率をクリーン条件下で90.04%に、ランダム化条件下で89.38%に向上させ、フロー認識型ゲーティングの有効性を示した。

2611.20971.tldr_en: Flow-Aware Visual Residual Alignment (FAVR), a lightweight framework for flow-aware visual conditioning of frozen VLA policies, is presented and a FISTA-based solver for joint gate optimization and derive an efficient closed-form approximation through diagonalization and rescaling is developed.

2611.20950.title: ROSE: A Shared Cross-Embodiment Facial-Motion Latent Space for Humanoid Robot Expression
2611.20950.abstract: Natural, coherent full-face dynamic expressions are central to making humanoid robots socially approachable, yet existing systems commonly realize only limited lip motion or scripted expressions. The limitation is both physical and algorithmic. A compact head leaves little room for densely packed, independently controllable actuation; meanwhile, learned systems often generate an avatar video, landmarks, or facial parameters and then infer actuator commands through visual retargeting. This render-and-invert path adds latency and artifacts, and it does not reliably transfer generated behavior to a physical robot. We present ROSE (RObot facial expression through Shared motion Embeddings), a framework that integrates biomimetic hardware, cross-embodiment motion representation learning, and multimodal motion generation. On the hardware side, we build a flexible tendon-sheath transmission structure that integrates 34 actuators into a 19.5 cm biomimetic head. By decoupling actuator placement from facial action points, it enables coordinated full-face expression within a compact volume. On the algorithmic side, ROSE-VAE learns an identity-independent shared facial-motion latent space from human, digital-human, and robot observations. ROSE-Flow directly maps text, audio, or their combination to trajectories in this motion space without using video as a generator input. ROSE-ACT then converts these trajectories into constrained actuator commands. Our system demonstrates how high-density biomimetic hardware and a shared executable facial-motion representation can jointly unify cross-embodiment learning, multimodal generation, and physical robot expression.

llm.title_ja: ROSE: ヒューマノイドロボットの表情のための共有クロスエンボディ顔面運動潜在空間
llm.tldr_ja: ROSEは、生体模倣ハードウェア、クロスエンボディ運動表現学習、マルチモーダル運動生成を統合し、ビデオを生成器の入力として使用せずにテキストや音声からロボットの制約されたアクチュエータコマンドを直接生成する。
llm.problem: 限られた頭部スペースでの高密度なアクチュエーションの物理的制約や、レンダリングと反転を経る従来手法の遅延・アーティファクト、実機への転移の困難さ。
llm.method: 柔軟な腱シース伝動構造を持つ生体模倣ヘッドの構築、人間・デジタル人間・ロボットの観察から共有顔面運動潜在空間を学習するROSE-VAE、テキストや音声から軌道を直接生成するROSE-Flowを統合する。
llm.result: 高密度な生体模倣ハードウェアと共有される実行可能な顔面運動表現により、クロスエンボディ学習、マルチモーダル生成、物理ロボットの表情表現を統合できることを実証した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット
生体模倣ハードウェア

2611.20950.tldr_en: ROSE is presented, a framework that integrates biomimetic hardware, cross-embodiment motion representation learning, and multimodal motion generation that demonstrates how high-density biomimetic hardware and a shared executable facial-motion representation can jointly unify cross-embodiment learning, multimodal generation, and physical robot expression.

2611.20939.title: TacBridge: Learning Unified Tactile Representations through Cross-Sensor Correspondence
2611.20939.abstract: Optical tactile sensors record tactile videos that capture local deformation and its temporal evolution during contact, supporting robot manipulation, force estimation, and tactile representation learning. Differences in imaging geometry, background appearance, illumination, resolution, and deformation response lead to sensor-dependent observations of the same contact across GelSight, DIGIT, GelSlim, TacTip, and other optical tactile sensors. This variability limits representation transfer and the joint use of multi-sensor data. We introduce TacBridge, a framework for learning unified representations from multi-sensor tactile videos through cross-sensor correspondence. Specifically, multi-sensor masked tactile-video pre-training learns spatiotemporal representations across sensors. We then train the same masked model jointly on same-sensor and cross-sensor reconstruction, using paired source and target videos of matched contact events. Experiments on cross-sensor translation and downstream perception demonstrate the cross-sensor generalization and task transferability of the learned tactile representations.

llm.title_ja: TacBridge: クロスセンサー対応を通じた統合触覚表現の学習
llm.tldr_ja: TacBridgeは、複数の光学式触覚センサーの間で、クロスセンサー対応を用いたマスク付き触覚ビデオの事前学習とクロスセンサー再構成を行うことで、センサー間に依存しない統合された触覚表現を学習するフレームワークである。
llm.problem: 画像化のジオメトリ、背景の外観、照明、解像度、変形応答の違いにより、GelSight、DIGIT、GelSlim、TacTipなどのセンサー間で観察が異なり、表現の転移やマルチセンサーデータの共同利用が制限される。
