llm.method: マルチセンサーのマスク付き触覚ビデオ事前学習により時空間表現を学習し、一致した接触イベントのペアデータを用いて同一センサーおよびクロスセンサーの再構成を共同で訓練する。
llm.result: クロスセンサー変換および下流の知覚タスクの実験において、学習された触覚表現のクロスセンサー汎化性とタスク転移性が実証された。

2611.20939.tldr_en: TacBridge, a framework for learning unified representations from multi-sensor tactile videos through cross-sensor correspondence, is introduced, which combines multi-sensor masked tactile-video pre-training with cross-sensor correspondence to learn spatiotemporal representations across sensors.

2611.20929.title: Transferable Neural CBFs via Generalized Closure
2611.20929.abstract: Classical control barrier functions (CBFs) provide safety constraints for controllers, but designing them by hand is difficult for underactuated vehicles and the resulting safe sets can be overly conservative. Neural CBFs can learn more informative barriers from data, yet a learned barrier is usually verified only for one fixed obstacle configuration. We study whether one neural barrier can be reused across environments by expressing the state relative to each obstacle. The key gap is that these relative coordinates may discard information needed to predict their own evolution. We give a generalized closure condition that represents this missing information as a residual and a lifting theorem that transfers a verified relative-coordinate barrier to every obstacle in a family. A rank test also identifies when symmetry alone cannot justify the transfer. We validate the conditions on a double integrator, a planar aircraft, and a 12-state quadrotor. Coordinates that fail the test lead to obstacle penetration or to a barrier condition that fails near hover, whereas body-frame coordinates close exactly for the quadrotor. The resulting barrier transfers to new maps without retraining and is effective in the reported deployment and fast-start experiments.
2611.20929.comment: 8 pages, 1 figure, 5 tables. Submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference (ACC 2027)

llm.tldr_ja: 本研究では、状態を各障害物に対する相対座標で表現し、不足情報を残差として表現する一般化された閉包条件とリフティング定理を導入することで、単一の環境で学習したニューラル制御バリア関数（CBF）を様々な障害物環境へ再学習なしに転移させる。
llm.problem: 古典的な制御バリア関数（CBF）の手動設計は低駆動車両に対して困難であり、ニューラルCBFで学習されたバリアは通常、固定された1つの障害物構成に対してしか検証されない。
llm.method: 状態を相対座標で表現し、不足する情報を残差として表す一般化された閉包条件と、検証済みバリアを家族内のすべての障害物に転移させるリフティング定理を提案する。
llm.result: 二重積分器、平面航空機、12状態クアッドロターで検証し、ボディフレーム座標がクアッドロターで正確に閉じ、再学習なしで新しいマップにバリアが転移することを確認した。

2611.20929.tldr_en: This work gives a generalized closure condition that represents this missing information as a residual and a lifting theorem that transfers a verified relative-coordinate barrier to every obstacle in a family and identifies when symmetry alone cannot justify the transfer.

2611.20888.title: Driving the Style: Velocity-Conditioned Whole-Body Control from Motion Demonstrations
2611.20888.abstract: Achieving human-like behavior on humanoid robots has advanced rapidly by leveraging motion-capture demonstrations rather than hand-crafted cost functions. Adversarial imitation supplies a style signal that lets a policy fulfill a task while adhering to a desired style, but is difficult to transfer to hardware. Whole-body tracking through reinforcement learning instead deploys reliably and imitates demonstrations faithfully, but the resulting policies are conditioned on the future reference, so they require a reference trajectory at runtime and can fail when the motion differs from the training data. We train a humanoid policy directly with whole-body tracking rewards while restricting its actor to compact locomotion commands and robot observations. Reference motion supervises the reward and privileged critic, without supplying reference joint trajectories to the actor or requiring teacher distillation. The demonstrated style is thereby encoded in the policy through the tracking reward, so the robot reproduces the whole-body style under commanded velocities. Trained on a single random-walk motion and commanded with velocity profiles from held-out motions, our policy reaches at least 98\% success in simulation and completes every trial on the Unitree G1. On held-out slow walking, whole-body tracking drops to 2\% success and command-conditioned distillation to 56\%, and both fail on the real robot. On the trained motions, the joint position error of our policy stays within 8\% of whole-body tracking, and it has a higher style coverage than adversarial motion priors (AMP), which fell on the real robot without a safety crane.

llm.title_ja: Driving the Style: 運動デモからの速度条件付き全身制御
llm.tldr_ja: 本研究では、アクターをコンパクトな移動コマンドとロボット観測に制限しつつ、全身追従報酬を用いてヒューマノイドポリシーを直接訓練し、参照軌道をランタイムで必要とせずに指定された速度で全身のスタイルを再現できるようにする。
llm.problem: 敵対的模倣は実機転移が難しく、強化学習による全身追従は将来の参照軌道をランタイムで必要とするため、訓練データと異なる運動時に失敗しやすい。
llm.method: アクターには参照関節軌道を渡さず、全身追従報酬と特権的 critic を用いてポリシーを直接訓練し、報酬を通じてデモのスタイルをエンコードする。
llm.result: 単一のランダムウォーク運動で訓練され、シミュレーションで98%以上の成功率に達し、Unitree G1の実機でもすべての試行を完了した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.20888.tldr_en: This work trains a humanoid policy directly with whole-body tracking rewards while restricting its actor to compact locomotion commands and robot observations, and finds that the policy has a higher style coverage than adversarial motion priors (AMP), which fell on the real robot without a safety crane.

2611.20872.title: MVSTF: Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Fusion for LiDAR-Based Moving Object Segmentation
2611.20872.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots confront significant chal lenges in recognizing the motion properties of objects in dy namic environments. However, existing methods are hindered by limitations such as boundary ambiguity, occlusion, viewpoint constraints, and training complexity. In this paper, we propose an innovative end-to-end Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Fusion network, named MVSTF, which utilizes sequential point clouds to generate multi-view images and feature differences, and designs a multi-branch network to extract spatio-temporal and dimen sional features in parallel, and realizes high-precision moving object segmentation. First, sequential point clouds are utilized to generate multi-view images and feature differences. Then, an end-to-end multi-branch network including Dual Down-sampling Blocks (DDB), Spatial Attention Blocks (SAB), Multi-Kernel Convolutional Neural Network blocks (MKCNN), Dual Feature Fusion Blocks (DFFB), and the Point Fusion (PF) module, is designed to extract motion features from feature differences and geometric and semantic features from multi-view images. Finally, an auxiliary semantic head is introduced to further improve the algorithm's robustness and the model's interpretability. This work is validated on the SemanticKITTI and KITTI-Road bench marks, achieving state-of-the-art results on the SemanticKITTI MOS validation set and the KITTI-Road validation set, and competitive results on the hidden SemanticKITTI-MOS test set. The code is available at https://github.com/ZhouJJ111/MVSTF.

llm.title_ja: MVSTF: LiDARベースの動的物体セグメンテーションのための多視点時空間融合
llm.tldr_ja: MVSTFは、連続点群から多視点画像と特徴差分を生成し、マルチブランチネットワークで時空間・次元特徴を並列抽出することで高精度な動的物体セグメンテーションを実現するエンドツーエンドのネットワークである。
llm.problem: 自律移動ロボットは動的環境における物体の運動特性の認識において、境界の曖昧さ、オクルージョン、視点の制約、訓練の複雑さなどの課題に直面している。
llm.method: 連続点群から多視点画像と特徴差分を生成し、DDBやSAB、MKCNNなどのマルチブランチネットワークを含むエンドツーエンドの構造で運動・幾何・セマンティック特徴を抽出する。
llm.result: SemanticKITTIおよびKITTI-Roadのベンチマークで検証され、SemanticKITTI MOS検証セットなどで最先端の結果を達成した。
keywords_ja: 動的物体セグメンテーション

2611.20872.tldr_en: An innovative end-to-end Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Fusion network, named MVSTF, which utilizes sequential point clouds to generate multi-view images and feature differences, and designs a multi-branch network to extract spatio-temporal and dimen sional features in parallel, and realizes high-precision moving object segmentation.

2611.20797.title: Correspondence-Free Camera Pose Estimation by Matching Moments
2611.20797.abstract: The blind perspective-$n$-point (PnP) problem is to estimate the pose of a calibrated camera from 2D and 3D point sets with unknown correspondences. We show that, for complete, noiseless observations, fourteen permutation-invariant image moments up to order four identify a fixed camera pose for almost every 3D point set containing at least twenty points. Our learning-free method, MomentPnP, matches these moments between the observed 2D points and the projected 3D points to initialize a camera pose without correspondences and refines the pose and correspondence weights using expectation--maximization. Across the test sets of three benchmarks, our method reduces median rotation error by $5$--$170\times$ relative to the best learned baseline, both with and without outliers. We recover accurate poses even with as many outliers as inliers. On dense ETH3D scans, pose accuracy improves as the point sets grow, even as individual correspondences become harder to resolve.
2611.20797.comment: 65 pages, including references and appendices; under review

llm.title_ja: モーメントマッチングによる対応付け不要のカメラ姿勢推定
llm.tldr_ja: MomentPnPは、対応付けが未知の2Dおよび3D点群の間で最大次数4までの14個の不変画像モーメントをマッチングすることで、対応付けなしでカメラ姿勢を初期化し、期待値最大化法で姿勢と対応重みを洗練する学習不要の手法である。
llm.problem: 未知の対応付けを持つ2Dおよび3D点群から較正されたカメラの姿勢を推定する盲目Perspective-n-Point（PnP）問題において、対応付けの解決は困難である。
llm.method: 観測された2D点と投影された3D点の間で、順序4までの14個の不変画像モーメントをマッチングして姿勢を初期化し、期待値最大化法により姿勢と対応重みを洗練する。
llm.result: 3つのベンチマークのテストセットにおいて、外れ値の有無にかかわらず、学習済みベースラインと比較して中央値回転誤差を5〜170倍削減した。
keywords_ja: モーメントマッチング
コンピュータビジョン

2611.20797.tldr_en: The learning-free method, MomentPnP, matches these moments between the observed 2D points and the projected 3D points to initialize a camera pose without correspondences and refines the pose and correspondence weights using expectation--maximization.

2611.20792.title: TRR: A Thermal Interaction Engine for Robot Simulation and RGBT Data Generation
2611.20792.abstract: A robot's actions change the thermal conditions of its next interaction: heat retained after release, carried with objects or stored beneath the surface can change a later contact's outcome despite similar current temperatures. Training trajectories must capture how these effects connect earlier actions to later observations and task outcomes. We present TRR, a \emph{Thermal Robot Renderer} that attaches spatial and depth-resolved thermal state to both contact partners, updates local heat exchange through contact, transport and separation, and generates synchronized RGB--thermal (RGBT) observations and event-local task checks on one execution clock. Controlled interventions show why retained heat, spatial transport and internal storage matter for subsequent contact outcomes. From the same state, TRR produces a paired six-task benchmark of 2,224 static--dynamic pairs, that is, 4,448 trajectories with synchronized dual-view observations, states and actions. Visible thermal history raises safe contact-site selection from 75.0\% to 91.7\% on a dedicated learning corpus, and training on dynamic histories raises simulated transfer completion by 50 percentage points under a new heating procedure with shared feedback execution. We demonstrate RGBT observation adapters on MuJoCo and Isaac Sim, report an engineering inventory of ten prepared robot configurations and six demonstrated camera viewpoints, and describe a developer workflow that carries an existing robot scene to exported RGBT records. The benchmark, the workflow and the platform resources described in Section 6 form the first items of a planned public release. Demonstrations and resource updates are available on the project page.

llm.title_ja: TRR: ロボットシミュレーションおよびRGBTデータ生成のための熱的相互作用エンジン
llm.tldr_ja: TRR（Thermal Robot Renderer）は、接触パートナーに空間および深度分解能を持つ熱状態を付与し、接触や輸送を通じた局所的な熱交換を更新して、同期されたRGB-RGBT観測とタスクチェックを生成する熱的相互作用エンジンである。
llm.problem: ロボットの行動は次の相互作用の熱的条件を変化させるが、従来のシミュレーションは過去の行動が後の観察やタスク結果に結びつく熱的影響を十分に捉えられない。
llm.method: 接触パートナーに空間・深度分解能を持つ熱状態を持たせ、接触、輸送、分離を通じた局所的熱交換を更新し、同期されたRGBT観測を生成するフレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: 可視化された熱的履歴により、学習コーパスでの安全な接触位置選択が75.0%から91.7%に向上し、シミュレーション転移完了率が50パーセントポイント向上した。
keywords_ja: ロボットシミュレーション

2611.20792.tldr_en: TRR, a TRR that attaches spatial and depth-resolved thermal state to both contact partners, updates local heat exchange through contact, transport and separation, and generates synchronized RGB--thermal (RGBT) observations and event-local task checks on one execution clock is presented.

2611.20791.title: QTOP: Scaling Humanoid Motion Tracking with Quantile Critics
2611.20791.abstract: Learning human motion tracking policies through reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a core capability that underpins a majority of recent progress in humanoid whole-body control. However, achieving generalization to unseen motions at high fidelity requires jointly scaling training to thousands of GPU and dataset hours. This work hypothesizes that motion tracking is inherently compute-bound because training on a diverse set of motions introduces learning interference, similar to multi-task RL. To tackle this, we propose Quantile Tracking Optimization (QTOP), which improves sample efficiency by introducing a distributional advantage estimate conditioned on state and reference pairs. QTOP outperforms on and off-policy RL baselines both in simulation and real-world tracking scenarios on multiple datasets by up to 10\%. Furthermore, we establish a scaling law for QTOP and find that, aside from scaling predictably, dataset size has minimal impact on performance for moderately sized GPU hour regimes.

llm.title_ja: QTOP: 分位点criticによるヒューマノイド運動追従のスケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: QTOPは、状態と参照のペアに条件付けられた分布的アドバンテージ推定を導入してサンプル効率を高めることで、多様な運動に対する汎化性能を向上させるヒューマノイド運動追従のための強化学習フレームワークである。
llm.problem: 多様な運動に対する汎化を高めるため数千のGPUとデータセット時間をかけてトレーニングをスケールさせると、マルチタスクRLと同様の学習干渉が発生して計算量ネックとなる。
llm.method: 状態と参照のペアに条件付けられた分布的アドバンテージ推定を導入し、サンプル効率を改善してオントレーニングおよびオオフラインRLベースラインを上回る最適化を行う。
llm.result: シミュレーションおよび実世界の追従シナリオにおいて、既存のオンポリシー・オフポリシーRLベースラインを最大10%上回る性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ヒューマノイドロボット

2611.20791.tldr_en: This work hypothesizes that motion tracking is inherently compute-bound because training on a diverse set of motions introduces learning interference, similar to multi-task RL, and proposes Quantile Tracking Optimization (QTOP), which improves sample efficiency by introducing a distributional advantage estimate conditioned on state and reference pairs.

2611.20771.title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: An Open and Efficient Small Language Model for Fast Conversational Agents
2611.20771.abstract: We introduce Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an open and efficient small language model further post-trained from Gemma-4-E4B-it and optimized for speed and intelligence per GB of memory used for fast conversational agents. The model carries forward Gemma's strong conversational capabilities and further improves multi-turn tool use, instruction following, and input grounding for fast, local voice/device assistants, interactive personas, and embedded/Edge interfaces. The model combines natural conversation with multi-turn agentic capabilities to power voice/device assistants, interactive characters and robotic/IoT interfaces running on GeForce RTX, Jetson, and RTX/DGX Spark. Experiments on 21 benchmarks show that Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB achieves the highest average accuracy while generating the fewest output tokens in both reasoning and non-reasoning modes, compared with Gemma-4-E4B-it and Qwen3.5-4B. The model is released with a DFlash drafter. With DFlash, Bolt E4B achieves $2.74\times$ the per-user decode speed of inference without speculative decoding at concurrency~1, and $1.21\times$ the generation throughput of Gemma-4-E4B-it with MTP at batch size 1.
2611.20771.comment: Animated versions of Figure 3 are available in the blog: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-E4B-4GB/

llm.title_ja: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB: 高速な会話型エージェントに向けたオープンで効率的な小型言語モデル
llm.tldr_ja: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GBは、Gemma-4-E4B-itをベースにポストトレーニングされ、限られたメモリ容量で高速かつ高精度なマルチターンツール使用や音声・デバイスアシスタントを実現するオープンな小型言語モデルである。
llm.problem: 高速な音声・デバイスアシスタント、インタラクティブキャラクター、組み込み/エッジインターフェースにおいて、メモリ使用量を抑えながらマルチターンツール使用や指示追従を高精度でこなす必要がある。
llm.method: Gemma-4-E4B-itをベースにポストトレーニングを行い、推論および非推論モードの両方で最高平均精度を維持しつつ出力トークン数を最小化し、DFlashドラフターを統合した。
llm.result: 21のベンチマークにおいて最高平均精度を達成し、スペキュラティブデコーディングなしの推論と比較して2.74倍のデコード速度を実現した。

2611.20770.title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications
2611.20770.abstract: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action. This review develops a unified framework linking mechanical load transmission, optical encoding, readout, and tactile inference to robotic task requirements. It examines reflective and waveguide-based devices, micro/nanofibers, fiber gratings, interferometric and resonant structures, and mechanoluminescent composites. Three considerations emerge across these approaches. First, high optical sensitivity supports accurate tactile estimation only when target variables remain identifiable under the relevant contact and calibration conditions. Second, spatial coverage and feedback timing must be assessed at the system level, accounting for multiplexing, acquisition, demodulation, and inference. Third, device characterization, offline recognition, and closed-loop robotic performance provide distinct levels of evidence and require different evaluation criteria. Representative studies illustrate how these considerations shape force estimation, contact localization, slip correction and distributed interaction. This review concludes with priorities for calibration transfer, reliable interfaces, scalable readout, and task-based validation, providing a basis for selecting and developing non-imaging optical tactile architectures for robotics.

llm.title_ja: ロボット向け非結像型光学式触覚センサ：変換原理、システム統合、ロボット応用
llm.tldr_ja: 非結像型光学式触覚センサの変換原理からシステム統合、ロボット応用までを網羅した統一的フレームワークを提案し、設計上の考慮事項と今後の課題を整理した。
llm.problem: 機械的・環境的影響から接触変数を識別し、タイムリーに情報を伝達する必要がある。
llm.method: 負荷伝達、光学エンコーディング、読取、触覚推論をタスク要件に結びつける統一的フレームワークを開発した。
llm.result: 力推定、接触局所化、滑り補正、分散インタラクションを形成する考慮事項を明らかにした。

2611.20767.title: UNITE: Consolidating Embodied VLM Specialists via Shared-Anchor One-Bit Factorization
2611.20767.abstract: Embodied capabilities such as visual grounding, spatial reasoning, navigation, and driving understanding are often developed in separate vision-language specialists fine-tuned from a common pretrained model.Deploying the specialists separately multiplies storage, whereas merging them into one dense model forces conflicting task updates to share parameters and loses part of each specialist's expertise.We introduce UNITE, a framework that consolidates such specialists into a compact shared-backbone mixture of experts. UNITE keeps the feed-forward block of each specialist as a routable expert and represents the expert bank through a shared-anchor one-bit factorization: a shared floating-point anchor plus expert-specific, row-scaled binary deviations.The anchor is optimized jointly with the scales and signs through closed-form alternating updates, using only source weights and no calibration data.Router adaptation then adjusts token-level expert selection with the backbone and experts frozen, updating fewer than $0.6$M parameters ($<0.01\%$ of the $8.8$B active parameters). Built from four Qwen3-VL-8B specialists, the complete UNITE model occupies $20.3$ GB, $1.16\times$ the storage of one dense specialist and $59.6\%$ below the uncompressed MoE. Across $22$ benchmarks and R2R Val-Unseen, UNITE matches six static merging methods in mean retention of best-specialist performance, leads all of them on Scan2Cap, ScanQA, and all four navigation metrics, and surpasses every source specialist on all five 3D scene understanding benchmarks (up to $+19.1$ on Scan2Cap) and on R2R navigation. Relative to the uncompressed MoE, factorization is nearly lossless on $21$ of $22$ benchmarks; the exception is VSI-Bench, where frame-count experiments suggest impaired use of cross-frame evidence.UNITE thus consolidates complementary embodied capabilities near single-model storage.

llm.title_ja: UNITE：共有アンカー1ビット因数分解による統合型身体性VLMスペシャリスト
llm.tldr_ja: UNITEは、共有アンカーと量子化を用いたコンパクトな共有バックボーン混合専門家（MoE）フレームワークにより、ストレージを抑えつつ複数の身体性VLMスペシャリストの性能を統合する。
llm.problem: 個別のVLMスペシャリストをデプロイするとストレージが増大し、単一モデルへの統合はタスクの競合を引き起こす。
llm.method: 共有アンカー型1ビット因数分解とルーター適応を用いて、複数のスペシャリストをコンパクトなMoEモデルに統合する。
llm.result: 22のベンチマークにおいて非圧縮MoEとほぼ同等の性能を維持しつつ、多様な3Dシーン理解やナビゲーションで既存手法を上回った。
llm.limitation: VSI-Benchにおいて、フレーム数の実験からクロスフレームのエビデンスの活用が阻害されることが示唆された。

2611.20767.tldr_en: UNITE, a framework that consolidates complementary embodied capabilities near single-model storage, is introduced, a framework that consolidates such specialists into a compact shared-backbone mixture of experts.

2611.20765.title: STA: A Split Temporal Adversary Method for Evaluating Robustness of Multimodal RL-based Driving Policies
2611.20765.abstract: Multimodal reinforcement learning (MRL) offers a promising paradigm for autonomous driving by jointly leveraging complementary sensor observations to learn effective decision-making policies. However, its effectiveness critically depends on temporal alignment across modalities, making temporal inconsistency a fundamental vulnerability. Even subtle misalignment or latency can corrupt fused representations and ultimately lead to decision failures. Existing studies have explored adversarial attacks to induce cross-modal temporal inconsistencies, thereby enabling systematic evaluation of the temporal robustness of MRL policies. However, existing methods remain limited in generality, realism, and adaptivity. To address these limitations, we propose the Split Temporal Adversary (STA), which formulates multimodal temporal attacks as a unified decision process that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection under realistic policy-aware and budget-constrained settings. STA includes two mechanisms: a) a unified multimodal temporal perturbation mechanism that delays observations via historical states, removing the need for modality-specific noise; b) a split multimodal adversarial decision mechanism that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection through adaptive optimization while leveraging the victim policy's clean actions to identify sensitive decision patterns. We provide a theoretical analysis of the induced distribution shift and a modality selection principle. Experiments in the CARLA simulator show that STA more than doubles the collision rate of the strongest baseline against PPO while using 17.8\% fewer attack attempts, and that it generalizes to a VLM-based driving policy. These results reveal temporal consistency as a critical vulnerability, highlighting temporal robustness as essential for safe autonomous driving.

llm.title_ja: STA：マルチモーダル強化学習ベースの運転方策のロバスト性評価のための分割時間的敵対的手法
llm.tldr_ja: マルチモーダル強化学習ベースの自動運転方策の致命的な脆弱性である時間的非同期性を効率的に評価するため、攻撃タイミングとモダリティ選択を最適化する分割時間的敵対的手法（STA）を提案する。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル強化学習におけるモダリティ間の時間的不整合や遅延が、融合表現の破損や意思決定の失敗を引き起こす。
llm.method: 履歴状態を介して観測を遅延させる統一的マルチモーダル時間摂動と、攻撃タイミングおよびモダリティ選択を最適化する分割敵対的メカニズムを組み合わせた。
llm.result: CARLAシミュレーターでの実験により、最強のベースラインと比較して、試行回数を17.8%削減しながら衝突率を2倍以上に高めることが示された。

2611.20765.tldr_en: The Split Temporal Adversary (STA), which formulates multimodal temporal attacks as a unified decision process that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection under realistic policy-aware and budget-constrained settings, and provides a theoretical analysis of the induced distribution shift and a modality selection principle.

2611.20741.title: Robotic Reward Models in the Foundation-Model Era
2611.20741.abstract: Robotic reward models (RRMs) use foundation models to replace per-task reward engineering with reusable, task-conditioned evaluation. Yet under one name, their outputs answer different questions, from whether a task succeeded to which execution is better. This survey organizes 114 methods into five semantic families by the question their native outputs answer: Outcome, Absolute Progress, Relative, Temporal Value, and Hybrid. Within this taxonomy, we review how model design determines what an evaluator can judge, how raw experience becomes supervision, and how existing evaluation practice tests the result. The review exposes a gap: agreement with demonstration order and downstream policy gains do not show whether a reward tracks task fulfillment. We therefore introduce RRM-Bench-1K, 1,117 real-robot videos of closed-loop executions with task-state and camera-evidence labels, and four contrast suites that separate the credited condition from its usual cues. A unified study of 27 evaluators shows that the strongest final scores rank whole executions well enough for selection and filtering. Dense credit, however, follows the progression of an execution more closely than its task state, and no evaluator signals when the decisive view is missing. How much fidelity a reward model needs therefore depends on the decision it drives. We outline directions from real-failure supervision to metrics that separate task state from chronology, and open-source RRM-Hub, a toolbox in which 14 existing RRMs can be readily applied and new evaluators tested on the same capabilities.

llm.title_ja: 基盤モデル時代のロボット報酬モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 114の手法を5つの意味論的ファミリーに分類してロボット報酬モデル（RRM）の現状を体系的に整理し、実ロボットの1,117本の動画を用いた評価ベンチマークを新たに提案した。
llm.problem: 報酬モデルの出力が成功判定から実行の良し悪しまで異なっており、タスク達成度を追跡できているかの検証が不足している。
llm.method: 114の手法を5つのファミリーに体系化し、実ロボットによる閉ループ実行動画とタスク状態ラベルを含むRRM-Bench-1Kを構築して評価を行った。
llm.result: 最高スコアの評価器は実行全体を順序付けできる一方、高密度なクレジットはタスク状態よりも実行の進行に追従することが示された。
llm.limitation: どの評価器も、決定的な視点が欠落していることを通知できない。

2611.20741.tldr_en: This survey organizes 114 methods into five semantic families by the question their native outputs answer: Outcome, Absolute Progress, Relative, Temporal Value, and Hybrid, and reviews how model design determines what an evaluator can judge, how raw experience becomes supervision, and how existing evaluation practice tests the result.

2611.20737.title: CLIFT: Contrastive LiDAR Instance Features for 3D Pedestrian Tracking
2611.20737.abstract: A social robot has to keep track of the people around it over time to plan its motion, a task handled by 3D multi-object tracking. For the LiDAR modality, trackers usually sit on top of a detector and link its detections across frames with a separate motion model or re-identification network. We instead show how a 3D LiDAR detector itself can be turned into a tracker by adding an instance-level contrastive objective on its intermediate voxel features. Each embedding is read from the voxels inside a detected box, and boxes are matched across frames by cosine similarity and the Hungarian algorithm, without a motion model. The detector backbone is fine-tuned together with this objective, which learns identity-aware features while leaving detection accuracy essen- tially intact. Because the method uses only the voxel features that Li- DAR detectors already produce, it is backbone-agnostic. On the JRDB 3D tracking leaderboard our LiDAR-only tracker ranks first on HOTA (38.58) and IDF1 (37.99), 13.04 and 9.30 points above the next pub- lished method, and second on MOTA and OSPA. Code is available at https://hermak56.github.io/CLIFT/.

llm.title_ja: CLIFT：3D歩行者追跡のための対照的LiDARインスタンス特徴
llm.tldr_ja: 3D LiDAR検出器の中間ボクセル特徴にインスタンスレベルの対照学習目的を追加することで、追加の運動モデルなしで検出器自体をトラッカーとして機能させるCLIFTを提案する。
llm.problem: LiDARのトラッカーは通常、検出器の出力に対して独立した運動モデルや再識別ネットワークを組み合わせて構築される。
llm.method: 検出されたバウンス内のボクセル特徴にコントラスト学習目的を適用し、コサイン類似度とハンガリーアルゴリズムによってフレーム間のマッチングを行う。
llm.result: JRDB 3Dトラッキングのリーダーボードにおいて、LiDAR単体の手法としてHOTAとIDF1で1位を獲得した。

2611.20737.tldr_en: This work shows how a 3D LiDAR detector itself can be turned into a tracker by adding an instance-level contrastive objective on its intermediate voxel features, which learns identity-aware features while leaving detection accuracy essen- tially intact.

2611.20730.title: Selective Sensor Acquisition for Multimodal Place Recognition
2611.20730.abstract: Multimodal Place Recognition (PR) can improve robustness, but most systems rigidly read and process every sensor for every query, even when the primary sensor is sufficient, with implications for energy consumption, second sensor update rate, and domain-specific considerations such as passive stealth. We introduce selective, controllable sensor acquisition, where a user specifies a desired second sensor usage rate and the system acquires the additional sensor only when the primary sensor's estimated performance is sufficiently poor. An online threshold adjustment achieves the requested usage rate by adapting to recent primary sensor performance, directing additional sensing towards queries where fusion is most likely to help without calibration specific to sensor modality, PR method, or environment. The approach requires only a PR method that produces a match score and applies to both single-frame and sequence-based PR. Our system, across multiple datasets, PR descriptors, and sensor combinations, recovers 55% of the available PR performance gain while using the second sensor on only 25% of queries, and 81% while using it on 50%. We further analyse alternative acquisition decision mechanisms and usage-rate control methods, and examine performance when the second sensor is stronger than, comparable to, or weaker than the primary sensor.

llm.title_ja: マルチモーダル場所認識のための選択的センサー取得
llm.tldr_ja: プライマリセンサーの推定性能低下に応じて追加センサーの取得を選択的に制御するオンライン閾値調整手法を提案し、センサー使用率を大幅に抑えつつ場所認識の性能向上を実現した。
llm.problem: マルチモーダル場所認識システムは、プライマリセンサーのみで十分な場合でもすべてのセンサーを常に処理するため、エネルギー消費などの問題がある。
llm.method: プライマリセンサーの過去の性能に適応して追加センサーの使用率を制御するオンライン閾値調整メカニズムを導入した。
llm.result: 複数のデータセットにおいて、セカンドセンサーの使用率を25%に抑えつつ利用可能な性能向上の55%を回収し、50%の使用率では81%を回収した。

2611.20720.title: AVD: A Multi-Sensor Teleoperated Wheelchair Platform with Safety-Aware Control
2611.20720.abstract: Electric wheelchairs predominantly rely on manual joystick interfaces, which present critical barriers to independent mobility for individuals with severe motor and visual impairments. This paper presents AVD (Autonomous Vehicle Drive), a dependable teleoperation architecture for assistive mobility that unifies perception, communication, embedded control, and remote supervision in a single low-cost platform built entirely from commercially available hardware. The central engineering contribution is a safety-oriented design framework: control authority follows a static hierarchy, a manual emergency stop and the occupant's joystick pre-empt remote commands, and the on-board sensing layer has stop-only authority. The compute design partitions primary and safety functions and specifies a heartbeat-driven safe-state transition for the fault cases considered. The sensing stack this framework depends on is characterized against measured data: per-channel acquisition latency, a 2,025-scan LiDAR degradation campaign spanning five target configurations and a control under water mist, airborne dust, and direct aperture occlusion, and attitude measurements across static inclines to 47 degrees. The lowest pooled environmental-condition mean retained 76.6% of the clear-baseline forward-sector yield, and no scan lost the sector completely. A logged vibration-induced inertial dropout occurred while LiDAR and camera logging continued, illustrating complementary channel behavior. The result is a documented prototype and an explicit validation path for a deployable wheelchair implementation.

llm.title_ja: AVD：安全性配慮型制御を備えたマルチセンサー遠隔操作車椅子プラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: 市販のハードウェアのみで構築され、厳格な静的制御階層やフォールト時の安全状態遷移を備えた低コストの支援モビリティ向け遠隔操作アーキテクチャ「AVD」を提案する。
llm.problem: 電動車椅子の多くは手動ジョイスティックに依存しており、重度運動・視覚障害者の移動の自由を阻んでいる。
llm.method: 停止権限を持つオンボードセンシング層や、ジョイスティックと緊急停止を優先する静的階層型制御、ハートビート駆動の安全状態遷移を備えたアーキテクチャを設計した。
llm.result: 様々な環境条件（水霧、粉塵など）下でのLiDARの劣化評価や車椅子実装における堅牢性が実証された。

2611.20720.tldr_en: AVD (Autonomous Vehicle Drive), a dependable teleoperation architecture for assistive mobility that unifies perception, communication, embedded control, and remote supervision in a single low-cost platform built entirely from commercially available hardware is presented.

2611.20719.title: ACiT: Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers
2611.20719.abstract: Visuomotor policies condition action prediction on visual and proprioceptive observations. While historical proprioceptive sequences carry rich dynamic priors, current methods treat them as equal to high-dimensional vision, causing the proprioceptive signal to be overwhelmed. To identify what is lost in equal-conditioning fusion, we analyze proprioceptive data and find that strong inter-joint coupling is the key action-determining structure. This finding aligns with the neural sensorimotor loop, in which proprioception first forms a body-centered prior and vision is later calibrated via parietal remapping. Inspired by this, we propose ACiT, Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers, which reinforces historical joint-coupling as the primary condition with vision as a later calibration. This design is instantiated through three modules: Inverted State Encoding builds a proprioceptive prior via per-joint tokens and inter-joint self-attention. State-Visual Grounding lets joint tokens query visual evidence, making vision goal- and calibration-only. Inverted Action Chunking decodes per-joint trajectories independently. ACiT improves success rates on most LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks, with the largest gains on those that require dynamics and coordination. The same conditioning design transferred to the VLA backbone pi_0-ACiT yields significant gains with better execution efficiency.

llm.title_ja: ACiT：反転トランスフォーマーを用いた固有受容感覚プライオに基づくアクションチャンキング
llm.tldr_ja: 関節間の強い結合関係をプライオとして優先し、視覚を事後的な較正として統合するACiTを提案し、動的協調を要するタスクの成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 従来の視覚運動方策は歴史的な固有受容感覚系列を高次元視覚と同等に扱うため、固有受容信号が埋もれてしまう。
llm.method: 逆方向の状態エンコーディング、関節トークンによる視覚情報のクエリ、および反転アクションチャンキングからなるACiTモジュールを設計した。
llm.result: LIBERO、RoboTwin 2.0、実世界のタスクにおいて成功率を向上させ、VLAバックボーン（π0）への適用でも顕著な性能向上が得られた。
keywords_ja: アクションチャンキング
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.20719.tldr_en: ACiT, Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers, which reinforces historical joint-coupling as the primary condition with vision as a later calibration and improves success rates on most LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks, with the largest gains on those that require dynamics and coordination.

2611.20718.title: TaF-Foundation: Wrench-Grounded Cross-Sensor Tactile Representations
2611.20718.abstract: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich manipulation, yet heterogeneous sensing mechanisms and observation formats hinder cross-hardware transfer. Since physical contact is governed by Newtonian mechanics, we ground tactile representations in six-dimensional wrenches, establishing a common physical reference across sensing mechanisms. Specifically, we pair tactile observations from all sensors with wrench measurements, enabling shared physical supervision without requiring direct tactile-to-tactile pairing between sensors. To support learning at scale, we develop a dedicated acquisition platform and collect over 100 million paired tactile observations and wrench measurements from 24 sensors spanning four families of sensing principles. Building on this dataset, our framework combines sensor-specific input adaptation with a shared tactile encoder. By learning to reconstruct wrenches, the encoder maps observations from different sensors into a shared, continuous feature space grounded in contact physics. To leverage these representations for manipulation, we introduce TaF-Policy, which integrates tactile features with visual observations and robot states to generate action chunks. We evaluate the learned representations through wrench estimation, cross-sensor retrieval, few-shot adaptation to unseen sensors, and robotic manipulation. On the core benchmark, our method reduces single-frame force RMSE by 17.1% and improves cross-sensor retrieval R@1 by 13.11 percentage points over the strongest baseline. In manipulation experiments, TaF-Policy achieves average success rates of 51.33% across three simulated tasks and 46.25% across four real-world tasks, compared with 47.33% and 23.75%, respectively, for the strongest baselines evaluated on the same task sets. Project page: https://mrjiangjm.github.io/TaF-Foundation/.

llm.title_ja: TaF-Foundation：6軸力に裏付けられたクロスセンサー触覚表現
llm.tldr_ja: ニュートン力学の6軸力（レンチ）を共通の物理的基準として用いることで、異なるハードウェア間の異種触覚データを統合するクロスセンサー触覚表現学習フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 触覚センシングのメカニズムや観察形式が多様であるため、異なるハードウェア間での転移学習が妨げられている。
llm.method: 4つのセンシング原則に基づく24種類のセンサーから1億件以上の触覚・レンチ対データを収集し、レンチの再構築を通じて共通の潜在空間にマップする。
llm.result: 単一フレームの力推定RMSEを17.1%削減し、クロスセンサーの検索性能や実世界・シミュレーションの操作タスクで優れた成功率を達成した。

2611.20718.tldr_en: This work pairs tactile observations from all sensors with wrench measurements, enabling shared physical supervision without requiring direct tactile-to-tactile pairing between sensors, and introduces TaF-Policy, which integrates tactile features with visual observations and robot states to generate action chunks.

2611.20710.title: SG-ODOM: Event-Driven Proprioceptive State Estimation with Stability-Gated Contact Updates for Legged Robots
2611.20710.abstract: Reliable proprioceptive state estimation for legged robots fuses inertial sensing with kinematic sensing from leg encoders. The latter assumes a foot is stationary during the stance phase; however, physical foot touchdown does not necessarily provide a stationary reference for odometry, particularly during impact and load transfer. Repeatedly applying kinematic corrections throughout the same contact phase can introduce redundant or unreliable information. We present SG-ODOM, a proprioceptive odometry framework that uses stability-gated contact selection to schedule kinematic updates. Following physical touchdown, a stability gate accepts the contact for state estimation only after the foot reaches a sufficiently stable support condition. The resulting validated touchdown event triggers an estimator correction, while additional timeout updates bound the maximum duration of uninterrupted IMU propagation. The framework is evaluated on multiple legged platforms, both quadrupedal and humanoid robots, against representative state-of-the-art proprioceptive estimators. Across the evaluated sequences, SG-ODOM demonstrates competitive or superior estimation accuracy, reducing Relative Pose Error (RPE) by up to 25% compared to the baseline estimator on outdoor sequences from the GrandTour dataset. Source code: https://github.com/ori-drs/SG-ODOM. Video: https://youtu.be/-583_RyuhqQ

llm.title_ja: SG-ODOM：脚式ロボットのための安定性ゲート接触更新を備えたイベント駆動型固有受容状態推定
llm.tldr_ja: 着地時の不安定な影響を排除するため、足先が十分に安定した支持状態に達した後にのみ接触情報を受け入れる安定性ゲートを導入した脚式ロボット向け固有受容オドメトリフレームワークSG-ODOMを提案する。
llm.problem: 脚式ロボットの運動学オドメトリは、衝撃や荷重移動時の接地において静止仮定が崩れ、信頼性の低い情報を導入してしまう。
llm.method: 物理的な接地後、足が安定した支持状態に達した時点でのみ接触を状態推定に受け入れる安定性ゲートによって運動学更新をスケジューリングする。
llm.result: 四足歩行およびヒューマノイドロボットを用いた評価において、屋外シーケンスでの相対姿勢誤差（RPE）を最大25%削減した。

2611.20710.tldr_en: SG-ODOM is presented, a proprioceptive odometry framework that uses stability-gated contact selection to schedule kinematic updates and demonstrates competitive or superior estimation accuracy, reducing Relative Pose Error by up to 25% compared to the baseline estimator on outdoor sequences from the GrandTour dataset.

2611.20700.title: Design of the Secure Smart Scooter with Automatic Lane Detection
2611.20700.abstract: The authors present a prototype of an electric scooter that uses computer vision to determine driving lanes and automatically modify vehicle configuration. Scooters steer on sidewalks, bike paths, or car lanes. The government imposes speed limits on the lanes in which electric scooters drive. Featuring computer vision, electric scooters can determine driving lanes and automatically modify vehicle configuration. However, such systems' safety is still a concern, and research into such vehicle systems' safety and security aspects is proceeding. First, we will present our vehicular setup. Then, we will present our implemented scooter with safety constraints. Finally, we present our security prototype for such an electric scooter.
2611.20700.comment: 4 pages, Published in 16th IEEE International Conference on Service Operations and Logistics, and Informatics (IEEE SOLI 2022)

llm.title_ja: 自動車線検出機能を備えたセキュアなスマートスクーターの設計
llm.tldr_ja: コンピュータビジョンを使用して走行車線を特定し、車両設定を自動的に変更する電気スクーターのプロトタイプを提案し、その安全・セキュリティ面の設計を示した。
llm.problem: 電動スクーターは歩道や自転車道、車道など多様な場所を走行し、政府による速度制限の遵守やシステム自体の安全性が懸念されている。
llm.method: 車線検出のためのコンピュータビジョンと、安全制約やセキュリティ対策を組み込んだ車両プラットフォームを実装した。
llm.result: 車線を自動認識して車両設定を調整可能なセキュアな電気スクーターのプロトタイプ構築に成功した。
keywords_ja: コンピュータビジョン

2611.20700.tldr_en: A prototype of an electric scooter that uses computer vision to determine driving lanes and automatically modify vehicle configuration is presented and the security prototype for such an electric scooter is presented.

2611.20692.title: ARMFUL: Learning Whole-Arm Grasp Configurations for Single-Arm Pickup of Large Objects
2611.20692.abstract: Many everyday objects, such as storage boxes, baskets, and chairs, are too large or heavy for a gripper to grasp, yet a single arm can still pick them up by wrapping around and supporting them. Such grasps are hard to learn: wrapping motions are difficult to teleoperate, and existing datasets contain little whole-arm pickup data. We introduce WAG (Whole-Arm Grasp Dataset), the first large-scale dataset for single-arm pickup of large objects, with 1.7~million joint configurations across 793 objects. We sample configurations directly in joint space, execute each through squeeze and lift primitives in simulation, and stress-test survivors under active shaking and external forces. To demonstrate the utility of WAG and accomplish the whole-arm pickup task, we develop ARMFUL, a whole-arm pickup pipeline that pairs a diffusion model trained on WAG, generating whole-arm grasps from the object's point cloud, with a motion planner that reaches them collision-free before the same squeeze-and-lift execution. In simulation, ARMFUL reaches 85.4\% lift success on training and 69.9\% on held-out objects, and it lifts the object in 70 of 100 trials on a physical Franka arm across 10 IKEA objects.

llm.title_ja: ARMFUL：大型物体の単腕ピックアップに向けた全身把持構成の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 大型物体を持ち上げるための大規模な全身把持データセット（WAG）と、点群から全身把持を生成して衝突回避プランナーと組み合わせるパイプライン「ARMFUL」を提案した。
llm.problem: 収納ボックスや椅子などの大型・重量物はグリッパーで把持できないが、単腕で抱え込む動作は教示や既存データセットが不足しているため学習が困難である。
llm.method: 170万の関節構成を含む大規模データセットWAGを構築し、拡散モデルを用いて物体点群から全身把持を生成してスクイーズ・リフト実行を行うパイプラインを開発した。
llm.result: シミュレーションで最大85.4%の持ち上げ成功率を達成し、実機のFrankaアームを用いた10種のIKEA物体実験でも70%の試行で持ち上げに成功した。

2611.20692.tldr_en: WAG (Whole-Arm Grasp Dataset), the first large-scale dataset for single-arm pickup of large objects, is introduced and ARMFUL, a whole-arm pickup pipeline that pairs a diffusion model trained on WAG, generating whole-arm grasps from the object's point cloud, with a motion planner that reaches them collision-free before the same squeeze-and-lift execution is developed.

2611.20676.title: Learning and Verifying Progress: Closed-Loop Agentic Planning with Progress-Enhanced Execution for Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation
2611.20676.abstract: Long-horizon vision-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to track instruction progress and recover from local errors before they propagate across subtasks. However, executors trained on expert trajectories encounter policy-induced state shifts during deployment, and their stop signals do not reliably indicate subtask completion. We introduce Learning and Verifying Progress for VLN (LeaP-VLN), an agentic VLN system that couples progress-aware execution with independent progress verification through plan--execute--verify--recover cycles. LeaP-VLN leverages progress both explicitly, through a progress verifier that verifies subtask completion before the agent advances and triggers dual-phase recovery upon route deviation, and implicitly, by co-training the executor on progress reasoning and action prediction to enhance the executor's progress awareness and corrective control. To adapt the executor to this closed-loop interface, we propose a two-stage progress-enhanced curriculum: behavior cloning on expert demonstrations, followed by joint training on demonstrations, expert action corrections, and progress-reasoning supervision. Policy-generated trajectories expose the executor to both intra-subtask drift and inter-subtask state shifts, aligning training with the deviations encountered during closed-loop execution. Extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrate state-of-the-art success rates among monocular methods trained without additional navigation datasets, while real-world experiments further validate the effectiveness of LeaP-VLN in long-horizon navigation.

llm.title_ja: 進捗の学習と検証：長期視覚言語ナビゲーションのための進捗強化実行を伴う閉ループエージェント型計画
llm.tldr_ja: 進捗を意識した実行と独立した進捗検証サイクルを結合することで、長期視覚言語ナビゲーション（VLN）におけるエラーの伝播を防ぐエージェント型システム「LeaP-VLN」を提案した。
llm.problem: 長期VLNにおいて、専門家の軌跡で訓練された実行者はデプロイ時の状態ドリフトに直面し、停止信号がサブタスクの完了を確実に示さない。
llm.method: サブタスクの完了を検証する進捗検証器と、進捗推論と行動予測を共同訓練する2段階のカリキュラム学習を組み合わせた閉ループシステムを構築した。
llm.result: R2R-CEおよびRxR-CEにおいて、追加のナビゲーションデータなしで訓練された単眼手法の中で最先端の成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: 視覚言語ナビゲーション
ロボットナビゲーション

2611.20676.tldr_en: This work introduces Learning and Verifying Progress for VLN (LeaP-VLN), an agentic VLN system that couples progress-aware execution with independent progress verification through plan--execute--verify--recover cycles and proposes a two-stage progress-enhanced curriculum.

2611.20648.title: Competent Autonomous Driving Through Fine Tuning Vision Language Action Models with Symbolic Traffic Rules
2611.20648.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models offer a unified approach to perception, reasoning, and control for autonomous driving, but accurate action prediction alone does not establish compliance with traffic regulations. This paper presents a rule-guided VLA framework that incorporates symbolic traffic-rule feedback into policy optimisation. The framework combines supervised fine-tuning on expert demonstrations with reinforcement learning (RL) refinement using a reward that encourages encoded-rule compliance while penalising deviations from expert actions. Selected provisions of the United Kingdom Highway Code are formalised as executable first-order logic rules using PyReason, covering speed adaptation, following distance, and road-user priority. A frozen vision-language model extracts scene predicates, which are combined with vehicle-state information to assess the projected consequences of candidate control actions. Offline evaluation on held-out data collected in the CARLA simulator compares three group-based RL methods. The results show improvements in both action prediction accuracy and encoded-rule compliance over the supervised baseline. The best-performing variant increases the overall rule pass rate from 92.9% to 97.6%, with zero observed violations of the encoded road-user-priority check in the evaluated samples. These findings support symbolic rule feedback as a means of improving VLA policy alignment with explicit traffic-rule criteria.

llm.title_ja: 記号的交通ルールを用いたビジョン言語アクションモデルのファインチューニングによる有能な自動運転
llm.tldr_ja: 記号的な交通ルールに基づく報酬を用いた強化学習によってVLAモデルを最適化し、交通規則の遵守と行動予測精度の両方を向上させるフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 自動運転向けVLAモデルは知覚・推論・制御を統合できるが、正確な行動予測だけでは交通規則の遵守が保証されない。
llm.method: イギリスの道路交通法を形式論理ルールとして定義し、監督ありファインチューニングの後にルール遵守を報酬とする強化学習（RL）による最適化を行った。
llm.result: CARLAシミュレーターでの評価において、ルール遵守率が92.9%から97.6%に向上し、道路利用者優先の違反がゼロになった。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語アクションモデル

2611.20648.tldr_en: A rule-guided VLA framework that incorporates symbolic traffic-rule feedback into policy optimisation is presented, which support symbolic rule feedback as a means of improving VLA policy alignment with explicit traffic-rule criteria.

2611.20631.title: Instructions Before Actions: Prospective and Retrospective Language Supervision for Driving Vision-Language-Action Data
2611.20631.abstract: Driving vision-language-action (VLA) models can accept navigation instructions, yet predicting a driver's trajectory does not establish that a model follows the instruction. We study how driving-language supervision is collected and evaluated, distinguishing prospective instructions issued before an action from retrospective labels written after observing it. We develop ADVLAT-Engine to synchronize spoken instructions, road-scene video, and vehicle trajectories, and compare three navigation apps on 48 replayed routes. On 87 maneuvers announced by both Google Maps and a passenger, the passenger uses more scene-dependent language. We evaluate four open driving VLAs before and after fine-tuning on prospective navigation-app drives. Fine-tuning reduces passenger-drive trajectory error by 23-59%, but instruction effects remain inconsistent. At real intersections, counterfactual instructions reveal stronger responsiveness: fine-tuned Alpamayo~2 Super gains 31 and 18 accuracy points at 15 and 5~m, while Qwen-Drive follows alternative maneuvers more reliably with a discrete command than with a sentence. We additionally collected retrospective annotations from four people for the driving recordings and describe controlled comparisons of annotation content, timing, and downstream learning; those analyses are pending. Our findings separate maneuver prediction from instruction-following and establish a framework for comparing prospective and retrospective supervision.

llm.title_ja: 行動の前の指示：運転用ビジョン言語アクションデータのための未来予測型および過去回顧型の言語的監督
llm.tldr_ja: 行動前に発話される未来予測型指示と、行動後に記述される過去回顧型ラベルを区別して収集・評価する枠組みを構築し、運転用VLAの指示追従能力を分析した。
llm.problem: 運転用VLAモデルはナビゲーション指示を受け入れられるが、単なる軌跡予測だけでは指示に従っているかどうかが確立されない。
llm.method: 音声指示、車載映像、車両軌跡を同期させる「ADVLAT-Engine」を開発し、未来予測型ナビゲーションデータのファインチューニング前後での軌跡誤差や交差点での応答性を評価した。
llm.result: ファインチューニングにより乗客運転時の軌跡誤差が23〜59%削減され、実際の交差点では反事実的指示に対するより強い応答性が確認された。

2611.20631.tldr_en: The findings separate maneuver prediction from instruction-following and establish a framework for comparing prospective and retrospective supervision, distinguishing prospective instructions issued before an action from retrospective labels written after observing it.

2611.20593.title: JEPTERA: A Platform Agnostic JEPA-Assisted Model Predictive Planner for Urban UAV Navigation
2611.20593.abstract: Urban navigation for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) requires planning that accounts for environmental geometry, vehicle dynamics, and moving obstacles. This paper presents JEPTERA, a navigation architecture that integrates a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), Model Predictive Control (MPC), PID control, and a safety layer. JEPA predicts the UAV's motion response to candidate commands for MPC action selection, while the safety layer checks trajectories against occupied space and predicted obstacle motion. Simulator adapters and platform-specific YAML configurations separate the planning core from simulator interfaces. An ablation study evaluated six configurations across three gym scenarios, totaling 180 runs. The complete architecture achieved the highest aggregate success rate, completing 28 of 30 runs. Additional tests completed one route across three city maps without collisions. Separate integration tests demonstrated operation in Gazebo/ROS 2, MuJoCo, and CARLA without modifying the core planning logic. These results support the feasibility of the integrated architecture for simulated urban UAV navigation and its portability across simulator interfaces.

llm.title_ja: JEPTERA：都市部UAVナビゲーションのためのプラットフォーム非依存型JEPA支援モデル予測プランナー
llm.tldr_ja: 環境ジオメトリや動的障害物を考慮してUAVの運動応答を予測するJEPAとモデル予測制御（MPC）を統合した都市部ナビゲーションアーキテクチャ「JEPTERA」を提案した。
llm.problem: 無人航空機（UAV）の都市部ナビゲーションには、環境の幾何学、車両ダイナミクス、移動障害物を考慮した計画が必要である。
llm.method: 候補コマンドに対するUAVの運動応答をJEPAで予測してMPCの行動選択に利用し、安全性レイヤーで軌道を検証するアーキテクチャを設計した。
llm.result: 3つのジムシナリオにおける180回の実行で最高成功率を達成し、Gazebo、MuJoCo、CARLAなどの異なるシミュレータ環境でコアロジックを修正せずに動作することが実証された。

2611.20593.tldr_en: JEPTERA, a navigation architecture that integrates a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture, Model Predictive Control, Model Predictive Control, PID control, and a safety layer, is presented, supporting the feasibility of the integrated architecture for simulated urban UAV navigation and its portability across simulator interfaces.

2611.20587.title: Stability Principle Inherent in Wheel Gait of Planar X-shaped Walker Generated Using Constant Torque Drive and Mechanical Stoppers
2611.20587.abstract: Since the late 19th century when the first walking toys were developed, it has been known that mechanical stoppers at the hip joint are crucial for generating stable passive dynamic walking. Recent research on passive-dynamic and limit-cycle walkers has also confirmed that mechanical stoppers at the hip and knee joints are effective for generating stable walking motion, but theoretical research on how this mechanical constraint enhances the overall gait stability remains insufficient. This paper introduces a planar X-shaped walker equipped with mechanical stoppers at the hip joint, and investigates the effect of the mechanical constraint on the stability of the wheel gait generated by constant torque drive on a downslope. By simply falling forward while using the stoppers to constrain itself to the target impact posture, the robot can generate a highly stable wheel gait. We divide the motion of one step into four phases, derive approximate analytical solutions for the state error transition function matrix in each phase using a linearized model, and analyze the increase or decrease in the state error norm using metrics such as its maximum singular value. Numerical simulations demonstrate that while two phases are unstable in terms of the increase in the state error norm, the remaining two phases are stable, resulting in overall asymptotic stability.
2611.20587.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. Published in the Proceedings of IEEE ICRA 2026. This author version corrects the author names in one reference; the scientific content remains unchanged
2611.20587.journal_ref: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), pp. 11226-11233, 2026

llm.title_ja: 定トルク駆動とメカニカルストッパーを用いて生成される平面X字型ウォーカーの車輪歩行に内在する安定性原理
llm.tldr_ja: ヒップ関節にメカニカルストッパーを備えた平面X字型ウォーカーを対象に、下り坂での定トルク駆動による車輪歩行の漸近安定性を線形化モデルを用いた近似解析で証明した。
llm.problem: 受動歩行やリミットサイクルウォーカーにおけるメカニカルストッパーの有効性は知られているが、歩行全体の安定性を高めるメカニズムの理論的研究が不十分である。
llm.method: 1歩の運動を4つのフェーズに分割し、線形化モデルを用いて各フェーズの状態誤差遷移関数行列の近似解析解を導出し、特異値などの指標で安定性を分析した。
llm.result: 数値シミュレーションにより、一部のフェーズが不安定であっても全体として漸近安定性が得られることが示された。
keywords_ja: メカニカルストッパー

2611.20587.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation

2611.20574.title: ExtremeDrive: A Real-World Dataset and Benchmark for Critical Driving
2611.20574.abstract: Existing autonomous driving datasets and benchmarks provide extensive resources for routine driving, yet real-world data covering safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions remain limited. To address this gap, we present ExtremeDrive, a real-world dataset and benchmark covering emergency maneuvers, complex traffic interactions, and adverse conditions such as slippery or snow-covered roads, alongside routine driving. The dataset comprises 589 driving scenes curated from a larger pool of real-world driving recordings, with calibrated and aligned multisensor data and reviewed annotations of road structure and traffic participants. We further establish a benchmark to evaluate planned trajectories through simulated vehicle execution, measuring safety-related metrics and driving performance. Experiments at equal training set sizes show that incorporating critical driving data reduces trajectory prediction errors and improves mean critical-success rates in critical scenarios. ExtremeDrive provides a unified resource for learning and evaluating autonomous driving in safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions.

llm.title_ja: ExtremeDrive：クリティカルドライビング向けの実世界データセットとベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 緊急機動や悪天候などの安全クリティカルなシナリオを網羅した実世界データセット「ExtremeDrive」を構築し、計画軌道の評価ベンチマークを提示した。
llm.problem: 既存の自動運転データセットは通常の運転シーンが中心であり、安全クリティカルなシナリオや極端な環境条件のデータが限られている。
llm.method: マルチセンサーデータを較正・同期し、緊急機動や滑りやすい道路などの悪天候を含む589の運転シーンを収集・注釈付けして評価ベンチマークを構築した。
llm.result: クリティカルな運転データの統合により、軌跡予測誤差が軽減され、危機的シナリオにおける平均成功率が向上することが示された。

2611.20574.tldr_en: ExtremeDrive is presented, a real-world dataset and benchmark covering emergency maneuvers, complex traffic interactions, and adverse conditions such as slippery or snow-covered roads, alongside routine driving that provides a unified resource for learning and evaluating autonomous driving in safety-critical scenarios and extreme environmental conditions.

2611.20570.title: OrthoMark: Place Recognition with Point-Anchored Orthographic Height Mark
2611.20570.abstract: LiDAR place recognition provides the loop closures of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping(SLAM). Perspective from Z-axis, a gravity-aligned scan is an orthographic map of the scene, and a revisit from another position and heading moves this map rigidly in the plane, a motion that a polar Fourier spectrum ignores and phase correlation recovers. Along the vertical, the heights of the returns describe the structures, but which heights are observed depends on the range, because the sensor's vertical field of view cuts nearby structures low; height thus misleads a global key, yet is decisive once two scans are aligned and compared cell by cell where they overlap. We present \method, a training-free method built on one principle: two LiDAR scans can only be compared through features computed from the same geometric surfaces in both scans. \method retrieves candidates with a translation- and rotation-invariant polar spectrum of the bird's-eye view (BEV), 1.9,KB per keyframe, and verifies each candidate by estimating its planar pose through phase correlation and scoring it with \emph{point-anchored height columns}: every BEV cell keeps a 16-bit mask of the heights of its own returns; within a session, the score is weighted by the expected overlap of the two scans' sensing ranges, computed from their distance. We show that this vertical link pays off in verification but hurts in retrieval, where what a height slice contains depends on the range to the structure. For single robot, \method has the highest AP of the training-free methods without 3D registration on the KITTI development sequences; across robots, on all multi-robot sequences, it matches or exceeds RING++ at 1/350 of its descriptor size and closes more inter-robot loops than the learned BEVPlace++ on all tests.

llm.title_ja: OrthoMark：点アンカー型正射影高さマークを用いた場所認識
llm.tldr_ja: 学習を必要とせず、鳥瞰図（BEV）の極フーリエスペクトルによる候補検索と、点アンカー型高さ列を用いた位相相関による姿勢検証を行うLiDAR場所認識手法「OrthoMark」を提案した。
llm.problem: LiDARスキャンの垂直視野によって観測される高さが距離に依存して変わるため、高さ情報を大域的なキーとして用いると誤りが生じやすい。
llm.method: BEVの極フーリエスペクトルで候補を検索し、各セルの高さの16ビットマスクを保持する点アンカー型高さ列と位相相関を用いて候補を検証する。

2611.20570.tldr_en: This work presents \method, a training-free method built on one principle: two LiDAR scans can only be compared through features computed from the same geometric surfaces in both scans, and shows that this vertical link pays off in verification but hurts in retrieval, where what a height slice contains depends on the range to the structure.

2611.20568.title: sqrtVINS-Based 360 Visual-Inertial SLAM Systems: Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge 2026 Entry
2611.20568.abstract: This report describes our submission to the 2026 Hilti-Trimble SLAM Challenge. The system is a 360-camera visual-inertial pipeline that uses only the provided dual-fisheye image streams and IMU measurements. First, raw images are preprocessed with low-light enhancement and static/dynamic masking, and then fed into a $\sqrt{\text{VINS}}$ frontend as the local odometry, with deep learning-based SuperPoint features, ELSED line segments, and LightGlue matching. The resulting trajectory is refined using a GTSAM-based backend that performs tightly-coupled factor graph optimization with SALAD global descriptor and visual bundle adjustment (BA). The backend performs local-to-global structureless BA, tightly regularized intrinsic and extrinsic refinement, and global scale adjustment supported by the known inter-camera baseline and cross-view constraints. The design targets long indoor sequences with dark regions, repetitive corridors, dynamic objects, and limited geometric parallax, while keeping the pipeline reproducible in the provided ROS2 workspace. Fig. 1 demonstrates that our proposed method aligns well with the floorplan across several indoor sequences.
2611.20568.comment: 2026 Hilti x Trimble SLAM Challenge at ICRA 2026 (2nd Place in the SLAM Category)
2611.20568.tldr_en: This report describes the design of a 360-camera visual-inertial pipeline that uses only the provided dual-fisheye image streams and IMU measurements and performs tightly regularized intrinsic and extrinsic refinement, and global scale adjustment supported by the known inter-camera baseline and cross-view constraints.

2611.20558.title: Vision-Language Grounded Semantic Navigation for Autonomous Mobile Robots
2611.20558.abstract: Language-guided navigation enables mobile robots to interpret natural language commands and navigate toward user-specified targets in unstructured environments. However, integrating open-vocabulary visual perception with classical robotics pipelines for mapping and navigation remains a challenging problem. In this work, we present a complete ROS2-based system that combines frontier-based exploration, open-vocabulary object detection using Grounding DINO, depth-based 3D localization, and semantic mapping to enable end-to-end vision-language grounded navigation in simulation. The system accepts natural language commands such as ``go to the yellow box,'' detects candidate objects from RGB images using text prompts, estimates their positions in the world frame, and generates navigation goals executed by the Nav2 stack. In a Gazebo-based indoor environment with a TurtleBot3 robot, the system autonomously explored the room, detected three of the five target objects, and successfully executed both natural language navigation commands tested, without task-specific training. The results indicate that open-vocabulary grounding models can be integrated into classical navigation pipelines, though performance is limited by detection uncertainty, depth-based localization error, and incomplete exploration coverage. These findings highlight both the feasibility and current limitations of deploying vision-language grounded navigation systems using lightweight, CPU-only architectures.

llm.title_ja: 自律移動ロボットのための視覚言語にグラウンディングされたセマンティックナビゲーション

2611.20557.title: AsymEEF: Bimanual Manipulation with Asymmetric End Effectors
2611.20557.abstract: Teleoperated demonstrations are costly to collect and rarely reusable across end-effectors with different kinematics and action spaces. This burden grows in bimanual manipulation, where each end-effector pair may require new data. We present AsymEEF, a framework for executable cross-end-effector demonstration generation and unified bimanual policy learning. Given a small source dataset, AsymEEF transfers demonstrations to heterogeneous combinations of two-, three-, and five-fingered end-effectors without additional teleoperation. Kinematic teacher anchors provide geometric supervision, while sparse real-world X-Calib anchors correct discrepancies in grasp execution. A shared encoder maps wrist poses and actuator states to a morphology-agnostic latent space, and a morphology-conditioned decoder reconstructs target commands. Generated trajectories undergo replay filtering for task-level executability. The representation also supports a unified bimanual visuomotor policy trained across multiple pairs. Across four simulated and six real-world tasks, AsymEEF improves replay success over adapted transfer baselines, achieves a mean replay-valid expansion gain of 16.6 times in simulation, and is evaluated through downstream policy training on real robots. Project website: https://asymeef.vercel.app/.

2611.20510.title: WTR-Drive: World-Task Decomposition with Structured Risk Supervision for End-to-End Driving
2611.20510.abstract: Proposal-conditioned scene predictions can lack a common object-level reference across candidate trajectories. Aggregate planning scores also leave the objects and times associated with violations implicit. We present WTR-Drive (World-Task-Risk Driving), a Drive-JEPA-based planner that separates shared scene estimation from proposal-conditioned reasoning. A proposal-independent World Memory estimates object states, map structure, and future motion by re-reading the original visual features at each refinement round. Proposal feedback updates a residual Task branch without writing back to World Memory. This branch guides refinement through candidate-specific retrieval and gated visual feedback. A final Task readout supplies candidate-conditioned features for scoring. We derive structured risk targets from existing candidate-scoring rollouts without additional simulator calls. For at-fault collision and time-to-collision violations, the targets encode event existence, association with shared object slots, and the first violation time bin. On the NAVSIM navtest split, WTR-Drive achieves 94.66 PDMS on v1 and 88.24 EPDMS on v2 (expert-frame sequential evaluation). These scores are 0.96 and 0.44 points above the published Drive-JEPA values, respectively. Candidate-level analysis shows that higher best-candidate scores can coexist with lower selected-trajectory scores, revealing a gap between candidate quality and selection effectiveness.

llm.tldr_ja: 共有シーン推定と提案条件付き推論を分離し、構造化リスクターゲットを用いてエンドツーエンド運転の性能を向上させるWTR-Driveを提案した。

llm.method: 提案非依存のワールドメモリと残差タスクブランチを分離し、追加のシミュレータ呼び出しなしで構造化リスクターゲットを導出するDrive-JEPAベースのプランナー

2611.20510.tldr_en: This work presents WTR-Drive (World-Task-Risk Driving), a Drive-JEPA-based planner that separates shared scene estimation from proposal-conditioned reasoning, and derives structured risk targets from existing candidate-scoring rollouts without additional simulator calls.

2611.20507.title: VoxSAOR: Semantic-Aware Occupancy Robustification via Aleatoric Uncertainty Modeling
2611.20507.abstract: Vision-based 3D occupancy prediction provides a dense semantic representation of scenes for autonomous driving and embodied perception, yet remains vulnerable to occlusion, depth ambiguity, and projection errors that induce spatially varying reliability in voxel features. Existing methods typically map voxel representations to semantic predictions without explicitly modeling such observation-induced feature variations. To address this limitation, we propose VoxSAOR, a semantic-aware occupancy robustification framework that models aleatoric uncertainty through feature-space proxies. It first quantifies Local Semantic Consistency (LSC) to derive a voxel-wise structural stability prior and uses cross-view semantic consensus to filter unreliable semantic correspondences. Within each semantic category, spatially matched stable and ambiguous voxels form stable-to-ambiguous feature transitions, which are modeled by a class-conditional diagonal Gaussian distribution, capturing both feature displacement and dispersion. Guided by these proxy distributions, Aleatoric Regime Ensemble Learning (AREL) trains independently parameterized prediction heads using feature perturbations at progressively increasing scales, with perturbation strength modulated by structural reliability. At inference, proxy modeling and sampling are disabled, and all heads process the same observed features; their output probabilities are then averaged to produce a deterministic consensus prediction without requiring sampling. Experiments across multiple datasets and occupancy backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of VoxSAOR in improving semantic occupancy prediction, long-tail recognition, and predictive calibration. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/VoxSAOR.
2611.20507.comment: The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/MengfeiD/VoxSAOR

llm.title_ja: VoxSAOR：異方性不確実性モデリングによるセマンティック認識型占有表現の堅牢化
llm.tldr_ja: 特徴空間のプロキシを通じて異方性不確実性をモデル化し、セマンティック占有予測の精度やロングテール認識を向上させるVoxSAORフレームワークを提案した。

2611.20481.title: Lift, See, Act: Hierarchical Robot Policy Pretraining with 3D Foundation Models
2611.20481.abstract: Robot policy pretraining based on human videos is crucial for improving the policy's generalization ability. One main challenge for this task is the lack of explicit action-relevant representations in such unlabeled data. Recent works tend to estimate 3D hand motion trajectories from videos using 3D foundation models (3D FMs). However, they keep solely the sparse trajectories as supervision, ignoring the rich, fine-grained information produced during the trajectory extraction process. To address this issue, we propose LSA, a hierarchical robot policy pretraining framework that includes three phases: Lift, See, and Act. Specifically, the Lift phase elevates 2D video observations into dense 3D representations by adaptively aligning features in the policy's shallow layers with the intermediate representations extracted from multiple 3D FMs. Building upon these lifted representations, the See phase equips the policy with explicit geometric and interactive awareness through dual guidance. It introduces depth-map reconstruction to help the model comprehend 3D spatial layouts and utilizes hand region cues to explicitly supervise the encoder's attention toward task-relevant interaction hotspots. Empowered by the dense 3D representation learning and precise spatial guidance, our policy achieves robust and accurate robotic manipulation in the Act phase. Extensive experiments on diverse simulation and real-world tasks demonstrate that LSA significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches. The project page is available at: https://yiyuan00.github.io/Lift-See-Act.

llm.title_ja: Lift, See, Act：3D基盤モデルを用いた階層的ロボットポリシー事前学習
llm.tldr_ja: 人間動画の2D観測を密な3D表現に持ち上げ、幾何学的・対話的ガイダンスを付与することでロボットマニピュレーションの性能を向上させる階層的事前学習フレームワークLSAを提案した。

llm.method: 2D動画観測を密な3D表現に変換するLiftフェーズと、深度再構成や手領域の手がかりを活用するSeeフェーズからなる階層的フレームワーク
llm.result: 多様なシミュレーションおよび実世界タスクにおいて、現在の最先端手法を大幅に上回る性能を達成した
keywords_ja: ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.20481.tldr_en: Empowered by the dense 3D representation learning and precise spatial guidance, the policy achieves robust and accurate robotic manipulation in the Act phase and significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches.

2611.20465.title: ReRead: Wrong Predictions, Useful Representations - Correcting Frozen Robot Policies by Re-reading Their Own Representations
2611.20465.abstract: When a pretrained robot policy fails on challenging tasks, common remedies include retraining the backbone, adding an external visual encoder, or introducing a memory module. We argue that wrong predictions do not imply wrong representations: a policy can retain the required information yet fail to read it out as the correct action. To test this view, we propose ReRead: with the backbone frozen, a corrector re-reads the current and two previous caches to predict an action residual. The corrector sees no images, is trained solely on offline demonstrations from all 50 RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, and adds only 4.17% latency. Ablations and interventions show that the correction relies on the backbone's own representations: none of four external visual encoders adds further gain, and swapping in past caches from other trajectories sharply increases action error. On the 11 hardest RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, ReRead improves the success rates of LingBot-VLA, $π_{0.5}$, and Fast-WAM by 23.45, 13.09, and 8.00 percentage points, respectively. In paired evaluation on all 50 tasks, it raises Fast-WAM's average success rate from 90.73% to 92.66%. On a Flexiv dual-arm robot, it raises success on a phase-ambiguous task from 0% to 36%.

llm.title_ja: ReRead：誤った予測と有用な表現 ― 自身の表現を再読み込みすることによる凍結されたロボットポリシーの修正

2611.20460.title: Stochastic Self-Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.20460.abstract: Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models achieve strong performance in robotics through imitation learning, yet fine-tuning them with on-policy reinforcement learning (RL) is limited. In group-based RL methods like Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), every rollout step requires multi-step ODE integration, and the sampler's limited stochasticity leads to rollout groups with low variance. We propose VLA-SSD, which addresses both high inference latency and limited stochasticity. In particular, our method self-distills a pretrained flow-matching action head into a stochastic one-step policy by conditioning a single-jump generator on a Brownian path. We derive a conditional action density via our stochastic one-step policy, enabling efficient post-training via likelihood-ratio RL algorithms. We show that distilling VLA-SSD from the $π_0$ VLA reduces the action head's forward-pass time by a factor of 7.7, at the cost of a 5.5% relative decrease in the success rate on the LIBERO benchmark. However, by leveraging the increased sample diversity of VLA-SSD during group generation, post-training a $π_{0.5}$ VLA using GRPO yields a 20.6% relative improvement.

llm.title_ja: フローベースのビジョン・言語・行動モデルのための確率的セルフ蒸留
llm.tldr_ja: フローベースのVLAモデルの推論遅延とサンプル多様性の制限を解決するため、事前学習済み行動ヘッドを確率的一ステップポリシーにセルフ蒸留するVLA-SSDを提案した。

2611.20452.title: XMimic and XSoma: Learning Humanoid Motion Tracking and Locomotion in Under a Minute
2611.20452.abstract: We present XMimic and XSoma, which learn humanoid motion tracking and locomotion on rough terrain in under a minute of training. Both follow SuperMimic, which learns a world model of the robot and optimizes the policy with analytic gradients through short rollouts imagined in this model. Existing implementations of this method do not make use of larger GPUs, as every training iteration is a long chain of small GPU operations that run one after another. XMimic and XSoma therefore shorten this chain and run the steps of every iteration at the same time on up to four GPUs. We compile the complete training loop with JAX, including the MuJoCo Warp simulator. For locomotion, XSoma leaves only the dynamics of the robot to the world model and computes everything else exactly, including the terrain height under the feet. It learns with a horizon of one second and without a critic. On four H100 GPUs, XMimic learns to track all 40 LAFAN1 clips with the Unitree G1 in 0.86 minutes, 3.7 times faster than BlinkMimic on one GPU. XSoma reaches the tracking target that Holosoma's tests set for FastSAC in 0.77 minutes, 12.3 times faster than FastSAC on one GPU, while needing only an eighth of its environment steps.

2611.20427.title: Fuzzy Explainable Continual Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Robotic Navigation
2611.20427.abstract: Continual robot navigation requires reinforcement learning policies to continuously adapt to new environments while retaining previously acquired knowledge. Meanwhile, explainable reinforcement learning aims to learn meaningful behavioral representations through policy interaction. However, these objectives are inherently conflicting, as continual learning emphasizes policy stability whereas explainable behavior learning requires adaptive exploration. Existing methods rarely address both simultaneously. To resolve this issue, this paper proposes a Fuzzy Explainable Continual Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (FECHRL) method. A two-stage behavior cloning strategy is introduced to balance rapid policy adaptation and explainable behavior evolution by progressively transitioning from strong imitation guidance to autonomous reinforcement learning. Furthermore, a fuzzy critic based on a Takagi--Sugeno fuzzy inference system is proposed to alleviate value extrapolation errors during the transition between imitation-guided learning and autonomous exploration, thereby improving continual training stability. Experimental results on sequential multi-scenario navigation tasks demonstrate that the proposed method effectively unifies continual learning capability and policy explainability within a single reinforcement learning framework, achieving stable knowledge retention and meaningful behavioral explanation.

llm.title_ja: ロボットナビゲーションのためのファジー説明可能継続的階層的強化学習

2611.20402.title: Making Koopman Control Guarantees Hold on Robots
2611.20402.abstract: A Koopman controller can stabilize its learned latent-space linear model yet fail to stabilize the nonlinear plant. The learned model propagates predictions in latent space, while the deployed controller repeatedly re-encodes the measured physical state. We show that nominal closed-loop stability transfers to the nonlinear plant when the learned and true closed-loop dynamics agree to first order on the embedding's tangent space at the target. We derive a robustness margin for approximate matching and show that a stable open-loop latent model cannot exactly match an unstable equilibrium. We introduce Tangent-Invariant Koopman (TIK), which estimates a local plant linearization from offline transitions and enforces first-order matching to this estimate. TIK recovers the fitted LQR gain at the target, while a bilinear predictor captures state-dependent actuation during large maneuvers. Across four simulated unstable benchmarks, all 40 Standard Koopman controllers have stable latent closed loops, but their deployed nonlinear systems are locally unstable. In contrast, all 40 TIK controllers locally stabilize their respective nonlinear plants. An offline stability test using empirical curvature estimates identifies stable TIK controllers on two cart-pole systems, but is inconclusive under high noise. Under explicit model-error and curvature bounds, an invariant terminal set guarantees constraint satisfaction after entry under local feedback. TIK achieves 88\% constrained cart-pole swing-up success with a 0.25 ms planning budget and controls simulated seven-joint arms within 1-5 ms per step.

llm.title_ja: ロボット上でkoopman制御保証を成立させる

llm.problem: Koopmanコントローラが学習された潜在空間の線形モデルを安定化できても、非線形プラントの安定化に失敗すること

llm.result: 4つのシミュレーションされた不安定なベンチマークにおいて、標準的なKoopmanコントローラが失敗する中、TIKコントローラは非線形プラントを局所的に安定化させた

2611.20402.tldr_en: It is proved that latent stability transfers to the robot when the latent model reproduces the true closed-loop dynamics to first order on the embedding's tangent space at the target, and derive a margin for approximate matching and show that an open-loop stable latent model cannot match the plant's linearization at an unstable equilibrium.

2611.20324.title: High-Speed Forward and Reverse Tractor-Trailer Driving with Learned Vehicle Dynamics
2611.20324.abstract: Tractor-trailer systems are difficult to control, especially unstable during reverse motion, and their dynamics depend on difficult-to-measure factors, including road friction and suspension coefficients. We introduce a learned dynamics model for tractor-trailer control and compare it with a reduced-order dynamics model with Fiala tire forces as an analytic baseline. Specifically, we compare a model predictive path integral (MPPI) controller that uses the learned dynamics model to an MPPI controller that uses the analytic model, as well as to three additional baseline controllers.
