In the main closed-loop tracking experiments across four simulated environments, MPPI with learned dynamics achieves mean speeds closer to the target magnitudes and lower root-mean-square (RMS) hitch angles than MPPI with the analytic model at every tested setpoint, with higher completion rates in seven of eight reverse configurations.
2611.20324.comment: The first three authors contributed equally to this work. Project page: https://ds12a.github.io/drift-with-trailer/

llm.title_ja: 学習された車両ダイナミクスを用いたトラクタ・トレーラの高速前方・後方走行
llm.tldr_ja: トラクタ・トレーラ制御のために学習されたダイナミクスモデルを導入し、モデル予測経路積分（MPPI）コントローラと解析的モデルを比較して優れた追従性能と完了率を示した。
llm.problem: トラクタ・トレーラシステムは制御が難しく、特に後退時は不安定であり、路面摩擦やサスペンション係数などの測定が困難な要因にダイナミクスが依存すること
llm.method: 学習されたダイナミクスモデルを用いたMPPIコントローラと、Fialaタイヤ力を用いた解析的低次元モデルを比較評価する手法
llm.result: 4つのシミュレーション環境における閉ループ追従実験において、学習ダイナミクスを用いたMPPIは目標速度により近く、ヒッチ角度の二乗平均平方根誤差が小さくなり、後退設定での完了率も向上した

2611.20324.tldr_en: In the main closed-loop tracking experiments across four simulated environments, MPPI with learned dynamics achieves mean speeds closer to the target magnitudes and lower root-mean-square hitch angles than MPPI with the analytic model at every tested setpoint, with higher completion rates in seven of eight reverse configurations.

2611.20320.title: Course-Referenced Lateral Control of Trail-Following Convoys: String Stability and Adaptive Feedforward under Load Uncertainty
2611.20320.abstract: Vehicles in a convoy can steer along the GNSS trails of the vehicles ahead when lane markings are unavailable, as on snow covered roads. Since each vehicle's tracking error enters the reference of the next, lateral errors can grow along the convoy. This paper presents a course referenced formulation of trail following in arc length, in which each follower takes the direction of its fitted trail as its heading reference. Error propagation then reduces to a single transfer function. We derive a condition under which combining the trails of the leader and the predecessor keeps the errors bounded for any convoy length, and show that following the predecessor alone lets the errors accumulate without bound, even without amplification, on roads that end turned or shifted sideways. Passenger and cargo loads and tire stiffness vary in practice, and we show that they enter the curvature feedforward through a single coefficient, whose mismatch leaves steady offsets on curves. We propose an adaptive law that estimates this coefficient on curves and removes the offsets. Simulations of an eleven vehicle convoy confirm the analysis.

llm.title_ja: トレイル追従車列のコース参照型横方向制御：荷重不確実性下での弦の安定性と適応型フィードフォワード
llm.tldr_ja: アーク長におけるトレイル追従のコース参照定式化を提案し、リーダーと先行車を組み合わせたトレイルにより任意の車列長で誤差をboundedに保つ条件を導出した。
llm.problem: 雪上などの車線標示がない場所でGNSSトレイルに沿って走行する際、各車両の追従誤差が蓄積して車列全体で横方向誤差が増大すること
llm.method: アーク長におけるコース参照型定式化の導入と、荷重やタイヤ剛性の不確実性に対応する適応法律（アダプティブ法）の提案
llm.result: 11台の車両からなる車列のシミュレーションにより、提案手法の解析の妥当性と定常オフセットの除去効果が確認された

2611.20314.title: NF-VLA: A Normalizing-Flow Baseline for Vision-Language-Action Learning
2611.20314.abstract: Autoregressive normalizing flows (NFs) provide a tractable density for learning and sampling continuous robot actions. We show that a single maximum-likelihood objective can train vision--language--action (VLA) policies competitive with leading methods on manipulation benchmarks. We present NF-VLA, which combines conditional autoregressive normalizing flows with score-based action refinement. Its deep--shallow architecture concentrates visual, language, and proprioceptive prefix conditioning in a high-capacity deep block, while unconditioned shallow blocks provide a shared invertible action transformation. The vision--language backbone and flow are jointly trained by exact maximum likelihood on Gaussian-smoothed action chunks. The same learned density supplies a single score-based correction at inference, refining generated actions to account for training-time smoothing without a separately trained denoiser. Trained on LIBERO from a pretrained vision--language backbone without robot pretraining, NF-VLA achieves 98.35\% success across the four standard suites and 72.6\% on LIBERO-Plus using the same checkpoint without further fine-tuning. Ablations show that deep-only prefix conditioning and score-based refinement both improve closed-loop success. Together, these results establish carefully structured autoregressive flows as a competitive approach to VLA control, with one learned density supporting policy training, action generation, and refinement.

llm.title_ja: NF-VLA：ビジョン・言語・行動学習のための正規化フローベースライン
llm.tldr_ja: 条件付き自己回帰正規化フローとスコアベースの行動補正を組み合わせたNF-VLAを提案し、単一の最大尤度目的関数で最先端のマニピュレーションベンチマークに匹敵する性能を達成した。
llm.problem: 連続的なロボット行動の学習とサンプリングにおいて、扱いやすい密度関数を持つ効果的なVLAポリシーの構築
llm.method: 高容量な深層ブロックでプレフィックス条件付けを行い、未条件の浅層ブロックで共有可逆変換を行うディープ・シャロウ構造を持つ正規化フローとスコアベース行動補正の統合
llm.result: LIBEROベンチマークの4つの標準スイートで98.35%の成功率を達成し、追加のファインチューニングなしでLIBERO-Plusでも72.6%を記録した
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.20314.tldr_en: These results establish carefully structured autoregressive flows as a competitive approach to VLA control, with one learned density supporting policy training, action generation, and refinement.

2611.20306.title: Ontology-Compiled Control Barrier Functions for Heterogeneous Robot Teams
2611.20306.abstract: Safety filters for heterogeneous robot teams fail because of missing constraints, overestimated braking capabilities and conflicts between individually satisfiable constraints. We present OntoCBF, which compiles a domain ontology with a class taxonomy, typed relations, safety axioms and a dynamics profile per robot class into a control barrier function filter with one quadratic program per agent. Description-logic entailment supplies the constraints of any team online, including those that follow from chains of relations and from classes defined by what a robot carries, so the existing safety axioms cover new robot classes, payload classes and combinations. We prove that a subclass may reuse the braking capability of its parent whenever it can produce every velocity of the parent, a property separate from subsumption. For box-bounded double integrators this property is also necessary, and every loss of safety then begins with a conflict. Once three robots interact, the safe set of pairwise barriers contains states from which a collision is unavoidable, and such states persist in larger teams under any fixed capability reduction. In a simulated warehouse where humans ignore the robots, a filter written for the design classes violates safety in 89-100 % of the episodes with unseen classes. In all scenarios, including one with 32 robots, OntoCBF violates safety in 20-70 % of the episodes, each time after a conflict, with a median deepest intrusion of 10-17 % of the keep-out distance. A multi-agent PPO policy trained with the filter in the loop lowers the rate of infeasible quadratic programs, nearly all of them conflicts, by 18-41 %.

llm.title_ja: 異種ロボットチームのためのオントロジーコンパイル型制御バリア関数
llm.tldr_ja: ドメインオントロジーを制御バリア関数フィルタにコンパイルし、記述論理の包含関係を用いてエージェントごとの安全制約をオンラインで提供するOntoCBFを提案した。
llm.problem: 異種ロボットチームの安全フィルタにおいて、制約の欠落、過大評価された制動能力、制約間の矛盾が生じること
llm.method: オントロジーの分類体系、関係、安全公理、ダイナミクスプロファイルをエージェントごとの二次計画法を用いた制御バリア関数フィルタにコンパイルする手法
llm.result: シミュレーションされた倉庫環境において、未見のクラスに対しても安全性の違反率を大幅に低減し、マルチエージェントPPOポリシーの性能を向上させた

2611.20306.tldr_en: It is proved that a subclass may reuse the braking capability of its parent whenever it can produce every velocity of the parent, a property separate from subsumption, and every loss of safety then begins with a conflict.

2611.20273.title: DexFormer 2.0: Towards a Cross-Embodiment Foundation Policy for Dexterous Grasping
2611.20273.abstract: Dexterous grasping policies are usually trained for one arm paired with one hand. Every new pairing then needs its own policy, and the number of policies grows with every arm and hand added. We ask whether a single policy can control many arm-hand combinations and transfer to pairings and hands it has never seen. This is hard because robots differ in the number, layout, and dynamics of their joints, so their observations and actions share no common interface. We present DexFormer 2.0, a single reinforcement learning policy for cross-embodiment dexterous grasping. It maps every robot to a canonical joint interface with validity masks, encodes each joint's morphology with attention biased by the kinematic tree, and uses a Transformer-XL memory to infer embodiment-dependent dynamics from recent interaction. Trained on 18 combinations of four arms and six hands, it reaches 89% stable success on seen combinations and 51% on six held-out arm-hand pairs, outperforming GRU and DexFormer 1.0 baselines. Without fine-tuning, it also grasps with four new hand types and, through retargeting, with parallel grippers. Ablations show that memory, the kinematic-tree bias, and broader pairing coverage each matter for transfer. On a physical Flexiv arm, distilled students transfer zero-shot from simulation with two hands, including a held-out pair. Project website: https://davidlxu.github.io/dexformer2-web/.

llm.title_ja: DexFormer 2.0：器用な把持に向けたクロス・エンボディメント基盤ポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な腕と手の組み合わせを単一のポリシーで制御するため、正規化された関節インターフェース、運動学木に基づくアテンション、Transformer-XLメモリを用いたDexFormer 2.0を提案した。
llm.problem: 器用な把持ポリシーが通常1つの腕と1つの手のペアに限定され、新しい組み合わせごとに個別のポリシーが必要になること
llm.method: 関節インターフェースの正準化、運動学木に基づくアテンションバイアス、およびTransformer-XLメモリを組み合わせた単一の強化学習ポリシー
llm.result: 18の訓練済み組み合わせで89%の安定した成功率を達成し、未学習の6つのペアや新しいハンドタイプへのゼロショット転移に成功した
keywords_ja: クロス・エンボディメント

2611.20273.tldr_en: This work presents DexFormer 2.0, a single reinforcement learning policy for cross-embodiment dexterous grasping that maps every robot to a canonical joint interface with validity masks, encodes each joint's morphology with attention biased by the kinematic tree, and uses a Transformer-XL memory to infer embodiment-dependent dynamics from recent interaction.

2611.20244.title: Right Goal, Wrong Body: Re-grounding Frozen VLAs under Actuation Shift
2611.20244.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are capable of producing desired robotic behaviors in ideal settings. However, they often fail when the robot's actuation changes at deployment. For example, remounting, mechanical wear, or command latency changes can lead to failed tasks and unsafe behaviors. To address the inevitable actuation shift, we propose ReGround, an inference-time method that keeps the VLA frozen and re-grounds its intended motion. ReGround learns the deployed robot's dynamics from task-agnostic motor babbling, and then tracks the policy's intended motion while staying close to the policy's own plan. ReGround activates only upon detecting a shift, and needs no rewards, demonstrations, or retraining. We show via two VLAs, eight LIBERO tasks, and five shift settings that ReGround can restore near-oracle success, such as raising $π_{0.5}$'s success from 0.16 to 0.90 under 400 ms latency, while remaining safer than a linear-calibration baseline. Project website and open-source code: https://umersiddique94.github.io/ReGround/.
2611.20244.comment: Accepted at the SPAIS Workshop at CoRL 2026

llm.title_ja: 正しい目標、誤った身体：作動シフト下での凍結VLAの再グラウンディング
llm.tldr_ja: 作動シフト（アクチュエーションシフト）発生時にVLAを凍結したまま、タスク非依存のモーターバブリングからロボットのダイナミクスを学習して意図された動きを再グラウンディングするReGroundを提案した。
llm.problem: デプロイ時にロボットの作動状態（再搭載、摩耗、コマンド遅延など）が変化すると、VLAモデルがタスク実行や安全な動作に失敗すること
llm.method: タスク非依存のモータバブリングにより配備されたロボットのダイナミクスを学習し、ポリシーの計画を追従しながら意図された動きを再グラウンディングする推論時手法
llm.result: 8つのLIBEROタスクと5つのシフト設定において、400msの遅延下でのπ0.5の成功率を0.16から0.90に向上させるなど、オラクルに近い成功率を回復した
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル
ロボットマニピュレーション

2611.20244.tldr_en: This work proposes ReGround, an inference-time method that keeps the VLA frozen and re-grounds its intended motion while staying close to the policy's own plan, and shows via two VLAs, eight LIBERO tasks, and five shift settings that ReGround can restore near-oracle success.

2611.20230.title: A Matrix with Steps: An Episodic and Procedural Memory Method for Tool-Using Agents and Robots
2611.20230.abstract: Agents that call tools and robots that execute tasks are challenged by two shortcomings: they repeat what failed before, and they learn from runs that they only believe succeeded. We describe the construction of a memory that addresses both, built for a production agent platform. Every run is recorded as an episode, and only an outcome confirmed by an external check, a test, a tool result or a person counts; the agent's own claim never does. What is learned from episodes is kept in a memory with two parts: an associative matrix, written with the delta rule, which finds the procedure that applies to a situation; and a section of ordered, addressable step records that answers what comes after a given step, where a step is a goal of the agent, not a motion. Because the matrix sums its associations, it keeps no order and cannot return or delete a single one; it serves as the finder, and order, outcome counts and deletion live in the records. We describe how execution outcomes are stored, how episodes are recalled and used for solving tasks, and the file format that stores the memory. In simulation, a robot that judged its own success and stopped when it believed it was done reported $96\%$ of its tasks as done and solved $35\%$; with external verification it solved $79%$. In a store of $100000$ synthetic episodes ($457$MB on disk), the oldest episode was still found first, no episode from another person's memory was returned, and a success vouched for only by the model was never recalled; a lookup took $16$ms on a laptop and $40$ms on a server node (median). Task outcomes were measured up to about $10000$ confirmed records, where the exact records solved every revisit at the first attempt.

llm.title_ja: ステップを持つ行列：ツールを使用するエージェントとロボットのためのエピソード・手続き型メモリ手法
llm.tldr_ja: 外部検証によって確認された成功のみを記録し、デルタ則を用いた連想行列と順序付きステップ記録を組み合わせたメモリ構造を構築してタスク解決能力を向上させた。
llm.problem: ツールを呼び出すエージェントやタスクを実行するロボットが、過去の失敗を繰り返し、自己判断による不確かな成功から学習してしまうこと
llm.method: 外部確認された結果のみをエピソードとして記録し、デルタ則による連想行列（検索用）とアドレス指定可能なステップ記録（順序・削除管理用）を組み合わせたメモリの構築
llm.result: 自己判断によるシミュレーションでは35%の解決率であったのに対し、外部検証を取り入れた場合は79%に向上し、10万件のエピソードストアでも高速な検索を実現した

2611.20230.tldr_en: How execution outcomes are stored, how episodes are recalled and used for solving tasks, and the file format that stores the memory are described, built for a production agent platform.

2611.20202.title: DAPPT: Domain-Aware Policies from Procedural Trajectories for Sim-to-Real Dexterous Tool Use
2611.20202.abstract: Sim-to-real RL has achieved impressive results in dexterous manipulation but remains limited to tasks with accurate rigid-body simulation. However, these methods cannot be applied to skills that involve deformable and particles, with which the simulation speed will become too slow for large-scale RL learning. We present DAPPT, a sim-to-real framework for end-to-end dexterous tool-use manipulation skills, e.g., sand scooping, play-dough rod-rolling, without simulating non-rigid materials. Our method learns a domain-aware RL policy by tracking procedural trajectories parameterized by domain parameters, and distills it into an end-to-end domain-aware sensorimotor policy. Furthermore, explicit domain represen-tation enables fast selection of domain parameters that can maximize downstream task performance. We evaluate DAPPT end-to-end on six dexterous manipulation tasks, including sand scooping, play-dough rod-rolling, sand scraping, mouse-wheel scrolling, dispenser pressing, and spray triggering. Our method achieves 1.5-3.8x in task metrics through the best domain parameter and transfers zero-shot to the real world.

llm.title_ja: DAPPT：手続き型軌跡からのドメイン認識型ポリシーによるシム・トゥ・リアル器用な道具使用
llm.tldr_ja: 非剛体材料を直接シミュレーションせず、ドメインパラメータでパラメータ化された手続き型軌跡を追従することで、器用な道具使用のシム・トゥ・リアル転移を実現するDAPPTフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 変形可能な材料や粒子を含むタスクでは、正確なシミュレーションの計算速度が遅くなり、大規模な強化学習に適用できないこと
llm.method: ドメインパラメータでパラメータ化された手続き型軌跡を追従するドメイン認識型強化学習ポリシーを学習し、エンドツーエンドのセンサーモータポリシーに蒸留する手法
llm.result: 砂すくいや粘土の棒転がしなど6つの器用な操作タスクにおいて1.5〜3.8倍の性能向上を達成し、実世界へのゼロショット転移に成功した
keywords_ja: 非剛体シミュレーション

2611.20202.tldr_en: DAPPT is presented, a sim-to-real framework for end-to-end dexterous tool-use manipulation skills, e.g., sand scooping, play-dough rod-rolling, without simulating non-rigid materials, and explicit domain represen-tation enables fast selection of domain parameters that can maximize downstream task performance.

2611.20196.title: DoF-Query Transformer for Adaptive Fusion of Egocentric Vision and Forearm HD-sEMG in Continuous Hand Kinematics
2611.20196.abstract: Continuous and accurate estimation of human hand kinematics is important not only for intuitive human-machine interaction, but also for capturing fine-grained human manipulation demonstrations that can provide action supervision for embodied-intelligence datasets and dexterous robot learning. However, individual sensing modalities may be insufficient for reliable estimation under varying operating conditions. We present a finger-unencumbered multimodal framework for continuous regression of 20 hand joint angles from egocentric RGB images and 128-channel forearm high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG). The framework combines a Vision Transformer-based visual encoder, a Transformer-based EMG encoder, and a degree of freedom (DoF) query Transformer fusion decoder. To account for the varying informativeness of visual and EMG cues across joint DoFs and input conditions, the decoder assigns a separate learnable query to each DoF, enabling DoF-specific and context-adaptive fusion of the two modalities. The framework was evaluated on synchronized multimodal data from 10 participants. Averaged across participants, the proposed fusion model achieved a mean coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of $0.88$ and a mean absolute error (MAE) of $2.80^\circ$, compared with $0.82$ and $3.21^\circ$ for the vision-only model and $0.68$ and $5.13^\circ$ for the EMG-only model. It also outperformed the evaluated representative unimodal baselines and alternative fusion designs. DoF-wise analyses showed larger fusion gains for visually ambiguous joints and viewing conditions, while synthetic visual occlusion demonstrated greater robustness than vision-only estimation. These results highlight the complementary value of egocentric vision and forearm HD-sEMG for capturing fine-grained human hand kinematics, with potential applications in human demonstration acquisition and dexterous robot learning.

llm.title_ja: 連続的な手の運動学における自己視覚と前腕HD-sEMGのアダプティブ融合のためのDoFクエリTransformer
llm.tldr_ja: 自己視覚RGB画像と前腕HD-sEMG信号を組み合わせ、自由度（DoF）ごとに学習可能なクエリを用いて文脈適応的なマルチモーダル融合を行うフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 様々な操作条件下において、単一のセンシングモダリティでは人間の手の運動学を信頼性高く推定するには不十分であること
llm.method: ビジョンTransformerベースの視覚エンコーダ、TransformerベースのEMGエンコーダ、およびDoFクエリTransformer融合デコーダを組み合わせたフレームワーク
llm.result: 10名の参加者による評価において、平均決定係数（R^2）0.88、平均絶対誤差（MAE）2.80°を達成し、単一モダリティのベースラインを大きく上回った
keywords_ja: ヒューマンマシンインタラクション

2611.20196.tldr_en: A finger-unencumbered multimodal framework for continuous regression of 20 hand joint angles from egocentric RGB images and 128-channel forearm high-density surface electromyography, highlighting the complementary value of egocentric vision and forearm HD-sEMG for capturing fine-grained human hand kinematics.

2611.20185.title: RoboKit: Accelerating Parallel Differentiable Optimization for Robot Learning
2611.20185.abstract: We present RoboKit, a high-performance, general-purpose toolkit for parallel differentiable optimization in robotics, built on three principles: (i) Performance and flexibility: GPU-parallel multi-seed solvers pair sampling with versatile optimizers, running 2-60$\times$ faster than task-specific baselines across seven tasks; (ii) Geometry, rendering and physics: hybrid and coarse-to-fine representations accelerate collision, differentiable rendering and simulation, optimizing 4096 grasps in 2.97 s; (iii) Integration with learning: costs are differentiable and simulation is parallel, so RoboKit both distills optimization into policies and trains RL; distilled policies run 9-240$\times$ faster at comparable accuracy, and RL reaches a GPU baseline's scores up to 2.1$\times$ sooner on the same simulator.
2611.20185.comment: Accepted to CoRL 2026. Project page: https://openrobokit.com/robokit

llm.title_ja: RoboKit：ロボット学習のための並列微分可能最適化の高速化
llm.tldr_ja: サンプリングと多様なオプティマイザを組み合わせたGPU並列マルチシードソルバーやハイブリッド表現を備えた、ロボット学習向け汎用並列微分可能最適化ツールキットRoboKitを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボット学習における並列微分可能最適化の柔軟性と計算性能の両立の難しさ
llm.method: GPU並列マルチシードソルバー、衝突・微分可能レンダリング・シミュレーションを加速するハイブリッド・段階的表現、および学習との統合
llm.result: タスク特化型ベースラインと比較して2〜60倍高速に動作し、蒸留されたポリシーは9〜240倍高速に実行され、強化学習も効率的にスコアを達成した

2611.20185.tldr_en: RoboKit both distills optimization into policies and trains RL, a high-performance, general-purpose toolkit for parallel differentiable optimization in robotics, built on three principles of performance and flexibility.

2611.20174.title: Weights & Caches: LLMs Can Program Tabular Foundation Models
2611.20174.abstract: Neural networks are typically programmed through optimization, rather than by explicitly specifying their computations. Recent work on weight-space programming suggests that large language models (LLMs) can instead reason about and manipulate neural-network weights directly. In this work, we show that LLMs can directly program statistical computations in tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose parameters enable inference across different datasets. We investigate three complementary settings using GPT-6 Astra, without gradient-based optimization. First, Astra directly programs nanoTabPFN from zero-initialized weights, achieving a mean ROC AUC of 0.849 across 20 TabArena datasets, compared to 0.876 for a pretrained baseline. Second, Astra diagnoses and repairs a signed-product regression failure in pretrained TabPFN-3.5, restoring near-perfect predictions on held-out synthetic datasets while preserving performance on TabArena-Lite, with only a 0.08% average relative increase in error. Third, it writes KV-cache-editing programs that steer TabPFN-3.5's predictions on unseen synthetic datasets, demonstrating transformations such as reversing linear trends and converting sine waves into approximate square waves, without modifying model weights. Together, our findings suggest that LLM-driven programming could complement gradient-based optimization across TFMs' development and usage, while offering a new way to investigate and intervene in their internal computations.

llm.title_ja: Weights & Caches: LLMによる表形式基盤モデルの直接プログラミング
llm.tldr_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）を用いて表形式基盤モデル（TFM）の統計計算を直接プログラムし、勾配ベースの最適化なしに推測や重みの修正、KVキャッシュ編集が行えることを示した。
llm.problem: ニューラルネットワークは通常最適化によってプログラムされ、直接的な理由付けや重みの操作が困難であること。
llm.method: GPT-6 Astraを用いて勾配最適化を行わずに、ゼロ初期化重みのプログラミング、事前学習済みモデルの重み修復、およびKVキャッシュ編集プログラムの作成を実施。
llm.result: nanoTabPFNの直接プログラミングでベースラインに匹敵する性能を達成し、モデルの修復やKVキャッシュ編集による予測制御が可能であることを実証した。
keywords_ja: ニューラルネットワーク

2611.20174.tldr_en: It is shown that LLMs can directly program statistical computations in tabular foundation models (TFMs), whose parameters enable inference across different datasets, and suggest that LLM-driven programming could complement gradient-based optimization across TFMs'development and usage.

2611.20137.title: Cleanly-DINO: Efficiently Learning Visual Task Spaces for Robotics
2611.20137.abstract: Learning manipulation tasks from few demonstrations requires abstractions that capture the changes relevant to task completion, such as object poses in rigid-body manipulation. However, tasks such as cleaning are defined by changes in visual state rather than object pose, making the choice of task representation less clear. In this work, we propose Cleanly-DINO to learn visual task spaces from few demonstrations. Given a mask of a task-relevant region and frozen ViT features, Cleanly-DINO fits a projection to isolate a task space and fit a progression metric to it. We train the model on diverse cleaning examples and evaluate its ability to localize incomplete task regions and transfer across visual domains. We also study its utility for robot learning by using it as an observation encoder and reward signal in a reinforcement learning setting. Finally, we deploy our fitted model within a real-world robotic wiping pipeline to evaluate its use in guiding task execution.
authors: José Arce y de la Borbolla
2611.20137.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, accepted at COMPOGEN Workshop CoRL 2026, Austin, USA

llm.title_ja: Cleanly-DINO: ロボット工学のための視覚的タスク空間の効率的な学習
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的状態の変化によって定義される清掃などのタスクに向けて、わずかなデモンストレーションから視覚的タスク空間を効率的に学習するCleanly-DINOを提案した。
llm.problem: 清掃などのタスクはオブジェクトの姿勢ではなく視覚的状態の変化で定義されるため、タスク表現の選択が困難であること。
llm.method: マスクと凍結されたViT特徴量を与え、投影と進行メトリックを適合させて視覚的タスク空間を学習するCleanly-DINOを構築した。
llm.result: 不完全なタスク領域の局所化やドメイン間転移が可能となり、強化学習の報酬信号や実世界のワイピングパイプラインに有効であることを示した。

2611.20137.tldr_en: This work proposes Cleanly-DINO, a model that fits a projection to isolate a task space and fit a progression metric to it, and trains the model on diverse cleaning examples and evaluates its ability to localize incomplete task regions and transfer across visual domains.

2611.20127.title: Aerial Person Detection under Edge Constraints: Held-Out Evaluation and Edge-Ground Verification
2611.20127.abstract: A search drone sees a missing person as a few pixels, carries a small computer, and shares a narrow radio link. We study person detection under those limits; the primary evaluations were declared before they ran, and later analyses are marked exploratory. In an exploratory comparison, holding out recording blocks inferred from thermal frame identifiers cut recall at a fixed false-alarm target from 32.7% to 12.3%. With nothing tuned on test blocks, a 46,000-parameter detector gated by a contrast cue finds 10.4% of people against 5.7% for the same network applied everywhere. A standard detector, YOLO11n, trained under the same folds finds 54.5% at a similar false-alarm rate for about eleven times the arithmetic, and on our 4K field footage at 117 m has a walking person among its top 16 detections in up to 92% of frames against 74% for our board. Run alone, YOLO11n's thresholds set at one location overshot their false-alarm target 1.7 to 3.4 times at new locations, and its best configuration at altitude cost 4 to 24 standard passes per frame. Re-scoring its 16 best crops (154 KB per frame) with an 842,000-parameter ground model, thresholds frozen on a validation location, raised recall from 44.9% to 53.7% against the same 16 crops with YOLO's own scores; in a post hoc paired analysis over 15 test locations the gain was +8.8 points [+2.4, +12.5]. Pooled false detections fell from 0.86 to 0.64 per frame, but that paired change was not distinguishable from zero. Coverage of a still person in earth tones was very low for both detectors in the clips we flew.
2611.20127.comment: 14 pages, 1 figure, 8 tables. Code, truth registers and result files: https://github.com/numberz-ai/aerial-person-detector

llm.title_ja: エッジ制約下での空中人物検出：ホールドアウト評価とエッジ・地上検証
llm.tldr_ja: 小型コンピュータと狭帯域無線リンクを持つ探索ドローンにおける人物検出の限界を評価し、エッジモデルと地上モデルの組み合わせによる性能向上を検証した。
llm.problem: 探索ドローンは限られた計算資源と狭い無線リンクで、非常に小さく見える行方不明者を検出する必要があること。
llm.method: 熱フレーム識別子に基づくホールドアウト評価を行い、軽量検出器と地上モデルによる再スコアリングを比較・検証した。
llm.result: 地上モデルによる上位検出結果の再スコアリングにより再現率が向上し、偽検出数が減少することが示された。

2611.20107.title: SAFER: Navigating the Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma in World-Model-Based Planning for Autonomous Driving
2611.20107.abstract: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. A world model offers this foresight, but only within the coverage of its training data, which poses an exploration-exploitation dilemma. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes, 0.95 and 0.77 from a privileged bird's-eye view, and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive, 53.4 in regular and 49.0 in safety-critical traffic. Project page: https://ys-qu.github.io/safer-website.

llm.title_ja: SAFER: 自動運転のための世界モデルベース計画における探索・活用のジレンマの克服
llm.tldr_ja: 他者の失敗からオフラインで学習しつつ自身の運転でオンライン学習を継続することで、世界モデルベースの自動運転における探索・活用のジレンマを解決する枠組みSAFERを提案した。
llm.problem: 自動運転の世界モデルは学習データの範囲外の状況でエラーを起こしやすく、安全確保のための探索と活用のジレンマが存在すること。
llm.method: 専門家が注釈を付けたシミュレーション上の失敗事例からオフライン学習を行い、リスクを考慮したサンプリングベースのプランナーとオンラインでのモデル洗練を組み合わせた。
llm.result: CARLAリーダーボードおよびMetaDriveにおいて、ルート完了率、報酬、安全性が大幅に向上した。

2611.20107.tldr_en: SAFER is proposed, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving, which reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive.

2611.20100.title: EgoSwarm: Learning Decentralized Robot Swarm Intelligence from Human Swarm Demonstrations
2611.20100.abstract: Advancing from individual embodied intelligence to swarm embodied intelligence is a key step toward scalable, general-purpose embodied intelligence. Complex tasks often require multiple agents to divide responsibilities, coordinate handovers, and manipulate shared objects collaboratively. However, existing robot learning methods rely primarily on individual demonstrations, which provide limited supervision for modeling dependencies among agent actions, while collecting multi-robot demonstrations at scale remains difficult. Human egocentric demonstrations offer a scalable alternative, yet distributed observations from multiple participants cannot directly supervise decentralized policies. We introduce EgoSwarm, the first robot learning framework for learning decentralized multi-robot collaboration from human swarm demonstrations. EgoSwarm collects more than 50 hours of collaborative experience using a robot-free multi-person egocentric system. We introduce the Swarm Interaction Packet (SIP) and Swarm Interaction Token (SIT) to recover cross-agent interaction relations from distributed observations and transform this experience into local supervision consistent with deployment-time information constraints. We further propose SwarmVLA, which transfers knowledge of swarm behavior to decentralized policies conditioned on local observations, local history, and limited neighbor messages. SwarmVLA achieves a mean success rate of 72.2% across three categories of multi-robot collaborative tasks. Project page:https://xitong-c.github.io/EgoSwarm_Page/.
2611.20100.comment: 22 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Includes supplementary materials. Project page: https://xitong-c.github.io/EgoSwarm_Page/

llm.title_ja: EgoSwarm: 人間の群れデモンストレーションからの分散型ロボット群知能の学習
llm.tldr_ja: ロボットを使わない多人数一人称視点システムを用いて人間の協調経験を収集し、分散型マルチロボット協調を学習する初のフレームワークEgoSwarmを提案した。
llm.problem: 複雑なタスクにはマルチエージェントの協調が必要だが、既存手法は個別のデモンストレーションに依存し、分散観測を直接指導することが難しいこと。
llm.method: Swarm Interaction Packet（SIP）とToken（SIT）を導入してクロスエージェント間の相互作用関係を復元し、SwarmVLAにより局所観測に基づく分散ポリシーを学習する。
llm.result: 3種類のマルチロボット協調タスクにおいて平均72.2%の成功率を達成した。

2611.20100.tldr_en: This work introduces EgoSwarm, the first robot learning framework for learning decentralized multi-robot collaboration from human swarm demonstrations, and proposes SwarmVLA, which transfers knowledge of swarm behavior to decentralized policies conditioned on local observations, local history, and limited neighbor messages.

2611.20098.title: A Geometric Observer for Visual-Inertial Odometry using Optical-Flow Constraints
2611.20098.abstract: This paper presents a geometric observer for monocular visual-inertial odometry driven by individual optical-flow constraints. For each tracked point, the bearing and its rotationally compensated derivative give a depth-free homogeneous constraint on the body-frame velocity. These constraints enter the innovation of an observer on the gravity-augmented group $\mathbb{SE}_3(3)$ through a Riccati gain, without estimating depths or reconstructing the direction of motion. The auxiliary gravity state makes the six-dimensional body-frame velocity-gravity error dynamics independent of the attitude correction, and their uniform observability is shown to be equivalent to persistent excitation of a matrix formed from the inertial bearings and their derivatives. Under this condition, the body-frame velocity and gravity errors converge globally and uniformly exponentially, and a gravity-based attitude correction renders the combined velocity, gravity, and reduced-attitude error almost globally asymptotically stable and locally uniformly exponentially stable. Simulations illustrate the excitation condition, recovery from initial errors, and sensitivity to perturbed measurements.

llm.title_ja: オプティカルフロー制約を用いた視覚慣性オドメトリのための幾何学的オブザーバー
llm.tldr_ja: 深度推定を行わず、個別のオプティカルフロー制約に基づいて単眼視覚慣性オドメトリを行う幾何学的オブザーバーを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来の視覚慣性オドメトリでは深度推定や運動方向の再構築が必要であり計算コストがかかること。
llm.method: 追跡された各ポイントのベアリングとその回転補償された導関数を用いて、重力拡張群上のオブザーバーの革新にリカッティ利得を介して入力する。
llm.result: 速度および重力誤差の大域的・一様的・指数関数的収束を示し、シミュレーションにより初期誤差からの復帰や測定外乱に対する感度を確認した。
keywords_ja: 幾何学的オブザーバー

2611.20098.tldr_en: This paper presents a geometric observer for monocular visual-inertial odometry driven by individual optical-flow constraints, and illustrates the excitation condition, recovery from initial errors, and sensitivity to perturbed measurements.

2611.20075.title: Prompt Re-Specification and Target-Mask Availability in Mask-Conditioned Visual Reinforcement Learning for Moving-Platform Landing
2611.20075.abstract: Visual reinforcement learning (RL) policies that land a drone on a moving platform can fail when the landing pad looks different from the one used in training. Using binary target masks as the visual input removes most pixel-level appearance information while preserving the spatial representation of the target, and lets a text prompt specify the target. In simulation, we test whether a frozen (fixed-weight) mask-based DrQ-v2 policy can handle a new pad when only the prompt of its fine-tuned SAM 3 detector changes. A banana-themed pad lowered landing success from 75.6% to 12.0%, and SAM 3 rarely detected it under the original prompt. A revised prompt, chosen after testing several candidates, restored success to 68.4% with no weight updates. In a separate experiment with a policy trained on ground-truth masks, filling in masks that were missing while the pad was visible helped landing far more than the tested mask-centroid and area corrections. Tracking the pad over time supplied masks more often and also kept producing them after the pad was confirmed absent from the rendered image, but it did not establish a reliable improvement in landing success. Whether a usable mask reaches the policy at all thus appears to be an important limiting factor for this approach.

llm.title_ja: 移動プラットフォームへの着陸におけるマスク条件付き視覚強化学習のプロンプト再指定とターゲットマスクの可用性
llm.tldr_ja: 移動プラットフォームへのドローン着陸において、ターゲットマスクを視覚入力として用い、SAM 3検出器のプロンプトを適切に再指定することで重み更新なしに着陸性能を回復できることを示した。
llm.problem: 訓練時と異なる着陸パッドに対しては視覚強化学習ポリシーが失敗しやすく、適切なビジュアル表現の維持が課題であること。
llm.method: 凍結されたマスクベースのDrQ-v2ポリシーに対し、ファインチューニングされたSAM 3検出器のプロンプト変更やマスク補完の効果をシミュレーションで検証した。
llm.result: 外観が大きく異なるパッドに対してプロンプトの修正により着陸成功率が大幅に回復し、利用可能なマスクの供給が性能を左右する重要な要因であることを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: プロンプトエンジニアリング

2611.20075.tldr_en: Whether a usable mask reaches the policy at all appears to be an important limiting factor for this approach, and filling in masks that were missing while the pad was visible helped landing far more than the tested mask-centroid and area corrections.

2611.20019.title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
2611.20019.abstract: Reinforcement learning agents learn from mistakes, yet their decisions can be difficult to trace back to those experiences. We investigate whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events. A fixed training log is replayed from the same initial Q-table under three conditions. FULL retains all updates, SKIP omits bad-experience updates, and NEUTRALIZE retains those updates without their event penalties. We illustrate the method on six classic Markov decision processes and evaluate it in closed-loop driving in CARLA. On the full driving task, FULL reached the goal from 33 of 40 test starts, whereas SKIP and NEUTRALIZE reached it from none, indicating that the bad experiences carry decision-relevant information. At the local level, for 47 decisions shortly before a failure of SKIP or NEUTRALIZE, removing or neutralizing a small group of bad experiences, with a median size of one, caused the trained agent to select the failing policy's action in 46 cases. For this agent, the results indicate that its decisions can be explained by its bad experiences.

llm.title_ja: D'BEAST: 自動運転エージェントの説明としての記録された失敗経験
llm.tldr_ja: 強化学習エージェントの意思決定がトレーニング中の「悪い経験（失敗経験）」によってどのように説明できるかを、CARLAでの自動運転評価を通じて調査した。
llm.problem: 強化学習エージェントの決定はその学習過程の経験、特に安全やタスクイベントに関する失敗に遡って追跡することが困難であること。
llm.method: 固定された訓練ログを、全ての更新を維持する条件、失敗経験の更新を省略する条件、ペナルティを除いて更新を維持する条件の3つでリプレイして比較した。
llm.result: 失敗経験を削除または中立化するとエージェントが失敗行動を選択するようになり、エージェントの意思決定が失敗経験によって適切に説明できることを示した。

2611.20019.tldr_en: This work investigates whether a tabular agent's decisions can be explained by its bad experiences, defined as the training transitions associated with safety or task events, and results indicate that its decisions can be explained by its bad experiences.

2611.20011.title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
2611.20011.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) and World-Action Models (WAMs) have emerged in autonomous driving with the promise of strong generalization to long-tail scenarios. Although these models achieve state-of-the-art results on autonomous driving benchmarks, most existing benchmarks are dominated by nominal scenarios and therefore cannot test this promise. To test one such long-tail capability that is critical for safety, we introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark that measures how driving models react to objects that appear in the ego vehicle's path. Built on real NAVSIM and PhysicalAI-Autonomous-Vehicles scenes, ReactBench-AD composites a crossing pedestrian, a standing pedestrian, or a stationary car consistently across all camera views and history frames. Each edited scene thus forms an exact, pixel-level counterfactual pair with its original, which allows us to isolate the causal effect of the inserted object on the predicted trajectory. Evaluating four VLAs and two WAMs, we find that they react weakly, often barely at all. Finally, we test how easily one of the evaluated VLAs, ReCogDrive, can be taught to brake hard for imminent hazards: a short fine-tuning stage on edited scenes substantially improves its reactions, with the learned behavior generalizing to unseen objects and fully real scenes, at minimal cost to nominal driving. These results call into question the out-of-the-box long-tail capabilities of these models, but suggest that they can be a strong foundation for acquiring them with little additional training, highlighting the value of real or synthetic data that demonstrates the long-tail behaviors nominal datasets rarely contain. Code and data will be made publicly available.

llm.title_ja: ReactBench-AD: 運転用VLAおよび世界・行動モデルは進路上の切迫した危険に反応するか？
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転における視覚言語行動モデル（VLA）や世界・行動モデル（WAM）が、進路上の障害物などの切迫した危険に対してどのように反応するかを評価するベンチマークReactBench-ADを提案した。
llm.problem: 既存の自動運転ベンチマークは通常シナリオが大部分を占め、安全性に不可欠なロングテールな危険回避能力を十分にテストできないこと。
llm.method: 実世界のシーンに歩行者や車両をピクセル単位で一貫して合成した正確な反事実的ペアを作成し、4つのVLAと2つのWAMの反応を評価した。
llm.result: 評価されたモデルの危険への反応は全体的に弱いが、編集されたシーンでの短時間のファインチューニングにより反応性能が大幅に改善されることを示した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.20010.title: PlanDiv: Test-Time Scaling with Latent Plans for Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.20010.abstract: Test-time scaling improves vision-language-action (VLA) policies by drawing several action candidates and executing the best one. We find that its returns diminish quickly when the candidates are resampled from one decoder: they differ by noise rather than by plan, and for each of three resampling sources, going from four to eight candidates adds only 0.06-0.07 to the average number of completed tasks on CALVIN. We introduce PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest. The plans are learned from demonstrations alone, without plan labels or rewards. With the backbone, data and training recipe held fixed, eight plan-conditioned candidates raise five-task chain success on CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D from 56.9% to 69.9%, while eight candidates from autoregressive, plan-free or same-plan resampling reach at most 64.9%. The same-plan baseline is PlanDiv's own checkpoint with the plan held fixed, so this gap comes from the plans, not from drawing more samples. On LIBERO-Long, four plans remove 40% of single-candidate failures, against at most 21% for matched resampling. On a real Franka arm the gain appears where a task admits more than one solution: PlanDiv is on par with a single-output OpenVLA-OFT+ baseline on a one-solution task and succeeds in 51 of 54 trials against 40 of 54 on two tasks with two solutions.

llm.title_ja: PlanDiv: 視覚言語行動モデルのための潜在計画を用いたテスト時スケーリング
llm.tldr_ja: 単一のデコーダーからのサンプリングの限界を克服し、多様な潜在計画に基づく複数の行動候補を生成することでVLAポリシーのテスト時スケーリング性能を向上させるPlanDivを提案した。
llm.problem: VLAポリシーのテスト時スケーリングにおいて、単一デコーダーからの複数候補の再サンプリングは計画の多様性がなく、リターンの向上がすぐに頭打ちになること。
llm.method: 軽量なプランナーがK個の潜在的な計画仮説を提案し、共有のマスク付き拡散エグゼキューターがバックボーンの1回のパスでプランごとにアクションチャンクをデコードするPlanDivを開発した。
llm.result: CALVINやLIBERO-Longにおいて、プランに基づく候補生成によりタスク成功率が大幅に向上し、実機のフランカアームでも複数解が存在するタスクで優れた性能を証明した。
keywords_ja: テスト時スケーリング

2611.20010.tldr_en: This work introduces PlanDiv, an action head that makes the candidates differ by plan: a lightweight planner proposes K latent plan hypotheses, a shared masked-diffusion executor decodes one action chunk per plan from a single backbone pass, and the policy executes the chunk that its own likelihood ranks highest.

2611.19998.title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
2611.19998.abstract: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. Project page: https://movicproject.github.io/ .

llm.title_ja: MoViC: 単眼ビデオストリームからのリアルタイム人型ロボット全身制御
llm.tldr_ja: ライブRGBビデオを入力として、装着型トラッカーを用いずに人型ロボットのリアルタイムな全身模倣制御を実現するフレームワークMoViCを提案した。
llm.problem: 単眼ビデオからのリアルタイム全身模倣には、頑健なトラッカーと高品質なリアルタイム再構成の両立が必要であること。
llm.method: 単眼の人体モーション再構成、ロボットリタイアリング、トランスフォーマーベースの行動基盤モデルを組み合わせ、非同期の視覚処理とポリシー実行を可能にする外挿法を導入した。
llm.result: ハードウェア実験において、ライブの単眼RGB入力を元に、双腕・単腕のマニピュレーションタスクや高動的な動作追跡がデバイス不要で可能であることを実証した。

2611.19998.tldr_en: MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices, is presented, which combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model.

2611.19979.title: Practice Is Not Free: Measuring the Embodied Cost of Reset-Free Robot Practice
2611.19979.abstract: When a robot practices without human resets, every attempt still costs wall-clock time, actuator wear, and sometimes a person's attention, yet the schedulers that decide what to practice next treat attempts as free. We present an open, low-cost testbed for measuring these costs: a self-built SO-101 arm runs two demonstration-trained ACT policies that reset each other, with a vision-based success detector and a ledger that records the time, joint travel, and human interventions of every attempt. We formulate cost-aware practice scheduling, in which task selection is rewarded by measured competence gain net of embodied cost, and specify in advance the comparison that will test it. Its first two conditions, run on hardware for 51 minutes of robot time, show that a fixed retry limit did not reduce the share of execution time lost to failures (36%, against 27% for a feasibility rule; not significant) and saved no robot time. The logs suggest why: failures showed no sign of clustering, so a retry right after a failure was as likely to succeed as any other attempt. The ledger also shows that most of the retry rule's extra human time came from cubes knocked out of reach rather than from the rule itself, and a cost-aware rule replayed on the logs recovers the sensible choice without a hand-set limit. We also report lessons from building the system, including a coverage effect in which concentrating demonstrations in a smaller workspace raised success there from 8/20 to 10/10.
2611.19979.comment: 16 pages, 6 figures. Code, data, logs and videos: https://github.com/Vedant2604/so101-cost-aware-scheduler

llm.title_ja: 練習はタダではない：リセット不要なロボットの練習における具現化コストの測定
llm.tldr_ja: リセット不要なロボットの自己学習において、時間、アクチュエータの摩耗、人間の注意といった「具現化コスト」を測定するためのオープンな低コストテストベッドを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットの自律的な練習における試行には壁時計時間やアクチュエータの摩耗などのコストが伴うにもかかわらず、従来のスケジューラーは試行を無料のものとして扱っていること。
llm.method: SO-101アームを用いて相互にリセットし合う2つのACTポリシーを動かし、成功検出器と時間・関節移動・人間の介入を記録する台帳を備えたコスト考慮型スケジュールを構築した。
llm.result: 失敗のクラスタリングは見られず即座の再試行が必ずしも有効ではないことや、試行錯誤に伴う現実的なコスト構造に関する知見を実機実験で明らかにした。

2611.19979.tldr_en: This work forms cost-aware practice scheduling, in which task selection is rewarded by measured competence gain net of embodied cost, and specifies in advance the comparison that will test it.

2611.19969.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
2611.19969.abstract: Autonomous vehicle (AV) decisions at intersections affect the delay, braking, and motion smoothness of surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs). Learning socially compatible behavior requires connecting imagined interaction outcomes with feedback from executed actions. We propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden. An interaction-aware latent model supports imagination, while off-policy correction and replay updates enable observed rewards and transitions to supervise both the critic and actor. Simulation experiments at an unsignalized intersection achieve a 100% success and reductions in following-HDV acceleration variation of 65.5% and 44.0% relative to PIWM and DreamerV3, respectively. Ablations identify complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency. Tests under out-of-distribution traffic shifts further show lower ego jerk and HDV acceleration variation than PIWM at comparable passage times.

llm.title_ja: 社会的に調和した運転のための実行フィードバックからの価値およびポリシー較正
llm.tldr_ja: 自動運転車が周囲の人間が運転する車両（HDV）の負担を考慮し、社会的調和のとれた運転行動を学習するための世界モデル強化学習フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 交差点での自動運転車の決定が周囲のHDVの遅延、制動、動きの滑らかさに影響を与えるため、想像上の相互作用と実行された行動のフィードバックを結びつける必要があること。
llm.method: インタラクションを考慮した潜在モデルによる想像上のポリシー改善と、完了したインタラクションからの直接的な価値・ポリシー較正を組み合わせた。
llm.result: シミュレーションの非信号交差点において100%の成功率を達成し、従来手法と比較して後続HDVの加速度変動を大幅に削減した。
keywords_ja: 交通シミュレーション

2611.19969.tldr_en: A world-model reinforcement learning framework combines imagined policy improvement with direct value and policy calibration from finalized interactions, balancing AV progress with HDV interaction burden, and identifies complementary roles for value calibration in reducing HDV burden and policy calibration in improving passage efficiency.

2611.19952.title: CRAFT: A Robot-Agent Harness with Scope-Aware Adaptation
2611.19952.abstract: A robot may know how to move an object yet still need to learn where it belongs. When a person rejects a placement, the robot must decide whether the correction applies only to that situation or expresses a broader rule. We study this problem in CRAFT (Contextual Requirement Adaptation with Frozen Tools), a framework for learning local requirements without retraining robot skills. It records physical success separately from whether an action meets the requirement. Our scope ladder uses memory when an action has already been judged in a nearly identical situation. Elsewhere, it combines memory, explicit rules and a learner for requirements beyond those rules, weighting their predictions by how well they predicted earlier feedback. Controlled studies show gains over correction memory alone in utility, which rewards acceptable actions and charges for mistakes and questions. In camera-grounded robot simulations, the ladder asks fewer questions than language-model agents with persistent memory, but some of those agents take fewer wrong actions and succeed more often after requirements change. All execution failures and timeouts remain in the evaluation. These results support combining specific memories with broader rules, while leaving reliable adaptation to changing requirements unresolved. All evidence comes from simulation with generated requirements and simulated feedback.

llm.title_ja: CRAFT: スコープ認識型適応を備えたロボット・エージェントハーネス
llm.tldr_ja: 人間の訂正が特定の状況のみに適用されるか、より広いルールを表すかを判断し、ロボットスキルを再学習せずにローカルな要件を学習するCRAFTフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: ロボットがオブジェクトの動かし方を知っていても、その置くべき場所を間違えた際、人間の訂正が個別適用か広範なルールかを適切に判断する必要があること。
llm.method: 物理的成功と要件適合性を区別して記録し、メモリ、明示的ルール、学習器を組み合わせ、過去のフィードバックの予測精度に基づいて予測を重み付けするスコープラダーを導入した。
llm.result: カメラ接地ロボットシミュレーションにおいて、訂正メモリ単体と比較して効用の向上が見られ、言語モデルエージェントよりも質問回数を削減できることを示した。
keywords_ja: ロボットエージェント

2611.19952.tldr_en: The scope ladder uses memory when an action has already been judged in a nearly identical situation, while leaving reliable adaptation to changing requirements unresolved, and Controlled studies show gains over correction memory alone in utility.

2611.19932.title: From Companion to Guardian: Designing an Emergency Support System Using a Quadruped Robot for Older Adults
2611.19932.abstract: As older adults increasingly live alone, emergency support becomes an important function for home companion robots. In Australia, demand for the care and support workforce is projected to nearly double between 2020-21 and 2049-50. Service robots such as robot dogs may support older adults by combining everyday companionship with assistance when human support is not immediately available. We present the design and implementation of a domestic companion-robot system on a Unitree Go1 quadruped platform that combines companionship with emergency awareness and response. The system uses a three-stage interaction model consisting of companion, danger-awareness, and emergency modes. A rule-based escalation policy combines signs detected from visual and speech input to determine the current risk level and adjust how long the robot waits for the user to confirm safety before entering emergency mode. Additional detected signs can shorten this waiting time. Users can confirm safety, request immediate help, stop robot motion, or reset the system. We verified the implemented decision rules and escalation timing through 105 automated trials and 25 staged physical trials. Additional visual evidence shortened the waiting time, and the system entered emergency mode when the waiting time ended without confirmation.
2611.19932.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures. Accepted at the Australasian Conference on Robotics and Automation (ACRA 2026)

llm.title_ja: コンパニオンからガーディアンへ：四足歩行ロボットを用いた高齢者向け緊急支援システムの設計
llm.tldr_ja: Unitree Go1四足歩行ロボットプラットフォームを活用し、日常的な見守りと危険検知・緊急時対応を統合した家庭用コンパニオンロボットシステムを設計・実装した。
llm.problem: 一人暮らしの高齢者が増加する中、日常の話し相手や見守りと、人間がすぐに対応できない場合の緊急支援機能を持つロボットの需要が高まっていること。
llm.method: コンパニオン、危険認識、緊急モードの3段階のインタラクションモデルを採用し、視覚・音声入力からの検知兆候に基づいてリスクレベルと安全確認の待機時間を調整するルールベースのポリシーを構築した。
llm.result: 105回の自動試行と25回の実機ステージ試行を通じて決定ルールとエスカレーションタイミングを検証し、追加の視覚的証拠によって待機時間が短縮され確実に緊急モードへ移行することを確認した。

2611.19932.tldr_en: This work presents the design and implementation of a domestic companion-robot system on a Unitree Go1 quadruped platform that combines companionship with emergency awareness and response and verified the implemented decision rules and escalation timing.

2611.19922.title: Lao Siji: Adapting openpilot to Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving in Neural Reconstruction
2611.19922.abstract: We present Lao Siji, an end-to-end driving policy that ranks third in the 2026 NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E Driving Challenge, ahead of most entries built on foundation models. Instead of training from scratch on a general-purpose vision backbone, we adapt openpilot, an open-source L2 production model. We freeze its vision encoder and fine-tune the policy layers with an ego-state adapter and a route memory. On closed-loop rollouts in neural-reconstructed scenes, we supervise the policy with a privileged map teacher for lateral self-correction and a body-extent loss for road and obstacle clearance, while distilling the base model's remaining outputs to retain car following. Ablations show that self-correction samples carry the gain, while the clearance loss substitutes for them where no teacher exists. Longitudinal safety instead rests on the base model's lead-vehicle estimate behind a rule-based speed layer. Longer training, imitating human logs, and human-log speed targets yield either no measurable gain or adverse effects. Without further training, Lao Siji also places among the leaders on HUGSIM and Odyssey. The final training takes only one GPU-hour and shifts the weights by 3.9% from the shipped model. Code will be released after review.

llm.title_ja: Lao Siji: ニューラル再構成におけるクローズドループ端から端までの運転へのopenpilotの適応
llm.tldr_ja: オープンソースのL2自動運転モデルであるopenpilotをベースに、視覚エンコーダを固定してポリシー層をファインチューニングすることで、クローズドループの端から端までの運転を実現したLao Sijiを提案した。
llm.problem: ゼロからの汎用ビジョンバックボーンの訓練にはコストがかかり、基盤モデルベースの手法は計算負荷やロングテール対応に課題があること。
llm.method: openpilotの視覚エンコーダを凍結し、エゴ状態アダプターとルートメモリを追加。ニューラル再構成シーンのクローズドループにおいて、特権マップ教師や車体範囲損失を用いてポリシー層をファインチューニングした。
llm.result: 2026 NVIDIA AlpaSim E2Eドライビングチャレンジで3位に入賞し、最小限の重み変更と1GPU時間の訓練で優れた性能を達成した。
keywords_ja: ファインチューニング
シミュレーション評価

2611.19922.tldr_en: This work presents Lao Siji, an end-to-end driving policy that ranks third in the 2026 NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E Driving Challenge, ahead of most entries built on foundation models, and adapts openpilot, an open-source L2 production model.

2611.19912.title: AgenticJevNav: Agentic Object Search and Navigation via Event-Driven Verification
2611.19912.abstract: Agentic navigation must maintain goals and adapt actions from incomplete evidence despite execution failures and delayed inference. We present AgenticJevNav, which links goal-directed planning, evidence memory, event-triggered verification, and bounded execution. The Agent plans from RGB, odometry, memory, and feedback, retaining goal ownership while authorizing a bounded action set. Jev reviews structured evidence after blocked/failed execution or two consecutive low-progress segments. Version, freshness, and once-only checks govern decision application. A single executor and independent RGB reflex constrain motion. Goal revisions revoke obsolete requests and actions before replanning. Across six simulated task families, AgenticJevNav achieves 73.33% SR over 60 trials, 21.67 percentage points above the next-best Agent-only aggregate control under differing historical protocols. A real-world GENISOM L1 quadruped deployment achieves 70.0% success over 30 trials, including bounded search reporting. Together, the simulation and physical-robot results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture, while remaining failures highlight opportunities to improve grounding, approach planning, and runtime.
2611.19912.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Project page: http://106.55.248.254/

llm.title_ja: AgenticJevNav: イベント駆動型検証による自律的オブジェクト探索とナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 目標指向の計画、証拠メモリ、イベント駆動型の検証、および境界付き実行を統合し、不完全な証拠や失敗に対応する自律ナビゲーションシステムAgenticJevNavを提案した。
llm.problem: エージェントによるナビゲーションでは、実行の失敗や推論の遅延がある中で、不完全な証拠から目標を維持し行動に適応する必要があること。
llm.method: RGB、オドメトリ、メモリ、フィードバックから計画を立て、ブロックされた実行や低進捗時に構造化された証拠をレビューするJevと、単一のエグゼキューターおよびRGB反射神経を組み合わせた。
llm.result: シミュレーションの6つのタスクファミリーで73.33%の成功率を達成し、実機のGENISOM L1四足ロボットでも70.0%の成功率を実証した。

2611.19912.tldr_en: Together, the simulation and physical-robot results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed architecture, while remaining failures highlight opportunities to improve grounding, approach planning, and runtime.

2611.19904.title: DiffWAM: Learning World Action Model from Consecutive Visual Difference
2611.19904.abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as an important paradigm in robot learning, jointly predicting future scene states and robot actions from current observations and instructions. However, future states entangle task-related changes with large amounts of task-irrelevant content, such as static backgrounds, which weakens the model's ability to capture changes relevant to task execution. To address this, we propose Difference World Action Model (DiffWAM), a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that enhances world representations by jointly learning future-state prediction and consecutive visual difference prediction. We define consecutive visual differences as differences between the latent representations of consecutive observations, providing an explicit learning signal for temporal variation. The framework comprises a World Expert for future frame prediction, an Action Expert for action generation, and a Diff Expert for predicting these latent differences along the trajectory. A structured unidirectional attention mask conditions the Diff, World, and Action Experts solely on the current-frame representation while blocking attention between experts. This design allows both the World and Diff Experts to be removed during inference, introducing no additional inference overhead. DiffWAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks and substantially improves over FastWAM on real-world manipulation tasks. Specifically, it attains average success rates of 98.8%, 92.65%, and 88.3%, outperforming the state-of-the-art baseline (i.e., FastWAM) by 1.75, 1.55, and 15.0 percentage points, respectively.

llm.title_ja: DiffWAM: 連続する視覚的差分からの世界行動モデルの学習
llm.tldr_ja: 将来の状態予測と連続する視覚的差分の予測を共同学習することで、タスクに関係のない背景情報を排除して関連する変化のキャプチャを強化する世界行動モデル（DiffWAM）を提案した。
llm.problem: 世界行動モデルにおける将来状態の予測は、静的な背景などのタスクに無関係な情報とタスク関連の変化が混ざり合い、モデルの実行能力を弱めること。
llm.method: 将来フレーム予測を行う世界エキスパート、行動生成を行う行動エキスパート、連続する観測間の潜在的差分を予測するDiffエキスパートからなるMixture-of-Experts（MoE）フレームワークを構築した。
llm.result: LIBEROおよびRoboTwin 2.0ベンチマークで最先端の性能を達成し、実世界のマニピュレーションタスクでもFastWAMを大幅に上回った。

2611.19904.tldr_en: Diff World Action Model (DiffWAM), a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) framework that enhances world representations by jointly learning future-state prediction and consecutive visual difference prediction, and substantially improves over FastWAM on real-world manipulation tasks.

2611.19894.title: EasyNav: A Modular Architecture for Real-Time Navigation Across Heterogeneous Robot Environments
2611.19894.abstract: Most robot navigation stacks implicitly bind mapping, localization, planning, and control to specific representations and data flows, yielding architectures hard to extend, compare experimentally, or reason about end-to-end timing. This is critical in heterogeneous scenarios, where multiple spatial representations, sensing modalities, and coordinate frames coexist and evolve at different rates. This paper presents a navigation architecture centered on an explicit, shared navigation state that serves as the sole interaction interface between modular components. Constraining mapping, localization, planning, and control to operate over this shared state enables interchangeable, representation-agnostic pipelines under explicit compatibility and timing contracts. We realize this architecture as EasyNav, an open source ROS 2 framework, and validate it through real-robot experiments, including indoor navigation with laser sensing and large-scale indoor-outdoor navigation with GPS and 3D LiDAR across multi-level routes. Compared with Nav2 under matched conditions, EasyNav reduces reaction latency from 377 to 33 ms indoors and from 71 to 8 ms outdoors, while also using less CPU and memory.

llm.title_ja: EasyNav: 異種ロボット環境におけるリアルタイムナビゲーションのためのモジュール式アーキテクチャ
llm.tldr_ja: 明示的かつ共有されたナビゲーション状態を中心に据えることで、多様な表現やセンサー、データフローに対応しつつ低遅延を実現するナビゲーションフレームワークEasyNavを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のロボットナビゲーションスタックはマッピング、ローカリゼーション、計画、制御が特定の表現に密結合しており、異種環境での拡張や時間遅延の管理が困難であること。
llm.method: 単一のインタフェースとして機能する明示的な共有ナビゲーション状態を定義し、交換可能で表現に依存しないパイプラインをROS 2フレームワーク（EasyNav）として実装した。
llm.result: Nav2と比較して、屋内での反応遅延を377msから33msへ、屋外を71msから8msへ短縮しつつ、CPUとメモリの消費量を削減できることを実機で検証した。
keywords_ja: モジュール式アーキテクチャ

2611.19894.tldr_en: This paper realizes this architecture as EasyNav, an open source ROS 2 framework, and validate it through real-robot experiments, including indoor navigation with laser sensing and large-scale indoor-outdoor navigation with GPS and 3D LiDAR across multi-level routes.

2611.19825.title: Foundation Pareto Flow Policy for Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
2611.19825.abstract: The overarching goal of reinforcement learning (RL) is to efficiently optimize the agent's policy for various environments, tasks, dynamics, and even user preferences, which often consist of multiple and potentially conflicting rewards/objectives. This necessitates the learning of Pareto-optimal policies that can navigate different trade-offs among objectives. However, existing multi-objective RL (MORL) methods, whether trained online or offline, are typically limited to task- or objective-specific policy learning and do not address generalization of learned trade-offs to unseen tasks/objectives. In this work, we propose the Foundation Pareto Flow Policy (FP2) for offline MORL in continuous robotic control, inspired by the pre-mid-post-training paradigm underlying recent foundation models. Specifically, we instantiate FP2 as a multi-modal diffusion transformer equipped with a likelihood-free flow matching loss, enabling unified, scalable, and instructable learning of diverse trade-off trajectories. We further develop a three-stage training pipeline to gradually optimize the policy: (1) pre-training on a large-scale MORL dataset, (2) mid-training on a carefully curated high-quality dataset, and (3) post-training on few collected trajectory data from new tasks and trade-offs. Empirical results demonstrate that FP2 outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods on most tasks of the D4MORL benchmark, achieving superior zero-shot interpolation and extrapolation on complex Pareto manifolds as well as efficient few-shot adaptation of the learned trade-off prior to new continuous-control tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/FibonacciRabbit/FP2.

llm.title_ja: マルチオージェクティブ強化学習のための基礎パレートフローポリシー
llm.tldr_ja: 事前・中・後訓練パラダイムにインスパイアされ、尤度フリーのフローマッチング損失を持つマルチモーダル拡散トランスフォーマーを用いて、多様なトレードオフ軌跡を統合的かつスケーラブルに学習するFoundation Pareto Flow Policy（FP2）を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のマルチオージェクティブ強化学習（MORL）手法はタスクや目的に特化しており、学習したトレードオフを未知のタスクへ汎用化することが困難であること。
llm.method: 大規模MORLデータセットでの事前訓練、高品質データセットでの中訓練、新タスクからの少量の軌跡データによる後訓練の3段階訓練パイプラインを設計した。
llm.result: D4MORLベンチマークにおいて従来手法を凌駕し、複雑なパレート多様体における優れたゼロショット補外・内挿と効率的な少ショット適応を実現した。
keywords_ja: マルチオージェクティブ強化学習

2611.19825.tldr_en: The Foundation Pareto Flow Policy (FP2) is proposed, inspired by the pre-mid-post-training paradigm underlying recent foundation models, and instantiate FP2 as a multi-modal diffusion transformer equipped with a likelihood-free flow matching loss, enabling unified, scalable, and instructable learning of diverse trade-off trajectories.

2611.19822.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
2611.19822.abstract: Video world models promise to predict the future of a scene from its present. Do current models keep this promise? We probe this question counterfactually. When a small change to the present flips the future, such as a box resting a few millimeters before or past a table edge, a model that tracks the state of the world must flip its prediction too. We build FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks. At the base, visual minimal pairs, two nearly identical frames whose true futures differ, test whether predictions change across the boundary; matched controls go further and test whether they change only where the future does; and dense sweeps, the strictest level, locate exactly where they change. All 11 video world models we evaluate fall short. The best averages 18.3% pair accuracy over real and simulated scenes, below the 25% of random guessing. Models flip as often on steps that leave the future unchanged as on steps that change it, and their response stays flat across the sweeps. On the same frames, a vision-language model is selective and traces a near S-shaped curve near the boundary, and a coding agent that measures the image comes close to the true boundary. This implies that the deciding information is in the frame, and video models just miss it. We therefore urge the community to rethink world modeling as pure video prediction. Next-frame prediction must do more than draw plausible pixels; it must also identify the causal states that control future dynamics.

llm.title_ja: フリップテスト：ビデオ世界モデルは世界状態の学習に失敗する
llm.tldr_ja: 11種類のビデオ世界モデルを評価した結果、未来のダイナミクスを支配する因果状態を捉えきれておらず、ランダム推測を下回る性能であることが示された。
llm.problem: ビデオ世界モデルが未来のシーンを正しく予測できるか検証されていないこと。
llm.method: わずかな変化で未来が変わる1,680個のフレームを用いた厳格なテスト階層「FlipTest」の構築。
llm.result: 評価した11種類のビデオ世界モデルすべてが基準を満たさず、ペア正解率の平均が18.3%とランダム推測を下回った。

2611.19822.tldr_en: This work builds FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks, and urges the community to rethink world modeling as pure video prediction.

2611.19818.title: Drone Navigation for Fast, Safe Emergency Response
2611.19818.abstract: In 2025, there was a total of 358 weather-related disasters worldwide affecting millions of people. For unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to autonomously aid these people, they need to be able to navigate around complex obstacles and reach their destinations to deliver supplies or quickly locate survivors in disaster-stricken areas. Our research addresses this need by providing a method to compute minimum-time trajectories in real time while providing guarantees of obstacle avoidance along the trajectory. Previous approaches treat the problem of computing time-optimal trajectories without considering obstacle avoidance. Our work not only includes obstacle avoidance constraints, but also improves overall mission time for navigation. We define mission time as the sum of planning time and traversal time. In time-sensitive emergencies, rapid trajectory planning is essential to ensure the prompt delivery of critical medical aid. As such, we consider the combined planning and traversal time as the key metric for how quickly the vehicle can reach a survivor. We show a sample mission in Fig. 1 where the quadrotor navigates through multiple canyon-like obstacles to deliver aid; during most of this trajectory, it is applying the near-maximum thrust.
2611.19818.comment: Submitted to the 2027 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

llm.title_ja: 迅速かつ安全な緊急対応のためのドローンナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 障害物回避の保証を備えつつ、リアルタイムで最小時間軌道を計算する手法により、災害時のドローンによる救助物資配送のミッション時間を短縮する。
llm.problem: 従来の時間最適軌道計算手法では障害物回避が考慮されていなかったこと。
llm.method: 障害物回避制約を組み込み、計画時間と走行時間を合わせたミッション時間を最小化するリアルタイムの最小時間軌道計算手法の提案。
llm.result: 複雑な障害物を回避しながら、ほぼ最大の推力を用いて迅速に目的地に到達するクアッドローターのサンプルミッションを示した。
keywords_ja: ドローンナビゲーション

2611.19818.tldr_en: This research addresses the need for minimum-time trajectories in real time by providing a method to compute minimum-time trajectories in real time while providing guarantees of obstacle avoidance along the trajectory.

2611.19803.title: Pros4D: Modeling Evolving 4D Worlds in Latent Space for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
2611.19803.abstract: Dynamic spatial reasoning from monocular video enables vision-language models (VLMs) to understand how 3D environments evolve over time, supporting physical world understanding and embodied intelligence. Existing efforts primarily address observed-dynamics understanding, whereas agents in dynamic environments also require future-dynamics prediction beyond the observation boundary. Moreover, external geometric processing and textual descriptions can increase inference complexity or lose information when representing continuous dynamics. These limitations motivate a shared internal state that preserves observed dynamics and remains predictive beyond the input video. Accordingly, we present Pros4D, a framework for modeling evolving 4D worlds in latent space that unifies retrospective understanding of observed-dynamics with prospective reasoning for future-dynamics prediction. Specifically, Pros4D-Engine derives geometry-grounded supervision and constructs paired examples for both tasks, while Pros4D-Bench evaluates them across eight spatial task categories spanning dynamic cameras, objects, and scenes. At the model level, Pros4D compresses observed dynamics into latent observed states and autoregressively rolls them forward into latent future states. 4D Latent Alignment (4DLA) grounds these states through complementary visual-semantic and geometric supervision, while joint language supervision connects them to task reasoning. Experiments across benchmarks show consistent improvements over strong baselines in both capabilities.

llm.title_ja: Pros4D：動的な空間推論のための潜在空間における進化する4D世界のモデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 観測された動的状態の過去の理解と未来予測を統合し、潜在空間で進化する4D世界をモデリングするフレームワークPros4Dを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存手法は観測されたダイナミクスの理解に終始し、外部の幾何学的処理やテキスト記述が推論の複雑性を高めること。
llm.method: 観測されたダイナミクスを潜在状態に圧縮し、自己回帰的に未来の潜在状態へと展開するPros4Dフレームワークの開発。
llm.result: ベンチマーク実験において、動的カメラ、オブジェクト、シーンにわたる8つの空間タスクカテゴリで強力なベースラインを上回る改善を示した。

2611.19803.tldr_en: Pros4D is a framework for modeling evolving 4D worlds in latent space that unifies retrospective understanding of observed-dynamics with prospective reasoning for future-dynamics prediction and shows consistent improvements over strong baselines in both capabilities.

2611.19785.title: DynLimit: A Simulation Benchmark for Dynamics-Critical Planning and Control
2611.19785.abstract: Experiments near vehicle handling limits must keep three questions apart: what a maneuver requests, what the closed-loop system executes, and whether the task is completed. We present DynLimit, a simulation platform that organizes this process end to end. Scenarios are composed from road, friction, obstacle, and reference objects; planners and controllers attach through a shared observation and control interface; a vehicle adapter runs either a license-free four-wheel model or an external dynamics solver; and synchronized records feed task evaluation, replay, and response inspection. The platform carries a task-oriented evaluation method that pairs a prescribed reference demand with a sampled passing set and event-aligned diagnosis. Across eight task families, three friction environments, and three reference-assisted baseline chains we executed 450 runs: 360 nominal, 18 locally refined, and 72 with prescribed initial offsets. Method differences depend on the task family, equal aggregate pass counts arise from different passing cells, and local refinement narrows two sampled transitions without locating a continuous boundary. Two case comparisons show why sideslip or tire-utilization peaks cannot replace task constraints. The three views therefore stay distinct in every reported run: an outcome can be traced from the prescribed demand, through the executed response, to the task rule that decided it. Code is available at https://github.com/Yang2581/dynlimit

llm.title_ja: DynLimit：限界領域のプランニングと制御のためのシミュレーションベンチマーク
llm.tldr_ja: 車両の限界付近での実験における要求、実行、タスク完了を分離して評価するエンドツーエンドのシミュレーションプラットフォームDynLimitを提案する。
llm.problem: 車両のハンドリング限界付近の実験において、操舵要求、システム実行、タスク完了の区別が曖昧であること。
llm.method: 道路、摩擦、障害物、参照オブジェクトからシナリオを構成し、タスク指向の評価方法を備えたシミュレーションプラットフォームの構築。
llm.result: 8つのタスクファミリー、3つの摩擦環境にわたる450回の実行を通じて、要求、応答、ルールを区別したタスク評価を実現した。
keywords_ja: シミュレーションベンチマーク

2611.19785.tldr_en: DynLimit, a simulation platform that organizes this process end to end near vehicle handling limits, is presented, carrying a task-oriented evaluation method that pairs a prescribed reference demand with a sampled passing set and event-aligned diagnosis.

2611.19775.title: Recovery-Guided Model-Based Diffusion for Safety-Critical Legged Locomotion
2611.19775.abstract: Safety-critical high-speed legged locomotion requires motion planners to balance safety foresight with online computational efficiency. Although short prediction horizons reduce rollout costs, they provide limited safety foresight, and strict safety constraints severely restrict the feasible trajectory space. We propose a recovery-guided model-based diffusion (MBD) framework for safety-critical legged locomotion. It incorporates a learned terminal recovery critic into short-horizon trajectory optimization. Specifically, the critic approximates the worst-case future clearance margin along rollouts of a designated recovery policy. We introduce a feasibility-guided refinement strategy that combines within-horizon constraints and terminal recoverability at each sampling stage, while retaining feasible elites to mitigate sampling-support loss. Across 50 paired randomized Unitree Go2 obstacle-avoidance trials, our approach achieves zero collisions and 98% strict-clearance success, while requiring substantially less computation than long-horizon MBD baselines. A project page is available at https://zack4417.github.io/rg-mbd/.

llm.title_ja: 安全性クリティカルな脚式ロコモーションのためのリカバリー誘導型モデルベース拡散
llm.tldr_ja: 端末リカバリー批評家を短ホライズン軌道最適化に組み込んだリカバリー誘導型モデルベース拡散フレームワークにより、安全性クリティカルな脚式ロボットの高速移動を実現する。
llm.problem: 短い予測ホライズンは安全性への配慮が限られ、厳格な安全制約は軌道空間を極度に制限すること。
llm.method: 学習された端末リカバリー批評家を短ホライズン軌道最適化に組み込み、実現可能性に基づく洗練戦略を導入する手法の提案。
llm.result: Unitree Go2を用いた50回の障害物回避試験で衝突ゼロ、厳格なクリアランス成功率98%を達成し、計算量も大幅に削減した。

2611.19775.tldr_en: This work proposes a recovery-guided model-based diffusion (MBD) framework that incorporates a learned terminal recovery critic into short-horizon trajectory optimization, and introduces a feasibility-guided refinement strategy that combines within-horizon constraints and terminal recoverability at each sampling stage, while retaining feasible elites to mitigate sampling-support loss.

2611.19774.title: When Backdoors Can Be Switched Off: Suppression-Aware Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models
2611.19774.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map visual observations, robot states, and natural-language instructions to robotic actions, but their multimodal interfaces introduce new security risks. Existing VLA backdoor attacks primarily study trigger-based activation and stealthy action manipulation, leaving conditional suppression of malicious behavior underexplored. We investigate suppression-aware backdoors, which combine conjunctive trigger activation with instruction-conditioned suppression. We instantiate this design through three variants: Cross-Modal Trigger, combining robot-state and spatially separated visual triggers; Self-Suppressing Trigger, requiring a state trigger and a [DISRUPT] instruction token for activation, with [RESTORE] token suppressing the attack; and Multi-Trigger, additionally requiring a visual trigger while retaining suppression even when physical triggers persist. We evaluate these attacks using SmolVLA on two SO-100 manipulation datasets against four baselines: State Backdoor, BadVLA, TabVLA, and SilentDrift. Self-Suppressing and Multi-Trigger reduce Isolation Forest detection from 96--98% to 1--18% and action-space l divergence by 10--14X, achieving 63--71% attack success rates with perfect clean-task performance. Experiments with OpenVLA on LIBERO further show that the attacks transfer to a 7B-parameter policy, evading STRIP and action-distribution-shift detection. Our findings establish conditional suppression as an important dimension for evaluating backdoor threats in VLA policies.

llm.title_ja: バックドアがオフにできるとき：ビジョン・言語・行動モデルに対する抑制認識型バックドア攻撃
llm.tldr_ja: VLAモデルに対する指示条件付き抑制を伴う「抑制認識型バックドア攻撃」を提案し、その脆弱性と検出回避性能を実証した。
llm.problem: 既存のVLAモデルのバックドア攻撃はトリガーベースの活性化と隠れた行動操作を主に研究しており、悪意ある行動の条件付き抑制が未探索であること。
llm.method: クロスモーダル、自己抑制、マルチトリガーの3つのバリアントを設計し、SO-100およびLIBEROデータセットで評価する。
llm.result: 自己抑制型およびマルチトリガー型は検出率を大幅に低下させ、クリーンタスクの性能を維持しつつ63〜71%の攻撃成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.19774.tldr_en: This work investigates suppression-aware backdoors, which combine conjunctive trigger activation with instruction-conditioned suppression, and establishes conditional suppression as an important dimension for evaluating backdoor threats in VLA policies.

2611.19771.title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
2611.19771.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

llm.title_ja: JEPA4R：4Dポイントプランニングを備えた身体性JEPA世界モデル
