llm.tldr_ja: 単一深度カメラの点群を観測し、その潜在空間で予測・計画を行い、ポリシーヘッドを介して行動するJEPA世界モデルJEPA4Rを提案する。
llm.problem: 2D画像ではマニプلوーションが依拠する距離幾何学が暗黙的かつ外観と絡み合っており、モデルの想像が隠されたままであること。
llm.method: 点群を入力とし、潜在空間での予測と計画を行う「4Dポイントプランニング」と、デジタルツインでの学習および実機でのゼロショット適用。
llm.result: OGBenchやMetaWorldなどのベンチマークでピクセルベースのJEPAモデルを上回り、実機のアームとグリッパー・器用な手でゼロショット動作を達成した。

2611.19771.tldr_en: JEPA4R is presented, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; it is called 4D point planning.

2611.19765.title: M-CROSS: A Multisensor Simulation Dataset for SLAM across Water--Land Transitions
2611.19765.abstract: Water--land cross-domain robots require continuous localization across land, transition and underwater phases, where sensor characteristics and availability change abruptly. Existing datasets and conventional metrics are not designed to capture transition-induced degradation and failures. We present \textbf{M-CROSS}, to the best of our knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions. It provides synchronized LiDAR, sonar, stereo camera, IMU, DVL, and depth measurements; 6DoF pose ground truth; sensor-wise medium-state annotations; and medium-dependent sensor degradation models. We establish a transition-aware protocol comprising the Trajectory Completion Rate (TCR), Piecewise Absolute Pose Error (PW-APE), Transition End Error (TEE), and Transition Survival Period (TSP), which measure trajectory completion, single-domain accuracy, transition-induced error, and localization survival under prolonged partial immersion, respectively. Experiments with 6 representative SLAM systems show that existing methods fail to maintain both localization accuracy and trajectory continuity across the full set of water--land transitions, exhibiting transition-induced drift, trajectory discontinuities, and tracking failures. M-CROSS is publicly available https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MCross-Dataset

llm.title_ja: M-CROSS：水陸移行にわたるSLAMのためのマルチセンサーシミュレーションデータセット
llm.tldr_ja: 水陸両用ロボットの継続的な自己位置推定評価のため、多様なセンサーデータと移行認識型プロトコルを備えた初のマルチセンサーシミュレーションデータセットM-CROSSを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のデータセットや指標が水陸移行時のセンサー劣化や失敗を捉えるように設計されていないこと。
llm.method: LiDAR、ソナー、ステレオカメラ、IMU等の同期データ、グランドトゥルース、センサー劣化モデル、および移行認識型評価プロトコルの提供。
llm.result: 6つの代表的なSLAMシステムの実験により、既存手法が水陸移行時にドリフト、不連続性、追跡失敗を引き起こすことを示した。

2611.19765.tldr_en: M-CROSS is presented, to the best of the knowledge, the first multisensor simulation dataset and benchmark for SLAM across continuous water--land transitions, and a transition-aware protocol comprising the Trajectory Completion Rate, Piecewise Absolute Pose Error, Transition End Error, and Transition Survival Period are established.

2611.19731.title: Cooperative Transport of Unknown Objects by Distributed Effort Regulation in Multi-agent Systems
2611.19731.abstract: A distributed multi-robot object transportation strategy is proposed for objects of unknown shape, size, geometry, mass and mass distribution without any prior knowledge about the object or number of robots involved in the transportation process. Robots follow the boundary of the object and dynamically determine viable pushing points. A novel object-model-free heading-error-driven pushing effort regulation method is proposed to promote goal-directed object motion; robots regulate their pushing effort using individual and collective heading errors. Robots dynamically relocate around the object boundary if a pushing point is lost or the required pushing effort exceeds its capability to correct its heading. The proposed method is validated using simple and complex shapes with convex and non-convex boundary regions and dynamically changing weight distribution of objects. Detailed analysis on the effects of robot distribution and initial object pose on the transportation performance in terms of required time and path efficiency is also presented. Scalability analysis revealed that object transportation time is dependent on the number of pushing surfaces available which in turn depends on the object size, shape, and set inter-robot safety distance. The proposed system yielded highly efficient object paths with consistent elapsed transport times over several trials robust to external disturbances such as non-uniform friction between contacting surfaces and robot wheel slip.
2611.19731.comment: 9 pages, 12 figures; supplementary video available at https://youtu.be/C2usYt0xzl8; submitted to ICRA 2027

llm.title_ja: 分散型努力調整による未知オブジェクトの分散型マルチエージェント協調搬送
llm.tldr_ja: オブジェクトやロボット数に関する事前知識なしで、ロボットがオブジェクトの境界に沿って押し出し努力を動的に調整する分散型協調搬送手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 未知の形状・サイズ・質量のオブジェクトを事前知識なしで複数ロボットで協調搬送することの難しさ。
llm.method: 個体および集団の見出し誤差を用いたオブジェクトモデル不要の見出し誤差駆動型押し出し努力調整法の提案。
llm.result: 多様な形状や動的変化する重量分布のオブジェクトに対し、外乱に対してロバストで効率的な搬送パスと安定した搬送時間を実証した。

2611.19731.tldr_en: A novel object-model-free heading-error-driven pushing effort regulation method is proposed to promote goal-directed object motion; robots regulate their pushing effort using individual and collective heading errors.

2611.19730.title: AlphaTruck: A Platform for High-Speed Off-Road Autonomy on Unstructured Terrain
2611.19730.abstract: Progress in autonomous navigation in off-road environments requires not only advances in algorithms, but also robust and capable physical platforms suited to both development and deployment. Today, off-road autonomy is typically developed and tested at one of two extremes of vehicle scale, each with different drawbacks. Full-size vehicles are capable but expensive, require large logistic infrastructure for deployment and maintenance, and expensive when pushed beyond their limits. RC-scale vehicles are small and inexpensive, but limited in the terrain they can traverse and the payload that they can carry, which includes their sensors and compute. We present the AlphaTruck platform, which leverages recent advances in compact sensing and compute to integrate multimodal sensing, embedded CPU-GPU compute, and an onboard autonomy stack for high-speed, off-road navigation, all integrated into a large-scale, 1/5th RC vehicle chassis. AlphaTruck is designed as both a research testbed and a field-deployable platform for commercial and defense missions such as survey, search and rescue, and agriculture, with the capacity to carry task-specific payloads. At 1/5 scale, the autonomy stack, sensors, and batteries all compete for the same mass, power, and cooling budget, so the platform must balance five needs: mobility over rough terrain, rich sensing, onboard computation, payload capacity to carry the autonomy stack while leaving room for task-specific equipment, and practical operation and repair. Thus, AlphaTruck navigates off-road environments autonomously at 6-10 m/s using only onboard sensing and compute.

llm.title_ja: AlphaTruck：非構造化地形における高速オフロード自律走行のためのプラットフォーム
llm.tldr_ja: コンパクトなセンシングと演算を活用し、1/5スケールのRCカーの車体にマルチモーダルセンシングと自律走行スタックを統合したオフロード自律走行プラットフォームAlphaTruckを提案する。
llm.problem: 既存のオフロード自律走行プラットフォームは大型車では高価・大規模すぎ、RCスケールでは積載量や走行地形が制限されること。
llm.method: 1/5スケールのRC車両に、マルチモーダルセンサー、組み込みCPU-GPU、オンボード自律走行スタックを統合し、重量・電力・冷却のバランスを最適化する。
llm.result: オンボードセンシングと演算のみを用いて、非構造化環境において秒速6〜10mでの自律的なオフロード走行を実現した。
keywords_ja: ハードウェアプラットフォーム

2611.19720.title: Sim-to-Real Room-Mediated Object-Goal Navigation with ROS 2 and Nav2
2611.19720.abstract: Although object-goal navigation (ObjectNav) approaches are usually evaluated in simulation, which offers scale and repeatable environments, real-world deployments are rarely examined beyond feasibility demonstrations. This paper presents the deployment of Room-Mediated Co-occurrence, an ObjectNav policy that reasons over Room Probability Vectors (RPVs), on two robotic platforms (Boston Dynamics Spot and Clearpath Robotics TurtleBot 4) through a robot-agnostic ROS 2 bridge. We study how these semantic priors generalise to physical environments and describe the adaptations required to transfer RPV from simulation to hardware, covering sensing, localisation, and the action interface. Across 66 trials on Spot, searching for 11 object categories from two starting positions in a university postgraduate research facility, RPV achieves a raw Success Rate (SR) of 0.455. Our analysis identifies undetected glass walls, entry into off-limits areas, limited usable depth range, target size, and mismatch between the room lexicon and physical layout as plausible contributors to the 8.4 percentage-point gap between the real-world SR and the reported simulated SR of 0.539. Code is available at https://github.com/Matthew-K-Chua/rpv-ros2-bridge.

2611.19709.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
2611.19709.abstract: Flow-matching robot policies generate each action chunk through repeated network evaluations, one per denoising step. Cross-cycle caches such as C$^3$ache reuse computation from earlier replanning calls, but whether they beat simply taking fewer steps is unclear. We compare the two in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, on LIBERO-Goal. Two uncached steps keep the success of ten: on all 500 initial states they are non-inferior within two percentage points, for one checkpoint and noise seed. Under PyTorch's default compile mode, they also cut a replanning call on an RTX A6000 from 202 to 92 ms. This leaves little room for caching. A cache that keeps two fresh steps cannot be faster than two uncached steps: every call still encodes the images, runs the video expert and computes those two steps. Caching the first of two steps, refreshed every fourth call, saves at most 11--14% of a call by our cost model. Cached policies are also fragile. Their losses tracked the share of the flow path the cached steps cover: under Fast-WAM's current time shift, C$^3$ache's eight cached steps cover 80% of the path instead of 44%, and the cached policy succeeds on 63% of states against 95% uncached. Resampling the noise on every call cost caches covering 60% or more of the path 14--40 points. These results argue for fewer-step baselines and for testing reuse under the deployed sampler and noise settings. We release our evaluation harness, logs and a checklist.
2611.19709.comment: Honorable Mention at the CoRL 2026 Workshop on Efficient Foundation Models for Real-Time Embodied AI (EEAI). Code and data available at https://github.com/gabhinav001/cache-or-denoise-less

llm.title_ja: キャッシュか、それともデノイズ削減か？フローマッチング型世界行動モデルにおける残差再利用

2611.19703.title: Real-Time Air Pollution Monitoring and Tracking via Adaptive Density-Driven Multi-UAV Coordination
2611.19703.abstract: Accurate and timely air pollution monitoring and tracking are critical for protecting public health and supporting effective environmental management. This paper presents an adaptive Density-Driven Control (D$^2$C) framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions. The proposed framework extends the D$^2$C strategy to guide UAV trajectories based on predictive pollutant propagation and dynamically updated reference densities. A sensor-driven surrogate plume update mechanism is employed, in which reference samples are propagated using locally sensed concentration gradients and wind estimates through gradient attraction, wind advection, inter-sample repulsion, and stochastic diffusion, enabling UAVs to maintain an accurate spatio-temporal representation of the pollution field. The framework utilizes a coordinated structure where individual UAVs share their local measurements with a central coordinator to maintain a unified set of reference samples, facilitating systematic target allocation and trajectory planning. Simulation results under both mild and strong wind conditions demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of Sinkhorn distance. Specifically, in scenarios where the plume drifts beyond a fixed monitoring domain under high-velocity, time-varying wind fields, the tested baseline methods fail to maintain tracking, whereas the proposed D$^2$C framework successfully adapts to the evolving distribution. These findings highlight D$^2$C as an efficient and resilient solution for atmospheric monitoring in dynamic environments.

llm.title_ja: 適応型密度駆動型マルチUAV協調によるリアルタイム大気汚染モニタリングと追跡
llm.tldr_ja: 動的に変化する汚染物質の分布を追跡・マッピングするため、予測的な汚染拡散と動的参照密度に基づく適応型密度駆動制御（D^2C）フレームワークを提案する。
llm.problem: 変動の激しい風環境下で、汚染物質のプルームが固定領域外に流出した際に既存手法が追跡に失敗すること。
llm.method: 局所的な濃度勾配や風推定を用いて参照サンプルを伝播させるセンサー駆動型サロゲートプルーム更新機構を備えた、マルチUAV協調制御フレームワークの構築。
llm.result: 強風環境下でのシミュレーションにおいて、既存手法が追跡に失敗するシナリオでも、D^2Cフレームワークがシンホーン距離の観点で優れた追跡と適応を示した。
keywords_ja: 大気汚染モニタリング

2611.19703.tldr_en: An adaptive Density-Driven Control framework for coordinating multiple unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to track and map dynamically evolving pollutant distributions and highlights D$^2$C as an efficient and resilient solution for atmospheric monitoring in dynamic environments.

2611.19688.title: Physics-Grounded STL Monitoring from Image Observations
2611.19688.abstract: Robotic manipulation missions must satisfy timed and conditional requirements that can be expressed in signal temporal logic (STL). While a practical means of monitoring these requirements is from camera images, this is challenging because STL robustness depends on physical margins, such as distances and clearances, that are not directly observed. Rather than learning a separate visual monitor for each formula, we learn a shared latent representation from multi-view images and decode physically meaningful margins for individual predicates. Co-training the encoder with predicate decoders increases the certification rate from 58.7% to 96.3% compared with a frozen encoder, despite nearly unchanged predicate sign accuracy. STL semantics then compose these margins into robustness estimates for any bounded formula over the trained predicates, without retraining. We further calibrate the decoding errors of selected STL clauses using conformal prediction, yielding two-sided intervals that certify both satisfaction and violation and propagate through interval STL to any formula composed from the clauses. In simulated kitchen missions (LIBERO), our monitor correctly predicts satisfaction or violation in 98.9% of 4662 evaluations across 18 unseen formulas. For missions lasting up to 17 min, calibrated bounds establish satisfaction or violation for 96.9% of missions without incorrect conclusions. A single calibration also provides simultaneous 91.0% coverage across all 255 conjunctions of eight clauses, allowing new formulas without recalibration.

llm.title_ja: 画像観測からの物理接地型STLモニタリング
llm.tldr_ja: マルチビュー画像から共有潜在表現を学習し、個々の述語に対する物理的意味のあるマージンを復元することで、カメラ画像から信号時相論理（STL）の要件を監視する手法を提案する。
llm.problem: カメラ画像からのSTLモニタリングにおいて、STLのロバスト性が直接観測されない物理的マージンに依存していること。
llm.method: エンコーダーと述語デコーダーを共同学習し、共形予測を用いてデコード誤差を較正する物理接地型監視フレームワークの構築。
llm.result: LIBEROのシミュレーション環境において、4,662回の評価のうち98.9%で満足・違反を正しく予測し、長期ミッションでも高い信頼性を示した。

2611.19688.tldr_en: This work learns a shared latent representation from multi-view images and decode physically meaningful margins for individual predicates in signal temporal logic to compose these margins into robustness estimates for any bounded formula over the trained predicates, without retraining.

2611.19684.title: Early Readability of Trajectory Quality in Diffusion Driving Planners
2611.19684.abstract: Diffusion-based driving planners can generate multiple trajectories for the same scene, but these candidates vary in quality. Can their internal states reveal which candidate will be better before denoising is complete? We systematically study this question in three pretrained planners: Alpamayo, ReCogDrive-IL, and HDP, using linear probes to predict final trajectory quality from intermediate states and evaluating candidate ranking and selection on held-out scenes. Across all three planners, we observe that states from the first denoiser evaluation already support informative selection, while further denoising does not consistently improve selection quality. Further analyses show that readout depends on the representation and reader, and that selection can coexist with limited overall ranking accuracy. These findings motivate an early-selection method that selects after the first denoiser evaluation and completes only the chosen candidate. This reduces computation relative to fully denoising every candidate and improves open-loop trajectory quality over random selection across all three planners. In particular, it reduces Alpamayo's average displacement error by 17.8% and 13.4% in one- and four-camera configurations, respectively. Closed-loop evaluations also show higher mean driving scores and progress.

llm.title_ja: 拡散駆動プランナーにおける軌道品質の早期読み取り可能性
llm.tldr_ja: 拡散ベースの駆動プランナーの中間状態からデノイズ完了前に最終的な軌道品質を予測可能であることを示し、計算量を削減する早期選択手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 拡散ベースのプランナーが生成する複数の軌道候補のうち、どれが優れているかをデノイズ完了前に識別できるかが不明であったこと。
llm.method: 3つの事前学習済みプランナーに対し、線形プローブを用いて中間状態から最終品質を予測し、最初のデノイズ評価後に候補を選択する手法の検証。
llm.result: 最初のデノイズ評価後の選択により計算コストが削減され、Alpamayoの平均変位誤差が大幅に改善されるなど開ループ・閉ループ性能が向上した。

2611.19684.tldr_en: An early-selection method is motivated that selects after the first denoiser evaluation and completes only the chosen candidate, which reduces computation relative to fully denoising every candidate and improves open-loop trajectory quality over random selection across all three planners.

2611.19660.title: PSK: A Matrix-Free Single-Loop Method for K-Level Physics-Based Control
2611.19660.abstract: Physics-based control is central to robot learning, but differentiating through implicit physics steps typically requires Hessian or Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) linear solves; we ask whether gradient steps suffice. Each simulation step minimizes an energy under many contact and collision constraints. Without constraints, we view control over $K$ steps as $K$-level optimization with strongly convex lower levels, recast as one min--max problem. Our Penalized Single-loop $K$-level method (PSK) uses only gradients and a projection, updates all levels in parallel, and reaches an $ε$-stationary control in $O(ε^{-3})$ iterations, with a $K$-independent exponent but a $K$-dependent constant. Contact-rich constraints, however, typically violate a constraint qualification (CQ). We replace each constraint by a smooth wall that acts on a band of constant width. Under mild assumptions that need no CQ, every exact solution of the banded lower levels is then feasible and banded Fritz--John, and PSK keeps the $O(ε^{-3})$ complexity. Without a CQ that is uniform in the band width, however, a shrinking band loses the $K$-independent exponent: with width $ε$ and fixed $K\geq2$, deterministic zero-respecting methods need $Ω(ε^{-(K+3)/4})$ calls on a hard instance whose control dimension grows with $1/ε$. We prove our assumptions for smoothed kinematic and dynamic multi-robot navigation among segment obstacles. In navigation experiments, PSK, tuned per case, reaches every goal with sixteen levels and, at equal time, reaches a lower loss than tuned unrolling in 17 of 18 cases, while implicit differentiation is lower in 10.

llm.title_ja: PSK：Kレベル物理ベース制御のためのマトリックスフリー単一ループ法
llm.tldr_ja: 暗黙的な物理ステップの微分を勾配と射影のみで行うKレベル物理ベース制御のための単一ループ法（PSK）を提案し、その収束性と有効性を示した。
llm.problem: 物理ベース制御において、暗黙的な物理ステップの微分にHessianやKKT線形ソルバーが必要となり計算コストが高いこと。
llm.method: Kレベル最適化を1つのミニマックス問題として定式化し、接触制約を滑らかな壁で置き換えて勾配と射影のみで更新するPSK法の開発。
llm.result: ナビゲーション実験において、PSKは調整されたアンローリング手法よりも少ない損失で目標に到達し、優れた性能を発揮した。

2611.19660.tldr_en: The Penalized Single-loop $K$-level method (PSK) is introduced, and the assumptions for smoothed kinematic and dynamic multi-robot navigation among segment obstacles are proved for smoothed kinematic and dynamic multi-robot navigation among segment obstacles.

2611.19621.title: Toward Planning Representations That Separate Task Structure from Visual Content
2611.19621.abstract: Effective planning requires representations that preserve task-relevant geometry and object identity while ignoring visual variation that does not alter the task. Existing evaluations of visual generalization often change several factors simultaneously, making the source of a failure difficult to identify. We introduce a controlled evaluation of object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), the task of reaching an instance of a named object category, in procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses. Training and evaluation houses share floor plans, object locations, goals, and start states, while visual factors are changed individually or in combination. Across model-free reinforcement learning (RL), model-based RL, and agents using frozen pretrained visual representations, our results show that appearance changes impair navigation, but their effects differ sharply by factor. Surface material changes account for most of the average change in success, whereas clutter and lighting have little effect. The magnitude of a global image statistics shift does not reliably predict performance: changing only the goal object's appearance can substantially impair an end-to-end agent despite a small image-level change. We found that a model based agent that plans over frozen features from the pretrained DINOv2 image encoder achieves the highest success (0.83) under the full shift, but remains sensitive to surface appearance. Our experiments reveal an important requirement for planning representations: they must separate invariant spatial task structure from appearance.

llm.title_ja: タスク構造を視覚的内容から分離するプランニング表現に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: ProcTHORの家屋環境を用いてオブジェクト目標ナビゲーション（ObjectNav）における視覚的変化の影響を分析し、不変な空間タスク構造を外観から分離する表現の必要性を示した。
llm.problem: 視覚的汎化の既存の評価では複数の要因が同時に変更されるため、失敗の原因特定が困難であること。
llm.method: モデルフリーRL、モデルベースRL、事前学習済み視覚表現を用いたエージェントを対象に、視覚的要因を個別または組み合わせて変更する制御された評価の実施。
llm.result: 表面素材の変化が成功率低下の大部分を占める一方、DINOv2エンコーダーの凍結特徴量を用いたモデルベースエージェントが最も高い成功率を達成した。
keywords_ja: オブジェクト目標ナビゲーション

2611.19621.tldr_en: This work introduces a controlled evaluation of object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), the task of reaching an instance of a named object category, in procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses, and reveals an important requirement for planning representations: they must separate invariant spatial task structure from appearance.

2611.19616.title: Towards Probabilistically Safe Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Deployment on Humanoid and Aerial Robots
2611.19616.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables robots to acquire complex skills, but standard RL formulations do not guarantee that learned policies satisfy safety constraints, which limits their use in safety-critical settings. Existing safe RL methods with provable guarantees typically support only restricted classes of constraints and require unbiased estimators of the objective and constraint functions, which prevents their direct integration with state-of-the-art algorithms such as proximal policy optimization (PPO). In this paper, we extend the recently introduced robust safe gradient flow-based reinforcement learning (RSGF-RL) framework to overcome these limitations. Our formulation accommodates a general class of trajectory-level safety constraints, including chance constraints such as collision avoidance with a prescribed probability, and our analysis allows for biased value and gradient estimators. We show that, with high probability, the constraint violation throughout training is bounded by the estimator bias plus a term that vanishes as the number of rollouts grows, and decays to this level if the initial policy is unsafe. We also establish the convergence properties of the iterates to approximate KKT points of the original safe RL problem. Finally, we show that RSGF-RL implemented with PPO-style estimates enables zero-shot sim-to-real deployment of whole-body control policies on a Unitree G1 humanoid and collision-free waypoint navigation on a Crazyflie drone.

llm.title_ja: 確率的安全強化学習に向けて：理論とヒューマノイド・空中ロボットへの展開
llm.tldr_ja: バイアスのある推定器を許容し、軌道レベルの安全制約を網羅するロバスト安全勾配流ベース強化学習（RSGF-RL）フレームワークを提案し、実機への展開を実証した。
llm.problem: 標準的な強化学習は安全性制約を満たす保証がなく、既存の安全RL手法は制約クラスが制限され、不偏推定量が必要であること。
llm.method: RSGF-RLフレームワークを拡張してバイアスのある値・勾配推定量に対応させ、PPOスタイルの推定と組み合わせてゼロショットSim-to-Realを実現する。
llm.result: Unitree G1ヒューマノイドでの全身制御ポリシーのゼロショットSim-to-Real展開と、Crazyflieドローンの衝突回避ウェイポイントナビゲーションを達成した。

2611.19616.tldr_en: This paper extends the recently introduced robust safe gradient flow-based reinforcement learning (RSGF-RL) framework and shows that RSGF-RL implemented with PPO-style estimates enables zero-shot sim-to-real deployment of whole-body control policies on a Unitree G1 humanoid and collision-free waypoint navigation on a Crazyflie drone.

2611.19609.title: Before the Word: Name Information in Description-Derived States of Small Language Models, With and Without Naming Failure
2611.19609.abstract: The tip-of-the-tongue (TOT) state, knowing an object but not its name, motivates this study as an analogy only. We ask whether small language models form a name-predictive state from a name-free description, and whether it differs when naming fails but description selection succeeds. In an internally pre-registered study (a frozen document, no external registry) of Qwen2-0.5B, SmolLM2-1.7B and Phi-3-mini with 200 items, we combine a similarity read-out, a Patchscopes-style read-out and activation patching with matched controls. H1 (name information in the state) was supported in all nine model-by-description-type combinations; the agreement rule was met by the similarity measure together with patching, while Patchscopes stayed near chance. Post-hoc robustness checks after internal review (logit lens, single-position patch, manipulation check) temper this reading: name information in middle layers is clearest under the multi-position patch and the similarity measure, and weak under single-position patching at 50% depth. H2' (description-paraphrase consistency of name-free states not lower in failure items) is mixed: the SmolLM2 deficit test is significant under the pre-registered specification but not robust; Phi-3 non-inferiority holds across margins and a word-overlap covariate, although its bootstrap interval includes zero; Qwen2-0.5B is inconclusive. A capacity explanation remains untested. We report vehicle-level signals only, not meaning.
2611.19609.comment: 22 pages, 9 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24228887

llm.title_ja: 言葉の前に：小規模言語モデルの記述由来状態における名前情報（命名失敗の有無にかかわらず）
llm.tldr_ja: 小規模言語モデルが名前のない記述から名前予測状態を形成するかどうかを、類似度読み出しやパッチング手法を用いて検証した。
