llm.method: Qwen2-0.5B、SmolLM2-1.7B、Phi-3-miniを対象に、類似度読み出し、Patchscopesスタイル読み出し、活性化パッチングを組み合わせた検証の実施。
llm.result: 名前情報は中間層においてマルチポジションパッチと類似度測定のもとで最も明確に確認され、モデルや記述タイプによる違いが示された。

2611.19609.tldr_en: It is asked whether small language models form a name-predictive state from a name-free description, and whether it differs when naming fails but description selection succeeds, and whether it differs when naming fails but description selection succeeds.

2611.19572.title: Spectral Steering: Local Inverse Geometry for Frozen Diffusion Generators
2611.19572.abstract: A frozen diffusion generator may need to change several output properties while preserving others. We study when guidance faithfully realizes such a structured request and whether local inverse correction improves its direction. Our account links this benefit to the interaction between the request and the objective-specific remaining-sampler Jacobian: conditioning alone is insufficient. Spectral steering combines a request-specific cosine-gain predictor with damped inverse correction and fixed-time relinearization for finite edits. Scalar nulls and matched-movement controls test the predicted mechanism. Across 8,923 instances in a retrospectively identified local regime, predicted and realized gains correlate at Spearman 0.79, versus -0.11 for condition number. Experiments span images, audio, robotics, and control and planning, including complex character motion generation. On 50 paired inpainting cases, four corrections improve unobserved-pixel PSNR over Adam by 3.25 dB at equal total derivative traversals. Together, the analysis and controls connect request-dependent geometry to directional gains and establish where these gains translate into downstream performance.

llm.title_ja: スペクトルステアリング：凍結された拡散ジェネレータのための局所逆幾何学
llm.tldr_ja: 凍結された拡散ジェネレータにおいて、要求に依存する幾何学と方向的ゲインを結びつけ、構造化された編集を忠実に実現する「スペクトルステアリング」手法を提案する。
llm.problem: 凍結された拡散ジェネレータにおいて、他のプロパティを維持しながら複数の出力プロパティを変更するためのガイダンスの動作条件が不明確であること。
llm.method: 要求固有のコサイン利得予測器とダンピング付き逆補正、固定時間再線形化を組み合わせた「スペクトルステアリング」の提案と検証。
llm.result: 画像、音声、ロボット工学、制御・計画の各領域において、予測された利得と実測された利得が高い相関を示し、インペインティング等の下流性能を向上させた。
keywords_ja: スペクトルステアリング

2611.19572.tldr_en: This account links the interaction between the request and the objective-specific remaining-sampler Jacobian to the interaction between the request and the objective-specific remaining-sampler Jacobian: conditioning alone is insufficient.

2611.19559.title: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
2611.19559.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) augment vision-language-action policies (VLAs) with future prediction so that the policy can anticipate how its actions will affect the physical world. Existing WAMs supervise complete future observations. However, observations typically change little over an action chunk, so the future loss is dominated by copying static background content rather than learning task-relevant robot and object motion, limiting policy learning. Moreover, existing WAMs rely on large video generation models or separate world models, incurring heavy training and inference compute that hinders closed-loop deployment. To improve policy performance, we propose visual residual learning, supervising only the feature change from the current frame to the future frame in a frozen DINOv3 space. Compared with complete future features, this residual learning target yields a higher feature rank with richer and more diverse representations of scene changes, and spatially concentrates on the robot arm and manipulated objects rather than the background. To further improve computational efficiency, we present ResWAM, a residual world-action model with 2.3B parameters in total, including a lightweight 0.5B dual-branch DiT that jointly trains an action branch and a residual branch via conditional flow matching. Without robot pretraining (i.e., pretraining on external robot action trajectories beyond the benchmark demonstrations), ResWAM achieves top average success rates on LIBERO-Plus (81.1%), RoboTwin 2.0 (93.8%), and RoboDojo (9.40% success, 13.41 score) at the lowest training (2.7-4.0 TFLOPs) and inference compute (1.0-1.4 TFLOPs), and leads real-robot Open, Put, and Stack (80.0% average, +10.0% over $π_{0.5}$) at 92.7 ms latency.

llm.title_ja: ResWAM: 世界・行動モデルのための変化する箇所の学習
llm.tldr_ja: 静的な背景ではなくビジュアルの残差変化を学習することで計算効率を高めた世界・行動モデルResWAMを提案し、優れた成功率と低い計算コストを達成した。
llm.problem: 既存の世界・行動モデルは完全な未来の観測を監督するため、静的な背景のコピーに損失が支配され、計算コストも高くロボットの閉ループ制御を妨げている。
llm.method: フリーズしたDINOv3空間において現在フレームから未来フレームへの特徴量変化のみを監督するビジュアル残差学習を導入し、条件付きフローマッチングにより訓練する。
llm.result: LIBERO-Plus等のベンチマークで最高平均成功率を達成しつつ、最低の訓練および推移計算量・実機での優れた性能を実現した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語行動モデル

2611.19559.tldr_en: ResWAM is presented, a residual world-action model with 2.3B parameters in total, including a lightweight 0.5B dual-branch DiT that jointly trains an action branch and a residual branch via conditional flow matching that achieves top average success rates on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin 2, and RoboDojo.
2611.19559.hf_summary_en: ResWAM combines visual residual learning in frozen DINOv3 features with a lightweight dual-branch DiT trained via conditional flow matching to improve vision-language-action policy success while lowering training and inference compute.

2611.19557.title: Steering Bayesian Inference and Decisions through Data Poisoning
2611.19557.abstract: Adversarial machine learning has revealed that statistical models can be manipulated through poisoned data, and Bayesian inference is no exception. Earlier work has shown that subtle poisoning attacks can drive the posterior toward a distribution of the attacker's choosing. Such posterior attraction attacks require a fully specified target posterior; however, attackers typically care about only a few posterior quantities or, more consequentially, about a downstream decision. Herein, we study how an attacker can alter Bayesian inference and decisions by deleting or replicating a few observations, chosen to minimize the maximum mean discrepancy between the resulting posterior and a target distribution. A suitable kernel lets the attacker steer selected posterior moments without specifying the rest of the target. Because Bayes actions depend on the posterior only through expected utilities, which are themselves posterior moments, the same approach can target a decision directly. We construct the attacks with a gradient-based heuristic that requires only posterior samples, and analyze its convergence. Experiments with regression and hierarchical models compare moment-based and full-posterior attacks, and illustrate how deleting a handful of observations can flip a Bayesian decision.

llm.title_ja: データポイズニングを通じたベイズ推論と意思決定の誘導
llm.tldr_ja: 少数の観測データの削除や複製を通じて、目的とする分布との最大平均不一致を最小化し、ベイズ推論や意思決定を誘導する手法を研究した。
llm.problem: 攻撃者は特定の事後分布の数量や下流の意思決定を変化させたいが、既存の事後確率惹起攻撃では完全に指定された目標事後分布が必要となる。
llm.method: 結果としての事後分布と目標分布間の最大平均不一致を最小化するように選択された、少数の観測データの削除や複製を行う手法を研究した。
llm.result: 勾配ベースのヒューリスティックを用いて攻撃を構築し、回帰モデルや階層モデルの実験により少数の観測データ削除でベイズの意思決定を反転できることを示した。

2611.19557.tldr_en: This work studies how an attacker can alter Bayesian inference and decisions by deleting or replicating a few observations, chosen to minimize the maximum mean discrepancy between the resulting posterior and a target distribution.

2611.19535.title: Cooperative Gradient Estimation for Multi-Robot Source Seeking with Heteroskedastic Measurements
2611.19535.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach for localizing the source of a three-dimensional scalar field using a team of heterogeneous cooperative mobile robots. Each robot measures the field intensity at its location and shares the information within the team. Measurement noise is explicitly considered, and heterogeneity arises from robot-dependent sensing accuracies, leading to heteroskedastic data. The proposed framework combines a weighted centroidal Voronoi tessellation-based formation strategy, defined on a spherical surface and parameterized by sensor noise variances, with a Weighted Least Squares estimator to compute the field gradient at the formation center. By explicitly accounting for sensor heterogeneity in both formation design and estimation, the method achieves robust gradient estimation under noisy measurements. In particular, we show analytically that this construction is nearly optimal. The covariance of the gradient estimate is derived in closed form, providing a lower bound on the attainable estimation variance for any formation on the sphere, and the proposed tessellation is shown to asymptotically satisfy the conditions under which this bound is attained. The estimated gradient is then exploited within a gradient-ascent strategy to guide the team toward the source location. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to alternative strategies and highlight its intrinsic ability to reconfigure online in response to robot failures, thereby enhancing its adaptability.
2611.19535.journal_ref: IFAC Journal of Systems and Control, Volume 38, 2026

llm.title_ja: 異質的測定を持つマルチロボットの線源探索に向けた協調的勾配推定
llm.tldr_ja: センサーの不確実性を明示的に考慮し、加重ボロノイ分割ベースのフォーメーションと重み付き最小二乗法を組み合わせて堅牢な勾配推定と線源探索を実現した。
llm.problem: センサー精度の違いによる異質的データや測定ノイズが存在する環境で、マルチロボットによるスカラー場の線源探索を高精度に行う必要がある。
llm.method: センサーノイズ分散でパラメータ化された球面上のフォーメーション戦略と重み付き最小二乗推定量を用いて場の勾配を計算する。
llm.result: 解析的にほぼ最適であることを示し、シミュレーションにより従来戦略に対する有効性やロボット故障時のオンライン再構成能力を実証した。

badges.venue: IFAC Journal of Systems and Control, Vol 2026

2611.19535.tldr_en: Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to alternative strategies and highlight its intrinsic ability to reconfigure online in response to robot failures, thereby enhancing its adaptability.
2611.19535.venue: IFAC Journal of Systems and Control

2611.19534.title: Depth-Aware Path Planning and Collision Avoidance for Robotic Nursing Assistants Using Real-Time 3D Vision
2611.19534.abstract: This paper presents a depth-aware path planning and collision avoidance framework for the safe navigation of robotic nursing assistants in cluttered environments with low-height obstacles. Conventional LiDAR-based navigation systems, while accurate for mapping and localization, fail to detect transparent or low-height obstacles, whereas vision-based systems are prone to noise and occlusion. The proposed framework integrates RGB-D depth sensing, rule-based obstacle avoidance, and the NavfnROS global path planner to drive the robot from an initial point to a goal point. The proposed approach is implemented on the Husky A200 robot, equipped with a Kinova Gen3 arm, to form a complete setup for a robotic nursing assistant. This system features a multi-layer architecture for global planning, perception fusion, and real-time control in the ROS-Gazebo environment. Experimental evaluations in a simulated cluttered environment demonstrate up to 40\% higher success rate and 35\% improvement in minimum clearance compared with single-sensor baselines. Furthermore, real-world experimental results validate the proposed approach as a computationally efficient and safety-aware navigation solution for autonomous healthcare robots.

llm.title_ja: リアルタイム3Dビジョンを用いた看護補助ロボットのための深度を考慮した経路計画と衝突回避
llm.tldr_ja: RGB-D深度センシングとNavfnROSグローバル経路計画を統合し、複雑な環境において安全なナビゲーションを実現するフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 従来のLiDARベースのナビゲーションは透明や低所の障害物を検出できず、ビジョンベースシステムはノイズやオクルージョンに弱い。
llm.method: RGB-D深度センシング、ルールベースの障害物回避、NavfnROSグローバル経路計画を統合したマルチレイヤーアーキテクチャを構築した。
llm.result: シミュレーション環境での評価で単一センサーベースラインと比較して最大40%高い成功率と35%のクリアランス改善を達成し、実機でも有効性を検証した。

2611.19534.tldr_en: A depth-aware path planning and collision avoidance framework for the safe navigation of robotic nursing assistants in cluttered environments with low-height obstacles and real-time control in the ROS-Gazebo environment is presented.

2611.19469.title: Representing Differential Inclusions as Monads: A Framework for Compositional Controller Synthesis
2611.19469.abstract: Sequential composition of safety-certified controllers for hybrid and non-smooth robotic systems is well studied piecewise. Yet no existing framework reduces this question to a single algebraic condition. We construct a \emph{trajectory monad} for Filippov-regular differential inclusions. Its Kleisli category treats controllers as morphisms and sequential execution as trajectory concatenation. Control Barrier Function (CBF) certification, a guarantee of forward invariance, corresponds to a sub-monad of this category. Joint safety of composed controllers then follows from one algebraic condition. All controllers must land in a common sub-monad, which is closed under the monad multiplication. The sub-monad condition recasts recasts existing CBF composition practice categorically. It explains why a smooth intersection of multiple barriers supports safe composition, while enforcing barriers phase by phase does not. For the phase-by-phase case, we derive a closed-form Bernoulli model of the failure rate. We validate it over a randomized sweep of 3{,}000 instances. The same sweep shows that the standard baseline degrades under constraint conflict as the barrier count grows. This baseline enforces all barriers simultaneously as constraints in a single quadratic program (QP). We instantiate the framework on a four-mode piecewise-affine system and on a unicycle reduced-order model over heterogeneous terrain.

llm.title_ja: 微分包摂のモナド表現：構成的コントローラ合成のためのフレームワーク
llm.tldr_ja: フィリッポフ正則微分包摂のための軌跡モナドを構築し、制御バリア関数の合成と安全性の保証を単一の代数条件に還元した。
llm.problem: ハイブリッドおよび非スムースなロボットシステムに対する安全性認証済みコントローラの逐次合成について、単一の代数条件に還元する既存の枠組みが存在しない。
llm.method: フィリッポフ正則微分包摂に対する軌跡モナドを構築し、制御バリア関数の保証をサブモナドとして捉えることで単一の代数条件による安全性を導出した。
llm.result: 連続的なバリアの滑らかな交差が安全な構成を支持する理由を説明し、4モードの区分的アフィンシステム等で検証した。

2611.19469.tldr_en: Ajectory monad for Filippov-regular differential inclusions for Filippov-regular differential inclusions, which explains why a smooth intersection of multiple barriers supports safe composition, while enforcing barriers phase by phase does not.

2611.19466.title: Successive Convexification in Learned World Models for Safe Offline Planning
2611.19466.abstract: World models learned from offline data allow an agent to plan without further interaction with the environment, but the sampling-based planners used with them handle safety constraints only by scoring or rejecting sampled action sequences. We instead pose safe planning in the latent space of a learned world model as a successive convex program (SCP), in which a learned discrete-time control barrier function is imposed as a constraint at every step of the horizon. SCP requires smooth dynamics, so we build the networks from smoothed MaxMin activations and spectrally normalised layers, and bound the resulting linearisation error in terms of the Lipschitz bound and the smoothing width. As SCP is a local method, we start it from a sampled plan. On two Safety-Gymnasium navigation tasks with offline data, this planner has fewer violations than MPPI and CEM drawing 128 times as many samples at equal wall-clock time in our main comparison, though not significantly, and earns greater return at longer horizons, and is much safer than SCP without a sampled start. SCP converged more often on Lipschitz-bounded models. Unlike sampling, it also reports at each step whether its plan is a feasible, first-order optimal KKT point of the planning problem in the model, or that no feasible plan was found nearby. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/youngers2006/scwm.
2611.19466.comment: 28 pages, 13 figures. Under review at L4DC 2027

llm.title_ja: 安全なオフライン計画のための学習済み世界モデルにおける逐次凸化
llm.tldr_ja: 学習済み世界モデルの潜在空間における安全な計画を逐次凸プログラムとして定式化し、安全性の向上と制約違反の削減を実現した。
llm.problem: オフラインデータから学習した世界モデルを用いるサンプリングベースのプランナーは、安全制約の処理がサンプリングされた行動列のスコアリングや棄却のみに依存している。
llm.method: 平滑化された活性化関数を用いたネットワークで滑らかなダイナミクスを構築し、学習済み制御バリア関数を制約として課す逐次凸プログラムとして安全計画を定式化した。
llm.result: Safety-Gymnasiumのタスクにおいて、MPPIやCEMと比較して同等の計算時間でより少ない違反数と長いホライゾンでの高い報酬を達成した。

2611.19466.tldr_en: This work poses safe planning in the latent space of a learned world model as a successive convex program (SCP), in which a learned discrete-time control barrier function is imposed as a constraint at every step of the horizon.

2611.19463.title: Semantics First, Pixels Later: Mission-Driven Event Streams for Drone Video over Bandwidth-Starved Links
2611.19463.abstract: A surveillance drone on a bandwidth-starved link cannot send the video its operator would need, yet the operator's questions are often not about pixels: did three people converge, when, and where? We study what should cross a link of 1 Mbps down to 1 kbps instead, and in what order. BPS, a behavior-primitive stream, sends semantics first and pixels later: it runs a detector and a tracker onboard and sends short records (25 bytes on average) of multi-frame events selected by a mission card of 16-125 bytes, ahead of positions and pictures. We measure it by what a ground-side language model answers from it, under a preregistered protocol with a held-out set, against H.265 read by the vision fine-tune of the same model, H.265 on which the ground runs our own perception, a stream of quantized tracks, and onboard captions. On the development set (84% of questions about convergence, mostly one location) the event stream answers 74.3% of questions at 0.13 kbps. A reader that receives nothing answers 57.4%, and the video reader 59.6% at 100 kbps and 64.7% on the source frames. When the ground instead runs our perception on the video, video matches the stream at 100 kbps, about 800 times the stream's rate, and falls behind at 64 kbps and below. A track stream matches it at 96 times the bytes and loses 0.03 at 17 times. On held-out data the result is weaker: with events taken from annotated tracks, an oracle, the stream beats H.265 at 100 kbps (+0.13), but with onboard perception it does not (+0.01 [-0.04, +0.06]) and is no better than receiving nothing. Sent alone through emulated links the event records answer 0.739 at 1 Mbps and still 0.724 at 0.3 kbps; an every-frame track stream holds down to 1 kbps and video with ground-side perception down to about 100 kbps. On a Jetson Orin Nano the unchanged pipeline runs at 4.5 fps and misses most events.
2611.19463.comment: 20 pages, 3 figures; includes the supplementary material as an appendix; a demonstration video is attached as an ancillary file

llm.title_ja: セマンティクスが先、ピクセルは後：帯域幅の限られたリンクにおけるドローン映像のためのミッション駆動型イベントストリーム
llm.tldr_ja: 限られた帯域幅環境においてピクセルではなく多フレームイベントの短い記録を優先して送信し、言語モデルでの質問回答性能を維持するストリーム手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 帯域幅の限られたリンク上の監視ドローンは十分な映像を送信できず、オペレーターの質問もピクセルそのものではなくイベントの発生時刻や場所にある。
llm.method: 検出器と追跡器をオンボードで実行し、ミッションカードによって選択された多フレームイベントの短い記録を位置や画像に先行して送信するBPSを提案した。
llm.result: 低帯域幅環境においても、動画ストリームと同等以上の質問回答精度を極めて低いデータレートで達成できることを確認した。

2611.19440.title: Few-Shot Visual Concept Extraction for Steering Diffusion Transformers
2611.19440.abstract: Image steering aims to provide fine-grained control over concepts in generated images, enabling targeted and continuous manipulation without broadly altering the generation process. Recent steering methods for diffusion models primarily focus on the text-conditioning space or rely on costly auxiliary training. Deviating from that, we here propose a novel steering approach that extracts visual concept directions directly from the image-side activations of Diffusion Transformers. Specifically, we showcase few-shot concept extraction in the activation space using a simple difference-of-means estimator over intermediate residuals. We observe (a) scene-level concepts such as lighting, weather, and style are distributed across image tokens, as well as (b) local concepts such as object colors, textures, materials, and facial attributes are concentrated in specific regions. Towards controlling both concepts, we introduce a new unified training-free framework that uses global difference-of-means for (a) distributed concepts and masked difference-of-means for (b) local concepts, preventing local signals from being diluted by global averaging. Notably, using only a handful of positive and negative prompt pairs, our method identifies and extracts reusable concept directions that can be injected at inference for continuous steering. Quantitatively, our method outperforms text-encoder steering and training-free activation-editing baselines, as well as is competitive with specialized editing models. Our results suggest that as concept directions can be applied at patch level, our method enables precise targeted and compositional steering, manipulating multiple concepts in the same image.

llm.title_ja: 拡散トランスフォーマを制御するための少数ショット視覚的概念抽出
llm.tldr_ja: 拡散トランスフォーマの活性化空間から少数ショットで視覚的概念方向を抽出し、追加の学習なしで画像生成をきめ細かく制御する手法を提案した。
llm.problem: 画像のきめ細かい制御を行う既存のステアリング手法は、テキスト条件付け空間に依存するか、コストのかかる追加学習を必要とする。
llm.method: 中間残差に対する単純な平均差分推定量を用いて、活性化空間における少数ショットの概念抽出を行い、大域的および局所的概念を統合的に制御するフレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: 少数のプロンプトペアを用いて再利用可能な概念方向を特定し、テキストエンコーダ制御や従来の活性化編集ベースラインを量的・質的に上回る性能を示した。

2611.19440.tldr_en: A novel steering approach that extracts visual concept directions directly from the image-side activations of Diffusion Transformers, and outperforms text-encoder steering and training-free activation-editing baselines, as well as is competitive with specialized editing models.

2611.19387.title: Long-Horizon Causal Inertial Odometry in Multistory Buildings
2611.19387.abstract: In indoor 3D localization inside multistory buildings, an elevator or an escalator accelerates for a few seconds and then cruises at constant velocity for tens of seconds. Gait excitation disappears, the specific force degenerates into a constant gravity reaction, and instantaneous velocity becomes unobservable within a 1-2 s window. The output of short-window learned inertial odometry consequently degrades toward the conditional mean of the training set, and vertical displacement is systematically underestimated. We propose Local-Token Causal Attention (LTCA), a long-horizon architecture that compresses each 1 s inertial window into a 1 Hz motion token and sustains, over a bounded 60 s causal cache, the motion state established at the onset event. We further introduce a pluggable barometer branch that, when online, supplies a direct elevation constraint to the vertical channel through local differential height observations, and we train it with paired online/fallback conditional training so that the barometer also regularizes the representation shared by the two modes during training. On MSIO, our benchmark of nine buildings, the RoNIN and TLIO instances reach 3D trajectory errors (ATE-3D) of 2.83/4.18 m and 2.44/5.12 m on the Seen and Unseen splits, respectively, with the barometer online. With the barometer disabled at inference, the same weights fall back to pure inertial inference and reach 3.24/4.28 m and 2.64/5.23 m, still below every native short-window baseline. We further validate the framework on the public RoNIN and TLIO benchmarks.

llm.title_ja: 多層階ビルにおける長期因果的慣性オドメトリ
llm.tldr_ja: 長期因果的アテンションと気圧計ブランチを組み合わせることで、多層階ビルにおける慣性オドメトリの垂直方向の変位の過小評価や劣化を抑制した。
llm.problem: 屋内多層階ビルではエレベーター等での加速後に定速走行となり歩行励振が消えるため、短窓の学習済み慣性オドメトリでは速度が観測不能となり垂直変位が過小評価される。
llm.method: 各1秒の慣性ウィンドウをモーション・トークンに圧縮し長期キャッシュで維持する局所トークン因果アテンション（LTCA）と、気圧計ブランチを導入した。
llm.result: 9棟のビルからなるベンチマークにおいて、SeenおよびUnseenの分割で優れた3次元軌跡誤差を達成し、気圧計なしの純粋な慣性推論でもベースラインを上回った。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.19387.tldr_en: Local-Token Causal Attention (LTCA), a long-horizon architecture that compresses each 1 s inertial window into a 1 Hz motion token and sustains, over a bounded 60 s causal cache, the motion state established at the onset event, is proposed.

2611.19381.title: AcousticBEV: Acoustic BEV Object Localization for Intelligent Vehicles
2611.19381.abstract: Modern autonomous driving and driver assistance systems rely predominantly on cameras, radars and LiDARs for environmental perception. However, these modalities face different environmental limitations, including poor illumination for cameras and adverse weather for LiDAR. Acoustic sensing, particularly using microphone arrays, could provide complementary perception capabilities for autonomous driving, but has remained largely underexplored. In this work, we design a horizontally arranged microphone array that functions as the "ears" of a vehicle, enabling localization of nearby moving vehicles in a bird's-eye view (BEV) representation that captures both their relative direction and distance. Using this array, we collect a real-world driving dataset, AcousticScenes, which contains 2,117 static and 2,863 dynamic samples with synchronized spatial acoustic signals, LiDAR point clouds and 3D bounding box annotations. Building on this dataset, we propose AcousticBEV, a learning-based method for acoustic BEV object localization, which estimates the center locations of moving traffic participants in BEV from the microphone-array signals, conditioned on the ego vehicle's own speed. Experimental results demonstrate that AcousticBEV outperforms both classical signal-processing baselines and other learning-based methods, achieving F1 scores of $47.7 \pm 1.2$% on "Easy" scenarios and $45.1 \pm 1.4$% on "Difficult" cases. Our findings demonstrate that acoustic signals from a low-cost, vehicle-mounted microphone array can localize nearby moving vehicles in both azimuth and distance.
2611.19381.comment: Ziang Liu and Shiming Wang have equal contributions. Shiming Wang is the project lead

llm.title_ja: AcousticBEV: 知能自動車のための音響BEV物体ローカライゼーション
llm.tldr_ja: 車載マイクアレイを用いて周囲の移動車両の相対方向と距離を鳥瞰図表現で推定する学習ベースの手法AcousticBEVを提案した。
llm.problem: 自動運転の環境知覚の主軸であるカメラ、レーダー、LiDARは、それぞれ悪天候や照明不足といった環境的制約に直面している。
llm.method: 水平方向に配置したマイクロフォンアレイにより空間音響信号を収集するデータセットを構築し、自車両の速度を条件としてマイク信号からBEV上の物体中心位置を推定する学習手法を提案した。
llm.result: 古典的な信号処理ベースラインや他の学習手法を上回り、イージーなシナリオとディフィカルトなシナリオの両方で高いF1スコアを達成した。
keywords_ja: センサーフュージョン

2611.19381.tldr_en: A horizontally arranged microphone array that functions as the "ears" of a vehicle is designed, enabling localization of nearby moving vehicles in a bird's-eye view (BEV) representation that captures both their relative direction and distance.

2611.19332.title: NI-ACT: A Neural Intent Interface for Brain-Embodied Manipulation
2611.19332.abstract: Intracortical brain-computer interfaces can drive robotic arms, but they keep the user inside the fast sensorimotor loop: every approach, correction, and grasp must be neurally specified. Whether intracortical population activity can instead serve as a task-level condition for a learned embodied policy, without symbolic commands or hand-designed skill libraries, remains unknown. NI-ACT addresses this question with a hierarchical brain-embodied framework: a brief motor-cortical signal is read once as a persistent intent, and a visuomotor policy then closes the perception-action loop from vision and proprioception. In a counterfactual grasping task where the scene cannot specify the target, the neural intent alone determined which object the robot grasped; replacing the intent changed the behavior accordingly. Passing the full population latent as a dedicated intent token, rather than a one-hot decoded direction, raised grasp completion from 69% to 81% over 132 held-out scenes, whereas a continuous direction alone did not improve on a one-hot label. Where the signal was read also mattered: in one dual-array session, with the readout window matched, premotor (PMd) intent completed more grasps than primary motor (M1) intent (77% vs. 53%), and the conventional post-cue M1 readout reached 42%. Preparatory activity was itself sufficient: in a center-out task, intent read only from PMd before the go cue (that is, before any movement) drove complete grasps, and in one recording it completed more grasps than the same animal's post-cue readout. These results show that how a neural signal is represented, and where and when it is read, jointly determine how effectively it conveys movement goals to an embodied agent.

llm.title_ja: NI-ACT: 脳・身体統合マニピュレーションのための神経意図インターフェース
llm.tldr_ja: 大脳皮質運動野の信号をタスクレベルの条件として視覚・固有受容感覚ポリシーに統合し、脳信号のみでロボットアームの把持対象を決定する階層的フレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 皮質脳コンピューターインターフェースはロボットアームを駆動できるが、ユーザーが把持や接近などの高速な感覚運動ループに常時関与し続ける必要がある。
llm.method: 短時間の運動皮質信号を永続的な意図として一度だけ読み取り、ビジョン・固有受容感覚ループを閉じる視覚運動ポリシーを構築した。
llm.result: 潜在表現を意図トークンとして渡すことで把持完了率が大幅に向上し、運動前野（PMd）からの意図読み取りが1次運動野（M1）よりも高い把持性能を達成することを示した。
keywords_ja: 脳波インターフェース
ブレイン・コンピュータ・インタフェース

2611.19332.tldr_en: Results show that how a neural signal is represented, and where and when it is read, jointly determine how effectively it conveys movement goals to an embodied agent.

2611.19324.title: MARS: Dynamic Routing of Reinforcement-Learned Atomic Skills for Multi-Stage Robotic Manipulation
2611.19324.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated strong capabilities in multi-task robotic manipulation. However, they still face limitations in control precision and execution stability during critical manipulation stages, such as object grasping, alignment and insertion. To combine general-purpose manipulation capabilities with task-specific fine-grained control, while enabling effective coordination between generalist and specialized policies throughout multi-stage manipulation tasks, this paper proposes MARS (Modular Atomic-skill Routing System), a dynamic routing framework for reinforcement learning-based atomic skills. MARS integrates a frozen generalist VLA policy with multiple independently trained atomic skill policies. Using a shared RL Token state representation and the reference action of VLA, specialized control policies are optimized through reinforcement learning for different cr`itical manipulation stages. For high-level policy selection, we develop a dynamic router that integrates temporal context and skill semantics. The router employs Mamba-based recurrent encoding and a historical feature window to capture state evolution during manipulation. Skill descriptions of candidate policies are encoded into semantic queries, and attention mechanisms are used to establish correspondences between skill semantics and temporal state features. Experimental results show that MARS achieves an average Macro-F1 score of 90.47% across four LIBERO task suites under fixed-trajectory evaluation, outperforming an MLP-based router by 7.08 percentage points. In the simulated Tube Transport task, the full-task success rate increases from 20.04% to 85.67%. These results demonstrate that stage-specific reinforcement learning and temporal state-aware dynamic policy routing can improve multi-policy coordination and overall task execution performance in multi-stage robotic manipulation.

llm.title_ja: MARS: 多段階ロボットマニピュレーションのための強化学習済みアトミック・スキルの動的ルーティング
llm.tldr_ja: 汎用VLAポリシーと強化学習済みのアトミック・スキルポリシーを時間的コンテキストと意味論に基づいて動的にルーティングするフレームワークMARSを提案した。
llm.problem: ビジョン言語行動モデルは多タスクロボットマニピュレーションで強力だが、把持や挿入などの重要な段階における制御精度や実行安定性に限界がある。
llm.method: 凍結した汎用VLAと複数の専門スキルポリシーを統合し、Mambaベースのエンコーダーとアテンション機構を用いた動的ルーターによりタスクの進捗に応じたルーティングを行う。
llm.result: LIBEROタスクスイートで高いMacro-F1スコアを達成し、Tube Transportシミュレーションタスクで成功率を大幅に向上させた。

2611.19324.tldr_en: The results demonstrate that stage-specific reinforcement learning and temporal state-aware dynamic policy routing can improve multi-policy coordination and overall task execution performance in multi-stage robotic manipulation.

2611.19318.title: Residual Reinforcement Learning for Visual Servo Control with Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer
2611.19318.abstract: We address tracking a moving object on a conveyor with a Franka Emika Panda robot arm, despite an imprecise digital twin, measurement errors, and noise. Our novel approach augments a loop-shaped inverse-Jacobian PI controller with a residual policy learned via Soft Actor-Critic in the digital twin. A delay-compensated Kalman filter fuses out-of-sequence camera measurements to provide latency-aware moving target position estimates. We compare the achieved performance to a performance bound for a class of model-based controllers derived from a frequency-domain sensitivity analysis, quantifying the minimum achievable error imposed by uncertain kinematic model mismatch. Simulation and hardware experiments indicate that our residual policy drives tracking error below the bound. Across conveyor speeds (27.9-41.8 mm/s), our method reduces mean tracking errors from 1.1-1.4 mm (baseline inverse-Jacobian PI) to 0.3-0.7 mm. These results show that learning residual corrections in a limited-fidelity simulator, combined with delay compensation, can substantially improve model-based control under modeling and measurement uncertainties while maintaining reliable sim-to-real transfer.
2611.19318.comment: This manuscript is currently under review in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)

llm.title_ja: ゼロショットSim-to-Real転移を用いたビジュアルサーボ制御のための残差強化学習
llm.tldr_ja: 不完全なデジタルツイン上でのソフトアクター・クリティックを用いた残差ポリシーにより、モデルベース逆ヤコビアンPIコントローラの追従誤差を大幅に削減した。
llm.problem: 不完全なデジタルツイン、測定誤差、ノイズが存在する環境で、コンベア上の移動物体を高精度に追従する必要がある。
llm.method: 逆ヤコビアンPIコントローラに、デジタルツイン上で学習した残差ポリシーを組み合わせ、遅延補償カルマンフィルターによってカメラ測定を融合する。
llm.result: コンベア速度の変化に対する平均追従誤差を大幅に削減し、限定的忠実度のシミュレータでの学習と遅延補償がモデルベース制御を改善することを示した。

2611.19318.tldr_en: The results show that learning residual corrections in a limited-fidelity simulator, combined with delay compensation, can substantially improve model-based control under modeling and measurement uncertainties while maintaining reliable sim-to-real transfer.

2611.19287.title: VLN-Flash: Parallel Action Decoding with Adaptive Execution for Vision-and-Language Navigation
2611.19287.abstract: When a vision-and-language navigation policy generates an action sequence autoregressively, the robot waits for a chain of dependent predictions. A small discrete action vocabulary makes it possible to score all short-horizon plans in parallel. We introduce VLN-Flash, a training-free decoder that evaluates the complete action-prefix tree in a single forward pass. Branch-specific attention and matched token positions preserve the original policy's conditional action distribution for each prefix in exact arithmetic. We use the score margin between the stepwise-greedy prefix and its strongest alternative at each depth to decide how many actions to execute. The robot then executes the plan with the highest joint score at the chosen depth before observing again. On matched inputs, VLN-Flash achieves a nearly $3\times$ speedup in action decoding over native autoregression on Uni-NaVid and StreamVLN. Compared with the native autoregressive decoders, it improves success rate and success weighted by path length (SPL) on R2R-CE and RxR-CE, with success gains up to 2.7 percentage points. On a Unitree GO2, VLN-Flash improves navigation success and cuts the mean wait between actions by about 160 ms after subtracting network transmission time.

llm.title_ja: VLN-Flash: 視覚言語ナビゲーションのための適応型実行を伴う並列行動デコード
llm.tldr_ja: 完全な行動プレフィックス木を単一のフォワードパスで評価するトレーニング不要のデコーダーVLN-Flashにより、自律ナビゲーションの行動デコードを高速化し成功率を向上させた。
llm.problem: 視覚言語ナビゲーションポリシーが自己回帰的に行動列を生成すると、ロボットは従属的な予測の連鎖を待つ必要が生じる。
llm.method: 小さな離散行動語彙を利用して行動プレフィックス木全体を単一フォワードパスで評価し、スコアの余裕度に基づいて実行すべき行動数を決定する。
llm.result: Uni-NaVidやStreamVLNにおいて自己回帰と比較して約3倍の高速化を達成し、R2R-CEや実機のUnitree GO2でナビゲーション成功率の向上と待機時間の短縮を実現した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン言語ナビゲーション

2611.19287.tldr_en: This work introduces VLN-Flash, a training-free decoder that evaluates the complete action-prefix tree in a single forward pass, and uses the score margin between the stepwise-greedy prefix and its strongest alternative at each depth to decide how many actions to execute.

2611.18562.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
2611.18562.abstract: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

llm.title_ja: シミュレーション内での強化学習によるオープンウェイト推論モデルの実機ロボット直接制御の学習
llm.tldr_ja: オープンウェイトの27B推論モデルを、実演データなし・完全シミュレーション上の強化学習により、実機ロボットをネイティブに制御できるよう訓練した。
llm.problem: オープンウェイトのロボット用エージェントモデルは、プロプライエタリなフロンティアモデルに比べて性能が大幅に劣っている。
llm.method: PEAR（Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics）を構築し、ロボット利用強化学習（RURL）を用いてシミュレーション環境でモデルを大規模に訓練した。
llm.result: LIBEROおよびRoboDojoでの訓練後、実機デュアルアームロボットでの試行の60%で成功し、LIBEROでは成功率が1.6%から74.4%に向上した。
keywords_ja: ロボット用エージェント

2611.18562.tldr_en: It is shown that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations, and finds that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks.

2611.18546.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
2611.18546.abstract: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption. This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots. Additionally, real-time implementation of this model can be achieved, meeting the demand for computational efficiency in robotic applications. Experimental validations demonstrated that this model is able to reduce the maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm in the frictionless model to 5.85 mm in our friction-included model with a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot.
2611.18546.comment: Accepted for publication in International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR). 21 pages, 18 figures

llm.title_ja: 線形相補性問題を用いた連続体ロボットと環境の摩擦接触モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: クーロン摩擦を仮定した相補性制約に基づく新しい摩擦モデルを提案し、連続体ロボットの静摩擦・動摩擦やヒステリシス、変形を予測できるようにした。
llm.problem: 現在の手法ではクーロン摩擦円錐の境界力に制限された内部摩擦しか予測できず、静摩擦や運動ヒステリシスを特徴づけられない。
llm.method: クーロン摩擦の仮定のもとで相補性制約に基づく新しい摩擦モデルを提案し、実時間での実装を実現した。
llm.result: 摩擦なしモデルでは45.4 mmであった最大先端位置誤差が、摩擦考慮モデルでは5.85 mmに減少した。

2611.18546.venue: The international journal of robotics research

2611.18505.title: Disturbance-Aware Informative Planning in Spatiotemporal Environments
2611.18505.abstract: Autonomous robots are widely used for persistent monitoring of spatiotemporal environments, where quantities of interest (QoI) change across space and time and require repeated measurements. In practice, robot motion can be affected by external disturbances that vary across the environment. When such external disturbances are not considered in trajectory optimization, it can lead to inaccurate predictions of robot motion and, consequently, the information acquired about the QoI during execution. However, estimating disturbances throughout the environment can be inefficient, as disturbances in regions with little overlap with monitoring trajectories have limited impact on monitoring performance. We therefore propose a two-stage informative planning framework for unknown, spatially varying but time-invariant disturbances, combining informed disturbance sampling with disturbance-aware trajectory optimization. First, we identify where QoI measurements are needed and generate alternative paths to these locations using the environment geometry. We then prioritize disturbance measurements based on their expected reduction of disturbance uncertainty along these paths. Second, rather than optimizing information acquisition based on nominal robot motion, we incorporate the learned disturbance belief into trajectory optimization to account for its effects on robot motion and information acquisition. Across four simulation scenarios, the proposed method reduces disturbance-learning time by 25.0--52.3 percent compared with environment-wide estimation and identifies paths that appear costly under nominal dynamics but become preferable when disturbances are considered.
2611.18505.comment: Submitted to Learning for Dynamics and Control Conference 2027. Project website: https://kalebbennaveed.github.io/dist-aware-ipp/

llm.title_ja: 時空間環境における外乱を考慮した情報的プランニング
llm.tldr_ja: 未知の空間変動・時間不変の外乱に対応するため、情報的な外乱サンプリングと外乱を考慮した軌道最適化を組み合わせた2段階のプランニングフレームワークを提案した。
llm.problem: 外乱を考慮せずに軌道最適化を行うと、ロボットの運動予測が不正確になり、実行時に得られる情報の精度が低下する。
llm.method: 環境形状を用いて代替パスを生成し外乱測定を優先度付けする段階と、学習した外乱の信念を軌道最適化に組み込む段階の2段階フレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: 4つのシミュレーションシナリオにおいて、環境全体での推定と比較して外乱学習時間を25.0〜52.3%削減した。

2611.18505.tldr_en: This work proposes a two-stage informative planning framework for unknown, spatially varying but time-invariant disturbances, combining informed disturbance sampling with disturbance-aware trajectory optimization, and incorporates the learned disturbance belief into trajectory optimization to account for its effects on robot motion and information acquisition.

2611.18501.title: In Situ Monitoring and Predictive Modeling of Harmful Algal Blooms with Autonomous Surface Vehicles
2611.18501.abstract: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. This paper presents an autonomous surface vessel-based sensing system for in-situ water-quality monitoring related to harmful algal bloom detection. The system integrates a BlueBoat Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV), a motorized winch for depth-controlled sonde deployment, a multiparameter water-quality sonde, side-scan sonar, and an event-camera payload. Autonomous waypoint missions were used to collect measurements across selected sampling regions and multiple depths, enabling both horizontal and vertical characterization of environmental conditions. Field deployments were conducted in Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana, with additional measurements collected in False River, Louisiana to increase dataset diversity. The collected measurements included algal pigment indicators, nutrient concentration, turbidity, temperature, and other water-quality parameters relevant to bloom formation. In addition, complementary sonar and event-camera data were collected during vehicle operation to provide contextual environmental information. A machine-learning classification approach was also evaluated using the collected water-quality measurements to support HAB and non-HAB classification. The results demonstrate the feasibility of using a modular ASV platform for repeatable, multi-modal water-quality data collection and support future development of autonomous monitoring systems.

llm.title_ja: 自律型水上艇を用いた有害藍藻ブルームの現場モニタリングと予測モデリング
llm.tldr_ja: 有害藍藻ブルーム（HAB）検出のための水質モニタリングを目的として、深度制御可能なウィンチやマルチパラメータ・ゾンデ、ソナー、イベントカメラを統合した自律型水上艇（ASV）センシングシステムを開発した。
llm.problem: 有害藍藻ブルームは環境・経済・公衆衛生上の大きな課題であり、空間的に分散した水質データを収集するスケーラブルな手法が求められている。
llm.method: BlueBoat ASVに深度制御ウィンチ付き水質ゾンデ、サイドスキャンソナー、イベントカメラを搭載し、自律的なウェイポイントミッションで水平・垂直方向のデータを収集した。
llm.result: モジュール式ASVプラットフォームを用いた再現性の高いマルチモーダルな水質データ収集の実行可能性を示し、機械学習によるHAB分類も評価した。

2611.18496.title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
2611.18496.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific research by integrating robotics, automated experimentation, and machine learning to execute experiments autonomously. Biology and chemistry have adopted these systems. However, increasing SDL complexity heightens susceptibility to unexpected faults in automated workflows, highlighting the need for efficient recovery mechanisms. In this study, we investigate telerobotic interventions to enhance SDL resilience against unexpected failures. We developed a teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks. The interface enables precise control of a six-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm (UR3e) using a 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro). Two velocity-based controller strategies were evaluated: (i) a coupled mode mapping all six DOFs to the 3D mouse's central knob and (ii) a decoupled mode separating translational and rotational motions. To evaluate the framework, teleoperators intervened across three SDL fault scenarios. In the first study, comparative trials showed that the decoupled controller was associated with shorter completion times and reduced rotational motion. In a second study, teleoperators performed an aiming task with and without reference-path guidance. Users were more target-driven and risk-tolerant without guidance but showed behavioral differences under different guidance strategies. These findings suggest that controller configuration and reference-path design influence operator performance during SDL fault recovery, informing teleoperation interface optimization. This work demonstrates the potential feasibility of teleoperation as a human-in-the-loop recovery mechanism for SDL workflows, combining robotic precision with human adaptability and problem-solving. These findings also provide a foundation for future studies in shared autonomy and semi-autonomous intervention.

llm.title_ja: テレロボティック介入を通じたレジリエントなセルフドライビングラボの実現に向けて
llm.tldr_ja: セルフドライビングラボ（SDL）の予期せぬ故障に対するレジリエンスを高めるため、3Dマウスを用いた6自由度ロボットアームの遠隔操作インターフェースと2つの速度ベース制御戦略を評価した。
llm.problem: SDLの複雑化に伴い自動化ワークフローにおける予期せぬ故障へのsusceptibilityが高まるため、効率的なリカバリメカニズムが必要である。
llm.method: UR3eロボットアームと3Dマウスを組み合わせた遠隔操作インターフェースを開発し、結合モードと分離モードの2つの速度ベースコントローラーを評価した。
llm.result: 分離型コントローラーは完了時間が短く回転動作が少ないこと、また参照パスガイダンスの有無がオペレーターの行動に影響を与えることが示された。
keywords_ja: セルフドライビングラボ
ヒューマンインザループ

2611.18496.tldr_en: A teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks, combining robotic precision with human adaptability and problem-solving is developed, demonstrating the potential feasibility of teleoperation as a human-in-the-loop recovery mechanism for SDL workflows.

2611.18491.title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
2611.18491.abstract: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed). We introduce hidden start-delay randomisation (HSD), a one-line rule on the learned partner that the receiver never observes. After 300 further updates, success with unseen scripted partners rises from 31% to 80% in both seeds, against 35--41% for a budget-matched control. The gain holds on a fresh scenario seed, on eleven held-out partner conditions and on partners that start later than any training delay; it cuts high-force contact three- to five-fold and needs no retraining of the partner.
2611.18491.comment: CoRL 2026, Human-Centered Robot Learning and Interaction (HumanRLI) Workshop. Code: https://github.com/mkhoshnam/Selfplay-PPO-handover

llm.title_ja: いつ受け渡すのか？隠れた開始遅延のランダム化により自己対戦型受け渡しを未知のパートナーに対してロバストにする
llm.tldr_ja: ヒューマノイドの自己対戦型物体受け渡しポリシーが未知のパートナーに対して機能しなくなる原因を特定し、学習された提供者側に「隠れた開始遅延のランダム化（HSD）」を導入することで成功率を大幅に向上させた。
llm.problem: 自己対戦で訓練された流暢な受け渡しポリシーは、訓練時に使用したのとは異なる未知のパートナーに出会うと破綻する。
llm.method: 報酬共有により提供者が即座に開始してしまうことが原因であると特定し、受動側からは観測できない隠れた開始遅延ランダム化（HSD）を導入した。
llm.result: 未知のスクリプト化されたパートナーに対する成功率が、両方のシードで31%から80%に向上した。

2611.18491.tldr_en: It is shown that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it, and hidden start-delay randomisation (HSD) is introduced, a one-line rule on the learned partner that the receiver never observes.

2611.18484.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
2611.18484.abstract: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. Healthcare robotics makes the transition from monitoring to action especially visible by translating AI-generated recommendations and decisions into speech, movement, prompting, physical assistance, escalation, and care coordination, making embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance fundamental design requirements. Further progress requires safe and interoperable care architectures in which intelligent components operate through clinically validated and accountable workflows. We propose agentic robotics as a future direction for supervised systems embedded in the care ecosystem, connecting AI agents and robots with clinicians, caregivers, and patients through auditable workflows that can be interrupted and remain subject to human oversight and explicit AI governance.
2611.18484.comment: 34 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Accepted for publication in Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems, Volume 10 (2027)
2611.18484.tldr_en: This paper proposes agentic robotics as a future direction for supervised systems embedded in the care ecosystem, connecting AI agents and robots with clinicians, caregivers, and patients through auditable workflows that can be interrupted and remain subject to human oversight and explicit AI governance.

2611.18422.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
2611.18422.abstract: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.
2611.18422.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. The technical supplement is included as an ancillary file. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

llm.title_ja: 状態はボトルネックではない：RTLからシリコンまでビット完全な、トライモードマルチキャストメッシュ上のページド状態Gated-DeltaNetタイル
llm.tldr_ja: エッジFPGA上での線形アテンション言語モデルの推論において、限られたオンチップメモリを超える再帰状態を外部メモリにページングするコストが、デコード性能の主要なボトルネックにならないことを示した。
llm.problem: 線形アテンション言語モデルの再帰状態が固定サイズであり、エッジFPGA上ではオンチップメモリを超えて外部メモリにページングする必要がある。
llm.method: Agilex 5 FPGA上にカスタムGated DeltaNetモデルの1層を計算し再帰状態をページングするハードウェアタイルを構築し、固定小数点演算の誤差を検証した。
llm.result: ページングが計算上の合計の最大11.2%のトラフィックしか追加せず、重みの配信がデコード性能を制限していることを示した。
keywords_ja: ハードウェアアクセラレーション

2611.18422.tldr_en: A hardware tile is built that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state, finding that state paging is practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.

2611.18397.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
2611.18397.abstract: We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds. We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction. These trajectories span simulated games and embodied environments, allowing the model to learn environmental dynamics across both physical and virtual domains. Sparse-thinking instruction tuning then substantially reduces redundant computation while preserving the reasoning needed for complex decisions. We train the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards. For real-time interaction, a cloud-edge inference engine serves numerous simulated game environments concurrently, supports unbounded-context execution, and keeps online inference latency low. Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks. These results suggest that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms. Training on these trajectories helps Gamer learn complex skills more steadily in environments with both physical and digital properties. This approach offers a path toward generalist agents that can interact across digital and physical worlds.
2611.18397.hf_summary_en: Gamer is a generalist agent framework that integrates perception, memory, and multi-step reasoning, trained through continued pre-training, sparse-thinking instruction tuning, and multi-turn reinforcement learning to interact efficiently in 2D and 3D environments.

llm.title_ja: Gamer：長期・実時間ゲームエージェントのための汎用ビジョン・言語・行動基盤モデル
llm.tldr_ja: 知覚・メモリ管理・多段階推論を統合し、継続事前学習・疎な思考の指示チューニング・マルチターン強化学習によって2Dおよび3D環境で効率的に動作する汎用エージェントフレームワーク「Gamer」を提案した。
llm.problem: 複雑なインタラクティブ環境における長期タスクをこなすための、知覚・メモリ・推論を統合した汎用エージェントの構築が求められている。
llm.method: デバイスレベルのキーボード・マウス操作データを用いた継続事前学習、疎な思考の指示チューニング、および安定したマルチターン強化学習を組み合わせた。
llm.result: 複数の挑戦的な3Dオープンワールドゲームにおいて熟練プレイヤーに匹敵する汎化性能と運用効率を示し、2Dゲームベンチマークでも競争力のある結果を達成した。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2611.18397.tldr_en: This work trains the policy for long-horizon interaction with a stable multi-turn reinforcement learning method that addresses finite context windows, accumulated rollout errors, and sparse rewards, and suggests that even repetitive keyboard and mouse trajectories can support substantial gains from scaling data and learning algorithms.

2611.18390.title: CS-MPC: Contraction-Certified Sampling-Based MPC for Nonlinear Systems Under Uncertainty
2611.18390.abstract: We present contraction-certified sampling-based model predictive control (CS-MPC) for tracking and safety of nonlinear robotic systems under parametric uncertainty, disturbances, and safety constraints that are revealed online. CS-MPC uses a contraction-certified tracking feedback inside every sampled rollout, which concentrates the rollouts around the reference, and an execution layer that verifies the applied input using a quantile-tightened discrete-time control barrier function condition. We derive a verification procedure for nonlinear contraction of the feedback-closed dynamics, and we prove a finite-sample stochastic stability bound and a mission-level probabilistic safety guarantee. We validate CS-MPC in simulation on a rover, a quadrotor, and an asteroid landing. When compared with standard model predictive path integral (MPPI) control, CS-MPC attains the same tracking error with 7 to 20 times fewer rollouts for the rover, and a 2 to 4 times lower tracking error for the quadrotor, with no safety violations in 200 Monte Carlo missions.

llm.title_ja: CS-MPC：不確実性下での非線形システムに向けた収縮保証付きサンプリングベースMPC
llm.tldr_ja: パラメータ不確実性や外乱を持つ非線形ロボットシステムの追従と安全性のために、サンプリングされたロールアウト内に収縮保証付き追跡フィードバックを組み込んだCS-MPCを提案した。
llm.problem: 非線形ロボットシステムにおいて、不確実性や外乱、オンラインで明らかになる安全制約の下での追従と安全性の担保が困難である。
llm.method: すべてのサンプリングロールアウト内で収縮保証付き追跡フィードバックを使用し、制御バリア関数条件を用いて入力を検証するCS-MPCを構築した。
llm.result: ローバーでは標準MPPIと比較して7〜20倍少ないロールアウト数で同等の追跡誤差を達成し、クワッドローターでは2〜4倍低い追跡誤差を達成した（200回のモンテカルロミッションで安全性違反ゼロ）。

2611.18390.tldr_en: This work derives a verification procedure for nonlinear contraction of the feedback-closed dynamics, and proves a finite-sample stochastic stability bound and a mission-level probabilistic safety guarantee for CS-MPC.

2611.18372.title: Vision-Language-Action Models: A Life-Cycle Survey of Design, Training and Deployment
2611.18372.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models adapt web-pretrained vision-language models to output robot actions, so that web knowledge carries over to physical control. In under 4 years the field has moved from RT-2, the first VLA, to open models that fine-tune on a single consumer GPU and to proprietary generalists that clean unseen homes. This survey reviews 88 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation. We follow a VLA through its life cycle, from model design to training and deployment, along seven axes. Model design covers (a) inputs and memory, what the model observes; (b) architecture, how its pipeline is built; (c) action output, how it produces motor commands; and (d) intermediate predictions, what else it predicts, from reasoning steps to future observations. Training covers (e) pretraining data, the mix of robot, web, human and simulated data, and (f) post-training, adaptation to the target robot. Deployment covers (g) real-time execution, keeping pace with the robot. We analyse 22 models on these axes and report their training data, model size, inference speed and hardware. Three trends emerge: (i) training data has broadened, from about 10,000 hours of teleoperated robot data ($π_0$) to 23,000 community-collected episodes (SmolVLA) and 20,000 hours of egocentric human video (GR00T N1.7); (ii) model sizes have split: most recent models have 3-7 billion parameters, while a new group under one billion runs on consumer GPUs; and (iii) generalist VLAs are emerging that handle both manipulation and navigation, such as UniVLA and Qwen-VLA. We also compare VLAs with world-action models, which predict future observations as well as actions. We review evidence that some VLAs with near-perfect benchmark scores fail when objects or the camera move slightly, and open up further research questions.

llm.title_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル：設計、訓練、デプロイのライフサイクルサーベイ
llm.tldr_ja: ウェブ事前学習済みのビジョン言語モデルをロボットの行動出力に適応させるVLAモデルについて、2022年12月から2026年10月までの88本の研究をライフサイクルの7つの軸に沿って包括的にレビューした。
llm.problem: VLA分野は急成長しているものの、モデル設計、訓練、デプロイに関する多様なアプローチやトレンドの体系的な整理が必要とされている。
llm.method: 入力・メモリ、アーキテクチャ、行動出力、中間予測、事前学習データ、ポストトレーニング、リアルタイム実行の7つの軸に沿って22のモデルを分析した。
llm.result: 訓練データの拡大、モデルサイズの二極化（30億〜70億パラメータのモデルとコンシューマGPU向け1億未満のモデル）、汎用VLAの台頭という3つのトレンドを明らかにした。
keywords_ja: ビジョン・言語・行動モデル

2611.18372.tldr_en: This survey reviews 89 works from December 2022 to October 2026, mainly on manipulation and navigation, plus humanoid control, world-action models and evaluation, and compares VLAs with world-action models, and review evidence that some VLAs with near-perfect benchmark scores fail after small scene changes.

2611.18365.title: Heavy Metal Acrobatics: Learning Dynamic Control for Skid-Steer Loaders
2611.18365.abstract: Automation of heavy machinery offers the opportunity to improve productivity in mechanized industries such as construction, mining, and material handling. Yet, automation of such machines is challenged by their complex dynamics, in part because of hydraulic actuation that involves fluids, flexible elements, and nonlinear delays. A concomitant challenge is the size and weight of these machines, which can make experiments on the physical systems exceedingly dangerous. Here, we show that \ac{RL} in simulation, followed by transfer of the learned policies from simulation to reality, can successfully automate acrobatic maneuvers that push a heavy construction machine to the limits of its actuation and have only previously been accomplished by a small number of elite human operators in official world-record performances. We trained policies that perform autonomous acrobatic maneuvers on a John Deere 332G, an operational 5-tonne skid-steer loader. The policies can autonomously swing the machine up onto two wheels and, while balancing on two wheels, drive over rough terrain, trace out specified trajectories, spin around, and swing the bucket back and forth before landing it safely back onto four wheels. This work demonstrates that \ac{RL} and sim-to-real transfer enable dynamic autonomous control of heavy machinery, directly contributing to greater automation in heavy equipment sectors. Videos: https://sites.google.com/leggedrobotics.com/heavy-metal-acrobatics This is the author's version of the work. It is posted here by permission of the AAAS for personal use, not for redistribution. The definitive version was published in Science Robotics on 11 November 2026, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1126/scirobotics.aef0894
2611.18365.journal_ref: P.-J. Lorentz, P. Egli, E. Jelavic, C. Li, R. Sundar, H. Suresh, P. Montgomery, L. Redden, M. Müller, O. Sener, V. Koltun, M. Hutter, Heavy metal acrobatics: Learning dynamic control for skid-steer loaders. Sci. Robot. 11, eaef0894 (2026)

llm.title_ja: ヘビーメタル・アクロバティックス：スキッドステアローダーのための動的制御の学習
llm.tldr_ja: シミュレーション内での強化学習と実機への転移（Sim2Real）により、5トンのスキッドステアローダーを二輪走行でバランスさせながら悪路走行やスピンなどの高度なアクロバティック機動を自律的に実行させることに成功した。
llm.problem: 重機はその複雑な動特性（流体や柔軟要素を含む油圧作動、非線形遅延）や巨大な重量とサイズのため、実機実験が極めて危険で自動化が困難である。
llm.method: シミュレーション環境で強化学習（RL）を用いてポリシーを訓練し、それを実機のジョンディア332Gスキッドステアローダーに転移させた。
llm.result: マシンを二輪で自律的に立ち上がらせ、悪路の走行、指定された軌跡のトレース、スピン、バケットの振動などを安全に実行できるようになった。
keywords_ja: スキッドステアローダー

badges.venue: P.-J. Lorentz, P. Egli, E. Jelavic, C. L 2026

2611.18365.tldr_en: Reinforcement learning in simulation, followed by transfer of the learned policies from simulation to reality, can successfully automate acrobatic maneuvers that push a heavy construction machine to the limits of its actuation and have only previously been accomplished by a small number of elite human operators in official world-record performances.

2611.18359.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
2611.18359.abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.
2611.18359.hf_summary_en: Agentic robotics, centered on an Embodied System 2 formed by a foundation model and embodied harness, requires a shared evaluation framework and research roadmap to achieve reliable physical autonomy.

llm.title_ja: エージェント型ロボティクスの展望：ロボットシステムの新しい時代
llm.tldr_ja: 基盤モデルと身体性ハーネスを組み合わせた「Embodied System 2」を中心に据えたエージェント型ロボティクスのパラダイムを提唱し、信頼性の高い物理的自律性を達成するための評価フレームワークと研究ロードマップを提示した。
llm.problem: フロンティアモデルがロボットベンチマークで高い性能を示す一方で、学術界は共通の定義、信頼できる評価フレームワーク、研究ロードマップを確立できていない。
llm.method: 基盤モデルと身体性ハーネスからなるEmbodied System 2を意思決定の核心と位置づけ、モデル能力と閉ループシステム性能を測定する評価フレームワークを提案した。
llm.result: 個別のプリミティブ実行から包括的な役割遂行へと責任を段階的に広げながら安全かつ信頼性高く作業を行うための持続的自律性へのロードマップを示した。
keywords_ja: エージェント型ロボティクス

2611.18359.tldr_en: It is argued that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics and an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance is proposed.

2611.18346.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
2611.18346.abstract: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. For each trajectory, VLAN provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments, while everyday obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and Blocked. Unlike goal-only evaluation, our benchmark measures physical safety and alignment with user-specific constraints via goal-reaching, collision-aware, and accessibility-aligned metrics. We benchmark modern vision-language models and find they often fail to consistently adapt obstacle relevance, path selection, and safety criteria across user profiles, suggesting accessibility-aware navigation requires dedicated datasets, tasks, and metrics beyond conventional embodied navigation evaluation. All data and code open-source at https://github.com/InSAI-Lab/VLAN.
2611.18346.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track. 25 pages, 17 tables, 6 figures. Code: https://github.com/InSAI-Lab/VLAN

llm.title_ja: VLAN：ビジョン・言語に基づくアクセシブルなナビゲーション
llm.tldr_ja: 多様な身体性（ヒューマノイド、四足歩行、視覚・運動障害者など）のアクセス可能性を考慮したナビゲーション評価のための大規模ベンチマーク「VLAN」を提案した。
llm.problem: 既存のベンチマークは固定された限られた身体性でのみ通行可能性を評価しており、アクセス可能な移動はシーン固有ではなくユーザー条件に依存する。
llm.method: 1,000シーン、2万本のナビゲーション軌道、16万個のキーフレームを含み、通行可能性を「Passable」「Bypass」「HighRisk」「Blocked」に分類したベンチマーク「VLAN」を構築した。
llm.result: 最新のビジョン言語モデルを評価した結果、障害物の関連性やパス選択をユーザープロファイルに応じて一貫して適応させることができないことが示された。
keywords_ja: アクセシブルナビゲーション

2611.18346.tldr_en: This work presents Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries, and benchmarking modern vision-language models find they often fail to consistently adapt obstacle relevance, path selection, and safety criteria across user profiles.

2611.18305.title: PROOF: Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion
2611.18305.abstract: Vision-based perceptive locomotion has enabled legged robots to achieve agile and terrain-aware locomotion across complex environments. However, the reliability of such systems heavily depends on visual observations, which are inherently susceptible to occlusion, reflective surfaces, and illumination variations, often resulting in catastrophic locomotion failures under degraded perception conditions. In this paper, we present PROOF (Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion), a perceptive locomotion framework that enables robust locomotion under severe visual disturbances. Our method adopts a two-stage teacher-student learning paradigm that explicitly models perception reliability: the teacher learns both perception-driven and proprioceptive fallback behaviors, while the student predicts exteroceptive features with uncertainty and suppresses them under out-of-distribution inputs. We evaluate our method on a Unitree Go2 quadruped equipped with a RealSense D435 depth camera in real-world settings. Under normal visual conditions, our method enables the robot to successfully perform high-dynamic parkour maneuvers, including traversing large gaps, elevated platforms, and narrow beam terrains. Under severe visual degradation, such as heavy occlusion and strong illumination changes, the robot continues to maintain stable and robust locomotion performance.

llm.title_ja: PROOF：脚式ロボットのためのオクルージョンフォールバックによる知覚的ロバスト性
llm.tldr_ja: 視覚的撹乱に対してロバストな歩行を実現するため、知覚の信頼性を明示的にモデル化する2段階の教師・生徒学習パラダイムに基づく知覚的歩行フレームワーク「PROOF」を提案した。
llm.problem: 視覚ベースの知覚的歩行はオクルージョンや反射面、照明変動に弱く、劣化した知覚条件下で壊滅的な歩行失敗を引き起こす。
llm.method: 教師が知覚駆動型およびプロプリオセプティブなフォールバック行動を学習し、生徒が不確実性つきの外セプティブ特徴を予測してOOD入力時にそれを抑制する2段階学習パラダイムを採用した。
llm.result: Unitree Go2実機を用いた実験により、隙間、高所プラットフォーム、狭い梁などのパルクール機動を成功させ、激しい視覚的劣化下でも安定した歩行を維持できた。

2611.18305.tldr_en: This paper presents PROOF (Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion), a perceptive locomotion framework that enables robust locomotion under severe visual disturbances and adopts a two-stage teacher-student learning paradigm.

2611.18298.title: Objectives as Policies: Vision-Language Model Cost Programs for Contact-Rich Manipulation
2611.18298.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown strong semantic and spatial reasoning capabilities in 3D environments. Recently, connecting VLMs with model-predictive controllers (MPC) has emerged as a paradigm for combining strong semantic reasoning with physics-based planning. However, connecting these two for contact-rich robotic manipulation requires a task representation that bridges the two and captures how physical interactions can be reasoned by VLMs. In this work, we introduce Objectives as Policies (OaP), a framework that connects a pretrained VLM to a shared sampling-based MPC through an editable objective program. Each program specifies a sequence of stages for completing a task, combining running and terminal costs from a cost library with stage completion conditions. Given a natural-language task instruction and scene observation, we build a simulation-based digital twin through real-to-sim, and the VLM generates an objective program that is executed by the MPC in the simulation. The program is iteratively updated by the VLM based on MPC rollouts, before being deployed in the real world. We evaluate our framework in both simulation and the real world on four tabletop manipulation tasks, and show that it outperforms strong baselines. Additional videos and examples are available on the project website: https://zihaolu001.github.io/oap-project/

llm.title_ja: 目的としてのポリシー：接触リッチなマニピュレーションのためのビジョン・言語モデルコストプログラム
llm.tldr_ja: 事前学習済みVLMを編集可能な目的プログラムを介して共有サンプリングベースMPCに接続し、自然言語の指示に基づいて接触リッチなタスクを実行するフレームワーク「Objectives as Policies (OaP)」を提案した。
llm.problem: VLMとモデル予測制御を接触リッチなロボットマニピュレーションで結合するには、物理的相互作用をVLMが推論できるタスク表現が必要である。
llm.method: タスク完了のためのステージのシーケンスを指定する編集可能な目的プログラムを介して、VLMとシミュレーションベースのデジタルツインをMPCに接続した。
llm.result: シミュレーションと実世界の4つの卓上マニピュレーションタスクにおいて、強力なベースラインを上回る性能を示した。

2611.18298.tldr_en: Objectives as Policies (OaP) is introduced, a framework that connects a pretrained VLM to a shared sampling-based MPC through an editable objective program that is executed by the MPC in the simulation.

2611.18230.title: Personalization of Basic and Moral Values Guiding LLM-Controlled Assistant Robots
2611.18230.abstract: Personal assistant robots powered by large language models (LLMs) are likely to enter everyday life within the next decade, but the values that should guide their behaviour remain largely unspecified. Current alignment practice steers a single model toward an aggregate of human values, ignoring that individual users may prefer a robot whose value profile differs from their own. We administer parallel self- and robot-targeted versions of three established psycho-metric instruments - the simplified Schwartz Values Survey (SVS), the Portrait Values Questionnaire (PVQ-21), and the Moral Foundations Questionnaire (MFQ) - to potential future users (N=22), capturing both their personal values and the values they would want an assistant robot to embody. We compare the three instruments as personalization tools using the UEQ-S and benchmark fifteen contemporary LLMs against the resulting profiles. Participants wanted their robot to score markedly lower than themselves on personal-focus values and higher on social-focus values; moral profiles were nearly identical. LLMs prompted to act as robots shifted only weakly toward the desired profile, indicating that default model behaviour and prompt engineering are no substitute for explicit value personalization.

llm.title_ja: LLM制御アシスタントロボットを導く基本的・道徳的価値観のパーソナライゼーション

llm.problem: 現在のアライメント手法は単一のモデルを人間全体の集約値に合わせるだけであり、個々のユーザーが好むロボットの価値観プロファイルの多様性を無視している。
llm.method: シュワルツ価値観調査（SVS）、肖像価値観質問票（PVQ-21）、道徳的基盤質問票（MFQ）を用いて将来のユーザーの価値観とロボットに求める価値観を測定し、15のLLMと比較した。

アシスタントロボット

2611.18186.title: NPU-Accelerated GNSS Signal Acquisition
2611.18186.abstract: On small single-board computers (SBCs), GNSS signal acquisition is a major CPU load. This paper proposes using the neural processing unit (NPU) of an SBC not for machine learning but as an accelerator for the parallel code search in GNSS signal acquisition. The discrete Fourier transform (DFT) used in acquisition is decomposed by the four-step DFT into matrix products of small DFTs and expressed by $1\times1$ convolutions, element-wise products, and transposes, which NPUs execute efficiently. Furthermore, we propose a method that divides the DFT, the non-coherent integration, and the peak detection between the CPU and the NPU according to the configuration of the NPU (an NPU with its own memory connected via PCIe, or an NPU sharing memory with the CPU). The proposed method is implemented in the open-source software GNSS receiver Pocket SDR and evaluated on a Raspberry Pi 5 combined with the external AX8850 NPU and on the NPU built into the SoC (RK3588) of the ROCK 5C, a small SBC of comparable size. Compared with acquisition by an optimized CPU implementation, the acquisition of short codes on the Raspberry Pi 5 with the AX8850 is 3.0-3.8 times faster. In the evaluation of the whole receiver, the number of tracking channels that reach their first lock within 30 s with the NPU is 1.5 times that with the CPU, and the time until 90% of the channels are locked is reduced from 66 s to 26 s. Furthermore, because the CPU load of acquisition is reduced, the number of tracking channels that can be processed in real time increases from about 175 to about 230. These results show that using the NPU on SBCs with limited CPU resources is effective for achieving both GNSS signal acquisition and tracking. The implementation is publicly available as open source under the name PocketSDR-NPU.

llm.title_ja: NPUアクセラレーテッドGNSS信号捕捉
llm.tldr_ja: 小型シングルボードコンピュータ（SBC）のNPUを機械学習ではなくGNSS信号捕捉の並列コード検索のアクセラレータとして活用し、CPU負荷を軽減しつつ高速化する手法を提案した。

llm.method: 4ステップDFTを用いた離散フーリエ変換をNPUが効率的に実行可能な小さなDFTの行列積、1x1畳み込み、要素積、転置に分解し、CPUとNPUの間で処理を分割した。
llm.result: Raspberry Pi 5と外部AX8850 NPUを用いた評価で、短コードの捕捉が3.0〜3.8倍高速化し、リアルタイム処理可能な追跡チャンネル数が増加した。
keywords_ja: シングルボードコンピュータ
